Set up three shallow bowls: flour in the first, the 2 remaining eggs beaten in the second, panko in the third. Roll each wrapped egg in flour, then egg wash, then press firmly into panko to coat all over.
Mist the air fryer basket with cooking spray. Arrange the eggs so they don't touch, then spray the tops generously so the panko crisps and browns evenly.
Air-fry at 390F for 14-18 minutes, flipping gently halfway and re-spraying any pale spots, until the coating is deep golden and the sausage reaches 165F internal with no pink.
Rest 3-5 minutes so the juices settle, then halve to reveal the center. Garnish with chopped parsley and serve warm with mustard for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy a roll of bulk breakfast sausage instead of links: it's cheaper per ounce and has no casings to strip.
Make your own panko by toasting and crushing a couple of stale bread slices in the oven or air fryer.
Boil and wrap a big batch on the weekend, store them coated but uncooked in the fridge, and air-fry fresh when you want a hot snack.

substitutions.swap: Ground pork or ground turkey mixed with extra paprika, salt, and pepper to mimic seasoned sausage
substitutions.savings: Often cheaper per serving than pre-seasoned sausage

substitutions.swap: Regular breadcrumbs or crushed crackers
substitutions.savings: Saves about $0.05 per cup

substitutions.swap: Quail eggs for bite-sized cocktail-style Scotch eggs
substitutions.savings: Fun party version, no real savings

recipes.name: Viral Grated-Egg Avocado Toast
recipes.description: The TikTok trick that finally fixed avocado toast: a cold hard-boiled egg grated into fluffy, pillowy clouds that melt into the smashed avocado instead of sliding off. Crunchy sourdough, everything seasoning, a squeeze of lemon, and a hit of hot sauce make it five-minute, dorm-friendly perfection.

ingredients.note: cold from the fridge so it grates into fluffy strands
ripe, gives easily to a gentle squeeze

steps: Hard-boil ahead if needed: place 1 egg in a small pot, cover with cold water by an inch, and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Cover, cut the heat, and let sit 11-12 minutes for a fully set, food-safe yolk. Drain, plunge into ice water for a minute, then peel and chill in the fridge until cold.
Toast 1 thick slice of sourdough in a toaster or under a broiler until deeply golden and crisp at the edges, 2-3 minutes. A sturdy, crunchy base keeps the toppings from going soggy.
Halve the avocado, scoop half onto the warm toast, and smash it on with a fork, spreading it edge to edge so every bite is covered.
Squeeze about a quarter lemon over the avocado and season with a pinch of salt and pepper; the acid keeps it bright green and seasons the base.
Hold the cold hard-boiled egg over the toast and grate it on the large holes of a box grater, letting the fluffy strands fall in an even, pillowy layer across the whole surface.
Shower with everything bagel seasoning and a few dashes of hot sauce. If you want extra heat and richness, add red pepper flakes and a thin drizzle of olive oil.
Eat right away while the toast is still crisp and the cold, pillowy egg contrasts the warm avocado.
cheapTips: Boil a whole carton of eggs at once and keep them peeled in the fridge so this snack comes together in two minutes flat all week.
Buy avocados firm and let them ripen on the counter, then refrigerate once soft to stop them browning and stretch them for days.
Skip a store-bought everything blend and shake your own from sesame seeds, poppy seeds, dried garlic, dried onion, and flaky salt you already have.

substitutions.swap: Boil a regular egg yourself (egg, ~12 min) and chill it before grating
substitutions.savings: Saves about $0.28 per egg vs pre-boiled

substitutions.swap: Any sturdy sandwich bread, toasted extra-crisp
substitutions.savings: Saves about $0.22 per slice

substitutions.swap: A pinch of sesame seeds plus salt and garlic powder
substitutions.savings: Pennies cheaper from pantry staples

recipes.name: Fluffy Souffle Omelette (Cloud Omelette)
recipes.description: A jiggly, melt-in-your-mouth omelette that rises into a golden cloud thanks to whipped egg whites, all from a few eggs and a nonstick pan. It looks like a restaurant flex but is dorm-easy and costs pennies.

ingredients.note: helps the whites whip to stiff, stable peaks

steps: Crack 3 eggs and carefully separate the yolks from the whites into two clean, dry bowls. Even a speck of yolk in the whites will keep them from whipping, so take your time.
Season the yolks with the salt and pepper and whisk until smooth and slightly pale; set aside.
Add the optional cream of tartar to the whites, then whip with a hand mixer or balloon whisk for 2-3 minutes until stiff, glossy peaks form and the foam holds its shape when you lift the beater.
Add the yolks to the whites and fold gently with a spatula, scooping from the bottom up, until just combined. Stop while a few streaks remain so you keep the air; do not stir.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over low heat and swirl to coat. Low heat is key, it should not sizzle hard. Pour in the airy batter and gently smooth the top into a mound.

Cover with a lid and cook undisturbed 7-9 minutes. The omelette will puff and the bottom will turn golden; the top is done when it looks just barely set and no longer wet or glossy. If using cheese, sprinkle it over one half during the last 2 minutes to melt.

Slide a spatula under one side, fold the omelette in half over itself, then slide it onto a plate. Garnish with snipped chives and eat right away while it is hot and jiggly; the eggs should be fully set and not runny.
cheapTips: You only need eggs, butter and salt for the full effect, skip every optional add-in and this is one of the cheapest hot breakfasts you can make.
No hand mixer? A regular whisk and 3-4 minutes of arm work gets the whites to stiff peaks for free.
Save the leftover butter wrapper to grease the pan instead of using a fresh tablespoon, the thin film is all a nonstick pan needs.

substitutions.swap: A quick spritz of cooking spray or a teaspoon of any neutral oil greases the nonstick pan just as well.
substitutions.savings: Saves about $0.15 per omelette

substitutions.swap: A few drops of lemon juice or white vinegar stabilize the whites the same way.
substitutions.savings: Skip buying a jar you may not use

substitutions.swap: Snipped scallion greens or a pinch of dried herbs add color and bite for less.
substitutions.savings: Saves about $2 versus a fresh chive bunch

recipes.name: Tornado Omurice (Swirled Egg over Ketchup Fried Rice)
recipes.description: A glossy, chopstick-swirled egg tornado draped over savory-sweet ketchup fried rice. It's the viral egg trick that turns a humble bowl of pantry rice into pure dinner theater, and nailing the swirl feels like unlocking a brand-new kitchen skill.

ingredients.note: cooked and cooled; day-old rice works best
fresh or pasteurized, for the tornado swirl
split between rice and egg pan
mixed with ketchup for the drizzle

steps: Finely dice 1/4 onion and 1/2 carrot. Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil and 1 tbsp butter in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat, then saute the onion and carrot for 2-3 minutes until softened and the onion is translucent.
Add 1.5 cups cooled cooked rice and 1/4 cup frozen peas. Break up any clumps and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until the rice is heated through and steaming.

Push the rice to one side, add 2 tbsp ketchup (and 1/2 tbsp soy sauce, if using) to the bare pan and let it sizzle for 20-30 seconds to deepen the flavor, then toss to coat every grain. Season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper, mound onto a plate and shape into a neat oval. Wipe the pan clean.

Crack 3 eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt, and beat thoroughly until completely uniform with no streaks of white — a smooth swirl needs fully blended eggs. Use fresh or pasteurized eggs, since the center is served soft.
Set the clean nonstick pan over medium heat and add the remaining 1/2 tbsp vegetable oil, swirling to coat. When the oil shimmers, pour in all the beaten egg at once.

As the edges begin to set but the center is still glossy and liquid (about 90% cooked, roughly 30-45 seconds), lower the heat. Plant two chopsticks straight down into the center and twirl steadily in one direction, gathering the loose egg into a spiraling tornado.

Once the swirl holds its shape and the egg is set on the outside but still soft in the very center, slide it off the pan onto the rice mound. For a fully set egg with no soft center, keep twirling over low heat an extra 20-30 seconds until no liquid egg remains before plating.
Stir 1 tsp sriracha into a little extra ketchup and drizzle over the tornado in a zigzag. Scatter sliced scallion on top and serve immediately while hot.
cheapTips: Use day-old leftover rice from a previous dinner. It's cheaper than cooking fresh, and the drier grains fry up far better without turning mushy.
Frozen peas and carrots from a single bag of mixed veg cost pennies per serving and keep for months. Skip buying fresh just for this dish.
Plain ketchup and a couple of eggs do almost all the flavor work here, so no specialty Asian sauces are required.

substitutions.swap: Any frozen mixed veg, frozen corn, or leftover cooked vegetables
substitutions.savings: Use whatever is already in your freezer instead of a dedicated bag

substitutions.swap: An extra 1/2 tbsp vegetable oil (keeps the dish dairy-free)
substitutions.savings: Saves a few cents and makes it fully dairy-free

substitutions.swap: Any hot sauce you already own, or just more ketchup
substitutions.savings: No need to buy sriracha for one drizzle

recipes.name: Croque Madame (Ham, Gruyere and Bechamel Toast with a Fried Egg)
recipes.description: A French bistro icon: crisp toasted bread layered with ham and nutty Gruyere, blanketed in a glossy bechamel, broiled until golden and bubbling, then crowned with a runny fried egg. It is basically a grilled cheese that went to Paris.

ingredients.note: sturdy white or sourdough, sliced thick
shredded; split between the filling and the top
1 tbsp for the roux, 1 tbsp for frying the eggs
warm, whisked in for the bechamel
grated, extra on top to help it brown

steps: Set an oven rack about 6 inches below the broiler and turn the broiler to high. Lightly toast the 4 bread slices (toaster or oven) so they stay crisp under the sauce, then set them on a foil-lined baking sheet.

Make the bechamel: melt 1 tbsp butter in a small saucepan over medium heat, whisk in the flour, and cook 1 minute until it smells nutty but stays pale. Slowly whisk in the warm milk and keep whisking 2 to 3 minutes until it thickens to a pourable, spoon-coating sauce. Stir in the pinch of nutmeg, the salt, and pepper, then take it off the heat.
Build the sandwiches: smear the optional Dijon on 2 of the toasts, lay 2 slices of ham on each, and top with about half the Gruyere. Close each with a second toast.
Spoon a generous layer of bechamel over the top of each closed sandwich, letting it run down the sides, then scatter the remaining Gruyere (and optional Parmesan) on top.
Broil 3 to 5 minutes, watching closely, until the cheese and bechamel are bubbling and spotted deep golden brown. Move them to plates.

Fry the eggs: melt the remaining 1 tbsp butter in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Crack in the eggs and cook 2 to 3 minutes until the whites are fully set and opaque but the yolks are still runny (cook an extra minute or two if you prefer firm yolks). Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Slide one fried egg onto each broiled sandwich, garnish with chives if using, and serve immediately while the cheese is molten and the yolk is glossy.
cheapTips: Gruyere is the splurge here — buy a small wedge or sub in cheaper Swiss/Emmental and you will not lose much of the nutty flavor.
Use whatever sturdy bread you already have; day-old sourdough or plain white sandwich bread both toast up perfectly and save you a special trip.
Make a double batch of bechamel and refrigerate half — it reheats with a splash of milk and turns next-day toast or pasta into something fancy for almost nothing.

substitutions.swap: swiss-cheese or emmental — melts the same nutty way
substitutions.savings: saves roughly $0.50 per serving

substitutions.swap: deli-turkey or canadian-bacon for a leaner crown
substitutions.savings: roughly the same cost, leaner

substitutions.swap: sourdough or brioche-buns for a richer base
substitutions.savings: pennies more for a bistro upgrade

recipes.name: Hawaiian Loco Moco
recipes.description: Hawaii's ultimate diner comfort plate: a juicy seared beef patty over a mound of hot white rice, smothered in savory brown mushroom gravy and crowned with a sunny-side-up egg whose runny yolk melts into every bite. Hearty, cheap, and deeply satisfying.
steps: Cook the rice: rinse 1 cup white rice, combine with about 1.5 cups water in a pot, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low 15-18 minutes until tender. Keep covered and warm while you build the rest.
Mix the ground beef with a big pinch of salt and pepper and about 1 tsp of the worcestershire, then form 2 firm patties slightly wider than your serving size since they shrink as they cook.

Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high. Sear the patties 3-4 minutes per side until well browned and cooked through to an internal temperature of 160F (no pink in the center) for food safety. Transfer to a plate.

In the same pan (keep the browned drippings), add the diced half onion and sliced mushrooms with the butter. Cook over medium 4-5 minutes until softened and golden, then stir in the minced garlic for 30 seconds.

Pour in 1.5 cups beef broth, the soy sauce, and remaining worcestershire; scrape up the browned bits and bring to a simmer. Whisk the cornstarch with 2 tbsp cold water, stir it in, and simmer 2-3 minutes until the gravy thickens enough to coat a spoon. Taste and adjust salt and pepper.
Nestle the patties back into the gravy and spoon it over them; keep warm on low heat while you fry the eggs.

In a separate nonstick pan over medium-low, fry the eggs sunny-side-up 2-3 minutes until the whites are fully set but the yolks are still runny, for that classic melt-into-the-gravy moment. A runny yolk is traditional here; if you are serving young children, anyone pregnant, or anyone with a weakened immune system, use pasteurized eggs or cook until the yolk is firm.
Plate it up: a mound of hot rice, a gravy-smothered patty on top, extra gravy ladled over, and a fried egg crowning each plate. Garnish with sliced scallions and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Plain white rice is one of the cheapest ways to bulk up any meal, so make a little extra and you've got tomorrow's lunch base ready to go.
Skip the mushrooms entirely if money's tight; an onion-only brown gravy is still classic and delicious, and saves you over a dollar.
Buy ground beef in the largest pack you can afford and freeze it in patty-sized portions; per-pound it's far cheaper than small trays.

substitutions.swap: Use ground turkey for a leaner, cheaper patty (cook fully to 165F)
substitutions.savings: ~$0.25/serving

substitutions.swap: Dissolve a beef bouillon cube in 1.5 cups hot water
substitutions.savings: ~$0.70 total

substitutions.swap: Canned mushrooms, drained, or just leave them out
substitutions.savings: ~$1.00 total

substitutions.swap: Swap butter for a splash of vegetable oil to make the dish fully dairy-free
substitutions.savings: ~$0.15 total

recipes.name: Classic Quiche Lorraine
recipes.description: A silky baked egg custard loaded with crisp smoky bacon and nutty Gruyere in a flaky crust. Make it on Sunday and you've got dinner-party-worthy slices for lunches all week, delicious hot or cold straight from the fridge.

ingredients.note: or half-and-half for a lighter custard

steps: Heat the oven to 325F and set the pie crust on a rimmed baking sheet (it catches drips). If the crust is a flimsy foil pan, leave it there; if it's a dough round, press it into a 9-inch pie dish.

Cook the bacon: lay the slices in a cold skillet over medium heat and fry 6-8 minutes, flipping, until deeply browned and crisp with no raw pink. Move to a paper towel, then crumble. Pour off all but a thin film of fat.
Whisk the custard: in a bowl, beat the 4 eggs with the heavy cream, salt, pepper, cayenne, and a tiny grating of nutmeg until fully smooth and uniform, with no streaks of white.
Scatter the crumbled bacon, shredded Gruyere, and sliced scallions evenly across the bottom of the crust.
Slowly pour the egg custard over the filling until it nearly reaches the rim, stopping just below the edge so it won't overflow as it puffs.

Bake at 325F for 45-50 minutes. It's done when the edges are set and puffed but the center still has a slight jiggle, like soft jello; a knife inserted 1 inch from center should come out mostly clean. The custard must be fully set, not liquid (eggs cooked to 160F for safety).
If the crust edges brown too fast, tent them with foil for the last 15 minutes.
Let the quiche rest 15-20 minutes before slicing; it firms up as it cools. Garnish with chopped parsley and cut into 6 wedges.
To meal-prep: cool fully, wrap, and refrigerate up to 4 days. Eat cold, or reheat a slice in the microwave for 45-60 seconds or in a 325F oven for 10 minutes.
cheapTips: Buy a block of Gruyere on sale and shred it yourself instead of buying pre-shredded, or swap in a milder Swiss-style melting cheese for the same nutty pull at a lower price.
Bacon ends and pieces (or turkey bacon) cost less than premium strips and disappear into the custard anyway.
A store-bought crust is cheaper than buying butter and flour for one pie, and a single quiche stretches into 6 lunches, so your cost per meal drops fast.

substitutions.swap: a milder Swiss-style melting cheese
substitutions.savings: often cheaper per ounce with a similar nutty melt

substitutions.swap: half-and-half, or whole milk plus a pat of butter
substitutions.savings: a few cents per quiche and a lighter custard

substitutions.swap: diced ham or turkey bacon
substitutions.savings: saves around $0.50-1.00 and runs leaner

recipes.name: Hong Kong Egg Tarts (Dan Tat)
recipes.description: Tender, buttery shortcrust shells cradling a glassy-smooth, lightly sweet egg custard, just like the dim-sum cart classic. Silkier and milder than its Portuguese cousin, and totally doable in a dorm with a single rolled pie crust and a muffin tin.

ingredients.note: one rolled refrigerated pie crust, cut into rounds and pressed into a muffin tin to make about 8 shells
dissolved into the hot water to make a smooth syrup
optional; a tiny splash rounds out the custard

steps: Heat the oven to 400F (200C) with a rack in the lower third. Cut the pie crust into rounds, press them into the cups of a muffin tin to form 8 small shells, and chill while the oven heats.
Make a sugar syrup: stir the sugar into the 1/2 cup of hot water until fully dissolved and clear, then let it cool to lukewarm (if it is still hot it will scramble the eggs).
In a bowl, gently whisk the 3 whole eggs with the evaporated milk and optional vanilla until just combined. Whisk slowly to avoid beating in air bubbles, which cause a bumpy surface.
Pour the cooled sugar syrup into the egg mixture and stir gently until you have a smooth, pale custard.
Strain the custard through a fine-mesh sieve into a measuring cup, then skim off any foam. This is what gives the tarts their signature glassy top, so do not skip it.
Pour the custard into each chilled shell, filling to about 80 percent so it does not overflow as it sets.

Bake at 400F for 10 minutes, then lower the oven to 350F (175C) and bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until the custard is just set with only a faint jiggle in the center and a toothpick inserted near the edge can stand upright on its own. Do not overbake, or the custard puffs and cracks.
Cool 5 to 10 minutes so the custard firms up and is fully set throughout (a clean, non-runny baked custard). Serve warm; they are best the day they are made.
cheapTips: One rolled pie crust pressed into a muffin tin yields about 8 tart shells, far cheaper than buying pre-formed tart shells.
Use the leftover half can of evaporated milk in coffee, oatmeal, or a second batch within a few days so nothing goes to waste.
Whole eggs plus a splash of evaporated milk cost pennies per tart compared to a bakery dan tat.

substitutions.swap: Use 2/3 cup whole milk warmed slightly; the custard is a touch less rich but still silky.
substitutions.savings: Saves about $1 if you already have milk on hand

substitutions.swap: Honey works too; just dissolve it fully into the warm water first.
A few drops of almond extract for a more floral, bakery-style aroma.

recipes.name: Japanese Purin (Caramel Custard Pudding)
recipes.description: A wobbly, tender egg custard nestled in a pool of bittersweet caramel, firmer and more spoonable than flan. Just a handful of humble ingredients turn into Japan's most nostalgic afternoon treat, single-serve and impossibly cute.

ingredients.note: 3 tbsp for the custard, 4 tbsp for the caramel
1 tbsp to start the caramel, 3 tbsp hot to thin it

steps: Make the caramel: in a small saucepan over medium heat, combine 4 tbsp sugar and 1 tbsp water. Let it melt undisturbed, swirling the pan occasionally (do not stir), until it turns a deep amber, about 5-7 minutes. Watch closely at the end, as it goes from amber to burnt fast.

Off the heat, carefully add 3 tbsp hot water at arm's length (it will sputter and steam violently). Swirl to combine, then immediately divide the hot caramel between 2 ramekins, tilting to coat the bottoms. Set aside to harden.

Make the custard base: warm the whole milk with 3 tbsp sugar in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring just until the sugar dissolves and the milk is steaming but not boiling, about 3 minutes. Remove from heat.

In a bowl, gently whisk the 3 eggs with the vanilla extract until just combined, avoiding too many bubbles. Pour the warm milk into the eggs in a thin, steady stream while whisking, so the eggs temper rather than scramble.
Strain the custard through a fine-mesh sieve into a measuring cup, then divide it evenly over the hardened caramel in the ramekins. Skim off any surface foam for a smooth top.

Set the ramekins in a baking dish and pour hot water into the dish until it reaches halfway up their sides. Bake at 320F (160C) for 35-40 minutes, until the custard is fully set with only a slight jiggle in the very center; the eggs should be cooked through, never runny.
Lift the ramekins from the water bath and cool to room temperature, then chill in the fridge at least 3 hours or overnight, until cold and firm.
To serve, run a thin knife around the edge of each purin, set a small plate on top, and invert so the caramel pools over the custard. Finish with a dollop of whipped cream if desired.
cheapTips: Whole milk gives the richest custard, but any milk already in your fridge works and shaves a few cents off.
No ramekins? Use small oven-safe mugs, glass jars, or one larger dish (just bake a little longer until set).
Caramel is only sugar and water, the cheapest part of the dish, so don't be afraid to practice it a couple of times until you nail the amber color.

substitutions.swap: Use evaporated milk or half-and-half for an extra-rich, denser purin
substitutions.savings: costs a bit more but tastes more luxurious

substitutions.swap: Swap in a scraped vanilla bean or a splash of rum for deeper flavor
substitutions.savings: vanilla bean costs more; rum is roughly even

substitutions.swap: Use brown sugar in the caramel for a deeper, almost toffee note
substitutions.savings: about the same cost

recipes.name: Homemade Lemon Curd
recipes.description: A bright, glossy, intensely tangy-sweet egg-yolk custard that comes together on the stovetop in about 10 minutes from five ingredients. Spread it on toast, swirl it into yogurt, or fill a tart - it's the perfect way to use up extra yolks.

ingredients.note: save the whites for another use

steps: Zest the lemons first, then juice them; you want about 1/2 cup of juice. Rub the zest into the sugar with your fingertips in a small bowl until the sugar smells lemony and looks slightly damp.
In a non-reactive (stainless or glass) saucepan off the heat, whisk the egg yolks with the lemon sugar until pale and smooth, then whisk in the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Add the cold butter pieces and set the pan over medium-low heat. Stir constantly with a whisk or silicone spatula, scraping the corners so the yolks never scramble.

Cook gently for about 8 to 10 minutes, until the curd goes from foamy and thin to smooth and glossy. It is done when it thickly coats the back of a spoon and a finger swiped through leaves a clean line (about 170°F). Do not let it boil - cooking the yolks to 170°F sets the curd fully and makes it food-safe, not runny.
Immediately pour the curd through a fine-mesh strainer into a clean jar or bowl to catch the zest and any cooked egg bits, leaving you with a silky spread.
Press a piece of plastic wrap directly onto the surface of the curd so a skin cannot form.
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate at least 2 hours until cold and thick.
Keep refrigerated and use within 1 to 2 weeks. Spread on toast or scones, swirl into yogurt, or use as a tart filling.
cheapTips: This is the ideal home for leftover egg yolks from any recipe that used only whites (meringue, macarons, egg-white omelets), so nothing goes to waste.
Bottled lemon juice works fine for the juice and is cheaper than fresh; just buy one fresh lemon for the zest, which carries most of the aroma.
No fine strainer? Skip it and just whisk hard at the end; a few specks of zest only add flavor and texture.

substitutions.swap: Use bottled lemon juice plus one fresh lemon for zest
substitutions.savings: About $1 cheaper than buying three fresh lemons

substitutions.swap: Plant butter or margarine for a dairy-free curd
substitutions.savings: Saves a few cents and makes it dairy-free

substitutions.swap: Honey or maple syrup, reduce juice slightly to keep it thick
substitutions.savings: Use what's already in the pantry

recipes.name: Sri Lankan Egg Hopper (Bittara Appa)
recipes.description: A bowl-shaped coconut-rice crepe with crispy lacy edges and a soft, spongy center, with an egg cracked right into the middle so the yolk stays gloriously runny. Served with a fiery, zesty pol sambol, it's a genuine showstopper breakfast and a fun weekend project.

ingredients.note: one cracked into the center of each hopper
for greasing the pan between hoppers
or Kashmiri chili, for pol sambol

steps: Make the batter: whisk 1 cup rice flour with about 3/4 can coconut milk, 1 tbsp sugar, 1/2 tsp instant yeast, and 1/2 tsp salt until smooth and pourable, like thin pancake batter. Add a splash of warm water if it's too thick.
Cover the bowl and ferment somewhere warm for 4-6 hours (or overnight in the fridge, then bring to room temp). It's ready when it looks bubbly, smells slightly tangy, and has grown a little.

Make the optional pol sambol while you wait: combine the shredded coconut, finely chopped red onion, red pepper flakes, lime juice, and a pinch of salt. Squeeze it together with your fingers until it turns blush-pink and fragrant, then set aside.
Stir the batter gently. Heat a small rounded hopper pan (or a small nonstick bowl-shaped pan) over medium heat and grease lightly with coconut oil using a folded paper towel.
Pour in a small ladle of batter (about 1/3 cup), then immediately lift the pan and swirl so the batter coats up the sides, forming a thin bowl with a slightly thicker pool at the bottom.

Crack one egg into the center, season with a pinch of salt, cover with a lid, and cook 2-3 minutes over medium heat: the lacy edges should turn deep golden and crisp and the white should set fully while the yolk stays soft and runny.
Slide a thin spatula around the crisp edge to release the hopper and lift it out whole onto a plate. Re-grease the pan and repeat with the remaining batter and second egg.

Serve right away while the edges are crisp and the yolk is warm. Scatter curry leaves over the top and spoon the pol sambol alongside. The yolk is intentionally soft-set, so use fresh, properly refrigerated eggs.
cheapTips: A bag of rice flour and one can of coconut milk make many hoppers, so the per-hopper cost is tiny once you've stocked up; batch the batter and feed a few friends.
No hopper pan? A small nonstick saucepan or even a deep ladle-shaped wok works, just swirl the batter up the sides the same way.
Skip the pol sambol if money's tight and just hit the runny yolk with salt, pepper, and a squeeze of lime; it's still delicious.

substitutions.swap: Use 1/4 tsp baking soda plus a splash of club soda for a quicker, no-wait batter (less tangy, but no overnight ferment needed).
substitutions.savings: skips the wait

substitutions.swap: Light coconut milk, or coconut milk thinned with water; you mainly need the coconut flavor and a pourable consistency.
Any chili powder, cayenne, or a chopped fresh chili for the pol sambol.
substitutions.savings: uses what you have

recipes.name: Beet Pickled Eggs
recipes.description: Jewel-magenta pickled eggs with a tangy-sweet bite and a stunning ombre ring under the shell, perfect sliced onto a snack board. Just hard-boil, drop into a beet-and-vinegar brine, and let the fridge do all the work for a week.

ingredients.note: sliced, plus all the juice from the can

steps: Place the 6 eggs in a small pot and cover with cold water by about an inch. Bring to a rolling boil over high heat, then turn off the heat, cover, and let sit 11-12 minutes for fully set yolks. The eggs must be hard-boiled (firm yolk, no runniness) so they cure safely in the brine.

While the eggs cook, fill a bowl with cold water and ice. Drain the hot eggs and dunk them into the ice bath for at least 5 minutes; the shock makes them far easier to peel. Peel under a trickle of running water and set the smooth eggs aside.
Open the can of beets and pour the juice into a clean pint jar or other lidded container. Add the sliced beets, thinly sliced red onion, smashed garlic, and the bay leaf if using.
Add the apple cider vinegar (1/2 cup), sugar, and salt to the jar. Stir or seal and shake until the sugar and salt fully dissolve into the brine.
Lower the peeled eggs into the jar so they are fully submerged in the magenta brine. If the liquid doesn't quite cover them, top up with a splash of water, then seal the lid.

Refrigerate at least 2-3 days before eating so the eggs absorb color and flavor. For a deep ruby ring all the way through, give them a full week, turning the jar now and then. Keep them refrigerated the entire time, never at room temperature.

To serve, lift an egg out, slice in half or into rounds, and arrange on a board. Scatter with fresh parsley if you like. Eat within 2 weeks, keep the jar cold, and make sure any remaining eggs stay submerged in the brine.
cheapTips: Buy eggs by the dozen and pickle the whole carton; the same brine works for 12 eggs as for 6, so double the batch at no extra effort.
Reuse the brine: after the eggs are gone, drop in a fresh batch of peeled hard-boiled eggs (keep refrigerated) for a second round of nearly-free snacks.
Canned beets with their juice are the cheapest path here; no need to roast fresh beets, and the can liquid is your ready-made dye.

substitutions.swap: Use 1 fresh beet, peeled, sliced, and simmered in 1 cup water until tender, then use that pink cooking water as the brine base.
substitutions.savings: Saves about $0.25 if beets are cheaper loose

substitutions.swap: Plain white or distilled vinegar works fine and is usually cheaper.
substitutions.savings: Saves a few cents per batch

substitutions.swap: Any yellow or white onion adds the same sweet-savory note to the brine.
substitutions.savings: Saves about $0.10

recipes.name: Pidan Doufu (Century Egg with Cold Silken Tofu)
recipes.description: A silky, no-cook Chinese appetizer: chilled silken tofu draped with creamy, jammy century egg and a punchy soy-sesame-scallion sauce. Cooling, savory, and deeply umami, it's a beloved classic that costs almost nothing to throw together.
steps: Chill the unopened block of silken tofu in the fridge for at least 30 minutes so it is cold and firm enough to hold its shape. This dish is served cold, so do not skip the chilling.

Make the sauce: in a small bowl stir together 2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tbsp Chinkiang black vinegar, 1 tsp toasted sesame oil, and 1/2 tbsp sugar until the sugar fully dissolves, then stir in 1 finely minced garlic clove.

Peel the century eggs: gently crack and remove the shell. The white will be a translucent amber jelly and the yolk a soft, dark, creamy center, which is normal and fully cured (no cooking needed). Rinse and pat dry.
Cut each century egg into quarters or rough chop. A thin knife rinsed in warm water slices the soft yolk cleanly without smearing.
Carefully turn the cold silken tofu out of its pack onto a shallow serving plate, draining off any liquid. Keep the block whole, or slice it into thick slabs for easier scooping.
Arrange the century egg pieces over and around the tofu so every bite gets some egg.
Spoon the soy-sesame sauce evenly over the top, letting it pool around the base of the tofu.
Scatter the sliced scallions over everything, then drizzle with chili oil and top with cilantro if using. Serve immediately while cold, scooping tofu, egg, and sauce together in each spoonful.
cheapTips: Century eggs are cheapest at Asian grocery stores, often sold 6 to a pack for a couple dollars, far less than buying singles. Buy a pack and they keep for weeks in the pantry.
One block of silken tofu easily stretches to feed 2-3 people as a snack, so this whole plate lands at well under a dollar per serving.
Skip bottled chili oil and make the cheap classic version: just soy, black vinegar, sesame oil, and scallions still tastes authentic and restaurant-good.

substitutions.swap: rice vinegar or a splash of regular black or balsamic vinegar
substitutions.savings: Use what you have; rice vinegar is milder but works fine

substitutions.swap: regular soy sauce, or tamari for a gluten-free version
substitutions.savings: No extra cost, likely already in your pantry

substitutions.swap: a pinch of red pepper flakes or a few drops of sriracha
substitutions.savings: Cheaper and probably already on hand

recipes.name: Arctic Char With Greens and Gribiche Dressing
recipes.description: Crisp-skinned arctic char laid over peppery mixed greens, all brightened by a punchy egg-and-herb gribiche dressing. A fast, elegant dinner that tastes like a restaurant plate. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/arctic-char-with-greens-and-gribiche-dressing

ingredients.note: part of 4 cups mixed greens (~1 cup)
2 tbsp finely chopped cornichons, for gribiche dressing

steps: Make the gribiche dressing: peel the hard-boiled eggs and finely chop. In a bowl whisk together the dijon and white wine vinegar, then stream in olive oil while whisking to emulsify (reserve a little oil for the fish). Stir in the chopped eggs, capers, cornichons, shallot, parsley and tarragon. Season with salt and pepper and set aside.
Season both sides of the arctic char fillets with salt and freshly ground pepper.
Swirl the olive oil in a cold large nonstick skillet to coat. Lay the fillets in skin side down, then set the pan over medium heat.

Cook the fish, occasionally pressing down very lightly on the fillets so the skin stays in even contact with the pan, until the skin is deep golden brown and the flesh is opaque around the edges, 6-8 minutes.
Turn the fillets and cook just until opaque on the flesh side, about 1 minute longer. Transfer to a platter.
Gently toss the mixed greens in a medium bowl with enough gribiche dressing to lightly coat; season with salt and pepper.
Scatter the dressed greens over the fish and spoon some additional gribiche dressing on top. Serve right away.
cheapTips: Arctic char is the splurge here; swap in salmon or trout fillets to cut the cost nearly in half without changing the method.
The gribiche is just hard-boiled eggs, mustard, vinegar, herbs and oil whisked together - far cheaper and fresher than any bottled dressing.
Use whatever peppery greens are on sale; a single bag of arugula stands in fine for the watercress/mizuna mix.

substitutions.swap: salmon or trout fillets
substitutions.savings: ~$3.50/serving

substitutions.swap: extra arugula or baby spinach
substitutions.savings: ~$0.50/serving

substitutions.swap: fresh chives or dill
substitutions.savings: minimal

recipes.name: Buckwheat Banana Cake With Yogurt-Espresso Frosting
recipes.description: A nutty, deeply banana-y loaf cake made with whole wheat and buckwheat flours, crowned with a tangy cream cheese-Greek yogurt frosting spiked with espresso. Wholesome enough for breakfast, special enough for dessert. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/buckwheat-banana-cake-with-yogurt-espresso-frosting

ingredients.note: nonstick vegetable oil spray, for pan
1/2 cup buckwheat flour (or whole wheat flour)
pinch of kosher salt, for frosting

steps: Preheat oven to 350F. Coat an 8.5x4.5-inch loaf pan with nonstick spray, then line with parchment, letting it overhang both long sides.
Whisk the whole wheat flour, buckwheat flour, cinnamon, salt, baking soda, and baking powder in a medium bowl.
In a large bowl, mash the bananas and brown sugar until virtually no banana lumps remain and the sugar dissolves.
Mix in the eggs, olive oil, and sour cream until smooth.
Add the dry ingredients and fold in with a rubber spatula just until combined. Scrape the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top.
Bake 55-65 minutes, until the top springs back when gently pressed and a tester inserted in the center comes out clean.
Transfer the pan to a wire rack and let the cake cool in the pan for 30 minutes, then turn out onto the rack and cool completely.
For the frosting, whisk the cream cheese, Greek yogurt, and a pinch of salt in a large bowl until no lumps remain.
Sift the powdered sugar into the bowl and whisk vigorously to combine, then stir in the espresso powder.
Slice the cooled cake and serve with the frosting alongside for spreading over.
cheapTips: Use overripe, heavily speckled bananas you'd otherwise toss; they're often marked down and mash sweeter.
Whole wheat flour can stand in for the buckwheat flour if you don't want to buy a separate bag.
Make the frosting from a single block of cream cheese and a small tub of yogurt; both keep for days so nothing goes to waste.

substitutions.swap: Use extra whole wheat flour (or all-purpose) in its place
substitutions.savings: skips a $0.45 specialty flour

substitutions.swap: Plain regular yogurt or sour cream, drained slightly for thickness
substitutions.savings: saves ~$0.70

substitutions.swap: Neutral vegetable or canola oil
substitutions.savings: saves ~$0.20/tbsp

recipes.name: Cherry Tomato Vinaigrette
recipes.description: A warm, jammy tomato vinaigrette where blistered cherry tomatoes burst into a glossy, tangy sauce brightened with shallot, red wine vinegar, and fresh chives. Spoon it over grilled fish, chicken, or crusty bread. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/cherry-tomato-vinaigrette
steps: Cut half of the cherry tomatoes in half, leaving the rest whole.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the shallot and cook, stirring often, until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the halved and whole tomatoes. Cook, stirring occasionally, until they begin to release their juices, 4 to 6 minutes. Mash some of the tomatoes with a spoon.
Stir in 1 tablespoon vinegar and the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, adding more vinegar to taste.
Serve warm or at room temperature, stirring in the chives just before serving.
Do ahead: The vinaigrette can be made (without chives) up to 2 days ahead. Cover and chill, then bring to room temperature and stir in chives before serving.
cheapTips: Grape tomatoes are usually cheaper and firmer than cherry tomatoes and work perfectly here.
Swap red wine vinegar for whatever vinegar you already have on hand to save a trip to the store.
Make a double batch and keep it chilled for up to 2 days; it dresses salads, grains, and proteins all week.

substitutions.swap: Any small cherry or heirloom tomato, halved
substitutions.savings: Use in-season tomatoes for the best flavor and price

substitutions.swap: Sherry vinegar or white wine vinegar
substitutions.savings: Use what you already have to avoid buying a new bottle

substitutions.swap: Thinly sliced green onion tops or fresh parsley
substitutions.savings: Often cheaper and more versatile than fresh chives

recipes.name: Daniel Boulud's Madeleines
recipes.description: Delicate, buttery little shell-shaped cakes with golden crisp edges, a tender citrus-kissed crumb, and a snowfall of powdered sugar. Serve them warm, fresh from the oven, the way a French pastry master intends. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/daniel-bouluds-madeleines

ingredients.note: 3/4 cup all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
2 teaspoons finely grated lemon or orange zest
nonstick vegetable oil spray, for pans

steps: Whisk the baking powder, salt, and flour together in a small bowl.
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs, granulated sugar, brown sugar, honey, and lemon zest until smooth.
Whisk in the dry ingredients until just incorporated, then whisk in the warm melted butter until the batter is smooth.
Transfer the batter to a pastry bag or a resealable plastic bag and chill at least 1 hour (or up to 1 day ahead).
Preheat the oven to 400 F. Lightly coat the madeleine pans with nonstick oil spray and dust with flour, tapping out the excess.
Snip the end off the pastry bag (or one corner of the resealable bag) and pipe batter into each mold, filling about two-thirds full.
Bake until the edges are golden brown and the centers are puffed and lightly spring back when gently pressed, about 5 minutes for mini and 8-10 minutes for regular madeleines.
Tap the pan against the counter to release the madeleines. Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm.
cheapTips: Skip the pastry bag and pipe from a zip-top bag with a corner snipped off, or just spoon the batter into the molds.
Use regular granulated sugar with a pinch extra molasses-y brown sugar instead of buying specialty sugars.
A standard nonstick mini muffin tin works if you don't own a madeleine pan, no need to buy one.

substitutions.swap: Orange zest for a sweeter, mellower citrus note
substitutions.savings: same cost

substitutions.swap: Browned butter for a deeper, nutty madeleine flavor
Light corn syrup or maple syrup if out of honey
substitutions.savings: similar

recipes.name: Duck Confit With Spicy Pickled Raisins
recipes.description: Meltingly tender duck legs slow-cooked in their own rendered fat until the meat falls off the bone, then roasted to crackling-crisp skin and served with sweet-tart, chile-spiked pickled golden raisins. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/duck-confit-with-spicy-pickled-raisins

ingredients.note: 1 tsp ground plus more freshly cracked
6 dried chiles de arbol, crushed, divided (or 1.5 tsp crushed red pepper flakes)

steps: Prick the duck leg skin all over with the tip of a knife or sharp fork. Rub with the sliced garlic (slices should stick to the skin) and season with 1 tsp ground black pepper and 2 Tbsp salt.

Preheat oven to 250 degrees F. Arrange the duck skin side down in a roasting pan or large Dutch oven and add 8 thyme sprigs, 4 crushed chiles (or 1 tsp red pepper flakes), and 1/2 cup water. Cover with foil or a lid and cook until the fat is rendered (expect a lot), about 2 hours.
Turn the duck skin side up and nestle it into the rendered fat. Cover and continue cooking until the meat is very tender and the bones easily wiggle, 2 to 2 1/2 hours longer.

Meanwhile, make the pickled raisins: bring the white wine vinegar, sugar, mustard seeds, rosemary sprig, remaining thyme sprig, 2 crushed chiles (or 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes), 1 tsp salt, and 1 cup water to a boil in a medium saucepan.
Reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the sugar dissolves, about 3 minutes. Stir in the golden raisins, remove from heat, and let cool at least 1 hour.

Increase oven temperature to 400 degrees F. Remove the duck from the fat and place skin side up on a rimmed baking sheet. Reserve the fat for another use (keeps 3 weeks refrigerated or 3 months frozen; reheat and strain before using).
Season the duck with cracked black pepper and roast until the skin is brown and crisp, 30 to 35 minutes.
Serve the crisp duck with the spicy pickled raisins.
cheapTips: Save every drop of the rendered duck fat - it keeps for weeks in the fridge and makes the best roast potatoes you'll ever eat, effectively giving you a second dish for free.
Swap the dried chiles de arbol for crushed red pepper flakes, which you likely already have and cost a fraction of specialty dried chiles.
Buy a whole duck and break it down yourself instead of pre-cut legs; you'll get the legs plus breast, carcass for stock, and extra fat for less per pound.

substitutions.swap: red-pepper-flakes (use 1.5 tsp total, divided)
substitutions.savings: Skip buying specialty dried chiles

substitutions.swap: apple-cider-vinegar or champagne vinegar
substitutions.savings: Use what's in the pantry

substitutions.swap: regular raisins or dried currants
substitutions.savings: About $0.05 per 1/4 cup

recipes.name: Fallen Chocolate Cake
recipes.description: A deeply rich, flourless-style chocolate cake that puffs up then collapses into a fudgy, crackly-topped masterpiece, crowned with airy mascarpone whipped cream. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/fallen-chocolate-cake

ingredients.note: 1/2 cup (1 stick), cut into 1in pieces, plus more for pan
3/4 cup plus 2 Tbsp, divided, plus more for pan
10 oz semisweet or bittersweet (61-72% cacao), coarsely chopped

steps: Preheat oven to 350F. Lightly butter a 9in springform pan and dust with sugar, tapping out any excess.
Combine the chocolate, oil, and 1/2 cup (8 Tbsp) butter in a large heatproof bowl. Set over a saucepan of simmering water and heat, stirring often, until melted. Remove the bowl from the saucepan.
Separate 4 of the eggs, placing whites and yolks in separate medium bowls. Add the cocoa powder, vanilla, salt, 1/4 cup sugar, and the 2 remaining whole eggs to the yolks; whisk until smooth.
Gradually whisk the yolk mixture into the chocolate mixture, blending well.
Using an electric mixer on high speed, beat the egg whites until frothy. With the mixer running, gradually beat in 1/2 cup sugar; beat until firm peaks form.
Gently fold the egg whites into the chocolate mixture in 2 additions, folding just until incorporated between additions.
Scrape the batter into the prepared pan, smooth the top, and sprinkle with the remaining 2 Tbsp sugar.
Bake until the top is puffed and starting to crack and the cake is pulling away from the edge of the pan, 35-45 minutes.
Transfer to a wire rack and let the cake cool completely in the pan; it will collapse in the center and crack further as it cools. (Can be made 1 day ahead, covered airtight at room temperature.)
Using an electric mixer on medium-high speed, beat the heavy cream, mascarpone, and powdered sugar until soft peaks form.
Remove the sides of the springform pan and mound the whipped cream mixture in the center of the cake before serving.
cheapTips: Buy a single bar of baking or semisweet chocolate and chop it yourself instead of pricier couverture pistoles.
Skip the mascarpone topping and whip the heavy cream alone with a little powdered sugar; the cake stands on its own.
Use store-brand butter and eggs here, since the chocolate is the star and quality differences disappear in the batter.

substitutions.swap: Cream cheese softened with a splash of cream
substitutions.savings: ~$4 cheaper than mascarpone

substitutions.swap: Dark chocolate chips, melted
substitutions.savings: Often cheaper per ounce

substitutions.swap: Melted coconut oil or any neutral oil

recipes.name: Kuku Sabzi
recipes.description: A vibrant Persian herb frittata packed with cilantro, dill, and parsley, set with eggs and a whisper of turmeric until lush and impossibly green. Traditionally served for Nowruz, it's equally good warm or at room temperature. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/kuku-sabzi

ingredients.note: 1 medium, white and pale-green parts only, finely chopped
1½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 tsp. Morton

steps: Heat 2 Tbsp. of the vegetable oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium heat. Cook the finely chopped onion and leek, stirring occasionally, until very soft but not browned, 10-12 minutes. Transfer to a plate and let cool. Wipe out the skillet and set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, salt, black pepper, baking powder, and turmeric until well combined.
Using a rubber spatula, mix in the cooled onion-leek mixture, cilantro, dill, parsley, and dried fenugreek leaves. The mixture should look thick and very green.
Preheat the broiler.
Heat the remaining 3 Tbsp. vegetable oil in the same skillet over medium heat. Pour in the egg mixture, spreading it evenly across the pan with the spatula.
Cover and cook until the bottom is just set, 8-10 minutes.
Uncover and broil, watching carefully, until the top is set, about 1 minute.
Let cool slightly, then slide the kuku sabzi onto a platter. Cut into wedges and serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Buy whole bunches of cilantro, dill, and parsley rather than packaged clamshells — you'll get far more herb per dollar for this herb-heavy dish.
Leftover kuku keeps well in the fridge for up to 4 days and is great cold in sandwiches or wraps, so treat this as built-in meal prep.
No fresh fenugreek leaves needed — the inexpensive dried fenugreek (only a tablespoon) delivers the signature flavor.

substitutions.swap: Use 2 extra scallions or a bit more onion if leeks are pricey or unavailable.
Any neutral oil like canola or sunflower works, or use olive oil for a richer flavor.
Omit if you can't find it, or add a pinch of ground fenugreek; the dish stays delicious.

recipes.name: Foolproof Roast Chicken
recipes.description: A golden, crackly-skinned whole roast chicken perfumed with caramelized lemon and garlic, finished with buttery pan juices spooned over every bite. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/no-fail-roast-chicken-with-lemon-and-garlic

ingredients.note: 1/4 cup (1/2 stick), melted; or olive oil

steps: Arrange a rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 425°F. Cut the lemon in half crosswise and remove any visible seeds.
Cut the head of garlic in half crosswise (don't worry if it falls apart a bit).
Melt the butter in a small saucepan or in the microwave.
Place the whole chicken on a cutting board and pat it completely dry with paper towels - dryness is key to good browning.

With the breast facing up and legs toward you, slice through the loose skin connecting each leg and breast, making a roughly 3-inch incision down to the leg joint. This exposes the joint so you can easily check doneness. Repeat on the other side.
Season every surface generously with salt and pepper - skin, cavity, under the wings, and the exposed leg joints. Expect about 4 teaspoons of kosher salt total.
Transfer the chicken breast side up to a large oven-safe skillet. Arrange the lemon and garlic cut sides down around the chicken.
Drizzle the chicken all over with the melted butter and transfer to the oven.
Roast until nicely browned and cooked through, checking after 45 minutes. Poke a knife into a leg joint: if the juices run clear it's done; if pink, roast and recheck every 5 minutes.
Let the chicken rest in the skillet at least 15 minutes. Transfer to a platter, pour the buttery pan juices over the top, and serve with the roasted lemon and garlic alongside.
cheapTips: A whole chicken is one of the cheapest per-pound proteins - buy on sale and freeze.
Save the carcass and pan drippings to simmer into a free batch of homemade stock.
Swap the butter for olive oil to cut cost without losing the crisp, golden skin.

substitutions.swap: Use olive oil for an equally crisp skin (dairy-free)
substitutions.savings: About the same cost

substitutions.swap: Use a Meyer lemon for a sweeter, floral note
substitutions.savings: Slightly pricier

substitutions.swap: Fine sea salt works - use about half the volume since it's denser
substitutions.savings: Roughly the same

recipes.name: No-Nut Granola
recipes.description: A crunchy, nut-free granola loaded with toasty seeds, cacao nibs, coconut, and chewy dried fruit, sweetened with pure maple syrup and a hit of flaky salt. Perfect over yogurt or by the handful. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/no-nut-granola

ingredients.note: 3 cups old-fashioned oats and/or kamut flakes
part of 1.5 cups mixed dried fruits
part of 1.5 cups mixed dried fruits (dates, figs, apricots, etc.)

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper or foil.
Toss the oats, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, cacao nibs, and coconut flakes together in a large bowl.
Add the olive oil and maple syrup and stir until everything is nicely coated. Season with 1 tsp kosher salt.
Scrape onto the prepared sheet, reserving the bowl, and spread in an even layer.
Bake, stirring and rotating the sheet front to back every 10-15 minutes, until golden brown, 25-35 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut the dried fruit into small pieces (kitchen shears work great for sticky dates and apricots) and transfer to the reserved bowl.
Let the granola cool 5 minutes, then carefully transfer it to the bowl with the dried fruit, reserving the baking sheet.
Toss well to combine, then spread back onto the sheet and let cool completely; the granola will crisp as it cools.
Taste and season with more salt if desired. Store airtight at room temperature up to 2 weeks, or freeze up to 3 months.
cheapTips: Buy oats and seeds from the bulk bin to cut the cost per batch dramatically.
Swap pricier cacao nibs and dried apricots for whatever dried fruit and chips are on sale; the ratios are forgiving.
Make a double batch and freeze up to 3 months so you only heat the oven once.

substitutions.swap: Use neutral vegetable or coconut oil for a milder flavor
substitutions.savings: Vegetable oil is cheaper at about $0.05/tbsp vs $0.27

substitutions.swap: Honey works 1:1 (note: no longer vegan)
substitutions.savings: Honey runs slightly cheaper per tbsp

substitutions.swap: Dark chocolate chips for a sweeter, less bitter crunch
substitutions.savings: Chocolate chips often cost less per ounce

recipes.name: One-Skillet Chicken With Buttery Orzo
recipes.description: Crisp-skinned chicken thighs roast atop nutty, toasted orzo simmered with sweet fennel and leek, then finished with lemon and butter for a one-pan dinner that tastes like a lot more effort than it is. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/one-skillet-chicken-with-buttery-orzo

ingredients.note: 6 skin-on, bone-in chicken thighs (about 2 pounds total), patted dry
1 leek, white and pale green parts only, chopped
1 tbsp fresh juice + 1 tsp zest (uses 1 lemon)

steps: Preheat oven to 400F. Season chicken thighs all over with salt and pepper.

Heat 2 Tbsp of the butter in a medium cast-iron skillet over medium-high. Nestle chicken skin side down in a single layer (add any pieces that don't fit once the chicken shrinks). Cook until the meat is opaque around the edges and the skin is deep golden brown, 6-8 minutes.
Turn chicken skin side up and transfer the skillet to the oven. Bake uncovered until cooked through, 10-15 minutes. Transfer chicken to a plate.
Set the same skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped fennel bulb and leek, season with salt and pepper, and cook, tossing occasionally, until the leek is golden around the edges, about 5 minutes.
Add the orzo and cook until the pasta is toasted and nutty brown in spots, about 3 minutes.
Pour in the white wine and cook, stirring, until the liquid has evaporated, about 1 minute.

Add the chicken broth 1/2 cup at a time, stirring constantly and letting each addition absorb before adding more, until the orzo is tender and the broth is mostly absorbed but the pan is not dry, 10-15 minutes.
Remove the skillet from the heat. Taste and adjust salt and pepper. Stir in the lemon juice, the remaining 1 Tbsp butter, and the chopped fennel fronds.
Pile the chicken on top of the orzo and finish with the lemon zest. Serve.
cheapTips: Buy bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs in a family pack and freeze extras; they're far cheaper per pound than boneless and the bone adds flavor to the orzo.
Skip the wine and deglaze with an extra splash of chicken broth plus a teaspoon of vinegar; you'll barely notice the difference.
Use the whole fennel bulb including the fronds and stalk so nothing goes to waste, and substitute a yellow onion for the leek if leeks are pricey.

substitutions.swap: Extra chicken broth with a splash of white-wine vinegar or lemon juice
substitutions.savings: Skips buying a bottle of wine

substitutions.swap: 1 stalk celery plus a pinch of fennel seed for that anise note
substitutions.savings: ~$2.50 vs a fresh fennel bulb

substitutions.swap: 1 yellow or white onion, chopped
substitutions.savings: ~$1.50 vs a leek

recipes.name: Parker House Rolls (Bon Appétit)
recipes.description: Soft, buttery, fold-over dinner rolls with a tender crumb and golden, flaky-salt-flecked tops that pull apart in pillowy rows. A timeless Thanksgiving classic worth the rise. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/parker-house-rolls-recipe

ingredients.note: 1½ tsp Diamond Crystal or 1 tsp Morton
3½ cups (438 g) all-purpose flour, plus more

steps: Whisk the yeast with ¼ cup warm water (110°–115°F) in a small bowl; let sit until foamy, about 5 minutes.

Heat the whole milk in a small saucepan over medium until just warm. In a large bowl, combine the shortening, sugar, and kosher salt. Pour in the warm milk, whisking constantly to blend and break the shortening into small clumps (it may not melt completely).
Whisk in the yeast mixture and the egg until combined. Add the flour and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until a dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead with floured hands until smooth, about 5 minutes.
Lightly coat a large bowl with vegetable oil; transfer the dough and turn to coat. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let sit in a warm spot until doubled in size, about 1½ hours.
Lightly brush a 13x9" baking dish with some of the melted butter. Punch down the dough and divide into 4 equal pieces.
Working one piece at a time, roll out to a 12x6" rectangle. Cut lengthwise into three 2"-wide strips, then cut each strip crosswise to make three 4x2" rectangles (9 per piece, 36 total).
Brush half of each rectangle (about 2x2") with melted butter, then fold the unbuttered side over the buttered side, leaving ¼" uncovered at the end.
Place the rolls flat side down, folded edge against a short side of the dish, side by side to form long rows until you have 4 rows.
Brush the tops with melted butter, loosely cover with plastic, and chill at least 30 minutes and up to 6 hours.
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Bake until golden and puffed, 25–35 minutes.
Brush with more melted butter and sprinkle with flaky sea salt. Let cool slightly before serving.
cheapTips: Active dry yeast is far cheaper bought in a jar than in single envelopes; one jar makes dozens of batches.
Vegetable shortening (or lard) is one of the cheapest baking fats and gives these rolls their classic soft, tender crumb.
Make the dough a day ahead and chill the shaped rolls overnight; baking fresh from the fridge means zero waste and no last-minute rush.

substitutions.swap: Use ¼ cup softened unsalted butter for a richer, all-butter roll
substitutions.savings: Often on hand; skips buying shortening

substitutions.swap: Use 2% milk or buttermilk thinned slightly
substitutions.savings: Uses what's in the fridge

substitutions.swap: Use 2¼ tsp instant yeast and skip the proofing step, adding it directly to the flour
substitutions.savings: Saves 5 minutes

recipes.name: Peanut Meringue Cookies
recipes.description: Light, crackly meringue cookies studded with crushed roasted peanuts for a salty-sweet crunch and an airy marshmallowy center. They come together with just five pantry ingredients and a stand mixer. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/peanut-meringue-cookies

ingredients.note: 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons skin-off unsalted roasted peanuts, crushed into large bits

steps: Preheat oven to 350F. Spread the peanuts on a rimmed baking sheet and crush into large bits with a mug or rolling pin; set aside.
Pour about 1 inch of water into a medium saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Combine the egg whites, powdered sugar, and salt in the bowl of a stand mixer. Set the bowl over the saucepan so it rests in the rim without touching the water.
Whisk constantly until the whites are hot to the touch (about 120F on an instant-read thermometer), about 5 minutes.
Transfer the bowl to the stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment and beat on high until soft peaks form.
Add the vanilla and keep beating until the meringue is very thick, glossy, and holds stiff peaks, about 5 minutes total.
Fold in half of the reserved peanuts with a rubber spatula, then add the rest and fold just enough to create streaks.
Immediately spoon heaping tablespoons onto a parchment-lined baking sheet into 1 1/2 inch mounds, spacing about 1 inch apart.
Place the meringues in the oven and prop the door ajar with the handle of a wooden spoon.
Bake until they puff slightly, crack along the sides, and feel dry outside but soft to the touch, 15 to 20 minutes.
Transfer to a wire rack and let cool. Store airtight at room temperature for up to 2 days.
cheapTips: Buy peanuts in bulk and crush them yourself instead of paying for pre-chopped nuts.
Save the leftover egg yolks for a custard, scramble, or pasta carbonara so nothing goes to waste.
Powdered sugar is cheap in bulk and you can make your own by blitzing granulated sugar in a blender.

substitutions.swap: Use dry-roasted peanuts or chopped almonds for a different nutty flavor
substitutions.savings: similar cost

substitutions.swap: Swap in almond extract (use half as much) for a marzipan note
substitutions.savings: comparable

substitutions.swap: Fine sea salt or table salt works; use slightly less since the grains are finer
substitutions.savings: cheaper

recipes.name: Quinoa, Fennel, and Pomegranate Salad
recipes.description: Golden cumin-spiced fennel and fluffy quinoa tossed with bright citrus and a tangle of fresh herbs, finished with jewel-like pomegranate seeds. A vibrant, refreshing grain salad that eats like a celebration. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/quinoa-fennel-and-pomegranate-salad

ingredients.note: freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps: Heat 1/4 cup of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced fennel and season with salt and pepper.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the fennel is just tender and lightly golden, 10 to 12 minutes.
Stir in the lemon juice, cumin, and sugar; cook for 1 minute. Season again with salt and pepper, then set aside.
Meanwhile, bring the quinoa and 3 cups water to a boil in a medium saucepan. Cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer until cooked, about 10 minutes.
Drain the quinoa and return it to the pan. Cover and let sit for 15 minutes, then fluff with a fork and transfer to a large bowl.
Using a small sharp knife, cut all peel and white pith from the whole lemon. Cut between the membranes to release the segments, discard the membranes, and roughly chop the segments.
Add the lemon segments with any juices and the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the quinoa; stir to combine.
Add the fennel mixture, chopped serrano, cilantro, mint, and dill. Toss gently to incorporate and season with salt and pepper.
Transfer the salad to a platter and sprinkle with pomegranate seeds before serving.
cheapTips: Buy whole fennel bulbs in season (fall/winter) when they're cheapest, and save the fronds to use in place of some of the dill.
Quinoa is much cheaper bought in bulk bins than in small boxes - cook extra and use it through the week.
Skip the pomegranate seeds if out of season; a handful of dried cranberries or fresh diced apple gives similar pops of color and sweetness for less.

substitutions.swap: jalapeño for milder heat, or a pinch of red pepper flakes
substitutions.savings: Often a few cents cheaper per pepper

substitutions.swap: couscous or bulgur (note: not gluten-free)
substitutions.savings: Roughly half the price per cup

substitutions.swap: thinly sliced celery plus a pinch of fennel seed for the anise note
substitutions.savings: About $2 per bulb

recipes.name: Red Sauce for Pizza
recipes.description: A bright, no-cook pizza sauce that lets sweet crushed tomatoes shine, sharpened with raw grated garlic and good olive oil. A short chill melds the flavors so it concentrates beautifully under a hot oven. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/red-sauce-for-pizza
steps: Finely grate the garlic cloves so they melt into the sauce rather than leaving raw chunks.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the grated garlic, crushed tomatoes, olive oil, and fine sea salt until evenly combined.
Resist adding more salt; the flavor concentrates as the sauce bakes with the pizza.
Cover the bowl and chill for at least 3 hours to let the flavors come together before using.
Spread onto pizza dough and bake. Sauce can be made up to 1 week ahead and kept chilled.
cheapTips: Buy a store-brand 28-oz can of crushed tomatoes — they are nearly identical to name brands at half the price.
Make a double batch and freeze portions in a muffin tin; it keeps for months and saves a future shopping trip.
Use the cheapest decent olive oil here since it is not cooked to a fine finish.

substitutions.swap: Whole peeled tomatoes crushed by hand, or tomato passata for a smoother sauce
substitutions.savings: Comparable cost; whole peeled often taste fresher

substitutions.swap: 1/2 tsp garlic powder if you have no fresh cloves
substitutions.savings: Pennies cheaper per batch

substitutions.swap: Kosher salt (use slightly more, by volume)
substitutions.savings: Cheaper per teaspoon

recipes.name: Red Wine–Braised Short Ribs with Carrots
recipes.description: Meltingly tender bone-in short ribs braised low and slow in a full-bodied red wine and tomato sauce, finished with sweet young carrots and a bright citrus-herb gremolata. Pure cold-weather comfort that practically falls off the bone. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/red-wine-braised-short-ribs-with-carrots

ingredients.note: 5 lb. English-style bone-in, cut between the bones (about 10)
1 lb. young carrots, unpeeled, halved if large

steps: Season the short ribs all over with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat. Working in batches, brown the ribs on all sides, 8–10 minutes per batch, then transfer to a plate. Pour off the fat from the pot.

Add the pancetta to the same pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until the fat renders and it begins to brown, 5–7 minutes. Add the onion, thyme sprigs, and carrots and cook, stirring, until the onion softens, about 5 minutes.

Pour in the red wine and tomatoes and bring to a boil. Return the short ribs to the pot, pressing down to submerge. Cover, reduce the heat, and simmer until the meat is very tender and almost falling off the bone, 3 1/2–4 hours.

Transfer the short ribs and carrots to a baking dish or platter and cover with foil to keep warm. Discard the thyme and any loose bones. Strain the cooking liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl, then return it to the pot.

Bring the strained liquid to a boil, reduce the heat to medium, and simmer until thickened and reduced by half, 15–20 minutes. Season with salt and pepper, return the short ribs to the pot, and turn to coat.
Make the gremolata: combine the parsley, chives, garlic, and orange zest in a small bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Arrange the short ribs, carrots, and sauce on a large serving platter and serve topped with the gremolata.
cheapTips: Short ribs go on sale around holidays — buy in bulk and freeze, since this dish reheats beautifully and is even better made 2 days ahead.
Skip the bottle of drinking wine; an inexpensive full-bodied red works perfectly once it's reduced into the braise.
Stretch the dish by serving over mashed potatoes, polenta, or egg noodles to soak up the rich sauce and feed more people.

substitutions.swap: Use chopped bacon instead of pancetta for a smokier, cheaper option.
Swap in bone-in beef chuck or beef shank for a more budget-friendly braise.
Replace half the wine with beef broth plus a splash of red wine vinegar if avoiding alcohol.

recipes.name: Salted-Butter Apple Galette with Maple Whipped Cream
recipes.description: A rustic free-form tart of thinly sliced apples glazed in vanilla brown butter and muscovado sugar, baked in a golden, flaky crust and served with billowy maple whipped cream. Cozy, buttery, and deceptively simple. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/salted-butter-apple-galette-with-maple-whipped-cream

ingredients.note: 1 lb baking apples (Pink Lady), sliced 1/8" thick
3 tbsp dark muscovado or dark brown sugar

steps: Place a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 375F. Put the salted butter in a small saucepan and scrape in the vanilla seeds; add the pod too. Cook over medium heat, stirring often, until the butter foams and then browns (don't let it burn), 5 to 8 minutes. Remove from heat and discard the pod.
Roll out the tart dough on a lightly floured surface into a rough 14x10" rectangle about 1/8" thick (or a 12" round). Transfer to a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Arrange the apple slices on top, overlapping, leaving a 1 1/2" border. Brush the apples with the vanilla brown butter and sprinkle with the muscovado sugar.
Fold the edges of the dough up over the apples, tucking and overlapping to keep the shape.
Beat the egg with 1 tsp water and brush the crust with the egg wash. Sprinkle the crust with the granulated sugar.
Bake, rotating once, until the apples are soft and juicy and the crust is golden brown, 40 to 50 minutes. Let cool slightly on the baking sheet before slicing.
Meanwhile, whip the heavy cream in a medium bowl to medium-soft peaks. Fold in the maple syrup.
Slice the galette and serve with the maple whipped cream alongside.
Do ahead: The galette can be baked 2 days ahead. Store tightly wrapped at room temperature and reheat slightly before serving.
cheapTips: Skip the vanilla bean and use 1 tsp vanilla extract stirred into the brown butter off the heat to save a few dollars.
Use regular dark brown sugar instead of muscovado; the flavor is nearly identical at a fraction of the cost.
A store-bought frozen pie crust works fine here and skips the dough-making step entirely.

substitutions.swap: 1 tsp vanilla extract added off the heat
dark brown sugar (3 tbsp)
substitutions.savings: minor

substitutions.swap: frozen pie crust

recipes.name: Sausage, Greens, and Beans Pasta
recipes.description: Spicy Italian sausage, crisped chickpeas, and wilted greens come together in a glossy, Parmesan-rich pasta finished with crumbled fried rosemary. A one-pot weeknight dinner that tastes like a special occasion. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/sausage-greens-and-beans-pasta

ingredients.note: 1 15.5-oz can, rinsed and patted dry (or cannellini)
12 oz paccheri, rigatoni, or other large tubular pasta
8 cups lightly packed, torn (or kale/Swiss chard)

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high. Fry the rosemary sprigs, turning, until crisp, about 2 minutes. Transfer to paper towels to drain.
Add the sausage to the same pot and cook, breaking it up with a wooden spoon and stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through, 8 to 10 minutes. Transfer with a slotted spoon to a plate.
Add the chickpeas to the pot and cook, tossing occasionally and mashing some with the spoon, until browned in spots, about 5 minutes. Transfer about half to the plate with the sausage.
Add the white wine to the pot, bring to a boil, and cook until the liquid is almost completely evaporated, about 2 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in a large pot of boiling salted water, stirring occasionally, until very al dente, about 3 minutes less than package directions. Reserve plenty of cooking liquid.

Using a spider or slotted spoon, transfer the pasta to the pot with the chickpeas. Add the escarole and 1 cup pasta cooking liquid. Cook, tossing often, until the escarole is wilted, the pasta is al dente, and the sauce is thickened, about 4 minutes.

Add another 1/4 cup pasta liquid, then gradually add 1/2 cup (8 tbsp) of the Parmesan, tossing until melted into a glossy sauce. Thin with more pasta liquid if needed. Season with pepper, and more salt if needed.
Add the butter and toss to combine, then mix in the reserved sausage and chickpeas.
Divide the pasta among bowls. Crumble the fried rosemary over the top and sprinkle with the remaining 1/4 cup (4 tbsp) Parmesan.
cheapTips: Swap escarole for kale or Swiss chard, whichever is cheapest and freshest that week — the recipe is built to take any of them.
Use a generic large tubular pasta (rigatoni or ziti) instead of pricier paccheri; the sauce clings just as well.
Canned chickpeas cost a fraction of cannellini beans and crisp up beautifully — buy the cheaper can.

substitutions.swap: Plant-based or smoked sausage works; for less heat use sweet Italian instead of spicy
substitutions.savings: smoked sausage is a bit cheaper

substitutions.swap: Cannellini (white kidney) or butter beans
substitutions.savings: chickpeas are usually the cheapest canned bean

substitutions.swap: Pecorino Romano or any hard aged grating cheese
substitutions.savings: buy a wedge and grate it yourself

recipes.name: Slow-Roasted Salmon With Fennel, Citrus, and Chiles
recipes.description: Silky, gently roasted salmon nestled over thinly shaved fennel, citrus, and Fresno chile, all bathed in fruity olive oil for a stunning yet effortless centerpiece. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/slow-roasted-salmon-with-fennel-citrus-and-chiles

ingredients.note: 1 blood or navel orange, very thinly sliced, seeds removed
1 Meyer or regular lemon, very thinly sliced, seeds removed
1 red Fresno chile or jalapeño, with seeds, thinly sliced
to season fennel mixture and salmon

steps: Preheat oven to 275°F.
In a shallow 3-quart baking dish, toss the thinly sliced fennel, orange, lemon, Fresno chile, and dill sprigs together. Season with kosher salt and coarsely ground black pepper.
Season the salmon with kosher salt and place it on top of the fennel-citrus mixture.
Pour the extra-virgin olive oil evenly over everything.
Roast until the salmon is just cooked through, 30 to 40 minutes for medium-rare. The tip of a knife should slide through easily and the flesh will be slightly opaque.
Transfer the salmon to a platter, breaking it into large pieces as you go.
Spoon the fennel mixture and oil from the baking dish over the salmon; discard the dill sprigs.
Season with flaky sea salt and pepper, and top with fresh dill sprigs before serving.
cheapTips: Swap the blood orange and Meyer lemon for a regular navel orange and lemon — the dish works just as well and costs a fraction.
Use a thinner, tail-end salmon fillet or even frozen salmon; slow-roasting is forgiving and keeps any cut moist.
Stretch the leftover citrus-fennel oil over rice or bread the next day so nothing goes to waste.

substitutions.swap: Regular navel orange
substitutions.savings: ~$0.20 each

substitutions.swap: Regular lemon
substitutions.savings: ~$0.20 each

substitutions.swap: Jalapeño
substitutions.savings: ~$0.05 each

recipes.name: White Beans with Broccoli Rabe and Lemon
recipes.description: Creamy cannellini beans simmered with garlicky greens, melty caramelized lemon, and a savory hit of anchovy and Parmesan for a saucy, comforting one-pot meal. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/white-beans-broccoli-rabe-lemon

ingredients.note: 1 small lemon, very thinly sliced, seeds removed

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium heat. Add the lemon slices, anchovies, and garlic.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the lemon is softened and brown in spots and the anchovies fall apart, about 5 minutes.
Add the broccoli rabe; season with salt and pepper and cook, tossing occasionally, until bright green and crisp-tender, about 5 minutes.

Add the beans and 1/2 cup water to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally, until flavors have melded and the liquid is reduced by half (you still want it saucy), about 5 minutes.
Mix in the parsley and 2 tablespoons Parmesan.
Transfer to a platter, sprinkle with red pepper flakes if desired, and top with more Parmesan.
cheapTips: Dried cannellini beans cooked from scratch cost a fraction of canned and freeze well in their cooking liquid.
Anchovy fillets or anchovy paste keep for months in the fridge and add big savory depth for pennies per dish.
Swap broccoli rabe for cheaper broccoli or kale when greens are pricey - the dish works with almost any sturdy green.

substitutions.swap: broccoli or broccolini, chopped
substitutions.savings: often cheaper and milder, no bitterness

substitutions.swap: white-beans or kidney-beans
substitutions.savings: about $0.25 per can

substitutions.swap: anchovy-paste (about 1 tsp)
substitutions.savings: less waste, longer shelf life

recipes.name: Whole Corn on the Grill
recipes.description: Sweet summer corn grilled right in the husk until smoky and tender, then slathered with a charred spring onion and sesame-chile butter that melts into every kernel. Simple, smoky, and irresistible. Recipe from Bon Appétit: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/whole-corn-on-the-grill

ingredients.note: for the charred spring onion and sesame-chile butter

steps: Prepare a grill for medium heat.
Grill the corn in its husk, rotating occasionally, until the husks are blackened (some leaves will flake and fall off) and the kernels are tender with browned, charred spots, 25 to 35 minutes.
Meanwhile, make the charred spring onion and sesame-chile butter: char the spring onions (scallions) on the grill until softened and blackened in spots, then finely chop.
Mash the softened butter with the charred onions, toasted sesame oil, toasted sesame seeds, chile flakes, and a pinch of salt until well combined.
Let the grilled corn cool slightly, then shuck off the charred husks and silk.
Serve the corn hot, slathered generously with the charred spring onion and sesame-chile butter.
cheapTips: Buy corn in season (summer) when ears are cheapest and sweetest, often under $0.50 each.
Skip the specialty compound butter and just use plain butter with a sprinkle of chili flakes and salt to cut cost.
Grill extra ears while the grill is hot and stash leftovers for salads or soups later in the week.

substitutions.swap: red onion or white onion, thinly sliced and charred
substitutions.savings: Roughly the same cost; uses a pantry staple
