substitutions.swap: regular sesame oil or olive oil
substitutions.savings: Saves a few cents and works with what you have

substitutions.swap: chili powder or a fresh Fresno chili, minced
substitutions.savings: Comparable cost

recipes.name: Spinach and Ricotta Tortellini with Creamy Tomato Sauce
recipes.description: Plump spinach-and-ricotta tortellini simmered straight into a silky tomato-parmesan cream sauce, all in one pan and ready in about 13 minutes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/10-min-one-pot-creamy-tomato-tortellini/

ingredients.note: 100 g freshly grated, plus extra to serve

steps: Heat the olive oil in a heavy-based pan with a lid over medium-high heat. Add the diced red onion and garlic and cook, stirring, for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes, stirring. Use the back of your spoon to gently squash them and release their juices.
Stir in the stock and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cream, grated parmesan and black pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Add the spinach and stir until just wilted.
Tip the tortellini straight into the pan from the bag (no need to precook) and stir through the sauce.
Reduce the heat to low, cover and cook for 3-4 minutes, until the pasta is just cooked through.
Top with extra parmesan and a drizzle of Italian chilli oil if using. Serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use vegetable stock or a crumbled bouillon cube instead of chicken stock to keep it meat-free and cheaper.
Buy a wedge of parmesan and grate it yourself - it's cheaper per gram than pre-grated and melts smoother.
Swap fresh grape tomatoes for half a can of crushed or fire-roasted tomatoes when fresh ones are pricey.

substitutions.swap: half-and-half or evaporated milk for a lighter sauce
substitutions.savings: ~$0.25/serving

substitutions.swap: half a can of crushed tomatoes
substitutions.savings: ~$0.20/serving

substitutions.swap: fresh ravioli or cheese tortellini of choice

recipes.name: 10 Minute Creamy Pesto Chicken Pasta
recipes.description: Silky pesto-cream sauce coats tender chicken, vegetables, and pasta for a weeknight dinner that comes together in about 13 minutes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/10-minute-creamy-pesto-chicken-pasta/

ingredients.note: 50 g freshly grated, plus extra to serve

steps: Cook the pasta as per packet instructions, less 1 minute, as it will finish cooking in the sauce. Drain and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add the sliced chicken and cook for 1-2 minutes, just until sealed (still uncooked in the centre).
Add the garlic and stir for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the pesto, cream and vegetables. Cover with a lid and cook 2-4 minutes for fresh vegetables, or 4-6 minutes for frozen, until the chicken is cooked through.
Remove from the heat and stir through the cooked pasta and parmesan, then season with salt to taste.
Serve sprinkled with extra parmesan and fresh chilli, if using.
cheapTips: Use store-bought pesto in jars on special, or blitz your own from a bunch of basil, nuts and parmesan to cut the cost per serve.
Frozen mixed vegetables are cheaper than fresh, keep for months, and go straight into the sauce with no prep.
Swap some of the heavy cream for a splash of pasta water plus cream cheese to stretch the sauce on a budget.

substitutions.swap: Boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced, for juicier meat
substitutions.savings: Often cheaper per kg than breast

substitutions.swap: Light cream or evaporated milk for a lighter sauce
substitutions.savings: ~30% cheaper per cup

substitutions.swap: Any short pasta you have such as fusilli or pasta shells

recipes.name: 5 Minute Cheesy Garlic Bread
recipes.description: Crusty bread slathered with a quick garlic-parsley butter, blanketed in molten melting cheese, and broiled until golden and bubbling in minutes. The fastest crowd-pleaser to round out any pasta night. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/5-minute-garlic-bread/

ingredients.note: 1 baguette, cut into thick 1.5 cm slices

steps: Preheat the oven grill (broiler) to high.
Melt the butter in the microwave in 10-second bursts until just softened, about 20 seconds total.
Stir the minced garlic, chopped parsley, and sea salt flakes into the melted butter.
Spread the garlic butter over one side of each bread slice.
Top each slice with grated melting cheese, if using.
Arrange the slices on a baking tray in a single layer so none overlap; use two trays if needed.
Grill (broil) for 2 to 5 minutes until golden and bubbling, watching closely as it cooks fast.
Serve immediately.
cheapTips: Skip pre-minced garlic and mince fresh cloves yourself for pennies and far better flavor.
Buy a block of mozzarella and grate it at home; it melts better and costs less than pre-shredded.
Day-old or marked-down bread works perfectly here since it gets toasted under the broiler.

substitutions.swap: salted butter (then halve the added salt)
substitutions.savings: Often cheaper and more common in the fridge

substitutions.swap: shredded cheddar or a pizza cheese blend
substitutions.savings: Use whatever melting cheese you already have on hand

substitutions.swap: 1 tsp dried parsley
substitutions.savings: Keeps longer and avoids buying a fresh bunch

recipes.name: Authentic Fettuccine Alfredo
recipes.description: Silky ribbons of fettuccine emulsified with nothing but real butter and freshly grated parmesan into a glossy, restaurant-worthy sauce — no cream required. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/authentic-fettuccine-alfredo/

ingredients.note: 250 g unsalted butter, cut into 1.5 cm cubes
Freshly cracked black pepper, to taste

steps: Optional: warm your serving bowls. Oven: heat to 80C (175F) and place bowls inside for 10-15 minutes until warm. Microwave: heat each microwave-safe bowl for 1-2 minutes on high.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the fettuccine and cook to 1 minute less than the packet instructions — it will finish cooking in the sauce.
Reserve about 250 ml (1 cup) of the starchy pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large, deep, heavy-based pan over medium-low heat. As soon as it has melted, turn off the heat.
Add the drained pasta to the melted butter and toss with tongs to coat evenly.
Gradually add the grated parmesan, tossing continuously, until the cheese melts and forms a creamy sauce with the butter.
Add the reserved pasta water 1-2 tablespoons at a time, tossing constantly, until the sauce reaches a glossy, creamy consistency (usually the full cup). Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately in the warm bowls, topped with extra parmesan and a crack of black pepper. Add roasted or chargrilled asparagus on the side if desired.
cheapTips: Skip the asparagus side to make this a true budget pantry dinner — the dish stands on its own with just pasta, butter, and parmesan.
Buy a wedge of parmesan and grate it yourself; it melts smoother and costs far less per gram than pre-grated.
Salted butter works fine if it is what you have — just go lighter on the added salt at the end.

substitutions.swap: Any long flat pasta like linguine or spaghetti
substitutions.savings: Spaghetti is often cheaper per serving

substitutions.swap: Salted butter (reduce added salt)
Grana Padano or Pecorino Romano (sharper, saltier)

recipes.name: Baked Lemon Garlic Butter Salmon
recipes.description: Tender, flaky salmon fillets bathed in a bright lemon garlic butter with honey, paprika and oregano, then roasted and broiled until caramelized. A 20-minute weeknight dinner that tastes like a restaurant entree. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/baked-lemon-garlic-butter-salmon/
steps: Preheat the oven to 220C (425F), or 200C/400F fan-forced, for at least 20 minutes.
Make the lemon garlic butter: in a bowl, whisk together the melted butter, olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, honey, paprika, oregano, salt, black pepper and chilli flakes (if using).
Place the salmon fillets skin-side down in a roasting tin. Spoon the marinade as evenly as you can over the top of each fillet.
Bake the salmon for 12 minutes.
Switch the oven to grill (broiler) on high and cook for a further 3 minutes, or until caramelized and cooked to your liking.
Serve with mashed potatoes, steamed greens or a green leafy salad, extra black pepper, fresh lemon slices and a sprinkling of chopped parsley.
cheapTips: Buy salmon fillets when on sale and freeze them; thaw overnight in the fridge before baking.
Bottled lemon juice works in the marinade and costs a fraction of fresh lemons - save the fresh lemon just for slices to serve.
Skip the parmesan-topped greens and serve with simple mashed potato to keep the cost-per-serving down.

substitutions.swap: salted butter (reduce added salt by half)
substitutions.savings: Usually cheaper and already on hand

substitutions.swap: frozen salmon fillets, thawed
substitutions.savings: ~$0.25/serving cheaper than fresh

substitutions.swap: smoked paprika for a deeper, smoky flavor
substitutions.savings: Pantry swap, no extra cost

recipes.name: Baked Miso Salmon
recipes.description: Sweet-savory miso-glazed salmon roasted until caramelized, served with steamed greens, fluffy rice, and a bright quick-pickled red onion. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/baked-miso-salmon/

ingredients.note: 2 tbsp tamari, or all-purpose soy sauce
1 tsp black and white sesame seeds
steamed bok choy or vegetables of your choice

steps: Preheat the oven to 200C (400F).
Make the pickle: combine the finely sliced red onion, 2 tbsp rice wine vinegar, and the caster sugar in a bowl. Toss and set aside to lightly pickle.

Make the marinade: in a small, shallow baking dish, mix the miso, tamari, sesame oil, brown sugar, and 2 tbsp rice wine vinegar until the sugar dissolves. It may stay slightly textured from the miso, which is fine.
Add the salmon fillets and turn a few times until fully coated in the marinade.
Bake the salmon for 12 minutes.
To caramelize, add 2-3 tablespoons of water to the base of the dish to keep the sauce from burning, then switch the oven to grill (broil) and grill for 3-5 minutes until browned and glossy.
Meanwhile, steam the bok choy and cook the rice.
Serve the salmon with the rice, steamed greens, and pickled red onion. Sprinkle with sesame seeds, spring onion, and sliced fresh chilli, if using.
cheapTips: Use frozen salmon fillets and thaw overnight in the fridge to cut the cost per serving significantly.
Swap bok choy for whatever greens are on sale (broccoli, cabbage, or green beans all work).
Miso, tamari, and sesame oil are pantry staples that last for months, so the marinade costs pennies per batch once stocked.

substitutions.swap: Regular or low-sodium soy sauce works in equal amount.
substitutions.savings: ~$0.10/batch

substitutions.swap: Frozen salmon fillets or even firm tofu for a budget/vegetarian version.
substitutions.savings: ~$1/serving

substitutions.swap: Any white or granulated sugar dissolves just fine in the pickle.
substitutions.savings: minimal

recipes.name: Stir-fried Pork and Green Beans
recipes.description: Caramelized minced pork and blistered green beans piled over quick egg fried rice, finished with steamed dumplings and a drizzle of chilli oil. A fast, savory weeknight dinner that tastes like takeout. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/beans-with-fried-rice-and-dumplings/

ingredients.note: 3 tbsp total cooking oil (2 tbsp for beans/pork, 1 tbsp for rice)
500 g frozen or fresh green beans
1 tbsp minced (~3 cloves) + 1 tsp minced (~1 clove)
2 tbsp (pork) + 1 tbsp (rice) tamari or all-purpose soy sauce
3 spring onions, finely chopped, white and green separated

steps: Heat a large, heavy-based frying pan over high heat. Add 1 tbsp oil, then immediately add the green beans.

For fresh beans: cook uncovered in a single layer 2-3 minutes until starting to soften, adding 2 tbsp water halfway to create steam. For frozen beans: cook covered 2-3 minutes, then uncover, add the water and cook a further 2-3 minutes until softened and blistered.
Remove the green beans from the pan and set aside on a plate.
Add another 1 tbsp oil to the same pan. Add the larger amount of garlic and cook, stirring, 30 seconds. Add the pork, breaking it up with a spoon, and cook until browned, about 2 minutes.
Add the Shaoxing wine, brown sugar, tamari and dark soy. Cook uncovered 4-6 minutes until the sauce starts to caramelize.
Return the green beans to the pan, stir through, then set the whole mixture aside.
Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in the pan over medium-high heat. Add the remaining garlic and the white parts of the spring onion. Cook, stirring, 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the whisked egg and cook 2 minutes until set, pushing it around and breaking it up with a spatula for even cooking.
Add the rice, green parts of the spring onion, sesame oil, tamari, salt and pepper. Cook 1-2 minutes until the rice is warmed through.
Serve the egg fried rice loaded with the pork and green beans. Top with steamed dumplings if desired and drizzle with chilli oil to serve.
cheapTips: Use leftover or day-old rice instead of cooking fresh — it fries up better and uses up what you already have.
Frozen green beans are cheaper and last longer than fresh, and work perfectly here.
Skip the optional dumplings and chilli oil to keep the cost down — the pork, beans and fried rice are a full meal on their own.

substitutions.swap: Dry sherry or a splash of rice vinegar
substitutions.savings: Use a pantry staple instead of buying a specialty wine

substitutions.swap: Regular or low-sodium soy sauce
substitutions.savings: ~$0.10 per tbsp

substitutions.swap: Ground chicken or turkey
substitutions.savings: Often cheaper and leaner

recipes.name: Beef Burrito Bowl
recipes.description: Smoky spiced ground beef simmered with tomato paste, piled over fluffy rice and loaded with all your favorite Mexican toppings. A 15-minute weeknight dinner that's endlessly customizable. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/beef-burrito-bowl/
steps: Combine the sweet paprika, cumin, onion powder, dried oregano and sea salt flakes in a small bowl.
Heat a large, heavy-based frying pan over high heat. Add the olive oil and diced onion and cook, stirring, for 1-2 minutes.
Add the ground beef and cook for 3-4 minutes, breaking it up as you go, until browned.
Stir in the spice mix, tomato paste and 1/3 cup (80 ml) water. Cook, stirring, for 2-3 minutes until thickened and fragrant.
Spoon the spiced beef over cooked rice in bowls and finish with your favorite Mexican toppings such as cheese, jalapeños, red cabbage, black beans, corn, lime wedges, sour cream and avocado.
cheapTips: Buy ground beef in a larger family pack and freeze in 500g portions to lock in the lower per-pound price.
Skip the pre-mixed taco seasoning packets — the pantry spices here cost pennies and make a bigger, fresher batch.
Use dried beans cooked in bulk or the cheapest canned beans, and stretch the bowl with extra rice to feed more for less.

substitutions.swap: Ground turkey or chicken for a leaner, cheaper bowl
substitutions.savings: ~$0.40/serving

substitutions.swap: Frozen cauliflower rice for a low-carb base
Smoked paprika for a deeper, smokier flavor

recipes.name: Bruschetta Salad
recipes.description: Juicy ripe tomatoes, red onion and fresh basil in a balsamic-olive oil dressing, topped with warm garlic-parmesan sourdough croutons for the perfect crunch. All the flavor of classic bruschetta in a fresh, shareable salad. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/bruschetta-salad/

ingredients.note: 25g fresh basil leaves, shredded, plus extra to serve
1/2 tsp for salad + 1/2 tsp for croutons
4 slices crusty sourdough, torn into chunks

recipes.name: Creamy Lemon Pepper Chicken
recipes.description: Golden pan-seared chicken steaks bathed in a silky lemon-pepper cream sauce with parmesan, dijon, and garlic — bright, peppery, and rich in 20 minutes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/creamy-lemon-pepper-chicken/

ingredients.note: 2 breasts, cut in half horizontally to make 4 steaks
1/2 tsp sea salt flakes, plus more to taste
1 tsp for chicken + 1 tsp for sauce, plus extra to serve
1 tbsp for searing + 1 tbsp for the sauce
1 lemon, juiced and zested; extra slices to serve
rice or mashed potatoes, to serve

steps: Season the chicken steaks all over with the salt, 1 tsp black pepper and the sweet paprika.
Spread the flour on a plate and press each chicken steak in to coat all sides evenly.
Heat the olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large, deep, heavy pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook 5-6 minutes, turning once, until just cooked through. Set aside on a plate.
Deglaze the pan with the water (or wipe it clean). Add the remaining 1 tbsp butter and the garlic and cook, stirring, 30-60 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken stock and cook 1-2 minutes until reduced by half.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Add the cream, dijon, lemon juice and zest, and 1 tsp black pepper. Simmer 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in the parmesan and season with salt to taste. Return the chicken and any resting juices to the pan and simmer 2-3 minutes until heated through.
Serve over rice or mashed potatoes with steamed green beans, lemon slices, an extra crack of pepper, and parsley if using.
cheapTips: Swap the chicken breasts for thighs — they cost less per serving and stay juicier in the cream sauce.
Use bottled lemon juice and skip fresh zest to save a bit; one fresh lemon still gives the brightest flavor for pennies.
Serve over plain rice instead of mashed potatoes — it stretches the rich sauce across four servings for almost nothing.

substitutions.savings: ~$0.20/serving and harder to overcook

substitutions.swap: double-cream or light-cream for a lighter sauce
substitutions.savings: light-cream trims richness; double-cream is more decadent

recipes.name: Creamy Lemon Tortellini
recipes.description: Pillowy spinach-and-ricotta tortellini simmered right in a bright, lemony parmesan cream sauce with tender zucchini and wilted spinach. A glorious one-pan dinner that's ready in 15 minutes flat. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/creamy-lemon-tortellini/

ingredients.note: 1/2 tsp sea salt flakes, or to taste
1/2 tsp freshly cracked, or to taste
100 g freshly grated, plus extra to serve

steps: Heat the butter in a large, deep, heavy-based pan over medium-high heat. Add the garlic and cook, stirring, for 30 seconds.
Add the sliced zucchini and cook for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Stir through the lemon juice, then the stock, cream, salt and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the fresh tortellini (no need to pre-cook) and stir to coat, gently submerging them as much as possible with the back of your spoon.
Reduce the heat to medium-low so the sauce is very gently simmering. Cover and cook for 3-5 minutes until the pasta is cooked through, stirring once halfway.
Stir through the baby spinach and parmesan. Once the spinach has wilted, turn off the heat.
Sprinkle with extra parmesan and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy a block of parmesan and grate it yourself; it's cheaper than pre-grated and melts more smoothly.
Swap the cream for half-and-half plus a splash of milk if you want to cut cost, or use veggie broth (same price) to keep it vegetarian.
A whole lemon gives you both juice and free zest; grate the peel before juicing and add a pinch for extra brightness at no cost.

substitutions.swap: Any fresh filled pasta like ravioli or cheese tortelloni works the same way
substitutions.savings: Store-brand fresh pasta is often cheaper

substitutions.swap: Use light cream or half-and-half for a lighter, cheaper sauce
substitutions.savings: ~$0.50/serving

recipes.name: Creamy Mushroom and Bacon Fettuccine
recipes.description: Silky fettuccine tangled in a rich parmesan-cream sauce loaded with golden mushrooms and crispy bacon — a 20-minute weeknight comfort bowl. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/creamy-mushroom-bacon-fettuccine/

ingredients.note: 2 sprigs, plus extra leaves to garnish
50 g freshly grated, plus extra to serve

steps: Cook the fettuccine as per packet directions, less 1-2 minutes so it stays al dente.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add the bacon and cook, stirring, for 2-3 minutes until starting to brown.
Add the red onion and cook 1-2 minutes, then add the mushrooms and cook 4-5 minutes until browned and golden.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook, stirring, for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken stock, scraping up any sticky bits from the base, and cook 1-2 minutes until most of the liquid has absorbed.
Add the cream and parmesan, bring to a simmer and cook 2-3 minutes until thickened. Season with salt to taste.
Drain the pasta and rinse with cold water to stop it cooking and prevent sticking.
Discard the thyme sprigs, then add the pasta to the sauce and toss with tongs for 1 minute until just warmed through.
Serve topped with extra parmesan, cracked black pepper and fresh thyme leaves.
cheapTips: Buy a whole block of parmesan and grate it yourself — it's cheaper per gram than pre-grated and melts smoother.
Plain white button mushrooms are the most budget-friendly option here and brown just as well as Swiss browns.
Swap heavy cream for a cheaper cooking cream or thin slightly with reserved pasta water to stretch the sauce.

substitutions.swap: turkey bacon or plant-based bacon for a lighter or meat-free version

recipes.name: Creamy Oatmeal
recipes.description: A warm, velvety bowl of oats simmered in milk and dressed with banana, fresh strawberries, crunchy walnuts, coconut flakes, and a drizzle of maple syrup. Ready in five minutes for a cozy, wholesome breakfast. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/creamy-oatmeal/

ingredients.note: 1/4 tsp in oats plus 1/4 tsp to serve

steps: Combine the oats, milk, chia seeds (if using), and 1/4 tsp cinnamon in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Cook, stirring continually, for 2-3 minutes or until it reaches your desired consistency. The oats will continue to thicken as they cool.
Spoon into a bowl and stir in a splash of the reserved milk to loosen.
Top with sliced banana, strawberries, walnuts, and coconut flakes.
Drizzle with maple syrup, dust with the remaining 1/4 tsp cinnamon, and serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy oats in a large bag rather than single-serve packets for a fraction of the cost per bowl.
Swap fresh strawberries for frozen ones (thawed) to save money out of season.
Use whatever nuts you have on hand instead of walnuts; any leftover nuts work for the crunch.

substitutions.swap: Use oat-milk or almond-milk for a dairy-free bowl
substitutions.savings: Comparable cost; makes it vegan

substitutions.swap: Drizzle with honey or a sprinkle of coconut sugar

recipes.name: Creamy Pesto Chicken Breast
recipes.description: Golden pan-seared chicken steaks bathed in a rich, basil-forward cream sauce studded with sweet semi-dried tomatoes, wilted spinach, and plenty of parmesan. A 20-minute weeknight dinner that tastes like it took far longer. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/creamy-pesto-chicken-breast/

ingredients.note: 900g boneless skinless, halved horizontally into thin steaks
100g freshly grated, plus extra to serve

steps: Season the chicken steaks all over with the sea salt flakes.
Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook for 3-4 minutes per side until golden. Transfer to a plate and set aside.
Deglaze the pan with about 60ml (1/4 cup) water, scraping up the crispy browned bits from the bottom with a wooden spoon.
Add the chopped garlic to the same pan and cook for 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant.
Stir in the semi-dried tomatoes, spinach, and cream. Bring to a gentle simmer, about 1-2 minutes, until the spinach wilts.
Stir through the pesto and grated parmesan until smooth, then return the chicken and any resting juices to the pan.
Simmer on low for 3-5 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Top with extra parmesan and serve.
cheapTips: Buy whole chicken breasts and butterfly them yourself instead of pre-cut cutlets to save per pound.
Make your own pesto from a bunch of basil, garlic, and oil when basil is cheap in season - it costs a fraction of store-bought jars.
A wedge of parmesan grated at home goes much further than pre-grated tubs and keeps for weeks.

substitutions.swap: Use half-and-half or evaporated milk plus a teaspoon of cornstarch for a lighter sauce
Roasted red peppers from a jar, or fresh halved cherry tomatoes
Frozen spinach (thawed and squeezed dry) or chopped kale

recipes.name: Creamy Pesto Chicken with Zoodles
recipes.description: Golden pan-seared chicken steaks over silky pesto cream sauce, burst cherry tomatoes, and tender zucchini noodles for a fresh, low-carb dinner ready in 20 minutes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/creamy-pesto-chicken-with-zoodles/

ingredients.note: 2 breasts, each cut in half horizontally into thinner steaks
1/2 tsp sea salt flakes, plus extra to serve
1/4 tsp freshly cracked, plus extra to serve
4 large, spiralized into zoodles or thinly sliced
25 g grated, plus extra to garnish

steps: Place the chicken steaks on a board. In a small bowl, combine the sea salt, black pepper, garlic powder and sweet paprika.
Sprinkle the spice mix evenly over both sides of the chicken, smoothing it in with your hands.
Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat.
Cook the chicken for 3-4 minutes on each side, until golden and cooked through, then set aside on a plate.
Add the minced garlic to the same pan and cook, stirring, for 30 seconds.
Add the cherry tomatoes and cook, stirring, for 1-2 minutes, pressing them with the back of a spoon to release their juices.
Pour in the cream and simmer for 1-2 minutes until slightly thickened.
Remove the pan from the heat. Stir in the zoodles, pesto and parmesan for 1-2 minutes until the zoodles slightly soften. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Top with the cooked chicken. Garnish with basil leaves and extra parmesan, dollop with extra pesto if desired, and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy whole chicken breasts and butterfly them yourself instead of pre-cut steaks to save per pound.
Make your own pesto from a bunch of basil, garlic and a handful of nuts when basil is in season — far cheaper than jarred.
Swap half the heavy cream for milk thickened with a little cornstarch to stretch the sauce without losing creaminess.

substitutions.swap: Boneless skinless chicken thighs for juicier, cheaper meat
substitutions.savings: ~30% cheaper per serving

recipes.name: Creamy Pesto Pasta Salad
recipes.description: A fresh, no-cook pasta salad tossed with peppery rocket, juicy tomatoes, and tender shredded chicken, all coated in a creamy pesto-yogurt dressing. Ready in 10 minutes and loaded with feta and toasted pine nuts. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/creamy-pesto-pasta-salad/
steps: In a large bowl, combine the rocket (or baby spinach), cooked pasta, halved tomatoes, shredded chicken, crumbled feta, basil leaves, toasted pine nuts, and grated parmesan.
In a small bowl, whisk together the pesto, Greek yoghurt, and water until smooth and pourable.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat everything evenly.
Taste, adjust seasoning, and serve straight away.

Swap pine nuts for toasted sunflower seeds or skip them entirely to cut cost.
Buy a block of parmesan and grate it yourself; it is cheaper than pre-grated and lasts longer.

recipes.name: Creamy Rose Pasta with Pork Sausage
recipes.description: Golden pork-and-fennel sausage simmered into a velvety rose sauce of crushed tomatoes and cream, tossed through rigatoni with wilted spinach and parmesan. A 20-minute weeknight pasta that tastes like comfort. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/creamy-rose-pasta-with-pork-sausage/

ingredients.note: 500g pork and fennel sausages, meat squeezed from casings
100g freshly grated, plus extra to serve

steps: Cook the rigatoni in salted water as per packet directions minus 1 minute. Reserve about 1/2 cup of the pasta cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the sausage meat and cook, breaking it up and turning, for 3-4 minutes until golden.
Add the grated garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 30 seconds, then add the crushed tomatoes, cream, baby spinach, salt and pepper.
Simmer for 5-6 minutes until the sauce begins to thicken and the spinach wilts.
Stir in the parmesan, then add the drained pasta and toss to coat, loosening with a splash of the reserved pasta water if needed.
Serve topped with extra parmesan and torn basil leaves.
cheapTips: Buy plain pork sausages and add 1/2 tsp fennel seeds yourself instead of paying for pork-and-fennel sausages.
Use any short tube pasta on sale (penne, ziti, rigatoni) instead of a specific shape.
Swap fresh baby spinach for frozen spinach, which is far cheaper and keeps for months.

recipes.name: Creamy Sausage Pasta
recipes.description: Browned Italian sausage simmered into a silky parmesan cream sauce with white wine and herbs, tossed through tender pasta for a 20-minute weeknight winner. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/creamy-sausage-pasta/

ingredients.note: 250g fresh lasagne sheets, torn into 1-inch strips (or pasta of choice)
125ml dry white wine (or more chicken stock)
50g freshly grated, plus extra to serve

steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil for the pasta.

If using fresh lasagne sheets, cut or tear them into strips roughly 1 inch thick and cook them only after the sauce is ready (30-60 seconds), then drain and add straight to the sauce. If using regular pasta, cook to 1 minute less than the packet instructions and drain well.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the sausage and cook, breaking it into small pieces, for about 5 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 1-2 minutes to caramelise and deepen its flavour.
Pour in the white wine (or extra stock) and simmer 2-3 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Once most of the wine has evaporated, add the chicken stock and cook 2-3 minutes until reduced by half.
Stir in the Italian herbs and chilli flakes, if using.
Add the cream, stir well, and simmer 3-4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in the grated parmesan and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Turn off the heat, add the cooked pasta and toss to coat in the sauce.
Garnish with fresh basil and serve immediately with extra parmesan.
cheapTips: Swap the Italian sausage for plain ground pork seasoned with fennel, garlic and Italian herbs to cut the cost per serving.
Skip the white wine and use extra chicken stock plus a splash of white wine vinegar for the same bright deglaze at a fraction of the price.
Buy a wedge of parmesan and grate it yourself rather than pre-grated tubs for more cheese per dollar.

substitutions.swap: Use extra chicken stock with a small splash of white wine vinegar
Seasoned ground pork or plant-based sausage
Double cream or evaporated milk thickened with a little cornstarch

recipes.name: Creamy Tomato Sausage Pasta
recipes.description: Golden sausage meatballs simmered into a rich, velvety tomato-cream sauce with pasta that cooks right in the pan for a one-pot weeknight winner. Finished with parmesan and fresh basil for a restaurant-worthy bowl in 20 minutes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/creamy-tomato-sausage-pasta/

ingredients.note: 600g good-quality pork or beef sausages, meat squeezed from casings
300g short pasta such as rigatoni, macaroni or penne
25g freshly grated, plus extra to serve
1/4 bunch fresh basil leaves, to serve

steps: Squeeze the sausage meat from the casings and roll it into small balls.
Heat the olive oil in a large, deep, heavy-based pan over medium-high heat. Cook the sausage meatballs for 2-3 minutes until golden brown on all sides.
Stir in the minced garlic, then immediately add the passata and beef stock.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then stir in the pasta, cream, salt and pepper.
Reduce the heat to keep it bubbling gently (it must keep bubbling or the pasta won't cook).
Cover with a lid and cook for 10-12 minutes until the pasta is just cooked, stirring regularly so the sauce doesn't stick to the bottom.
Turn off the heat and leave to rest, covered, for 3 minutes so the extra sauce absorbs into the pasta.
Sprinkle with parmesan and fresh basil, if using, and serve with extra parmesan.
cheapTips: Buy plain pork sausages on special and freeze extras — squeezing the meat from cheap sausages works just as well as premium ones here.
Use store-brand passata and beef stock cubes dissolved in water instead of liquid stock to cut costs without losing flavor.
Grate a block of parmesan yourself rather than buying pre-grated — it's cheaper per gram and melts more smoothly into the sauce.

substitutions.swap: Plant-based sausage or browned ground beef for a different protein
substitutions.savings: Ground beef can be cheaper per serving

substitutions.swap: A can of crushed tomatoes blended smooth
substitutions.savings: Often cheaper than bottled passata

substitutions.savings: Light cream is lower cost and lighter

recipes.name: Crispy Chicken Caesar Sandwich
recipes.description: Golden garlic-parmesan rolls piled with crispy chicken schnitzel and a creamy, anchovy-spiked caesar slaw for the ultimate handheld lunch. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/crispy-chicken-caesar-sandwich/

ingredients.note: 4 small rolls (mini sub, baguette, sourdough or pane di casa)
1 tsp total freshly minced (1/2 tsp for butter, 1/2 tsp for dressing)
1 tsp total sea salt flakes (split between butter and dressing)

steps: Preheat the oven grill (broiler) to high. Cut each roll in half lengthways and arrange cut-side up on a baking tray.
Combine the softened butter with half the garlic, the parsley and half the salt.
Spread the garlic butter over both cut sides of the rolls and sprinkle with half the parmesan.
Grill (broil) for 2-3 minutes, until crispy and golden.
Meanwhile, make the dressing: whisk the mayonnaise, remaining garlic, anchovies (if using), lemon juice, dijon, Worcestershire, remaining salt and the pepper in a large bowl.
Add the shredded cos lettuce and toss with tongs to coat generously in the dressing.
Pile the toasted rolls with the chicken schnitzels and the caesar salad.
Finish with a generous sprinkle of the remaining parmesan and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use rotisserie chicken sliced thin instead of cooked schnitzels to skip frying and cut cost.
Skip the anchovies and lean on Worcestershire for the savory caesar depth at no extra spend.
Make the garlic butter and dressing from pantry staples you likely already have to keep the grocery run small.

substitutions.swap: 1 tsp anchovy paste, or simply omit
sourdough slices or brioche buns

recipes.name: Crispy Chicken Schnitzel Alfredo
recipes.description: Golden, crunchy chicken schnitzel sliced over silky parmesan Alfredo fettuccine — a 20-minute comfort-food mashup that feels like a restaurant treat. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/crispy-chicken-schnitzel-alfredo/

ingredients.note: 100 g freshly grated parmesan, plus extra to serve
freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley or basil, to garnish

steps: Cook the fettuccine in a large pot of salted boiling water for 1-2 minutes less than the packet says. Reserve about 1/2 cup (125 ml) of the pasta cooking water, then drain.
While the pasta cooks, reheat leftover schnitzels (or cook fresh ones) in the oven or air fryer at 350F (180C) until hot and crispy. Slice into strips.
Melt the butter in a large, deep, heavy-based pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the cream and bring to a gentle simmer. Stir in the parmesan, chicken stock powder, and black pepper, then let it bubble for 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the drained pasta to the sauce and toss with tongs to coat. Splash in reserved pasta water as needed to loosen the sauce so it stays glossy and coats the fettuccine.
Divide the pasta among four bowls, top with the sliced crispy schnitzel, and finish with extra parmesan and parsley or basil, if desired.
cheapTips: Use store-bought or leftover schnitzels to skip breading and frying from scratch.
Buy a wedge of parmesan and grate it yourself — it's cheaper per ounce and melts better than pre-shredded.
Swap the chicken bouillon for a crushed stock cube you already have; a pinch goes a long way.

substitutions.swap: Use rotisserie chicken or crispy chicken tenders instead of schnitzel
substitutions.savings: Saves time and a few dollars per serving

recipes.name: Crispy Garlic Parmesan Croutons
recipes.description: Golden, crunchy chunks of sourdough tossed in garlicky butter and olive oil, then showered with parmesan while still hot. They turn any salad or bowl of soup into something special. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/crispy-garlic-parmesan-croutons/

ingredients.note: 4 slices crusty bread, torn into chunks

steps: Preheat the oven to 200C (400F), or 180C/350F fan-forced.
In a large bowl, combine the melted butter, olive oil, minced garlic and sea salt flakes.
Add the torn bread chunks and toss well until evenly coated.
Spread the bread in a single layer on a parchment-lined baking tray.
Bake for 10-15 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Sprinkle the grated parmesan over the croutons while still hot, then set aside to cool.
Air fryer method: preheat the air fryer to 180C (350F) and toss the bread with butter, oil, garlic and salt as above.
Air fry for 6-8 minutes, shaking the basket halfway, until golden and crisp (work in batches if needed).
Sprinkle with parmesan while hot and set aside to cool before serving.
cheapTips: Use up stale or day-old bread heels instead of buying fresh loaf - croutons are the perfect way to rescue them.
Swap fresh garlic for a pinch of garlic powder to save money and skip the mincing.
Buy a block of parmesan and grate it yourself; it is cheaper per ounce than pre-grated tubs.

substitutions.swap: Any crusty bread, baguette, or even regular sliced bread works.
substitutions.savings: Plain sliced bread is about half the price of sourdough

substitutions.swap: Use all olive oil (4 tbsp total) to make them dairy-free aside from the cheese.

recipes.name: Crispy Honey Soy Chicken
recipes.description: Golden, crunchy bite-sized chicken tossed in a glossy honey-soy glaze and served over steamed rice with scallions and sesame. A faster, lighter take on takeout that comes together in 20 minutes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/crispy-honey-soy-chicken/
steps: Make the sauce: in a small bowl, whisk together the cornstarch, water, honey, tamari, rice vinegar, garlic and ginger. Set aside.

Prep the chicken: place the chicken pieces in a large bowl. Add the cornstarch, salt, pepper and whisked egg, then mix with a spoon until the coating is thick and sticky and the chicken is evenly coated.
Pan method: heat the oil in a large heavy-based frying pan over medium heat. Cook the chicken in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden, then drain on paper towel. (Air fryer alternative below.)

Air fryer method: preheat the basket to 200C (400F) and spray with oil. Arrange the coated chicken in a single layer, spray generously, and cook 8-10 minutes, shaking halfway, until crispy and golden.
Wipe the pan clean, reduce heat to low and pour in the sauce. Cook, stirring, for about 2 minutes until slightly thickened and caramelised.
Return the chicken to the pan and toss for 1-2 minutes until evenly coated and glossy.
Divide the steamed rice among four bowls, top with the chicken and sauce, and garnish with sliced scallion and sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
cheapTips: Swap chicken breast for chicken thighs, which are usually cheaper and stay juicier when fried.
Cornstarch is a pantry staple that gives the same crunch as pricier coating mixes for pennies.
Make a double batch of the honey-soy sauce and freeze half for a quick weeknight stir-fry later.

substitutions.swap: chicken thighs for a juicier, cheaper cut
substitutions.savings: ~$0.20/serving

substitutions.swap: regular or light soy sauce
apple cider vinegar or white wine vinegar

recipes.name: Crispy Sesame Chicken and Fried Rice
recipes.description: Golden, crunchy chicken thighs tossed in a glossy sweet-sticky sesame sauce, piled over quick buttery egg fried rice for a takeout-beating weeknight dinner. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/crispy-sesame-chicken-and-fried-rice/

ingredients.note: 60ml tamari or all-purpose soy sauce (for rice)
500g boneless skinless chicken thighs, diced (breast works too)
60ml tamari or all-purpose soy sauce (for sauce)
1 spring onion, finely sliced, to garnish

steps: Make the fried rice: Heat the butter in a large heavy-based pan over high heat. Add the frozen vegetables and the whisked eggs, and cook 1-2 minutes, moving and breaking up the eggs with a spatula until set.
Add the cooked rice and 60ml tamari or soy sauce. Stir to combine and cook for 2 minutes, then set aside.
Coat the chicken: In a large bowl, combine the egg, garlic powder, sweet paprika, salt, pepper and 60g cornflour. Add the diced chicken and toss until a thick paste coats every piece.

Pan-fry: Heat the frying oil in a deep saucepan over medium heat. Fry the chicken 3-4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. (Or air-fry at 200C/400F for 10-12 minutes, oiling generously and shaking halfway.)
Drain the chicken on paper towel.
Make the sauce: In a small bowl, combine the olive oil, minced garlic, 60ml tamari or soy sauce, brown sugar and sesame oil.
Heat a frying pan over medium-low and add the sauce. Simmer 2-3 minutes until thickened.
Make a slurry by mixing the 1 tbsp cornflour with 60ml water.
Stir the slurry into the sauce, raise the heat to medium-high and simmer 2-3 minutes until glossy and honey-like. Thin with a splash of water if too thick.
Remove from the heat, return the chicken to the pan and toss to coat evenly in the sauce.
Serve the fried rice topped with the sesame chicken, sprinkled with sesame seeds and sliced spring onion.
cheapTips: Chicken thighs are cheaper than breast and stay juicier under the crispy coating, so buy thighs and dice them yourself.
Use day-old leftover rice instead of cooking fresh; it fries up drier and crispier and uses up what you already have.
Air-frying with an oil spray uses a fraction of the deep-frying oil, saving money and cleanup while keeping it crispy.

substitutions.swap: Use chicken breast for a leaner, slightly cheaper option
substitutions.savings: ~$0.20/serving

substitutions.swap: Regular soy sauce works identically

recipes.name: Crispy Sticky Tofu Bowls
recipes.description: Golden, cornflour-crusted tofu tossed in a glossy garlic-tamari glaze, piled over fluffy jasmine rice with a bright, tangy cucumber salad. A fast, crave-worthy weeknight bowl that hits sweet, savory, and crunchy in every bite. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/crispy-sticky-tofu-bowls/

ingredients.note: 2 tbsp total (1 tbsp salad + 1 tbsp sauce), as 6 tsp
500 g firm tofu, drained, cut into 2 cm cubes
30 g to coat (~4 tbsp) + 1 tbsp for slurry
60 ml tamari or all-purpose soy sauce
steamed jasmine rice, ~1 cup dry per serving
1 spring onion, finely sliced, to garnish

steps: Make the cucumber salad: combine the chopped cucumbers, minced ginger, rice vinegar, 1 tbsp soy sauce, and 1 tbsp (3 tsp) sesame oil in a medium bowl. Set aside.
Cook the jasmine rice according to package directions and keep warm.
Cut the tofu into small ~2 cm squares, then dust each piece all over in cornflour (cornstarch).
Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu for 6-8 minutes, turning every 1-2 minutes, until golden brown on all sides. Set aside on a plate.
Reduce the heat to low. Add the garlic, tamari, brown sugar, and remaining 1 tbsp (3 tsp) sesame oil. Cook, stirring, for about 1 minute until slightly thickened.
Combine the remaining 1 tbsp cornflour with the water in a small bowl. Add to the pan 1 tablespoon at a time, stirring, to thicken the sauce to your desired consistency.
Return the tofu to the pan and toss to coat in the sticky sauce. If it gets too thick, loosen with 1 tablespoon of water at a time.
Divide the rice and cucumber salad among four bowls. Top with the tofu and sprinkle with sesame seeds and spring onion.
cheapTips: Tofu is one of the cheapest proteins out there - buy the larger block and press it well for a better crispy crust.
Cornflour and a hot pan deliver fried-food crunch for a fraction of the cost (and oil) of deep frying.
Jasmine rice cooked at home costs pennies per bowl versus takeout - make a big batch and reheat leftovers.

substitutions.swap: Regular or low-sodium soy sauce works 1:1 if you don't need it gluten-free.
Any neutral high-heat oil (vegetable, canola, rice bran) for frying.
Brown rice or any steamed rice you have on hand.
substitutions.savings: varies

recipes.name: Crispy Sweet Chilli Chicken
recipes.description: Golden, crunchy bites of chicken tossed in a glossy, sticky-sweet chilli sauce with a hint of garlic and ginger, served over fluffy steamed rice. Faster and tastier than takeout, and ready in just 20 minutes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/crispy-sweet-chilli-chicken/

ingredients.note: 600g boneless skinless chicken breast or thigh, cut into bite-sized pieces
60ml rice wine vinegar, apple cider vinegar or lime juice

steps: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and place in a large bowl with the sweet paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper, egg and cornflour. Mix well until the coating forms a paste around the chicken. Set aside.
Make the sauce: in a medium bowl, combine the minced garlic, minced ginger, sweet chilli sauce, tamari (or soy sauce) and rice wine vinegar. Set aside.
Heat the oil over medium-high heat in a large, deep, heavy-based frying pan.
Cook the chicken for 5-6 minutes until cooked through and golden all over, turning once halfway. Set aside on paper towel to drain.
Drain the oil from the pan and wipe it clean.
Return the pan to medium-low heat and add the sauce. Stir for 2-3 minutes until it begins to bubble gently and thicken.
Turn off the heat and return the chicken to the pan, stirring so each piece is evenly coated in the glossy sauce.
Serve immediately, heaped over steamed rice and topped with sliced spring onion and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

Air fryer option: coat the chicken in egg, spices and seasoning (no cornflour yet), then dip each piece individually in cornflour to coat. Spray the basket and chicken generously with oil and air fry at 200C/400F for 6-8 minutes, shaking halfway, then toss through the warm sauce.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs instead of breast - they are cheaper, stay juicier, and crisp up just as well.
Skip the deep-fry oil and use the air fryer method with a quick oil spray to cut cost and cleanup.
Buy a large bottle of sweet chilli sauce and tamari - they last for months and power dozens of stir-fries.

substitutions.swap: Regular or low-sodium soy sauce works one-for-one.
Apple cider vinegar or fresh lime juice.
substitutions.savings: about even

substitutions.swap: Potato starch or tapioca starch for an equally crisp coating.
substitutions.savings: about even

recipes.name: Curried Egg Sandwiches
recipes.description: Jammy grated eggs folded with creamy mayo, warming curry powder, and fresh scallion, piled onto toasted sourdough with peppery rocket. A quick, comforting lunch that tastes far fancier than the 13 minutes it takes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/curried-egg-sandwiches/

ingredients.note: rocket or baby spinach, to serve

steps: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, then plunge into cold water to stop the cooking.
Peel the cooled eggs and coarsely grate them into a small bowl.
Add the onion powder, curry powder, sliced spring onion, mayonnaise, and a pinch of salt and freshly cracked black pepper.
Mix until creamy and well combined; taste and adjust seasoning.
Toast the sourdough roll until golden.
Pile the curried egg onto the toasted sourdough, top with rocket or baby spinach leaves, and serve.
cheapTips: Buy eggs by the dozen and boil a few extra to keep peeled in the fridge for fast sandwiches all week.
Plain mayonnaise works just as well as whole-egg mayo and is usually cheaper.
Skip the bagged rocket and use any leftover salad greens, or leave it off entirely to save money.

substitutions.swap: Any bread, hoagie roll, or kaiser roll you have on hand
substitutions.savings: Use sandwich bread at ~$0.18/slice instead of a roll

substitutions.swap: Baby spinach or any leafy greens
substitutions.savings: Use loose spinach instead of a bagged green

substitutions.swap: Kewpie mayo or plain Greek yogurt for a tangier, lighter mix

recipes.name: Drunken Noodles (Simple Home Edit)
recipes.description: Wide rice noodles tossed with seared chicken and crisp veggies in a savory-sweet soy and oyster sauce, finished with fragrant Thai basil and a hit of chili oil. Fast, bold, and far better than takeout. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/drunken-noodles/

ingredients.note: 500g boneless skinless chicken breast, finely sliced
4 spring onion stems, cut into batons

steps: Make the sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together the oyster sauce, light soy, dark soy, rice vinegar, fish sauce, brown sugar and 2 tbsp water until the sugar dissolves.

Cook the noodles: Cook the wide rice noodles per packet instructions only until just pliable (about 3 minutes, not the full 6-8), then rinse under cold water and drain. They will finish cooking in the pan.
Sear the chicken: Heat the sesame oil in a large deep frying pan or wok over high heat. Add the sliced chicken and stir-fry until it just starts to change colour.
Add aromatics: Add the onion and garlic and cook, stirring, for about 30 seconds until fragrant.

Combine: Add the carrot, bok choy, spring onion, partially cooked noodles and the sauce. Toss with tongs until well combined and simmer 2-3 minutes, until the veg softens slightly and the noodles absorb the sauce.
Finish: Remove from the heat and stir through the Thai basil leaves.
Serve: Divide among bowls and top with chilli oil vinegar and crushed roasted peanuts, if using.
cheapTips: Buy a value pack of chicken breast and freeze in portions — it's cheaper per serving than pre-sliced.
Dark and light soy plus a pinch of sugar can stand in for pricier specialty sauces if you're missing one.
Skip the peanuts and chili oil garnish if budget is tight — the dish is complete without them.

substitutions.swap: tamari or all-purpose soy sauce
substitutions.savings: uses what you already have

substitutions.swap: white vinegar or apple cider vinegar
regular fresh basil
substitutions.savings: often cheaper and easier to find

recipes.name: Easy Butter Chicken
recipes.description: Tender chicken thighs simmered in a velvety, spiced tomato-cream sauce that comes together in just 20 minutes. Serve over fluffy basmati rice for a weeknight takeaway favorite made at home. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/easy-butter-chicken/
steps: Heat the olive oil and butter in a large, heavy-based frying pan over medium heat.
Add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook, stirring, for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken, garam masala, cumin, yellow mustard seeds, turmeric, salt and pepper. Cook, stirring, for 3-4 minutes until the chicken is slightly browned.
Stir in the tomato paste and cream until combined, then cook for 8 minutes more until the sauce thickens and the chicken is cooked through.
Serve dolloped with plain yoghurt and scattered with coriander, cucumber, red onion and chilli (if using).
Spoon over steamed basmati rice and top with crispy fried shallots if you like.
cheapTips: Chicken thighs are far cheaper than breast and stay juicier in this quick-simmer sauce.
Build your own spice mix from garam masala, cumin and turmeric instead of buying a pricey jarred butter-chicken paste.
Stretch the dish further by serving over rice and skipping the optional garnishes.

substitutions.swap: Use coconut milk for a dairy-free sauce
substitutions.savings: about $0.30/serving

substitutions.swap: Swap in chicken breast if you prefer leaner meat
Use ghee for a more authentic, richer flavor

recipes.name: Cheat's Chicken Laksa
recipes.description: A speedy, fragrant Malaysian-style laksa with tender chicken, springy noodles, and tofu puffs swimming in a creamy coconut-curry broth. Crowned with crunchy bean sprouts, lime, and fresh herbs for a 15-minute weeknight win. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/easy-curry-laksa/

ingredients.note: 250g ramen, egg noodles or rice vermicelli
500g boneless skinless thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
2 tbsp laksa or Thai red curry paste

steps: Cook the noodles per packet instructions, less 1 minute. Rinse in cold water and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over high heat.
Add the chicken and cook for 1-2 minutes until it begins to brown slightly.
Stir in the laksa (or curry) paste and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and chicken stock and cook for 2 minutes.
Halve the tofu puffs with kitchen scissors. Add to the pot with the fish sauce and lime juice, and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir through half the bean sprouts, then turn off the heat.
Divide the noodles among bowls and ladle over the laksa. Top with the remaining bean sprouts, lime wedges, crispy fried shallots, spring onion, coriander and fresh chilli, if using.
cheapTips: Swap chicken thighs for breast or even firm tofu to stretch the budget further.
Bulk-buy a tub of laksa paste and freeze in tablespoon portions so it lasts months.
Use store-brand chicken stock cubes diluted in water instead of 2L of cartoned stock to slash cost.

substitutions.swap: Red curry paste plus a pinch of turmeric and ground coriander
substitutions.savings: Uses pantry staples instead of a specialty jar

substitutions.swap: Rice vermicelli or egg noodles
substitutions.savings: Often cheaper per serving and naturally gluten-aware (vermicelli)

substitutions.swap: Cubed firm tofu, lightly pan-fried
substitutions.savings: Easier to find and a bit cheaper than puffs

recipes.name: EASY Fluffy Pancakes
recipes.description: Light, tender, and impossibly fluffy pancakes from a handful of pantry staples, ready in 15 minutes and begging for your favourite toppings. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/easy-fluffy-pancakes/

ingredients.note: 1 tsp olive oil or spray, for the pan

steps: Add the self-raising flour and baking powder to a large bowl and whisk to combine.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the milk and egg, then whisk in the melted butter and vanilla extract. The butter may go a little lumpy as it cools, and that is okay.
Pour the wet ingredients into the flour and whisk just until combined.
Preheat a non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat; the lower heat keeps the pancakes from browning too fast. Add a small drizzle of olive oil if the pan needs it.
Use an ice-cream scoop to dollop the batter into the pan, leaving room between each.
Cook 1-2 minutes per side, placing a lid on the pan halfway through to help them cook through, until golden and puffed.
Serve immediately with your favourite toppings. Makes about 8 pancakes.
cheapTips: Make your own self-raising flour: per cup of plain flour add about 1.5 tsp baking powder and a pinch of salt.
Melt the butter in the microwave in 20-second bursts to save dirtying a pan.
Batter is cheapest scaled up - double it and freeze cooked pancakes, then reheat in the toaster.

substitutions.swap: Any milk you have - 2% or oat milk both work fine
substitutions.savings: Use what's already open

substitutions.swap: Salted butter or a neutral oil
substitutions.savings: Skip buying a second butter

substitutions.swap: Halve the amount or omit if you're out
substitutions.savings: ~$0.25 per batch

recipes.name: Easy Fried Rice
recipes.description: A fast, savory weeknight fried rice loaded with crispy bacon, sweet peas and corn, and fluffy egg, all tossed in nutty sesame oil and tamari. Best made with day-old rice for that perfect, separate-grain texture. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/easy-fried-rice/
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add the diced bacon and cook for 2-3 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and cook, stirring, for 30 seconds.
Add the frozen peas and corn. Cook for a further 1 minute, stirring, until just thawed.
Push everything to one side of the pan and pour in the whisked eggs. Cook for 2-3 minutes until firm, breaking them up with a spatula into pieces.
Add the cooked rice, sliced spring onion, sesame oil and tamari. Stir gently to combine and heat the rice through.
Serve hot, topped with crispy fried shallots if using.
cheapTips: Use leftover or day-old rice instead of cooking fresh - it fries up drier and saves you a step.
Swap bacon for any leftover cooked protein (ham, chicken, or shrimp) to use up the fridge.
Buy frozen peas and corn in large bags - you only need a partial cup, so they stretch across many meals.

substitutions.swap: Regular soy sauce works just as well; tamari is just the gluten-free option.
substitutions.savings: Soy sauce is often a bit cheaper than tamari

substitutions.swap: Diced ham or turkey bacon for a leaner, lower-cost protein.
substitutions.savings: Turkey bacon runs cheaper per slice

substitutions.swap: Any neutral cooking oil like corn or rice bran oil for high-heat frying.
substitutions.savings: Neutral oils are usually cheaper than olive oil

recipes.name: Easy Greek Chicken
recipes.description: Juicy pan-seared chicken thighs in a bright marinade of paprika, oregano, garlic, olive oil, and lemon — on the table in 15 minutes. Serve with Greek salad, warm flatbread, and tzatziki for a fresh weeknight feast. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/easy-greek-chicken/

ingredients.note: 6 boneless skinless thighs, fat trimmed, pounded even

steps: Cover the chicken thighs with parchment paper and pound them with a rolling pin or mallet to an even thickness.
In a bowl, combine the chicken with the paprika, oregano, sea salt, black pepper, garlic, olive oil, and the lemon juice and zest. Toss to coat well.
Cook immediately, or marinate for up to 24 hours for deeper flavor.
Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for about 8 minutes, turning once halfway through.
Add 2 tablespoons of water to scrape up the crispy bits on the bottom of the pan, then cook for 2 more minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Serve with Greek salad, warm flatbread, and tzatziki.
cheapTips: Chicken thighs are cheaper and juicier than breasts — buy a bulk family pack and freeze portions.
Skip store-bought tzatziki: stir grated cucumber, garlic, and lemon into plain yogurt for pennies.
Marinate ahead in the morning so dinner is just a 10-minute sear.

substitutions.swap: Chicken breast, pounded thin (cook slightly less to avoid drying out)
substitutions.savings: similar cost

substitutions.swap: Smoked paprika for a deeper, smoky note
substitutions.savings: pantry swap

substitutions.swap: 2 tbsp bottled lemon juice if no fresh lemon
substitutions.savings: cheaper

recipes.name: Falafel Bowl (Simple Home Edit)
recipes.description: A vibrant Mediterranean-style bowl piling crispy falafel, fluffy brown rice, fresh veg, briny olives and feta over a swoosh of beetroot hummus. Ready in 10 minutes for a no-fuss, satisfying lunch. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/falafel-bowl/
steps: Heat the brown rice medley pouch according to the packet instructions (usually about 90 seconds in the microwave).
Heat the falafel balls as per the packet instructions until hot and crisp.
Drain and rinse the canned chickpeas.
Slice the cucumber, halve the grape tomatoes, and finely slice the red onion.
Divide the warm rice between two bowls as a base.
Arrange the baby spinach, cucumber, tomatoes, chickpeas, red onion and olives over the rice.
Top each bowl with three falafel balls and a swoosh of beetroot hummus.
Scatter over the crumbled feta.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon juice and a drizzle of olive oil, then serve.
cheapTips: Make your own falafel from a boxed falafel mix instead of buying pre-made balls — it's a fraction of the cost.
Cook a big batch of brown rice from dry instead of using single-serve microwave pouches to slash the per-bowl price.
Swap the beetroot hummus for regular plain hummus, or blend a can of chickpeas with tahini, lemon and garlic to make your own.

substitutions.savings: Often cheaper than specialty beetroot hummus

substitutions.swap: Use black olives or green olives instead
substitutions.savings: Roughly $1-2 less per jar

substitutions.swap: Use goat cheese or skip for a vegan bowl
substitutions.savings: Saves ~$0.75 per serving when omitted

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Prawn (Shrimp) Linguine
recipes.description: Juicy paprika-kissed prawns tossed with silky garlic-butter linguine, bright lemon, and a flurry of parmesan and parsley. A restaurant-worthy dinner that comes together in 20 minutes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/garlic-butter-prawn-shrimp-linguine/

ingredients.note: 400 g linguine (or any pasta of choice)
500 g raw prawns (shrimp), peeled and deveined
1/2 tsp for prawns, plus more to taste
1/4 tsp for prawns, plus more to taste
1 tbsp extra-virgin to marinate + 2 tbsp to cook
1 lemon juiced, plus lemon wedges to serve
1 tbsp chopped flat-leaf parsley, plus extra for garnish

steps: Cook the linguine in salted boiling water according to packet instructions, less 1 minute. Drain and set aside, reserving about 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the pasta water.

Meanwhile, marinate the prawns: toss them in a bowl with the sweet paprika, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp pepper, and 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil until coated. Only marinate once you're ready to cook (no longer than 20 minutes).
Heat a large, deep pan over medium-high heat. Cook the prawns in batches so the pan isn't crowded, about 1 minute per side, until just pink. Remove and set aside on a plate.
To the same pan, add the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil and the garlic. Cook, stirring, for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the white wine and cook, stirring, for 1-2 minutes until mostly evaporated.
Add the butter and, once just melted, stir in the lemon juice, cooked prawns, drained pasta, and reserved pasta water. Toss to coat everything in the glossy butter sauce.
Stir the parsley through and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Divide among four bowls, sprinkle with parmesan and extra parsley, and serve with lemon wedges.
cheapTips: Frozen peeled prawns are usually far cheaper than fresh and work perfectly here just thaw and pat dry before marinating.
No white wine? Swap in chicken stock for the same bright deglaze at a fraction of the cost.
Skip pricey fresh parmesan and finish with a more economical pre-grated parmesan you won't taste the difference once it melts in.

substitutions.swap: chicken stock
substitutions.savings: Avoids buying a bottle of wine

substitutions.swap: frozen shrimp
substitutions.savings: Cheaper than fresh prawns per serving

substitutions.swap: salted butter (reduce added salt)
substitutions.savings: Use what you already have on hand

recipes.name: Homemade Nachos
recipes.description: Crispy corn chips loaded with spiced beef and beans, melted cheddar, and finished with fresh avocado salsa, tomato salsa, sour cream, and jalapenos. The ultimate sharing plate that comes together in 15 minutes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/homemade-nachos/

ingredients.note: 1 tsp in spice mix plus salt to taste for the salsas
1 tbsp for avocado salsa plus 1 tbsp for tomato salsa
1 tbsp lime juice for each salsa (~half a lime each)

steps: Preheat the oven to grill (broil).
Combine the sweet paprika, cumin, onion powder, oregano, and 1 tsp sea salt in a small bowl to make the spice mix.
Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-based frying pan over high heat. Add the diced onion and garlic and cook for 1-2 minutes until softened.
Add the ground beef and cook until browned, 3-4 minutes. Stir in the spice mix, tomato paste, and drained kidney beans.
Add 1/4 cup (60 ml) of water and cook for 2 minutes until thickened.
Meanwhile, make the avocado salsa: mash the avocado with 1 tbsp cilantro, 1 tbsp lime juice, and a pinch of sea salt.
Make the tomato salsa: combine the diced tomato, diced red onion, 1 tbsp cilantro, 1 tbsp lime juice, and a pinch of sea salt.
Arrange the corn chips in an ovenproof dish and top with the beef mixture and grated cheddar. Grill (broil) for 2-4 minutes until golden and the cheese is melted.
Top the nachos with sour cream, avocado salsa, tomato salsa, and sliced fresh jalapenos. Serve immediately.
cheapTips: Swap the kidney beans for a second portion of beans instead of beef, or use them to stretch the beef further and cut the cost per serving.
Buy a block of cheddar and grate it yourself, it's cheaper per ounce than pre-shredded and melts better.
Use bottled lime juice instead of fresh limes for the salsas to save a little when limes are pricey.

substitutions.swap: ground turkey or plant-based ground for a leaner or vegetarian version
substitutions.savings: lower cost with turkey or beans

substitutions.swap: black beans or pinto beans, or an extra portion of beef

recipes.name: Honey Garlic Chicken Thighs
recipes.description: Golden, crisp chicken thighs glazed in a glossy honey-garlic sauce with a hit of sesame and tamari, served over steamed rice and Asian greens. Ready in 20 minutes for a fast, sticky-sweet weeknight dinner. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/honey-garlic-chicken-thighs/

ingredients.note: 6 boneless thighs, skin on or off
steamed gai lan / Asian greens, to serve

steps: Pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towel and season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large, deep pan over medium-high heat.

Add the chicken skin- or smooth-side down and cook 4-5 minutes until golden and crisp, pressing gently for skin-on thighs. Flip and cook 4-5 minutes more until cooked through. Set aside, leaving at least 2 tablespoons of fat in the pan.
Make the sauce: in a small bowl, whisk together the tamari, honey, brown sugar, minced garlic, rice vinegar, sesame oil, cornstarch and water until smooth.
Reduce heat to medium and pour the sauce into the pan. Let it bubble and simmer 2-3 minutes until thickened and glossy.
Return the chicken to the pan, turning to coat in the sauce.
Slice the chicken into strips if desired and serve over steamed rice with the steamed greens alongside.
Spoon over extra sauce and top with sliced spring onion and chili oil, if using.
cheapTips: Buy bone-in thighs and debone them yourself, or use whole legs — usually cheaper per pound than pre-trimmed boneless.
Regular soy sauce works in place of tamari and costs less; only swap to tamari if you need gluten-free.
Cook rice in a big batch and freeze portions so a serving costs pennies and reheats in minutes.

substitutions.swap: Chicken breast — pound to even thickness and cook a touch less to avoid drying out
substitutions.savings: similar

substitutions.swap: All-purpose or light soy sauce
substitutions.savings: ~$0.40 for the dish

substitutions.swap: Regular broccoli or bok choy, steamed
substitutions.savings: ~$1.70 vs broccolini

recipes.name: Honey Soy Glazed Salmon
recipes.description: Crispy-skinned salmon fillets pan-seared and basted in a sticky honey-soy glaze, served over jasmine rice with edamame, cucumber, and a drizzle of spicy mayo. Ready in 15 minutes for a fresh, restaurant-worthy bowl. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/honey-garlic-salmon/

ingredients.note: 2 tbsp all-purpose soy sauce or tamari
2 tbsp apple cider vinegar or rice wine vinegar or fresh lime juice
370 g cooked jasmine rice (~0.75 cup dry)
4 tbsp spicy mayonnaise or plain whole-egg mayonnaise

steps: Combine the soy sauce, apple cider vinegar, honey, minced garlic, and ginger in a small bowl to make the glaze.
Pat the salmon fillets dry and sprinkle all over with the sea salt and black pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Add the salmon skin-side down and cook for 4 minutes until the skin is crisp.
Flip the fillets and cook for a further 3 minutes.
Pour the sauce into the pan. Cook for 1-2 minutes, continuously basting the salmon with a spoon, until the sauce becomes sticky and glazes the salmon.
Stir the sriracha into the mayonnaise to make a spicy mayo (skip for plain).
Divide the cooked jasmine rice, edamame, and sliced cucumber among four bowls.
Top each bowl with a glazed salmon fillet and any sticky sauce from the pan.
Finish with a sprinkle of sesame seeds and a drizzle of the spicy mayo. Serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use frozen salmon fillets and thaw them overnight to cut the cost of fresh fish significantly.
Make your own spicy mayo by stirring sriracha into plain mayonnaise instead of buying a premixed bottle.
Cook a big batch of jasmine rice and freeze portions so weeknight bowls come together in minutes.

substitutions.savings: use what you have on hand

substitutions.swap: brown sugar
substitutions.savings: saves about $0.30 per batch

substitutions.swap: frozen salmon fillets
substitutions.savings: saves roughly $0.25 per serving

recipes.name: Juicy Thai Beef Lettuce Cups
recipes.description: Savory-sweet Thai-style minced beef tossed with green beans, carrot and fragrant Thai basil, spooned into crisp lettuce cups and topped with crunchy peanuts and a squeeze of lime. A fast, messy, hands-on dinner that's bursting with flavor. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/juicy-thai-beef-lettuce-cups/

ingredients.note: 1 tbsp tamari or all-purpose soy sauce
100g green beans, finely sliced into 1cm lengths
2 handfuls Thai basil leaves, 1 sprig reserved for garnish

steps: Make the sauce: in a small bowl, combine the tamari, dark soy, fish sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, cornflour and water, stirring well to dissolve. Set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add the diced onion, garlic and ginger. Cook, stirring, for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the beef, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, and cook for 2-3 minutes until just browned.
Add the green beans and carrot, tossing for a further 1 minute.
Pour in the sauce and simmer 2-3 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the beef is cooked through. Stir through the Thai basil until wilted.
Serve the beef mixture in a bowl alongside the lettuce leaves, sliced spring onion, chilli (if using), chopped peanuts, lime wedges and reserved Thai basil.
Let everyone spoon the filling into lettuce cups and add their own toppings. Eat with your hands and enjoy, this one's meant to be messy, so keep napkins handy!
cheapTips: Ground beef is the priciest item — swap in ground chicken, pork, or turkey when on sale to cut the cost.
Use a regular soy sauce in place of tamari and dark soy if you don't want to buy multiple bottles.
Buy a head of romaine or iceberg instead of bagged leaves and peel off the large outer leaves — cheaper per cup.

substitutions.swap: Ground chicken, pork, or turkey work just as well
substitutions.savings: Often cheaper per serving on sale

substitutions.swap: Vegetarian oyster sauce or extra soy sauce
substitutions.savings: Makes it pescatarian/veg-friendly

substitutions.swap: Regular sweet basil or fresh cilantro
substitutions.savings: Use what's already in the fridge

recipes.name: Kale, Quinoa and Halloumi Salad
recipes.description: A fresh, hearty salad of fluffy quinoa, shredded kale, and crunchy almonds tossed in a bright lemon-dijon dressing, topped with golden pan-fried halloumi. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/kale-quinoa-halloumi-salad/

ingredients.note: 3 tbsp for dressing + olive oil spray for cooking

steps: Cook the quinoa: rinse 1 cup quinoa and drain. Add to a saucepan with 2 cups water, bring to a boil, stir once, then reduce to a simmer. Cover and cook 15 minutes, then rest covered 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork. (Or microwave covered with 2 cups water on high 5 min, stir, 2 min more, then stand until cool.)
Make the dressing: in a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, dijon mustard, sea salt flakes, and cracked black pepper.
Toss the salad: add the cooked quinoa, shredded kale, sliced red onion, and chopped almonds to a large bowl. Drizzle over the dressing and toss to combine.
Cook the halloumi: heat a large, heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat. Spray with olive oil and cook the halloumi flat-side down for about 1 minute per side, turning once, until golden.
Serve the salad topped with the warm halloumi and lemon wedges on the side.
cheapTips: Buy halloumi when on sale and freeze it - it pan-fries just as well from frozen-thawed.
Cook a big batch of quinoa ahead; it keeps in the fridge for 4-5 days and stretches across multiple meals.
Swap almonds for whatever nut or seed you have on hand - sunflower seeds work and cost a fraction of almonds.

substitutions.swap: Firm feta or paneer, pan-fried
substitutions.savings: Often cheaper per ounce than halloumi

substitutions.swap: Fresh lemon juice from 1 lemon
substitutions.savings: Brighter flavor for similar cost

substitutions.swap: Toasted sunflower seeds or walnuts

recipes.name: Korean Beef Rice Bowls
recipes.description: Sweet-savory gochujang-glazed ground beef piled over fluffy jasmine rice with crunchy carrot, cucumber, and tangy kimchi, all finished with a creamy gochujang mayo drizzle. A 20-minute weeknight bowl that tastes like takeout. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/korean-beef-rice-bowls/

ingredients.note: 1 tbsp in sauce + 1 tsp in mayo
1 tsp in sauce + 1/2 tsp in mayo
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil or neutral oil
2 spring onions, finely sliced, 1 tbsp reserved for garnish
370 g cooked jasmine rice (~1.5 cup dry)
1 Lebanese (short/Persian) cucumber, sliced into half moons

steps: Make the stir-fry sauce: in a small bowl, whisk together the garlic, ginger, soy sauce, brown sugar, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp gochujang, 1 tsp rice vinegar and the sesame seeds until combined. Set aside.
Cook the beef: heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the sauce: pour in the stir-fry sauce and stir well to coat the beef. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Turn off the heat and stir through most of the sliced spring onion, reserving 1 tbsp for garnish.
Make the gochujang mayo: in a small bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, 1 tsp gochujang, 1/2 tsp sesame oil and 1/2 tsp rice vinegar until smooth. Set aside.
Assemble: divide the cooked jasmine rice among four bowls. Top each with the Korean beef mixture and a generous serving of kimchi, julienned carrot and cucumber half moons.
Drizzle the gochujang mayo over the top and garnish with extra sesame seeds and the reserved spring onion. Serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy a larger pack of ground beef and freeze portions; the per-bowl cost drops sharply versus single packs.
Make a bigger batch of kimchi-friendly jasmine rice and reuse leftovers for next-day fried rice.
Skip store-bought gochujang mayo by mixing your own from pantry mayonnaise and gochujang in seconds.

substitutions.swap: ground turkey or ground chicken for a leaner, cheaper bowl
substitutions.savings: ~$1/serving

recipes.name: One-pan Lemon Gnocchi Chicken
recipes.description: Tender pan-seared chicken steaks and pillowy gnocchi simmered in a bright, creamy lemon-parmesan sauce with wilted baby spinach — a luxurious dinner in just 15 minutes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/lemon-gnocchi-chicken/

ingredients.note: 2 boneless skinless breasts, halved lengthways into 4 thin steaks

steps: Sprinkle the chicken steaks all over with the sea salt, black pepper, paprika and dried thyme, rubbing the mixture in with your hands so they are evenly coated.
Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-based frying pan over medium heat, then add the butter.
Once the butter has melted, add the chicken and cook for 3 minutes. Flip, cover with a lid, and cook a further 3 minutes or until cooked through. Set aside.
To the same pan, add the minced garlic and cook, stirring, for 30 seconds.
Pour in the lemon juice, chicken stock and cream. Once simmering, stir in the parmesan and the gnocchi, and cook for 2 minutes until the sauce thickens and the gnocchi are tender.
Stir through the baby spinach until wilted, top with the cooked chicken, and serve.
cheapTips: Buy a larger bag of fresh or shelf-stable gnocchi and portion it — it's far cheaper per serving than small packs.
Grate parmesan from a wedge yourself instead of buying pre-grated; it melts better and costs less per ounce.
Swap chicken breast for cheaper boneless thighs — they stay juicier and cost less per serving.

substitutions.swap: Use half-and-half or evaporated milk for a lighter sauce
