recipes.name: Macaroni and Cheese (Simple Home Edit)
recipes.description: Creamy stovetop mac and cheese with a silky cheddar sauce, finished under the broiler with a golden panko crunch. Comfort food on the table in 20 minutes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/macaroni-and-cheese/

ingredients.note: olive oil spray, for the top

steps: Cook the macaroni according to the packet instructions, minus 1 minute. Drain and run under cold water to cool immediately.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large, deep frying pan over low heat.
Once melted, add the flour and stir for about 30 seconds until a smooth paste forms.
Pour in about one-quarter of the milk, whisking for 30 seconds until combined.
Add the remaining milk and whisk over low heat for about 5 minutes, until the sauce thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Stir in the chicken stock powder and grated cheddar until melted. Turn off the heat and stir the cooked pasta through. Serve as is, or continue for extra crunch.
Preheat the oven grill (broiler). Transfer to a baking dish if needed, sprinkle with panko breadcrumbs, and spray with olive oil.
Grill (broil) for 2-3 minutes until golden, watching closely as it browns quickly.
cheapTips: Buy a block of cheddar and grate it yourself - it melts smoother than pre-shredded and costs less per ounce.
Store-brand elbow macaroni and whole milk are just as good here and save the most on a family-sized batch.
Skip the chicken stock powder if you don't have it; a good pinch of salt seasons the sauce just fine.

substitutions.swap: Use sharp-cheddar or white-cheddar for a tangier, more grown-up flavor.
substitutions.savings: Similar cost

substitutions.swap: Two-percent milk works fine and is slightly lighter.

recipes.name: Malaysian-inspired Hokkien Mee
recipes.description: Crispy pork belly, juicy prawns and chewy udon tossed in a glossy dark soy sauce with wilted napa cabbage and Chinese broccoli — a fast, savory stir-fry that tastes like takeout. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/malaysian-inspired-hokkien-mee/

ingredients.note: 2 tbsp neutral oil or extra-virgin olive oil
250 g pork belly, skin removed, cut into bite-sized pieces
600 g fresh udon noodles, prepared per packet
1 bunch Chinese broccoli (gai lan), roughly chopped

steps: Make the sauce: whisk together the dark soy, light soy, oyster sauce, brown sugar, cornstarch, water and sesame seeds in a jug. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a large, deep, heavy-based pan or wok over high heat. Add the pork belly and cook for 4-5 minutes, tossing, until crisp and browned all over (watch for spitting fat).
Add the prawns and toss for about 30 seconds until almost cooked through, then add the garlic and cook, tossing, for another 30 seconds.
Add the napa cabbage and Chinese broccoli. Toss for about 1 minute until the vegetables start to wilt.
Add the udon noodles and the sauce. Toss with tongs until everything is well combined and coated in the glossy sauce.
Divide among four bowls and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Swap prawns for the same weight of regular shrimp or thinly sliced chicken thigh to cut the per-serving cost significantly.
Pork belly delivers the most flavor, but pork shoulder or ground pork works for a budget version.
Use whatever leafy greens you have — regular cabbage, bok choy or broccoli stems all wilt nicely into the sauce.

substitutions.swap: Use shrimp or sliced chicken thigh
substitutions.savings: Saves ~$2-4 per serving

substitutions.swap: Use lo-mein, egg, or rice noodles

recipes.name: Mango Salad with Sweet Chilli Lime Dressing
recipes.description: Juicy ripe mango, creamy avocado and crunchy peanuts tossed in a zingy sweet chilli lime dressing for a bright, fresh salad that comes together in 15 minutes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/mango-salad-with-sweet-chilli-lime-dressing/

ingredients.note: 2 tsp all-purpose soy sauce or tamari
freshly cracked black pepper, to taste

steps: Make the dressing: in a small bowl, whisk together the sweet chilli sauce, soy sauce (or tamari), lime juice, olive oil, honey and grated ginger until well combined.
Season the dressing with sea salt flakes and freshly cracked black pepper to taste.
Peel and dice the mangoes and avocado, finely slice the red onion, and halve and slice the cucumber.
In a shallow serving bowl, layer the mango, cucumber, avocado, red onion and chopped coriander in that order.
Drizzle the sweet chilli lime dressing over the salad.
Sprinkle with the crushed peanuts and toss gently just before serving.
cheapTips: Use slightly firm, in-season mangoes from a market case for the best price and easiest dicing.
Swap fresh lime for a splash of bottled lime juice to save money when limes are pricey.
Maple syrup keeps it fully vegan and is often cheaper by the spoon than honey.

recipes.name: Maple Kale Salad with Cranberries and Blue Cheese
recipes.description: Massaged kale tossed in a sweet-tangy maple dijon dressing, then piled high with crisp apple, chewy cranberries, toasted pecans, and crumbles of sharp blue cheese. A bright, hearty salad that holds its crunch. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/maple-kale-salad-with-cranberries-and-blue-cheese/

ingredients.note: 1 large bunch, about 6 cups, stems removed, finely chopped
1 medium pink lady apple, unpeeled, finely sliced

steps: Make the dressing: in a small bowl or jar, whisk together the olive oil, maple syrup, dijon, apple cider vinegar, and garlic powder. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Place the chopped kale in a large mixing bowl and pour half of the dressing over it.
Massage the dressing into the kale with your hands for 1-2 minutes, until the leaves soften and reduce in volume.
Add the sliced apple, red onion, dried cranberries, toasted pecans, and crumbled blue cheese to the kale.
Drizzle with the remaining dressing and toss gently to combine.
Serve immediately, or refrigerate up to 4 hours. For the best texture, add the pecans just before serving.
cheapTips: Buy a whole bunch of curly kale and strip the stems yourself instead of pre-bagged chopped kale; it's a fraction of the price.
Toast raw pecans in a dry pan for a few minutes rather than buying pre-toasted nuts.
Feta works just as well as blue cheese and is usually cheaper per ounce.

recipes.name: Mediterranean Pizza
recipes.description: Crisp, golden pizza loaded with melty mozzarella, spicy salami, briny kalamata olives and roasted capsicum, finished with garlicky oil and fresh basil, served with a bright balsamic rocket salad. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/mediterranean-pizza/

ingredients.note: 3 tbsp for pizza + 2 tbsp for salad
1 tsp for pizza + 1/2 tsp for salad

steps: Preheat the oven to 220C (425F) and line two baking trays.
Spread the tomato paste evenly over both pizza bases.
Sprinkle with two-thirds of the mozzarella, then top with the salami, mushrooms, kalamata olives and roasted capsicum strips. Scatter over the remaining cheese.
In a small bowl, stir together the minced garlic, 3 tbsp olive oil and 1 tsp sea salt flakes. Drizzle over the pizzas and brush any leftover oil over the crusts.
Bake for about 12 minutes until the bases are crisp and golden, placing one tray on the top rack and one on the bottom and swapping halfway through.
Meanwhile, make the salad: toss the rocket with the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil, balsamic vinegar, 1/2 tsp sea salt flakes and the black pepper.
Serve the pizzas topped with fresh basil leaves and a drizzle of chilli oil if using, with the rocket salad alongside.
cheapTips: Use a store-bought pizza dough ball and stretch your own bases to save over pre-made bases.
Swap kalamata olives for cheaper black olives and skip the chilli oil garnish to trim cost.
Buy a block of mozzarella and shred it yourself rather than paying extra for pre-shredded.

recipes.name: Nasi Goreng (Indonesian Fried Rice)
recipes.description: Smoky-sweet Indonesian fried rice tossed with tender soy-glazed chicken, garlic, and onion, then crowned with a runny fried egg and crispy shallots. A fast, deeply savory weeknight one-pan dinner. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/nasi-goreng/

ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for marinade + 1 tbsp to finish

steps: In a medium bowl, toss the sliced chicken with 1 tbsp of the dark soy sauce and set aside to marinate.
Heat a large, heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the olive oil, onion, and garlic and cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the marinated chicken and cook, stirring, for 3-4 minutes until just cooked through.
Stir in the brown sugar and all-purpose soy sauce. Cook for about 30 seconds, until the sugar dissolves.
Add the cooked rice and stir until evenly combined and heated through.
Stir through the remaining 1 tbsp dark soy sauce to coat the rice.
Divide between bowls and top each with a fried egg, crispy fried shallots, and sambal oelek if using.
Serve with sliced cucumber and tomato on the side.
cheapTips: Use day-old leftover rice — it fries up drier and cheaper than cooking fresh, and keeps grains separate.
Chicken thighs can replace breast for a lower price and juicier result.
Skip the optional garnishes (shallots, sambal, cucumber, tomato) to cut cost without touching the core dish.

substitutions.swap: chicken-thighs

recipes.name: Not Spicy, Not Vodka Pasta
recipes.description: A silky, creamy tomato pasta with all the rich, comforting flavor of vodka pasta but no vodka and no heat, finished with torn burrata and fresh basil. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/not-spicy-not-vodka-pasta/

ingredients.note: 75 g finely grated, plus extra to serve

steps: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta 1 minute less than the package instructions; it will finish cooking in the sauce.
Before draining, reserve about 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the pasta cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil and butter in a large, deep, heavy-based frying pan over medium heat.
Add the red onion and cook for 3-4 minutes until very soft and lightly caramelised.
Add the garlic and cook, stirring, for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomato paste and cook, stirring, for 1-2 minutes until the oil is absorbed and the paste deepens in color.
Add the red wine vinegar and cook, stirring, for 1-2 minutes until evaporated.
Turn the heat to low. Stir in the cream and simmer for 3-4 minutes until thickened, then stir through the parmesan, salt and pepper.
Add the drained pasta and stir gently to coat. Loosen with half the reserved pasta water, adding more as needed until the sauce is creamy, silky and smooth.
Divide among four bowls and top with the halved burrata, basil leaves, chilli flakes (if using) and extra parmesan.
cheapTips: Swap the burrata for a spoonful of fresh ricotta or torn fresh mozzarella to cut the cost while keeping it creamy.
Use any short pasta you already have, like penne or rigatoni, instead of trottole.
Buy a tube or can of double-concentrated tomato paste; it's cheaper than jarred sauce and lasts for many meals.

recipes.name: One-pan Chicken and Broccoli Ramen Noodles
recipes.description: Tender chicken thighs and crisp-tender broccoli tossed in a glossy honey-soy sauce with springy ramen noodles, all cooked in a single pan in just 20 minutes. A fast, deeply savory weeknight dinner that delivers takeout flavor with almost no cleanup. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/one-pan-chicken-and-broccoli-ramen-noodles/

ingredients.note: 1 tbsp light olive oil or neutral oil
2 spring onions, white and green parts separated

steps: Make the sauce: combine the honey, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, mirin, ketchup, sesame oil and black pepper in a jug. Mix well and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the diced chicken and cook, stirring, for 5 minutes.
Add the white parts of the spring onion, the garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant.
Add the broccoli florets, cover the pan with a lid and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the sauce and toss to coat the chicken and broccoli evenly.

Push the chicken and broccoli to one side of the pan. Place 2 bundles of ramen in the empty side, then slide the chicken and broccoli over the top. Add the remaining 2 bundles beside the first, then spread the stir-fry evenly over all the noodles.
Pour the water over the entire pan so it runs underneath the noodles. Cover and cook for 1 minute.
Remove the lid and use tongs to gently turn and loosen the noodles, making sure any firm sections touch the liquid. Cover and cook another 1-2 minutes until the noodles have softened.
Remove the lid and toss everything for 1-2 minutes, until the noodles separate, the chicken is cooked through, the liquid absorbs and the sauce thickens to coat the noodles.
Serve sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds and the green parts of the spring onion, with crispy chilli oil if using.
cheapTips: Skip the discarded ramen seasoning sachets and save them to flavor a future soup or fried rice instead of tossing them.
Buy a whole head of broccoli and use the stalk too: peel it, slice thin, and add it with the florets so nothing goes to waste.
Chicken thighs are cheaper than breast and stay juicier here, but use whichever is on sale - both work.

recipes.name: One-pan Creamy Sausage Gnocchi
recipes.description: Pillowy gnocchi simmered right in a rich, creamy tomato sauce loaded with browned Italian sausage, fresh spinach, and parmesan — all in one pan in 20 minutes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/one-pan-creamy-sausage-gnocchi/
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large, deep, heavy-based pan over medium-high heat.
Add the sausage with casings removed and break it into small pieces with a wooden spoon. Cook, stirring, for 4-5 minutes until fully cooked and browned.
Add the minced garlic and cook, stirring, for 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for another 30 seconds.
Pour in the white wine and cook for 1-2 minutes until most of the liquid has evaporated.
Add the crushed tomatoes and cream. Stir to combine and bring to a simmer.
Add the gnocchi, cover, and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir the gnocchi, then continue cooking uncovered for 2-3 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the gnocchi is soft and cooked through.

Season to taste with salt and pepper, then serve topped with fresh basil, chilli flakes, and extra parmesan.

Shelf-stable gnocchi and canned crushed tomatoes are cheaper than fresh refrigerated versions and work perfectly here.

substitutions.savings: Avoids buying a whole bottle of wine

substitutions.swap: Plant-based sausage for a vegetarian version

recipes.name: One-pan Korean-style Beef Noodles
recipes.description: Saucy, caramelized ground beef and slurpy ramen noodles simmered together in a sweet-spicy gochujang sauce enriched with coconut milk — a fast, comforting weeknight one-pan dinner. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/one-pan-korean-style-beef-noodles/

ingredients.note: 3 x 85g bundles ramen noodles, flavour sachets discarded
2 spring onions, finely sliced, plus extra to serve

steps: Make the sauce: combine the soy sauce, dark soy sauce, brown sugar, rice wine vinegar, sesame oil, gochujang and peanut butter in a small bowl. Whisk to combine and set aside.
Heat the neutral oil in a large heavy-based pan with a lid over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef, break it up with a spatula, and leave undisturbed for 4-5 minutes until it begins to caramelize.

Add the garlic and ginger and cook, stirring, for 60 seconds.
Stir through the tomato paste.

cheapTips: Discard the seasoning sachets and use the cheapest instant ramen bundles — they cook into the sauce beautifully.
Swap honey for the brown sugar if you already have it, and use any neutral oil you keep on hand.
Use 80/20 ground beef for more flavor at a lower price; the extra fat enriches the sauce.

substitutions.savings: Saves about $1.30 per recipe

recipes.name: Oysters with Red Wine Vinaigrette

recipes.name: Peanut Chicken Satay
recipes.description: Tender bites of curry-spiced chicken tossed in a quick, creamy peanut-chilli sauce that comes together in just 15 minutes. Serve over rice with cucumber, fresh herbs and a squeeze of lime for a weeknight takeaway favourite. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/peanut-chicken-satay/

ingredients.note: 500g, boneless skinless, cut into bite-sized pieces
1 tbsp rice wine vinegar or white vinegar

steps: Sprinkle the chicken with curry powder and salt, toss to coat and set aside.
In a small bowl, combine the peanut butter, sweet chilli sauce, soy sauce, vinegar and garlic with 2-3 tablespoons of water, stirring until smooth.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Add the onion and cook for 1-2 minutes until softened.
Add the chicken and cook for 5-6 minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Turn off the heat and stir through the peanut sauce, adding 2-3 more tablespoons of water to loosen if needed.
Serve over rice with cucumber, coriander, fresh chilli, crushed peanuts and lime wedges.
cheapTips: Chicken thighs are cheaper and juicier than breast for this dish, and they stay tender even if slightly overcooked.
Make your own sweet chilli sauce stand-in with sugar or honey plus a pinch of chilli flakes to skip buying a whole bottle.
Skip the optional garnishes if budget is tight; the chicken and peanut sauce over rice is satisfying on its own.

substitutions.swap: Chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
substitutions.savings: similar cost

substitutions.swap: 1/4 cup sugar or honey for a simpler sweet note
substitutions.savings: saves on a specialty sauce

recipes.name: Peking-style Beef
recipes.description: Crispy, caramelized ground beef glazed in a glossy hoisin-soy sauce, served over fluffy jasmine rice with cool cucumber ribbons and scallions. A 20-minute weeknight take on Peking flavors. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/peking-style-beef/

ingredients.note: 1 tbsp light olive oil or any neutral oil
1 tsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water

steps: Make the sauce: In a small bowl or jug, whisk together the hoisin, soy sauce, dark soy, rice wine vinegar, brown sugar and five-spice (if using). Set aside.
Heat the oil in a large, heavy-based pan over high heat. Add the beef and break it up so it spreads across the pan.
Let the beef cook untouched for 5-6 minutes so it browns and develops crispy edges. Flip and break it apart further, then cook 1-2 minutes more until cooked through.
Stir in the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour the sauce over the beef and simmer for 1-2 minutes, stirring to coat.
Stir in the cornflour-and-water slurry and cook 30-60 seconds until the sauce thickens and clings to the beef.
Spoon the beef over steamed jasmine rice. Top with cucumber ribbons, sliced spring onion and toasted sesame seeds, then drizzle with sesame oil and serve.
cheapTips: Buy regular (not extra-lean) ground beef — it's cheaper and the extra fat gives you the crispy, caramelized edges this dish needs.
Skip the dark soy and use a touch more regular soy plus an extra pinch of brown sugar for color; you likely already have both.
A cucumber and a couple of scallions stretch this into a full, fresh-feeling meal for pennies — no need for pricey sides.

substitutions.swap: Extra regular soy sauce with a pinch of brown sugar for color
substitutions.savings: Skip a specialty bottle

substitutions.swap: Any neutral oil like vegetable or canola
Ground turkey or chicken for a leaner, cheaper option
substitutions.savings: ~30% on the protein

recipes.name: Perfect Soft-boiled Eggs
recipes.description: Jammy, golden-centered soft-boiled eggs with a tender white, served with crisp buttered toast soldiers for dipping. A foolproof 6-minute breakfast that nails the runny yolk every time. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/perfect-soft-boiled-eggs/

ingredients.note: 8 large eggs, directly from the fridge
buttered toast, cut into soldiers (use gluten-free if needed)

steps: Bring a pot of water to a rapid boil. Use a pot large enough to hold the eggs in a single layer with at least 3 cm (1 1/4 inches) of water covering them.
Place the cold eggs in a bowl of hot tap water, fully covered, for 1-2 minutes. This tempers them so they don't crack when they hit the boiling water.
Gently lower the eggs into the boiling water and cook at a rapid boil for exactly 5 minutes (set a timer).
As soon as the timer goes off, lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon and run them under cold tap water for 30 seconds to stop the cooking and cool them enough to handle.
Use a butter knife or spoon to crack the top of the shell off. If the top of the yolk looks watery, swirl it gently with a spoon so the residual heat finishes cooking it.
Toast the bread, butter it, and cut into strips (soldiers). Season the eggs with sea salt flakes and serve with the toast soldiers for dipping.
cheapTips: Eggs are one of the cheapest protein sources around - buy by the dozen or larger flats to drop the per-egg cost further.
Use the heel ends of a sandwich loaf for the toast soldiers instead of buying fresh bread.
A pat of butter goes a long way; whipped or plant butter spreads thinner and stretches even further.

substitutions.swap: regular table salt or kosher salt
substitutions.savings: Saves about $0.09 per tsp

substitutions.swap: plant butter or olive oil
substitutions.savings: Saves a few cents and makes it dairy-free

substitutions.swap: gluten-free bread for a GF version
substitutions.savings: Keeps it celiac-friendly

recipes.name: Perfect Steak with Peppercorn Sauce
recipes.description: Perfectly seared ribeye rested to juicy perfection, draped in a silky creamy peppercorn sauce built right in the pan. A steakhouse-quality dinner you can pull off in 20 minutes flat. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/perfect-steak-with-peppercorn-sauce/

ingredients.note: Scotch fillet (rib eye) steaks, approx. 250g/9oz each, 2.5-3cm thick
2 tsp green peppercorns in brine, drained
1 tsp freshly cracked, plus extra to serve
for a rocket and parmesan side salad
air fryer chips or oven fries, to serve

steps: Prep the steak: Bring the steaks to room temperature for 20-40 minutes. Pat dry with paper towel and sprinkle all sides with the sea salt just before cooking.
Cook the steak: Heat a large, heavy cast-iron pan over high heat. Add the olive oil, then the steaks. Don't overcrowd the pan so a good crust forms.
Cook to your preference, using a timer: blue 1 min/side, rare 2 min/side, medium-rare 3 min/side, medium 4 min/side, well-done 5 min/side (lower to medium heat after the first flip for well-done).
Rest: Transfer steaks to a plate, cover loosely with foil, and rest 5-10 minutes while you make the sauce.
Start the sauce: Turn off the heat and let the pan cool 1-2 minutes so nothing burns.
Add the butter, then immediately the garlic, green peppercorns (if using) and cracked black pepper. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return to medium heat. Add the white wine (if using), scraping up the browned bits, and cook 2-3 minutes until reduced by at least half.
Add the beef stock and simmer 2-3 minutes until reduced by at least half.
Stir in the cream, dijon and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer gently 5-6 minutes until thickened. Taste and season with salt if needed.
Turn off the heat and set the sauce aside.
Slice the steaks against the grain if you like, and sprinkle with extra salt.
Serve with the rocket and parmesan salad, fries, and generous spoonfuls of peppercorn sauce. Finish with extra cracked black pepper.
cheapTips: Swap ribeye for a cheaper cut like sirloin or flat-iron steak; the creamy peppercorn sauce makes any steak taste premium.
Skip the optional white wine and just use a splash of extra beef stock plus a little vinegar to deglaze.
Use regular cracked black pepper instead of brined green peppercorns; the sauce is still excellent.

substitutions.swap: Sirloin or flat-iron steak
substitutions.savings: Cuts the per-serving meat cost by more than half

substitutions.swap: Extra beef stock with a splash of white wine vinegar
substitutions.savings: Avoids buying a bottle of wine

substitutions.swap: Double cream or full-fat manufacturing cream
substitutions.savings: Use what you already have on hand

recipes.name: Poached Chicken Asian Soup
recipes.description: A light, restorative bowl of silky egg noodles, tender shredded poached chicken, and crisp bok choy in a savoury tamari-garlic broth, finished with sesame oil and a kick of chilli. Ready in 20 minutes for a cosy weeknight dinner. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/poached-chicken-asian-soup/

ingredients.note: 2 tbsp tamari or all-purpose soy sauce
2 boneless skinless breasts, poached and shredded
chilli oil or chilli sauce, to serve
black and white sesame seeds, to serve

steps: Start the broth: add the chicken stock, tamari (or all-purpose soy sauce) and whole garlic cloves to a large pot over high heat and bring to the boil.
Add the sliced mushrooms, reduce the heat to medium and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the egg noodles and halved bok choy and cook for a further 2 minutes, until the noodles are tender and the bok choy is bright and just wilted.
Fish out and discard the garlic cloves.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top each with the shredded poached chicken.
Drizzle with sesame oil and finish with crispy-fried shallots, chilli oil or sauce and a sprinkle of black and white sesame seeds, if using. Serve hot.
cheapTips: Poach the chicken breasts in the same broth you'll serve to deepen flavour and save a pan.
Swap the egg noodles for whatever noodle is cheapest in your pantry; rice or soba both work.
Buy whole mushrooms and slice them yourself, which costs noticeably less than pre-sliced.

substitutions.swap: regular soy sauce or light soy sauce
substitutions.savings: save ~$0.10/tbsp

substitutions.swap: rice noodles or soba noodles
substitutions.savings: comparable or cheaper

substitutions.swap: baby bok choy or napa cabbage
substitutions.savings: save ~$1.00

recipes.name: Pork Belly Fried Rice
recipes.description: Crispy golden pork belly tossed with cold jasmine rice, bok choy, and silky scrambled egg in a savory soy-sesame glaze. A fast, deeply satisfying weeknight fried rice that tastes like takeout. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/pork-belly-fried-rice/

ingredients.note: 400g pork belly rashers, skin off, cut into ~2cm pieces
1 tsp sea salt flakes, plus extra to taste
555g cooked, cold jasmine rice (~1.5 cups dry)
2 spring onions, finely sliced, plus extra to garnish
2 tbsp tamari or all-purpose soy sauce
freshly cracked black pepper, to taste

steps: Heat the cooking oil in a large, deep, heavy-based pan over high heat. Add the pork belly and salt and cook for 5-6 minutes until golden and crispy. Remove and set aside on a plate. Pour off excess fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the pan.
To the same pan add the minced garlic and ginger and cook, stirring, for 30 seconds. Stir through the sliced bok choy.
Push the veggies to one side of the pan and add the whisked egg. Cook for 1-2 minutes until just firm, then stir together with the bok choy.
Return the cooked pork to the pan along with the cold rice, spring onion, Shaoxing wine or mirin, dark soy sauce, tamari and sesame oil. Toss everything to combine and heat through.
Season to taste with extra salt and cracked black pepper. Serve topped with extra sliced spring onion, toasted sesame seeds, and kimchi on the side.
cheapTips: Use day-old leftover rice instead of cooking fresh — it fries up better and uses up what you already have.
Pork belly rendering gives you free flavored fat; you don't need extra oil for the veggies and egg.
Skip the optional Shaoxing wine and kimchi to cut cost — the dish is still great with just soy and sesame.

substitutions.swap: ground-pork or diced bacon for a cheaper, faster crispy protein
substitutions.savings: ~$4 per batch

substitutions.swap: mirin or dry sherry, or simply omit
substitutions.savings: skip entirely to save

substitutions.savings: uses up leftovers

recipes.name: Pork Tonkatsu
recipes.description: Shatteringly crisp panko-crusted pork cutlets fried until golden, served over steamed rice with shredded cabbage and a tangy-sweet homemade tonkatsu sauce. Ready in just 20 minutes for a Japanese comfort-food classic. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/pork-tonkatsu/

ingredients.note: 8 pork loin steaks (chops), ~1 cm/1/2 inch thick

steps: Lay the pork loin steaks flat on a board and cover with parchment paper. Pound with a mallet or rolling pin to an even ~1 cm (1/2 inch) thickness if needed.
Sprinkle both sides of the pork with the salt and pepper.
Spread the flour on one sheet of parchment and the panko on another. Have the whisked egg ready in a large shallow bowl.
Press both sides of each cutlet into the flour, then into the egg (letting excess drip off), then into the panko, coating all sides evenly. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining pork.
Heat the oil in a large, heavy-based pan over medium-high heat. Once hot, fry the pork in batches for 5-6 minutes until crisp, golden and cooked through, turning every few minutes.
Drain the cooked cutlets on a paper-towel-lined plate.
Make the tonkatsu sauce: stir together the ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce and brown sugar in a small bowl until well combined.
Serve the pork with steamed rice, a side of finely shredded cabbage and a generous drizzle of tonkatsu sauce.
cheapTips: Buy a whole pork loin and slice your own thin cutlets - far cheaper per pound than pre-cut steaks.
The 4-ingredient tonkatsu sauce costs pennies versus bottled - keep ketchup, Worcestershire, soy and brown sugar on hand.
Shallow-fry in a smaller pan with less oil and reuse the strained oil once cooled to stretch your frying budget.

substitutions.swap: pork-cutlet or pork-tenderloin sliced into thin medallions
substitutions.savings: Tenderloin trim is often cheaper and just as tender

substitutions.swap: regular breadcrumbs (less crunchy but works)
substitutions.savings: Saves about $0.05/cup

substitutions.swap: canola-oil or sunflower-oil for frying
substitutions.savings: Canola is typically the cheapest neutral frying oil

recipes.name: Portuguese Chicken Burger
recipes.description: Crispy paprika-crumbed chicken schnitzels tucked into soft buns with melty gouda, creamy mayo, and a drizzle of chilli oil for a quick weeknight burger that beats takeout. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/portuguese-chicken-burger/

ingredients.note: 400g boneless skinless, halved horizontally into thin schnitzels

steps: Place the chicken breast schnitzels on a flat surface, cover with parchment paper, and pound with a mallet or rolling pin to an even thickness, about 1 cm (1/2 inch).
On a large sheet of parchment paper, stir together the breadcrumbs, flour, sea salt flakes, and sweet paprika.
Dredge each piece of chicken in the breadcrumb mixture, coating all sides evenly and shaking off any excess.
Heat a large heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat and spray generously with olive oil.
Cook the chicken for 4-5 minutes until golden and cooked through, turning once halfway and adding more spray oil if needed.
While the chicken rests, lightly toast the burger buns if desired and add a slice of gouda to the hot chicken to melt.
Spread mayonnaise on the buns, pile on shredded lettuce, top with the crumbed chicken and cheese, and finish with chilli oil if using. Serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy a whole chicken breast and slice your own thin schnitzels instead of paying for pre-cut cutlets.
Make your own breadcrumbs by blitzing stale bread, then season the dredge yourself to skip pricey coating mixes.
Swap gouda for any cheese you already have on hand; a basic melting cheese works just as well.

substitutions.swap: Use chicken thighs, pounded thin, for juicier and cheaper schnitzels
substitutions.savings: ~$0.20/serving

substitutions.swap: Use cheddar or any sliced melting cheese you have
substitutions.savings: ~$0.10/serving

substitutions.swap: Use brioche buns for a softer, richer bun

recipes.name: Portuguese-style Chilli Chicken Wrap
recipes.description: Juicy paprika-marinated chicken schnitzels tucked into warm pita with melty gouda, crisp iceberg, and a punchy garlic-ginger chilli sauce. A fast, fiery weeknight wrap that tastes like a takeaway favourite. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/portuguese-style-chilli-chicken-wrap/

ingredients.note: 600g boneless skinless, sliced into thin schnitzels
1 tsp for marinade + more to taste
2 tbsp for chicken + 60ml (4 tbsp) for sauce

steps: Marinate the chicken: in a large bowl, combine the sliced chicken schnitzels with the sweet paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Drizzle with 2 tbsp olive oil and toss to coat.

Cook the chicken on the stovetop: heat a large, heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through. (Air fryer: 200C/400F in a single layer for 8-10 minutes, turning halfway.)
Make the chilli sauce: in a small bowl, stir together the chilli paste/sambal oelek, 60ml olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, minced ginger, caster sugar, and salt and pepper to taste.
Warm the wraps in a dry frying pan or microwave for a few seconds until soft.
Spread a dollop of mayonnaise on each wrap and lay down a slice of gouda.
Top with the hot chicken so the cheese melts slightly.
Add the shredded iceberg lettuce, a generous drizzle of the chilli sauce, and a little extra mayo.
Roll up tightly and serve immediately, with fries on the side if desired.
cheapTips: Swap chicken breast for chicken thighs to cut cost while keeping the meat juicier.
Sambal oelek is the budget hero here; a big jar lasts weeks and powers many marinades and sauces.
Skip store fries and roast a couple of potatoes into wedges for a cheaper side.

substitutions.swap: chicken-thighs
substitutions.savings: ~15% cheaper and more forgiving to cook

substitutions.swap: sriracha or chili-garlic-sauce for a milder, cheaper sauce
swiss-cheese or any melty slice; omit for dairy-free (use dairy-free mayo)

recipes.name: Prawn (Shrimp) Fried Rice
recipes.description: Juicy prawns, fluffy day-old rice and crisp-tender veggies tossed in a glossy tamari-oyster-sesame sauce for a takeout-style fried rice that comes together in 20 minutes. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/prawn-shrimp-fried-rice/

ingredients.note: 1 tbsp, for the prawn marinade (or all-purpose soy sauce)
part of 270g frozen pea, corn and carrot mix
part of 270g frozen pea, corn and carrot mix
part of 270g frozen pea, corn and carrot mix
2 tbsp, for the sauce (or all-purpose soy sauce)
store-bought crispy fried shallots, to garnish
sriracha or chilli sauce, to serve

steps: Place the prawns in a small bowl, add 1 tbsp tamari and toss to coat. Cook immediately rather than leaving to marinate.
Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large, deep, heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the prawns and cook for about 45 seconds per side, until just cooked. Remove and set aside.

Add another tablespoon of oil to the same pan, then the onion, garlic and ginger. Cook 2-3 minutes until fragrant and slightly softened. Stir in the frozen pea, corn and carrot mix briefly to combine.
Push the vegetables to one side, add the last tablespoon of oil to the empty side along with the whisked eggs. Scramble until just set, then stir everything together.
Add the rice, then the 2 tbsp tamari, oyster sauce and sesame oil. Stir until the rice is evenly coated and heated through.
Stir through the sliced spring onions and the cooked prawns. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with extra spring onion and crispy fried shallots if using. Serve with lime wedges and a drizzle of sriracha or chilli sauce, if desired.
cheapTips: Use leftover or day-old rice you already have on hand instead of cooking a fresh batch just for this - it fries up better and costs nothing extra.
A frozen pea, corn and carrot mix is far cheaper than buying each vegetable fresh and there's zero prep or waste.
Swap prawns for frozen shrimp or even scrambled-egg-only to cut the most expensive ingredient while keeping the dish satisfying.

substitutions.savings: skips a specialty bottle

substitutions.swap: frozen shrimp
substitutions.savings: ~$2 per serving cheaper

recipes.name: Quick Beef and Broccoli Noodles
recipes.description: Savory ground beef and tender broccoli tossed with thin egg noodles in a glossy hoisin-soy glaze, all cooked in one pan in just 20 minutes. A weeknight takeout fix that's faster than delivery. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/quick-beef-and-broccoli-noodles/

ingredients.note: 2 tbsp tamari or all-purpose soy sauce

steps: Make the sauce: combine the dark soy sauce, hoisin, and mirin in a small bowl and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the onion and garlic and cook, stirring, for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the ground beef and cook, stirring and breaking it up with a wooden spoon, for 3-4 minutes until browned.
Pour in the sauce and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring, until caramelised.
Add the broccoli florets, cover with a lid, and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Push the beef and broccoli to the outside of the pan to make a well in the centre.

Pour 1 1/2 cups (375 ml) of the water into the well and add the uncooked noodles. Cover and cook without stirring for 1 minute, then flip the noodles and cook another 1 minute, covered, until just pliable.
Using tongs, toss the noodles through the beef and broccoli.
In a small bowl, mix the cornflour with the remaining 1/4 cup (60 ml) of water into a slurry.
Add the slurry to the pan, stir through, and cook, tossing, for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens into a glossy glaze.
Season to taste with the tamari or soy sauce.
Serve scattered with sesame seeds and sliced spring onion, and drizzle with chilli oil if using.
cheapTips: Buy a head of fresh broccoli and use the florets here, saving the stalks for soups or slaws to stretch your money.
Ground beef is the priciest item; swap in ground turkey or pork, or stretch it with extra broccoli and noodles to feed more.
Skip the optional tamari, sesame seeds, and chilli oil if you don't have them on hand. The dish is fully seasoned by the hoisin-soy glaze.

substitutions.swap: Rice wine vinegar with a pinch of sugar
substitutions.savings: Uses a cheaper pantry staple

substitutions.swap: Ground turkey or ground pork
substitutions.savings: Often cheaper per pound than beef

recipes.name: Quick Creamy Miso Chicken Ramen
recipes.description: Crispy golden chicken mince piled over silky miso-and-coconut broth with springy ramen noodles, ready in about 20 minutes. Cozy, savory, and deeply slurpable. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/quick-creamy-miso-chicken-ramen/

ingredients.note: 2 tbsp tamari or all-purpose soy sauce
2 tbsp tamari or all-purpose soy sauce, to taste

steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large heavy-based pan over high heat.
Add the ground chicken and cook 3-4 minutes, breaking it up, until browned all over and any excess moisture has cooked off.
Add the remaining olive oil, the tamari, brown sugar and dark soy (if using). Cook 2-3 minutes until the chicken is crispy and golden, then set aside in a bowl.
To the same pot over medium heat, add the sesame oil, butter, garlic, ginger and the 3 sliced spring onions. Cook, stirring, 1-2 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Add the chicken stock, water, coconut milk, miso paste, the second measure of tamari and the rice wine vinegar.
Bring the broth to a boil. Add the ramen noodles, pushing them under the liquid, and cook 1 minute (or 1 minute less than the packet says), separating them with tongs as they cook.
Season the broth to taste with extra tamari.
Divide the ramen among bowls. Top each with the crispy chicken mince, soft-boiled egg halves, corn, grated carrot, the remaining sliced spring onion, sesame seeds and a drizzle of crispy chilli oil.
cheapTips: Buy a block of fresh ginger and garlic rather than jars and grate as needed; they freeze well and cost a fraction per serving.
Plain instant ramen blocks are cheaper than fresh ramen and work perfectly here; just discard the seasoning packet.
Skip the optional chilli oil and sesame garnish to trim cost without touching the core flavor.

substitutions.swap: Use ground turkey or ground pork for the same crispy mince texture.
substitutions.savings: Ground turkey is often cheaper per ounce

substitutions.swap: Regular soy sauce works in place of tamari.
substitutions.savings: Standard soy sauce is cheaper than tamari

recipes.name: Quick Dumpling Laksa
recipes.description: A speedy, restaurant-worthy laksa built on a fragrant red curry and coconut broth, loaded with juicy dumplings, crunchy bean sprouts, and a bright squeeze of lime. Ready in just 20 minutes for a cozy weeknight bowl. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/quick-dumpling-laksa/

ingredients.note: 20 freezer dumplings (veggie, chicken, pork or prawn)

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and ginger and cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the red curry paste and cook for another minute to release its oils.
Pour in the coconut milk (or cream), chicken stock, fish sauce, and sugar if using. Stir to combine.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then carefully drop in the frozen dumplings. Simmer gently for 5 to 7 minutes, until the dumplings are cooked through.
Add the bok choy for the last 2 minutes of cooking so it stays bright and tender.
Ladle into bowls and top with bean sprouts, coriander, sliced chilli if using, crispy fried shallots, and a squeeze of lime.
cheapTips: Buy a bag of frozen dumplings in bulk and freeze the rest; they're the cheapest way to bulk out this soup.
Use a can of coconut milk instead of cream and stretch it with extra stock for a lighter, lower-cost bowl.
Skip the optional garnishes (fresh chilli and fried shallots) to trim the cost without losing the core flavour.

Coconut cream for a richer, thicker broth

recipes.name: Red Curry Chicken Coconut Noodles
recipes.description: Silky coconut red curry coats tender chicken, crisp veg, and slippery rice noodles for a weeknight dinner that's on the table in 15 minutes. Bright, fragrant, and finished with crushed peanuts and a squeeze of lime. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/red-curry-coconut-noodles/
steps: Cook the rice noodles per packet instructions in boiling water until just softened, about 2-3 minutes. Rinse under cold water and drain.
Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the garlic and ginger and cook, stirring, for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the sliced chicken and cook for 1-2 minutes until it turns from pink to white.
Stir through the tomato paste, then the red curry paste, coating the chicken.
Add the green beans and coconut milk and cook for 2 minutes until the sauce slightly thickens and the beans soften.
Stir in the capsicum and cooked noodles. Cook 1 more minute until heated through.
Serve topped with crushed peanuts and a squeeze of lime.
cheapTips: Buy a whole red bell pepper and chicken breast in bulk packs; portion and freeze the extra for your next stir-fry.
Swap fresh green beans for frozen ones to cut cost and skip the trimming.
A jar of red curry paste lasts many meals, making the per-serving spice cost tiny.

substitutions.savings: Thighs often cost less per pound

substitutions.swap: Frozen green beans or snow peas work equally well
substitutions.savings: Frozen is cheaper and longer-lasting

recipes.name: Red Curry Peanut Noodles
recipes.description: A 15-minute one-pan noodle dish with savory minced pork, creamy coconut-peanut sauce, and a bright hit of lime. Cozy, slurpable, and packed with Thai-inspired flavor. Recipe from Simple Home Edit: https://simplehomeedit.com/recipe/red-curry-peanut-noodles/

ingredients.note: 2 tbsp fresh lime juice (or apple cider / rice wine vinegar)

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-based frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the minced pork (or chicken) for 3-5 minutes until it has changed colour from pink to brown.
Add the shredded cabbage, curry powder and garlic. Cook, stirring, for 1 minute, then stir through the red curry paste and dark soy sauce.
Make a well in the centre of the meat and vegetables and pour in the chicken stock. Once simmering, push the egg noodles into the stock so they are as submerged as possible.
Cook the noodles for 1 minute, flip them, then cover with a lid and cook for a further 1 minute.
Use tongs to separate the noodles, then add the coconut milk, peanut butter and lime juice. Toss to combine and heat through, then remove the pan from the heat.
Serve immediately, sprinkled with crushed peanuts, coriander and fresh chilli, if using. Serve with lime wedges on the side.

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and season generously with the sea salt flakes.

recipes.name: Easy Chana Masala

recipes.name: Easy Stuffed Shells
recipes.description: Tender jumbo pasta shells each cradle a juicy Italian meatball, all blanketed in marinara and gooey melted mozzarella for a weeknight twist on a classic baked pasta. recipes.name: Frittata Florentine

ingredients.note: 1/4 cup finely chopped sweet red pepper

As the eggs begin to set, gently push the cooked edges toward the center so the runny egg flows to the pan. Continue until the eggs are almost set.

Buy a block of mozzarella and shred it yourself to save money over pre-shredded bags.

recipes.name: Grilled Beef & Blue Cheese Sandwiches

recipes.name: Mushroom Grilled Cheese
recipes.description: A loaded, melty grilled cheese where crisped golden portobellos meet a four-cheese blend of brie, sharp cheddar, jack, and nutty gruyere, all tucked between buttery toasted sourdough with a hit of fresh thyme. The outside gets a Parmesan-mayo schmear so it fries up extra crunchy and savory. Recipe from Taste of Home: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/grilled-cheese-and-mushroom-sandwich/

steps: Heat the olive oil with 2 tablespoons of the butter in a large cast-iron or heavy skillet over medium-high. Lay the sliced portobellos in a single layer and cook 10 to 12 minutes, flipping once, until deeply golden and crisping at the edges. Pearl barley is one of the cheapest filling grains around, so lean on it to stretch the pricier sausage further.
Swap in any in-season hardy green like collards or chard for the kale when it's cheaper at your store.

substitutions.swap: pinto-beans or white-beans

substitutions.swap: lacinato-kale or baby-kale

recipes.name: Lemony Chickpeas
recipes.description: Tender chickpeas simmered with onion, tomatoes, and broth, then brightened with a hit of fresh lemon zest and juice over fluffy brown rice. A fast, cozy, and budget-friendly vegan dinner that comes together in half an hour. Recipe from Taste of Home: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/lemony-chickpeas/
steps: Cook the brown rice according to the package directions and set aside.
While the rice cooks, warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and saute the chopped onion for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.
Add the chickpeas, tomatoes with their liquid, broth, red pepper flakes, and black pepper. Bring up to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Uncover and simmer another 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the liquid reduces slightly.
Stir in the lemon zest and lemon juice, then spoon over the cooked rice and serve.
cheapTips: Dried chickpeas cooked from scratch cost a fraction of canned ones if you soak a batch ahead.
Bottled lemon juice is far cheaper than fresh lemons and works perfectly here, with a little zest for aroma.
Buy onions and rice in bulk; they keep for weeks and anchor cheap weeknight dinners.

substitutions.swap: Plain white rice or couscous
substitutions.savings: white rice is cheaper per cup

substitutions.swap: Water with a pinch of salt and a bouillon cube
substitutions.savings: saves about $0.50

substitutions.swap: A splash of white vinegar plus extra zest
substitutions.savings: vinegar is cheaper and shelf-stable

recipes.name: Lemony Tortellini Bacon Salad
recipes.description: Tender cheese tortellini and crisp-tender broccoli get tossed in a bright lemon-balsamic mayo dressing, then piled over fresh spring greens and showered with smoky crumbled bacon for a fast, satisfying main-dish salad. Recipe from Taste of Home: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/lemony-tortellini-bacon-salad/
steps: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil and cook the tortellini per its package timing, dropping the broccoli florets in for the final 5 minutes so they turn crisp-tender.
While the pasta cooks, whisk the mayonnaise, balsamic vinegar, lemon juice, dried oregano, and salt together in a small bowl to make the dressing.
Drain the tortellini and broccoli, then rinse gently under cold water to cool and stop the cooking.
Tip the drained tortellini and broccoli into a large bowl, pour over the dressing, and toss until everything is evenly coated.
Spread the spring mix on plates or a platter, spoon the dressed tortellini and broccoli on top, and finish with the crumbled bacon.
cheapTips: Buy a block of cheese tortellini in bulk and freeze portions; it's cheaper per serving than small fresh packs.
Cook the bacon yourself from a value pack instead of buying pre-cooked bits to cut cost and add more crunch.
Swap the 5 oz spring mix bag for whatever leafy greens are on sale, or use chopped romaine for a budget-friendly base.

substitutions.swap: plain Greek yogurt or a yogurt-mayo blend for a lighter, tangier dressing
substitutions.savings: Cuts fat and often costs less per serving

substitutions.swap: turkey bacon
substitutions.savings: About $0.13 less per slice

substitutions.swap: red wine vinegar with a pinch of sugar

recipes.name: Mahi Mahi & Veggie Skillet
recipes.description: Tender, flaky mahi mahi fillets seared until golden, then nestled over a bright tangle of sweet peppers, mushrooms, and onions simmered in lemon juice. Finished with fresh chives and a scatter of pine nuts, it's a fast, vibrant one-pan dinner. Recipe from Taste of Home: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/mahi-mahi-veggie-skillet/

ingredients.note: large sweet onion, cut into rings

steps: Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the fish fillets and cook until they flake easily, about 4 to 5 minutes per side, then transfer to a plate.
Pour the remaining oil into the pan and add the peppers, mushrooms, onion, lemon juice, and a quarter teaspoon of the salt.
Cover and cook over medium heat, stirring now and then, until the vegetables soften, 6 to 8 minutes.
Lay the fish back on top of the vegetables and season with the pepper and remaining salt.
Cover and cook about 2 more minutes until everything is heated through.
Scatter chives over the top, add pine nuts if using, and serve.
cheapTips: Swap mahi mahi for frozen salmon fillets, which are usually far cheaper and just as good in this skillet.
Buy whole peppers and onions and slice them yourself instead of pre-cut to cut the cost in half.
Skip the pricey pine nuts or use toasted sunflower seeds for a similar crunch at a fraction of the price.

substitutions.swap: frozen salmon or tilapia fillets
substitutions.savings: Save $2-3 per fillet

substitutions.swap: white button mushrooms

substitutions.swap: toasted slivered almonds or sunflower seeds
substitutions.savings: Save $2+ per portion

recipes.name: Meatball Submarine Casserole
recipes.description: All the comfort of a saucy meatball sub baked into a bubbly, cheesy casserole. Toasted garlic-rubbed sourdough soaks up mushroom-studded marinara under a blanket of melty mozzarella and Parmesan. Recipe from Taste of Home: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/meatball-submarine-casserole/

ingredients.note: clove halved, rubbed on toast then discarded

steps: Heat the broiler. Cover the meatballs and microwave on high until hot through, about 4 to 6 minutes.
While they heat, lay the sourdough on a baking sheet and brush one side of each slice with olive oil. Broil a few inches from the heat until golden, 1 to 2 minutes.
Rub the toasted bread with the cut side of the garlic, then discard the garlic. Tear the slices into bite-sized chunks and scatter them in a greased 11x7-inch baking dish.
Drop the oven temperature to 350F.
Toss the hot meatballs with the marinara, half the mozzarella, and half the Parmesan until coated.
Spoon the meatball mixture over the bread, then top with the remaining mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake uncovered until the cheese is melted and bubbly, 15 to 18 minutes. Serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy a bulk bag of frozen meatballs and portion out what you need; the per-piece price drops well below buying fresh.
Use day-old sourdough or any stale bread you have on hand instead of fresh slices to cut waste and cost.
A plain marinara plus a can of cheap mushrooms is far cheaper than a specialty mushroom pasta sauce.

substitutions.swap: plant-based-meatballs for a vegetarian version
substitutions.savings: none, but makes it meat-free

substitutions.swap: any crusty bread or a torn hoagie roll
substitutions.savings: use up bread you already have

substitutions.swap: plain tomato-sauce simmered with sauteed mushrooms
substitutions.savings: about $0.50 per cup

recipes.name: Mediterranean Omelet
recipes.description: A fluffy two-egg omelet folded around tangy feta, juicy tomato, and fresh green onion for a bright, sun-soaked breakfast that comes together in ten minutes flat. Light, savory, and effortlessly elegant. Recipe from Taste of Home: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/mediterranean-omelet/
steps: Whisk the eggs with the water, salt, and pepper until evenly blended.
Melt the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until it coats the pan.
Pour in the egg mixture; the edges should set on contact.
As the eggs cook, gently push the set portions toward the center and tilt the pan so the runny egg flows to the edges.
Keep going until the omelet is thickened and no wet egg remains on top.
Scatter the feta, tomato, and green onion over one half of the omelet.
Fold the empty half over the filling and slide it onto a plate.
Cut in half to serve two.
cheapTips: Buy a block of feta and crumble it yourself; it costs less than pre-crumbled tubs and lasts longer.
Use the white and green parts of the scallion so nothing goes to waste.
Eggs and a pat of butter make this one of the cheapest hot breakfasts you can plate.

substitutions.swap: plant butter or a splash of olive oil

recipes.name: Mediterranean Pork and Orzo
recipes.description: Tender peppered pork tenderloin tossed with orzo, wilted baby spinach, juicy grape tomatoes, and salty feta for a bright, fast Mediterranean dinner that comes together in half an hour. Recipe from Taste of Home: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/mediterranean-pork-and-orzo/
steps: Coat the pork tenderloin all over with the coarse black pepper, then cut it into 1-inch cubes.
Warm the olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the pork and cook, stirring, until no longer pink, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, bring the water to a boil in a large pot. Add the orzo and salt and cook uncovered for 8 minutes.
Stir the spinach into the orzo and cook just until the pasta is tender and the greens wilt, roughly 1 minute more, then drain well.
Add the halved grape tomatoes to the skillet with the pork and toss until warmed through.
Fold in the drained orzo and spinach along with the crumbled feta, then serve right away.
cheapTips: Buy a whole pork tenderloin and trim it yourself instead of pre-cut cubes to save a few dollars per pound.
Swap feta for the store-brand block and crumble it yourself; it costs less than pre-crumbled tubs.
Use frozen spinach when fresh is pricey or out of season, stirring it in until just heated through.

recipes.name: Mediterranean Turkey Skillet
recipes.description: A bright, one-pan weeknight dinner where lean ground turkey simmers with tender zucchini, sweet banana peppers, black beans, and tomatoes, all finished with a splash of balsamic for tangy depth. Hearty, protein-packed, and on the table in half an hour. Recipe from Taste of Home: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/mediterranean-turkey-skillet/

ingredients.note: quartered lengthwise and sliced into half-inch pieces
diced tomatoes, undrained; chop if whole

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.

Add the ground turkey, zucchini, onion, banana peppers, garlic, and oregano. Cook for 10 to 12 minutes, breaking the turkey into crumbles as it browns, until the meat is cooked through and the vegetables soften.
Pour off any excess fat from the pan.
Stir in the black beans, undrained tomatoes, balsamic vinegar, and salt.
Continue cooking, stirring now and then, just until everything is heated through, then serve.
cheapTips: Buy ground turkey in bulk and freeze portions; it's usually cheaper per pound than the pre-packaged trays.
Swap fresh banana peppers for a few spoonfuls of jarred ones to save money and skip the seeding.
Use dried beans cooked from scratch instead of canned for a fraction of the cost.

recipes.name: Moo Shu Mushroom Wraps
recipes.description: A speedy vegetarian take on moo shu: silky scrambled eggs and tender mushrooms tossed with crisp broccoli slaw in a tangy garlic-ginger-soy sauce, then rolled up in hoisin-smeared tortillas. Fresh, savory, and on the table in half an hour. Recipe from Taste of Home: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/moo-shu-mushroom-wraps/
steps: Heat 1 teaspoon of the sesame oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Pour in the beaten eggs and scramble until set with no runny liquid left, then scrape them out onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the same skillet and raise the heat to medium-high. Cook the sliced mushrooms, stirring, until softened.
Stir in the broccoli slaw, garlic, and ginger; cook just 1 to 2 minutes until the slaw is crisp-tender.
Whisk the rice vinegar, soy sauce, and sriracha together in a small bowl, then pour it into the skillet. Fold in the bean sprouts and reserved eggs and toss until heated through.
Smear about 2 teaspoons of hoisin over each warmed tortilla, leaving a small border at the edge.
Spoon roughly 1/2 cup of the filling onto each tortilla, scatter with sliced green onion, and roll up tightly to serve.
cheapTips: Swap the broccoli coleslaw mix for plain shredded cabbage and a handful of grated carrot to cut the cost without losing crunch.
Buy whole mushrooms and slice them yourself; pre-sliced mushrooms usually carry a markup.
Eggs and cabbage do the heavy lifting here, so this is an inexpensive way to stretch a few tortillas into a full dinner.

recipes.name: Lasagna Cups
recipes.description: These adorable individual lasagnas use crisp wonton wrappers in place of noodles, layered with creamy ricotta, melty Italian cheese, and zesty marinara for a fun, hand-held twist on the classic. They bake up golden in a muffin tin and make a crowd-pleasing dinner or party snack. Recipe from Taste of Home: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/muffin-tin-lasagnas/
steps: Heat the oven to 375 F. In a mixing bowl, stir together the beaten egg, ricotta, and about 1-1/4 cups of the Italian cheese blend until combined.
Brush 12 muffin cups generously with olive oil, then press a wonton wrapper into each one.
Spoon roughly 1 tablespoon of the ricotta mixture and 1-1/2 tablespoons of marinara into each wrapper.
Set a second wonton wrapper on top of each, turning it 90 degrees from the first and pressing the center down to form a sturdy cup.
Add another layer of ricotta and marinara to each cup, then scatter the remaining cheese blend over the tops.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and melted.
Let cool a couple of minutes, then garnish with fresh parsley if you like and lift the cups out of the tin.
cheapTips: Wonton wrappers are far cheaper than lasagna noodles and come in big packs, so a single batch costs very little per cup.

recipes.name: Spinach Beef Soup
recipes.description: A hearty one-pot soup where savory browned beef and garlic simmer in a rich tomato-flecked broth, finished with tender bow tie pasta and a flurry of fresh spinach. Cozy, filling, and on the table in half an hour. Recipe from Taste of Home: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/one-pot-spinach-beef-soup/

ingredients.note: diced tomatoes with green pepper, celery and onion, undrained

Pour in the beef broth and undrained tomatoes, then season with basil, oregano, salt and pepper. Bring everything up to a boil.
Add the dry bow tie pasta, return to a boil, and cook uncovered until the pasta is tender, roughly 7 to 9 minutes.
Stir in the chopped spinach and let it wilt into the soup. Ladle into bowls and top with grated Parmesan.
cheapTips: Use 80/20 ground beef and drain it well, or stretch the meat with half a can of beans to cut cost per bowl.
Swap the fresh spinach for frozen spinach, which is far cheaper and keeps in the freezer until you need it.
Plain canned diced tomatoes plus a chopped bell pepper and onion stand in for the pricier seasoned variety.

recipes.name: Chicken Parm Sandwich
recipes.description: Crispy Parmesan-breaded chicken cutlets tucked into toasted rolls with melty provolone and warm marinara, this is comfort-food Italian-American in handheld form. Ready in under half an hour and built for a satisfying lunch or easy weeknight dinner. Recipe from Taste of Home: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/parmesan-chicken-sandwiches/

ingredients.note: boneless skinless, ~5 oz each, pounded to 1/2-inch

steps: Set up a breading station: put the flour in one shallow bowl, the beaten egg in another, and stir the breadcrumbs together with the grated Parmesan in a third.
Pound each chicken breast to an even 1/2-inch thickness, then season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Dredge each cutlet in flour and shake off the excess, dip it through the egg, then press it into the Parmesan-breadcrumb mixture to coat fully.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Cook the chicken about 4 to 5 minutes per side, until the crust is golden brown and the chicken is cooked through with no pink inside.
Optionally toast the split rolls for extra crunch and flavor.
Lay a cutlet in each roll, top with a slice of provolone, and spoon the warm marinara over the top before serving.

Make your own seasoned breadcrumbs from stale bread plus dried Italian herbs instead of buying a box.

recipes.name: Honey-Garlic Pork Chops

steps: Coat a large skillet with cooking spray and heat over medium.
Sear the pork chops until an instant-read thermometer hits 145F, about 5 to 6 minutes per side.
Transfer the chops to a plate and let them rest 5 minutes so the juices redistribute.
Stir together the lemon juice, honey, soy sauce, and minced garlic, then pour into the same hot pan.
Scrape up the browned bits and simmer over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring now and then until the sauce thickens into a glaze.
Loosen with a splash of water if needed, then spoon the sauce over the rested chops (or return them to the pan briefly to coat).
cheapTips: Buy a value pack of bone-in chops and freeze what you don't use; bone-in cuts are usually cheaper than boneless and stay juicier.

It is a fast, elegant skillet dinner that tastes far fancier than its 30-minute timeline. Recipe from Taste of Home: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/pork-medallions-in-mustard-sauce/
steps: Whisk together the chicken broth, apple juice concentrate, and mustard in a small bowl and set aside.
Season the pork medallions on both sides with salt and pepper.

Add the garlic to the same pan and cook for about a minute, then pour in the broth mixture and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom.

recipes.name: Tuna Nicoise Salad
recipes.description: A bright, composed French-style salad piling tender potatoes, crisp-cooked green beans, sliced hard-boiled eggs, flaky tuna, and juicy tomatoes over a bed of romaine, all finished with a zesty lemon-spiked oil-and-vinegar dressing. It comes together fast and eats like a full, satisfying meal. Recipe from Taste of Home: https://www.tasteofhome.com/recipes/quick-nicoise-salad/
steps: Cube the potatoes, add them to a large saucepan, and cover with water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer uncovered until just tender, 8 to 10 minutes.

Drain everything and plunge the potatoes and beans into ice water to stop the cooking; drain again and pat dry.

recipes.name: Tomato-Poached Halibut
recipes.description: Tender halibut fillets gently poached in a smoky, garlicky tomato broth studded with green olives and mild chiles, finished with bright cilantro and a squeeze of lemon. recipes.name: Turkey Biscuit Stew

recipes.name: Zippy Breaded Pork Chops

recipes.name: Rice Cooker Chana Masala
recipes.description: A hearty, deeply spiced chickpea and tomato curry that simmers itself while you do absolutely nothing.

ingredients.note: two 15 oz cans, drained and rinsed

steps: Set the rice cooker to its cook/saute setting. Add the vegetable oil, diced onion, garlic, ginger, and jalapeno if using. Let them soften and turn golden, stirring once or twice, about 8 minutes (if your cooker only has a Cook button, just close the lid and let it run).

Run a full cook cycle. When it clicks off, stir, then run a second cook cycle to let the curry thicken and the flavors deepen, roughly 20 to 25 minutes total of simmering.
If it looks too thick, stir in a splash of water; if too thin, run a few more minutes with the lid cracked. Mash a few chickpeas against the side to thicken the sauce naturally.
Switch to Keep Warm, stir in the lemon juice, and taste for salt. Top with fresh cilantro and serve over rice.
cheapTips: Dried chickpeas cost a fraction of canned. Soak overnight, then cook a batch in the rice cooker with water and freeze portions.
Buy whole spices in bulk-bin quantities and grind as needed. They are cheaper and last far longer than pre-ground jars.
This curry tastes even better the next day, so double the batch for nearly free meal-prep lunches.

When the rice cycle finishes and clicks to warm, fluff the rice, set the heatproof plate of fish directly on top of the hot rice (or on the steam tray if you have one), close the lid, and run a SECOND cook cycle for 12-15 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Carefully lift out the fish plate, pour off any watery liquid, and drizzle the soy sauce, sugar, and a splash of the fish steaming liquid over the fillets; scatter the sliced scallion greens on top.

Heat the vegetable oil and sesame oil together for 30-40 seconds in the microwave (or briefly in the rice cooker pot) until very hot, then pour it sizzling over the scallions and ginger to bloom their aroma.
Top with fresh cilantro and serve the fish over the steamed rice, spooning the pan sauce across both.
cheapTips: Frozen white fish fillets are far cheaper than fresh and steam just as tender straight from thawed.
Use the whole scallion: smash the white parts under the fish for flavor and save the green tops for the sizzle garnish.
