Add the butter, soy sauce, sesame oil, and sugar. Stir until the butter fully melts and coats every grain in a glossy, savory sauce. Taste and add a splash more soy if you want it saltier.
Scoop into bowls and top with sliced scallion, toasted sesame seeds, a sprinkle of gochugaru, and crumbled nori if using. Eat right away while hot.
cheapTips: Plain rice and eggs are two of the cheapest dorm staples, so this bowl lands well under a dollar a serving even before toppings.
Skip the garnishes if money's tight, the butter-soy-sesame trio is the real flavor and works on its own.
Buy a big bag of jasmine rice and a dozen eggs at once and you can make this same bowl a dozen mornings in a row for almost nothing.

substitutions.swap: Any leftover cooked white rice, reheated in the cooker on Keep Warm until steaming hot before adding the eggs
substitutions.savings: Uses up leftovers for free

substitutions.swap: Equal amount of tamari for a gluten-free, slightly richer salt hit
substitutions.savings: About the same cost

substitutions.swap: Plant butter for a dairy-free bowl with the same melty richness
substitutions.savings: Saves a few cents per tbsp

recipes.name: Rice Cooker Pumpkin Coconut Sweet Rice
recipes.description: Cubes of pumpkin steam right on top of sticky sweet rice until they collapse and melt into the grains, turning everything gold, creamy, and naturally sweet with rich coconut milk. It's a cozy one-pot snack that tastes way fancier than its tiny price tag, and your whole room will smell incredible. Inspired by a viral rice-cooker trend on Reddit.

ingredients.note: glutinous/sticky rice; rinse until water runs mostly clear

steps: Rinse 1.5 cups sweet rice in the rice cooker pot 2-3 times, swirling with your hand and pouring off the cloudy water until it runs mostly clear, then drain well. If you have 20 extra minutes, cover the rinsed rice with water, soak, and drain again for an even softer, stickier result.
Add the whole can of coconut milk, the water, brown sugar, sugar, salt, and cinnamon (if using). Stir until the sugar dissolves, then spread the rice into an even layer under the liquid.
Scatter the cubed pumpkin evenly over the top of the rice. Don't stir it in: let the pieces rest on the surface so they steam while the rice cooks underneath.
Close the lid and run the normal White Rice cycle. The cooker simmers the rice and gently steams the pumpkin until it is fork-tender, about 30-40 minutes.
When the cycle ends, keep the lid closed and let it sit on Keep Warm for 10 minutes so the rice finishes plumping and the pumpkin softens fully.

Open the lid and gently fold everything together: the soft pumpkin will break down and melt into the rice, turning it gold and creamy. Stir in a splash more coconut milk or water if you want it looser.
Taste. If it's a touch thin or undercooked, close the lid and run Keep Warm for another 5-10 minutes; if it's too sweet, stir in a small pinch of salt to balance.
Spoon into bowls and top with toasted coconut flakes and pepitas if you have them. Serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy a wedge of pumpkin or kabocha by weight instead of a whole one. You only need about 2 cups cubed, and it's cheaper than canned puree.
Sweet rice (glutinous rice) is one of the cheapest grains per bag at any Asian market and keeps for months in your dorm, so a single bag makes this snack many times over.
Save the rest of the coconut milk can in the fridge for up to 4 days and use it in oatmeal, curry, or a second batch so nothing goes to waste.

substitutions.swap: Use sweet-potato cubes or butternut squash; both steam down sweet and gold the same way.
substitutions.savings: Sweet potato can be cheaper per pound when pumpkin is out of season

substitutions.swap: Swap in coconut-cream for a richer pudding-like result, or whole-milk for a lighter, non-coconut version.
substitutions.savings: Whole milk is much cheaper than a can of coconut milk

substitutions.swap: Regular jasmine-rice works in a pinch; it'll be a little less sticky but still creamy.
substitutions.savings: Use whatever rice is already in your cabinet

recipes.name: Rice Cooker Loaded Egg and Veggie Ramen
recipes.description: The quintessential dorm glow-up: a packet of instant ramen simmered with real vegetables until the broth goes rich and savory, then a cracked-in egg poaches right in the bubbling pot. Cheap, fast, deeply comforting, and entirely no-stove. Inspired by a viral rice-cooker ramen trend on TikTok.

ingredients.note: discard the seasoning packet or use half for less sodium
carrots, peas, corn mix — no chopping or thawing needed
thinly sliced, white and green parts kept separate
stir in at the end to wilt

steps: Add the water, minced garlic, and frozen veg to the rice cooker bowl. Close the lid and start the Cook / White Rice cycle to bring the broth to a simmer (no need to thaw the veg first).

Once the water is steaming and bubbling, about 4-5 minutes, drop in the ramen brick and the white parts of the sliced scallion. Press the noodles down with a fork or chopsticks so they stay submerged.
Let it simmer on the cycle for about 3 minutes, gently loosening the noodles as they soften.
Stir in the soy sauce and sesame oil. If using, add the spinach now so it wilts into the hot broth.

Make a small well in the center of the noodles and crack the egg directly into the bubbling broth. Close the lid and let it poach undisturbed for 3-4 minutes — keep it on Cook for a firmer white, or switch to Keep Warm for a softer, jammier yolk.
Open the lid and check the egg: the white should be fully set and opaque, the yolk still runny. Give it another 1-2 minutes on Cook if you like the yolk firmer.
Pour everything into a bowl. Top with the green scallion slices, a squeeze of sriracha, and a sprinkle of sesame seeds. Slurp immediately.
cheapTips: Skip the dusty ramen seasoning packet and build flavor with soy sauce, garlic, and sesame oil instead — cheaper per bowl and way less sodium.
A bag of frozen mixed veg is the dorm MVP: pennies per cup, never goes bad, and zero chopping or washing.
Buy ramen by the multipack and eggs by the dozen — this whole bowl lands well under a dollar when you stock up.

substitutions.swap: Use frozen-broccoli or frozen-corn if that's what's in your freezer
substitutions.savings: about the same cost, uses what you have

substitutions.swap: Swap in rice-noodles or udon for a slurpier bowl
substitutions.savings: ramen is cheapest, but udon feels like takeout

substitutions.swap: Cube in tofu instead of poaching an egg for a vegan bowl
substitutions.savings: tofu costs a bit more but adds more protein

recipes.name: Rice Cooker Creamy Parmesan Polenta
recipes.description: Luxuriously creamy, cheesy polenta with a silky parmesan finish — pure Italian comfort in a bowl, with no constant stovetop stirring required. The rice cooker does the work while you study, then you fold in cheese and butter for that glossy, restaurant-worthy texture. Inspired by a viral rice-cooker polenta trend on TikTok.
steps: Lightly grease the inner pot of the rice cooker with a thin smear of butter or a wipe of oil so the cornmeal doesn't stick. Add the cornmeal, chicken broth, water, and 2 smashed garlic cloves, then whisk until there are no dry lumps.

Whisk in the salt and pepper, close the lid, and run the normal White Rice cycle. After about 8 to 10 minutes, open the lid and whisk hard for 15 seconds to keep the polenta smooth and lift any grain settling on the bottom.

Whisk again about 10 minutes later. The mixture should look thick, glossy, and creamy with no raw, gritty bite. If it still tastes grainy, add a splash of the milk and let the cycle keep running until tender.
When the cycle finishes or clicks to Keep Warm, pour in the whole milk and whisk until the polenta loosens into a smooth, pourable cream. Fish out the smashed garlic cloves.
On Keep Warm, fold in the parmesan and butter, stirring until both fully melt and the polenta turns silky and rich. Taste and add more salt or pepper as needed.
If it stiffens while sitting, whisk in a little hot water or milk, a splash at a time, to bring back the loose, creamy texture. Spoon into bowls.
Finish each bowl with a drizzle of olive oil, a little extra parmesan, and a sprinkle of fresh parsley if you have it. Serve right away while hot and creamy.
cheapTips: Cornmeal is one of the cheapest grains in the store — a single bag makes many batches, so this dish costs pennies per serving even loaded with cheese.
Swap the chicken broth for water plus a crumbled bouillon cube or a spoon of chicken bouillon to get the same savory depth for a fraction of the price.
Buy a wedge of parmesan and grate it yourself instead of the pre-shredded tubs — it's cheaper per ounce, melts creamier, and keeps for weeks in the fridge.

substitutions.swap: Use water plus a bouillon-cube, or veggie-broth, to make it fully vegetarian
substitutions.savings: saves about $2 per batch

substitutions.swap: Pecorino-romano or a sharp cheddar block melts in just as creamy
substitutions.savings: often cheaper per serving

substitutions.swap: Heavy cream for extra richness, or oat-milk to keep it dairy-light
substitutions.savings: use whatever's already in your fridge

recipes.name: Rice Cooker Cheesy Jalapeno Cornbread
recipes.description: Golden, moist cornbread loaded with melty cheddar and a real kick of fresh jalapeno, baked right in your rice cooker so it comes out tender and pull-apart soft. Perfect torn into a bowl of chili or grabbed warm straight from the pot for a dorm crowd. Inspired by a viral rice-cooker cornbread trend on Instagram Reels.

ingredients.note: thawed; folds in for sweet pops of corn
drizzle on top once it's done

steps: Spray the rice cooker bowl well with cooking spray, bottom and a couple inches up the sides, so the cornbread releases cleanly. Drop the butter into the bowl and set the cooker to Keep Warm for 3-4 minutes to melt it, then pour the melted butter into a large mixing bowl and quickly wipe the cooker bowl with a paper towel.
In a separate bowl, stir together the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt until evenly combined with no dry clumps.
Whisk the milk and eggs into the melted butter, then pour this wet mix into the dry ingredients. Stir just until you have a thick, lumpy batter; don't overmix or the cornbread turns tough.

Finely chop the jalapenos (scrape out the seeds for less heat, or leave them in for a real kick) and shred or finely cube the cheddar. Fold the jalapenos, most of the cheese, and the thawed corn (if using) into the batter, saving a small handful of cheese for the top.
Scrape the batter into the greased cooker bowl, smooth the top, and scatter the reserved cheese over it. Close the lid and run the standard White Rice / Cook cycle.

When the cycle clicks over to Keep Warm, leave the lid closed for 10 minutes, then poke the center with a chopstick. If it comes out with wet batter, run a second Cook cycle and check again. It's done when the center springs back and a tester comes out clean.

Set the cooker to Keep Warm for 5 minutes to firm the edges, then run a butter knife around the rim and invert the bowl onto a plate (or lift the cornbread out by the edges). Drizzle with honey if you like, slice into wedges, and serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy a block of cheddar instead of pre-shredded bags; it's cheaper per ounce, melts better, and you control how much goes in.
Cornmeal and flour are pantry staples that cost pennies per batch, so this whole pan of cornbread feeds six for well under two dollars.
One fresh jalapeno goes a long way; buy a couple and freeze the extras, since they chop straight from frozen for the next batch.

substitutions.swap: Use pickled-jalapenos from a jar (drained and chopped) for a tangier, milder kick and zero chopping fuss.
substitutions.savings: Roughly the same cost, and the jar keeps for months so nothing goes to waste.

substitutions.swap: Swap in almond-milk or oat-milk to make it dairy-light; the batter behaves the same.
substitutions.savings: About the same price; handy if you keep plant milk on hand instead of dairy.

substitutions.swap: Use shredded mozzarella for an even gooier, milder cheese pull.
substitutions.savings: Saves around $0.15 per ounce versus block cheddar.

recipes.name: Rice Cooker Honey-Poached Spiced Pears
recipes.description: Tender pears bathed in a glossy honey-and-spice syrup, gently poached until they glisten like something off a fancy restaurant dessert cart. It smells like cinnamon and warm orange and is secretly a hands-off rice-cooker job you can pull off in a dorm with no stovetop. Inspired by a viral rice-cooker dessert trend on Instagram Reels.

ingredients.note: firm but ripe; halved and cored
about 3 whole cloves' worth of ground; fish them out if using whole
a cool dollop on the side

steps: Peel the pears if you like (the skin is fine to leave on). Slice each in half lengthwise and scoop out the core and seeds with a spoon. Lay the halves cut-side down in the rice cooker bowl so they sit snugly in a single layer.
Pour the apple juice and water over the pears, then drizzle the honey across the top. Squeeze in the juice from the lemon half — this keeps the pears from browning and balances the sweetness.

Add the cinnamon, ground ginger, cloves, vanilla, and the star anise if using. Gently stir the liquid around the pears so the spices spread out; the pears should sit about halfway submerged in the spiced honey bath.

Close the lid and run the normal White Rice cycle. As it heats, the cooker brings the liquid to a low simmer and poaches the pears — no stovetop needed. If your cooker has a Porridge or Slow Cook setting, that works even better.
About 15 minutes in, carefully open the lid and either spoon syrup over the tops of the pears or flip them so both sides take on color and flavor. Close and let the cycle continue.

When the cycle ends and switches to Keep Warm, leave the pears in for another 15-20 minutes. The gentle heat finishes softening them until a fork slides in easily and the edges look glossy and slightly translucent.

Lift the pears into bowls. For a thicker syrup, leave the remaining liquid on Keep Warm with the lid open for another 10-15 minutes to reduce, then spoon it over the pears. Remove any whole star anise and cloves first.
Top with chopped walnuts and a dollop of Greek yogurt if using, and serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy firmer, slightly underripe pears — they're often cheaper, hold their shape better when poached, and won't turn to mush.
Apple juice makes the poaching liquid taste 'fancy,' but plain water plus an extra tablespoon of honey works just as well if that's all you have.
Skip the fresh garnishes and lean on pantry spices — a 30-cent hit of cinnamon does more for this dessert than $4 of toppings.

substitutions.swap: Use orange juice, or plain water with an extra drizzle of honey
substitutions.savings: Water is free if you're broke

substitutions.swap: Maple syrup or brown sugar both poach beautifully and taste just as cozy
substitutions.savings: Brown sugar is much cheaper per serving

substitutions.swap: Firm apples work just as well and poach in about the same time
substitutions.savings: Apples are often on sale by the bag

recipes.name: Rice Cooker Cajun Red Beans & Rice
recipes.description: Smoky, creamy, and deeply savory, this one-pot Cajun classic turns a few cheap pantry cans into a soul-warming dinner that feeds the whole apartment. The rice cooker melds smoked sausage, red beans, and the Cajun "holy trinity" of onion, celery, and bell pepper into pure comfort with zero stovetop fuss. Inspired by a viral rice-cooker trend on TikTok.

ingredients.note: andouille if you can find it; sliced into coins

steps: If your cooker has a Saute or Cook setting, switch it on, add the vegetable oil, and brown the sliced smoked sausage for 4-5 minutes until the edges crisp. No saute mode? Skip the browning — the sausage is already fully cooked, so just add it raw with everything else in step 4.

If you browned the sausage, add the diced onion, celery, bell pepper, and garlic and saute 4-5 minutes until softened, scraping up any browned bits. Otherwise just have the diced vegetables ready to add in the next step.
Rinse the 2 cups of rice in a strainer until the water runs clear and drain well, then add it to the cooker pot.

Drain and rinse both cans of red beans and add them. Add the diced onion, celery, bell pepper, and garlic (if not already in), the chicken broth, Cajun seasoning, smoked paprika, and the bay leaf. Stir so the rice is evenly submerged and level, with the liquid sitting just above the rice.
Close the lid and run the normal White Rice cycle. Let it cook fully undisturbed so the rice steams while the broth turns creamy and smoky.
When the cycle ends, leave the lid closed and let it rest on Keep Warm for 10 minutes so the flavors set and any extra liquid absorbs.

Open the lid and check the rice is tender all the way through (no chalky center); if it still has a bite, add a splash of broth or water, stir, and run another 5-10 minutes on Keep Warm. Fish out the bay leaf, then fluff and stir, mashing a few beans against the side for extra creaminess.
Taste and add more Cajun seasoning or a pinch of salt if needed. Scoop into bowls and top with sliced scallions, fresh parsley, and a few dashes of hot sauce.
cheapTips: Red beans are one of the cheapest cans on the shelf — buy a few when they're on sale and this becomes a sub-$1.50-per-bowl dinner.
No Cajun seasoning? Mix your own from pantry staples: smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, oregano, and salt. Cheaper and you control the heat.
Stretch it further by leaning on the beans instead of more sausage — beans are the cheapest protein here and the leftovers taste even better the next day.

substitutions.swap: Use sliced kielbasa, spam, or even bacon for the same smoky punch
substitutions.savings: Spam runs cheaper per serving and keeps forever in the cupboard

substitutions.swap: Kidney beans or pinto beans work just as well
substitutions.savings: Both are the same ~$1.10/can and often more available

substitutions.swap: Dissolve a bouillon cube in 2.5 cups water instead
substitutions.savings: A box of bouillon cubes costs pennies per cup vs. canned broth

recipes.name: Rice Cooker Spanakorizo (Greek Spinach Rice)
recipes.description: Silky, lemon-bright spinach rice that melts a whole bag of greens into creamy, risotto-soft grains — vegetarian comfort food with fresh dill, good olive oil, and a salty crumble of feta on top. It tastes like something your Greek grandma simmered for an hour, but the rice cooker does all the work in one pot. Inspired by a viral rice-cooker spanakorizo trend on TikTok.

ingredients.note: medium- or long-grain white rice, rinsed
fresh, roughly chopped (about a standard bag); it cooks way down
or water plus a bouillon cube; the spinach also releases water as it wilts
juiced at the end, plus wedges to serve

steps: Optional but worth it: set the rice cooker to Cook or Saute, add the olive oil, diced onion, and garlic, and stir occasionally for 4-5 minutes until softened and fragrant. No Saute setting? Skip this and just stir the raw onion, garlic, and oil straight into the pot in the next steps — it still works.
Rinse the rice under cold water until it runs mostly clear, then add it to the pot.

Pile in the chopped spinach — it will look like far too much, but it wilts down to almost nothing. Add the dill, salt, and pepper (and the raw onion, garlic, and oil now if you skipped the saute step).

Pour in the veggie broth and stir so the rice is evenly spread under the liquid and greens. If your cooker tends to run wet, hold back about 1/4 cup of the broth — the spinach adds moisture as it cooks.
Close the lid and run the normal White Rice cycle. Let it go without lifting the lid so the spinach steams down into the grains.
When the cycle ends, leave the lid on and let it sit on Keep Warm for 8-10 minutes to finish absorbing and turn creamy.
Fluff gently with a fork, then squeeze in the fresh lemon juice and stir. Taste and adjust with more salt or lemon as needed.
Spoon into bowls, crumble feta over the top, and finish with lemon zest, sliced scallion, and a lemon wedge on the side.
cheapTips: Frozen spinach is cheaper than fresh and works great here — swap in about 2 cups frozen (thawed and squeezed dry) and you'll barely notice the difference.
Skip the bottled broth: dissolve a bouillon cube in 3 cups of water instead. It's a fraction of the cost and the dill and lemon carry the flavor.
Feta is the splurge, so treat it as a finishing touch, not a filler — a little crumbled on top goes further than stirring a whole block through.

substitutions.swap: Use about 2 cups frozen spinach (thawed and well drained) for a lower-price, zero-prep option
substitutions.savings: saves about $4 vs a fresh bag

substitutions.swap: Use water plus a crumbled bouillon cube
substitutions.savings: saves about $2

substitutions.swap: Use 1.5 tsp dried dill stirred in before cooking
substitutions.savings: cheaper and keeps in the cupboard

recipes.name: Rice Cooker Mediterranean Farro Pilaf
recipes.description: Chewy, nutty farro simmers right in your rice cooker, then gets folded with bright lemon, fresh herbs, chickpeas, and sweet-tart dried fruit for a hearty grain bowl that eats like a meal-prep dream. It's higher in fiber and way more satisfying than plain rice, and it keeps beautifully all week. Inspired by a viral rice-cooker trend on TikTok.

ingredients.note: chopped, folded in at the end

steps: Rinse the 1.5 cups farro in a strainer under cold water for about 30 seconds, then tip it into the rice cooker pot. Rinsing washes off dusty surface starch so the grains stay separate and chewy instead of gummy.

Add the 2 tbsp olive oil, 3 minced garlic cloves, and the finely diced half red onion on top of the farro. If your cooker has a Cook or Saute setting, run it 2-3 minutes and stir to soften the aromatics; if it doesn't, just skip ahead — the dish still works.
Pour in the 3 cups veggie broth plus 3/4 cup water (roughly the 2.5-to-1 liquid ratio farro needs), then stir in the 1 tsp oregano, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp pepper. Close the lid.

Set the cooker to the Brown Rice or Whole Grain cycle and let it run — no stovetop, no oven, the cooker does all the work. This takes about 45-50 minutes, until the farro is tender with a little bite.
When the cycle ends, leave the lid closed and let it rest on Keep Warm for 10 minutes so the last of the liquid absorbs and the grains finish steaming.

Fluff the farro with a fork, then fold in the drained chickpeas, chopped dried apricots, and dried cranberries. Close the lid for 5 more minutes on Keep Warm to gently warm the chickpeas and plump the fruit.
Fold in the lemon zest and a big squeeze of fresh lemon juice, then taste and adjust salt. Top each portion with chopped parsley and mint, crumbled feta, and slivered almonds if using.
Let it cool, then divide into 4 containers. It keeps in the fridge up to 5 days and tastes great cold or gently rewarmed — an ideal grab-and-go meal-prep bowl.
cheapTips: Buy farro from the bulk bin and scoop just what you need — it's a fraction of the price of boxed grains and stores for months in a jar.
Swap the veggie broth for water plus a bouillon cube or a teaspoon of chicken bouillon; you get the same savory depth for pennies.
If you're broke, skip the fresh herbs — an extra pinch of dried oregano plus more lemon does most of the heavy lifting for brightness.

substitutions.swap: Use barley or bulgur instead — both cook chewy in the rice cooker and cost even less per cup.
substitutions.savings: ~$0.25 per batch

substitutions.swap: Use plain water with a bouillon cube dissolved in it.
substitutions.savings: ~$1.50 per batch

substitutions.swap: Use raisins, which are cheaper and add the same sweet-tart pop.
substitutions.savings: ~$0.45 per batch

recipes.name: Rice Cooker Bulking Chicken & Rice Meal Prep
recipes.description: The bodybuilder cheat code: cubed chicken, fluffy rice, and veg all cook together in one rice cooker cycle, giving you four high-protein, macro-friendly meal-prep boxes for the week with mostly hands-off time. Set it, forget it, portion it, gain. Inspired by Animal Pak's easy rice cooker chicken and rice (https://www.animalpak.com/blogs/fitness-bodybuilding/bulk-gains-in-a-bowl-evan-s-easy-rice-cooker-chicken-rice).

ingredients.note: cut into even 3/4-inch cubes so they cook through
rinsed until the water runs mostly clear
or 3 cups water plus a bouillon cube
mixed peas, carrots, corn, green beans; no need to thaw
drizzle over portions for flavor; contains gluten, so skip it (or use tamari) to keep boxes gluten-free

steps: Add 2 cups jasmine rice to the rice cooker pot and rinse under cold water, swirling and draining, until the water runs mostly clear. Drain well. This keeps the meal-prep rice fluffy instead of gummy.
In a bowl, toss the 3/4-inch chicken cubes with the salt, pepper, garlic-powder, onion-powder, paprika, and minced garlic until every piece is evenly coated.
Spread the drained rice in an even layer in the pot, pour in the 3 cups chicken broth, and drizzle the 2 tbsp olive oil over the top. Stir once so the rice is level and submerged.

Scatter the seasoned chicken cubes evenly over the rice, then tip the frozen veg straight from the bag on top. Do not stir after this, so the rice cooks evenly underneath while the chicken and veg steam above.
Close the lid and run a full White Rice cycle. The cooker steams the chicken and veg while the rice absorbs the seasoned broth, all in one shot.
When the cycle ends, leave the lid closed on Keep Warm for 10 minutes to finish cooking the chicken through and let the rice set.

Open and check the chicken: cut into a couple of the largest cubes to confirm they are opaque all the way through with no pink (165F). If any pieces are still pink or rice at the bottom looks wet, close the lid and run a short second cycle or 10 more minutes on Keep Warm, then check again.

Stir everything together so the seasoning and chicken juices fold through the rice. Divide into 4 meal-prep containers, top with optional scallion, soy sauce, and sriracha, then cool and refrigerate up to 4 days.
cheapTips: Buy chicken breast in a family-size pack and freeze it in portions; the per-meal cost drops hard when you split a bulk pack across several preps.
Swap the chicken broth for water plus a 25-cent bouillon cube and you still get the savory backbone for a fraction of the price.
Frozen mixed veg is cheaper than fresh, never wilts in your dorm fridge, and goes straight in with zero chopping or waste.

substitutions.swap: chicken-thighs for juicier meat that is harder to dry out on reheat
substitutions.savings: about $0.20 cheaper per serving and stays tender

substitutions.swap: plain long-grain rice or brown rice for more fiber (add a splash more broth for brown rice)
substitutions.savings: plain rice is the cheapest grain in the catalog

substitutions.swap: water plus a bouillon cube
substitutions.savings: cuts the liquid cost to roughly a quarter

recipes.name: Rice Cooker Korean Tuna Mayo Rice Bowl (Chamchi Deopbap)
recipes.description: Fluffy hot rice straight from the cooker, piled with creamy canned tuna whipped into tangy Kewpie mayo, finished with a drizzle of nutty sesame oil and crispy crumbled gim for around 30g of protein in minutes. It's the ultimate no-stovetop dorm dinner: the rice cooker does all the work while the topping comes together in a single bowl. Inspired by a viral rice-cooker tuna-mayo trend on TikTok.

ingredients.note: rinsed until the water runs clear
Japanese-style mayo; richer and tangier than regular
split: 1 tsp in the tuna, 1 tsp over the rice
or stir in gochujang, for heat
gim/seaweed, crumbled or cut into thin strips

steps: Add the rinsed jasmine rice and water to the rice cooker pot. If you want the optional egg topper, crack the eggs into a small heatproof cup or foil cup and nestle it on top of the rice now so it steams as the rice cooks. Close the lid and run a normal White Rice cycle until it switches to Keep Warm (about 25-30 minutes).

While the rice cooks, make the topping: in a bowl, flake the well-drained tuna with a fork, then stir in the Kewpie mayo, soy sauce, 1 tsp of the sesame oil, the sugar, and the sriracha if using. Mix until creamy, then taste and adjust. Set aside.

When the cycle finishes, lift out the egg cup; the whites and yolk should be fully set and cooked through (if they look at all runny, close the lid and steam a few minutes more on the cook setting). Then fluff the rice with the paddle.
Spoon the hot rice into two bowls and drizzle the remaining 1 tsp sesame oil over the top.
Spoon the creamy tuna mayo generously over each bowl of rice.
Scatter the sliced scallions, crumbled gim (nori), and toasted sesame seeds over the top, and add the steamed egg if you made one.
Mix everything together right before eating so the warm rice loosens the mayo into a silky sauce, and dig in while it's hot.
cheapTips: Canned tuna and jasmine rice are pantry staples that cost pennies per serving, so buy the tuna in multipacks when it's on sale and stock up.
No Kewpie mayo? Regular mayonnaise plus a tiny splash of rice vinegar and a pinch of sugar mimics that tangy-sweet flavor for a fraction of the price.
Skip the egg and fancy garnishes when money's tight, the tuna-mayo-on-rice base alone is a filling, satisfying meal.

substitutions.swap: Regular mayonnaise with a few drops of rice vinegar and a pinch of sugar
substitutions.savings: ~$0.05 per bowl

substitutions.swap: Canned salmon or canned chicken for a different protein
substitutions.savings: spend a bit more for variety

substitutions.swap: Plain white rice or sushi rice, cooked the same way
substitutions.savings: ~$0.03 per cup

recipes.name: Greek Yogurt Protein Pancakes
recipes.description: Fluffy, satisfying pancakes blended from rolled oats and Greek yogurt — no flour needed, naturally high in protein and ready in under 15 minutes.
steps: Blend rolled oats in a blender or food processor until a coarse flour forms.
Add eggs, Greek yogurt, honey, vanilla, baking powder, and cinnamon to the blender and blend until smooth. Rest the batter 3 minutes.
Heat a nonstick pan over medium heat and brush with a thin layer of oil.
Pour roughly ¼ cup batter per pancake, cook 2–3 minutes until bubbles form across the surface and edges look set.
Flip and cook another 1–2 minutes. Serve warm with fresh fruit or a drizzle of maple syrup.
cheapTips: Rolled oats are one of the cheapest protein bases per gram
Greek yogurt on sale can cut the cost under $0.40/serving

substitutions.swap: Maple syrup or mashed banana for natural sweetness
Cooking spray to cut ~60 kcal/batch

recipes.name: Savory Cottage Cheese Power Toast
recipes.description: Thick-scooped cottage cheese on toasted whole-grain bread, loaded with sliced tomato, fresh spinach, and a crack of black pepper — a 5-minute, 36-gram-protein breakfast.
steps: Toast bread to your preferred level of crispness.
Spread 1 serving (½ cup) of cottage cheese generously on each slice.
Layer fresh spinach leaves on top, followed by thin tomato slices.
Drizzle with a small amount of olive oil, season with salt, pepper, and optional red pepper flakes.
Eat immediately while the toast is still warm.
cheapTips: Cottage cheese is one of the cheapest protein sources per gram — about $0.30/serving
Spinach from a bag is far cheaper than pre-washed mini-containers

substitutions.swap: Any leafy green you have — arugula, romaine, or kale work great
Skip entirely and use a squeeze of lemon instead

recipes.name: Meal-Prep Turkey Egg Muffin Cups
recipes.description: Twelve savory egg muffins packed with ground turkey, bell pepper, spinach, and a whisper of cheese — made on Sunday, grabbed all week.
steps: Preheat oven to 375 °F (190 °C). Mist a 12-cup muffin tin generously with cooking spray.
Brown ground turkey in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up. Add garlic, diced onion, and bell pepper; cook 3 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in spinach and cook until wilted. Remove from heat.
Crack all 8 eggs into a large bowl, whisk until combined. Stir in the turkey-vegetable mixture and shredded cheese.
Divide the mixture evenly among the 12 muffin cups — about ⅓ cup each.
Bake 18–22 minutes until the centers are fully set and the tops are lightly golden.
Cool 5 minutes before removing. Refrigerate in an airtight container up to 5 days; reheat 30–45 seconds in a microwave.
cheapTips: Frozen spinach (thawed, squeezed dry) saves money and works perfectly here
This batch costs about $0.50 per muffin at mid-range grocery prices

substitutions.swap: Lean ground chicken or crumbled tofu for vegetarian version
Any vegetable that will fit — mushrooms, zucchini, or frozen corn

recipes.storageInstructions: Fridge up to 5 days or freeze up to 2 months.
recipes.reheatingInstructions: Microwave 30–45 s from fridge; 90 s from frozen.

recipes.name: Protein-Packed Overnight Oats
recipes.description: Creamy overnight oats stirred together in 3 minutes, with Greek yogurt and a scoop of protein powder — pull them from the fridge at 7 a.m. and get 28 grams of protein before you leave the house.
steps: In a jar or container with a lid, combine oats, Greek yogurt, milk, protein powder, honey, and vanilla.
Stir vigorously until protein powder is fully incorporated and there are no lumps.
Top with frozen berries (they thaw overnight, becoming jammy and sweet).
Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight.
Stir well before eating. Add a splash more milk if you prefer a looser consistency.
cheapTips: Make 5 jars on Sunday — each jar takes 3 minutes and costs about $1.20

substitutions.swap: Any plant milk for dairy-free
Extra ¼ cup Greek yogurt — less protein but still great

recipes.name: Smashed White Bean Avocado Toast
recipes.description: Creamy white beans smashed with lemon and garlic, spread over toast alongside mashed avocado — a hearty plant-based breakfast with 22 grams of protein and 12 grams of fiber.
steps: Drain and rinse white beans. In a bowl, combine beans with a minced garlic clove, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Smash with a fork until mostly smooth with some texture remaining.
In a second bowl, mash the avocado with salt, a squeeze of lemon, and red pepper flakes.
Toast the bread slices.
Spread half the white bean mixture on two slices, then half the avocado on the other two — or layer both on each slice.
Sprinkle with extra red pepper flakes and eat immediately.
cheapTips: A can of white beans at $1.10 is one of the most protein-dense cheap foods available
Use whichever avocado is on sale — ripe avocados are often discounted

substitutions.swap: Chickpeas or cannellini beans for slightly different texture
Extra white bean spread if avocados are expensive

recipes.name: Spinach Mushroom Egg Scramble
recipes.description: Silky scrambled eggs folded with earthy mushrooms and fresh spinach — a 10-minute breakfast that feels complete and delivers 22 grams of protein without any meat.
steps: Whisk eggs in a bowl until the whites and yolks are fully combined. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a small nonstick pan over medium heat. Add sliced mushrooms and cook 3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden.
Add garlic and spinach; toss until spinach wilts, about 1 minute.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Pour in eggs and fold gently with a spatula, pulling cooked egg from the edges to the center.
When eggs are just barely set but still glossy, remove from heat. Scatter cheese on top, cover for 30 seconds to melt, and serve.
cheapTips: Mushrooms stretch the volume of the scramble significantly for low cost
Buy spinach in a large bag — use it across several days of breakfasts

substitutions.swap: Any vegetable you have — zucchini, frozen broccoli, or bell pepper
Nutritional yeast for a dairy-free cheesy note

recipes.name: Blueberry Protein Smoothie Bowl
recipes.description: Thick blended blueberries and Greek yogurt poured into a bowl and loaded with crunchy granola and fresh toppings — the satisfying version of a smoothie that actually keeps you full until lunch.
steps: Blend frozen berries, Greek yogurt, protein powder, milk, and honey until very thick and smooth. Use as little liquid as possible so the base holds toppings.
Pour into a wide, shallow bowl.
Top with fresh blueberries, granola, and any other toppings you like.
Eat immediately before the base softens.
cheapTips: Frozen berries are far cheaper than fresh and work better in smoothie bowls
Make your own granola (see mfr-high-protein-granola) to cut costs further

substitutions.swap: Sliced banana, fresh strawberries, or more frozen berries

recipes.name: Black Bean Morning Burrito
recipes.description: A warm flour tortilla stuffed with fluffy scrambled eggs, spiced black beans, and melted cheese — a hand-held, budget-friendly breakfast that packs 29 grams of protein.
steps: Warm black beans in a small pan with cumin, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt until hot.
Heat a nonstick pan with a small amount of oil. Whisk eggs with salt and scramble over medium heat until just set.
Warm the tortillas briefly in the same pan or over an open flame.
Fill each tortilla with half the eggs, half the beans, a serving of shredded cheese, and a spoonful of salsa.
Fold and roll the burritos tightly. Serve immediately or wrap in foil for a portable breakfast.
cheapTips: A can of black beans + 4 eggs makes 2 filling burritos for well under $2 total
Homemade salsa from pantry staples is cheaper than jarred and tastes better

substitutions.swap: Pinto beans or refried beans for a creamier filling

recipes.name: Savory Quinoa Breakfast Bowl
recipes.description: Warm quinoa acting as a protein-rich grain base for a poached egg, sautéed spinach, and a drizzle of olive oil — the savoury breakfast bowl that keeps you full well into the afternoon.
steps: Rinse quinoa and cook according to package directions (about 15 minutes in twice its volume of water). Season with salt.
While quinoa cooks, heat olive oil in a pan over medium. Sauté mushrooms until golden, 3 minutes. Add garlic and spinach and cook until wilted.
To poach eggs, bring a small pot of water to a bare simmer. Crack each egg into a cup, swirl the water, and gently tip the egg in. Poach 3–4 minutes for a runny yolk.
Divide quinoa between two bowls. Top with the mushroom-spinach mixture and a poached egg each.
Drizzle with lemon juice, olive oil, and red pepper flakes. Serve immediately.
cheapTips: Quinoa bought in bulk drops to roughly $0.25 per ½ cup dry
A splash of vinegar in the poaching water keeps eggs tidy without extra cost

substitutions.swap: Brown rice or farro for a similar texture at lower cost

recipes.name: Salmon Cucumber Cream Toast
recipes.description: Toasted bread spread with cream cheese, layered with canned salmon and crisp cucumber slices, finished with capers and lemon — a Scandinavian-inspired breakfast ready in 5 minutes with 38 grams of protein.
steps: Drain canned salmon and flake it into a small bowl. Season with lemon juice, dill, salt, and pepper.
Toast the bread slices until golden.
Spread 1 tablespoon of cream cheese on each slice.
Layer thin cucumber rounds on the cream cheese, then top with the seasoned salmon.
Finish with extra dill, a crack of pepper, and optional red pepper flakes.
cheapTips: Canned salmon is cheaper per gram of protein than most other options — under $0.10/gram
Dried dill is a one-time pantry purchase that lasts a year

substitutions.swap: Canned tuna for a slightly different flavour at the same price point
Greek yogurt mixed with a pinch of salt for a lighter spread

recipes.name: Ginger Sesame Chicken Lettuce Wraps
recipes.description: Ground chicken seasoned with ginger, garlic, and soy sauce, spooned into crisp lettuce cups and topped with shredded carrots and sesame seeds — a light, high-protein lunch that comes together in 15 minutes.
steps: Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large pan over high heat. Add ground turkey and cook, breaking it up, until cooked through and lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; stir-fry 1 minute until fragrant.
Season with soy sauce, sesame oil, and rice vinegar. Toss to coat evenly.
Shred or grate carrots.
Separate large lettuce leaves into cups. Spoon the turkey mixture into each cup, top with shredded carrot, sliced scallion, and sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Ground turkey is cheaper than chicken breast per gram of protein
Iceberg lettuce provides the best cups at the lowest price

substitutions.swap: Lean ground chicken or crumbled firm tofu
Cabbage leaves work just as well and are cheaper per serving

recipes.name: Korean-Spiced Ground Beef Rice Bowl
recipes.description: Savory ground beef cooked with gochujang, soy, and sesame and spooned over white rice — a pantry-friendly bowl with bold Korean flavours ready in 20 minutes.
steps: Cook rice according to package directions.
Brown ground beef in a pan over medium-high heat, breaking it up well.
Add garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute. Drain any excess fat.
Stir in gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, and honey. Cook 2 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Divide rice between bowls and spoon the beef mixture over the top. Garnish with sliced scallions and sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Ground beef is one of the most economical high-protein options
Gochujang keeps months in the fridge — one tub flavors dozens of dishes

substitutions.swap: Ground turkey for a leaner option with similar macros after fat drain
Sriracha + a tiny splash of soy sauce if gochujang isn't available

recipes.name: Miso-Glazed Tofu Grain Bowl
recipes.description: Firm tofu roasted until crispy in a miso-sesame glaze, served over brown rice with steamed broccoli and a soft-boiled egg — a complete Japanese-inspired bowl with 28 grams of protein.
steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Press tofu dry between paper towels for 5 minutes, then cut into cubes.
Whisk miso, soy sauce, sesame oil, honey, and garlic together. Toss tofu in this glaze and spread on a lined baking sheet.
Roast 20–25 minutes until caramelised and crispy, flipping halfway.
Meanwhile cook brown rice and steam broccoli. Soft-boil eggs 6½ minutes, then cool in ice water and peel.
Build bowls: rice, broccoli, tofu, halved egg. Drizzle any remaining glaze over the top and sprinkle sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Tofu is one of the cheapest complete proteins available
Batch the miso glaze — it keeps a week in the fridge and works on any veg or protein

substitutions.swap: Quinoa or couscous for a different grain
Tempeh for more protein and a nuttier flavour

recipes.name: Vietnamese Shrimp Rice Noodle Salad
recipes.description: Cold rice noodles tossed with shrimp, shredded carrots, cucumber, fresh herbs, and a bright fish-sauce lime dressing — a refreshing, no-cook assembly bowl with 30 grams of protein.
steps: Cook rice noodles per package directions. Drain and rinse under cold water; set aside.
Season shrimp lightly with salt and cook in a dry hot pan 1–2 minutes per side until pink. Remove and cool.
Make dressing: combine lime juice, fish sauce, honey, minced garlic, and red pepper flakes.
Toss noodles with the dressing, julienned carrots, sliced cucumber, and shredded lettuce.
Divide into bowls, top with shrimp and plenty of fresh cilantro and mint.
cheapTips: Frozen shrimp is far cheaper than fresh and thaws quickly under cold water
Rice noodles bought dry cost about $0.50 per serving

substitutions.swap: Canned tuna, sliced chicken breast, or extra tofu for a different protein
Soy sauce for a vegetarian-friendly dressing

recipes.name: Thai Peanut Tempeh Bowl
recipes.description: Pan-seared tempeh glazed in a peanut-soy-lime sauce over brown rice with shredded cabbage and scallions — a hearty plant-based bowl with 30 grams of protein and great crunch.
steps: Slice tempeh into thin rectangles. Heat oil in a pan over medium-high and sear tempeh 3 minutes per side until golden.
Mix peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, honey, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes with 2–3 tbsp water to make the sauce.
Pour the sauce into the pan with the tempeh and toss to coat over low heat for 2 minutes.
Shred cabbage finely.
Serve tempeh and sauce over brown rice. Top with raw shredded cabbage and sliced scallions for crunch.
cheapTips: Tempeh is one of the densest plant proteins per dollar — typically under $1/serving
Cabbage is one of the cheapest vegetables available, especially raw

substitutions.swap: Extra-firm tofu for a milder flavour
Any cooked grain — quinoa, couscous, or noodles

recipes.name: Soy-Ginger Glazed Salmon Rice Bowl
recipes.description: A salmon fillet seared and glazed with soy sauce, fresh ginger, and honey, served over steamed white rice with blanched broccoli — a 25-minute bowl that tastes like a restaurant order.
steps: Cook rice. Steam or blanch broccoli until just tender.
Mix soy sauce, honey, grated ginger, garlic, and sesame oil for the glaze.
Heat vegetable oil in a pan over medium-high. Season salmon with salt and cook skin-side up for 3 minutes until golden, then flip and cook 2 more minutes.
Pour the glaze into the pan; let it bubble and reduce for 1 minute, basting the salmon.
Serve salmon over rice with broccoli. Spoon the pan glaze on top and garnish with scallions and sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Fresh salmon on sale is around $7/lb — at 2 servings per pound that's $3.50 each for a restaurant-quality meal
Frozen salmon fillets are reliable and often cheaper

substitutions.swap: Canned salmon mixed with the glaze for a budget version (different texture but same flavours)

recipes.name: Edamame Sesame Noodle Bowl
recipes.description: Room-temperature soba noodles tossed with edamame and a garlicky sesame-soy dressing — an entirely no-heat assembly option for lunch that delivers 24 grams of plant protein.
steps: Cook soba noodles per package instructions. Drain, rinse under cold water, and set aside.
Whisk soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, peanut butter, honey, garlic, and ginger to make the dressing.
Thaw edamame under warm water.
Toss noodles with dressing, shredded carrot, sliced cucumber, and edamame.
Divide between bowls and top with scallions and sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Soba noodles are a budget staple — 2 servings for under $1 in most stores
A single jar of peanut butter dresses dozens of portions at pennies each

substitutions.swap: Any noodle works — udon, rice noodles, or regular pasta

recipes.name: Spicy Tofu Bibimbap Bowl
recipes.description: A colourful Korean rice bowl with crispy pan-fried tofu, quick-pickled vegetables, a fried egg, and bold gochujang — each component takes minutes and the result is a meal that looks as good as it tastes.
steps: Cook rice. Press tofu dry and cut into rectangles; pan-fry in oil over medium-high until golden and crispy on both sides, about 4 minutes per side.
In the same pan, quickly sauté mushrooms with garlic and a splash of soy sauce until golden.
Quickly wilt spinach with sesame oil. Julienne or shred carrots; toss with rice vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Fry 1 egg per bowl sunny-side-up.

Build bowls: rice in the base, then arrange tofu, spinach, carrot, and mushrooms around the bowl. Place the egg in the center. Add a big spoonful of gochujang and sesame seeds. Mix everything together before eating.
cheapTips: Bibimbap is a great use of whatever vegetables need using up — the gochujang brings everything together

substitutions.swap: Sriracha or chili garlic sauce for a simpler but still spicy version

recipes.name: Teriyaki Mushroom and Edamame Rice Bowl
recipes.description: Meaty mushrooms glazed in teriyaki sauce over white rice with edamame and shredded carrot — an entirely plant-based lunch bowl with 23 grams of protein and plenty of umami.
steps: Cook rice.
Heat sesame oil in a pan over high heat. Add mushrooms and cook without stirring for 2–3 minutes until browned and slightly crispy.
Add garlic and ginger; stir 30 seconds. Pour in teriyaki sauce and toss to coat. Cook 1 more minute until the sauce thickens.
Warm edamame from frozen. Shred or julienne carrots.
Serve mushrooms over rice with edamame and shredded carrot. Top with scallions and sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Mushrooms absorb teriyaki sauce beautifully — a cheap way to get meat-like satisfaction from vegetables
Edamame bought frozen in a 1 lb bag lasts weeks in the freezer

substitutions.swap: King oyster or portobello mushrooms for the meatiest texture

recipes.name: Hoisin Chicken Soba Noodles
recipes.description: Tender strips of chicken breast tossed with chewy soba noodles, bok choy, and a sweet-savory hoisin sauce — a complete one-bowl Chinese-American classic ready in 20 minutes.
steps: Cook soba noodles per instructions; drain and rinse cold.
Slice chicken breast into thin strips and season with salt.
Stir-fry chicken in vegetable oil over high heat until cooked through, 4–5 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, broccoli florets, and shredded carrot; stir-fry 2 minutes.
Add noodles, hoisin sauce, soy sauce, and sesame oil; toss everything together over heat for 1–2 minutes. Garnish with scallions.
cheapTips: Chicken breast bought in a family pack costs roughly $1.20 per serving
Soba noodles are affordable and cook faster than pasta

substitutions.swap: Oyster sauce with a touch of honey
Regular pasta for a cheaper option at slightly different texture

recipes.name: Greek-Spiced Baked Chicken Thighs
recipes.description: Bone-in chicken thighs marinated in lemon, garlic, and oregano then roasted until deeply golden — the Mediterranean family meal that fills a sheet pan and reheats beautifully all week.
steps: Combine lemon juice, zest, olive oil, minced garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper. Coat chicken thighs and marinate at least 15 minutes (or overnight).
Preheat oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Arrange chicken on a baking sheet with quartered potatoes.
Roast 35–40 minutes until chicken skin is deep golden and juices run clear (internal 165 °F/74 °C).
Rest 5 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Bone-in chicken thighs are much cheaper per pound than boneless breasts and stay juicier
Potatoes roasted in the drippings are essentially free flavour

substitutions.swap: Bone-in chicken drumsticks for an even cheaper option

recipes.name: White Bean Shakshuka
recipes.description: Eggs poached directly in a bold tomato-pepper sauce loaded with white beans — a one-pan Middle Eastern dinner that's ready in 25 minutes and loaded with protein and fibre.
steps: Heat olive oil over medium; sauté diced onion and bell pepper until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, cumin, paprika, and cayenne; cook 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and drained white beans. Simmer 10 minutes, season with salt.
Make 4 wells in the sauce. Crack an egg into each well. Cover and cook over medium-low until whites are set but yolks are still soft, about 5–7 minutes.
Top with fresh cilantro and serve with crusty bread or pita.
cheapTips: This feeds two people for about $3 total — one of the best value dinners going
A 28-oz can of crushed tomatoes is the base — buy in bulk to save even more

substitutions.swap: Chickpeas or black beans for a different flavour profile

recipes.name: Lemon Herb Salmon with Couscous
recipes.description: Oven-baked salmon fillets over fluffy couscous with cucumber and herbs — a 25-minute Mediterranean dinner that tastes elaborate but comes together with almost no effort.
steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F. Place salmon on a lined sheet pan. Drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil, season with salt, pepper, garlic, and dill. Squeeze half the lemon over the top.
Bake 12–15 minutes until salmon flakes easily.
Pour boiling chicken broth over couscous in a bowl. Cover for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Toss couscous with remaining olive oil, lemon juice, chopped parsley, and diced cucumber.
Serve salmon over the herbed couscous.
cheapTips: Couscous is one of the quickest and cheapest grains available — no cooking required beyond boiling water
Wild-caught canned salmon can substitute for fresh at a fraction of the cost

substitutions.swap: Quinoa or bulgur for a higher-protein grain base
White fish like tilapia or cod for a milder, cheaper option

recipes.name: Lebanese Red Lentil Soup
recipes.description: Red lentils simmered with onion, cumin, and lemon until they collapse into a silky, bright-yellow soup — a classic Levantine staple that's both warming and cheap, with 22 grams of protein per bowl.
steps: Heat olive oil over medium; sauté diced onion until golden, about 8 minutes. Add garlic, cumin, and turmeric; cook 1 minute.
Add rinsed lentils, diced carrot, and 6 cups of water or veggie broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 25 minutes until lentils are completely soft.
Use an immersion blender (or blend in batches) until smooth. Add water to reach your preferred consistency.
Finish with lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Top with fresh cilantro and a drizzle of olive oil.
cheapTips: 1 lb of lentils makes 4 generous servings for about $2 total
This soup tastes better the next day — make a double batch on the weekend

substitutions.swap: Yellow split peas for a similar texture and flavour

recipes.storageInstructions: Fridge up to 5 days, freezes well up to 3 months.

recipes.name: Moroccan Chicken and Chickpea Stew
recipes.description: Chicken thighs braised with chickpeas, crushed tomatoes, cumin, cinnamon, and ginger in a one-pot stew inspired by North African flavours — warm, aromatic, and ready to serve over couscous.
steps: Season chicken thighs with cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Brown in olive oil over medium-high, 3 minutes per side.
Add onion; soften 3 minutes. Add garlic, ginger, and cinnamon; cook 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes and chickpeas. Nestle chicken into the sauce.
Simmer covered 30 minutes until chicken is tender. Remove chicken and shred the meat off the bone.
Return shredded chicken to the pot, adjust seasoning, finish with lemon juice. Serve over couscous.
cheapTips: Bone-in thighs are the most economical option — the bones add flavour to the stew
This recipe makes great leftovers and is even better the next day

substitutions.swap: Canned chicken for a truly minimal-effort version — add it at the end

recipes.name: Protein Quinoa Tabbouleh Bowl
recipes.description: A modern take on the Lebanese herb salad using quinoa as the grain base instead of bulgur — packed with parsley, mint, tomato, and cucumber, and dressed with lemon and olive oil. The quinoa swaps in a complete protein for a bowl that's both refreshing and substantial.
steps: Cook quinoa in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes. Spread on a plate and refrigerate to cool quickly.
Dice tomatoes and cucumber. Finely chop parsley and mint.
Once quinoa is cool, toss with tomatoes, cucumber, scallions, herbs, olive oil, and lemon juice.
Season generously with salt and pepper. Taste and adjust — it should taste very lemony and herbaceous.
Serve at room temperature or cold.
cheapTips: Quinoa tabbouleh keeps 3 days in the fridge — make a big batch for several lunches
Fresh parsley is one of the cheapest fresh herbs and is the star of this dish

substitutions.swap: Couscous cooks in 5 minutes if you need a quicker option

recipes.name: Turkish-Style Spiced Ground Beef Rice
recipes.description: A one-pan dinner of ground beef cooked with onion, cumin, cinnamon, and tomato paste over aromatic rice — inspired by the flavours of kofte and pilaf, ready in 25 minutes.
steps: Heat olive oil and sauté onion until golden, 5 minutes. Add garlic, cumin, cinnamon, and paprika; cook 1 minute.
Add ground beef and cook until browned, breaking up well. Drain excess fat.
Stir in tomato paste and cook 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook rice separately. Serve spiced beef mixture over rice, topped with fresh parsley.
cheapTips: Ground beef at 80/20 becomes leaner after draining the fat — the flavour stays rich

substitutions.swap: Ground lamb for a more authentic Turkish flavour if available

recipes.name: Roasted Chickpea and Vegetable Plate
recipes.description: A sheet pan full of crispy, spiced chickpeas and caramelized vegetables served over garlicky couscous with a drizzle of tahini — the plant-based sheet-pan dinner that proves vegan meals can be deeply satisfying.
steps: Preheat to 425 °F. Drain, rinse, and dry chickpeas thoroughly. Toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, cumin, paprika, garlic powder, and salt.
Cut zucchini, bell pepper, and onion into bite-size pieces. Toss with the remaining olive oil and salt.
Spread chickpeas on one side of a baking sheet and vegetables on the other. Roast 25–30 minutes until chickpeas are crispy and vegetables are caramelized.
Meanwhile, cook couscous. Whisk tahini with lemon juice and a splash of water to make the dressing.
Serve chickpeas and vegetables over couscous; drizzle with tahini dressing.
cheapTips: The secret to crispy roasted chickpeas is drying them very thoroughly before roasting

substitutions.swap: Quinoa or brown rice for a different grain base
Hummus thinned with lemon juice makes a great dressing

recipes.name: Harissa Shrimp with Pearl Couscous
recipes.description: Large shrimp tossed in harissa paste and seared until charred, served over pearl couscous with roasted tomatoes and fresh herbs — a North African-inspired dinner with serious depth for a 30-minute meal.
steps: Cook couscous per instructions; fluff with olive oil and season.
Toss shrimp with harissa and a pinch of salt.
Sear shrimp in a hot pan over high heat, 1–2 minutes per side until opaque and charred at the edges.
In the same pan, quickly cook onion and garlic; add chopped tomatoes and cook 3 minutes.
Stir the shrimp back into the tomato mixture. Serve over couscous with lemon juice and parsley.
cheapTips: Frozen shrimp thawed overnight is the same quality as fresh at half the price
Harissa paste lasts months in the fridge and adds big flavour for cents

substitutions.swap: Sriracha or chili paste if harissa isn't available

recipes.name: Feta and Spinach Stuffed Chicken Breast
recipes.description: Chicken breasts slit open, stuffed with wilted spinach and crumbled feta, then baked until golden — a show-stopping Greek-inspired dinner that looks elaborate and takes 30 minutes.
steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F. Quick-wilt spinach with garlic in a dry pan; let cool.
Slice each chicken breast horizontally to create a pocket (don't cut all the way through).
Mix wilted spinach with crumbled feta, lemon zest, and oregano.
Stuff each chicken breast with the spinach-feta mixture; secure with toothpicks.
Rub the outside with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Bake 22–25 minutes until internal temperature reaches 165 °F.
cheapTips: Stuffed chicken breasts are impressive but use the cheapest protein going
Block feta crumbled at home is cheaper than pre-crumbled

substitutions.swap: Cottage cheese mixed with herbs for a lower-fat, higher-protein stuffing

recipes.name: Green Chicken Pozole
recipes.description: A bright, herbaceous Mexican hominy soup with shredded chicken in a tomatillo-cilantro broth — deeply warming, high in protein, and built from pantry staples.
steps: Simmer chicken breasts in 4 cups of chicken broth with halved onion, garlic, cumin, and oregano for 20 minutes until cooked through.
Remove chicken and shred. Blend or mince jalapeño with cilantro and lime juice to make a rough green sauce.
Add white beans (standing in for hominy) and the green sauce to the broth. Simmer 10 minutes.
Return shredded chicken to the soup. Season and serve with lime wedges, extra cilantro, and optional toppings like shredded cabbage.
cheapTips: White beans work as a budget substitute for canned hominy
Making this with chicken breast on the bone adds more flavour — simmer with the bone, then shred

substitutions.swap: A can of hominy (maíz pozolero) if available for the authentic texture

recipes.name: Beef and Bean Enchilada Casserole
recipes.description: Layers of corn tortillas, spiced ground beef, black beans, salsa, and melted cheese baked into a hearty casserole — Mexican comfort food that serves a crowd and reheats perfectly.
steps: Preheat oven to 375 °F. Brown ground beef with onion, garlic, cumin, and chili powder. Drain fat.
Stir in drained black beans and 2 servings of salsa.
Spread a spoonful of salsa on the base of a 9×13 baking dish. Layer 3 tortillas, half the meat mixture, and a layer of cheese. Repeat.
Top with remaining salsa and cheese.
Bake 25–30 minutes until bubbly and golden. Rest 5 minutes before slicing.
cheapTips: This casserole feeds 6 for about $10 total — one of the best value family meals
Use store-brand salsa and cheese — flavour is identical to name brands

substitutions.swap: Ground turkey for a lighter version

recipes.name: Spicy Shrimp Tacos with Mango Slaw
recipes.description: Chili-spiced shrimp tucked into warm corn tortillas with a crunchy mango-cabbage slaw and a lime crema — a coastal Mexican taco that's ready in 15 minutes and feels like a summer meal any night of the week.
steps: Season shrimp with chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt.
Toss shredded cabbage with thawed diced mango, lime juice, cilantro, and a pinch of salt for the slaw.
Make the crema: mix Greek yogurt with lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Heat oil in a pan over high heat. Cook shrimp 1–2 minutes per side until pink.
Warm tortillas. Fill each with shrimp, slaw, and a drizzle of lime crema.
cheapTips: Frozen mango is a fraction of the price of fresh and tastes just as good in a slaw
Shrimp cooks in 4 minutes — this is one of the fastest high-protein dinners possible

substitutions.swap: Pineapple tidbits from a can work perfectly

recipes.name: Black Bean Sweet Potato Tamale Bowl
recipes.description: Spiced black beans and roasted sweet potato chunks over a bed of seasoned cornmeal — a deconstructed tamale bowl that's entirely plant-based, budget-friendly, and deeply warming.
steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F. Cube sweet potatoes, toss with olive oil, cumin, chili powder, and salt. Roast 25 minutes until caramelised.
Heat black beans with onion, garlic, corn, smoked paprika, and a pinch of cumin until hot.
Serve sweet potato and beans in bowls, topped with salsa, cilantro, and lime.
cheapTips: This hearty vegan bowl costs under $2 per serving
Sweet potatoes on sale make this even cheaper

substitutions.swap: Regular potato for an even cheaper option

recipes.name: Peruvian-Style Chicken with Herb Sauce
recipes.description: Oven-roasted chicken marinated in cumin, garlic, and citrus, served with a vibrant green cilantro-lime dipping sauce inspired by Peruvian aji verde — a restaurant favourite made in your own kitchen.
steps: Whisk cumin, paprika, 4 cloves minced garlic, lemon juice, 1 tbsp olive oil, and salt. Coat chicken thighs and marinate 20 minutes.
Roast at 425 °F for 35–40 minutes until deeply golden.
Make the green sauce: blend cilantro, jalapeño, remaining garlic, Greek yogurt, lime juice, and remaining olive oil until smooth. Season to taste.
Serve chicken drizzled with the vivid green sauce.
cheapTips: The green sauce uses cheap pantry ingredients — it's the secret to making this taste like restaurant food

substitutions.swap: Chicken breast for a leaner version — reduce cook time to 25 minutes

recipes.name: Chorizo and Potato Breakfast Hash
recipes.description: Crispy diced potatoes cooked with spiced ground pork, bell pepper, and onion, finished with eggs cracked right into the pan — a hearty Tex-Mex breakfast hash built for big appetites.
steps: Dice potatoes into small cubes. Cook in oil over medium heat in a cast-iron or nonstick pan, stirring occasionally, until golden and crispy, about 12 minutes.
Push potatoes to the side and crumble sausage into the pan; cook until browned.
Add onion, bell pepper, garlic, cumin, and paprika. Cook 3 minutes.
Make 3 wells in the mixture; crack an egg into each. Cover and cook until whites are set.
Serve with hot sauce.
cheapTips: Hash is a great use-up meal for potatoes and meat that need to be cooked soon
Ground turkey seasoned with Mexican spices substitutes cheaply for chorizo

substitutions.swap: Ground turkey + extra cumin and chili powder for a lighter version

recipes.name: Colombian-Style Red Beans and Rice
recipes.description: Kidney beans braised with onion, tomato, cumin, and hogao-inspired sofrito, served over white rice with a soft-boiled egg — a filling, budget-friendly plate straight from the Colombian tradition of bandeja staples.
steps: Dice tomato and onion finely. Cook in vegetable oil over medium heat until soft and fragrant — this is the sofrito base.
Add garlic and cumin; cook 1 minute. Add drained kidney beans and 1 cup of water.
Simmer 20 minutes, mashing some beans against the pot to thicken the sauce.
Soft-boil eggs 7 minutes; cool and peel.
Cook rice. Serve beans over rice with a halved egg, cilantro, and salt to taste.
cheapTips: Two cans of kidney beans + rice feeds 4 people for about $5 total
This dish is intentionally simple — the sofrito is where all the flavour lives

substitutions.swap: Pinto beans or black beans for a different Colombian regional variation

recipes.name: Grilled Mexican Street Corn Salad
recipes.description: All the bold flavours of elote — charred corn, crumbled feta, lime, chili powder, and cumin — tossed into a no-grill salad that works as a side or a light main with added beans.
steps: Char corn in a dry cast-iron or nonstick pan over high heat, stirring occasionally, until some kernels have dark spots — about 4–5 minutes.
Combine lime juice, Greek yogurt, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt to make the dressing.
Toss charred corn with the dressing, crumbled feta, sliced scallions, and fresh cilantro.
Serve at room temperature or cold.
cheapTips: Frozen corn charred in a skillet tastes just like grilled summer corn
This keeps 3 days in the fridge — make a big batch as a side for several meals

substitutions.swap: Cotija cheese (more authentic) if available

recipes.name: Spiced Lamb and Quinoa Stuffed Peppers
recipes.description: Bell peppers filled with a fragrant mixture of ground beef, quinoa, cumin, cinnamon, and pine nuts then roasted until tender — a Latin-Mediterranean fusion dish that looks impressive and delivers 34 grams of protein per pepper.
steps: Cook quinoa until tender, about 15 minutes. Preheat oven to 375 °F.
Brown ground beef with onion, garlic, cumin, and cinnamon. Drain fat. Stir in tomato paste and cooked quinoa.
Slice tops off peppers and remove seeds. Fill each with the beef-quinoa mixture.
Place in a baking dish; add a splash of water to the bottom. Roast 30–35 minutes until peppers are tender.
Garnish with fresh parsley.
cheapTips: Stuffed peppers are a great way to stretch ground beef across 4 full servings

substitutions.swap: Ground turkey for a leaner version with nearly identical results

recipes.name: Cumin-Spiced Lentil Taco Bowls
recipes.description: French lentils seasoned with Mexican taco spices served over rice with salsa, corn, and shredded cabbage — a plant-based taco night that's faster than cooking ground meat and packed with fibre.
steps: Simmer lentils in 2 cups of water with cumin, chili powder, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt for 25 minutes until tender and nearly dry.
Cook rice and warm corn.
Thinly shred cabbage and toss with lime juice.
Build bowls: rice, spiced lentils, warm corn, shredded cabbage, and salsa. Add sliced avocado if using.
cheapTips: Lentils are the cheapest complete protein per serving available — this bowl costs under $1.50 each
French or green lentils hold their shape better than red lentils for taco-style fillings

substitutions.swap: Canned lentils for a 20-minute shortcut

recipes.name: Tuscan White Bean and Kale Soup
recipes.description: Creamy white beans and ribbons of hearty kale simmered in a garlicky tomato broth with Italian herbs — a classic ribollita-inspired soup that's cheap, filling, and even better the next day.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium. Sauté diced onion, carrot, and celery until softened, about 6 minutes.
Add garlic, Italian seasoning, and red pepper flakes; cook 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes, both cans of white beans (one slightly mashed), and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Roughly chop kale into ribbons and add to the pot. Simmer 20 minutes until kale is tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Drizzle with a little olive oil to serve.
cheapTips: Two cans of beans + a bunch of kale + pantry broth makes 4 servings for under $6
The soup thickens beautifully as it cools — perfect for meal prep

substitutions.swap: Spinach or Swiss chard — add in the last 2 minutes as they wilt quickly

recipes.storageInstructions: Fridge up to 5 days; freeze up to 3 months.

recipes.name: Roasted Red Pepper Tomato Soup
recipes.description: Roasted red peppers and crushed tomatoes blended into a sweet, smoky, velvety soup — finished with a swirl of Greek yogurt for protein and creaminess without heavy cream.
steps: Halve and seed bell peppers. Place cut-side down on a baking sheet; toss onion and garlic alongside. Roast at 450 °F for 20–25 minutes until peppers are charred and collapsed.
Peel peppers once cool enough to handle.
Blend roasted peppers, onion, and garlic with crushed tomatoes, smoked paprika, and veggie broth until smooth.
Pour into a pot; simmer 10 minutes. Stir in Greek yogurt off the heat.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve with extra yogurt swirled on top.
cheapTips: Canned roasted red peppers can replace fresh peppers to skip the roasting step — cost is similar

substitutions.swap: Coconut milk for a vegan version

recipes.name: Thai Coconut Chicken Soup
recipes.description: A fragrant Thai-inspired soup of chicken breast simmered in coconut milk with lemongrass-inspired ginger, lime, and fish sauce — warming, aromatic, and ready in 25 minutes.
steps: Slice chicken breast into thin strips.
Combine coconut milk, chicken broth, red curry paste, ginger, and garlic in a pot. Bring to a simmer over medium.
Add chicken and mushrooms; simmer 10 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Season with fish sauce and lime juice. Taste and adjust — it should balance sweet, sour, salty, and spicy.
Serve topped with fresh cilantro and scallions.
cheapTips: Full-fat coconut milk gives the best flavour — a single can is enough for 4 bowls
Fish sauce is the secret to depth — a bottle costs $3 and lasts many months

substitutions.swap: Soy sauce for a vegetarian-friendly soup
A pinch of chili powder and extra ginger if curry paste isn't available

recipes.name: Lentil and Vegetable Minestrone
recipes.description: A hearty Italian-inspired minestrone with French lentils, pasta, zucchini, and crushed tomatoes — a meal-in-a-bowl that uses the entire vegetable drawer and keeps you full for hours.
steps: Heat olive oil over medium; sauté onion, carrot, and celery until soft, 6 minutes. Add garlic and Italian seasoning; cook 1 minute.
Add rinsed lentils, crushed tomatoes, and veggie broth. Simmer 20 minutes.
Add pasta, diced zucchini, and chopped kale. Cook until pasta is al dente, about 10 minutes.
Season well. The soup thickens as it sits — add more broth to reheat.
cheapTips: This makes 6 large servings for about $8 total — one of the most cost-efficient meals
Add any vegetables that need using up — minestrone is forgiving

substitutions.swap: Spinach, cabbage, or Swiss chard

recipes.name: Smoky Black Bean Soup
recipes.description: Black beans blended into a thick, smoky, satisfying soup with chipotle-inspired depth, finished with sour cream and lime — a 30-minute pantry dinner that costs almost nothing.
steps: Sauté onion in olive oil until soft, 5 minutes. Add garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and chili powder; cook 1 minute.
Add drained black beans and chicken broth; simmer 15 minutes.
Use a hand blender to partially blend — leave some beans whole for texture.
Finish with lime juice and season. Serve with sour cream and cilantro.
cheapTips: Two cans of black beans + pantry spices feeds 4 people for about $3
This soup freezes perfectly — make a double batch

substitutions.swap: Greek yogurt for more protein at fewer calories
Veggie broth to make the soup vegan

recipes.name: Broccoli Cheddar Protein Soup
recipes.description: Rich, cheesy broccoli soup made with a Greek yogurt base instead of heavy cream — gets its creaminess and protein from dairy, with 24 grams of protein per bowl and the same comforting flavour as the classic.
steps: Sauté onion and garlic in butter over medium heat until soft, about 4 minutes.
Add broccoli florets and chicken broth; bring to a simmer. Cook 12 minutes until broccoli is very tender.
Remove from heat. Stir in milk and use a hand blender to partially blend — some texture is good.
Return to low heat. Stir in shredded cheese in small handfuls until melted. Remove from heat again.
Stir in Greek yogurt and mustard. Season with salt and pepper.
cheapTips: Greek yogurt adds protein and creaminess for a fraction of the cost of heavy cream

substitutions.swap: Low-fat sour cream for a similar result

recipes.name: Chicken Tortilla Soup
recipes.description: A Mexican-inspired soup of shredded chicken in a cumin-tomato broth loaded with black beans and corn, topped with crushed tortilla chips — a one-pot meal that feeds four for under $8.
steps: Sauté onion until soft; add garlic, cumin, and chili powder.
Add raw chicken, crushed tomatoes, black beans, corn, and broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Remove chicken and shred with two forks. Return to pot.
Adjust seasoning. Serve with crushed tortilla chips, lime, and cilantro.
cheapTips: Cooking the chicken directly in the broth keeps it moist without any extra effort
Store-brand crushed tomatoes are identical to premium brands for this use

substitutions.swap: Leftover rotisserie chicken — add at the end and just warm through

recipes.name: Pork and Miso Ramen
recipes.description: A warming bowl of ramen in a rich miso-spiked pork broth topped with a soft-boiled egg, crisp scallions, and a drizzle of sesame oil — a Japanese comfort bowl built from affordable pantry ingredients in under 25 minutes.
steps: Soft-boil eggs 6½ minutes; cool in ice water and peel.
Brown crumbled sausage in a pot over medium-high heat. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté garlic and ginger 30 seconds. Add chicken broth and bring to a simmer.
Whisk miso into the broth off the heat (do not boil miso). Add soy sauce and sesame oil.
Cook noodles separately per package (discard seasoning packet — you have real flavour). Drain.
Assemble bowls: noodles, ladle over broth, top with pork, halved egg, wilted spinach, and sliced scallions.
cheapTips: Instant ramen noodles (discarding the flavour packet) are one of the cheapest noodle options
Miso paste adds enormous depth for pennies per tablespoon

substitutions.swap: Ground turkey or crumbled tofu for a lighter version

recipes.name: Ethiopian Spiced Red Lentil Stew
recipes.description: Misir wot-inspired red lentils braised with berbere spice blend, onion, garlic, and ginger until thick and deeply fragrant — a spiced lentil stew served over rice or with flatbread that costs almost nothing and provides exceptional plant protein.
steps: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium. Cook diced onions until golden brown, about 10 minutes — this is the flavour foundation.
Add garlic, ginger, and all spices; cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste; cook 1 minute.
Add rinsed lentils and 3 cups of water. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick.
Season with salt. Serve over rice.
cheapTips: 1 lb of lentils at $2 makes 4 generous servings — one of the absolute best values in cooking
Toasting the spices in oil (taddka technique) is the key to the deep, layered flavour

substitutions.swap: Red split lentils cook faster (20 minutes) and produce a silkier stew

recipes.name: Herbed Chicken and Barley Soup
recipes.description: A deeply comforting old-fashioned soup of tender chicken and nutty pearl barley in a herb-scented vegetable broth — the kind of meal that heals everything, packed with 36 grams of protein per bowl.
steps: Place chicken, broth, onion, and a bay leaf in a large pot. Bring to a simmer and cook 20 minutes.
Remove chicken and shred. Add brown rice (or barley if available) to the broth. Cook 25 minutes.
Add diced carrots, celery, garlic, and thyme; cook 15 more minutes until everything is tender.
Return shredded chicken. Remove bay leaf. Season and stir in fresh parsley.
cheapTips: This recipe makes 6 large bowls for about $8 — ideal for the week
Using chicken thighs on the bone instead of breast adds even more flavour

substitutions.swap: Pearl barley for the traditional version if available (cook time is similar)

recipes.storageInstructions: Fridge up to 5 days; freeze up to 3 months (grain absorbs liquid — add broth when reheating).

recipes.name: Turkey Meatballs in Marinara
recipes.description: Juicy baked turkey meatballs simmered in a garlicky tomato sauce — a lighter spin on a classic that works over pasta, rice, or zucchini noodles.
steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F. Combine turkey, egg, garlic, Italian seasoning, onion powder, and salt. Mix until just combined — don't overwork.
Roll into 20 meatballs (about 1.5 tbsp each). Arrange on a lined baking sheet and bake 20 minutes until cooked through.
Warm marinara in a wide skillet over medium. Add baked meatballs and simmer 8 minutes.
Cook pasta. Serve meatballs and sauce over pasta.
cheapTips: Baking instead of pan-frying saves time and oil
Bulk ground turkey is much cheaper per pound than pre-formed patties

substitutions.swap: Zucchini noodles or cauliflower rice for low-carb

recipes.name: BBQ Chicken Stuffed Sweet Potato
recipes.description: Baked sweet potato split open and piled high with shredded BBQ chicken, black beans, and corn — a sweet-savory combination with 38 grams of protein that's perfect for meal prep.
steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F. Pierce sweet potatoes and bake 45–50 minutes until tender.
Season chicken with garlic powder, paprika, and salt. Bake alongside potatoes for the last 25 minutes. Shred and toss with BBQ sauce.
Warm black beans and corn. Split potatoes; pile with BBQ chicken, beans, and corn.
cheapTips: Baking the chicken in the same oven as the potatoes saves time and energy

substitutions.swap: Canned chicken for a 5-minute shortcut

recipes.name: Salmon and Asparagus Sheet Pan
recipes.description: Salmon fillets and spears of asparagus roasted together on one pan with lemon and garlic — a 20-minute dinner that requires almost no cleanup.
steps: Preheat oven to 425 °F. Toss broccoli (or asparagus-like vegetable) with 0.5 tbsp oil and salt.
Place salmon on one half of the pan, vegetables on the other. Drizzle salmon with remaining oil, garlic, dill, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Roast 12–15 minutes until salmon flakes and vegetables are tender with caramelized edges.
cheapTips: One sheet pan, 15 minutes, and almost no cleanup

substitutions.swap: Any quick-roasting vegetable — zucchini, bell pepper, or green beans

recipes.name: Ginger Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
recipes.description: Thin strips of beef stir-fried at high heat with broccoli in a ginger-soy-oyster sauce — the takeout version of a takeout favourite, ready in 15 minutes at a fraction of the cost.
steps: Cook rice. Mix soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sesame oil for the stir-fry sauce.
Heat oil in a wok or large pan over very high heat. Add beef and stir-fry 3 minutes until browned.
