Add garlic and ginger; cook 30 seconds. Add broccoli florets and 2 tbsp water; stir-fry 3 minutes.
Pour in sauce and toss everything together for 1 minute. Serve over rice with scallions.
cheapTips: Ground beef works in place of thinly-sliced beef for a much cheaper version

substitutions.swap: Extra soy sauce + a teaspoon of honey

recipes.name: High-Protein Chicken Caesar Wrap
recipes.description: Sliced grilled chicken, crisp romaine, and a Greek yogurt Caesar dressing rolled tight in a flour tortilla — 44 grams of protein in a hand-held lunch.
steps: Season chicken with salt and pepper; cook in olive oil over medium-high until cooked through, 5–6 minutes. Slice thinly.
Make the dressing: whisk Greek yogurt, parmesan, lemon juice, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Toss shredded romaine with half the dressing. Fill tortillas with romaine, sliced chicken, and extra dressing.
Roll tightly, cut in half, and serve.
cheapTips: Greek yogurt Caesar is cheaper and higher in protein than store-bought dressing

substitutions.swap: Nutritional yeast for a dairy-free version with similar flavour

recipes.name: Shrimp Scampi Pasta
recipes.description: Plump shrimp sautéed in garlic and lemon butter, tossed with pasta — an Italian-American classic that's actually quick and affordable when built with frozen shrimp.
steps: Cook pasta. Heat olive oil and butter over medium-high; add garlic and red pepper flakes; cook 30 seconds.
Add shrimp; cook 1–2 minutes per side until pink.
Add lemon juice and a splash of pasta water; toss with drained pasta and parsley.
cheapTips: Frozen shrimp thaws in 10 minutes under cold water — just as good as fresh for a fraction of the cost

substitutions.swap: Zucchini noodles for a lower-carb version

recipes.name: Cilantro Lime Chicken Burrito Bowl
recipes.description: Seasoned chicken breast, cilantro-lime rice, black beans, corn, and salsa in one bowl — a Chipotle-style meal at home for a fraction of the cost.
steps: Season chicken with cumin, chili powder, garlic powder, and salt. Cook in olive oil 5–6 minutes per side. Slice.
Cook rice; stir in lime juice and cilantro to make cilantro-lime rice.
Warm beans and corn.
Build bowls: rice, beans, corn, chicken, salsa. Top with extra lime and cilantro.
cheapTips: This meal costs about $2.50 per serving vs $12+ at a fast-casual restaurant

substitutions.swap: Ground beef or shrimp for variation

recipes.name: Tuna and White Bean Pasta Salad
recipes.description: Cold pasta tossed with canned tuna, white beans, cherry tomatoes, and a lemon-olive oil dressing — a no-cook assembly lunch with 35 grams of protein per serving.
steps: Cook pasta and rinse cold. Drain tuna.
Toss pasta with white beans, tuna, diced tomatoes, cucumber, olive oil, lemon juice, parsley, and chilli flakes.
Season with salt. Serve at room temperature or cold.
cheapTips: Two cans of tuna + canned beans + pasta makes a complete protein-rich meal for about $3.50

substitutions.swap: Chickpeas or black beans work equally well

recipes.name: Ground Turkey Veggie Skillet
recipes.description: A one-pan weeknight dinner of ground turkey browned with bell peppers, zucchini, and garlic in Italian seasoning — ready in 20 minutes and endlessly customizable.
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Brown turkey, breaking up well, about 5 minutes.
Add onion, bell pepper, zucchini, and garlic. Cook 5 minutes until vegetables soften.
Add diced tomatoes and Italian seasoning. Cook 3 minutes more. Season and serve.
cheapTips: One-skillet meals save on washing up — use whatever vegetables are about to turn

substitutions.swap: Ground beef or chicken

recipes.name: Chickpea Avocado Salad Wrap
recipes.description: Mashed chickpeas with avocado, lemon, and celery rolled in a tortilla — a creamy, filling plant-based wrap that takes 5 minutes and delivers 18 grams of plant protein.
steps: Drain and mash chickpeas roughly — leave some texture.
Mash avocado with lemon juice, cumin, salt, and cilantro. Fold in chickpeas, diced celery, and onion.
Spread onto tortillas, roll tightly, and serve.
cheapTips: Chickpeas + one avocado makes 2 filling wraps for about $2 total

substitutions.swap: Hummus for a lower-fat filling

recipes.name: Honey Garlic Baked Chicken Thighs
recipes.description: Chicken thighs glazed in a four-ingredient honey-garlic sauce and roasted until caramelized — the weeknight chicken recipe that disappears every time.
steps: Preheat oven to 425 °F. Whisk honey, soy sauce, minced garlic, and olive oil.
Season chicken with salt and pepper; place in a baking dish. Pour sauce over.
Bake 35–40 minutes, basting halfway, until deeply caramelized.
Cook rice. Serve chicken over rice with pan juices.
cheapTips: Bone-in thighs are much cheaper than boneless and produce more flavour

substitutions.swap: Maple syrup for a slightly different but equally good result

recipes.name: Lemon Herb Baked Cod with Roasted Veg
recipes.description: Flaky cod fillets baked with lemon, garlic, and herbs over a bed of roasted vegetables — a clean, high-protein dinner ready in 25 minutes.
steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F. Toss broccoli and bell pepper with 0.5 tbsp olive oil, salt.
Place fish on the vegetables. Season with garlic, Italian seasoning, lemon juice, and remaining oil.
Bake 15–18 minutes until fish flakes.
cheapTips: White fish like cod is one of the cheapest fresh proteins per gram

substitutions.swap: Any white fish — tilapia, haddock, or pollock — bake the same way

recipes.name: Asian-Style Ground Beef Lettuce Cups
recipes.description: Savory ground beef with ginger, hoisin, and sesame in crisp iceberg lettuce cups — a crowd-pleasing appetizer that doubles as a satisfying low-carb dinner.
steps: Brown beef over high heat, breaking up well. Drain fat.
Add garlic and ginger; cook 30 seconds. Add hoisin, soy sauce, and sesame oil.
Cook 1 minute until thickened. Serve in lettuce cups with scallions and sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Ground beef + pantry sauces makes this taste like a restaurant appetizer for about $1.50 per serving

substitutions.swap: Ground turkey or chicken for a leaner version

recipes.name: Egg and Vegetable Fried Brown Rice
recipes.description: Day-old brown rice stir-fried with eggs, frozen vegetables, and soy sauce — the quick, protein-rich staple that uses whatever's in the fridge.
steps: Heat oil in a wok over very high heat. Scramble eggs and push to sides.
Add frozen vegetables and garlic; stir-fry 2 minutes.
Add cold rice, breaking up clumps. Stir-fry until hot, 3 minutes.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil. Top with scallions.
cheapTips: This turns leftover rice into a complete meal for almost nothing extra

substitutions.swap: White rice or cauliflower rice

recipes.name: Turkey and Quinoa Stuffed Zucchini Boats
recipes.description: Large zucchini halved, scooped, and filled with Italian-seasoned ground turkey and quinoa, then baked until golden — a low-carb stuffed vegetable that's complete in one serving.
steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F. Halve zucchini lengthwise; scoop out flesh, leaving a shell. Chop flesh.
Cook quinoa. Brown turkey with garlic, Italian seasoning, and zucchini flesh. Add diced tomatoes and cooked quinoa.
Fill zucchini shells; top with shredded cheese.
Bake 20–25 minutes until zucchini is tender and cheese is golden.
cheapTips: Zucchini boats are a great way to serve a filling meal with almost no starchy carbs

substitutions.swap: Cauliflower rice for even fewer carbs

recipes.name: Honey-Dijon Salmon Grain Bowl
recipes.description: Pan-seared salmon glazed in honey and Dijon mustard over quinoa with roasted broccoli — a restaurant-quality grain bowl assembled at home in 25 minutes.
steps: Cook quinoa. Roast broccoli at 425 °F for 15 minutes.
Mix honey, Dijon, garlic, and lemon juice. Brush salmon with the glaze.
Sear salmon skin-side up in olive oil over medium-high for 3 minutes; flip and cook 2 more minutes. Pour remaining glaze into the pan.
Serve over quinoa with broccoli.
cheapTips: Dijon mustard costs almost nothing per teaspoon and adds incredible flavour

substitutions.swap: Brown rice, couscous, or farro

recipes.name: White Chicken Chili
recipes.description: A creamy, mildly spiced chili of shredded chicken, white beans, corn, and green chiles in a cumin broth — a one-pot dinner that comes together in 30 minutes.
steps: Sauté onion and garlic in oil. Add cumin and chili powder.
Add raw chicken, white beans, corn, and broth. Simmer 20 minutes.
Remove chicken and shred. Return to pot.
Stir in Greek yogurt off heat for creaminess without cream. Finish with lime.
cheapTips: Greek yogurt gives this chili creaminess for a fraction of the cost of heavy cream

substitutions.swap: Sour cream or omit for a broth-based version

recipes.name: Spinach and Feta Frittata
recipes.description: A Mediterranean oven frittata packed with spinach and feta — starts on the stovetop and finishes in the oven for a perfectly set, easy weeknight dinner that also works for brunch.
steps: Preheat oven to 375 °F. Sauté onion and garlic in an oven-safe skillet; add spinach until wilted.
Whisk eggs with milk, salt, and pepper. Stir in feta.
Pour egg mixture over the vegetables in the skillet. Cook undisturbed on stovetop for 3 minutes.
Transfer to oven and bake 15–18 minutes until fully set and lightly golden.
Slice into wedges and serve.
cheapTips: 8 eggs at $0.42 each = $3.36 feeds 4 people — incredible value per gram of protein

substitutions.swap: Any cheese — goat, cheddar, or mozzarella

recipes.name: Smoky Pulled Chicken Sweet Potato Bowl
recipes.description: Slow-simmered shredded chicken in a smoky chipotle-tomato sauce over baked sweet potato — a hearty bowl with great depth of flavour.
steps: Bake sweet potatoes 40–45 minutes at 400 °F.
Simmer chicken in tomato sauce with smoked paprika, cumin, garlic, and onion for 20 minutes. Shred.
Split potatoes and fill with pulled chicken, lime juice, and optional toppings.
cheapTips: Pulled chicken makes 3 stuffed sweet potatoes — filling and cheap

substitutions.swap: Crushed tomatoes with the same spices

recipes.name: Chickpea and Spinach Curry
recipes.description: Chickpeas and wilted spinach simmered in an aromatic tomato-coconut curry sauce — a satisfying Indian-inspired vegan dinner ready in 25 minutes.
steps: Cook rice. Sauté onion in olive oil until golden, 5 minutes. Add garlic, ginger, curry powder, cumin, and turmeric; cook 1 minute.
Add chickpeas (both cans) and crushed tomatoes; simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in coconut milk (half can) and spinach; cook until spinach wilts.
Season and serve over rice.
cheapTips: Two cans of chickpeas make 4 generous servings for about $2.20 in beans alone

substitutions.swap: Veggie broth for a lighter, oil-free version

recipes.name: Pesto Chicken Caprese
recipes.description: Golden pan-seared chicken topped with pesto, fresh mozzarella, and tomatoes — a 25-minute Italian-inspired dinner that looks restaurant-worthy.
steps: Pound chicken breasts to even thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high. Sear chicken 5 minutes per side until golden.
Spread pesto on each breast. Top with a slice of mozzarella and tomato.
Broil 3–4 minutes until mozzarella melts and bubbles.
Garnish with fresh basil and a drizzle of balsamic glaze. Serve immediately.
cheapTips: Pesto from a jar works great — no need for fresh basil in bulk
Low-moisture mozzarella melts better and is cheaper than fresh

substitutions.swap: Provolone or any melting cheese you have
Sun-dried tomato spread for a different flavor

recipes.name: Lime Shrimp Tacos with Cabbage Slaw
recipes.description: Chili-lime sautéed shrimp in corn tortillas with a crunchy cabbage slaw and a chipotle Greek yogurt crema — taco night done right.
steps: Toss shrimp with chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, salt, and a squeeze of lime.
Make slaw: shred cabbage and toss with lime juice, salt, and chopped cilantro. Let sit 5 minutes.
Make crema: stir Greek yogurt with lime juice, a pinch of chili powder, and salt.
Sauté shrimp in olive oil over high heat 1–2 minutes per side until pink and slightly charred.
Warm tortillas. Build tacos: slaw, shrimp, avocado slices, and crema.
cheapTips: Frozen shrimp is just as good thawed overnight — costs about $6–8/lb
Cabbage is one of the cheapest vegetables per pound

substitutions.swap: Tilapia fillet for a budget-friendly fish taco
Skip or use guacamole from a packet to control cost

recipes.name: Smoky Ground Beef and Sweet Potato Bowl
recipes.description: Smoky-seasoned ground beef over roasted sweet potato chunks with black beans and a lime drizzle — hearty, warming, and only one pan to clean.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Cube sweet potatoes, toss with olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Roast 22 minutes until caramelized.
Season ground beef with cumin, garlic powder, chili powder, and salt.
Brown beef in a skillet 6–8 minutes; drain excess fat.
Warm black beans with a pinch of cumin in the same pan.
Build bowls: roasted sweet potato, beef, black beans, lime squeeze, scallions.
cheapTips: Ground beef is one of the cheapest animal proteins
Canned black beans add protein and fiber for under $1

substitutions.swap: Ground turkey for a leaner, slightly cheaper option
Regular potato is even cheaper and just as filling

recipes.name: Crispy Tofu and Vegetable Stir-Fry
recipes.description: Extra-firm tofu pan-fried until golden and tossed with broccoli, bell pepper, and a savory ginger-soy sauce — a vegan dinner as satisfying as takeout.
steps: Press tofu 10 minutes between paper towels. Cut into ½-inch cubes.
Cook rice. Whisk soy sauce, ginger, garlic, rice vinegar, and brown sugar into a sauce.
Fry tofu in sesame oil over medium-high 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Add broccoli and bell pepper to the pan; stir-fry 3–4 minutes.
Pour sauce over and toss everything 1–2 minutes. Serve over rice with sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Firm tofu costs about $2–3 and provides 20g protein for the block
Pressing is the key to crispy tofu — don't skip it

substitutions.swap: Tempeh for a nuttier flavor and more protein
Honey or maple syrup works equally well

recipes.name: Salmon and Black Bean Tacos
recipes.description: Flaky chili-lime salmon in corn tortillas with black beans, avocado crema, and crunchy cabbage — a taco night that feels special but costs $4 a serving.
steps: Season salmon with chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and salt.
Cook salmon in olive oil 3–4 minutes per side until it flakes easily. Break into chunks.
Mash avocado with lime juice and salt for a quick crema.
Shred cabbage and toss with lime juice and cilantro.
Warm tortillas. Build tacos: black beans, salmon, cabbage slaw, avocado crema.
cheapTips: Canned salmon is an excellent budget substitution at half the cost
Half a can of black beans rounds out the tacos without overpowering the fish

substitutions.swap: Canned salmon or tilapia for a cheaper option
Plain Greek yogurt thinned with lime juice

recipes.name: Ground Turkey and Kale Soup
recipes.description: Savory broth with seasoned ground turkey, white beans, and hearty kale — a filling, nutrient-dense soup perfect for meal prep.
steps: Sauté onion and carrot in olive oil 5 minutes. Add garlic 1 minute.
Add ground turkey, breaking apart, and cook 5–6 minutes until browned.
Pour in chicken broth and Italian seasoning. Bring to a boil.
Add drained white beans and chopped kale. Simmer 10 minutes until kale is tender.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve with crusty bread if desired.
cheapTips: Kale is one of the cheapest nutrient-dense greens
White beans add protein and fiber for under $1/can

substitutions.swap: Spinach or Swiss chard — add in last 2 minutes so it doesn't overcook
Chickpeas or lentils work equally well

recipes.name: Egg White and Roasted Vegetable Frittata
recipes.description: A golden, puffy frittata made with egg whites and packed with roasted bell pepper, zucchini, and feta — low-fat, high-protein, oven-set in 20 minutes.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Sauté onion in olive oil 3 minutes; add garlic and bell pepper 3 minutes; add zucchini and spinach 2 minutes.
Separate 6 eggs; whisk 6 egg whites with 4 whole eggs, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Pour egg mixture over vegetables in an oven-safe skillet. Crumble feta on top.
Cook on stovetop 2 minutes until edges set, then transfer to oven 12–15 minutes until fully set and golden.
Let cool 5 minutes before slicing into wedges.
cheapTips: Eggs are one of the cheapest complete proteins
Using mostly egg whites drops fat and calories while keeping volume

substitutions.swap: Goat cheese or mozzarella for a different flavor
Mushrooms, asparagus, or whatever vegetables need using up

recipes.name: Lentil Shepherd's Pie with Cauliflower Mash
recipes.description: Savory lentil and vegetable filling under a cloud of creamy cauliflower mash — plant-based comfort food at its most satisfying.
steps: Cook lentils in vegetable broth 20 minutes until tender.
Sauté onion, carrot, garlic in olive oil 8 minutes. Add tomato paste and thyme; cook 2 minutes.
Add cooked lentils, frozen peas, worcestershire sauce, and broth. Simmer 5 minutes.
Steam and mash potatoes (or substitute cauliflower for lower calories) with olive oil and salt.
Pour filling into a baking dish, spread mash on top, and broil 5 minutes until golden.
cheapTips: Lentils are one of the cheapest plant proteins at $1–2/lb
The whole dish costs about $1.50 per serving

substitutions.swap: Cauliflower steamed and mashed for a lower-carb topping
Soy sauce for a vegan-friendly umami boost

recipes.name: Chicken and Roasted Veggie Sheet Pan
recipes.description: Bone-in chicken thighs roasted alongside a colorful mix of seasonal vegetables — one pan, minimal prep, maximum flavor.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Cube sweet potato; chop other vegetables into large pieces.
Toss all vegetables with 1 tbsp olive oil, half the seasonings, salt, and pepper on a large sheet pan.
Season chicken thighs with remaining olive oil, Italian seasoning, smoked paprika, garlic, salt, and pepper. Nestle among the vegetables.
Roast 30–35 minutes until chicken is golden and vegetables are caramelized.
Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Bone-in chicken thighs are the cheapest cut and the most forgiving to roast
Use whatever vegetables are on sale — this is a framework, not a fixed recipe

substitutions.swap: Regular potato or butternut squash
Drumsticks for even cheaper; bone-in breast for leaner option

recipes.name: Spiced Black Bean and Quinoa Bowl
recipes.description: Protein-packed quinoa paired with warmly spiced black beans, corn, avocado, and a fresh lime dressing — a complete plant-based meal in 25 minutes.
steps: Cook quinoa in vegetable broth or water with a pinch of salt, 15 minutes.
Warm black beans in a small pan with cumin, chili powder, garlic powder, and a squeeze of lime. Cook 3 minutes.
Warm frozen or canned corn. Make lime dressing: lime juice, olive oil, salt.
Divide quinoa into bowls. Top with spiced beans, corn, and sliced avocado.
Drizzle with lime dressing and scatter fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Quinoa + black beans is a complete protein pairing at under $3 per batch
Skip the avocado to cut cost and calories when on a tight budget

substitutions.swap: Brown rice for a cheaper complete-carb base
Hummus for creaminess at lower cost

recipes.name: Teriyaki Salmon with Steamed Broccoli
recipes.description: Glazed salmon fillets in a homemade teriyaki sauce served with fluffy rice and crisp steamed broccoli — a Japanese-American classic in 25 minutes.
steps: Cook rice. Mix teriyaki sauce with grated ginger and minced garlic.
Heat sesame oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high. Cook salmon 3–4 minutes per side.
In the last minute, pour teriyaki glaze over the salmon. Let it caramelize 30 seconds per side.
Steam broccoli 4–5 minutes until bright green and tender.
Plate over rice. Garnish with sesame seeds and sliced scallion.
cheapTips: Bottled teriyaki sauce is cheap and removes the need for mirin and sake
Frozen salmon fillets cost half of fresh and taste identical when glazed

substitutions.swap: Chicken breast pounded thin — cook 6 minutes per side
Bok choy or snap peas for a different green

recipes.name: Ground Turkey Taco Salad
recipes.description: Seasoned lean turkey over shredded romaine with black beans, corn, pico, avocado, and a chili-lime dressing — a taco without the tortilla that still hits.
steps: Brown ground turkey in olive oil over medium-high 6–8 minutes. Drain fat.
Add taco seasoning and ¼ cup water; simmer 2 minutes until sauce thickens.
Divide romaine among three bowls. Top with warm turkey, black beans, corn, and pico.
Add avocado slices and a squeeze of lime.
Serve with a small handful of tortilla chips for crunch.
cheapTips: Ground turkey is lean and cheap — about $4–5/lb
Skip the avocado to drop cost and save 80 kcal per serving

substitutions.swap: Skip for a fully low-carb version
Guacamole from a packet for portion control

recipes.name: Chickpea Coconut Milk Curry
recipes.description: Creamy, warming chickpea curry in a fragrant coconut-tomato base with spinach — a satisfying vegan dinner that costs $2 per serving.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot. Sauté diced onion 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and ginger 2 minutes.
Add curry powder and cumin; toast 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes and cook 3 minutes. Pour in coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add drained chickpeas. Simmer 12 minutes until sauce thickens.
Stir in spinach until wilted. Serve over rice with fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Two cans of chickpeas + one can of coconut milk is the entire protein-fat base for under $4
Make a double batch and freeze portions for the week

substitutions.swap: Light coconut milk to cut fat by half
Frozen spinach thawed and squeezed works perfectly

recipes.name: Egg-Fried Cauliflower Rice
recipes.description: Cauliflower rice stir-fried with scrambled egg, vegetables, and soy sauce — a 15-minute low-carb fried rice that's genuinely satisfying.
steps: Microwave frozen riced cauliflower 4 minutes. Spread on a clean towel and squeeze out excess moisture.
Heat sesame oil in a large skillet over high heat. Add garlic and ginger 30 seconds.
Add frozen vegetables, edamame, and corn. Stir-fry 3 minutes.
Push everything to the side. Scramble eggs in the cleared space 1–2 minutes.
Add cauliflower rice and soy sauce. Toss everything together 2 minutes. Top with scallions and sesame seeds.
cheapTips: A bag of frozen riced cauliflower costs $2–3 and contains 4 servings
Eggs are one of the cheapest complete proteins available

substitutions.swap: Any mixed vegetables you have in the freezer
Peas for a cheaper, still-protein-adjacent option

recipes.name: Turkey and Vegetable Skillet Patties
recipes.description: Lean turkey mixed with grated zucchini and onion, pan-fried into juicy skillet patties — serve as burgers or over rice for a versatile high-protein dinner.
steps: Grate zucchini and squeeze out as much moisture as possible. Finely mince onion and garlic.
Mix turkey with grated zucchini, onion, garlic, egg, and all seasonings until combined.
Form into 6 patties, pressing firmly to hold shape.
Heat olive oil over medium. Cook patties 4–5 minutes per side until cooked through.
Serve in lettuce cups or on buns with tomato and your favorite condiments.
cheapTips: Grated zucchini extends the turkey without adding calories or cost
Ground turkey costs about half of ground beef with less fat

substitutions.swap: Grated carrot or mushroom — any moisture-heavy vegetable works
Ground chicken for similar macros

recipes.name: Shrimp and Cauliflower Grits Bowl
recipes.description: Cajun shrimp nestled in creamy cauliflower grits with a simple pan sauce — a lower-carb Southern classic that still tastes deeply comforting.
steps: Microwave frozen riced cauliflower 4 minutes. In a small pot, melt butter over medium; add cauliflower rice, cream cheese, and chicken broth. Stir until creamy — 3–4 minutes.
Season shrimp with Cajun seasoning. Heat olive oil in a skillet over high heat.
Cook shrimp 1–2 minutes per side until pink. Remove; add garlic to pan for 30 seconds.
Deglaze with chicken broth and lemon juice to make a quick pan sauce.
Serve shrimp over cauliflower grits. Pour pan sauce over. Top with scallions.
cheapTips: Frozen shrimp thawed is just as good for this dish
Cauliflower grits with cream cheese taste much richer than their ingredient list suggests

substitutions.swap: Goat cheese or mascarpone for a different richness
Old Bay for a different coastal seasoning

recipes.name: Red Lentil Bolognese with Pasta
recipes.description: Red lentils simmered with aromatics, crushed tomatoes, and Italian herbs make a rich bolognese-style sauce that even meat-eaters love over pasta.
steps: Sauté diced onion and carrot in olive oil 6 minutes. Add garlic and tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Add red lentils, crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, and Italian seasoning.
Bring to a boil, then simmer 20 minutes until lentils are very soft and sauce is thick.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Reserve some pasta water.
Toss pasta with lentil bolognese (thin with pasta water if needed). Serve with parmesan.
cheapTips: Red lentils cost $2/lb and provide 18g protein per cooked cup
This sauce freezes perfectly — make a double batch

substitutions.swap: Zucchini noodles or lentil pasta for different macros
Nutritional yeast for vegan parmesan flavor

recipes.name: Chicken Fajita Bowl
recipes.description: Sizzling fajita-spiced chicken strips with caramelized peppers and onions over cilantro rice — the deconstructed fajita that tastes even better without the tortilla.
steps: Slice chicken into thin strips. Toss with taco seasoning and half the lime juice.
Cook rice; season with remaining lime juice and fresh cilantro.
Heat olive oil in a cast-iron or heavy skillet over high heat until smoking.
Cook chicken strips 5–6 minutes until charred and cooked through. Remove.
In the same pan, caramelize peppers and onion 5 minutes. Build bowls: rice, beans, chicken, peppers, sour cream.
cheapTips: Three bell peppers + one onion is less than $3 total
Taco seasoning from a packet costs under $1 and does all the flavor work

substitutions.swap: Greek yogurt for more protein at fewer calories
Cauliflower rice to drop 140 kcal

recipes.name: Edamame Shrimp Fried Rice
recipes.description: Shrimp and edamame stir-fried with day-old rice, egg, and a savory soy-sesame sauce — better than takeout and ready in 15 minutes.
steps: Use day-old cold rice (or microwave fresh rice spread on a plate to dry). Thaw edamame.
Heat sesame oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add garlic and ginger 30 seconds.
Add shrimp and cook 1–2 minutes until pink. Push to the side and scramble eggs.
Add rice, edamame, peas, and soy sauce. Stir-fry everything together 3–4 minutes until rice is lightly crispy.
Plate and scatter sliced scallions on top.
cheapTips: Frozen shrimp and frozen edamame are the two protein powerhouses here — both affordable frozen
Day-old rice is actually better for fried rice — plan ahead

substitutions.swap: Diced tofu for a vegan protein option
Cauliflower rice for a lower-carb version

recipes.name: Baked Salmon with Lemon Caper Sauce
recipes.description: Salmon fillets roasted to silky perfection with a bright lemon-caper-butter sauce — an elegant dinner that's embarrassingly easy.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Season salmon with salt, pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil.
Bake salmon 12–15 minutes until it flakes at the thickest part.
While salmon bakes, make the sauce: melt butter in a small pan over medium. Add minced garlic 1 minute.
Add lemon juice, dijon mustard, and a pinch of capers or a squeeze of lemon zest. Whisk together 1 minute.
Serve salmon over brown rice. Spoon sauce over and garnish with fresh parsley.
cheapTips: Frozen salmon fillets cost half as much as fresh and taste identical when baked
Lemon + dijon + butter is the simplest luxurious sauce you can make

substitutions.swap: Quinoa or roasted vegetables for different macros
Olive oil for a dairy-free sauce

recipes.name: Turkey Chili with Cornbread Topping
recipes.description: A thick, smoky turkey and bean chili baked with a golden cornbread crust — cozy one-dish comfort food that feeds a crowd for under $10.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Sauté onion in olive oil 4 minutes. Add garlic, chili powder, cumin, and paprika; toast 1 minute.
Add ground turkey and cook 6–8 minutes. Add crushed tomatoes and beans. Simmer 10 minutes. Season well.
Make quick cornbread batter: mix flour, corn, sugar, baking powder, salt, milk, and egg until just combined.
Transfer chili to an oven-safe dish. Spread cornbread batter over the top.
Bake 20–22 minutes until cornbread is golden and cooked through. Rest 5 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Ground turkey is lean and cheap; the whole dish costs under $2/serving
Canned kidney beans do double protein duty here — use two cans

substitutions.swap: Ground beef for a classic chili flavor
Cornmeal or a box of Jiffy mix for authentic cornbread

recipes.name: Tuna Niçoise Power Bowl
recipes.description: Canned tuna, hard-boiled eggs, green beans, cherry tomatoes, and olives over mixed greens with a Dijon vinaigrette — a French classic made fast and affordable.
steps: Boil small potatoes 12 minutes until tender; cool and halve. Simultaneously hard-boil eggs 9 minutes.
Make vinaigrette: whisk dijon, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Arrange mixed greens on plates. Add tuna (drained and flaked), halved eggs, potato, and tomato.
Drizzle generously with vinaigrette.
Finish with fresh parsley.
cheapTips: Canned tuna provides 25g protein per can for under $1.50
Hard-boiled eggs are the cheapest protein per gram available

substitutions.swap: Canned salmon for more omega-3s at a similar price
Skip for a lower-carb version, or swap for white beans

recipes.name: Dal Tadka with Basmati Rice
recipes.description: Silky yellow lentils simmered with turmeric and finished with a sizzling tempering of garlic, cumin, and chili — an Indian comfort staple that costs almost nothing.
steps: Rinse red or yellow lentils. Simmer in 4 cups water with turmeric and a pinch of salt for 20 minutes until very soft. Mash slightly.
Sauté diced onion in 1 tbsp oil 5 minutes until golden. Add garlic, ginger, and diced tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes.
Stir onion-tomato masala into the cooked lentils. Add garam masala and simmer 5 minutes.
Make the tadka (tempering): heat remaining oil in a small pan. Add cumin seeds and red chili; sizzle 30 seconds. Immediately pour over the dal.
Serve over basmati rice with fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Lentils are one of the cheapest plant proteins — $2/lb feeds a family
Dal stores for 5 days and actually improves on reheating

substitutions.swap: Red lentils cook faster (15 min) and make a silkier dal
Curry powder for a slightly different but equally delicious spice blend

recipes.name: Turmeric Tofu Scramble Bowl
recipes.description: Crumbled tofu scrambled with turmeric, vegetables, and nutritional yeast for a cheesy umami flavor — a hearty vegan breakfast or dinner bowl.
steps: Press tofu 5 minutes, then crumble into small pieces resembling scrambled egg texture.
Sauté diced onion and bell pepper in olive oil 3 minutes. Add garlic 1 minute.
Add crumbled tofu, turmeric, soy sauce, and salt. Stir and cook 3 minutes.
Stir in nutritional yeast and spinach until spinach wilts, 1 minute.
Serve in a bowl with sliced avocado and toast on the side.
cheapTips: A block of firm tofu costs $2–3 and replaces 4 eggs of protein
Nutritional yeast adds a cheesy umami flavor for under $5 for a whole bag

substitutions.swap: Skip it — the tofu is still good with just turmeric and soy sauce
Sliced tomato for a lower-calorie topping

recipes.name: Italian Sausage White Bean and Kale
recipes.description: Browned Italian sausage with creamy white beans and wilted kale in a light white wine-chicken broth sauce — a one-pot dinner that tastes like it took hours.
steps: Slice sausage into rounds. Brown in olive oil over medium-high 3–4 minutes per side.
Add sliced onion and garlic; cook 3 minutes until softened.
Add red pepper flakes and drained white beans; stir 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth and add chopped kale. Simmer 5–7 minutes until kale is tender.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon. Serve topped with parmesan.
cheapTips: Italian sausage links or bulk sausage cost under $5/lb and add loads of flavor
White beans are one of the most underrated protein-and-fiber ingredients at $1/can

substitutions.swap: Turkey sausage or chicken sausage for a leaner option
Spinach — add in the last minute so it doesn't overcook

recipes.name: Greek Chicken and Orzo Lemon Soup
recipes.description: Bright, lemony chicken soup with tender orzo pasta — inspired by the Greek avgolemono, made easy without the egg-tempering step.
steps: Sauté diced onion, carrot, and celery in olive oil 5 minutes. Add garlic and oregano 1 minute.
Add chicken breasts whole and chicken broth. Bring to a boil; reduce and simmer 15 minutes until chicken is cooked.
Remove chicken and shred with two forks. Return to pot.
Add orzo (or small pasta) and cook 8 minutes until al dente.
Squeeze in lemon juice generously. Taste and season. Serve with fresh parsley.
cheapTips: Chicken breast poached directly in the broth is the easiest and most flavorful approach
Orzo is cheap pasta — any small pasta shape works

substitutions.swap: Rice for a more traditional avgolemono-adjacent soup
Rotisserie chicken meat added at the end to skip the cooking step

recipes.name: Beef Bulgogi Rice Bowl
recipes.description: Thinly sliced beef marinated in a soy-pear-sesame sauce and sizzled in a hot pan — the beloved Korean BBQ in a 20-minute weeknight bowl.
steps: Cook rice. Mix marinade: soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and gochugaru.
Make quick cucumber banchan: thinly slice cucumber, toss with rice vinegar, sesame oil, salt, and sesame seeds.
Cook ground beef in a hot pan 5–6 minutes until browned. Drain fat. Add marinade sauce; cook 2 minutes until caramelized.
Build bowls: rice, bulgogi beef, and cucumber on the side.
Top with scallions and extra sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Ground beef is an excellent budget substitute for thinly-sliced ribeye in bulgogi
Gochugaru (Korean chili flakes) can be found at Asian grocery stores for very cheap

substitutions.swap: Ground turkey for a leaner option
Regular red pepper flakes — use half the quantity

recipes.name: Cottage Cheese and Berry Power Bowl
recipes.description: Creamy cottage cheese topped with fresh berries, granola, honey, and a sprinkle of seeds — a high-protein breakfast that takes 3 minutes to assemble.
steps: Spoon cottage cheese into a bowl. Stir in a drop of vanilla extract if desired.
Top with fresh or thawed frozen blueberries and sliced strawberries.
Scatter granola for crunch.
Drizzle with honey and a sprinkle of seeds.
Eat immediately or refrigerate for up to 2 hours (granola softens over time).
cheapTips: Cottage cheese provides 25g protein per cup — cheaper than Greek yogurt in many stores
Frozen berries thawed overnight are just as good and cost half as much

substitutions.swap: Any fruit you have — banana, peach, mango
Skip to reduce sugar and calories, or use nuts for crunch

recipes.name: Cajun Chicken and Vegetable Pasta
recipes.description: Sliced Cajun-spiced chicken tossed with colorful bell peppers and onions in a light cream sauce over pasta — bold Southern flavor in 25 minutes.
steps: Cook pasta; reserve ½ cup pasta water.
Slice chicken breast and toss with Cajun seasoning.
Sear chicken in olive oil over medium-high 3–4 minutes per side until cooked. Remove.
Add garlic, onion, and peppers to the same pan; cook 4 minutes until softened.
Add cream cheese and chicken broth; whisk into a sauce. Add pasta and pasta water. Return chicken. Toss and serve with parsley.
cheapTips: Cajun seasoning is one spice blend that punches way above its cost
Cream cheese makes a quick, rich sauce with zero effort — 1 oz goes far

substitutions.swap: Greek yogurt stirred in at the end off the heat for a lighter sauce
Zucchini noodles for a low-carb version

recipes.name: Marinated Tempeh Buddha Bowl
recipes.description: Nutty, protein-rich tempeh marinated in soy-ginger sauce and pan-seared over a vibrant bowl of brown rice, roasted vegetables, and a creamy tahini dressing.
steps: Slice tempeh into strips. Marinate in soy sauce, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil for 5 minutes.
Cook brown rice. Cube sweet potato and roast at 400°F with olive oil 20 minutes.
Pan-sear marinated tempeh over medium 2–3 minutes per side until golden.
Steam or roast broccoli. Make dressing: whisk tahini, lemon juice, water, salt.
Build bowls: rice, sweet potato, broccoli, tempeh. Drizzle with tahini dressing. Top with scallions and sesame.
cheapTips: Tempeh costs about $2–4 per block and provides 30g protein — excellent value
Tahini dressing elevates the whole bowl and takes 1 minute to make

substitutions.swap: Tofu if tempeh isn't available — press and marinate the same way
Butternut squash or regular potato

recipes.name: Lightened Butter Chicken
recipes.description: Creamy, gently spiced tomato-based chicken curry made lighter with Greek yogurt instead of heavy cream — still deeply warming, still addictive over basmati rice.
steps: Cut chicken into chunks. Marinate in half the Greek yogurt, half the garam masala, and a pinch of salt for 5 minutes.
Heat butter and oil in a large pan. Sear marinated chicken 3–4 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté diced onion 5 minutes. Add garlic and ginger paste; cook 2 minutes. Add remaining spices and toast 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes and simmer 8 minutes until sauce deepens. Stir in remaining Greek yogurt off heat.
Return chicken to the sauce and simmer 5 minutes. Serve over basmati rice with cilantro.
cheapTips: Greek yogurt is the secret lighter-cream swap — costs a fraction of heavy cream
Chicken breast keeps fat low; thighs work too and are even cheaper

substitutions.swap: Light coconut milk for a dairy-free version
Chickpeas for a vegetarian butter chickpea

recipes.name: Palak Paneer-Style Tofu
recipes.description: Silky blended spinach curry with cubed pan-fried tofu standing in for paneer — a deeply satisfying vegan take on the Indian classic.
steps: Press tofu and cube. Pan-fry in olive oil 3–4 minutes per side until golden. Set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onion 5 minutes. Add garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, and garam masala; cook 2 minutes.
Add diced tomato and cook 4 minutes until softened. Add thawed spinach.
Blend the spinach-tomato mixture until smooth (use immersion blender or pour into blender). Return to pan.
Stir in coconut milk, season, and simmer 5 minutes. Fold in tofu cubes gently. Serve over rice.
cheapTips: Frozen spinach is much cheaper than fresh and blends perfectly into this sauce
One block of tofu costs about $2 and provides the entire protein base

substitutions.swap: Paneer cheese for a non-vegan version closer to the original
Plain plant-based yogurt for a tangier, lower-fat sauce

recipes.name: Chana Masala with Rice
recipes.description: Boldly spiced chickpeas in a tangy tomato-onion gravy — the beloved North Indian street food that costs pennies to make at home.
steps: Finely chop onion and cook in olive oil 6–7 minutes until golden. Add minced garlic and ginger; cook 2 minutes.
Add all dry spices and tomato paste; toast 1 minute. Add crushed tomatoes and simmer 5 minutes.
Drain and rinse chickpeas. Add to the sauce with ½ cup water. Simmer 10 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Finish with lemon juice and fresh cilantro. Season generously.
Serve over basmati rice.
cheapTips: Two cans of chickpeas cost under $2 and feed four people
Chana masala is one of the most affordable Indian dishes to make at home

substitutions.swap: Two fresh tomatoes blended for a lighter sauce
Ground coriander (same amount) — saves buying whole seeds

recipes.name: Chicken Tikka Bowl
recipes.description: Yogurt-marinated chicken tikka broiled until charred and fragrant, served bowl-style over rice with raita and cucumber — Indian BBQ at home.
steps: Cut chicken into large chunks. Mix yogurt, garam masala, cumin, paprika, turmeric, garlic, ginger, and lemon juice to make tikka marinade.
Coat chicken thoroughly. Marinate 10 minutes (or overnight for deeper flavor).
Thread onto skewers or spread on a lined baking sheet. Broil 8–10 minutes, flipping halfway, until charred on edges.
Make raita: mix remaining yogurt with diced cucumber, a pinch of cumin, and salt.
Serve tikka over rice with raita and fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Greek yogurt marinade tenderizes the chicken while adding protein
Broiling gives the charred tikka effect without a tandoor

substitutions.swap: Chicken thighs stay juicier and cost less
Naan bread for a more takeout-style experience

recipes.name: Rajma (Kidney Bean Curry) with Rice
recipes.description: Punjabi-style kidney bean curry slowly simmered with aromatic spices until the beans are creamy and the sauce is rich — a north Indian Sunday classic for under $3.
steps: Sauté finely diced onion in olive oil 8 minutes until deeply golden — this is the flavor foundation.
Add garlic and ginger; cook 2 minutes. Add all dry spices and tomato paste; toast 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes, simmer 5 minutes. Drain and add kidney beans.
Simmer 15 minutes. Mash about ¼ of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the sauce.
Finish with garam masala and cilantro. Serve over basmati rice.
cheapTips: Two cans of kidney beans is the whole protein base for under $2
The long onion cook is the secret — don't rush it

substitutions.swap: Black beans for a similar flavor profile
Two large diced fresh tomatoes when in season

recipes.name: Aloo Gobi with Lentils
recipes.description: The beloved Indian potato-cauliflower stir-fry elevated with red lentils for protein — fragrant with cumin, turmeric, and coriander.
steps: Cook red lentils in 1.5 cups water 12 minutes until just soft. Drain.
Cube potatoes into 1-inch pieces. Heat oil, add cumin seeds (or ground cumin) and sizzle 30 seconds.
Add onion, garlic, ginger; cook 5 minutes. Add remaining spices and diced tomatoes; cook 3 minutes.
Add potato cubes with ¼ cup water. Cover and steam 12 minutes until tender.
Fold in cooked lentils; heat through 2 minutes. Finish with cilantro. Serve over rice.
cheapTips: Potatoes are one of the cheapest calorie sources — about $0.20 each
Red lentils add 9g protein per serving for about $0.25

substitutions.swap: Sweet potato for more fiber and vitamins
Chickpeas for a chunkier, less blended texture

recipes.name: Saag Chicken
recipes.description: Tender chicken pieces in a velvety blended spinach gravy spiced with garam masala and ginger — richer than palak paneer, fully restaurant-worthy.
steps: Cut chicken thighs into pieces. Season with salt, a pinch of turmeric, and garam masala.
Brown chicken in olive oil 5–6 minutes. Remove from pan.
Sauté onion 5 minutes. Add garlic, ginger, cumin, and remaining spices; cook 2 minutes. Add tomatoes and cook 4 minutes.
Add thawed spinach and blend the entire sauce with an immersion blender until smooth.
Return chicken to the pan. Simmer in the saag sauce 10 minutes. Serve over rice with cilantro.
cheapTips: Frozen spinach blends into a perfectly smooth sauce and costs a fraction of fresh
Chicken thighs stay juicy even after the long simmer

substitutions.swap: Chicken breast for a leaner option
Any leafy green — kale, mustard greens, or fresh spinach

recipes.name: Tandoori-Spiced Shrimp with Basmati
recipes.description: Shrimp marinated in tandoori yogurt spices and grilled or pan-seared until smoky at the edges — paired with fragrant basmati and raita.
steps: Marinate shrimp in half the yogurt, garam masala, paprika, cumin, turmeric, garlic, ginger, and lemon juice for 5 minutes.
Cook rice. Sear marinated shrimp in olive oil over high heat 1–2 minutes per side until charred at edges.
Make raita: mix remaining yogurt, diced cucumber, a pinch of cumin, and salt.
Serve shrimp over rice with raita and fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Frozen shrimp thawed overnight is the same quality as fresh for marinated dishes
The yogurt marinade takes 5 minutes and does all the flavor work

substitutions.swap: Firm tofu cubes for a vegan tandoori option
Naan or pita for a different experience

recipes.name: Moong Dal Soup
recipes.description: A light, healing yellow mung bean soup tempered with cumin and garlic — the Indian equivalent of chicken noodle soup, ready in 30 minutes.
steps: Rinse yellow moong dal (or red lentils). Simmer with turmeric and 4 cups water 20 minutes until mushy.
Make tadka: heat olive oil in a small pan. Add cumin and let it sizzle 30 seconds. Add onion and cook 4 minutes. Add garlic and ginger 2 minutes. Add tomatoes; cook 4 minutes.
Pour tadka into the dal; stir to combine. Add spinach; wilt 1 minute.
Finish with lemon juice and fresh cilantro. Season with salt.
Serve with bread or rice for a heartier meal.
cheapTips: Moong dal or red lentils cost $1–2/lb and make 4 generous servings
The simplest, most healing meal in Indian cooking — total cost under $2

substitutions.swap: Yellow split peas for a slightly different texture
Any leafy green wilts beautifully into dal

recipes.name: Egg Curry with Rice
recipes.description: Hard-boiled eggs simmered in a spiced onion-tomato gravy — an underrated Indian dish that's protein-rich, vegetarian, and deeply flavorful.
steps: Hard-boil 6 eggs: cover with cold water, bring to boil, simmer 9 minutes, ice bath, peel.
Score the eggs lightly with a knife so the sauce can penetrate.
Sauté onion in olive oil 6 minutes until deeply golden. Add garlic and ginger 2 minutes. Add all spices and toast 1 minute. Add crushed tomatoes; simmer 6 minutes.
Gently nestle eggs into the sauce. Simmer 5 minutes, spooning sauce over them.
Serve over rice with cilantro.
cheapTips: Six eggs feed three people for under $1.50 total — one of the cheapest proteins available
Egg curry is a brilliant use of pantry ingredients when the fridge is low

substitutions.swap: Tofu cubes pan-fried for a vegan version
Two large fresh tomatoes diced

recipes.name: Chicken Pad See Ew
recipes.description: Wide rice noodles stir-fried with chicken, egg, and Chinese broccoli in a sweet dark-soy sauce — Thailand's beloved noodle dish in 20 minutes.
steps: Soak rice noodles in warm water 15 minutes until pliable; drain.
Make sauce: combine soy sauce, dark soy, oyster sauce, and brown sugar.
Heat sesame oil in a wok over high. Stir-fry sliced chicken 3–4 minutes until cooked. Push to the side; scramble eggs.
Add broccoli and noodles. Pour sauce over and toss everything 2–3 minutes until noodles absorb the sauce.
Finish with white pepper and minced garlic.
cheapTips: Rice noodles are cheap and soak up the sauce beautifully — any width works
Dark soy adds the signature color; regular soy works but the dish will be lighter

substitutions.swap: Tofu for a vegan version
Regular soy sauce plus a pinch of brown sugar for similar color

recipes.name: Thai Larb Chicken Salad
recipes.description: Ground chicken cooked with lime juice, fish sauce, and toasted rice powder — a light, herb-forward Thai salad that's surprisingly filling.
steps: Toast 1 tbsp uncooked rice in a dry pan 3 minutes until golden; cool and grind to a coarse powder.
Cook ground turkey in olive oil over medium-high 5–6 minutes, breaking apart. Don't let it dry out completely.
Off heat, dress with lime juice, fish sauce, and chili flakes. Fold in sliced shallots.
Transfer to a platter over lettuce. Top with fresh mint, cilantro, scallions, and toasted rice powder.
Serve with extra lime wedges.
cheapTips: Ground turkey is cheaper than ground chicken with nearly identical flavor here
Fresh herbs are the soul of larb — don't skimp on mint and cilantro

substitutions.swap: Soy sauce + a squeeze of lime for a vegan version
Ground pork for the more traditional version

recipes.name: Tom Yum Shrimp Soup
recipes.description: Thailand's iconic hot-and-sour soup with shrimp, mushrooms, and fresh lime — a bold, aromatic broth that takes 20 minutes to make.
steps: Bring broth to a simmer. Add red curry paste, ginger, garlic, and Thai chilis; simmer 3 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms and cook 3 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook 2–3 minutes until pink.
Season with fish sauce and generous lime juice — it should be bright, sour, and spicy.
Serve over rice in deep bowls with scallion and cilantro.
cheapTips: Tom yum paste or red curry paste is a convenient shortcut to complex flavor
Mushrooms add body and umami for under $2/pack

substitutions.swap: Tofu or chicken for the protein
Tom yum paste for a more authentic base

recipes.name: Thai Basil Ground Beef Stir-Fry
recipes.description: Ground beef stir-fried with garlic, Thai chilis, and fragrant basil in a savory oyster-soy sauce — pad kra pao made fast and cheap over jasmine rice.
steps: Cook rice. Combine oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, and brown sugar into a stir-fry sauce.
Heat sesame oil in a wok over screaming-high heat. Add minced garlic and chilis; stir 30 seconds.
Add ground beef; stir-fry 4–5 minutes until cooked through. Drain excess fat.
Add sauce and toss 1 minute. Remove from heat; fold in fresh basil leaves.
Fry eggs sunny-side up. Serve beef over rice with a fried egg.
cheapTips: Ground beef is the classic protein for this dish — cheaper cuts work fine as they're fully broken up
A fried egg on top is the Thai street food touch that completes the meal

substitutions.swap: Ground turkey or chicken for a leaner option
Red pepper flakes — use ¼ tsp per chili called for

recipes.name: Green Curry Tofu and Vegetables
recipes.description: Creamy green curry with crispy tofu, bell pepper, and zucchini in coconut milk — a Thai-inspired vegan dinner with restaurant flavors.
steps: Press tofu and cube. Pan-fry in sesame oil 3–4 minutes per side until golden.
In the same pan, add green curry paste and garlic; stir-fry 1 minute until fragrant.
Add coconut milk and broth; bring to a simmer.
Add bell pepper and zucchini; cook 5 minutes. Add soy sauce and lime juice.
Fold in tofu and fresh basil. Serve over jasmine rice.
cheapTips: Green curry paste costs about $1–2 for a whole jar — use 2 tbsp for intense flavor
Coconut milk is the affordable luxury that makes this taste like restaurant food

substitutions.swap: Chickpeas for a bean-based protein
Red or yellow curry paste — each has a slightly different flavor profile

recipes.name: Vietnamese Chicken Pho
recipes.description: A fragrant ginger-and-spice broth with shredded chicken and rice noodles — a shortcut chicken pho that tastes like it simmered all day.
steps: Char ginger (halved) and garlic directly over a gas flame or in a dry pan 3 minutes until slightly blackened.
Add chicken broth, charred ginger, garlic, cinnamon, and a pinch of cloves. Simmer 10 minutes.
Poach chicken breasts in the broth 12 minutes. Remove, shred, and return to broth.
Soak rice noodles in warm water 15 minutes; blanch in boiling water 30 seconds.
Add fish sauce to season. Serve noodles in bowls, ladle broth and chicken over. Top with scallions, lime, cilantro, and sriracha.
cheapTips: Charring the ginger and garlic is the trick that gives pho its complex smoky depth
Store-bought broth works fine — enhance it with the charred aromatics

substitutions.swap: Zucchini noodles for a low-carb pho
Rotisserie chicken shredded in saves 15 minutes

recipes.name: Bun Cha-Style Pork Meatball Rice Noodles
recipes.description: Grilled pork meatballs in a sweet fish sauce dipping broth with cold rice noodles and fresh herbs — Hanoi's famous street food in a bowl.
steps: Mix ground turkey with minced garlic, ginger, a splash of fish sauce, and sesame oil. Roll into 18 small meatballs.
Pan-fry meatballs in a lightly oiled pan 3–4 minutes per side until cooked through and slightly caramelized.
Make dipping broth: mix fish sauce, brown sugar, lime juice, and ½ cup warm water until sugar dissolves.
Cook rice noodles and rinse cold.
Serve cold noodles in bowls, meatballs alongside, dipping broth poured over. Top with lettuce, mint, cilantro, and cucumber.
cheapTips: Ground turkey is a leaner substitute for pork that still makes great meatballs
Fish sauce costs about $3 for a whole bottle that lasts months

substitutions.swap: Ground pork for the traditional version
Soy sauce + lime for a non-fish sauce version

recipes.name: Singapore-Style Curry Shrimp Noodles
recipes.description: Thin rice vermicelli stir-fried with shrimp, egg, and vegetables in a fragrant curry powder — one of Singapore's most famous hawker dishes.
steps: Soak thin rice noodles (vermicelli) in warm water 10 minutes; drain.
Heat sesame oil in a wok over high. Stir-fry garlic and ginger 30 seconds.
Add shrimp 1–2 minutes per side. Push to side; scramble eggs.
Add bell pepper and onion; stir-fry 2 minutes. Add noodles, curry powder, and soy sauce.
Toss everything together 2 minutes until noodles are evenly golden-yellow from the curry. Top with scallion.
cheapTips: Curry powder is the entire flavor base — a $2 jar goes a long way
Thin rice noodles cook faster and cost less than thicker noodles

substitutions.swap: Diced tofu or chicken for a different protein
Turmeric + cumin + coriander for a DIY mix

recipes.name: Chicken Japchae Glass Noodles
recipes.description: Korean sweet potato glass noodles stir-fried with chicken, spinach, mushrooms, and a sweet soy-sesame dressing — a festive dish that works for everyday eating.
steps: Cook glass noodles (or use soba as substitute) according to package directions; rinse cold. Toss with 1 tsp sesame oil.
Make japchae sauce: soy sauce, sesame oil, brown sugar, garlic.
Stir-fry sliced chicken 4–5 minutes. Remove. Stir-fry mushroom, carrot, and onion 3 minutes. Add spinach to wilt.
Combine noodles, vegetables, and chicken in the pan. Add sauce and toss over medium heat 2 minutes.
Finish with sesame seeds and scallion.
cheapTips: Soba noodles are a good substitute for glass noodles and widely available
Japchae keeps well for 3 days — make extra

substitutions.swap: True sweet potato glass noodles (dangmyeon) from an Asian grocery
Ground beef for a more traditional japchae

recipes.name: Mapo Tofu Rice Bowl
recipes.description: Silky tofu in a spicy, numbing Sichuan-inspired sauce with ground beef and fermented black beans — a bold, warming bowl that costs $3 per serving.
steps: Cut tofu into 1-inch cubes. Cook rice.
Brown ground beef in sesame oil 3–4 minutes. Add garlic and ginger 1 minute.
Add gochujang, soy sauce, and chili flakes; stir 1 minute.
Pour in broth. Gently nestle tofu in the sauce and simmer 4–5 minutes.
Serve over rice, topped with sliced scallion.
cheapTips: Half a pound of beef + one block of tofu for 3 servings is the budget-conscious split
Gochujang is a Korean fermented paste — one tub lasts months

substitutions.swap: Ground turkey for a leaner version
Doubanjiang for the true Sichuan version if available

recipes.name: Lightened Chicken Marsala
recipes.description: Thin chicken cutlets in a Marsala wine and mushroom pan sauce made lighter with broth instead of heavy cream — an Italian-American classic in 25 minutes.
steps: Pound chicken breasts to ½-inch thickness. Season with salt, pepper, and dredge lightly in flour.
Sear chicken in olive oil over medium-high 3–4 minutes per side until golden. Remove.
In the same pan, sauté shallot 2 minutes. Add mushrooms and garlic; cook 4–5 minutes until golden.
Deglaze with ¼ cup red wine (or extra broth). Add chicken broth, thyme, and butter; simmer 3 minutes.
Return chicken; simmer in sauce 3 minutes. Serve over brown rice with parsley.
cheapTips: Thin pounded chicken breast cooks fast and stretches further
Skip the wine if you don't have it — extra broth with a splash of vinegar works

substitutions.swap: Turkey cutlets or thin pork chops
Any mushroom variety — cremini, shiitake, or white button

recipes.name: Pasta e Fagioli
recipes.description: Italy's humble pasta-and-bean soup — a thick, warming bowl of cannellini beans, small pasta, and vegetables in a savory tomato broth. Under $2 per serving.
steps: Sauté diced onion, carrot, and celery in olive oil 6 minutes. Add garlic and rosemary 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes and Italian seasoning; simmer 4 minutes.
Add broth and one can of drained beans. Simmer 5 minutes.
Blend one ladle of soup (or use an immersion blender on a corner of the pot) for a creamier texture.
Add remaining beans and small pasta. Cook 8–10 minutes until pasta is al dente. Serve with parmesan.
cheapTips: Two cans of white beans + a handful of pasta = substantial protein for $3
This soup is even better the next day — the pasta absorbs the broth and thickens it

substitutions.swap: Cannellini or borlotti beans for a more Italian version
Nutritional yeast for a vegan parmesan flavor

recipes.name: Salmon Puttanesca Pasta
recipes.description: Canned salmon tossed with a bold olive-caper-tomato puttanesca sauce over pasta — no-cook protein with a pantry sauce that tastes luxurious.
steps: Cook pasta. Heat olive oil in a pan; add garlic, red pepper flakes, and anchovy paste (if using). Cook 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes; simmer 8 minutes until sauce deepens.
Drain and flake canned salmon. Fold gently into the sauce.
Toss with drained pasta, a squeeze of lemon, and parsley.
Taste and season — puttanesca should be punchy and salty.
cheapTips: Canned salmon costs $2–3/can and has more omega-3s than many fresh options
Anchovy paste is optional but adds that deep savory layer for about $0.10 worth

substitutions.swap: Canned tuna works great here too
Skip or use a dash of worcestershire sauce

recipes.name: Tuscan Ribollita Bean and Bread Soup
recipes.description: Thick Tuscan stew of white beans, kale, and stale bread slow-cooked into a hearty, silky soup — the original peasant food that's had a gourmet revival.
steps: Sauté onion, carrot, and celery in olive oil 6 minutes. Add garlic and rosemary 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes; cook 4 minutes. Pour in broth.
Add drained white beans and chopped kale. Simmer 15 minutes.
Tear stale bread into chunks (or use toasted bread). Stir into the soup.
Simmer 10 more minutes until bread dissolves and soup thickens into a porridge-like stew. Season and serve with good olive oil.
cheapTips: Day-old bread is traditionally used — this is the dish that was invented to use up stale bread
The whole pot costs under $6 and improves over 3 days

substitutions.swap: Cavolo nero (black kale) is traditional; spinach works too
Croutons or skip for a gluten-free version

recipes.name: Chicken Piccata with Zucchini Noodles
recipes.description: Thin chicken cutlets in a bright lemon-caper-white wine sauce served over zucchini noodles — elegant Italian cooking that's naturally low-carb.
steps: Pound chicken to ½-inch thick. Season and dredge lightly in flour.
Sear in olive oil 3–4 minutes per side until golden. Remove from pan.
Add garlic 30 seconds. Deglaze with broth and lemon juice (leave out wine if not available). Add butter.
Spiralize or ribbon-cut zucchini; sauté 2 minutes in the pan.
Return chicken to the sauce. Serve over zucchini noodles with parsley.
cheapTips: Zucchini noodles cost about $1–2 per zucchini and make this naturally low-carb
Lemon and chicken broth do all the sauce work — no wine needed

substitutions.swap: Regular pasta or cauliflower rice for different macros
Olive oil for a dairy-free version

recipes.name: French Onion-Style Chicken Skillet
recipes.description: Juicy chicken nestled in deeply caramelized onions with a Gruyère-melted finish — all the magic of French onion soup on a skillet chicken dinner.
steps: Thinly slice 3 onions. Melt butter and oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-low. Add onions and a pinch of salt. Cook 20–25 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until deeply caramelized.
Push onions to the side. Raise heat to medium-high. Season chicken and sear skin-side down 4 minutes until golden.
Add garlic, thyme, and broth. Nestle chicken in the onions.
Simmer 10 minutes covered, then remove lid and cook 5 minutes more.
Top chicken with shredded cheese and broil 2 minutes until bubbly. Serve over rice.
cheapTips: The patience in caramelizing onions is the entire secret — don't rush it
Cheap yellow onions become something magical after 25 minutes of heat

substitutions.swap: Gruyère is traditional; Swiss or provolone work well
Chicken broth or water — any liquid deglazes the pan

recipes.name: Spanish Chickpea and Spinach Tapas Bowl
recipes.description: Espinacas con garbanzos — a classic Andalusian tapa of chickpeas with spinach in a garlicky tomato-cumin sauce served over crusty bread or rice.
steps: Heat olive oil over medium. Add garlic and cook 1 minute. Add smoked paprika and cumin; toast 30 seconds.
Add crushed tomatoes and cook 3 minutes. Add drained chickpeas.
Add fresh spinach and stir until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Add a splash of red wine vinegar and lemon juice for brightness. Season.
Serve with crusty bread for scooping.
cheapTips: Two cans of chickpeas is the cheapest plant protein base — under $2
Smoked paprika is the key spice — worth buying a small tin

substitutions.swap: Frozen spinach thawed — add and stir vigorously
Brown rice or skip for a grain-free meal

recipes.name: German Lentil and Turkey Sausage Soup
recipes.description: Hearty brown lentil soup with sliced turkey sausage, smoked paprika, and mustard — deeply satisfying German-style comfort in a bowl.
steps: Slice sausage into rounds. Brown in olive oil 3–4 minutes; remove.
Sauté onion, carrot, and celery in same pot 5 minutes. Add garlic and paprika 1 minute.
Add lentils and broth. Bring to a boil; simmer 25 minutes until lentils are very tender.
Stir in dijon mustard and red wine vinegar for a traditional German tang.
Return sausage; simmer 5 minutes. Serve with parsley.
cheapTips: Brown lentils hold their shape in soup better than red — ideal for this dish
Turkey sausage costs less than pork while keeping the smoky flavor

substitutions.swap: Smoked kielbasa for a more authentic German flavor
Whole-grain mustard for more texture in the finished soup

recipes.name: Greek Avgolemono Chicken Soup
recipes.description: Greece's silky egg-lemon chicken soup with orzo — bright, comforting, and almost absurdly easy when made with the shortcut method.
steps: Poach chicken breasts in broth with onion and garlic 15 minutes. Remove; shred.
Add rice to the simmering broth; cook 15 minutes until tender.
In a bowl, whisk 3 eggs with lemon juice vigorously. Slowly ladle 1 cup of hot broth into the egg mixture while whisking (tempering).
Pour the tempered egg-lemon mixture back into the pot slowly while stirring. Heat gently — do not boil.
Fold in shredded chicken. Season. Serve with parsley and extra lemon.
cheapTips: Avgolemono is pure pantry magic — chicken, eggs, lemon, broth
The egg-tempering step is what creates the silky texture — take your time

substitutions.swap: Orzo or any small pasta for a different texture
Rotisserie chicken shredded in saves 15 minutes of poaching

recipes.name: West African Jollof Chicken Rice
recipes.description: The iconic West African one-pot rice dish — chicken thighs simmered with tomatoes, peppers, and spices until the rice turns a brilliant red-orange and every grain is smoky.
steps: Blend crushed tomatoes, 1 onion, and bell peppers into a smooth red paste.
Season chicken with smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Brown in olive oil 4 minutes per side. Remove.
Fry the remaining diced onion in the same pot 5 minutes. Add garlic and tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Add the blended pepper-tomato paste. Fry on medium-high, stirring often, 10–12 minutes until deeply reduced and oil separates.
Add rice, broth, thyme, bay leaf, and cayenne. Nestle chicken in. Cover tightly; cook on low 25 minutes until rice is done.
cheapTips: Jollof is a one-pot dish — everything cooks together for minimal effort
The slow tomato fry (step 4) is what develops the characteristic deep flavor

substitutions.swap: Chicken breast or drumsticks
More paprika for a milder version

recipes.name: Jamaican Jerk Chicken and Rice
recipes.description: Chicken thighs marinated in a fiery, fragrant jerk spice blend and baked until smoky — served over rice and peas for the full Jamaican experience.
steps: Make jerk marinade: blend garlic, ginger, allspice, cayenne, paprika, thyme, brown sugar, soy sauce, lime juice, and oil.
Coat chicken thighs thoroughly. Marinate 10 minutes (or overnight for best results).
Bake at 425°F 30–35 minutes until crispy and caramelized at the edges.
Make rice and peas: cook rice with drained kidney beans, a pinch of thyme, and scallion.
Serve jerk chicken over rice and peas with lime wedges.
cheapTips: Jerk spices are pantry staples — no jerk paste needed
Marinating even for 10 minutes makes a big difference; overnight is incredible

substitutions.swap: Bone-in drumsticks for an even cheaper and more authentic presentation
Any bean works in the rice for the 'rice and peas' element

recipes.name: Cuban Black Beans and Rice
recipes.description: The heart of Cuban cooking — black beans slow-simmered with sofrito (onion, garlic, peppers), cumin, and bay leaf until creamy and deeply flavorful.
steps: Make sofrito: finely dice onion, garlic, and green pepper. Sauté in olive oil 6 minutes.
Add cumin, oregano, and tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Add drained black beans and 1 cup water. Add bay leaf. Simmer 15 minutes, mashing some beans for thickness.
Finish with red wine vinegar for brightness and cilantro. Season generously.
Serve over white rice. Cuban beans should be saucy — use a ladle.
cheapTips: Two cans of black beans is the entire protein base for under $2
Red wine vinegar is the finishing touch that makes Cuban beans taste authentic

substitutions.swap: Any color pepper — green is traditional in Cuban cooking
A squeeze of lime for a brighter finish

recipes.name: Haitian-Style Chicken and Vegetable Stew
recipes.description: A vibrant Haitian stew of chicken and soft-cooked vegetables in a rich Epis-spiced broth — warming, colorful, and deeply comforting.
steps: Blend garlic, scallion, bell pepper, and half the onion into an epis (Haitian spice paste).
Marinate chicken in epis for 5 minutes.
Brown chicken in olive oil over medium-high 4 minutes per side. Remove.
Sauté remaining diced onion 3 minutes. Add tomato paste and spices; cook 2 minutes.
Add broth, chicken, and sliced carrot. Simmer 20 minutes until chicken is tender. Finish with lime. Serve over rice.
cheapTips: The epis (spice paste) is the whole flavor base — garlic, scallion, and pepper blended together
Chicken thighs work best here as they stay juicy through the long simmer

substitutions.swap: Chicken breast for less fat
Any root vegetable — potato, sweet potato, or chayote

recipes.name: Ethiopian Spiced Chicken and Egg Stew
recipes.description: Doro wat-inspired stew — chicken thighs and hard-boiled eggs in a deeply spiced berbere-style sauce. Warming, complex, and deeply satisfying.
steps: Hard-boil 4 eggs; peel and score with a knife so sauce penetrates.
Caramelize 3 onions in butter over medium-low heat 20 minutes — this is the foundation.
Add garlic, ginger, and all spices; cook 3 minutes. Add tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Add chicken thighs and broth. Simmer 20 minutes until chicken is tender.
Add scored eggs and simmer 5 more minutes. Serve over rice with extra sauce.
cheapTips: Caramelized onions are the soul of Ethiopian cooking — don't rush step 2
The spice blend approximates berbere; adjust heat to preference

substitutions.swap: Chicken drumsticks for an even more authentic presentation
Cloves (just a small pinch) for a similar warm note

recipes.name: Kenyan Coconut Kidney Bean Stew
recipes.description: Maharagwe — East African kidney beans slow-simmered in coconut milk with tomatoes and spices. Creamy, warming, and deeply comforting over rice.
steps: Sauté onion in olive oil 5 minutes. Add garlic and ginger 2 minutes. Add cumin, turmeric, and coriander; toast 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes and cook 3 minutes.
Add drained kidney beans and coconut milk. Simmer 12 minutes until sauce thickens.
Finish with lime juice and cilantro. Season well.
Serve over rice — this is equally good with chapati or flatbread.
cheapTips: Kidney beans and coconut milk make this a $3 batch that serves four
This dish keeps beautifully for 4 days and gets better each day

substitutions.swap: Black-eyed peas for a traditional variation
Light coconut milk for a lower-calorie version

recipes.name: Trinidadian Pelau (One-Pot Chicken Rice)
recipes.description: Chicken caramelized in brown sugar then braised with rice, pigeon peas, and coconut milk — Trinidad's beloved one-pot Sunday dish.
steps: In a large pot, heat brown sugar with a tiny splash of water until it caramelizes to amber. Add chicken pieces — they'll sizzle dramatically. Coat for 1–2 minutes.
Add diced onion, garlic, and bell pepper; stir 2 minutes. Add thyme, scallion, and cayenne.
Add rice, drained kidney beans, broth, and half the coconut milk. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat 25 minutes until rice is done.
Uncover and fluff. Serve with coleslaw or a simple salad.
cheapTips: The brown sugar caramelization step (step 1) gives pelau its characteristic color and depth — don't skip it
A one-pot dish that feeds 5 for under $10 total

substitutions.swap: Chicken drumsticks or any bone-in piece
Pigeon peas (gandules) are traditional; kidney beans work perfectly

recipes.name: Ghanaian Red Red (Black-Eyed Pea Stew)
recipes.description: Ghana's famous black-eyed pea stew — cooked with palm oil or olive oil, tomatoes, and warming spices, served with fried plantain.
steps: Sauté onion in olive oil 6 minutes. Add garlic, ginger, smoked paprika, cayenne, and tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes and cook 5 minutes. Add drained black-eyed peas (or black beans as substitute).
Simmer 10 minutes until sauce is thick and flavorful. Season well.
Slice plantain or banana and pan-fry in a lightly oiled pan until caramelized.
Serve beans over rice with fried plantain on the side.
cheapTips: Ripe banana is a budget substitute for plantain — both work great
Two cans of black-eyed peas costs under $2 and makes a complete meal for four

substitutions.swap: Black-eyed peas (cowpeas) for the traditional Ghanaian ingredient
Skip for a lower-calorie version or use sweet potato

recipes.name: Smoked Salmon Protein Bagel Bowl
recipes.description: Everything bagel flavor in a bowl — smoked salmon with cream cheese, cucumber, capers, and red onion over a toasted bagel or crackers. Ready in 3 minutes.
steps: Toast half a bagel (or use crackers).
Spread cream cheese generously on the bagel.
Top with flaked canned salmon, thinly sliced cucumber, and a few rings of red onion.
Sprinkle with everything bagel seasoning and fresh dill if you have it.
Squeeze lemon over the top and eat immediately.
cheapTips: Canned salmon provides 25g protein for about $2 — nearly the same as smoked salmon but at a fraction of the cost
Half a bagel keeps carbs reasonable for a morning meal

substitutions.swap: Actual smoked salmon for the full lox experience
Rice cakes or crackers for a gluten-free version

recipes.name: Peanut Butter Banana Baked Oats
recipes.description: A single-serving baked oat cake that tastes like a warm peanut butter cookie — made with just oats, banana, egg, and PB. Meal-prep breakfast magic.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Mash a ripe banana in a bowl.
Add rolled oats, peanut butter, egg, honey, baking powder, cinnamon, vanilla, and milk. Mix well.
Pour into a small greased baking dish or two individual ramekins.
Bake 22–25 minutes until set and lightly golden on top.
Serve warm, topped with banana slices or a drizzle of peanut butter.
cheapTips: Ripe bananas are the sweetener here — buy overripe ones for half price
Rolled oats are one of the cheapest breakfast bases

substitutions.swap: Almond butter or any nut butter works
Oat milk or almond milk for dairy-free

recipes.name: Veggie Egg Breakfast Quesadilla
recipes.description: Scrambled eggs with spinach, bell pepper, and cheese folded in a crispy flour tortilla — a fast, satisfying Mexican-American breakfast.
steps: Dice bell pepper and onion. Sauté in olive oil 2 minutes. Add spinach; wilt 1 minute.
Beat eggs with salt and pepper. Pour over vegetables. Scramble until just set.
Lay tortilla flat. Spread egg mixture on half. Add shredded cheese. Fold tortilla.
Cook folded quesadilla in the same pan 1–2 minutes per side until golden and cheese melts.
Slice and serve with salsa.
cheapTips: Four eggs + one tortilla is under $1.50 for a filling breakfast
Any cheese works — use whatever you have open

substitutions.swap: Any vegetable that scrambles well — mushroom, tomato, zucchini
Skip for dairy-free; add avocado for richness

recipes.name: Shakshuka with Feta Cheese
recipes.description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato-pepper sauce with crumbled feta — a Middle Eastern and North African breakfast that works for any meal of the day.
steps: Sauté diced onion and bell pepper in olive oil over medium 5 minutes. Add minced garlic 1 minute.
Add cumin, smoked paprika, and chili powder; toast 30 seconds.
Add crushed tomatoes. Simmer 5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly. Season well.
Make 5 small wells in the sauce. Crack one egg into each. Cover and cook 6–8 minutes until whites are set but yolks are still runny.
Top with crumbled feta and fresh cilantro. Serve with crusty bread for scooping.
cheapTips: Five eggs for three people is the entire protein base at under $1.50
Canned crushed tomatoes are the perfect sauce base — cheap and consistently good

substitutions.swap: Goat cheese or ricotta for a different creamy topping
Pita bread or skip for a lower-carb version

recipes.name: Chia Seed Pudding with Berries
recipes.description: Overnight chia pudding made with almond milk and topped with fresh berries and a drizzle of honey — the no-cook, no-wake meal prep breakfast.
steps: Mix chia seeds (about 3 tbsp per serving) with almond milk, honey, vanilla, and cinnamon. Stir well.
Refrigerate 4 hours or overnight. Stir once after 30 minutes to prevent clumping.
When ready, the chia will have absorbed the milk into a thick pudding.
Top with mixed berries and a sprinkle of granola.
Serve cold. Keeps in the fridge for 4 days.
cheapTips: Chia seeds cost about $0.25 per serving — one of the cheapest meal-prep breakfasts
Make 4 jars at once for the week

substitutions.swap: Coconut milk for a richer pudding
Maple syrup or dates for different sweeteners

recipes.name: Huevos Rancheros Power Bowl
recipes.description: Fried eggs on warm corn tortillas with refried beans and roasted ranchero salsa — the classic Mexican breakfast with a protein-first upgrade.
steps: Warm corn tortillas directly over a gas flame or in a dry pan 20 seconds per side.
Warm refried beans with a pinch of cumin. Spread on tortillas.
Fry eggs sunny-side up in olive oil 3–4 minutes.
Slide eggs onto the bean-spread tortillas. Spoon salsa over.
Top with a few avocado slices, a light sprinkle of cheese, and fresh cilantro. Serve with lime.
cheapTips: Canned refried beans cost under $1 and add 8g protein per half can
Corn tortillas are cheaper than flour and naturally gluten-free

substitutions.swap: Black beans mashed with cumin for a homemade version
Guacamole from a packet for portion control

recipes.name: Tempeh Breakfast Scramble
recipes.description: Crumbled tempeh sautéed with turmeric, bell pepper, and onion — a plant-based breakfast scramble with more protein than scrambled eggs.
steps: Crumble tempeh into small, egg-like pieces.
Heat sesame oil over medium. Sauté diced onion and bell pepper 3 minutes.
Add garlic and crumbled tempeh. Cook 4 minutes until lightly browned.
Season with turmeric, smoked paprika, soy sauce, and nutritional yeast. Stir well.
Serve topped with sliced scallion and avocado. Great with toast on the side.
cheapTips: Tempeh provides 30g protein per block — more than eggs — at about $2–4
Nutritional yeast adds a cheesy, savory flavor and B12 for about $0.15 per serving

substitutions.swap: Firm tofu for a softer scramble
Skip — the turmeric and paprika carry the dish

recipes.name: Lox and Cream Cheese Power Toast
recipes.description: Whole-grain toast with cream cheese, smoked salmon, capers, and microgreens — a 5-minute breakfast that tastes like it came from a fancy brunch spot.
steps: Toast two slices of whole-grain bread.
Spread cream cheese generously on each slice.
Top with canned salmon flaked over the cream cheese.
Add thin red onion rings and a sprinkle of everything bagel seasoning and dried dill.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon. Eat immediately.
cheapTips: Canned salmon is 80% cheaper than actual lox with similar protein content
Whole-grain bread provides fiber and keeps you fuller longer

substitutions.swap: Actual smoked salmon or lox for the traditional experience
Rice cakes for a gluten-free, lower-carb alternative

recipes.name: Spinach Protein Green Smoothie
recipes.description: A thick, creamy green smoothie with spinach, banana, Greek yogurt, and protein powder — tastes like a treat, delivers like a meal.
steps: Blend frozen spinach, banana, Greek yogurt, almond milk, protein powder, peanut butter, and honey.
Start on low speed to break up the spinach, then increase to high. Blend 60 seconds until silky.
Taste and adjust sweetness. Pour into a glass or jar.
Drink immediately for best texture, or refrigerate up to 8 hours.
cheapTips: Frozen spinach costs about $1–2 per bag and you'll only use a handful
Banana is the natural sweetener — the riper it is, the sweeter the smoothie

substitutions.swap: Regular milk or oat milk
Extra Greek yogurt for a whole-food protein approach

recipes.name: 5-Day Chicken and Veggie Meal Prep Bowls
recipes.description: Sheet-pan chicken breast with roasted sweet potato and broccoli over brown rice — five identical, perfectly portioned lunch boxes you prep once on Sunday.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Cook brown rice according to package (or use a rice cooker).
Cube sweet potatoes; cut broccoli into florets. Toss both with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and smoked paprika on a large sheet pan.
Season chicken breasts with garlic powder, Italian seasoning, remaining olive oil, salt, and pepper. Place on a separate sheet pan or the other half of the same pan.
Roast everything 25–30 minutes until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are caramelized.
Slice chicken and divide everything evenly into 5 meal-prep containers with rice. Refrigerate up to 5 days.
cheapTips: Buying chicken in bulk (family packs) cuts the per-pound cost by 30%
Brown rice in a large bag costs about $0.20 per serving

substitutions.swap: Regular potato or butternut squash
Green beans, zucchini, or any vegetable that roasts well

recipes.name: Ground Turkey Brown Rice Meal Prep
recipes.description: Seasoned lean ground turkey with brown rice and sautéed zucchini — a simple, endlessly flexible meal-prep base you can customize with different sauces each day.
steps: Cook brown rice (use a rice cooker for hands-off ease). Season 2 lbs ground turkey with Italian seasoning, paprika, and salt.
Brown turkey in olive oil over medium-high 8 minutes, breaking apart. Drain excess fat.
In the same pan, sauté diced onion 4 minutes. Add garlic and diced zucchini; cook 4 more minutes.
Divide rice, turkey, and vegetables evenly into 5 containers.
Top with your sauce of choice each day — salsa, hot sauce, sriracha, or simple soy sauce.
