cheapTips: Two pounds of ground turkey for 5 days costs about $8–10 total
Brown rice in bulk is about $0.20 per serving

substitutions.swap: Any seasonal vegetable — swap throughout the week for variety
Quinoa or farro for different protein and fiber profiles

recipes.name: Teriyaki Tofu and Broccoli Prep Boxes
recipes.description: Oven-baked crispy tofu with broccoli and brown rice in a teriyaki glaze — a vegan meal prep that actually stays crispy in the box.
steps: Press two blocks of tofu between towels 10 minutes. Cube into ½-inch pieces.
Toss tofu with sesame oil, garlic powder, and a splash of teriyaki sauce. Spread on a baking sheet.
On another section of the sheet, add broccoli florets tossed with sesame oil and salt.
Bake at 400°F 25–28 minutes, flipping tofu halfway, until tofu is golden and broccoli is caramelized.
Cook rice. Divide into 4 boxes. Drizzle extra teriyaki over tofu. Top with sesame seeds and scallion.
cheapTips: Baked tofu stays crispier than pan-fried when refrigerated — better for meal prep
Two blocks of tofu + two bags of frozen broccoli costs about $6–8

substitutions.swap: Tempeh for a nuttier, higher-protein option
Homemade: soy sauce + honey + ginger + garlic

recipes.name: Big-Batch Lentil Vegetable Soup
recipes.description: A giant pot of hearty red lentil soup with carrots, celery, cumin, and turmeric — makes 6–8 servings that freeze perfectly for up to 3 months.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot. Sauté diced onion 5 minutes. Add garlic, cumin, turmeric, and paprika; cook 1 minute.
Add diced carrots and celery; stir 3 minutes.
Add rinsed lentils, crushed tomatoes, and broth. Bring to a boil.
Simmer 25 minutes until lentils are soft and falling apart.
Finish with lemon juice, season generously. Cool completely before portioning into containers.
cheapTips: 3 cups of red lentils feed 7 people for about $3 — one of the cheapest meals per serving
This freezes beautifully in individual portions for up to 3 months

substitutions.swap: Vegetable broth or water — lentils provide enough flavor
Split peas cook similarly and cost about the same

recipes.name: Salmon and Quinoa Prep Bowls
recipes.description: Lemon-herb baked salmon over quinoa with cucumber and cherry tomatoes — a premium meal-prep bowl that stores up to 4 days.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Cook quinoa (2 cups dry = ~4 servings cooked).
Season salmon fillets with olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, Italian herbs, salt, and pepper.
Bake salmon 12–15 minutes until it flakes easily. Cool completely before boxing.
Dice cucumber and halve tomatoes.
Divide quinoa into 4 containers. Top each with a salmon fillet, cucumber, and tomatoes. Add lemon wedge. Refrigerate up to 4 days.
cheapTips: Frozen salmon fillets thawed overnight work perfectly for this
Quinoa provides all 9 essential amino acids — it's a complete protein grain

substitutions.swap: Tilapia or cod for a more affordable white-fish prep
Brown rice for a cheaper complete carb base

recipes.name: Black Bean and Brown Rice Prep Jars
recipes.description: Layered mason jar meals — spiced black beans over brown rice with corn, pico de gallo, and lime — a vibrant, 5-day vegetarian prep for under $1.50 per jar.
steps: Cook brown rice. Warm black beans in a pan with cumin, chili powder, salt, and a splash of lime.
Warm or use canned corn as-is.
Layer in jars or containers: rice on the bottom, beans, corn, and pico de gallo.
Squeeze lime over everything. Add avocado just before eating (don't pre-cut if prepping for the week).
Refrigerate up to 5 days — the beans and rice keep well; add avocado fresh each day.
cheapTips: Two cans of black beans + a bag of brown rice makes 5 jars for about $6 total
Pack avocados separately and add day-of to prevent browning

substitutions.swap: Salsa from a jar to save time and money
Skip for a lower-fat prep; add guacamole day-of instead

recipes.name: Egg and Veggie Muffin Meal Prep (12-pack)
recipes.description: Twelve portable egg muffins baked in a muffin tin with bell pepper, spinach, and cheese — the original grab-and-go high-protein breakfast.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Spray a 12-cup muffin tin generously with cooking spray.
Finely dice bell pepper and onion. Tear or chop spinach.
Whisk together eggs, milk, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Divide diced vegetables and spinach among the 12 cups. Pour egg mixture over, filling each about ¾ full. Top with cheese.
Bake 18–22 minutes until eggs are set and tops are lightly golden. Cool before storing. Refrigerate up to 5 days; reheat 30 seconds in microwave.
cheapTips: 10 eggs makes 12 muffins for under $2 total — about $0.16 per muffin
These freeze perfectly — make 24 at once and freeze half for next week

substitutions.swap: Any vegetable that holds up to baking — mushroom, broccoli, or tomato
Feta for a tangier, Mediterranean-style muffin

recipes.name: Roasted Chickpea and Grain Bowl Prep
recipes.description: Crispy roasted chickpeas over farro (or quinoa) with roasted vegetables and a lemon-tahini dressing — a vegan prep bowl with serious staying power.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Drain, rinse, and thoroughly pat-dry chickpeas.
Toss chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, and salt. Spread on one half of a sheet pan.
Toss cubed sweet potato and broccoli with olive oil and salt on the other half.
Roast 25–28 minutes until chickpeas are crispy and vegetables are golden.
Cook quinoa. Make tahini dressing: tahini, lemon, garlic, water, salt. Pack 4 boxes with grain, vegetables, chickpeas, and dressing on the side.
cheapTips: Chickpeas get genuinely crispy when completely dry before roasting — the key step
Two cans of chickpeas + quinoa + vegetables costs about $8 for 4 boxes

substitutions.swap: Brown rice or farro for a different grain base
Regular potato or butternut squash

recipes.name: 4-Jar Overnight Oats Variety Pack
recipes.description: Four different overnight oat jars prepped Sunday — PB banana, blueberry, apple cinnamon, and chocolate — each ready in the morning with no cooking.
steps: Base for all 4 jars: ½ cup oats + ½ cup Greek yogurt + ½ cup milk + 1 scoop protein powder (divided) + drizzle of honey.
Jar 1 (PB Banana): add 1 tbsp peanut butter and half a sliced banana.
Jar 2 (Blueberry): add ¼ cup blueberries and a pinch of vanilla.
Jar 3 (Apple Cinnamon): add ¼ cup diced apple and ½ tsp cinnamon.
Jar 4 (Chocolate): add 1 tbsp cocoa powder, 1 tbsp peanut butter, and a drizzle of honey. Seal and refrigerate all 4 jars overnight — ready in the morning.
cheapTips: Rolled oats are one of the cheapest ingredients per serving
Making 4 jars at once means a week of breakfast is done in 15 minutes

substitutions.swap: Plain yogurt or skyr for slightly different macros
Extra Greek yogurt — adds protein without powder

recipes.name: Greek Chicken Salad Prep Containers
recipes.description: Chopped chicken with cucumber, tomato, olive, feta, and a lemon-herb vinaigrette — Greek salad elevated with protein, ready to grab from the fridge.
steps: Season chicken breasts with oregano, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Cook in olive oil 6–7 minutes per side; cool and dice.
Make vinaigrette: lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, garlic, salt.
Dice cucumber, tomato, and red onion. Crumble feta.
Divide lettuce among 4 containers. Top with vegetables, chicken, and feta.
Store dressing separately and add just before eating. Keeps 4 days.
cheapTips: Two chicken breasts make 4 generous protein-packed salads for under $5
Store dressing in a small sealed container inside the main one

substitutions.swap: Goat cheese for a creamier topping
Canned chicken for a no-cook prep option

recipes.name: High-Protein Tuna Pasta Salad Prep
recipes.description: Cold pasta salad with tuna, celery, red onion, peas, and a light Greek yogurt dressing — a 5-day protein-packed lunch that gets better as it marinates.
steps: Cook pasta; rinse under cold water until completely cool.
Make dressing: Greek yogurt, dijon, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Drain and flake 4 cans of tuna. Dice celery and red onion. Thaw peas.
Combine pasta, tuna, celery, onion, and peas. Pour dressing over and toss well.
Divide into 5 containers. Refrigerate up to 5 days (the flavors deepen over time).
cheapTips: 4 cans of tuna for 5 servings costs about $5 and provides 100g total protein
Greek yogurt dressing is cheaper and higher-protein than mayo-based dressings

substitutions.swap: Light mayo for a more traditional pasta salad flavor
Diced cucumber or cherry tomatoes for crunch

recipes.name: Ground Beef and Sweet Potato Prep Boxes
recipes.description: Seasoned lean ground beef with roasted sweet potato and green beans — a hearty, high-protein prep box with zero refined carbs.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Cube sweet potatoes. Toss with olive oil, smoked paprika, and salt. Roast 25 minutes.
Add broccoli florets to the pan for the last 10 minutes.
Brown ground beef in a skillet with garlic, cumin, worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper. Drain excess fat.
Cool everything completely before boxing.
Pack 5 containers with sweet potato, broccoli, and seasoned beef. Refrigerate up to 5 days.
cheapTips: Ground beef in family packs costs about $4–5/lb
Sweet potatoes keep the carbs nutrient-dense and filling

substitutions.swap: Ground turkey for a leaner, slightly cheaper option
Green beans, asparagus, or any vegetable that roasts well

recipes.name: Batch Lentil Curry and Rice Prep
recipes.description: A big pot of red lentil curry made on Sunday portions into 5 meal-prep boxes over rice — warming Indian-spiced comfort food for every day of the week.
steps: Sauté diced onion in olive oil 5 minutes. Add garlic, ginger, curry powder, garam masala, and turmeric; cook 2 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes and cook 3 minutes. Add lentils and 4 cups water.
Simmer 20 minutes until lentils are completely soft. Stir in coconut milk and simmer 5 more minutes.
Cook rice. Season curry generously with salt.
Cool completely. Divide curry and rice into 5 boxes. Add cilantro. Refrigerate up to 5 days; freezes up to 3 months.
cheapTips: Red lentils in bulk cost about $2/lb — 2.5 cups makes 5 generous servings
Freeze half the batch if you're not eating it all within 5 days

substitutions.swap: Light coconut milk for a lower-fat version
Cauliflower rice to drop carbs and calories

recipes.name: Greek Chicken Quinoa Power Prep
recipes.description: Mediterranean-spiced chicken over quinoa with kalamata olives, feta, and roasted red pepper — a prep box that tastes like a restaurant bowl.
steps: Roast quartered bell peppers at 425°F 20 minutes until charred. Cool.
Season chicken with oregano, garlic powder, lemon, olive oil, salt. Bake alongside 20 minutes.
Cook quinoa. Dice cucumber and tomato. Cool all components.
Slice chicken and bell pepper.
Pack 4 boxes with quinoa, chicken, roasted pepper, cucumber, tomato, and feta. Squeeze lemon over. Dressing on side.
cheapTips: Roasting bell peppers yourself is far cheaper than buying jarred
Two chicken breasts for 4 boxes is economical — add extra if you want bigger portions

substitutions.swap: Goat cheese for a creamier topping
Couscous cooks in 5 minutes and is a great alternative

recipes.name: Baked Protein Oatmeal (Make-Ahead Slices)
recipes.description: A full baking dish of protein oatmeal baked with banana, peanut butter, and Greek yogurt — cut into 6 slices for the week's breakfasts.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Grease an 8×8-inch baking dish.
Mash 3 bananas. Mix with Greek yogurt, peanut butter, eggs, milk, honey, vanilla, and cinnamon.
Stir in rolled oats and baking powder. Mix until well combined.
Pour into baking dish. Bake 28–32 minutes until set and golden on top.
Cool completely, slice into 6 portions. Refrigerate up to 6 days or freeze up to 2 months. Microwave 60 seconds to serve.
cheapTips: The whole dish costs about $5 and provides 6 breakfasts — under $1 each
Freeze individual slices for grab-and-go mornings

substitutions.swap: Almond butter or any nut butter
Unsweetened applesauce (½ cup per banana) for less sweetness

recipes.name: Spicy Roasted Chickpea Snack
recipes.description: Chickpeas roasted until shatteringly crispy with smoked paprika, cumin, and cayenne — a protein-rich snack that satisfies chip cravings for a fraction of the cost.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Drain, rinse, and spread chickpeas on a clean towel. Pat VERY dry.
Toss dry chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, cayenne, garlic powder, and salt.
Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet — no overlapping.
Roast 28–32 minutes, shaking the pan halfway, until golden and crispy.
Cool completely on the pan — they get crispier as they cool. Store in an open container (covered traps steam and softens them).
cheapTips: Two cans of chickpeas make 4 large snack portions for under $2
The drying step is crucial — any moisture prevents crispiness

substitutions.swap: Regular paprika works; add a pinch of liquid smoke for smokiness
Skip for a mild version, or use chili powder for a different heat profile

recipes.name: Chili Lime Edamame
recipes.description: Frozen edamame steamed and tossed with chili powder, lime zest, and salt — a 5-minute high-protein snack that outdoes any bag of chips.
steps: Microwave frozen edamame (in-shell or shelled) 3–4 minutes until hot.
Drain if needed. Toss with lime zest, lime juice, chili powder, garlic powder, and salt.
Serve hot or at room temperature. Eat immediately or refrigerate up to 3 days.
cheapTips: A bag of frozen edamame costs $2–3 and provides 17g protein per cup shelled
This is one of the healthiest snacks per dollar you can eat

substitutions.swap: Old Bay, tajin seasoning, or furikake for completely different flavor profiles
Lemon works equally well — add zest for more punch

recipes.name: Turkey and Hummus Lettuce Roll-Ups
recipes.description: Sliced turkey breast wrapped in romaine with hummus, cucumber, and roasted red pepper — a no-carb snack that's both satisfying and genuinely portable.
steps: Lay out 6 large romaine leaves as wrappers.
Spread each with hummus. Lay 1 slice of deli turkey on each.
Add thin cucumber rounds and strips of bell pepper.
Add a tiny smear of dijon if desired.
Roll tightly and serve immediately, or wrap in foil for up to 2 hours.
cheapTips: Deli turkey slices are one of the leanest ready-to-eat proteins
Making this at home is 4× cheaper than a store-bought protein box

substitutions.swap: Canned chicken or sliced rotisserie chicken
Avocado smash or cream cheese for a different spread

recipes.name: Cottage Cheese Herb Veggie Dip
recipes.description: Blended cottage cheese with herbs and garlic into a silky, high-protein dip — served with whatever vegetables you have on hand.
steps: Blend cottage cheese, garlic, lemon juice, dill, parsley, and salt until completely smooth.
Taste and adjust seasoning — it should be punchy and herby.
Transfer to a serving bowl.
Cut carrots into sticks, slice cucumber, and cut bell pepper into strips.
Serve dip with vegetables. Stores in the fridge for 5 days.
cheapTips: A whole tub of cottage cheese makes 3 large snack portions for under $2
This is one of the most protein-dense dips per calorie available

substitutions.swap: Everything bagel seasoning for an easier one-spice dip
Greek yogurt for a tangier version

recipes.name: High-Protein Deviled Eggs
recipes.description: Classic deviled eggs upgraded with Greek yogurt and a dash of sriracha — each egg is 6g protein at 50 calories.
steps: Hard-boil 8 eggs (9 minutes from cold water). Ice bath, peel, halve.
Pop out yolks into a bowl. Mash with Greek yogurt, dijon, sriracha, and salt until smooth.
Spoon or pipe filling back into the whites.
Sprinkle with smoked paprika. Refrigerate up to 3 days.
cheapTips: Eight eggs make 16 deviled egg halves for about $1.50 total
Greek yogurt replaces mayo — adds protein while cutting fat by 70%

substitutions.swap: Light mayo for a more traditional flavor
Hot sauce or mustard for a different kick

recipes.name: Peanut Butter Banana Protein Bites
recipes.description: No-bake energy balls made from oats, peanut butter, banana, and protein powder — roll them out Sunday for a week of grab-and-go snacks.
steps: Mash banana in a bowl until smooth.
Add peanut butter, honey, vanilla, cinnamon, and protein powder. Mix well.
Stir in rolled oats until the mixture holds together when pressed. If too wet, add more oats.
Roll into 18 balls (about 1 tablespoon each).
Refrigerate 30 minutes to set. Store in an airtight container in the fridge up to 1 week.
cheapTips: One banana + 1 cup oats + half a jar of PB makes 18 bites for about $3
These are the cheapest portable high-protein snack you can make

substitutions.swap: Almond butter or sunflower seed butter for nut-free
Extra oats — the bites are still great without powder

recipes.name: Tuna Salad Cucumber Rounds
recipes.description: Tuna salad dolloped onto cucumber slices — a crunchy, protein-rich no-carb snack ready in 5 minutes.
steps: Drain and flake canned tuna.
Mix with Greek yogurt, dijon, finely diced celery, lemon juice, and salt. Taste and adjust.
Slice cucumber into ½-inch rounds.
Spoon tuna salad onto each cucumber round.
Serve immediately or refrigerate the tuna salad (separately from cucumber) for up to 3 days.
cheapTips: Two cans of tuna cost about $2–3 and make a snack for two that's over 40g protein total
Greek yogurt tuna salad has more protein and fewer calories than mayo-based

substitutions.swap: Light mayo for the traditional version
Celery sticks or rice cakes for a different crunchy base

recipes.name: Black Bean Guacamole Protein Dip
recipes.description: Classic guacamole bulked out with mashed black beans — doubles the protein and fiber while stretching expensive avocado further.
steps: Halve and pit avocados. Scoop flesh into a bowl.
Add drained black beans and roughly mash both together — some chunks are good.
Add lime juice, minced garlic, finely diced red onion, chopped cilantro, and salt.
Taste and adjust — should be bright, garlicky, and well-seasoned.
Serve with tortilla chips or vegetable sticks.
cheapTips: Black beans stretch expensive avocado to 4 servings instead of 2
Mashing beans with guac is invisible — no one notices they're there

substitutions.swap: Edamame (mashed) for a different plant protein
Vegetables — cucumber rounds or carrot sticks for fewer carbs

recipes.name: No-Bake Oat Protein Energy Balls
recipes.description: Chewy, chocolatey no-bake energy balls with oats, protein powder, and peanut butter — batch them on Sunday for a week of pre-workout snacks.
steps: Mix peanut butter, honey, vanilla, and 2 tbsp milk until smooth.
Stir in oats, protein powder, cocoa, and cinnamon. Mix until combined.
If the mixture is too dry, add milk a tablespoon at a time. It should hold together when pressed.
Roll into 24 balls (about 1 heaped tablespoon each).
Refrigerate 30 minutes until firm. Store in an airtight container up to 10 days.
cheapTips: Oats and peanut butter are pantry staples — the protein powder is the only 'special' ingredient
One batch of 24 costs about $5 total — under $0.25 per ball

substitutions.swap: Sunflower seed butter for nut-free
Extra oats — you'll lose 10g protein but it's still a great snack

recipes.name: Cottage Cheese Stuffed Mini Peppers
recipes.description: Mini sweet peppers stuffed with herbed cottage cheese — a colorful, zero-carb snack with 18g protein per serving.
steps: Slice mini peppers in half lengthwise and remove seeds.
Mix cottage cheese with minced garlic, dill, and a pinch of salt.
Fill each pepper half with a spoonful of cottage cheese filling.
Sprinkle with everything bagel seasoning.
Serve immediately or refrigerate up to 2 days.
cheapTips: Mini sweet peppers cost about $3 for a bag of 20 — find them in bulk for better deals
Cottage cheese filling keeps well — prep it Sunday and fill peppers fresh each day

substitutions.swap: Cream cheese or goat cheese for a richer filling
Za'atar, smoked paprika, or dried herbs

recipes.name: Frozen Greek Yogurt Berry Bark
recipes.description: Greek yogurt spread thin on parchment, topped with berries and granola, then frozen — sliced into bark pieces for a cold protein snack.
steps: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Mix Greek yogurt with honey and vanilla until smooth. Spread into a thin, even layer about ¼-inch thick.
Scatter fresh or frozen berries across the top. Add a sprinkle of granola.
Freeze at least 3 hours or overnight.
Break or slice into irregular pieces. Store frozen — eat straight from freezer. Keeps 2 weeks.
cheapTips: Two cups of Greek yogurt makes 6 snack servings for about $2
Frozen berries thawed slightly work better than fresh for pressing into the bark

substitutions.swap: Any fruit — mango chunks, sliced banana, or kiwi
Nuts, seeds, or shredded coconut for a different topping

recipes.name: Greek Yogurt and Cucumber Dip
recipes.description: A simplified tzatziki — Greek yogurt, grated cucumber, garlic, and dill — served with warm pita or vegetable crudités.
steps: Grate cucumber and squeeze out as much water as possible in a clean towel.
Mix Greek yogurt with drained cucumber, minced garlic, chopped dill, lemon juice, olive oil, and salt.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Refrigerate at least 15 minutes (better after 1 hour).
Serve with warm pita triangles and vegetable sticks.
cheapTips: Tzatziki is one of the most protein-dense dips available for the price
Squeezing out cucumber water is the key to thick, not watery dip

substitutions.swap: Dried dill — use half the amount
Cucumber rounds, carrot sticks, or rice cakes

recipes.name: High-Protein Egg Salad Celery Sticks
recipes.description: Classic egg salad lightened with Greek yogurt and served in celery boats — a 5-minute snack with 22g protein.
steps: Use pre-boiled eggs (or hard-boil ahead). Chop roughly.
Mix with Greek yogurt, dijon, salt, and paprika. Mash slightly.
Wash and trim celery stalks.
Fill celery concaves with egg salad.
Serve immediately or refrigerate egg salad up to 3 days.
cheapTips: Four eggs for two people costs under $0.75 for 28g total protein
Greek yogurt egg salad has more protein and fewer calories than mayo

substitutions.swap: Light mayo for a more traditional flavor
Cucumber rounds or bell pepper halves

recipes.name: Smoked Salmon and Cream Cheese Cucumber Bites
recipes.description: Cucumber rounds topped with cream cheese and flaked canned salmon — an elegant snack that takes 3 minutes to assemble and has 24g protein per serving.
steps: Slice cucumbers into ½-inch rounds — about 20–24 rounds total.
Spread a small dollop of cream cheese on each.
Top with flaked canned salmon.
Sprinkle with dill, everything bagel seasoning, and a tiny squeeze of lemon.
Serve immediately.
cheapTips: Canned salmon at $2–3/can makes this a premium-tasting snack for very little money
These assemble in 3 minutes — faster than making toast

substitutions.swap: Cottage cheese or Greek yogurt for more protein
Deli turkey or canned tuna for different protein options

recipes.name: White Bean and Herb Crostini
recipes.description: Creamy mashed white bean spread on toasted bread with lemon and fresh herbs — the Italian appetizer that works equally well as a high-protein snack.
steps: Toast bread slices until golden.
In a pan, warm olive oil over medium. Add garlic and rosemary; cook 1 minute.
Add drained white beans and cook 2–3 minutes until heated through.
Mash roughly with a fork — keep some beans whole for texture.
Add lemon juice, red pepper flakes, and salt. Spoon onto toast slices.
cheapTips: One can of white beans makes 4 generous crostini servings for under $1
The rosemary-garlic oil elevates simple pantry ingredients into something special

substitutions.swap: Dried rosemary (half the amount) or thyme
Rice cakes or gluten-free bread for GF version

recipes.name: Tropical Mango Protein Smoothie
recipes.description: Frozen mango, Greek yogurt, and vanilla protein powder blended with coconut milk — sunshine in a glass with 30g protein.
steps: Add frozen mango, Greek yogurt, coconut milk, protein powder, honey, and lime juice to a blender.
Blend on high 60 seconds until smooth.
If too thick, add a splash of water or coconut milk. If too thin, add more frozen mango.
Pour into a glass and drink immediately.
cheapTips: Frozen mango is cheaper than fresh and makes a thicker smoothie
One bag of frozen mango costs $3–4 and makes 3–4 smoothies

substitutions.swap: Almond milk or oat milk for a less rich version
Frozen pineapple for a different tropical fruit base

recipes.name: Chocolate Peanut Butter Protein Shake
recipes.description: Rich, thick chocolate-PB shake with Greek yogurt, protein powder, and almond milk — the post-workout drink that tastes like a milkshake.
steps: Blend almond milk, Greek yogurt, peanut butter, protein powder, cocoa, honey, and half a frozen banana.
Blend on high 60 seconds until smooth and creamy.
Add ice cubes for a thicker, milkshake consistency.
Drink immediately.
cheapTips: Half a frozen banana is the cheapest thickener — buy overripe bananas at discount
Greek yogurt + protein powder gives a double protein punch

substitutions.swap: Frozen cauliflower florets (sounds weird, tastes neutral and adds creaminess)
Powdered PB for 85% fewer calories with the same flavor

recipes.name: Strawberry Cottage Cheese Smoothie
recipes.description: Frozen strawberries blended with cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, and vanilla — one of the highest-protein smoothies you can make for under $2.
steps: Blend frozen strawberries, cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, honey, vanilla, and almond milk.
Blend 90 seconds until completely smooth — cottage cheese takes a moment to break down.
Taste and add more honey if needed.
Drink immediately.
cheapTips: Cottage cheese is the cheapest protein per gram in this smoothie — about $0.50 for 14g protein
Frozen strawberries cost half as much as fresh and blend better

substitutions.swap: Any frozen berry — blueberry and raspberry work beautifully
Extra Greek yogurt for a tangier, smoother smoothie

recipes.name: Iced Coffee Protein Shake
recipes.description: Cold brew or instant coffee blended with Greek yogurt, protein powder, and almond milk — the ultimate morning multitasker: coffee + protein in one glass.
steps: Brew 1 cup of strong coffee or dissolve 2 tsp instant coffee in ¼ cup hot water. Cool.
Blend cooled coffee, almond milk, Greek yogurt, protein powder, honey, cocoa, and vanilla.
Blend with ice until smooth and thick.
Pour and enjoy cold. Add more almond milk if too thick.
cheapTips: Instant coffee is the cheapest option — dissolves perfectly in cold smoothies
One cup of coffee turns a protein shake into your morning coffee too

substitutions.swap: Regular milk for a creamier texture
Skip for a pure coffee protein shake

recipes.name: Banana Oat Breakfast Smoothie
recipes.description: Rolled oats blended with banana, Greek yogurt, and cinnamon — a filling, whole-food smoothie that keeps you full until lunch.
steps: Add all ingredients to blender: banana, rolled oats, Greek yogurt, almond milk, peanut butter, honey, cinnamon, and vanilla.
Blend on high 90 seconds — the oats need more time to fully break down.
Pour into a glass. The smoothie will be thick and filling.
Drink immediately or refrigerate up to 4 hours.
cheapTips: Rolled oats cost $0.10 per serving and add fiber and staying power
A ripe banana provides natural sweetness — reduce honey accordingly

substitutions.swap: Almond butter or skip for fewer calories
A Medjool date blended in for natural sweetness

recipes.name: Blueberry Spinach Power Smoothie
recipes.description: Wild blueberries and baby spinach blended with Greek yogurt — an antioxidant-rich purple-green smoothie with 26g protein.
steps: Blend frozen blueberries, spinach, Greek yogurt, protein powder, almond milk, honey, and lemon juice.
Blend on high 90 seconds until completely smooth.
It will be a deep purple-blue color — the spinach flavor is completely masked by the blueberries.
cheapTips: Frozen wild blueberries are smaller, cheaper, and have more antioxidants than fresh
Frozen spinach dissolves completely in a high-powered blender

substitutions.swap: Frozen mixed berries for variety
Skip or substitute orange juice for a sweeter citrus note

recipes.name: Cherry Almond Smoothie Bowl
recipes.description: Thick frozen cherry and almond butter smoothie bowl topped with granola and fresh fruit — eat it with a spoon for a satisfying morning meal.
steps: Blend frozen cherries (or berry mix) with Greek yogurt, protein powder, and just enough almond milk to blend — keep it very thick.
Pour into a wide bowl.
Top with sliced almonds, a small scoop of granola, and a drizzle of honey.
Eat immediately with a spoon before it melts.
cheapTips: Frozen mixed berries cost $3–4 per bag and make 3–4 smoothie bowls
The key is using minimal liquid — you want it thick enough to hold toppings

substitutions.swap: Frozen mango or peach for a tropical version
Any nut or seed you have on hand

recipes.name: Tart Cherry Recovery Smoothie
recipes.description: Tart cherry juice, Greek yogurt, and protein powder — a scientifically-backed post-workout recovery drink that reduces muscle soreness.
steps: Blend frozen tart cherries (or berry mix with a squeeze of lemon), Greek yogurt, protein powder, almond milk, honey, and vanilla.
Blend 60 seconds until smooth.
Drink within 30–60 minutes of completing a hard workout.
cheapTips: Frozen berry mixes include sour cherries or work as a substitute — much cheaper than fresh tart cherries
Greek yogurt provides casein protein that's ideal for overnight recovery

substitutions.swap: Actual frozen tart cherries if available at your grocery store
Regular milk for a creamier protein profile

recipes.name: Grilled Chicken Quinoa Power Salad
recipes.description: Tender grilled chicken over fluffy quinoa and crisp greens, dressed with a bright lemon-herb vinaigrette and crumbled feta — a lunch that keeps you full for hours.
steps: Cook quinoa: bring 2 cups water + quinoa to a boil, reduce heat, cover and simmer 15 minutes. Fluff and cool slightly.
Season chicken breasts with salt, pepper, and minced garlic. Sear in 1 tbsp olive oil over medium-high heat, 5–6 minutes per side until cooked through. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Whisk remaining olive oil, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, salt, and pepper into a dressing.
Divide spinach between two bowls. Top with quinoa, sliced chicken, diced tomato, and cucumber rounds.
Drizzle with dressing and crumble feta on top. Serve immediately.
cheapTips: Quinoa bought in bulk costs as little as $0.80 per dry cup
Thigh meat works just as well and costs 30% less than breast

substitutions.swap: Goat cheese or skip for dairy-free
Brown rice or farro (cook per package instructions)

recipes.name: Mediterranean Tuna White Bean Salad
recipes.description: A no-cook pantry powerhouse: canned tuna and white beans tossed with cucumber, tomato, and a zingy lemon-herb dressing. Ready in 5 minutes, endlessly satisfying.
steps: Drain and flake tuna; drain and rinse white beans.
Dice tomatoes and cucumber. Mince garlic and parsley.
In a large bowl, whisk olive oil, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Add tuna, beans, tomatoes, and cucumber; toss gently to combine.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Scatter fresh parsley on top. Serve immediately or refrigerate up to 2 days.
cheapTips: Two cans of tuna + one can of white beans cost around $3.50 total
This recipe has no cooking — save on energy costs too

substitutions.swap: Canned salmon or canned chicken for variety
Chickpeas or cannellini beans

recipes.name: Kale Caesar Salad with Chicken
recipes.description: Massaged kale stands up to a bold anchovy-Dijon Caesar dressing and stays crisp for days — topped with golden-seared chicken and a shower of Parmesan.
steps: Make dressing: whisk together 2 tbsp olive oil, mayo, lemon juice, anchovy paste, Dijon, minced garlic, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Strip kale from stems and tear into bite-sized pieces. Pour half the dressing over kale and massage 2–3 minutes until softened.
Season chicken with salt, pepper, and 1 tbsp olive oil. Cook in a hot skillet 5–6 min per side. Rest and slice.
Divide kale between two bowls. Top with sliced chicken, drizzle remaining dressing, and finish with Parmesan.
cheapTips: A bunch of kale costs ~$3 and makes 6+ cups — better value than romaine
Anchovy paste comes in a tube; a little goes a long way and keeps for months

substitutions.swap: 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce for a fish-free Caesar
Greek yogurt for a lighter, tangier dressing

recipes.name: Warm Lentil and Roasted Vegetable Salad
recipes.description: Earthy green lentils and sweet caramelized roasted vegetables dressed with a mustardy red wine vinaigrette — hearty, vegan, and packed with plant protein.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Cube sweet potatoes and slice bell peppers; toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, cumin, and half the garlic on a sheet pan. Roast 25–30 minutes.
Simmer lentils in 2.5 cups water with remaining garlic and a pinch of salt for 20–25 minutes until tender. Drain.
Whisk remaining olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper into a dressing.
Fold spinach into the warm lentils so it wilts slightly. Add roasted vegetables.
Drizzle dressing over everything and toss gently. Serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: A 1 lb bag of lentils costs ~$2 and makes 3 substantial servings
Sweet potatoes are among the cheapest nutrient-dense vegetables available

substitutions.swap: Butternut squash or regular potato
Zucchini, eggplant, or whatever vegetable needs using up

recipes.name: Quinoa and Chickpea Herb Salad
recipes.description: Nutty quinoa (an easy swap for farro) tossed with chickpeas, fresh herbs, cucumber, and tomato in a lemon-olive oil dressing — a Mediterranean grain salad that travels beautifully.
steps: Cook quinoa in 2 cups water (15 min). Spread on a plate to cool.
Drain and rinse chickpeas. Dice tomatoes and cucumber.
Chop parsley and mint together.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Toss all ingredients with the dressing. Taste and adjust. Serve room-temperature or chilled.
cheapTips: This salad gets better overnight — make ahead and the costs-per-meal drop further
Fresh parsley at $1/bunch adds generous flavor across 3 servings

substitutions.swap: Extra parsley or a handful of fresh basil
Couscous (5 min cook time) or brown rice

recipes.name: Salmon and Spinach Power Salad
recipes.description: Pan-seared salmon chilled over peppery spinach greens with cucumber and a bright lemon-Dijon dressing — elegant enough for guests, fast enough for a weekday lunch.
steps: Pat salmon dry and season with salt, pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil.
Cook skin-side down in a hot skillet over medium-high heat, 4 minutes. Flip and cook 2–3 minutes more. Let cool 5 minutes.
Whisk remaining olive oil, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, Dijon, garlic, salt, and pepper into a dressing.
Arrange spinach in two bowls. Add sliced cucumber, tomato, and flaked salmon.
Drizzle with dressing and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Canned salmon works perfectly here at a fraction of fresh cost — just drain and flake

substitutions.swap: Canned salmon (drain well) to cut cost significantly
Any peppery salad green — baby kale, romaine, or mixed greens

recipes.name: Edamame and Quinoa Asian Salad
recipes.description: Fluffy quinoa, sweet edamame, crisp cucumber, and scallions tossed in a toasted sesame-soy-ginger dressing — a cold salad that packs 22 g plant protein.
steps: Cook quinoa (15 min). Spread to cool — or chill in the fridge for a cold salad.
Microwave edamame 3–4 minutes. Cool.
Make dressing: whisk toasted sesame oil, soy sauce, vinegar, Dijon, honey, grated ginger, and minced garlic.
Slice cucumber and scallions.
Toss quinoa, edamame, cucumber, and scallions with dressing. Top with sesame seeds. Serve cold.
cheapTips: Edamame is the most affordable complete plant protein at around $0.60 per cup
This salad keeps 3 days refrigerated — make a double batch for the week

substitutions.swap: Tamari for a gluten-free version
Rice vinegar for a milder tang

recipes.name: Seared Chicken and Spinach Power Salad
recipes.description: Pan-seared chicken thighs sliced over fresh spinach with avocado, walnuts, and a sweet balsamic-Dijon dressing — the kind of salad that actually fills you up.
steps: Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper. Sear in 1 tbsp olive oil over medium-high heat, 5–6 min per side until golden and cooked through (165°F internal). Rest 5 min, then slice thin.
Make balsamic dressing: whisk remaining olive oil, balsamic, Dijon, honey, salt, and pepper.
Divide spinach between two plates. Top with sliced chicken, diced avocado, tomato, and walnuts.
Drizzle dressing and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Chicken thighs cost 20–30% less than breasts and have more flavor when seared
A small handful of walnuts adds crunch and healthy fats for ~$0.75 per serving

substitutions.swap: Almonds, pecans, or sunflower seeds
Chicken breast or a pan-seared beef patty sliced thin

recipes.name: Poached Egg and Lentil Bowl
recipes.description: Cumin-spiced lentils on a bed of wilted spinach, crowned with a perfectly poached egg that breaks into a silky sauce — wholesome, filling, and under $2 per serving.
steps: Sauté diced onion in olive oil over medium heat, 5 minutes. Add garlic, cumin, and paprika; cook 1 minute.
Add lentils and 2.5 cups water; bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover and cook 20–22 minutes until lentils are tender.
Stir spinach into the hot lentils until wilted. Squeeze in lemon juice and season with salt.
Poach eggs: bring a small saucepan of water to a gentle simmer. Swirl the water, slip in eggs, and cook 3 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Divide lentils between two bowls and top each with 2 poached eggs.
cheapTips: A cup of dried lentils costs ~$0.85 and serves two generously
Poached eggs are the most luxurious-looking thing you can do with a $0.42 egg

substitutions.swap: Canned lentils for a 5-minute shortcut (skip cooking step)
Kale or any leafy green

recipes.name: Shrimp and Avocado Citrus Salad
recipes.description: Juicy sautéed shrimp, creamy avocado, fresh orange segments, and spinach tossed in a cilantro-lime dressing — bright, tropical, and ready in 15 minutes.
steps: Thaw shrimp if frozen. Pat dry and season with salt, pepper, and minced garlic.
Sauté shrimp in 1 tbsp olive oil over medium-high heat, 2 minutes per side until pink and curled. Cool slightly.
Make dressing: remaining olive oil, lime juice, chopped cilantro, salt.
Segment orange. Dice avocado. Slice tomato.
Toss spinach with dressing. Top with shrimp, avocado, orange, and tomato. Serve immediately.
cheapTips: Frozen shrimp is just as nutritious as fresh and costs half as much
One orange adds sweetness, vitamin C, and color for about $0.90

substitutions.swap: Grapefruit or mango for different citrus
Romaine, mixed greens, or any salad base

recipes.name: Thai Ground Beef Larb Bowl
recipes.description: Boldly spiced ground beef with lime, fish-sauce-style seasoning, mint, and cilantro over rice — Thailand's most satisfying salad-bowl hybrid.
steps: Cook rice. Brown ground beef in a dry skillet over medium-high heat, breaking up lumps, 8–10 min until cooked through.
Off heat, stir in lime juice, soy sauce, chili-garlic sauce, and minced garlic.
Tear lettuce leaves. Slice scallions. Chop mint and cilantro.
Serve beef over rice in bowls, top with lettuce, herbs, scallions, and sesame seeds. Squeeze extra lime over everything.
cheapTips: Ground beef on sale makes this one of the cheapest Asian-inspired bowls
Dried mint works in a pinch — use 1 tsp instead of fresh

substitutions.swap: Ground turkey or ground chicken for leaner larb
Cauliflower rice to cut carbs by ~150 kcal

recipes.name: Japanese Sesame Spinach Brown Rice Bowl
recipes.description: Blanched spinach in a toasted sesame-mirin dressing over brown rice — a simple Japanese-inspired bowl that's deeply savory and ready in 20 minutes.
steps: Cook brown rice (20 min). Microwave edamame 3 min.
Blanch spinach in boiling salted water 30 seconds, drain well and squeeze out water.
Dress spinach with sesame oil, soy sauce, mirin, grated garlic, ginger, and sesame seeds.
Serve rice in bowls, top with dressed spinach, edamame, and scallions.
cheapTips: Brown rice in bulk is one of the cheapest whole grains
Frozen edamame stores for months — always have it on hand

substitutions.swap: 1 tsp honey + 1 tsp rice vinegar
White rice cooks faster if you're short on time

recipes.name: Korean-Spiced Ground Beef Salad Bowl
recipes.description: Gochujang-glazed ground beef over crunchy greens and rice — a deconstructed bibimbap that comes together in 15 minutes.
steps: Cook rice. Brown ground beef over medium-high heat.
Mix gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, and honey; pour over cooked beef and stir 2 min.
Thinly slice cucumber. Wilte spinach in the warm pan if desired.
Bowl: rice, beef, spinach, cucumber, scallions, sesame seeds.
cheapTips: A jar of gochujang costs ~$7 and seasons dozens of meals
Ground beef in family packs is often 20% cheaper per pound

substitutions.swap: 1 tbsp sriracha + 1 tsp miso paste
Ground turkey for leaner Korean bowl

recipes.name: Cold Soba Noodle Peanut Bowl
recipes.description: Chilled soba noodles tossed in a creamy peanut-sesame-ginger dressing with edamame and crunchy vegetables — a 25-minute meal that's equally satisfying hot or cold.
steps: Cook soba noodles per package (4–5 min), rinse under cold water, drain.
Microwave edamame. Slice cucumber. Chop scallions.
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, sesame oil, lime juice, ginger, garlic, sriracha, and 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Toss noodles with dressing, edamame, spinach, and cucumber. Top with scallions.
cheapTips: Soba noodles cost ~$4 for a bag that serves 4+ people
Peanut butter dressing costs pennies per serving

substitutions.swap: Rice noodles (gluten-free) or spaghetti
Almond butter or sunflower butter for nut-free

recipes.name: Chinese Sesame Ginger Chicken Salad
recipes.description: Shredded chicken tossed with sesame-ginger dressing, crunchy lettuce, and scallions — the classic takeout salad made at home for under $3 per serving.
steps: Poach chicken breasts in simmering water with ginger and garlic, 15 min. Cool and shred.
Cook rice. Make dressing: sesame oil, soy sauce, vinegar, honey, ginger, garlic.
Tear lettuce, slice cucumber, chop scallions.
Toss chicken with dressing. Serve over rice with lettuce, cucumber, scallions, sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Poaching is the cheapest no-oil cooking method for chicken
Sesame seeds last a year — buy once, use everywhere

substitutions.swap: Rice vinegar or lime juice
Skip rice for a lighter, pure-salad version

recipes.name: Vietnamese Shrimp and Herb Rice Noodle Salad
recipes.description: Plump shrimp over cold rice noodles with a forest of fresh herbs, cucumber, and a zingy lime-chili dressing — bright, refreshing, and ready in 20 minutes.
steps: Soak rice noodles in boiling water 6–8 min, drain and rinse cold.
Cook shrimp in a hot pan with garlic, 2 min per side. Cool.
Whisk lime juice, chili-garlic sauce, soy sauce, honey, and garlic into a bright dressing.
Tear lettuce. Slice cucumber. Chop mint, cilantro, scallions.
Arrange noodles in bowls; top with shrimp, herbs, cucumber, lettuce. Drizzle dressing.
cheapTips: Rice noodles cost ~$0.50 per serving and are naturally gluten-free
Fresh herbs make this salad — a single bunch goes a long way

substitutions.swap: Poached chicken breast, shredded
Soba or thin pasta

recipes.name: Miso-Glazed Salmon Brown Rice Bowl
recipes.description: Caramelized miso-marinated salmon over brown rice with sesame spinach — a Japanese-style bowl that feels restaurant-worthy.
steps: Marinate salmon in soy sauce, mirin, honey, and grated ginger, 5–30 min.
Bake salmon at 400°F for 12–14 min (or broil for caramelization). Cook brown rice.
Sauté spinach in 1 tsp sesame oil and garlic until wilted.
Bowl: rice, sesame spinach, glazed salmon. Top with sesame seeds and scallions.
cheapTips: Canned salmon can substitute — stir the miso glaze in after heating

substitutions.swap: 1 tsp honey + 1 tsp rice vinegar
Tofu (marinate and bake the same way)

recipes.name: Spicy Tofu Rice Noodle Bowl
recipes.description: Crispy pan-fried tofu and rice noodles in a fiery chili-garlic-sesame sauce with fresh vegetables — a weeknight vegan bowl with real heat.
steps: Press tofu dry and cube. Fry in vegetable oil over high heat, 3–4 min per side until golden.
Soak rice noodles in boiling water 6 min, drain.
Sauté garlic and ginger 30 sec, add chili-garlic sauce, soy sauce, sesame oil.
Add bell pepper, spinach, and noodles; toss 2 min.
Top with crispy tofu and scallions.
cheapTips: Tofu absorbs sauce better when pressed and fried — don't skip the press step
Rice noodles need no boiling pot — just a bowl of boiling water

substitutions.swap: Tempeh for a nuttier texture
Gochujang + a splash of water for Korean twist

recipes.name: Asian Chicken Lettuce Slaw Bowl
recipes.description: Crunchy shredded lettuce slaw with pulled chicken, edamame, and a sesame-lime dressing — a cool, textured bowl that's a refreshing change from hot lunches.
steps: Poach chicken, shred. Cook rice. Microwave edamame.
Shred lettuce into thin strips. Slice cucumber and scallions.
Whisk sesame oil, soy sauce, lime, ginger, garlic into dressing.
Toss lettuce, cucumber, edamame, scallions with dressing. Top with chicken and sesame seeds over rice.
cheapTips: A head of lettuce provides 2–3 servings of slaw for ~$2.50
Shredding lettuce finely makes it feel like a real restaurant slaw

substitutions.swap: Canned chicken for an even quicker prep
Skip the rice for a pure low-carb slaw bowl

recipes.name: Teriyaki Tofu and Spinach Bowl
recipes.description: Pan-glazed teriyaki tofu over brown rice and wilted sesame spinach — a completely plant-based bowl that satisfies like a classic Japanese dinner.
steps: Press and cube tofu. Fry in vegetable oil over medium-high heat until golden, 4 min per side.
Mix soy sauce, mirin, honey, ginger into teriyaki glaze. Pour over tofu and cook 2 min until sticky.
Cook brown rice. Wilt spinach in sesame oil and garlic.
Bowl: rice, sesame spinach, teriyaki tofu, scallions, sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Homemade teriyaki sauce costs pennies vs. bottled at $4–6
A block of tofu at $2.75 gives 28 g protein

substitutions.swap: Tempeh for a heartier, fermented option
1 tbsp sugar + 1 tbsp rice vinegar

recipes.name: High-Protein Cobb Salad
recipes.description: The classic Cobb — grilled chicken, hard-boiled eggs, crispy bacon, and avocado over spinach — rebuilt for serious protein with every bite.
steps: Hard-boil eggs (7 min). Cool, peel, and halve.
Season and cook chicken in 1 tbsp olive oil, 5–6 min per side. Slice.
Cook bacon strips until crispy; drain on paper towel and crumble.
Make vinaigrette: olive oil, vinegar, Dijon, salt, pepper.
Arrange spinach in bowls; top in rows with chicken, eggs, bacon, avocado, tomato, and feta. Drizzle dressing.
cheapTips: Bacon adds big flavor — 3 strips across 2 servings keeps cost and calories in check
Hard-boiled eggs are the cheapest protein per gram in the salad

substitutions.swap: Turkey bacon for less saturated fat
Blue cheese crumbles for traditional Cobb flavor

recipes.name: Buffalo Chicken Salad Bowl
recipes.description: Spicy buffalo-glazed chicken over crisp lettuce with creamy dressing and celery — all the bar-food flavor in a macro-friendly bowl.
steps: Cook chicken in olive oil, 5–6 min per side. Toss with buffalo sauce while still hot.
Make ranch-style dressing: Greek yogurt + garlic + salt + a splash of water.
Chop lettuce and spinach. Dice tomato. Slice cucumber.
Serve buffalo chicken over greens with ranch drizzle, tomato, cucumber, and feta.
cheapTips: Buffalo sauce costs ~$0.15 per tbsp and transforms plain chicken
Greek yogurt dressing is healthier and cheaper than bottled ranch

substitutions.swap: Sriracha + melted butter (1:1 ratio) in a pinch
Blue cheese crumbles for classic buffalo pairing

recipes.name: Southwest Chicken and Black Bean Salad
recipes.description: Smoky grilled chicken, black beans, corn, and avocado over lettuce with a zesty lime-cumin dressing — a Tex-Mex salad that's bold, filling, and budget-friendly.
steps: Season chicken with cumin, chili powder, garlic, salt. Cook in olive oil, 5–6 min per side. Slice.
Microwave corn 3 min. Drain and rinse black beans.
Dressing: lime juice, 1 tbsp olive oil, cumin, garlic, cilantro.
Serve spinach topped with chicken, beans, corn, avocado, tomato. Drizzle dressing.
cheapTips: Canned black beans and frozen corn make this salad under $2 per serving in protein
Avocado can be replaced with guacamole from a tube for convenience

substitutions.swap: Guacamole (2 tbsp per serving)
Canned chicken breast for a no-cook protein

recipes.name: Warm Bacon and Egg Spinach Salad
recipes.description: Hot pan drippings wilt fresh spinach into a glossy salad, topped with crispy bacon bits and soft-boiled eggs — a bistro classic done in 15 minutes.
steps: Soft-boil eggs (7 min for jammy centers), cool in ice water, peel and halve.
Cook bacon until crispy. Remove bacon, leave 1 tbsp drippings in the pan.
Off heat, whisk vinegar, Dijon, honey, garlic, salt into warm drippings.
Pour warm dressing over spinach; it will wilt slightly. Add tomatoes.
Top with crumbled bacon and halved eggs.
cheapTips: 4 strips of bacon gives huge flavor at ~$2.30 for 2 servings
Soft-boiled eggs are faster than hard-boiled and creamier

substitutions.swap: Turkey bacon reduces fat by ~50%
Apple cider vinegar works perfectly

recipes.name: Honey Mustard Turkey Salad
recipes.description: Pan-seared turkey tenderloins sliced over mixed greens with a glossy honey-Dijon dressing, crisp apple slices, and walnuts — a crowd-pleaser in under 25 minutes.
steps: Form ground turkey into 2 patties; season with salt, pepper, garlic. Cook in 1 tbsp olive oil, 5–6 min per side. Slice into strips.
Whisk Dijon, honey, apple cider vinegar, remaining olive oil, salt — this is both dressing and marinade.
Core and slice apple thin. Roughly chop walnuts.
Toss spinach with dressing. Top with turkey, apple, and walnuts.
cheapTips: Ground turkey patties are a budget-smart way to get the same seared texture as a turkey breast cutlet
A single apple stretches across 2 full servings

substitutions.swap: Almonds or pecans — or sunflower seeds for nut-free
Pear or mandarin orange segments

recipes.name: Greek Protein Salad
recipes.description: The full Greek — chicken, chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, olives, feta, and red onion in a tangy oregano vinaigrette. Done in 20 minutes, travels well.
steps: Season chicken with Italian seasoning, salt, garlic. Cook in olive oil, 5–6 min per side. Slice.
Drain and rinse chickpeas. Dice cucumber, tomato. Chop spinach.
Whisk remaining olive oil, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, garlic, salt.
Toss vegetables and chickpeas with dressing. Top with chicken and feta.
cheapTips: Chickpeas make this salad more filling and add 18 g protein for $1.10
Oregano or Italian seasoning is the key flavor — use generously

substitutions.swap: Canned tuna or salmon for a no-cook version
Romaine lettuce for a more traditional Greek salad

recipes.name: BBQ Chicken Corn Salad
recipes.description: Sweet-smoky BBQ chicken over corn, black beans, and spinach with a tangy BBQ-lime dressing — summer cookout flavors in a 20-minute salad.
steps: Mix buffalo sauce (as BBQ substitute) with honey and garlic into a glaze. Coat chicken and cook in olive oil, 5–6 min per side.
Microwave corn. Drain black beans.
Make lime-cumin-cilantro dressing.
Serve spinach topped with sliced BBQ chicken, corn, beans, tomato, dressing.
cheapTips: Buffalo sauce + honey makes a convincing quick BBQ glaze for under $0.50
Canned black beans and frozen corn keep the cost under $1.50 for the salad base

substitutions.swap: Actual BBQ sauce if you have it
Parsley if you're not a cilantro fan

recipes.name: Chef Salad Protein Bowl
recipes.description: The diner classic rebuilt for macros: deli turkey, hard-boiled eggs, cheese, cucumber, tomato, and spinach with a tangy red wine vinaigrette.
steps: Hard-boil eggs (7 min). Cool and halve.
Roll deli turkey slices and cut into strips.
Make vinaigrette: olive oil, vinegar, Dijon, honey, salt.
Build bowls: spinach, turkey, halved eggs, cheese, cucumber, tomato. Drizzle dressing.
cheapTips: Deli turkey from the deli counter costs less per serving than packaged slices
A chef salad requires no cooking except the eggs — ultra low effort

substitutions.swap: Canned chicken or deli ham
Feta for a Mediterranean twist

recipes.name: Waldorf-Inspired Chicken Salad
recipes.description: Creamy-tangy shredded chicken with crisp apple, crunchy walnuts, celery-like cucumber, and spinach — the hotel classic reinvented as a macro-friendly bowl.
steps: Poach and shred chicken breasts. Cool.
Make Waldorf dressing: Greek yogurt, mayo, Dijon, lemon juice, honey, salt, pepper.
Core and cube apple. Slice cucumber. Roughly chop walnuts.
Toss shredded chicken with dressing, apple, walnuts, cucumber.
Serve over spinach.
cheapTips: Greek yogurt replacing half the mayo cuts fat without losing creaminess
Poached chicken is the cheapest protein — use leftover chicken to skip cooking entirely

substitutions.swap: Extra Greek yogurt for a lighter, tangier dressing
Pecans or sliced almonds

recipes.name: Apple Walnut Spinach Salad with Chicken
recipes.description: Crisp apple, toasted walnuts, tangy feta, and grilled chicken over baby spinach with a maple-Dijon dressing — a flavor-packed salad that doubles as a weekday treat.
steps: Season and cook chicken in olive oil, 5–6 min per side. Slice.
Toast walnuts in a dry pan 2–3 min until fragrant.
Dressing: whisk maple syrup, Dijon, vinegar, olive oil, garlic, salt.
Thinly slice apple. Arrange spinach, apple, walnuts, and feta in bowls.
Top with chicken and drizzle dressing.
cheapTips: One apple and one serving of walnuts keep this well under $2 per serving for the salad components
Toasting walnuts in a dry pan takes 2 min and doubles their flavor

substitutions.swap: Honey for the same sweet-tangy effect
Goat cheese for a creamier option

recipes.name: Greek Chicken Grain Bowl
recipes.description: Herb-marinated chicken over quinoa with cucumber, tomato, Kalamata-style feta, and tzatziki-inspired yogurt — a Greek island lunch in a bowl.
steps: Marinate chicken in lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, Italian seasoning, salt, 10 min.
Cook quinoa (15 min). Cook chicken in same pan over medium-high heat, 5–6 min per side.
Make quick tzatziki: Greek yogurt + minced garlic + dill + lemon juice + salt.
Dice cucumber and tomato.
Bowl: quinoa, sliced chicken, cucumber, tomato, feta, and a big spoonful of tzatziki.
cheapTips: Tzatziki made from Greek yogurt costs a fraction of the store-bought version
Italian seasoning as a stand-in for individual dried herbs cuts the spice cabinet cost

substitutions.swap: 1 tsp dried dill weed
Couscous (5 min cook time) for a faster base

recipes.name: Falafel-Spiced Chickpea Grain Bowl
recipes.description: Pan-crisped chickpeas seasoned with classic falafel spices over quinoa with tahini dressing, cucumber, and tomato — all the falafel flavor without the frying.
steps: Toss drained chickpeas with olive oil, cumin, paprika, garlic, salt. Roast at 425°F, 20 min until crispy.
Cook quinoa. Dice cucumber, tomato. Chop parsley.
Make tahini dressing: tahini + lemon juice + garlic + water + salt (whisk until smooth).
Bowl: quinoa, spinach, crispy chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, parsley. Drizzle tahini dressing.
cheapTips: A can of chickpeas costs $1.10 and feeds two generously
Tahini lasts months — buy once and use it in dozens of dishes

substitutions.swap: Peanut butter for a nutty dressing
Couscous or brown rice

recipes.name: Moroccan-Spiced Lentil Grain Bowl
recipes.description: Warming cumin-coriander lentils over couscous with roasted sweet potato and a bright lemon dressing — North African comfort food made weekday-easy.
steps: Cube sweet potato; toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, paprika, salt. Roast at 425°F, 25 min.
Simmer lentils in 2.5 cups water with garlic, cumin, curry powder, 22 min.
Prepare couscous: pour boiling water over couscous (1:1 ratio), cover 5 min, fluff.
Stir spinach into warm lentils. Season with lemon juice.
Bowl: couscous, Moroccan lentils, roasted sweet potato, cilantro.
cheapTips: Couscous is the fastest-cooking grain — 5 minutes with boiling water
Lentils and sweet potato together cost about $1.50 for 3 servings

substitutions.swap: Quinoa for a gluten-free version
Butternut squash or regular potato

recipes.name: Shakshuka-Spiced Egg Grain Bowl
recipes.description: Shakshuka's smoky tomato-pepper sauce spooned over quinoa with poached eggs and feta — all the magic of the skillet dish served over grains.
steps: Cook quinoa (15 min). Sauté onion and bell pepper in olive oil, 5 min.
Add garlic, cumin, paprika; cook 1 min. Add crushed tomatoes; simmer 8 min.
Make 4 wells in the sauce. Crack an egg into each. Cover and cook 5 min for jammy yolks.
Serve sauce and eggs over quinoa. Crumble feta and parsley on top.
cheapTips: A can of crushed tomatoes costs $2 and forms the entire sauce base
Shakshuka for 2 costs under $5 total — one of the best value meals here

substitutions.swap: Brown rice or couscous
Goat cheese or skip for dairy-free

recipes.name: Lemon Herb Chicken Couscous Bowl
recipes.description: Fluffy couscous with lemon-herb-marinated chicken, roasted vegetables, and a bright parsley dressing — a Mediterranean bowl that's ready in under 30 minutes.
steps: Slice bell pepper and zucchini; toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and cumin. Roast at 425°F, 20 min.
Marinate chicken in lemon juice, garlic, 1 tbsp olive oil, cumin, salt. Cook in a hot pan, 5–6 min per side.
Prepare couscous: boil 1 cup water, pour over couscous, cover 5 min, fluff with a fork.
Toss couscous with lemon juice, parsley, garlic, salt.
Bowl: herbed couscous, sliced chicken, roasted vegetables.
cheapTips: Couscous is the fastest and cheapest grain base — under $0.40 per serving
Lemon juice brightens every component of this dish for under $0.70

substitutions.swap: Quinoa or bulgur wheat
Eggplant, cherry tomatoes, or asparagus

recipes.name: Hummus and Roasted Veggie Grain Bowl
recipes.description: A thick layer of hummus anchors a grain bowl piled with caramelized roasted vegetables and crispy chickpeas — proof that vegan bowls can be wildly satisfying.
steps: Cube sweet potato and slice bell pepper. Toss with half the olive oil, cumin, paprika, salt. Roast at 425°F, 25 min.
Toss chickpeas with remaining oil and spices; add to the pan for the last 10 min.
Cook quinoa. Wilt spinach with garlic and lemon.
Spread hummus thick on bottom of each bowl. Add quinoa, roasted veg, crispy chickpeas, wilted spinach.
cheapTips: Store-bought hummus is fine — or make your own from canned chickpeas for half the cost
Roasting the veggie and chickpeas on one pan means one pan to wash

substitutions.swap: Tahini dressing if you prefer less thickness
Butternut squash or regular potato

recipes.name: Turkish-Spiced Ground Beef Rice Bowl
recipes.description: Ground beef fragrant with cumin, cinnamon, and allspice over rice with roasted tomato and a cool yogurt drizzle — Istanbul in a bowl.
steps: Cook rice. Sauté onion in olive oil, 5 min. Add garlic and spices; cook 1 min.
Add ground beef; cook 8 min until browned.
Dice tomatoes and stir in; cook 3 more min.
Mix yogurt with lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Bowl: rice, spiced beef, lemon yogurt, fresh parsley.
cheapTips: Cinnamon and cumin transform ground beef into something exotic for under $0.10 in spices
Ground beef in family packs is often $1–1.50 per serving

substitutions.swap: Ground lamb (traditional) or ground turkey (leaner)
A pinch of allspice + nutmeg as a substitute

recipes.name: Persian Herb Chicken Rice Bowl
recipes.description: Turmeric-golden chicken over fragrant herb rice with caramelized onions and a saffron-yogurt drizzle — a simplified Persian rice bowl that's aromatic and nourishing.
steps: Cook rice. Slice onion and caramelize in 1 tbsp olive oil over medium-low heat, 15 min until golden.
Season chicken with cumin, paprika, salt, garlic. Cook in 1 tbsp olive oil, 5–6 min per side.
Stir most of the parsley and mint into the warm rice.
Make yogurt sauce: yogurt + lemon + salt + remaining herbs.
Bowl: herb rice, sliced chicken, caramelized onions, yogurt drizzle.
cheapTips: Caramelized onions take time but cost $0.55 and transform a simple rice bowl
Fresh parsley and mint at $1–1.50 per bunch make a major flavor impact

substitutions.swap: A pinch of dried mint works in the rice
Chicken thighs for more flavor

recipes.name: North African Spiced Chickpea Bowl
recipes.description: Harissa-spiced roasted chickpeas over couscous with roasted carrots, raisins, and a cooling yogurt — North African flavors done in 30 minutes.
steps: Toss chickpeas and sliced carrot with harissa, olive oil, cumin, honey, salt. Roast at 425°F, 25 min.
Prepare couscous. Wilt spinach.
Make yogurt sauce: yogurt + lemon + garlic + salt.
Bowl: couscous, wilted spinach, harissa chickpeas and carrots, yogurt.
cheapTips: Harissa paste lasts months refrigerated and makes any bowl interesting for $0.38/tbsp
Carrots are one of the cheapest vegetables available year-round

substitutions.swap: Sriracha + a pinch of cumin as a substitute
Quinoa for a protein-boosted base

recipes.name: Mediterranean Tuna Couscous Bowl
recipes.description: Herb-tossed couscous with canned tuna, chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, and lemon — a 10-minute bowl with zero cooking that delivers 38 g protein.
steps: Prepare couscous: boil 1 cup water, pour over couscous, cover 5 min, fluff.
Drain tuna and chickpeas. Dice cucumber, tomato. Chop parsley.
Dress couscous with olive oil, lemon juice, vinegar, garlic, salt.
Fold in tuna, chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, spinach, and parsley.
Serve at room temperature or refrigerate up to 2 days.
cheapTips: Two cans of tuna + one can of chickpeas cost ~$3.60 and fill two generous bowls
Couscous needs only boiling water — no pot, no stove required

substitutions.swap: Canned salmon or canned chicken
Quinoa (15 min cook time) for gluten-free

recipes.name: Tahini Buddha Bowl
recipes.description: The quintessential plant-based bowl: roasted sweet potato, crispy chickpeas, quinoa, kale, and a creamy tahini-lemon dressing over everything.
steps: Cube sweet potato and toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, cumin, paprika, salt. Roast at 425°F, 25 min.
Toss chickpeas with remaining oil and spices; add to pan for the last 10 min.
Cook quinoa. Massage kale with a pinch of salt until softened.
Make tahini dressing: tahini + lemon juice + garlic + water + salt.
Build bowls: quinoa, kale, sweet potato, chickpeas. Drizzle tahini generously.
cheapTips: This bowl is under $3 per serving with all pantry-friendly ingredients
Kale lasts a week refrigerated — buy once, use across multiple meals

substitutions.swap: Spinach or arugula (no massaging needed)
Roasted butternut squash or beets

recipes.name: Roasted Bell Pepper and Goat Cheese Quinoa Bowl
recipes.description: Caramelized roasted peppers, cherry tomatoes, and chickpeas over herb quinoa with crumbled feta — a simple, colorful Mediterranean bowl.
steps: Slice peppers and tomatoes; toss with olive oil, garlic, balsamic, Italian seasoning. Roast at 425°F, 20 min.
Toss chickpeas with remaining oil and herbs; add to pan last 8 min.
Cook quinoa. Stir spinach into warm quinoa.
Build bowls: quinoa-spinach, roasted peppers and chickpeas, crumbled feta.
cheapTips: Bell peppers roasted become sweet and concentrated — 3 peppers feel like 6
A small amount of feta goes a long way as a flavor accent

substitutions.swap: Goat cheese crumbles or skip for vegan
Red wine vinegar for a sharper glaze

recipes.name: Southwest Black Bean Grain Bowl
recipes.description: Smoky black beans, roasted corn, avocado, and cilantro over quinoa with a zesty lime dressing — a vegan Tex-Mex bowl that costs under $2.50 per serving.
steps: Cook quinoa. Warm black beans in a pan with cumin, chili powder, garlic, salt.
Char corn in the same pan 3–4 min until slightly blackened.
Make lime-cilantro dressing: lime juice + olive oil + cilantro + garlic + salt.
Bowl: quinoa, spinach, black beans, charred corn, diced avocado, tomato. Drizzle dressing.
cheapTips: Black beans and quinoa together cost about $1.50 per serving and deliver complete protein
Charring frozen corn in a dry pan takes 3 min and adds major flavor

substitutions.swap: Guacamole if the avocado isn't ripe
Brown rice for a cheaper base

recipes.name: Green Goddess Tofu Bowl
recipes.description: Crispy pan-fried tofu over brown rice and blanched spinach with a vibrant green yogurt-herb dressing — a bowl that earns its regal name.
steps: Press and cube tofu. Fry in olive oil until golden on all sides, 8–10 min.
Cook brown rice. Blanch spinach 30 seconds; squeeze dry.
Blend Greek yogurt, parsley, lemon juice, garlic, Dijon, salt, and a splash of water into a smooth green dressing.
Bowl: rice, blanched spinach, cucumber, tofu. Drizzle green goddess dressing generously.
cheapTips: A blender or immersion blender makes the dressing silky — but whisking finely chopped herbs works too
Tofu is the cheapest high-protein ingredient per gram after eggs

substitutions.swap: Tempeh or grilled chicken
Blended silken tofu for a vegan dressing

recipes.name: Savory Mushroom Brown Rice Bowl
recipes.description: Umami-rich sautéed mushrooms with garlic and soy over brown rice and spinach — an understated bowl that punches well above its cost.
steps: Cook brown rice (20 min). Microwave edamame.
Heat vegetable oil in a wide pan over high heat. Add mushrooms in a single layer — don't stir for 3 min to get a sear.
Add garlic, ginger; cook 1 min. Deglaze with soy sauce. Add spinach; wilt.
Stir in sesame oil off heat.
Bowl: rice, sautéed mushroom-spinach, edamame. Top with scallions and sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Mushrooms are one of the few vegetables that taste better the less you cook them (high heat, don't crowd)
Edamame adds 18 g protein per cup for just $1.20

substitutions.swap: King oyster or shiitake mushrooms for extra meatiness
Soba noodles for a different carb base

recipes.name: Mango Black Bean Tropical Bowl
recipes.description: Sweet-spicy black beans with frozen mango chunks over quinoa — a tropical Caribbean-inspired bowl that's vegan, vibrant, and ready in 20 minutes.
steps: Cook quinoa (15 min). Thaw mango or use as semi-frozen chunks.
Warm black beans with cumin, chili powder, garlic, and a squeeze of lime.
Make mango-lime dressing: mango juice from thawing + lime + honey + cilantro.
Bowl: quinoa, spinach, seasoned black beans, mango chunks. Drizzle dressing.
cheapTips: Frozen mango is far cheaper than fresh and year-round available at ~$1.35/cup
Black beans and quinoa together cost about $1.50 per serving

substitutions.swap: Canned pineapple chunks or fresh mango
Brown rice for a budget swap

recipes.name: Tempeh and Roasted Vegetable Bowl
recipes.description: Marinated and pan-seared tempeh over brown rice with a rainbow of roasted vegetables and a tangy soy-ginger dressing — the heartiest vegan bowl in the collection.
steps: Slice tempeh. Marinate in soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, ginger for 10 min.
Roast bell pepper, zucchini, broccoli with olive oil at 425°F, 20 min.
Pan-sear tempeh in the marinade over medium heat, 4 min per side.
Cook brown rice.
Bowl: rice, roasted veg, seared tempeh. Drizzle with remaining marinade. Top sesame seeds and scallions.
cheapTips: Tempeh absorbs marinade aggressively — even 10 minutes makes a big difference
Broccoli, zucchini, and bell pepper all roast perfectly together at 425°F

substitutions.swap: Tofu or extra-firm seitan
Eggplant or mushrooms

recipes.name: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Grain Bowl
recipes.description: Roasted sweet potato cubes and warm black beans over quinoa with avocado and a lime-cumin dressing — a filling, colorful bowl that costs $2 per serving.
steps: Cube sweet potato; toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, cumin, chili powder, salt. Roast at 425°F, 25 min.
Cook quinoa. Warm black beans with garlic and cumin.
Make lime-cilantro dressing with remaining olive oil.
Bowl: quinoa, spinach, roasted sweet potato, black beans, diced avocado. Drizzle dressing.
cheapTips: Sweet potatoes + black beans is one of the most nutritionally complete and affordable meal combos
Two sweet potatoes, one can of black beans, and quinoa cost about $3.50 total

substitutions.swap: Guacamole or sour cream for a non-vegan version
Brown rice for a cheaper base

recipes.name: Avocado and Chickpea Grain Bowl
recipes.description: Creamy avocado and crispy roasted chickpeas over herbed quinoa with lemon-tahini — a bowl so satisfying you'll stop reaching for wraps.
steps: Toss chickpeas with olive oil, cumin, salt. Roast at 425°F, 20 min.
Cook quinoa with garlic and a pinch of salt.
Make tahini dressing: tahini + lemon + garlic + water + salt.
Dice avocado, tomato, cucumber.
Bowl: quinoa, spinach, avocado, tomato, cucumber, crispy chickpeas. Drizzle tahini.
cheapTips: Crispy roasted chickpeas add the crunch of croutons at a fraction of the calories
A can of chickpeas at $1.10 is the only real protein cost here

substitutions.swap: Almond butter for a different nutty dressing
Edamame for less fat and more protein

recipes.name: Harissa Roasted Vegetable Grain Bowl
recipes.description: Fiery harissa-glazed mixed vegetables over couscous with a cooling yogurt drizzle — a North African bowl with maximum flavor for minimal effort.
steps: Toss bell peppers, sweet potato, and chickpeas with harissa, olive oil, garlic, honey, salt. Roast at 425°F, 25 min.
Prepare couscous. Wilt spinach.
Make cool yogurt drizzle: yogurt + lemon + salt.
Bowl: couscous, spinach, harissa vegetables, drizzle of cool yogurt.
cheapTips: Harissa paste transforms a simple vegetable roast into something special for $0.38/tbsp
One can of chickpeas stretches this bowl to a full protein-balanced meal

substitutions.swap: Sriracha + cumin as a quick harissa substitute
Labneh or sour cream

recipes.name: Shrimp, Corn, and Avocado Bowl
recipes.description: Sautéed shrimp with charred corn and diced avocado over brown rice — a simple, summery bowl with great flavors in under 20 minutes.
steps: Cook brown rice (20 min). Char corn in a dry pan over high heat, 4 min.
Melt butter in same pan; add garlic, chili powder, shrimp. Cook 2 min per side.
Squeeze lime over shrimp. Dice avocado.
Bowl: rice, spinach, shrimp, charred corn, avocado, cilantro.
cheapTips: Frozen corn charred in a dry pan tastes just as good as fresh corn off the cob
Frozen shrimp thaws in 10 min under cold water — always have a bag in the freezer

substitutions.swap: Olive oil or coconut oil
Quinoa for extra protein

recipes.name: Sardine and White Bean Herb Salad
recipes.description: Canned sardines with white beans, cherry tomatoes, fresh herbs, and a bright lemon dressing — one of the most nutritious no-cook lunches in the book at under $3.
steps: Drain sardines (reserve a little oil if packed in olive oil). Drain and rinse white beans.
Dice tomatoes. Chop parsley.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, vinegar, Dijon, garlic, salt into a dressing.
Toss everything together. Taste and season. Serve immediately.
cheapTips: Two cans of sardines cost ~$4 and provide 46 g protein total — the best protein value in the collection
Sardines are also one of the richest food sources of omega-3 fatty acids

substitutions.swap: Canned mackerel or canned salmon
Chickpeas or cannellini beans

recipes.name: Salmon and Avocado Quinoa Bowl
recipes.description: Pan-seared salmon over quinoa with sliced avocado, cucumber, and a creamy lemon-tahini dressing — a restaurant-quality bowl at a fraction of the price.
steps: Cook quinoa (15 min). Season salmon with salt, pepper, and dijon.
Sear salmon in olive oil over medium-high heat, 4 min skin-down, flip 2–3 min. Rest.
Make tahini-lemon dressing: tahini + lemon + garlic + water + salt.
Slice avocado and cucumber.
Bowl: quinoa, spinach, salmon, avocado, cucumber. Drizzle tahini dressing.
cheapTips: Canned salmon works here — drain well, mix with Dijon, and serve as a cold protein
Searing salmon with the skin on protects it from overcooking

substitutions.swap: Canned salmon for a no-cook version
Miso + lemon for a Japanese-inspired dressing

recipes.name: Tuna and Avocado Brown Rice Bowl
recipes.description: Soy-seasoned canned tuna, creamy avocado, and cucumber over brown rice with a sesame-ginger dressing — a deconstructed tuna poke bowl for under $3.
steps: Cook brown rice. Drain tuna.
Season tuna with soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, sriracha.
Dice avocado and cucumber.
Bowl: rice, spinach, seasoned tuna, avocado, cucumber, scallions, sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Two cans of tuna give 52 g protein for $2.80 — this is the most economical poke bowl possible
Sesame oil is the secret that makes canned tuna taste like something special
