Add minced garlic, ginger, paprika, cayenne, and fenugreek and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken pieces and brown on all sides for 5 minutes.
Pour in water and salt, bring to simmer and cook covered for 25 minutes.
Hard boil eggs separately, then peel and add to the stew in the last 5 minutes of cooking.
cheapTips: Use chicken drumsticks instead of thighs for lower cost
Buy spices from ethnic markets in bulk

recipes.name: Misir Wot
recipes.description: Ethiopian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice onions and cook in butter over medium heat until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, paprika, and cayenne and stir for 1 minute.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add rinsed lentils and water, bring to boil.
Reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 25-30 minutes until lentils are very soft.
Stir frequently and mash some lentils against the pot to thicken the stew.
cheapTips: Red lentils are one of the cheapest proteins at the grocery store
Buy in bulk and store in airtight containers for months

recipes.name: Shiro
recipes.description: Ethiopian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice the onion and cook in butter over medium heat until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, ginger, paprika, and cayenne and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk chickpea flour into water until smooth with no lumps.
Pour flour mixture into the pot with onions, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat to medium-low and continue stirring frequently for 15-20 minutes until thickened.
Add salt and stir well to combine.
cheapTips: Use Bob's Red Mill or store-brand chickpea flour
Make large batches and reheat for multiple meals

recipes.name: Gomen
recipes.description: Ethiopian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Wash collard greens thoroughly and remove tough stems, then chop into bite-sized pieces.
Dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion for 5 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, paprika, and red pepper flakes and cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped collard greens and salt, stirring to coat with oil.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until greens are tender.
cheapTips: Buy collard greens when on sale and freeze for later
Use mustard greens or kale as substitutes

recipes.name: Kitfo
recipes.description: Ethiopian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Add minced garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in paprika, cayenne pepper, and mitmita and cook for 30 seconds.
Add ground beef and cook while stirring, breaking it into small pieces as it cooks, about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and adjust spices to taste.
cheapTips: Use 80/20 ground beef for better flavor and lower cost
Buy in bulk and freeze portions

recipes.name: Tibs
recipes.description: Ethiopian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut beef into 1-inch cubes and season with salt and paprika.
Dice onion, bell pepper, and tomato; mince garlic.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Brown beef cubes in batches for 5 minutes, then set aside.
In the same skillet, sauté onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, and bell pepper and cook for 2 minutes.
Return beef to the skillet, add diced tomato, and simmer for 10 minutes until beef is tender.
cheapTips: Use chuck roast instead of sirloin and cube yourself
Buy vegetables in season for better prices

recipes.name: Injera
recipes.description: Ethiopian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix teff flour, all-purpose flour, and salt in a large bowl.
Add water gradually while whisking to form a smooth batter without lumps.
Stir in yeast and cover bowl with a towel.
Let batter ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, stirring once daily until it smells sour.
Heat a non-stick skillet or crepe pan over medium heat.
Pour about 1/2 cup batter into the center of the hot skillet and tilt to spread into a thin circle.
Cover the skillet with a lid and cook for 2-3 minutes until the top is set but still slightly moist.
Transfer to a plate and cool completely before stacking.
cheapTips: Buy teff flour online in bulk for much better pricing
Make several batches at once and freeze between parchment

recipes.name: Wat
recipes.description: Ethiopian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook diced onions until soft, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and ginger, stirring constantly for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in paprika and cayenne pepper and cook for 1 minute to bloom the spices.
Add beef cubes and brown on all sides for 5 minutes.
Mix in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in water, add salt, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer for 50-60 minutes until beef is very tender, stirring occasionally.
Adjust seasonings and serve hot over injera bread.
cheapTips: Use beef chuck instead of premium cuts for authentic flavor at lower cost
Buy paprika and cayenne in bulk from ethnic markets

recipes.name: Doro Tibs
recipes.description: Ethiopian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add onions and cook until golden, about 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken cubes and cook until lightly browned on all sides, about 8 minutes.
Add jalapeños and diced tomato, cooking for 3 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, then squeeze lemon juice over the dish.
Simmer for 10 minutes until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender.
Serve hot over injera or with rice.
cheapTips: Buy chicken in family packs and freeze portions
Use fresh tomatoes when in season for better flavor and cost

recipes.name: Shiro Wot
recipes.description: Ethiopian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté onions until soft, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and ginger, stirring for 2 minutes.
Mix paprika and cayenne into the onion mixture and cook for 1 minute.
In a bowl, whisk chickpea flour with 1 cup water to create a smooth paste.
Gradually add the flour mixture to the pot, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Pour in remaining water and stir well, bringing to a gentle simmer.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes, stirring frequently, until thickened and smooth.
Season with salt and serve on a platter lined with injera.
cheapTips: Buy chickpea flour in bulk from Indian or specialty stores
Make a double batch and freeze portions for quick meals

recipes.name: Kik Alicha
recipes.description: Ethiopian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse split peas under cold water and set aside.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté onions until soft, about 6 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger, stirring for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric and cook for 30 seconds.
Add rinsed split peas and stir to coat with oil.
Pour in water and bring to a boil, then reduce to simmer.
Cover and simmer for 35-40 minutes until peas are very soft and break down.
Stir occasionally and add salt and pepper to taste, serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy split peas in bulk from any grocery store
This dish freezes well for meal prep

recipes.name: Misir Alicha
recipes.description: Ethiopian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse red lentils thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté diced onions for 6 minutes.
Add minced garlic and ginger, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric and cook for 30 seconds to bloom.
Add rinsed lentils and stir well to combine.
Pour in water and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 30-35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lentils are soft and creamy.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve warm on injera.
cheapTips: Red lentils are one of the cheapest proteins available
Store in airtight containers for months

recipes.name: Beyaynetu
recipes.description: Ethiopian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Make wat: heat 2 tbsp oil, sauté 1.5 diced onions, add half the garlic and ginger, stir in paprika and cayenne, add beef, brown for 5 minutes.
Add 1.5 cups water to beef and simmer covered for 45 minutes until tender.
Make lentil stew: heat 2 tbsp oil, sauté 1 diced onion, add remaining garlic and ginger, add turmeric, then red lentils and 2 cups water, simmer 30 minutes.

Make shiro: heat 2 tbsp oil, sauté remaining diced onions until soft, add 1 tbsp paprika and 0.5 tsp cayenne, whisk chickpea flour with 1 cup water and add to pot, stir constantly while cooking for 20 minutes.
Arrange all three dishes on separate sections of a large platter lined with injera bread.
Serve warm and allow diners to mix flavors as desired.
cheapTips: Prepare components separately ahead of time for easier assembly
Make extra wat and lentil stew to freeze individually

recipes.name: Doro Alicha
recipes.description: Ethiopian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook diced onions until golden, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and ginger, stirring for 2 minutes.
Stir in turmeric and cook for 30 seconds.
Add chicken thighs and brown on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Pour in water and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer for 35-40 minutes until chicken is very tender, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot over injera bread.
cheapTips: Chicken thighs are cheaper than breasts and have better flavor for stewing
Buy onions in bulk when they go on sale

recipes.name: Beef Tibs
recipes.description: Ethiopian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat until very hot.
Add beef cubes and cook until browned on all sides, about 6 minutes; remove and set aside.
In the same skillet, add onions and cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Add garlic, ginger, and jalapeño, stirring for 1 minute.
Return beef to skillet and add bell pepper and diced tomato.
Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Serve hot over injera or with rice.
cheapTips: Buy beef on sale and freeze in portions
Use seasonal peppers for better prices

recipes.name: Lamb Tibs
recipes.description: Ethiopian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat until smoking.
Add lamb cubes in a single layer and sear for 4-5 minutes until browned; remove and set aside.
Add onions to the skillet and cook for 3 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, and rosemary, stirring for 1 minute.
Return lamb to skillet and add bell pepper and tomato.
Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lamb is cooked through.
Season with salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Remove rosemary sprigs and serve hot over injera.
cheapTips: Buy lamb shoulder instead of premium cuts for tibs
Make once a month when on sale and freeze portions

recipes.name: Niter Kibbeh
recipes.description: Ethiopian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Melt butter in a small saucepan over low heat, about 3 minutes.
Add minced onions and cook gently for 5 minutes without browning.
Stir in garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Add paprika, turmeric, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaf, stirring well.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes to infuse flavors, then remove from heat.
Let cool for 5 minutes, then pour through a fine-mesh strainer into a clean jar, leaving sediment behind.
Store in the refrigerator and use as a cooking base or bread dip.
cheapTips: Make a large batch and store for weeks
Buy butter when on sale and freeze until needed

recipes.name: Ful
recipes.description: Ethiopian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried fava beans in water overnight, then drain and rinse thoroughly.
Bring 6 cups fresh water to boil in a large pot and add the drained beans.
Simmer beans for 15-20 minutes until very soft and beginning to break apart.
Dice the onion and mince the garlic cloves finely.
Heat olive oil in a skillet and sauté onion and garlic until fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Add the cooked beans to the skillet and mash them roughly with a wooden spoon until chunky.
Season with salt and black pepper, stir well, and serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy dried fava beans in bulk from international aisles—much cheaper than canned.
Make a big batch and refrigerate for multiple breakfasts throughout the week.

recipes.name: Chikla
recipes.description: Ethiopian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix whole wheat flour, salt, and water in a bowl until a thick, lumpy batter forms.
Heat butter in a large skillet over medium heat until melted and foamy.
Pour the batter into the hot skillet and stir constantly with a wooden spoon.
Continue stirring for 8-10 minutes until the mixture thickens and browns slightly.
Transfer to a serving bowl and drizzle honey over the top.
Serve warm while still soft and slightly steaming.
cheapTips: Buy whole wheat flour from bulk bins to reduce cost.
Substitute honey with brown sugar or molasses if budget is tight.

recipes.name: Shakla Dist
recipes.description: Ethiopian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut beef into 1-inch cubes and pat dry with paper towels.
Dice onions finely and mince garlic and fresh ginger.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown beef in batches, about 3-4 minutes per batch.
Remove meat and set aside, then sauté onion, garlic, and ginger in the same pot for 5 minutes.
Add paprika, cayenne pepper, and tomato paste; stir constantly for 2 minutes.
Return beef to the pot, add water and salt, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-35 minutes until beef is very tender.
Adjust seasonings and serve hot with injera.
cheapTips: Use chuck roast instead of stew meat—cube it yourself to save 30%.
Buy onions and garlic in bulk; they store for weeks.

recipes.name: Misir Siga
recipes.description: Ethiopian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse red lentils thoroughly under cold water and set aside.
Dice onions finely and mince garlic and ginger.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown ground beef, breaking it apart with a spoon, about 5 minutes.
Add diced onion, garlic, and ginger; sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in paprika and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add lentils, water, salt, and black pepper; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-35 minutes until lentils completely fall apart and thicken.
Stir occasionally and adjust water if too thick; serve hot with injera.
cheapTips: Buy red lentils from bulk bins—significantly cheaper per pound.
Ground beef often goes on sale; freeze for future use.

recipes.name: Doro Wot Firfir
recipes.description: Ethiopian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces and pat dry.
Dice onions very finely and mince garlic and ginger.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion for 5-7 minutes until golden and soft.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add paprika and cayenne, stir constantly for 1 minute to avoid burning.
Add chicken pieces and stir to coat with spices, cooking for 3 minutes.
Pour in water and salt, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 20-25 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Peel and halve the hard-boiled eggs, add to the wot, and serve warm.
cheapTips: Use chicken legs instead of thighs for even more savings.
Buy eggs in bulk and hard-boil several at once.

recipes.name: Teff Injera
recipes.description: Ethiopian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix teff flour, salt, yeast, and water in a large bowl until you have a smooth batter with no lumps.
Cover the bowl loosely with a towel and let it ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until it smells sour and tangy.
Stir the batter once daily during fermentation.
After fermentation, heat a non-stick skillet or injera pan over medium-high heat until very hot.
Pour about 3/4 cup batter onto the hot surface and quickly tilt and rotate the pan to spread it into a thin, even circle about 10 inches wide.
Cover with a lid and cook for about 2-3 minutes until the top is set and small holes appear.
Remove from heat and carefully peel the injera onto a clean plate.
Repeat with remaining batter and serve as a base for stews and vegetables.
cheapTips: Find teff flour at international markets or online in bulk—cheaper than specialty stores.
Make a large batch and freeze extras for up to 3 months.

recipes.name: Kik Wot
recipes.description: Ethiopian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse dried split peas under cold water and drain completely.
Dice onion finely and mince garlic and fresh ginger.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in paprika and turmeric; cook for 30 seconds.
Add split peas, water, salt, and cayenne pepper; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until peas are completely soft and broken down.
Stir occasionally; the mixture should be thick and creamy; serve hot with injera.
cheapTips: Buy split peas in bulk bins at grocery stores for 50% savings.
Make double and freeze half for quick future dinners.

recipes.name: Siga Tibs
recipes.description: Ethiopian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut beef sirloin into small, thin strips and pat dry.
Dice bell peppers, onion, and tomatoes; mince garlic and ginger.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat until very hot.
Add beef strips in a single layer and cook without stirring for 2 minutes until browned, then stir and cook another 2 minutes.
Remove beef and set aside, then add onion and peppers to the skillet; stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the skillet, add tomatoes, salt, black pepper, and dry mustard; stir well.
Cook over high heat for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp and beef is cooked through; serve hot.
cheapTips: Use flank steak instead of sirloin and cut it thin against the grain.
Buy peppers and onions when on sale and store in the refrigerator.

recipes.name: Mitmita
recipes.description: Ethiopian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Remove seeds and stems from fresh chili peppers.
Place peppers and garlic cloves in a mortar and pestle.
Pound together roughly until you have a chunky, textured paste.
Transfer to a small bowl and mix in salt, olive oil, and lime juice.
Taste and adjust heat and saltiness to your preference.
Serve immediately as a condiment with injera or any Ethiopian meal.
cheapTips: Make a large batch and store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.
Use cheaper jalapeños or serrano peppers instead of specialty hot peppers.

recipes.name: Lentil Wat
recipes.description: Ethiopian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse brown lentils thoroughly under cold water and drain.
Dice onions very finely and mince garlic and fresh ginger.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion for 5-7 minutes until golden and soft.
Add garlic and ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in paprika and cumin; cook for 1 minute to release flavors.
Add lentils, water, salt, and cayenne pepper; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-35 minutes until lentils are tender but not mushy.
Stir occasionally and add more water if needed; serve hot with injera.
cheapTips: Buy brown lentils from bulk bins—30% cheaper than packaged.
Make a large pot and freeze portions for quick future meals.

recipes.name: Collard Greens Wot
recipes.description: Ethiopian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Wash collard greens thoroughly and remove thick stems, then chop into bite-sized pieces.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat and sauté diced onion until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in berbere spice and cook for 30 seconds to bloom the spices.
Add chopped collard greens and vegetable broth, stirring to combine.
Simmer covered for 12-15 minutes until greens are tender, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy collard greens in season (winter) for lowest prices
Make your own berbere spice blend to save 50% versus pre-mixed

recipes.name: Feijoada
recipes.description: Brazilian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook bacon in a large pot over medium-high heat until crispy, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, brown the cubed pork shoulder in batches, about 5-7 minutes per batch, then set aside.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in remaining oil and fat until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute to caramelize.
Return pork and bacon to the pot, add black beans, bay leaves, and vegetable broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 45-50 minutes until pork is tender.
Season generously with salt and pepper, then serve hot with white rice.
cheapTips: Use pork shoulder instead of premium cuts; it gets more tender with slow cooking
Buy canned beans in bulk at warehouse stores for 40% savings

recipes.name: Churrasco
recipes.description: Brazilian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine garlic, parsley, cilantro, olive oil, lime juice, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes in a bowl to make chimichurri marinade.
Pat meat dry and score the surface lightly with a knife to help marinade penetrate.
Coat beef generously with chimichurri marinade and let rest at room temperature for 20 minutes, or refrigerate up to 4 hours.
Preheat grill to high heat (or use a cast-iron skillet over high heat on stovetop).
Grill meat 4-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness is reached.
Transfer to a cutting board and rest for 5 minutes before slicing against the grain.
Drizzle with additional chimichurri sauce and serve with grilled vegetables or rice.
cheapTips: Buy flank steak on sale and freeze; it's naturally tender and affordable
Make chimichurri with dried herbs if fresh herbs are expensive

recipes.name: Pão de Queijo
recipes.description: Brazilian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F and grease a mini muffin tin or place parchment paper on a baking sheet.
Heat milk and oil in a saucepan until steaming, then remove from heat.
In a bowl, whisk together eggs, salt, and black pepper.
Add the hot milk mixture to eggs while whisking constantly to temper them.
Stir in cassava flour and Parmesan cheese until a sticky dough forms.
Spoon dough into prepared muffin cups about two-thirds full, or form 12-15 golf-ball-sized portions on baking sheet.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until puffed and golden brown, then serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy cassava flour at Latin American or Asian markets for half the price of specialty stores
Use store-brand Parmesan to reduce costs

recipes.name: Caldo Verde
recipes.description: Brazilian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion until translucent, about 4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add cubed potatoes and vegetable broth, bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Partially mash potatoes with a potato masher to thicken the broth slightly.
Stir in thinly sliced collard greens and cook for 5-7 minutes until tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then ladle into bowls and serve with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Use kale instead of collard greens if on sale
Buy potatoes in bulk at farmers markets for significant savings

recipes.name: Brigadeiro
recipes.description: Brazilian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine condensed milk, cocoa powder, and butter in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium heat.
Stir constantly for 8-10 minutes as the mixture thickens and darkens, scraping the sides and bottom.
Remove from heat when mixture pulls away from the side of the pan and a wooden spoon leaves a trail.
Let cool until safe to handle, about 5 minutes.
Pour chocolate sprinkles onto a shallow plate.
Using a small spoon or candy scoop, form small balls and roll in chocolate sprinkles.
Place each brigadeiro in a paper candy cup and serve at room temperature.
cheapTips: Make in bulk for parties; costs less per piece than store-bought
Use generic chocolate sprinkles to save 30%

recipes.name: Moqueca
recipes.description: Brazilian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large shallow pan or earthenware dish over medium heat.
Add sliced onion and sauté until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add sliced bell pepper, minced garlic, and diced tomato, cooking for 5 minutes.
Gently place fish fillets on top of the vegetable mixture.
Pour coconut milk over the fish and season with salt, pepper, and lime juice.
Cover and simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until fish is opaque and cooked through.
Sprinkle with fresh cilantro and serve directly from the pan with white rice or crusty bread.
cheapTips: Use frozen cod fillets instead of fresh snapper for 40% savings
Buy canned coconut milk at ethnic markets for 30% less than regular grocery stores

recipes.name: Pastéis de Nata
recipes.description: Brazilian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F and prepare a muffin tin by brushing with melted butter.
Mix condensed milk, egg yolks, butter, and vanilla extract in a bowl until smooth.
Cut puff pastry sheets into 3-inch squares and gently press each into a muffin cup, allowing edges to rise slightly.
Spoon about 1 tablespoon of filling into each pastry cup, leaving 0.5 inch at the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until pastry is golden and filling is set.
Combine cinnamon and sugar in a small bowl.
Remove from oven, sprinkle with cinnamon-sugar mixture while still warm, cool slightly, and serve.
cheapTips: Use store-brand puff pastry to save 30%
Make filling ahead and refrigerate to streamline day-of preparation

recipes.name: Acarajé
recipes.description: Brazilian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Drain soaked black-eyed peas and transfer to a food processor with onion, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Pulse until mixture is thick and somewhat coarse, resembling wet sand (do not over-blend).
Stir in shrimp paste if using.
Heat vegetable oil to 350°F in a deep pot or dutch oven.
Using a small ice cream scoop, carefully drop spoonfuls of batter into hot oil, frying 3-4 at a time.
Fry for 3-4 minutes, turning halfway, until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with hot sauce and lime on the side.
cheapTips: Buy dried black-eyed peas in bulk at ethnic markets for 50% savings versus packages
Omit shrimp paste to reduce costs without major flavor loss

recipes.name: Coxinha
recipes.description: Brazilian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Make dough by mixing mashed potato, butter, flour, and broth in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring constantly for 5 minutes until it pulls from the sides.
Transfer to a plate and let cool until handling temperature.
Mix shredded chicken with minced onion, salt, and pepper for filling.
Shape about 2 tablespoons of dough around 1 tablespoon of chicken filling, forming a teardrop shape.
Beat egg in a bowl, then dip each coxinha in egg and roll in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pot and fry coxinhas 3-4 at a time for 3-4 minutes until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with hot sauce or lime.
cheapTips: Use rotisserie chicken to save time and money on preparation
Make filling and fry-ahead; reheat in oven to save time when serving

recipes.name: Pudim de Leite Condensado
recipes.description: Brazilian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and place a roasting pan filled with hot water on the lowest rack.
In a saucepan, melt 3/4 cup sugar over medium heat, stirring constantly until it turns golden caramel, then quickly pour into a pudding mold or round baking dish, coating the bottom.
Blend condensed milk, evaporated milk, eggs, vanilla, and remaining 1/4 cup sugar in a blender until completely smooth.
Pour the mixture into the caramel-coated mold and place it in the water bath in the oven.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the pudding is set but slightly jiggles in the center when gently shaken.
Remove from oven and water bath, then cool completely at room temperature for 1 hour.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Run a thin knife around the edges and invert onto a serving plate so the caramel sauce drips over the top.
cheapTips: Buy condensed and evaporated milk on sale in bulk; they store well.
Use regular granulated sugar instead of specialty sugars.

recipes.name: Stroganoff de Carne
recipes.description: Brazilian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut the beef sirloin into thin strips and season with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches, about 3-4 minutes per side; set aside.
In the same pan, add remaining oil and sauté diced onions and minced garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms and cook for 4-5 minutes until they release their moisture and begin to brown.
Stir in tomato paste and paprika, cooking for 1 minute to combine.
Return the beef to the pan, pour in beef broth, and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in sour cream until fully combined, being careful not to boil.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper, then serve over rice or egg noodles.
cheapTips: Use less expensive sirloin tips or chuck cut into thin strips.
Buy mushrooms in bulk and freeze; sour cream often goes on sale.

recipes.name: Angu
recipes.description: Brazilian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat milk and salt in a large pot over medium heat until it begins to steam.
Slowly whisk in cornmeal in a thin stream, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Continue stirring and cooking the mixture for 10-12 minutes until it thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Stir in butter until fully melted and combined.
In a separate small skillet, heat oil and sauté diced white onion until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Pour the angu into a serving bowl, top with the sautéed onions and chopped green onions, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy cornmeal in bulk from ethnic markets.
Use inexpensive store-brand butter and milk.

recipes.name: Pamonha
recipes.description: Brazilian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blend corn kernels with milk in a blender until you reach a smooth puree consistency.
Pour the corn puree into a saucepan and add butter, sugar, and salt over medium heat.
Stir constantly for 10-12 minutes until the mixture becomes thick and creamy, then remove from heat and cool slightly.
Soak dried corn husks in warm water for 10 minutes until pliable.
Place 2-3 tbsp of the corn mixture in the center of each corn husk, fold the sides and ends to create a packet, and tie with kitchen twine or strips of corn husk.
Boil water in a large pot and carefully place the pamonha packets in the water.
Simmer for 20 minutes, then remove and let cool slightly before unwrapping and serving.
cheapTips: Buy corn in summer farmers markets when it's cheapest.
Dried corn husks are inexpensive and found in Latin markets.

recipes.name: Açaí na Tigela
recipes.description: Brazilian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Remove frozen acai puree from the freezer and let sit for 2-3 minutes to soften slightly.
Combine acai puree and almond milk in a blender and blend until thick and smooth like soft-serve ice cream.
Pour the acai mixture into two bowls.
Slice banana and arrange over the acai along with strawberries.
Top with granola, shredded coconut, sliced almonds, and drizzle with honey.
Serve immediately while the acai is still thick and cold.
cheapTips: Buy frozen acai packets in bulk from warehouse stores.
Use store-brand granola instead of premium brands.

recipes.name: Pirarucu de Casa
recipes.description: Brazilian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: If using salt cod, soak it in cold water for 24 hours, changing water several times, then drain and flake the fish.
Peel and dice green plantains, then boil in salted water for 10-12 minutes until just tender; drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a large pot and sauté diced onions and minced garlic for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to break down.
Gently add the flaked fish and cooked plantains to the pot, then fold together carefully without breaking the plantain pieces.
Simmer gently for 8-10 minutes, season with salt and pepper, and top with fresh cilantro.
Serve hot in a shallow bowl or plate with the broth.
cheapTips: Use frozen white fish fillets instead of expensive salt cod.
Buy plantains at Latin markets where they are cheaper.

recipes.name: Tacacá
recipes.description: Brazilian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a large pot with salt.
In a separate skillet, heat oil and sauté minced garlic with crushed hot peppers for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add shrimp to the skillet and cook for 3-4 minutes until pink, then remove from heat and set aside.
While boiling water maintains a gentle simmer, slowly whisk in cassava flour in batches, stirring constantly to form a smooth broth.
Simmer the broth for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it becomes thick and creamy.
Stir in the cooked shrimp, cilantro, and lime juice, then adjust seasoning.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot, traditionally sipped from a gourd cup (cuia) with a wooden spoon.
cheapTips: Use frozen shrimp instead of fresh for better pricing.
Buy cassava flour online or at Latin markets in bulk.

recipes.name: Bolo de Milho
recipes.description: Brazilian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9-inch round or square cake pan.
In a bowl, whisk together cornmeal, flour, baking powder, and salt.
In another bowl, cream butter and sugar together using an electric mixer until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Beat in eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition, then stir in vanilla.
Alternately add the dry ingredients and milk to the butter mixture, beginning and ending with dry ingredients, stirring just until combined.
Pour batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.
cheapTips: Buy cornmeal in bulk from ethnic or wholesale markets.
Use store-brand ingredients to minimize cost.

recipes.name: Frango com Quiabo
recipes.description: Brazilian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper, then heat 2 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken on all sides, about 4-5 minutes per side; remove and set aside.
Add remaining oil and sauté diced onions and minced garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and cumin, cooking for 1 minute to combine.
Return chicken to the pot and pour in chicken broth, bringing to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes until chicken is nearly cooked through.
Add okra cut into 1-inch pieces and stir to combine.
Simmer uncovered for 10-12 minutes until okra is tender and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning, then serve hot over rice.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs when on sale and freeze for later.
Use frozen okra to save money year-round.

recipes.name: Ceviche
recipes.description: Peruvian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut fresh white fish fillets into bite-sized cubes and place in a non-reactive bowl.
Squeeze fresh lime juice over the fish until mostly covered, then add salt and stir gently.
Refrigerate for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the fish becomes opaque and firm (the acid will 'cook' the fish).
While the fish marinates, thinly slice red onion, mince jalapeño, dice tomatoes, and chop cilantro.
Add the sliced onion, jalapeño, diced tomatoes, and cilantro to the ceviche and gently toss to combine.
Season with pepper and adjust salt to taste.
Divide among chilled serving bowls and top with sliced avocado.
Serve immediately with crunchy tortilla chips or crackers on the side.
cheapTips: Buy fish on sale and freeze; it works perfectly for ceviche.
Buy limes in bulk when in season for better pricing.

recipes.name: Picadinho à Mineira
recipes.description: Brazilian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the ground beef, breaking it apart with a spoon until no pink remains.
Add diced onion and garlic, stirring constantly for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, then add canned tomatoes with juice.
Mix in olives, raisins, cumin, salt, and pepper, stirring well.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally until flavors blend.
Taste and adjust seasonings, then serve hot over rice.
cheapTips: Use less expensive ground beef chuck instead of premium cuts
Buy olives and raisins from bulk bins to reduce cost

recipes.name: Escondidinho
recipes.description: Brazilian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil cassava cubes in salted water for 20 minutes until very tender, then drain and mash with butter and milk until smooth.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat, brown the ground beef, then add onion and garlic, cooking until softened.
Stir in canned tomatoes, salt, and pepper, then simmer for 8 minutes until slightly thickened.
Spread half the cassava puree in a greased 9x13 baking dish, layer the meat mixture evenly on top.
Cover with remaining cassava puree and spread evenly, then sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake at 375°F for 15 minutes until golden and heated through, then let rest 5 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Find cassava at Latin American markets cheaper than specialty stores
Use store-brand ground beef and cheddar cheese

recipes.name: Vatapá
recipes.description: Brazilian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat, sauté onion, garlic, and ginger for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add bread cubes and stir constantly for 2 minutes to lightly toast, then add shrimp and cook for 2 minutes per side.
Pour in coconut milk, broth, and canned tomatoes with juice, bringing to a simmer.
Let simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until shrimp are cooked through and flavors meld.
Use an immersion blender to partially blend the mixture until creamy but still textured, or mash with a potato masher.
Season with salt and red pepper to taste, then stir in cilantro and serve hot over white rice.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp when on sale and thaw before cooking
Use canned tomatoes instead of fresh for better value

recipes.name: Bobó de Camarão
recipes.description: Brazilian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil cassava cubes in salted water for 15 minutes until very tender, then drain and mash into a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a large pot, sauté onion, garlic, and ginger for 3 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Add the mashed cassava, coconut milk, and canned tomatoes with juice, stirring well to combine.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally until thickened.
Add shrimp and stir gently, cooking for 5 minutes until shrimp turn pink and are cooked through.
Season with salt and red pepper flakes, garnish with cilantro, and serve over white rice.
cheapTips: Buy shrimp on sale and freeze in portions
Purchase cassava at Latin markets for better pricing

recipes.name: Arroz com Feijão
recipes.description: Brazilian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot, sauté half the diced onion and 1 garlic clove for 2 minutes, then add beans with 1 cup water and bring to a simmer.
Cook beans for 10 minutes while occasionally mashing some against the pot sides to thicken the broth, then season with salt, pepper, and cumin.
In another large pot, heat 2 tbsp oil and sauté remaining onion and garlic for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add rice and stir constantly for 2 minutes to lightly toast the grains.
Pour 3 cups water into the rice pot, add bay leaf and salt, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and cook for 18 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let rest 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and combine with the beans, garnish with green onion, and serve.
cheapTips: Buy rice and beans in bulk for significant savings
Use canned beans for convenience without soaking dried beans

recipes.name: Rissoles
recipes.description: Brazilian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a large bowl, combine mashed potatoes, ground beef, onion, garlic, 1 egg, salt, pepper, and Parmesan cheese, mixing until well combined.
Divide mixture into 8 portions and shape each into an oval, placing half an olive in the center and sealing the meat around it.
Set up breading station with beaten egg in one shallow bowl and bread crumbs in another.
Dip each rissole in beaten egg, then roll in bread crumbs until fully coated, and place on a plate.
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350°F, then carefully add rissoles in batches without crowding.
Fry for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown, then transfer to a paper towel-lined plate to drain.
cheapTips: Make a double batch and freeze unbaked rissoles for quick future snacks
Buy ground beef on sale and portion into freezer bags

recipes.name: Tapioca
recipes.description: Brazilian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat butter in a non-stick skillet or tapioca maker over medium heat until melted and bubbling.
Spread 1/2 cup tapioca pearls evenly over the skillet surface and let cook for 1 minute without stirring.
Sprinkle 2 tbsp coconut and a pinch of salt over the tapioca, then drizzle 2 tbsp condensed milk and 2 tbsp water over the mixture.
Let cook undisturbed for 2-3 minutes until the bottom is set and slightly golden, then carefully flip and cook the other side for 1-2 minutes.
Transfer to a plate and repeat with remaining tapioca, coconut, condensed milk, and water.
Top finished tapiocas with banana slices, drizzle with honey, sprinkle cinnamon, and serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy tapioca pearls in bulk from Asian or Latin markets
Use overripe bananas from discount produce sections

recipes.name: Bife à Brasileira
recipes.description: Brazilian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Season both steaks generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over high heat until very hot, then sear the steaks for 2 minutes per side, then transfer to a plate.
In the same skillet, add 1 tbsp oil and sauté onion and garlic over medium heat for 5 minutes until softened and golden.
Pour in beef broth, tomato sauce, vinegar, and bay leaf, scraping up any browned bits from the pan.
Return steaks to the skillet and bring sauce to a simmer, cooking for 3-4 minutes per side until steaks reach desired doneness.
Remove steaks to serving plates, garnish the sauce with cilantro, and pour over the meat, then serve with rice and beans.
cheapTips: Buy less expensive cuts like chuck steak instead of premium cuts
Look for meat sales at the grocery store and freeze extras

recipes.name: Galinha à Passarinho
recipes.description: Brazilian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toss chicken pieces with lime juice, 2 minced garlic cloves, salt, and pepper, then let marinate for 15 minutes.
Place flour in a shallow bowl, dredge each chicken piece to coat lightly, then set aside on a plate.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, then fry chicken in batches for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through, transferring to a plate.
Add onion, bell pepper, remaining garlic, and bay leaves to the same skillet and sauté for 3 minutes until softened.
Pour in chicken broth and return chicken to the skillet, gently simmering for 5 minutes to blend flavors.
Taste and adjust seasonings, then serve hot over white rice or with fried potatoes on the side.
cheapTips: Buy chicken breasts in bulk when on sale and freeze
Use fresh limes from discount produce or buy bottled lime juice

recipes.name: Brás de Olho
recipes.description: Brazilian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a non-stick skillet over medium heat, melt butter and add cassava flour, stirring constantly for 2 minutes until lightly toasted and fragrant.
Add brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt, stirring well to combine, then toast for another minute.
Slice bananas into thin rounds and arrange 4-5 slices in the skillet, pressing gently into the cassava mixture.
Scatter raisins and olive halves (for 'eyes') around the banana slices, then cover with a thin layer of remaining cassava mixture.
Cook without stirring for 3-4 minutes until the bottom is golden and set, creating a crust.
Flip carefully using two spatulas and cook the other side for 2 minutes until lightly golden, then transfer to a serving plate.
cheapTips: Buy cassava flour from Latin markets instead of specialty stores
Use overripe bananas for better sweetness and lower cost

recipes.name: Lomo Saltado
recipes.description: Peruvian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat until very hot.
Season beef strips with salt and pepper, then sear in batches for 2-3 minutes until browned; set aside.
Add remaining oil to the same skillet and stir-fry onions for 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Add garlic and aji amarillo paste, cooking for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return beef to the skillet and add tomato wedges, soy sauce, and vinegar.
Toss everything together over high heat for 2-3 minutes until tomatoes soften slightly.
Fold in fresh cilantro and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately over fried potatoes or rice.
cheapTips: Buy beef sirloin on sale and freeze; use chuck steak as budget alternative
Make aji amarillo paste from yellow peppers blended with garlic if paste is unavailable

recipes.name: Aji de Gallina
recipes.description: Peruvian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil chicken in broth with half the onion until cooked through (20 minutes); shred and reserve broth.
Blend aji amarillo peppers with garlic, remaining onion, bread pieces, walnuts, and 1 cup broth until smooth.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pot and sauté the blended mixture for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add evaporated milk and shredded chicken to the sauce, stirring well.
Pour in remaining broth gradually until sauce reaches desired consistency; simmer 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Arrange boiled potatoes on a serving plate and pour aji de gallina over them.
Garnish with hard-boiled egg halves, black olives, and fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Use chicken breast instead of thighs to reduce cost
Substitute walnuts with cheaper peanuts if needed

recipes.name: Causa Limeña
recipes.description: Peruvian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 15 minutes; drain well.
Mash warm potatoes with aji amarillo paste, lime juice, and oil until creamy.
Season potato mixture with salt and pepper; divide evenly onto lettuce-lined serving plates.
Mix tuna or chicken with mayonnaise, red onion, cilantro, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Mound the tuna or chicken mixture on top of each potato base.
Arrange hard-boiled egg slices beside the causa.
Serve chilled or at room temperature with lime wedges on the side.
cheapTips: Use canned tuna in water to save money compared to fresh fish
Buy potatoes in bulk when on sale and store in cool, dark place

recipes.name: Papa a la Huancaína
recipes.description: Peruvian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil potatoes in salted water until completely tender, about 20 minutes; drain and peel while warm.
Blend aji amarillo paste, walnuts, onion, garlic, and lime juice until smooth.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté the blended mixture for 3 minutes over medium heat.
Gradually stir in evaporated milk until sauce reaches a pourable consistency; simmer 5 minutes.
Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Arrange warm whole potatoes on a serving platter.
Pour huancaína sauce generously over the potatoes.
Garnish with black olives and hard-boiled egg halves; serve at room temperature.
cheapTips: Substitute walnuts with peanut butter to reduce cost
Buy potatoes on sale and store in bulk

recipes.name: Ceviche de Atún
recipes.description: Peruvian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Place diced tuna in a glass or ceramic bowl; pour lime juice over it and stir gently.
Add sliced red onion, cilantro, and aji pepper; mix carefully to combine.
Season with salt and pepper; let sit at room temperature for 15 minutes (the acid will 'cook' the fish).
Add diced sweet potato, corn, and celery; toss gently.
Divide ceviche among serving bowls.
Top each bowl with avocado slices.
Serve immediately in chilled bowls with lime wedges and crackers on the side.
cheapTips: Buy frozen tuna and thaw completely; less expensive than fresh sushi-grade
Make during peak lime season when prices are lower

recipes.name: Tiradito
recipes.description: Peruvian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk aji amarillo paste with lime juice, olive oil, and minced garlic until smooth; season with salt and pepper.
Arrange thinly sliced fish on a chilled serving plate in a single layer.
Scatter red onion slices and jalapeno slices evenly over the fish.
Drizzle the aji amarillo-lime sauce generously over the entire dish.
Sprinkle with fresh cilantro leaves.
Serve immediately on cold plates with lime wedges and crispy tortilla chips.
cheapTips: Use less expensive white fish like flounder instead of premium options
Buy fish on sale and prepare same day

recipes.name: Anticuchos
recipes.description: Peruvian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine aji mirasol paste, vinegar, garlic, cumin, olive oil, salt, and pepper in a bowl to make marinade.
Add beef cubes to marinade and coat thoroughly; refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Thread marinated beef onto soaked wooden skewers, alternating with onion rings.
Heat a grill or grill pan to high heat.
Grill skewers for 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until meat is cooked through and slightly charred.
Baste with remaining marinade while grilling.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro and lime wedges.
Accompany with boiled potatoes and corn on the cob.
cheapTips: Use beef sirloin tip steak instead of heart; more accessible and similar price
Marinate in bulk and freeze extras for future use

recipes.name: Chupe de Camarones
recipes.description: Peruvian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté onion and garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Stir in aji amarillo paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add vegetable broth and bring to a boil; add diced potatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
Add shrimp and corn; cook 5 minutes until shrimp begins to turn pink.
Reduce heat to low and slowly stir in evaporated milk.
In a small bowl, beat eggs lightly; slowly drizzle into the soup while stirring to create egg ribbons.
Season with salt and pepper to taste; simmer gently for 2 more minutes.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with fresh cilantro; serve hot with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Use frozen shrimp instead of fresh; thaw and drain well before cooking
Buy corn frozen in bulk when on sale

recipes.name: Rocoto Relleno
recipes.description: Peruvian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut the top off each rocoto pepper and carefully scoop out seeds and membranes using a small spoon; set aside.
Heat oil in a skillet and sauté onion and garlic until soft; add ground beef and cook until browned, breaking up as it cooks.
Stir in raisins, olives, hard-boiled eggs, and cooked potatoes; season with salt and pepper and cook 5 minutes.
Stuff each rocoto pepper generously with the beef mixture; arrange in a baking dish.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Whisk evaporated milk with salt and pepper; pour around (not over) the rocotos in the baking dish.
Sprinkle shredded cheese over each stuffed pepper.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until peppers are tender and cheese is melted.
Serve hot with the creamy sauce spooned over the peppers.
cheapTips: Substitute rocoto with larger poblano peppers for easier sourcing and lower cost
Make filling ahead and refrigerate until ready to stuff and bake

recipes.name: Tamales Peruanos
recipes.description: Peruvian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried corn husks in warm water for 30 minutes to soften; drain and pat dry.
Beat butter or lard with an electric mixer until light and fluffy, about 5 minutes.
Gradually add masa harina, alternating with chicken broth, beating constantly to incorporate air.
Fold in baking powder and salt; mixture should be light and spreadable.
Spread about 2 tbsp masa on each corn husk, leaving edges clear.
Mix cooked chicken with diced aji pepper, olives, and onion for filling.
Place 1 tbsp filling in the center of each masa rectangle; add egg slice on top.
Fold corn husk sides over filling and fold bottom up; place seam-side down.
Stand tamales upright in a steamer basket with water below; steam for 45 minutes covered.
Serve hot with aji sauce or fresh salsa.
cheapTips: Buy masa harina in bulk from Latin markets at lower prices than grocery stores
Prepare filling a day ahead and refrigerate to save morning prep time

recipes.name: Sopa de Mondongo
recipes.description: Peruvian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean the tripe thoroughly under cold water and cut into 1-inch pieces.
Boil tripe in salted water for 45 minutes until tender, then drain.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion, garlic, and ají pepper until fragrant.
Add the cooked tripe to the pot and pour in chicken broth, then bring to a boil.
Cut potatoes into cubes and add to the broth, simmering for 15 minutes.
Season with cumin, vinegar, salt, and pepper to taste.
Simmer for 10 more minutes until potatoes are tender.
Serve hot topped with fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Buy tripe from butcher counter where it's often cheaper than pre-packaged
Use homemade or store-brand chicken broth instead of organic brands

recipes.name: Chupe de Papa
recipes.description: Peruvian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and cut potatoes into 1-inch cubes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion, garlic, and ají pepper until soft.
Add cubed potatoes and vegetable broth, bringing to a boil and then simmering for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Mash some potatoes in the broth to thicken the soup slightly.
Stir in heavy cream and cumin, then season with salt and pepper.
Crumble fresh cheese into the soup and stir gently.
Gently crack eggs into the simmering soup one at a time and poach for 3-4 minutes until whites set.
Serve hot with one egg per bowl.
cheapTips: Use regular potatoes instead of specialty varieties
Buy store-brand cream and substitute with evaporated milk if budget is tight

recipes.name: Picadillo
recipes.description: Peruvian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet and sauté diced onion, garlic, and ají pepper until fragrant.
Add ground beef and cook over medium-high heat, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then add cumin.
Dice potatoes into small cubes and add to the skillet with beef broth.
Simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are nearly tender.
Add peas and simmer for 5 more minutes until potatoes are fully cooked.
Season generously with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve garnished with fresh cilantro over rice.
cheapTips: Buy ground beef in bulk when on sale and freeze portions
Use frozen peas instead of fresh to save money year-round

recipes.name: Escabeche de Pescado
recipes.description: Peruvian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat fish fillets dry and season with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and pan-fry fish until golden on both sides, about 4 minutes per side, then set aside.
In the same skillet, heat remaining oil and sauté sliced onions, garlic, and diced ají peppers until soft.
Deglaze the skillet with white wine vinegar and scrape up any brown bits.
Add fish broth, bay leaves, and cumin, bringing to a simmer.
Return fish fillets to the skillet and gently simmer for 5 minutes.
Add green olives and simmer 2 more minutes to blend flavors.
Transfer to a serving dish and let cool to room temperature before serving, or serve warm.
cheapTips: Use frozen white fish fillets which are often cheaper than fresh
Buy canned olives in bulk sections instead of jars

recipes.name: Caldo de Gallina
recipes.description: Peruvian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut chicken into 4 pieces, removing excess skin, and place in a large pot with 8 cups water.
Bring to a boil, then skim off any foam that rises to the surface.
Add quartered onion, smashed garlic cloves, and halved ají pepper to the pot.
Simmer for 40 minutes, then add cubed carrots, potatoes, and celery pieces.
Continue simmering for 20 minutes until vegetables are tender and chicken is fully cooked.
Remove chicken pieces and shred the meat, discarding bones and skin.
Return shredded chicken to the broth and season with cumin, salt, and pepper.
Serve hot in bowls garnished with fresh cilantro and accompanied by lime wedges.
cheapTips: Buy whole chickens instead of breasts or thighs for better value
Use regular potatoes and carrots from bulk bins

recipes.name: Raya al Ajillo
recipes.description: Peruvian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat ray fillets dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook fillets 4-5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through, then transfer to a plate.
Add remaining olive oil to the skillet and add minced garlic, sautéing for 2 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden.
Stir in vinegar, diced ají pepper, and cook for 1 minute.
Return fish to the skillet and gently toss to coat with the garlic mixture.
Squeeze lemon juice over the fish and sprinkle with chopped parsley and cilantro.
Cook for 1 more minute to warm through.
Serve immediately with the garlic oil drizzled over white rice or boiled potatoes.
cheapTips: Buy ray or skate from the fish counter when on sale
Use regular garlic instead of pre-minced to save 30%

recipes.name: Sudado de Pescado
recipes.description: Peruvian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté sliced onions, minced garlic, and diced ají peppers until soft.
Add diced tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they begin to break down.
Pour in white wine and fish broth, bringing to a simmer.
Add cumin and season with salt and pepper.
Gently place fish fillets into the simmering broth, making sure they are mostly submerged.
Cover and simmer for 12-15 minutes until fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve in shallow bowls with the broth spooned over the fish, garnished with fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Use frozen fish fillets which are often cheaper and just as good quality
Make your own fish broth by simmering fish scraps with water and aromatics

recipes.name: Pollo a la Brasa
recipes.description: Peruvian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Butterfly the chicken by cutting along both sides of the backbone and flattening it, then cut into 4 pieces.
Blend garlic cloves, ají peppers, lime juice, olive oil, cumin, vinegar, salt, pepper, and paprika into a smooth paste.
Coat all chicken pieces thoroughly with the marinade and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat oven to 425°F or prepare an outdoor grill.
If using oven, place chicken on a roasting pan and roast for 50-60 minutes until golden and cooked through, basting every 15 minutes.
If using grill, cook over medium-high heat for 30-40 minutes, turning frequently and basting with remaining marinade.
The chicken is ready when the internal temperature reaches 165°F at the thickest part.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving with aji verde on the side.
cheapTips: Buy whole chickens when they're on sale and freeze until needed
Make marinade with store-brand items and fresh citrus from discount grocers

recipes.name: Quispiño
recipes.description: Peruvian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 15 minutes, then peel and mash thoroughly.
Blend ají pepper and garlic into a smooth paste.
Mix mashed potatoes with ají-garlic paste, crumbled fresh cheese, milk, egg, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Heat vegetable oil to 350°F in a deep pan or fryer.
Using two spoons or an ice cream scoop, carefully form small oval patties and slide them into hot oil.
Fry for 3-4 minutes until golden brown on all sides, turning once halfway through.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve hot, optionally with ají verde or huancaína sauce for dipping.
cheapTips: Use regular potatoes from bulk bins and yellow onion instead of ají if budget is tight
Make a double batch and freeze uncooked patties for quick snacks later

recipes.name: Saltado de Camarones
recipes.description: Peruvian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat shrimp dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until smoking, then add shrimp and stir-fry for 2 minutes until they start to turn pink, then remove to a plate.
Add remaining 2 tbsp oil to the skillet and stir-fry sliced onions, garlic, and diced ají pepper for 3 minutes.
Add diced red bell pepper and tomatoes, stir-frying for 3 more minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Return shrimp to the skillet and toss everything together.
Add soy sauce and white wine vinegar, tossing constantly for 2 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Serve immediately over white rice, garnished with fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp in bulk which is cheaper than fresh and thaws quickly
Use store-brand soy sauce and white onions if yellow are unavailable

recipes.name: Ocopa Arequipeña
recipes.description: Peruvian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil potatoes until tender, peel, and slice into rounds.
Hard boil eggs, peel, and halve them.
Blend peanut butter, cilantro, garlic, jalapeños, and oil until smooth.
Arrange potato slices on a plate and top with egg halves.
Pour the cilantro-peanut sauce over potatoes and eggs.
Garnish with crumbled queso fresco and black olives.
cheapTips: Buy store-brand peanut butter in bulk.
Use russet potatoes which are cheaper than specialty varieties.

recipes.name: Adobo Arequipeño
recipes.description: Peruvian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried chilies in hot water for 15 minutes, then blend with garlic, cumin, vinegar, and tomato paste.
Heat oil in a large pot and brown pork cubes on all sides.
Add diced onion and cook until softened.
Pour the chili paste mixture over the pork and stir well.
Add cubed potatoes and enough water to cover by 1 inch.
Simmer covered for 60 minutes until pork is tender and potatoes are cooked.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder on sale and freeze for later use.
Dried chilies are cheaper than fresh and store long-term.

recipes.name: Chanfainita
recipes.description: Peruvian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook diced potatoes until golden and set aside.
Brown beef heart cubes in the same skillet, then remove.
Sauté onion and garlic until fragrant, then add aji amarillo paste and cumin.
Return beef heart to pan with liver slices and cook until liver is no longer pink.
Add potatoes back to the pan and stir everything together.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with cilantro, and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Organ meats are significantly cheaper than regular cuts.
Buy potatoes in bulk when on sale.

recipes.name: Caldo Negro
recipes.description: Peruvian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté diced onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add beef broth and bring to a boil.
Add diced potatoes and cook until they soften.
Whisk beef blood to prevent clotting and slowly add to the simmering broth while stirring.
Add cumin and oregano, and simmer for 20 minutes without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot garnished with fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Buy beef blood from specialty meat markets or butchers at discount.
Use homemade or budget-friendly store broth.

recipes.name: Patasca
recipes.description: Peruvian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil tripe pieces in water with onion and garlic for 90 minutes until very tender.
Drain and cut tripe into smaller pieces.
Heat beef broth in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Add tripe, diced potatoes, and corn to the broth.
Mix aji amarillo paste with some broth and add to the pot.
Add cumin and oregano, simmer for 30 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve steaming hot.
cheapTips: Tripe is an inexpensive organ meat; buy from butcher shops.
Buy corn in season or frozen for best prices.

recipes.name: Leche de Tigre
recipes.description: Peruvian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix lime juice, garlic, cilantro, and aji amarillo paste in a bowl.
Add diced fish and red onion slices.
Season with salt and cumin.
Add jalapeños and celery and stir gently.
Let sit in the refrigerator for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Serve cold as a shot or appetizer.
cheapTips: Buy white fish on sale and use frozen for convenience.
Limes are cheaper in bulk or when in season.

recipes.name: Ackee and Saltfish
recipes.description: Jamaican breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak saltfish in water overnight, then boil and flake the meat, discarding bones.
Heat oil in a skillet and sauté onion, garlic, and thyme until fragrant.
Add bell pepper and tomato, cooking until softened.
Add flaked saltfish to the pan and cook for 5 minutes.
Gently fold in ackee without breaking up the delicate fruit.
Add scallions and black pepper, cook 2 more minutes.
Serve hot with boiled dumplings or fried plantains.
cheapTips: Buy saltfish in bulk sections at Caribbean markets.
Use canned ackee instead of fresh, which is rare in US grocery stores.

recipes.name: Jamaican Patty
recipes.description: Jamaican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Make pastry by mixing flour, turmeric, and salt, then cut in cold butter until crumbly.
Add cold water gradually until dough forms, wrap and refrigerate 20 minutes.
Brown ground beef in a skillet with onion, garlic, and scotch bonnet.
Add beef broth and simmer until liquid reduces, then cool the filling.
Roll out pastry thin and cut into 4-inch circles.
Fill each circle with beef mixture, fold in half, and crimp edges with a fork.
Bake at 375°F for 25-30 minutes until golden brown.
cheapTips: Make several batches and freeze unbaked patties for quick meals.
Buy ground beef on sale and freeze in portions.

recipes.name: Oxtail Stew
recipes.description: Jamaican dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and brown oxtail pieces on all sides.
Remove oxtail and sauté onion and garlic until fragrant.
Return oxtail to pot with beef broth, thyme, and allspice.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 60 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrots, simmer another 40 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot in deep bowls with the rich gravy.
cheapTips: Buy oxtail from butcher shops or Caribbean markets where it is cheaper.
Make a large batch and freeze portions for later.

recipes.name: Curry Goat
recipes.description: Jamaican dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and brown goat meat on all sides, set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic until fragrant, then stir in curry powder.
Return goat meat to pot and cook for 3 minutes to coat.
Add coconut milk, thyme, and whole scotch bonnet pepper.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 50 minutes until meat is tender.
Add potatoes and cook uncovered for 25 minutes until potatoes are done.
Remove scotch bonnet, season with salt and pepper, and serve with rice.
cheapTips: Buy goat meat from Caribbean or halal butcher shops for best prices.
Use canned coconut milk on sale and buy in bulk.

recipes.name: Pepper Shrimp
recipes.description: Jamaican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add minced garlic, ginger, and whole scotch bonnet pepper, stirring until fragrant about 1 minute.
Add shrimp and cook for 2 minutes per side until they begin to turn pink.
Season with salt, black pepper, and fresh thyme leaves.
Pour in lime juice and cook for 2 more minutes until shrimp are fully pink and cooked through.
Remove scotch bonnet pepper and stir in green onions just before serving.
Serve hot over rice or with hard dough bread.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp when fresh is expensive; thaw before cooking.
Substitute lime with lemon juice or vinegar for savings.

recipes.name: Jerk Chicken
recipes.description: Jamaican dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blend scotch bonnet peppers, garlic, ginger, thyme, green onions, allspice, soy sauce, lime juice, and olive oil in a food processor until smooth.
Rub jerk marinade all over chicken pieces, coating thoroughly.
Place chicken in a large container or zip-top bag and refrigerate for 4-8 hours or overnight.
Preheat grill or oven to 400°F.
If grilling, place chicken on medium-high heat for 25-30 minutes, turning every 5-7 minutes.
If baking, place on a lined sheet pan and bake for 40-45 minutes until internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving with rice and peas or festival bread.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs instead of breasts; they're cheaper and more flavorful.
Make jerk paste in bulk and freeze in portions.

recipes.name: Jerk Pork
recipes.description: Jamaican dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine scotch bonnet peppers, garlic, ginger, thyme, green onions, allspice, soy sauce, lime juice, and oil in a blender.
Coat pork cubes with the jerk marinade and refrigerate for 3-6 hours.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet or grill to medium-high heat.
Sear marinated pork for 2-3 minutes per side until golden.
Transfer to a covered roasting pan and bake at 350°F for 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until pork is tender.
Remove lid and bake for an additional 15 minutes to caramelize the exterior.
Serve with rice and peas and fried plantains.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder on sale and marinate longer for deeper flavor.
Use dried thyme if fresh is unavailable.

recipes.name: Rice and Peas
recipes.description: Jamaican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat and sauté garlic and green onions for 1 minute.
Add rice and stir constantly for 2 minutes until lightly toasted.
Pour in coconut milk and broth, stirring to combine.
Add red kidney beans and thyme, and season with salt, black pepper, and cayenne.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover tightly.
Simmer for 20 minutes without lifting the lid until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff rice with a fork and remove thyme sprigs before serving.
cheapTips: Buy canned beans in bulk and store dried beans for even cheaper options.
Use regular milk mixed with a little oil if coconut milk is too expensive.

recipes.name: Run Down
recipes.description: Jamaican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Melt butter in a large pot and sauté onion and garlic for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add potatoes and green bananas, cooking for 5 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and add thyme and whole scotch bonnet pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Gently flake sardines or mackerel and add to the pot, stirring carefully to avoid breaking fish apart.
Simmer for another 5 minutes to heat through.
Remove scotch bonnet pepper and serve hot as a stew or soup.
cheapTips: Canned fish is already affordable; buy store brands for savings.
Use regular potatoes if green bananas aren't available.

recipes.name: Mannish Water
recipes.description: Jamaican dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil water in a large pot and add meat with salt, cooking for 20 minutes to remove impurities; drain and rinse meat.
Return meat to the pot with fresh water and bring to a boil.
Add onion, garlic, thyme, allspice berries, and whole scotch bonnet pepper.
Simmer for 40-50 minutes until meat is tender.
Add potatoes, carrots, and green bananas to the pot.
Continue simmering for 20-25 minutes until all vegetables are fully cooked.
Season to taste with salt and black pepper, remove scotch bonnet pepper and thyme sprigs, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy goat meat from specialty stores or butchers; often cheaper than lamb.
Substitute with beef chuck if goat is unavailable.

recipes.name: Cod Fritters
recipes.description: Jamaican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak salted cod overnight to remove salt, then boil for 15 minutes; drain, cool, and shred finely.
Combine flour and baking powder in a large bowl.
Mix in shredded cod, onion, garlic, thyme leaves, and minced scotch bonnet pepper.
Gradually add water while stirring to form a thick, sticky batter.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350°F.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into hot oil and fry for 2-3 minutes until golden brown; flip and fry another 1-2 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with hot sauce or lemon wedges.
cheapTips: Buy salted cod at Caribbean or ethnic markets for better prices.
Reuse frying oil carefully for multiple batches.

recipes.name: Fried Dumplings
recipes.description: Jamaican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine flour, baking powder, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl.
Cut in butter or shortening until mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Gradually add water while stirring until a soft dough forms.
Knead dough lightly for 2-3 minutes on a floured surface.
Divide dough into small balls and flatten each into a 1/4-inch thick oval.
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350°F.
Fry dumplings 2-3 at a time for 1-2 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot, optionally tossed with a mix of salt and sugar.
cheapTips: Make a large batch and freeze unbaked dumplings for quick future snacks.
Use any neutral oil for frying; reuse carefully.

recipes.name: Boil and Fry
recipes.description: Jamaican breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Fill a large pot with water, add salt, and bring to a boil.
Add green bananas and potatoes; boil for 15-20 minutes until fork-tender.
Drain vegetables thoroughly and pat dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350°F.
Working in batches, fry boiled vegetables for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Transfer fried vegetables to a plate lined with paper towels.
In a small saucepan, melt butter and sauté onion and garlic for 2 minutes.
Toss fried vegetables with the butter mixture, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy potatoes and bananas in bulk from farmers' markets.
Reuse frying oil for multiple batches.

recipes.name: Roast Breadfruit and Ackee
recipes.description: Jamaican breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel breadfruit, remove the core, and cut into large chunks.
Roast breadfruit pieces at 400°F on a lined baking sheet for 25-30 minutes until golden and tender, stirring halfway through.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté onion and garlic for 2 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes, thyme, and whole scotch bonnet pepper; simmer for 5 minutes.
Gently fold in canned ackee, being careful not to break it apart.
Add roasted breadfruit chunks to the skillet and toss gently.
Season with salt and black pepper, remove scotch bonnet pepper and thyme sprigs, and serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy canned ackee online if not available locally; cheaper than fresh.
Substitute breadfruit with plantains in a pinch.

recipes.name: Mackerel Run Down
recipes.description: Jamaican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Drain and rinse the canned mackerel, removing any large bones and skin.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion, minced garlic, and chopped tomato until softened.
Add the prepared mackerel, coconut milk, thyme, and whole scotch bonnet pepper to the pot.
Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mixture thickens and flavors blend.
Remove the scotch bonnet pepper, season with salt and black pepper to taste, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use canned mackerel instead of fresh for lower cost and longer shelf life
Buy coconut milk in bulk at Caribbean or Asian markets for better prices

recipes.name: Stew Peas
recipes.description: Jamaican dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak kidney beans overnight, then drain and rinse thoroughly.
Heat oil in a large pot and brown the beef chunks on all sides, about 5 minutes per side.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the pot and cook until softened.
Pour in water, add beans and thyme, then bring to a boil and reduce heat to simmer.
Cover and cook for 45 minutes until beans are tender.
Add diced carrots and potatoes, then simmer uncovered for 20 more minutes.
Stir in coconut milk, season with salt and pepper, and cook for 5 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Buy dried beans in bulk instead of canned to save significantly
Use tougher beef cuts like chuck roast which become tender with long cooking

recipes.name: Saltfish Fritters
recipes.description: Jamaican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak saltfish in cold water for 12-24 hours, changing water several times to remove excess salt.
Boil the soaked saltfish for 15 minutes, drain, and flake the flesh, discarding skin and bones.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Combine flaked fish, finely minced onion, minced garlic, and thyme in another bowl.
Mix wet and dry ingredients together, adding water gradually until you reach a thick batter.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pan or Dutch oven.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil and fry until golden brown on both sides, about 3-4 minutes total.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with hot sauce or lime.
