While cake bakes, mix condensed milk, evaporated milk, and regular milk together.
Pierce cooled cake all over with a fork, then slowly pour milk mixture over the entire surface until absorbed.
Beat heavy cream with vanilla and remaining sugar until stiff peaks form, then spread or pipe over cooled cake.
Top with fresh strawberries and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.
cheapTips: Use frozen strawberries instead of fresh for lower cost
Skip the strawberry garnish and just use whipped cream

recipes.name: Éclair
recipes.description: French snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F and line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Bring water and butter to a boil, remove from heat, and stir in flour until a ball forms.
Cool slightly, then beat in eggs one at a time until dough is smooth and glossy.
Transfer to piping bag with large round tip and pipe 4-inch long strips onto prepared baking sheets.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until puffed and golden, then cool on wire racks.
Make pastry cream by heating milk, then whisking yolks with sugar and cornstarch before slowly adding hot milk.
Return cream to heat and cook until thick, stirring constantly, then cool completely.
Slice cooled eclairs horizontally and fill with pastry cream, then top with melted chocolate mixed with cream.
cheapTips: Use store-brand chocolate chips instead of premium brands
Make chocolate glaze with cocoa powder instead of chocolate chips

recipes.name: Baumkuchen
recipes.description: German snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a bundt cake pan thoroughly with butter.
Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy, then beat in eggs one at a time.
Mix flour, cornstarch, and baking powder together, then fold into egg mixture with vanilla extract.
Transfer batter to piping bag and pipe concentric circles into the bottom of the bundt pan, starting from center.
Continue piping layers on top of each other to fill the pan completely.
Bake for 45-55 minutes until a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 15 minutes, then invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Mix melted chocolate chips with powdered sugar and water to make glaze, then pour over cooled cake.
cheapTips: Use store-brand chocolate chips
Simplify by omitting the chocolate glaze and dusting with powdered sugar

recipes.name: Sacher Torte
recipes.description: Austrian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9-inch round cake pan.
Sift cocoa powder with flour and salt in a medium bowl.
Cream together butter and sugar until light and fluffy, then beat in egg yolks one at a time with vanilla extract.
Fold the flour-cocoa mixture into the butter mixture gently.
In a separate bowl, whip egg whites until stiff peaks form, then fold into batter in two additions.
Pour batter into prepared pan and bake for 40-45 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cake completely, then split into two layers and spread apricot jam between them.
Melt chocolate with cream over low heat, pour over entire cake, and let set for 30 minutes.
cheapTips: Use store-brand chocolate and cocoa powder
Buy eggs in bulk during sales

recipes.name: Basbousa
recipes.description: Middle Eastern snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix shredded coconut, condensed milk, whole milk, and 1/2 cup sugar in a bowl until well combined.
Press mixture firmly into a greased 9x13 baking pan and smooth the top.
Cut into diamond or square shapes and place one clove in the center of each piece.
Bake at 350°F for 25-30 minutes until golden brown.
While basbousa bakes, combine 1 cup sugar, 1 cup water, and lemon juice in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Simmer syrup for 10 minutes, then remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Pour warm syrup over hot basbousa as soon as it comes out of the oven.
Allow to cool completely and absorb the syrup before serving.
cheapTips: Buy coconut in bulk at warehouse stores
Make syrup with basic pantry sugar and water

recipes.name: Stroopwafel
recipes.description: Dutch snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cream together 3/4 cup butter and 1/2 cup brown sugar until light, then beat in eggs and vanilla.
Mix flour and baking powder, then fold into wet ingredients until dough forms.
Preheat a stroopwafel iron or waffle iron to medium-high heat and lightly grease it.
Press small portions of dough into the iron and cook until golden brown on both sides.
While warm, immediately sandwich the wafers with filling made from 1/4 cup melted butter, 1/2 cup dark brown sugar, cinnamon, and honey.
Place filled wafel between the two halves and press gently, then set on a rack to cool and harden.
Repeat with remaining dough and filling until all wafels are made.
Store in an airtight container for up to 5 days.
cheapTips: Use a regular waffle iron if you don't have a stroopwafel iron
Buy honey at discount stores in bulk

recipes.name: Medovik
recipes.description: Russian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat honey, 1/2 cup butter, and sugar in a saucepan until combined, then cool slightly and beat in eggs.
Sift flour with baking soda and salt, then fold into honey mixture to form a stiff dough.
Divide dough into 8-10 equal portions and roll each thin between parchment paper.
Bake each layer on a baking sheet at 375°F for 5-7 minutes until light golden, then cool on racks.
Make frosting by beating 1 cup butter with condensed milk and powdered sugar until fluffy.
Layer cooled honey cakes with frosting between each layer, stacking them like a cake.
Frost the top and sides of the assembled cake with remaining frosting.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours to allow layers to soften and flavors to meld before serving.
cheapTips: Buy honey at warehouse clubs in large quantities
Use store-brand condensed milk instead of name brands

recipes.name: Panna Cotta
recipes.description: Italian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Sprinkle gelatin over 3 tablespoons cold water and let sit for 5 minutes to bloom.
Heat cream, milk, and sugar in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves, then remove from heat.
Stir in bloomed gelatin and vanilla extract until gelatin completely dissolves.
Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl.
Pour into serving glasses or ramekins, filling about 3/4 full.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours or until set and firm.
Top each serving with fresh berries drizzled with honey just before serving.
cheapTips: Buy heavy cream on sale and freeze for later use
Use frozen berries instead of fresh to save money

recipes.name: Donut
recipes.description: American breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk together flour, 1/4 cup sugar, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, beat egg and mix with milk.
Fold wet ingredients into dry ingredients until just combined; do not overmix.
Transfer dough to a piping bag or donut dispensing bottle and pipe into a deep fryer or Dutch oven filled with oil heated to 350°F.
Fry donuts for 1-1.5 minutes per side until golden brown, then remove with a slotted spoon.
Mix cinnamon with 1 cup granulated sugar in a shallow bowl.
Toss warm donuts in cinnamon-sugar mixture to coat.
Cool on a wire rack before serving.
cheapTips: Reuse frying oil multiple times by straining it carefully
Buy flour and sugar in bulk bags

recipes.name: Bacio di Dama
recipes.description: Italian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cream together butter and powdered sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in egg and vanilla extract until well combined.
Fold in flour and ground hazelnuts until dough comes together.
Refrigerate dough for 30 minutes, then roll into small marble-sized balls.
Place balls on parchment-lined baking sheets spaced 1 inch apart.
Bake at 350°F for 10-12 minutes until golden, then cool completely on racks.
Melt dark chocolate with coconut oil over low heat.
Sandwich two cooled cookies together with a spoonful of melted chocolate in the center and let set.
cheapTips: Buy hazelnuts already ground to save processing time and cost
Use cocoa powder mixed with shortening instead of chocolate for filling

recipes.name: Mango Sticky Rice
recipes.description: Thai dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse sticky rice thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear, then drain well.
Combine rice and 1.5 cups water in a rice cooker or pot and cook according to package directions until tender.
While rice cooks, heat coconut milk with sugar and salt in a saucepan over medium heat until sugar dissolves; do not boil.
Transfer cooked rice to a bowl and pour 3/4 of the coconut mixture over it, stirring gently until absorbed.
Peel and pit mangoes, then slice into thin pieces.
Transfer sticky rice to serving plates and arrange mango slices alongside.
Drizzle remaining coconut sauce over rice and mango.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve immediately while rice is still warm.
cheapTips: Buy mangoes when in season and on sale, then freeze for later use
Sticky rice in bulk is less expensive than pre-packaged

recipes.name: Puttu
recipes.description: Kerala breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix rice flour, grated coconut, jaggery, and salt in a bowl.
Add water gradually and mix until the batter reaches a crumbly, wet sand consistency.
Grease a puttu kudam (cylindrical steamer) or use a tall can and fill it with alternating layers of batter and sliced banana.
Steam the filled kudam in boiling water for 8-10 minutes until cooked through.
Push the puttu out onto a plate using a stick or rod.
Serve hot with banana or chickpea curry.
cheapTips: Use fresh grated coconut instead of packaged for better flavor and lower cost
Jaggery is cheaper than white sugar in Indian grocery stores

recipes.name: Idiyappam
recipes.description: Kerala breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix rice flour, all-purpose flour, salt, and coconut oil in a bowl.
Add water slowly while mixing to form a smooth, thick batter.
Heat the idiyappam press (or rice noodle maker) by pouring boiling water through it.
Fill the press with batter and press directly onto a greased steamer plate in circular coils.
Steam for 8-10 minutes until cooked through and set.
Gently remove with a spatula and serve hot with sambar or curry.
cheapTips: Make your own rice flour by grinding rice at home or using a blender
Sesame seeds can be omitted to reduce cost

recipes.name: Avial
recipes.description: Kerala lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat coconut oil in a pot and add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies; sauté for 30 seconds.
Add carrots, green beans, potato, and banana pepper to the pot.
Stir-fry for 5 minutes until vegetables start to soften.
Pour coconut milk and add salt and curry leaves.
Cook on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until all vegetables are tender but not mushy.
Serve hot as a side dish with rice or flatbread.
cheapTips: Use seasonal vegetables to reduce cost and improve freshness
Coconut milk can be replaced with water and a spoon of coconut oil if needed

recipes.name: Sambar
recipes.description: Kerala lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pressure cook toor dal with 2 cups water for 5 minutes until soft; drain and set aside.
Heat coconut oil in a pot and add mustard seeds; when they pop, add curry leaves.
Add carrots, okra, and drumstick pieces; sauté for 3 minutes.
Pour remaining 2 cups water, add tamarind paste, sambar powder, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then add cooked dal and simmer for 10-12 minutes.
Taste and adjust salt and spice; serve hot with rice or idli.
cheapTips: Buy sambar powder in bulk from Indian markets to save money
Use regular vegetables like tomato and onion if drumstick is unavailable

recipes.name: Rasam
recipes.description: Kerala lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat coconut oil in a pot and add cumin seeds and black peppercorns; toast for 30 seconds.
Add curry leaves, green chilies, and minced ginger; sauté for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Pour water and add tamarind paste and salt; bring to a boil.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes until the flavors blend well.
Strain through a fine sieve or serve as is; taste and adjust spices.
cheapTips: Make tamarind paste at home by soaking dried tamarind in water
Buy tomatoes in season when they are cheapest

recipes.name: Olan
recipes.description: Kerala lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil cowpeas in water with salt until tender, about 12-15 minutes; drain and set aside.
Heat coconut oil in a pot and add cumin seeds; when they sizzle, add green chilies, ginger, and curry leaves.
Add cubed pumpkin and sauté for 2 minutes.
Pour coconut milk and add the cooked cowpeas and salt.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 8-10 minutes until pumpkin is tender.
Serve hot as a mild, creamy side dish with rice.
cheapTips: Use canned cowpeas to save on cooking time and cost
Buy pumpkin in fall when it is cheapest and freeze pieces for later use

recipes.name: Erissery
recipes.description: Kerala lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil cowpeas in salted water until tender, about 12-15 minutes; drain.
Grind grated coconut, cumin seeds, green chilies, and ginger into a coarse paste with minimal water.
Heat coconut oil in a pot and add curry leaves.
Add pumpkin cubes and sauté for 3 minutes.
Add boiled cowpeas and the ground coconut paste; mix well.
Cook on medium heat for 8-10 minutes until pumpkin is tender and flavors meld; serve hot with rice.
cheapTips: Grind the paste by hand with a mortar and pestle to save on blender wear
Buy whole coconuts and grate fresh when on sale

recipes.name: Pulissery
recipes.description: Kerala lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Grind grated coconut, green chilies, ginger, and cumin seeds with 1/4 cup water into a fine paste.
Heat coconut oil in a pot and add curry leaves.
Add pumpkin pieces and turmeric powder; sauté for 2 minutes.
Pour 1 cup water, add salt, and bring to a boil.
Add the ground coconut paste and stir well; simmer for 10-12 minutes until pumpkin is tender.
Adjust spices to taste and serve hot as a creamy side dish with rice.
cheapTips: Use a blender to quickly grind the coconut paste, or do it by hand for authenticity
Pumpkin can be replaced with mango or butternut squash when available and cheap

recipes.name: Kalan
recipes.description: Kerala lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Grind grated coconut, green chilies, ginger, and 1/4 cup water into a smooth paste.
Heat coconut oil in a pot and add curry leaves.
Add raw banana, eggplant, and yam pieces; sauté for 3 minutes.
Pour coconut milk and add salt.
Bring to a boil, then add the ground coconut paste and stir well.
Simmer for 15-18 minutes until all vegetables are very tender; serve hot with rice.
cheapTips: Buy raw bananas and yam at Indian or Asian markets for better prices than regular supermarkets
Make coconut milk at home by blending grated coconut with hot water and straining

recipes.name: Thoran
recipes.description: Kerala lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat coconut oil in a large pan and add cumin seeds; let them sizzle for 20 seconds.
Add curry leaves, green chilies, and ginger; sauté for 1 minute.
Add shredded cabbage and salt; stir-fry on high heat for 5-6 minutes until cabbage is just tender.
Add grated coconut and mix well; cook for 2 more minutes.
Taste and adjust salt; serve hot as a side dish with rice and curry.
cheapTips: Cabbage is one of the cheapest vegetables year-round at any grocery store
This dish works with any shredded vegetable like carrots, beets, or cucumber

recipes.name: Oyster Vermicelli
recipes.description: Taiwanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried oysters in warm water for 15 minutes until softened, then drain and chop.
Mince garlic and slice green onions, keeping white and green parts separate.
Heat vegetable oil in a pot over medium heat and stir-fry minced garlic until fragrant.
Add chopped oysters and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Add vermicelli noodles and cook for 3-4 minutes until tender.
Stir in soy sauce, sesame oil, and white pepper.
Garnish with white parts of green onions and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy dried oysters in bulk from Asian markets
Use regular soy sauce instead of premium brands

recipes.name: Popiah
recipes.description: Taiwanese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Stir-fry garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add mushrooms and cook for 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Add jicama and carrots, stir-fry for 3 minutes until tender-crisp.
Season with soy sauce and remove from heat, let cool slightly.
Place a lettuce leaf on each popiah wrapper.
Add 2-3 tablespoons of filling down the center of each wrapper.
Drizzle with peanut sauce and sprinkle with green onions.
Roll wrapper tightly, tucking in sides, and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy jicama in season at farmers markets
Make peanut sauce from peanut butter to save money

recipes.name: Braised Beef Noodles
recipes.description: Taiwanese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and brown beef chunks on all sides, about 8 minutes total, then remove.
Add garlic and ginger to the pot and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to pot and add soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and beef broth.
Add star anise and rock sugar, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until beef is very tender.
Cook noodles separately according to package directions and drain.
Divide noodles into bowls and ladle braised beef and sauce over top.
Garnish with scallions and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy chuck roast on sale and freeze
Use regular soy sauce if dark soy sauce unavailable

recipes.name: Tainan Danzai Noodles
recipes.description: Taiwanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook noodles according to package directions, drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a pot and fry shallot and garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add pork belly and cook for 2 minutes until edges are crispy.
Add shrimp and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until pink.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Add cooked noodles and soy sauce, simmer for 2 minutes.
Drizzle sesame oil and season with white pepper.
Top with green onions and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp instead of fresh
Use chicken thighs instead of pork belly for savings

recipes.name: Har Gow
recipes.description: Cantonese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Chop shrimp finely and mix with salt, white pepper, sesame oil, bamboo shoots, and water chestnuts.
Mix tapioca starch, wheat starch, and vegetable oil in a bowl.
Pour boiling water into the starch mixture and stir quickly until a dough forms.
Knead dough for 2 minutes until smooth, cover with damp cloth.
Divide dough into 10 pieces and roll each into a thin circle.
Place 1 tablespoon filling on each circle, fold in half and pleat edges to seal.
Line steamer basket with parchment paper and arrange dumplings.
Steam over boiling water for 6-8 minutes until translucent and cooked through.
Serve hot with soy sauce for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp in bulk
Mix wheat and tapioca starch instead of buying specialty dumpling flour

recipes.name: Siu Mai
recipes.description: Cantonese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix ground pork, shrimp, water chestnuts, mushrooms, green onions, and garlic in a bowl.
Add soy sauce, sesame oil, and cornstarch to filling and mix well.
Place 1 wrapper on your palm and add 1 tablespoon filling in the center.
Gather edges around filling and press down slightly so filling shows at the top.
Line steamer basket with parchment paper and arrange siu mai.
Steam over boiling water for 8-10 minutes until filling is cooked through.
Serve hot with soy sauce and chili oil for dipping.
cheapTips: Use all pork if shrimp is expensive
Buy wonton wrappers as substitute for siu mai wrappers

recipes.name: Char Siu Bao
recipes.description: Cantonese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and oil in a bowl.
Add warm milk gradually and knead into a soft dough, let rest 20 minutes.
Mix char siu, hoisin sauce, sesame oil, and onion in a separate bowl.
Divide dough into 6 pieces and roll each into a thin circle.
Place 1 tablespoon filling in center of each circle.
Gather edges around filling and pinch to seal, then roll gently into a ball.
Place bao seam-side down on parchment squares and let rise 15 minutes.
Steam over boiling water for 12-15 minutes until fluffy.
Serve warm.
cheapTips: Use store-bought char siu pork
Make filling day ahead to save time

recipes.name: Cheung Fun
recipes.description: Cantonese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix rice flour, tapioca starch, salt, and 1 tablespoon oil in a bowl.
Gradually add water while stirring until batter is smooth and pourable.
Oil a 10-inch round plate or steamer tray generously.
Pour 1/4 cup batter onto oiled plate and spread evenly.
Steam for 1-2 minutes until set but still slightly wet on top.
Remove from steamer and slide onto a cutting board.
Place char siu and green onions on one edge and roll up tightly.
Repeat with remaining batter.
Mix soy sauce and sesame oil, pour over cheung fun and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Make filling from cheap ground pork if char siu unavailable
Buy rice flour at Asian markets for better price

recipes.name: Lo Mai Gai
recipes.description: Cantonese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse glutinous rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Heat oil in a pot and stir-fry garlic for 30 seconds.
Add diced chicken and cook for 3 minutes until mostly cooked.
Add mushrooms and cook for 2 minutes.
Add rice and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add chicken broth, soy sauce, and salt, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until rice is tender.
Drizzle with sesame oil, garnish with green onions, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs in bulk on sale
Use regular rice if glutinous rice unavailable but soak longer

recipes.name: Jian Dui
recipes.description: Cantonese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix glutinous rice flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Add warm water gradually and knead until smooth dough forms.
Divide dough into 6 pieces and form into balls.
Flatten each ball and add 1 tablespoon red bean paste in center.
Fold edges over filling and seal, forming a ball.
Roll each ball in sesame seeds until coated.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pot or wok.
Carefully lower jian dui into oil and fry for 3-4 minutes until golden brown, turning occasionally.
Remove with slotted spoon and drain on paper towels, serve warm.
cheapTips: Make red bean paste from scratch if budget-conscious
Reuse frying oil for multiple batches

recipes.name: Coconut Rice
recipes.description: South Indian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse basmati rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Heat ghee in a pot and fry cashews and curry leaves until golden, then remove and set aside.
Add rice to the same pot and toast for 1 minute.
Pour in coconut milk, water, and salt, then stir once.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes.
Turn off heat and let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork and fold in shredded coconut, fried cashews, and curry leaves.
cheapTips: Buy unsweetened shredded coconut in bulk or use frozen coconut.
Use regular white rice if basmati is too expensive.

recipes.name: Tamarind Rice
recipes.description: South Indian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix tamarind paste with 0.5 cup warm water and set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan and add mustard seeds; when they sputter, add curry leaves and peanuts.
Fry until peanuts are golden, then add turmeric and chili powder.
Add cooked rice and mix well, breaking up any clumps.
Pour tamarind water over the rice and stir thoroughly for 2-3 minutes.
Add salt to taste and mix until rice is evenly coated with tamarind.
cheapTips: Use tamarind pulp from whole pods instead of paste for better value.
Buy peanuts raw and roast them at home.

recipes.name: Lemon Rice
recipes.description: South Indian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pan and add mustard seeds; when they sputter, add urad dal and fry until golden.
Add curry leaves, green chili, and turmeric, then cook for 30 seconds.
Add cooked rice and mix well, breaking up clumps.
Squeeze juice from both lemons and add to the rice, stirring constantly for 2 minutes.
Add salt to taste and mix thoroughly until rice is evenly coated.
Fold in fried cashews and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy lemons in bulk when in season and freeze the juice.
Skip cashews if budget is tight; the rice tastes great without them.

recipes.name: Curd Rice
recipes.description: South Indian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat ghee in a pan and add mustard seeds; when they sputter, add urad dal and fry until golden.
Add curry leaves, green chili, and ginger, then cook for 30 seconds.
Add cooked rice to the pan and mix well.
In a bowl, whisk yogurt with salt until smooth.
Pour yogurt over the rice and fold gently until fully combined, cooking for 1 minute.
Serve immediately while warm.
cheapTips: Use store-brand plain yogurt instead of Greek yogurt.
Make this with leftover cooked rice for minimal prep.

recipes.name: Bisi Bele Bath
recipes.description: South Indian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse rice and toor dal together under cold water.
Heat oil in a pot and add mustard seeds and cumin seeds; when they sputter, add curry leaves.
Add mixed vegetables and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add rice, dal, turmeric, and salt, then stir for 1 minute.
Pour in water and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes until rice and dal are fully cooked.
Add bisi bele bath powder and mix well, cooking for 2 more minutes.
Serve hot with ghee drizzled on top.
cheapTips: Make your own bisi bele bath powder by grinding roasted spices and dal.
Use frozen mixed vegetables to save money and prep time.

recipes.name: Hyderabadi Biryani
recipes.description: South Indian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice onions thinly and deep fry in oil until golden and crispy; drain and reserve half for garnish.
Marinate chicken in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, half the fried onions, chili, cilantro, mint, biryani masala, and salt for 30 minutes.
Soak saffron in warm milk.
Boil water with whole spices and salt, then add basmati rice and cook until 70% done; drain well.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, layer half the marinated chicken, then half the rice, then remaining chicken, then remaining rice.
Sprinkle saffron milk, reserved fried onions, and remaining cilantro and mint on top.
Cover the pot tightly with foil, then place the lid on top and cook on high heat for 2 minutes until steam forms.
Reduce heat to low and cook for 25-30 minutes without opening the lid.
Turn off heat and let rest for 5 minutes, then gently mix with a fork.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs instead of breast for more flavor at lower cost.
Skip saffron and use turmeric mixed with a little milk for color.

recipes.name: Masala Dosa
recipes.description: South Indian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak rice and urad dal separately for 4 hours, then drain and grind together with water until smooth batter forms (2-3 hours of fermentation time needed).
Boil and mash potatoes with turmeric and salt, then mix in sautéed onions, mustard seeds, curry leaves, and chana dal.
Heat oil on a non-stick griddle or dosa pan over medium-high heat.
Pour batter onto the griddle and spread thin with the back of a spoon using circular motions.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until the bottom is golden and crispy, about 2 minutes.
Add a spoonful of potato filling in the center and fold the dosa in half.
Cook for another 30 seconds and transfer to a plate.
Serve hot with sambar and coconut chutney.
cheapTips: Buy urad dal and rice in bulk from Indian grocery stores.
Make batter in advance and refrigerate for up to 3 days.

recipes.name: Gunpowder
recipes.description: South Indian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a pan and add peanuts, then roast on medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add chana dal and roast together for 2 more minutes until golden.
Add dry red chilies, cumin seeds, and sesame seeds, then roast for 1 minute.
Let cool completely, then grind to a coarse powder using a food processor or blender.
Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.
cheapTips: Buy raw peanuts in bulk from wholesale stores.
Use it as a dip with rice or crackers instead of buying pre-made seasoning packets.

recipes.name: Murukku
recipes.description: South Indian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix rice flour, urad dal flour, cumin seeds, carom seeds, chili powder, turmeric, and salt in a bowl.
Add 0.5 cup oil and mix with your fingers until breadcrumb texture forms.
Gradually add water and knead into a stiff dough.
Fill a murukku press with dough and pipe spirals directly into hot oil (350°F).
Fry until golden and crispy, about 2-3 minutes per side, then remove with a slotted spoon.
Drain on paper towels and cool completely.
cheapTips: Buy rice flour and urad dal flour from Indian grocery stores in bulk.
Make in batches and store in airtight containers for up to 1 week.

recipes.name: Chakli
recipes.description: South Indian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix rice flour, urad dal flour, cumin seeds, carom seeds, chili powder, turmeric, salt, and sesame seeds in a bowl.
Add 2 tablespoons oil and mix with your fingers.
Gradually add water while mixing until a smooth, thick batter forms (consistency should be like thick dough).
Heat oil in a deep pan to 325°F.
Transfer batter to a chakli maker (spiral mold) and carefully pipe into hot oil in circular motions.
Fry for 30 seconds on each side until golden and crispy, then remove with a slotted spoon.
Drain on paper towels and cool completely to crisp up further.
cheapTips: Buy a chakli maker from Indian stores for under $5 and reuse for years.
Double the recipe and freeze cooked chaklis for up to 1 month.

recipes.name: Fish Ball Soup
recipes.description: Taiwanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried mushrooms in hot water for 20 minutes, then slice.
Bring chicken broth to a boil in a large pot with ginger slices.
Add sliced mushrooms and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add frozen fish balls and simmer for 8 minutes until they float.
Add bok choy and cook for 3 minutes until tender-crisp.
Season with soy sauce, salt, and white pepper to taste.
Drizzle with sesame oil and top with chopped scallions before serving.
cheapTips: Buy frozen fish balls in bulk at Asian markets for 30% less
Use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth to reduce cost

recipes.name: Taro Ball
recipes.description: Taiwanese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and dice taro root into 1/2-inch cubes.
Mix tapioca starch, flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Pour boiling water into dry mixture and stir until shaggy dough forms.
Knead dough until smooth and divide into small balls about 3/4 inch diameter.
Bring 3 cups water, brown sugar, and ginger to boil in a pot.
Drop taro balls into boiling syrup and simmer for 15 minutes until they float and turn translucent.
Serve warm in bowls with syrup and ginger slices.
cheapTips: Buy taro root at Asian markets for half the price of regular supermarkets
Make larger batches and freeze uncooked balls for later use

recipes.name: Shaved Ice with Red Beans
recipes.description: Taiwanese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine brown sugar and water in a saucepan and bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Add canned red beans (with liquid) to the syrup and simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Mix evaporated milk with vanilla extract and salt.
Place shaved ice in a serving bowl.
Pour cooled red bean syrup over the shaved ice.
Drizzle evaporated milk mixture on top and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Make your own shaved ice using a blender and ice cubes instead of buying pre-shaved
Buy canned beans in bulk at discount grocers

recipes.name: Minced Pork Noodles
recipes.description: Taiwanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook egg noodles according to package directions, drain and set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large pan over medium-high heat.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes, cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add ground pork and cook for 5 minutes, breaking into small pieces, until browned.
Stir in soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, and sesame oil.
Toss cooked noodles with the pork mixture until well coated.
Top with chopped scallions and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy ground pork on sale and freeze for future batches
Use regular vinegar mixed with a pinch of sugar if black vinegar is unavailable

recipes.name: Tea Eggs
recipes.description: Taiwanese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil eggs for 8 minutes in a pot of water.
Remove eggs and let cool, then gently crack shells all over without peeling.
Brew tea bags in 4 cups boiling water for 5 minutes, then remove bags.
Add soy sauce, star anise, cinnamon, ginger, and salt to the tea.
Return cracked eggs to the pot and simmer for at least 8 hours or overnight.
Remove eggs from liquid and gently peel to reveal the marbled pattern.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Use store-brand black tea bags instead of premium varieties
Make a large batch and refrigerate for up to 5 days

recipes.name: Stewed Pork Rib Soup
recipes.description: Taiwanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blanch pork ribs in boiling water for 3 minutes, drain and rinse under cold water.
Soak dried mushrooms in hot water for 20 minutes, then slice.
Bring 8 cups water to a boil in a large pot and add blanched ribs and ginger slices.
Add red dates, mushrooms, and ginseng if using, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer covered for 90 minutes until ribs are tender.
Add goji berries in the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Season with salt to taste and garnish with chopped scallions.
cheapTips: Buy pork ribs when on sale at ethnic markets, cheaper than premium supermarkets
Skip ginseng to reduce cost; soup is still delicious without it

recipes.name: Chicken Cutlet
recipes.description: Taiwanese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound chicken breasts to 1/4-inch thickness between plastic wrap.
Set up three shallow bowls with flour, beaten egg, and panko mixed with salt and pepper.
Coat each chicken piece first in flour, shaking off excess, then dip in egg, then coat in panko.
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (or until a piece of bread browns in 30 seconds).
Fry chicken pieces for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Transfer to paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve hot with lemon wedges on the side.
cheapTips: Buy chicken breast on sale and freeze individual pieces
Reuse frying oil by straining it through cheesecloth

recipes.name: Shrimp Rolls
recipes.description: Taiwanese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Chop shrimp into small pieces and mix with bamboo shoots, scallions, garlic, sesame oil, soy sauce, and cornstarch.
Place about 1 tbsp filling on the lower third of each spring roll wrapper.
Fold bottom corner over filling, then fold in side corners, and roll tightly to the top.
Wet the top edge with a little water to seal.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep skillet or wok.
Fry shrimp rolls for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with sweet chili sauce.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp and thaw in advance rather than fresh shrimp
Make rolls ahead and freeze; fry directly from freezer without thawing

recipes.name: Pig's Blood Cake
recipes.description: Taiwanese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry pig's blood cake slices for 2 minutes per side until lightly crispy on the outside.
Remove blood cake and set aside on a plate.
In the same skillet, fry sticky rice for 2 minutes until warm and lightly golden.
Return blood cake to the skillet with the rice.
Mix soy sauce, black vinegar, sesame oil, garlic, and red pepper flakes in a small bowl.
Pour sauce over blood cake and rice, toss gently to combine, and top with scallions before serving.
cheapTips: Buy pig's blood cake at Asian markets where it's less expensive than specialty stores
Cook sticky rice in bulk and refrigerate for quick breakfast assembly

recipes.name: Xiao Long Bao
recipes.description: Taiwanese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pour boiling water into flour while mixing with a spoon to form shaggy dough, then knead smooth and let rest 20 minutes covered.
Bloom gelatin in cold chicken broth for 5 minutes, then heat to dissolve.
Mix cooled gelatin mixture with ground pork, soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, scallions, and sugar.
Divide dough into 12 equal pieces and roll each into a 3-inch circle on a floured surface.
Place about 1 tbsp filling in center of each wrapper and gather edges to form a pouch, twisting the top to seal.
Place pleated side up in a bamboo steamer lined with parchment paper.
Steam over boiling water for 8-10 minutes until skin is translucent and filling is cooked through.
Serve hot with black vinegar and chili oil for dipping.
cheapTips: Make dough and filling ahead; assemble and freeze uncooked for quick steaming later
Use an instant pot or regular pot with a steamer basket if bamboo steamer unavailable

recipes.name: Egg Tart
recipes.description: Cantonese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, 6 tablespoons cold butter cubed, and salt until breadcrumb texture forms.
Add 1 egg yolk and 3 tablespoons water, mix until dough comes together.
Chill dough for 20 minutes, then press into muffin tins.
Preheat oven to 400°F and bake shells for 8 minutes until lightly golden.
Whisk together 3 eggs, sweetened condensed milk, evaporated milk, sugar, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Pour custard filling into pre-baked tart shells until three-quarters full.
Bake at 350°F for 15-18 minutes until custard is set but slightly jiggly in center.
Cool completely before removing from pan and serving.
cheapTips: Make pastry shells from scratch instead of buying pre-made
Use evaporated milk instead of heavy cream to reduce costs

recipes.name: Roast Duck
recipes.description: Cantonese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat duck dry inside and out with paper towels.
Mix soy sauce, honey, five-spice, ginger, garlic, vinegar, and salt to create marinade.
Rub marinade all over duck, inside cavity and under skin, and let sit 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°F and place duck on roasting pan with 0.5 cup water.
Roast for 20 minutes at 400°F, then reduce heat to 350°F and roast 50-60 minutes until skin is mahogany brown.
Baste duck with pan juices every 15 minutes during cooking.
Let rest 10 minutes before carving and serving with pan sauce.
cheapTips: Buy whole duck rather than parts to save money
Save duck fat for cooking vegetables and other dishes later

recipes.name: Roast Goose
recipes.description: Cantonese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat goose dry completely and prick skin all over with fork to release fat.
Combine soy sauce, honey, five-spice, star anise, ginger, garlic, and salt.
Rub marinade generously inside cavity and under skin, let rest 30 minutes.
Place goose on roasting rack with 1 cup water in pan and preheat oven to 425°F.
Roast at 425°F for 30 minutes, then reduce to 325°F and roast 2-2.5 hours until internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Baste with pan juices and rendered fat every 20 minutes.
Let rest 15 minutes before carving and serve with pan gravy.
cheapTips: Purchase goose from Asian markets where prices are typically lower
Goose fat renders out during cooking—save it for cooking and flavor

recipes.name: Roast Pork
recipes.description: Cantonese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Score pork skin in crosshatch pattern, cutting through skin but not meat.
Rub salt and pepper all over scored skin and let sit 30 minutes.
Mix soy sauce, honey, five-spice, ginger, garlic, and vinegar into marinade.
Rub marinade all over pork belly, especially under skin.
Place skin-side up on roasting pan with 0.5 cup water and roast at 400°F for 50-60 minutes until skin is crackling and meat reaches 160°F.
If skin isn't crispy, increase oven temperature to 450°F for final 5 minutes.
Let rest 10 minutes, then slice and serve with pan sauce.
cheapTips: Pork belly is cheaper than premium cuts and develops amazing crackling skin
Save rendered pork fat for cooking and flavor enhancement

recipes.name: Whole Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallions
recipes.description: Cantonese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Fill steamer pot with water and bring to boil, adjusting rack so fish doesn't touch water.
Clean fish thoroughly, pat dry, and score skin on both sides with diagonal cuts.
Place fish on heatproof plate, season inside cavity and outside with salt and white pepper.
Stuff cavity with half the ginger and half the scallions.
Place plate in steamer, cover, and steam 12-15 minutes until fish is cooked through and flakes easily.
While fish steams, whisk soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and water together.
Heat vegetable oil in small pan until smoking, then pour over remaining ginger and scallions on fish.
Pour sauce around fish, garnish with cilantro, and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy whole fish from Asian markets where prices are lower than supermarkets
Use affordable white fish like tilapia or snapper instead of expensive varieties

recipes.name: Oyster Sauce Beef
recipes.description: Cantonese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice beef thinly against the grain and set aside.
Mix oyster sauce, soy sauce, water, and cornstarch in a bowl.
Heat oil in wok or large skillet over high heat until smoking.
Add beef in batches and stir-fry 2-3 minutes until browned, then remove and set aside.
Add garlic and ginger to wok, stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return beef to wok and pour in sauce mixture.
Toss beef and sauce together 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens and coats beef.
Stir in sesame oil and scallions, toss once more, and serve over rice.
cheapTips: Use flank steak or chuck instead of expensive sirloin cuts
Buy oyster sauce in bulk from Asian markets for significant savings

recipes.name: Salt and Pepper Squid
recipes.description: Cantonese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.

ingredients.note: 1.25 lbs cleaned and cut into rings

steps: Pat squid dry thoroughly with paper towels.
Mix flour, cornstarch, salt, and white pepper in a shallow bowl.
Toss squid pieces in flour mixture until evenly coated.
Heat oil in wok or deep pan to 350°F.
Fry squid in batches 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy, stirring occasionally.
Remove squid to paper towels to drain.
Pour off most oil, leaving 2 tablespoons in wok.
Stir-fry garlic, scallions, and chilies for 30 seconds, then toss with fried squid.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges and extra salt for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy squid from Asian or seafood markets for better prices than supermarkets
Pre-cleaned squid costs more—buy whole and clean yourself to save money

recipes.name: Lobster Cantonese Style
recipes.description: Cantonese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Chop lobster into chunks with shell on, removing sand sac from head.
Rinse fermented black beans and mash lightly with fork.
Heat oil in wok over high heat and stir-fry lobster pieces 3-4 minutes until shell begins to redden.
Push lobster to side, add garlic, ginger, and black beans, stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in soy sauce, oyster sauce, and stock, tossing to coat lobster.
Cover and cook 8-10 minutes until lobster is cooked through and tender.
Stir cornstarch slurry and pour into wok, stirring constantly until sauce thickens.
Garnish with scallions and serve immediately over steamed rice.
cheapTips: Buy lobster when prices drop in fall/winter rather than summer
Ask fishmonger for pre-cut or cracked lobster at discount prices

recipes.name: Shrimp with Lobster Sauce
recipes.description: Cantonese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat shrimp dry and season lightly with salt.
Heat 1.5 tablespoons oil in wok over high heat and stir-fry shrimp 2-3 minutes until pink, then remove.
Add remaining oil, garlic, and ginger, stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in lobster sauce, soy sauce, and chicken stock, stirring to combine.
Bring to simmer and add cornstarch mixed with water, stirring until sauce thickens.
Return shrimp to wok and toss to coat with sauce.
Slowly pour beaten egg into sauce while stirring to create egg ribbons.
Garnish with scallions and serve immediately over steamed rice.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp instead of fresh for significant savings
Use canned or jarred lobster sauce from Asian markets for convenience

recipes.name: Wonton Noodle Soup
recipes.description: Cantonese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix ground pork, shrimp, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 teaspoon sesame oil, green onions, and ginger to make filling.
Place 1 teaspoon filling in center of each wonton wrapper, wet edges with water, fold triangle, then bring corners together.
Bring chicken stock to boil in large pot.
Add egg noodles and cook according to package directions until just tender.
In separate boiling water, cook wontons until they float, then continue 2-3 minutes until they float higher.
Transfer cooked wontons to the stock pot with noodles.
Add bok choy to pot and simmer 2 minutes until tender.
Season with remaining 1 tablespoon soy sauce and 0.5 teaspoon sesame oil, garnish with cilantro, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy wonton wrappers in bulk from Asian markets—much cheaper than supermarkets
Use homemade or boxed stock instead of fresh for major savings

recipes.name: Malabar Biryani
recipes.description: Kerala lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak basmati rice in water for 30 minutes, then drain.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot and fry sliced onions until golden brown, reserving half for garnish.
Mix chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, salt, and half the fried onions, then marinate for 15 minutes.
Boil water in a large pot with whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaves) and salt.
Add drained rice to boiling water and cook until 70% done, then drain.
Layer marinated chicken in the heavy pot, then layer partially cooked rice on top.
Cover the pot with foil and lid, and cook on high heat for 2 minutes until steam forms, then reduce to low heat for 45 minutes.
Turn off heat and let rest for 5 minutes without opening the lid, then gently fluff with a fork and serve with reserved fried onions.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs instead of breasts for lower cost
Use regular long-grain rice if basmati is unavailable

recipes.name: Fish Curry
recipes.description: Kerala lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat coconut oil in a large pan and sauté onions until translucent.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in red chili powder, turmeric, and chopped tomatoes, cooking for 3 minutes until tomatoes soften.
Pour in water and coconut milk, then bring the mixture to a simmer.
Gently add fish fillets to the curry and cook for 8-10 minutes until fish is cooked through.
Season with salt and add curry leaves, then simmer for 2 more minutes.
Transfer to a serving dish and serve hot with rice or flatbread.
cheapTips: Use canned fish or frozen fillets for better prices
Substitute coconut milk with evaporated milk for savings

recipes.name: Prawn Curry
recipes.description: Kerala lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat coconut oil in a large pan and sauté chopped onions until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Mix in red chili powder, turmeric, and coriander powder, cooking for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes and cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Pour in water and coconut milk, bringing to a simmer.
Add shrimp and cook for 5-7 minutes until pink and cooked through.
Season with salt and stir in curry leaves, then simmer for 2 minutes.
Serve hot with steamed rice or paratha.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp in bulk during sales
Use half coconut milk and half heavy cream to reduce cost

recipes.name: Chemmeen Roast
recipes.description: Kerala dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat coconut oil in a large wok or heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Add sliced onions and fry until they turn light golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and julienned ginger, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in red chili powder and turmeric powder, cooking for 30 seconds.
Add shrimp and green chilies, then fry over high heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring frequently.
Reduce heat to medium and continue cooking for another 4-5 minutes until shrimp are fully cooked and starting to caramelize at edges.
Add curry leaves and salt, tossing everything together for 1 minute.
Serve hot as a side dish or with rice.
cheapTips: Use frozen shrimp which is often cheaper than fresh
Reduce oil slightly and add extra onions for bulk

recipes.name: Meen Pollichathu
recipes.description: Kerala dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean fish and make 2-3 diagonal slits on both sides, then season with salt and turmeric powder.
Soak banana leaves briefly in water to soften, then wipe dry.
Layer sliced onions, tomatoes, ginger, and green chilies on each banana leaf.
Place seasoned fish on top of the vegetable layer.
Drizzle coconut oil over fish and sprinkle red chili powder, curry leaves, and remaining salt.
Fold banana leaf to create a secure parcel, tucking edges tightly.
Place parcels on a hot griddle or pan over medium heat and cook for 15-18 minutes per side until fish is cooked through.
Carefully open parcel at the table, being cautious of escaping steam, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use any whole fish available; cheaper varieties work equally well
Substitute banana leaves with parchment paper for easier handling

recipes.name: Chicken Stew
recipes.description: Kerala dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat coconut oil in a large pot and sauté onions until softened.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring well.
Add chicken pieces and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally until partially cooked.
Add potatoes, carrots, turmeric powder, and green chilies, cooking for 2 minutes.
Pour in water and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in coconut milk and simmer for 5 more minutes until chicken is fully cooked and flavors blend.
Season with salt and add curry leaves, then simmer for 1 minute.
Serve hot with rice or bread.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs or drumsticks instead of breast for better flavor and lower cost
Buy frozen vegetables instead of fresh to save significantly

recipes.name: Beef Fry
recipes.description: Kerala dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat coconut oil in a large pan and fry sliced onions until deep golden brown, then remove and set aside.
In the same oil, cook beef cubes over high heat for 3-4 minutes until browned on all sides.
Add minced garlic and ginger, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in red chili powder, turmeric, and coriander powder, coating all beef pieces evenly.
Pour in water, reduce heat to low, and simmer covered for 35-40 minutes until beef is tender.
Once beef is cooked, increase heat to high and add reserved fried onions and curry leaves.
Stir continuously for 3-5 minutes until the mixture dries and beef gets a caramelized coating.
Season with salt to taste and serve hot with rice or flatbread.
cheapTips: Buy beef chuck or bottom round, which are tougher but become tender with longer cooking
Purchase onions in bulk when on sale for this dish

recipes.name: Luchi
recipes.description: Kerala snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, salt, sugar, and turmeric powder in a bowl.
Add 3 tbsp oil to the dry ingredients and rub with fingertips until mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Gradually add water and knead into a smooth, soft dough, then cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide dough into 10-12 equal balls and roll each into a thin circle about 5-6 inches diameter.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan until it reaches 350°F (a piece of dough should sizzle and float immediately).
Carefully slide rolled dough into hot oil and fry for about 20 seconds per side until puffed and light golden.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve hot.
Serve with curry, dal, or enjoy plain with jaggery.
cheapTips: Make large batches and freeze uncooked luchi for up to 1 month
Reuse frying oil for 3-4 batches to save cost

recipes.name: Achappam
recipes.description: Kerala snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix all-purpose flour and rice flour together in a bowl.
Add coconut milk, mashed banana, jaggery, cardamom, and salt, then whisk until smooth batter forms.
Add 3 tbsp ghee to batter and mix well until fully incorporated.
Let batter rest for 10 minutes to allow flour to fully hydrate.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 325°F (medium heat, as achappam browns easily).
Dip achappam mold (rose-shaped waffle iron) into hot oil, then dip into batter coating the mold.
Carefully slide the coated mold back into oil, twisting gently to release the achappam, and fry until golden brown on both sides (about 2 minutes total).
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and cool slightly before serving.
cheapTips: Buy jaggery in bulk from Indian grocery stores for significant savings
An achappam mold is essential and costs $8-12; share cost with friends

recipes.name: Medu Vada
recipes.description: South Indian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak urad dal in water for 4 hours, then drain completely.
Grind soaked urad dal with water into a smooth, fluffy batter using a food processor or wet grinder (batter should be thick, not runny).
Transfer batter to a bowl and let rest for 10 minutes to allow it to fluff slightly.
Add minced onion, green chilies, ginger, curry leaves, salt, and black pepper to batter and mix gently.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pan.
Wet your hand lightly with water and hold a small portion of batter, then shape into a donut by pushing thumb through center and widening gently.
Carefully slide shaped vada into hot oil and fry 4-5 at a time until golden brown on all sides (about 2-3 minutes).
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and serve hot with sambar or coconut chutney.
cheapTips: Buy urad dal from Indian grocery stores in bulk for best prices
Prepare batter in large batches and refrigerate for up to 2 days

recipes.name: Black Bean Clams
recipes.description: Cantonese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak clams in salt water for 30 minutes, then rinse thoroughly under cold running water.
Rinse fermented black beans, then mash them with minced garlic and ginger.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until very hot.
Add the black bean mixture and stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add clams, soy sauce, rice wine, and water to the wok.
Cover and cook for 5-7 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally, until clams open.
Discard any clams that don't open, then drizzle with sesame oil and garnish with sliced green onions.
Serve immediately in a bowl with the cooking liquid.
cheapTips: Buy clams on sale and freeze for later
Fermented black beans last months in pantry, so buy bulk

recipes.name: Chongqing Chicken
recipes.description: Sichuan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut chicken thighs into bite-sized chunks and toss with cornstarch and salt.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry chicken until golden, then set aside.
In the same wok, toast dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns for 1 minute until fragrant, then crush slightly.
Add minced garlic and ginger to the wok and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Return chicken to the wok and add soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar.
Toss everything together over high heat for 3-4 minutes until well coated and heated through.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more soy sauce or salt as needed.
Transfer to a serving plate and garnish with the toasted chilies and peppercorns.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs instead of breasts—cheaper and more flavorful
Dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns can be found in Asian markets for less

recipes.name: Sichuan Hot Pot
recipes.description: Sichuan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons sesame oil in a large pot over medium heat and toast dried chilies, Sichuan peppercorns, star anise, and ginger for 2 minutes.
Pour beef broth into the pot and add minced garlic, then bring to a simmer.
Arrange thinly sliced beef, bok choy, cubed tofu, and rice noodles on separate plates.
Transfer the hot broth to a hot pot or keep simmering in the pot at the table.
Have guests use chopsticks or small strainers to cook ingredients in the broth for 10-30 seconds.
Mix soy sauce with remaining sesame oil in small bowls as a dipping sauce.
Continue cooking and eating in courses, adding more ingredients to the broth as desired.
Serve until all ingredients are cooked and consumed.
cheapTips: Buy beef scraps or thin-sliced sirloin tips instead of premium cuts
Buy vegetables in season and use what's on sale

recipes.name: Fish-Flavored Pork Shreds
recipes.description: Sichuan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice pork loin thinly, then cut into thin shreds and toss with cornstarch and a pinch of salt.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering.
Add pork shreds in batches and stir-fry until cooked through, about 3-4 minutes total, then set aside.
In the same wok, stir-fry minced garlic, ginger, and dried chilies for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Mix soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, and water in a small bowl.
Pour the sauce into the wok and stir until it begins to bubble.
Return pork to the wok and toss everything together for 1-2 minutes until well coated.
Garnish with sliced green onions and serve over steamed rice.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder instead of loin for cheaper shreds
Make extra sauce and freeze for next time

recipes.name: Chongqing Rabbit
recipes.description: Sichuan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut rabbit meat into bite-sized pieces and blanch in boiling salted water for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Heat oil in a large wok over medium-high heat and toast dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns for 1 minute.
Add minced garlic and ginger, stirring constantly for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add blanched rabbit pieces and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned.
Mix soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, water, and star anise in a bowl.
Pour sauce into the wok and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes until rabbit is tender, stirring occasionally.
Taste and adjust seasoning, then transfer to serving dish with all the chilies and peppercorns.
cheapTips: Order rabbit online or find at specialty meat shops—often cheaper than stores
Use chicken thighs as substitute if rabbit unavailable

recipes.name: Smoked Duck
recipes.description: Sichuan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast Sichuan peppercorns, star anise, and cinnamon in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then mix with salt.
Rub the entire duck inside and out with the spiced salt mixture and let sit for 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Place ginger slices and star anise inside the duck cavity, then steam the duck for 45 minutes until cooked through.
Let duck cool slightly, then dry the skin thoroughly with paper towels.
Line a wok or large pot with aluminum foil and combine tea leaves, sugar, and rice on the bottom.
Place a rack above the smoking mixture and set the duck on top, breast-side up.
Cover the wok tightly with foil and lid, then smoke over medium heat for 30-40 minutes until dark and fragrant.
Remove from heat, let cool for 5 minutes, then chop into pieces and serve with soy sauce for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy whole duck when on sale and freeze until needed
Share with friends to spread the cost

recipes.name: Tea-Smoked Eggs
recipes.description: Sichuan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil eggs in water for 10 minutes until hard-boiled, then cool in ice water.
Gently crack the shell all over without removing it, creating a web of cracks.
Bring 2 cups of water to a boil with soy sauce, salt, sugar, star anise, cinnamon, and ginger.
Add black tea leaves and let steep for 5 minutes.
Place cracked eggs into the brewed mixture.
Simmer for 30-40 minutes, allowing the liquid to seep through the cracks.
Remove from heat and let eggs soak in the liquid for at least 2 hours, or overnight for deeper color.
Peel and serve cold or at room temperature with sliced ginger on the side.
cheapTips: Eggs are always cheap; buy larger cartons for snacks
Make big batches to last the whole week

recipes.name: Sichuan Peppercorn Fish
recipes.description: Sichuan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean and scale fish, then make shallow diagonal cuts on both sides for even cooking.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet and pan-fry fish over medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes per side until golden, then transfer to a plate.
In a small wok or pan, heat remaining 2 tablespoons oil over medium heat.
Toast Sichuan peppercorns and dried chilies for 1 minute, then add minced garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Mix soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar together, then add to the wok.
Pour the sauce mixture over the cooked fish.
Scatter the toasted peppercorns and chilies over the top and garnish with sliced green onions.
Serve hot with steamed rice.
cheapTips: Buy whole fish from Asian markets—much cheaper than fillets
Ask the fishmonger to scale and gut it for free

recipes.name: Boiled Fish in Spicy Broth
recipes.description: Sichuan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean fish and cut into thick steaks or leave whole if small enough to fit in pot.
Bring chicken broth to a boil in a large pot and add fish, then reduce heat and simmer for 12-15 minutes until just cooked through.
Carefully remove fish and place in a serving bowl, then strain broth through a sieve.
Heat oil in a small wok over medium-high heat and toast dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns for 1 minute.
Add minced garlic and ginger slices, stirring constantly for 30 seconds.
Pour the hot chili oil mixture over the fish.
Return the broth to the pot, add soy sauce and vinegar, then pour over the fish.
Top with bean sprouts and green onions, then serve immediately in the spicy broth.
cheapTips: Buy whole fish and ask fishmonger to cut steaks
Use vegetable broth instead of chicken for cheaper vegetarian version

recipes.name: Strange Flavor Chicken
recipes.description: Sichuan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Poach chicken breasts in boiling salted water for 12-15 minutes until fully cooked through.
Remove chicken and let cool slightly, then shred by hand into bite-sized pieces.
Toast Sichuan peppercorns and dried chilies in a dry pan for 1 minute, then crush coarsely.
Whisk together soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, and sugar in a bowl.
Mince garlic and ginger, then stir into the sauce mixture.
Place shredded chicken on a serving plate and pour the sauce over the top.
Sprinkle toasted peppercorns, chilies, crushed peanuts, and sliced green onions over the chicken.
Let sit for 5 minutes before serving to allow flavors to develop, and serve at room temperature.
cheapTips: Buy chicken on sale and freeze until ready to cook
Make sauce in bulk and store in fridge for 2 weeks

recipes.name: Upma
recipes.description: South Indian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat and add cumin seeds, letting them splutter for 30 seconds.
Add urad dal and peanuts, stirring constantly until golden brown, about 2 minutes.
Add diced onion, green chili, and ginger; sauté until onion becomes translucent, about 3 minutes.
Pour in semolina and stir continuously for 2 minutes to lightly toast it.
Carefully add water while stirring to avoid lumps, then add salt to taste.
Reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until the semolina absorbs all water.
Transfer to a serving plate and garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.
cheapTips: Buy semolina in bulk from Indian grocery stores for significant savings.
Use regular peanuts instead of roasted; they're cheaper and toast during cooking.

recipes.name: Pongal
recipes.description: South Indian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse rice and split peas separately under cold water until water runs clear.
Heat ghee in a large pot and add cumin seeds and peppercorns, stirring for 30 seconds.
Add cashews and toast until golden, about 1 minute, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, add ginger and green chili, sauté for 1 minute.
Add rice and split peas, stirring constantly for 2-3 minutes to coat with ghee.
Pour in 4 cups water, add salt, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes until rice and dal are soft and water is absorbed.
Stir in toasted cashews and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use vegetable oil instead of ghee to reduce costs by half.
Buy rice and moong dal from Indian bulk bins to save 30-40%.

recipes.name: Pesarattu
recipes.description: South Indian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak moong dal and rice together in water for 3-4 hours, then drain completely.
Grind the soaked dal and rice to a slightly coarse batter using a blender with minimal water, adding water gradually.
Transfer batter to a bowl and mix in green chili, ginger, onion, cumin seeds, and salt.
Let the batter rest for 5-10 minutes.
Heat oil in a non-stick skillet or dosa pan over medium-high heat.
Pour 0.5 cup batter onto the hot pan and gently spread into a circular shape, about 0.25-inch thick.
Cook for 3-4 minutes until the bottom is golden, then flip carefully and cook the other side for 2-3 minutes.
Transfer to a plate and serve hot with coconut chutney or tamarind chutney.
cheapTips: Buy moong dal in bulk at Indian stores for 40% less than grocery stores.
Skip the rice entirely and use just moong dal for a cheaper option.

recipes.name: Beef Noodle Soup
recipes.description: Taiwanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blanch beef cubes in boiling water for 3 minutes, drain, and rinse under cold water.
Heat oil in a large pot and fry ginger slices, garlic, and dried chili peppers for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add doubanjiang and stir-fry for 1 minute, then add beef and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in beef broth, add star anise, cinnamon stick, bay leaves, and rock sugar; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 60 minutes until beef is tender.
Add soy sauce and taste; adjust seasoning as needed.
Cook egg noodles separately in boiling water according to package directions, then drain.
Divide noodles into serving bowls, ladle beef and broth over them, and garnish with green onion and a drizzle of sesame oil.
cheapTips: Use beef stew meat (already cubed) instead of chuck to save prep time.
Make broth from scratch using beef bones; it's much cheaper than store-bought.

recipes.name: Oyster Omelette
recipes.description: Taiwanese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, cornstarch, and water together in a small bowl to create a slurry.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add oysters and sauté for 1 minute, then push to the side of the pan.
Add remaining oil to the pan, then add minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds.
Pour the flour slurry evenly over the oysters and pan, then distribute the oysters throughout.
Beat eggs in a bowl with salt and white pepper, then pour over the slurry mixture and cook without stirring for 2-3 minutes.
As the bottom sets, push cooked egg toward the center and tilt pan to allow uncooked egg to flow to the edges.
Once mostly set, fold the omelette in half, cook for 1 more minute, then transfer to a plate.
Drizzle with soy sauce and sesame oil, then garnish with green onion before serving.
cheapTips: Buy frozen oysters instead of fresh; they're 50% cheaper and work just as well.
Use 1 tablespoon flour instead of 3 for a thinner, more economical omelette.

recipes.name: Stinky Tofu
recipes.description: Taiwanese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut stinky tofu blocks into 1-inch cubes.
Heat oil in a deep pan or wok to 350°F (175°C).
Carefully add tofu cubes to hot oil in batches and fry for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy on all sides.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, chili oil, garlic, and sugar to make the dipping sauce.
Transfer fried stinky tofu to a serving plate and drizzle with dipping sauce.
Garnish with green onion and cilantro, then serve immediately while still warm and crispy.
cheapTips: Buy stinky tofu from Asian markets instead of specialty shops for 40% savings.
Reuse frying oil by straining it through cheesecloth for the next batch.

recipes.name: Bubble Tea
recipes.description: Taiwanese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Brew tea bags or loose leaf in 1 cup hot water for 5 minutes, then remove and let cool for 10 minutes.
In a separate pot, boil 2 cups water and add tapioca pearls, stirring occasionally for 8-10 minutes until translucent.
Drain tapioca pearls and immediately rinse under cold water, then toss with 2 tablespoons brown sugar.
Divide remaining 1 tablespoon brown sugar between two tall glasses.
Fill each glass halfway with ice cubes.
Pour cooled tea into glasses over ice, dividing equally.
Pour 0.375 cup milk into each glass and stir to combine.
Divide cooked tapioca pearls between glasses and serve with wide-mouth straws.
cheapTips: Buy tapioca pearls in bulk from Asian markets; they cost 60% less than specialty shops.
Use regular black tea bags instead of premium loose leaf for maximum savings.

recipes.name: Gua bao
recipes.description: Taiwanese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix warm water, sugar, and yeast together; let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, combine flour and salt, then make a well in the center and add yeast mixture and oil.
Mix until a shaggy dough forms, then knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place in an oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let rise for 20 minutes.
While dough rises, cook pork with garlic and ginger in a pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until starting to brown.
Add soy sauce, brown sugar, five-spice powder, and sesame oil to pork; simmer for 5 minutes.
Divide risen dough into 6 equal pieces and roll each into a thin 4-inch circle on parchment paper.
Steam buns on parchment in a bamboo steamer or pot with steamer basket for 8-10 minutes until puffy.
Gently peel away parchment and fold each bun in half.
Fill each bun with pork mixture, pickled mustard greens, and cilantro, then serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use ground pork shoulder instead of pork belly to save $1.50 per serving.
Skip pickled mustard greens and use sliced cucumber for a budget option.

recipes.name: Scallion Pancake
recipes.description: Taiwanese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pour hot water over flour and salt in a bowl, stirring with a wooden spoon until the dough comes together.
Knead dough on a lightly oiled surface for 5 minutes until smooth, then cover and let rest for 15 minutes.
Divide dough into 3 equal portions and roll each into a thin 10-inch circle.
Brush each circle generously with oil and sprinkle evenly with chopped green onions and a pinch of salt.
Starting from one edge, tightly roll the dough into a long coil, then coil it into a spiral shape.
Flatten the spiral gently with your palm into a 6-inch pancake, adjusting thickness as desired.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook each pancake for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds if desired and serve hot, optionally cut into quarters for easier eating.
cheapTips: Use vegetable oil exclusively; it's cheaper than sesame oil and works fine for cooking.
Buy bulk green onions from farmer's markets for 50% less than grocery stores.

recipes.name: Braised Pork Rice
recipes.description: Taiwanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blanch pork belly cubes in boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large pot and cook garlic and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add pork and brown for 3-4 minutes on all sides.
Deglaze the pot with Shaoxing wine, then add soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, star anise, and cinnamon stick.
Add water or broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 30 minutes until pork is tender.
Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear, then add to the braising liquid.
Stir well, cover, and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes until rice is cooked.
Turn off heat and let sit covered for 5 minutes.
Arrange hard-boiled egg halves on top of rice, garnish with green onion, and serve directly from the pot.
cheapTips: Use pork shoulder or leg instead of belly to reduce cost by $2 per serving.
Skip the hard-boiled eggs and save 75 cents per serving.

recipes.name: Mozuku
recipes.description: Okinawan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse the mozuku seaweed under cold water for 1 minute to remove excess salt and drain well.
In a small bowl, whisk together rice vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, water, and sesame oil.
Pour the dressing over the mozuku and toss gently to coat evenly.
Transfer to serving bowls and top with sesame seeds and sliced green onion.
Chill for 10 minutes before serving if time allows.
cheapTips: Buy canned mozuku in bulk from Asian markets
Skip the sesame oil if needed; use regular soy sauce only

recipes.name: Tondaburu
recipes.description: Okinawan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork into 3-inch cubes and blanch in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Heat a pot over medium-high heat and add the pork to brown slightly on all sides (about 4 minutes).
Add ginger and garlic, stirring for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in water, soy sauce, mirin, and sake, then bring to a boil and reduce heat to medium-low.
Simmer for 20 minutes, then add daikon radish and continue simmering for 8 minutes until pork is tender.
Season to taste and garnish with sliced green onion before serving.
cheapTips: Use pork shoulder instead of belly to save money
Daikon can be substituted with potatoes

recipes.name: Asechi
recipes.description: Okinawan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice green papaya into thin matchsticks and place in a bowl.
Sprinkle salt over papaya and let sit for 5 minutes, then squeeze out excess liquid gently.
Drain the canned tuna and flake it with a fork.
In a small bowl, whisk together vinegar, sesame oil, and minced garlic.
Combine papaya and tuna in a serving bowl, pour dressing over, and toss gently.
Garnish with sliced red chili and sesame seeds before serving.
cheapTips: Use cucumber if green papaya is unavailable
Buy canned tuna in bulk during sales

recipes.name: Awamori
recipes.description: Okinawan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Steam or boil sweet potatoes until fully cooked, then cool completely.
Mash the cooked sweet potatoes thoroughly and mix with koji spores in a clean jar.
Let the mixture sit at room temperature (68-75°F) for 48 hours covered with cheesecloth, stirring daily.
Add yeast and sugar to the koji mixture and stir well.
Cover loosely and let ferment at room temperature for 7-14 days, stirring every 2-3 days.
Strain through cheesecloth into clean bottles and seal.
Age for at least 3 months in a cool, dark place before consuming.
cheapTips: Buy sweet potatoes in bulk from farmers markets
Use regular baker's yeast if sake yeast unavailable

recipes.name: Andagi
recipes.description: Okinawan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In another bowl, beat eggs with vanilla extract until well combined.
Combine wet and dry ingredients, stirring until a thick dough forms.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Drop spoonfuls of dough into hot oil and fry 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and cool slightly before serving.
cheapTips: Buy flour in bulk
Reuse frying oil multiple times before discarding

recipes.name: Pani Andagi
recipes.description: Okinawan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, sugar, and baking powder in a bowl.
Beat eggs with 3 tablespoons water and combine with flour mixture until a stiff dough forms.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Drop small spoonfuls of dough into hot oil and fry 3-4 minutes total, turning occasionally until golden.
While frying, heat brown sugar and 1/2 cup water in a saucepan over medium heat until syrupy (about 5 minutes).
Drain fried andagi on paper towels, then toss in warm brown sugar syrup.
Serve warm with syrup clinging to each piece.
cheapTips: Make syrup while frying to save time
Brown sugar sometimes costs less than white sugar

recipes.name: Somin Chanpuru
recipes.description: Okinawan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook somen noodles according to package directions, drain, and set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook pork until browned (about 4 minutes).
Add diced vegetables and stir-fry for 3 minutes until slightly softened.
Push ingredients to the side, add remaining oil to empty space, and scramble eggs until cooked (about 2 minutes).
Add cooked noodles to the skillet and toss everything together.
Pour soy sauce over and mix well, season with salt and pepper.
Garnish with sliced green onion and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use any leftover vegetables on hand
Buy somen noodles in bulk from Asian markets

recipes.name: Kakigori
recipes.description: Okinawan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a small pot, combine sugar and water over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves completely (about 2 minutes).
Remove from heat and stir in fruit juice, then cool to room temperature.
Crush ice in a blender or with an ice crusher until fine and fluffy.
Divide crushed ice into 2 serving bowls.
Drizzle the fruit syrup and condensed milk over the shaved ice.
Serve immediately with a spoon.
cheapTips: Make your own fruit syrup instead of buying commercial versions
Use frozen fruit juice concentrate to save money

recipes.name: Konnyaku no Nimono
