Pour mixture onto parchment paper and spread to about 0.5-inch thickness.
Let cool for 10-15 minutes, then cut into squares and serve.
cheapTips: Buy jaggery in bulk from Indian markets for better prices
Use regular sugar instead of jaggery if unavailable

recipes.name: Jaggery Cake
recipes.description: Sri Lankan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9-inch round baking pan.
In a small bowl, dissolve grated jaggery in warm water and let cool slightly.
In a large bowl, whisk together eggs and coconut oil until well combined.
Add the jaggery-water mixture to the egg mixture and stir well.
In another bowl, combine flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and shredded coconut.
Gently fold the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients until just combined.
Pour batter into prepared pan and smooth the top.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.
cheapTips: Buy jaggery in powder form which is often cheaper than grated
Use regular sugar as a substitute if jaggery is unavailable

recipes.name: Cutlet
recipes.description: Sri Lankan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil potatoes until soft, then peel and mash them in a large bowl.
Brown ground meat in a skillet with chopped onion, garlic, and curry powder, breaking it apart as it cooks for 5-6 minutes.
Mix the cooked meat into mashed potatoes along with salt and pepper to taste.
Let mixture cool slightly, then shape into oval patties about 2 inches long.
Set up three shallow bowls with beaten eggs in one and bread crumbs in another.
Dip each cutlet into beaten egg, then coat thoroughly with bread crumbs.
Heat oil in a deep pan over medium-high heat.
Fry cutlets in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with lime wedges or curry sauce.
cheapTips: Use ground pork which is usually cheaper than beef
Make and freeze uncooked cutlets for future meals

recipes.name: Cake and Curry
recipes.description: Sri Lankan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9-inch square baking pan.
In a large bowl, beat eggs with jaggery until pale and thick, about 3 minutes.
Add coconut oil and mix well.
In a separate bowl, combine all-purpose flour, rice flour, baking powder, and salt.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients until just combined.
Heat coconut milk in a pan and briefly heat curry leaves, green onion, and green chili for 1 minute, then add to batter.
Pour batter into prepared pan and smooth the top.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until golden brown and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool slightly, cut into squares, and serve warm with a simple curry broth on the side.
cheapTips: Use leftover coconut milk from curry preparations
Substitute jaggery with brown sugar in equal amounts

recipes.name: Rolle
recipes.description: Sri Lankan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, 1 beaten egg, and salt together, then gradually add water to form a thick batter.
Heat a non-stick pan or crepe maker and grease lightly with oil.
Pour thin layer of batter and cook until set but still pliable, about 1 minute per side, creating crepe-like sheets.
Boil potatoes until soft, peel, and mash with salt to taste.
Brown ground meat in a skillet with onion, curry powder, and garlic for 5-6 minutes.
Mix cooked meat into mashed potatoes and let cool.
Spread thin layer of filling on each crepe sheet, roll tightly into cylinder, then fold like a spring roll.
Beat remaining 2 eggs in a bowl for egg wash.
Dip rolle in beaten egg and shallow fry in hot oil until golden brown on all sides, about 3-4 minutes total.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with chutney or curry sauce.
cheapTips: Make and freeze uncooked rolle before frying for future meals
Use ground pork instead of beef for cost savings

recipes.name: Acharu
recipes.description: Sri Lankan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and cut unripe mangoes into thin strips or bite-sized pieces.
Slice red chili peppers and mince garlic and ginger together.
Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds until they crackle.
Add minced garlic and ginger, cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add mango pieces and chopped chilies, then stir and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add salt and vinegar, mix well and simmer for 5 minutes until flavors combine.
Cool completely and transfer to a glass jar for storage.
cheapTips: Buy unripe mangoes in bulk when in season and make larger batches
Use basic mustard seeds from bulk bins instead of pre-packaged

recipes.name: Seeni Sambol
recipes.description: Sri Lankan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice onions thinly and finely chop garlic, ginger, and red chilies.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat and add onions, cooking until golden brown and caramelized (about 15 minutes).
Add garlic, ginger, and red chilies, stirring constantly for 2 minutes.
Add drained tuna and break it up with a spoon, cooking for 2 minutes.
Add tamarind paste, jaggery, salt, and curry leaves, stirring well.
Cook for 5-8 minutes on medium-low heat until flavors meld and mixture becomes sticky.
Cool completely before serving or storing in an airtight container.
cheapTips: Use regular canned tuna instead of premium brands to reduce cost
Make large batches and freeze to use over several weeks

recipes.name: Black Pork Curry
recipes.description: Sri Lankan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Crush black peppercorns coarsely and finely mince garlic and ginger.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot and add chopped onions, cooking until golden.
Add minced garlic and ginger, stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add pork cubes and brown on all sides for 5-7 minutes.
Sprinkle curry powder and crushed peppercorns over pork, stir well for 2 minutes.
Add vinegar and deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits.
Pour in coconut milk and water, add salt, bring to a boil then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour until pork is very tender, stirring occasionally.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder on sale and freeze until ready to cook
Use standard curry powder instead of premium blends

recipes.name: Muddy
recipes.description: Sri Lankan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix rice flour, grated coconut, salt, and chopped green onions in a bowl.
Add water gradually while stirring until a thick, pancake-like batter forms.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil and flatten slightly with the back of the spoon.
Fry for 2-3 minutes on each side until golden brown and crispy at edges.
Transfer cooked muddy to a paper towel-lined plate.
Serve warm with curry or sambols.
cheapTips: Buy rice flour and frozen coconut in bulk at Asian markets
Make extra batter and fridge to prepare quick breakfasts

recipes.name: Momo
recipes.description: Nepali snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt, then add water gradually while kneading until a smooth, firm dough forms.
Cover dough and let rest for 30 minutes.
Combine ground meat, minced onion, garlic, ginger, cilantro, soy sauce, and oil in a bowl for filling.
Roll dough into a thin sheet and cut into 2-inch circles using a glass or cutter.
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each circle.
Fold the circle in half, then bring the two corners together and press to seal, creating a pouch shape.
Bring a large pot of water to boil and add momos in batches, stirring gently.
Remove momos once they float and cook an additional 2-3 minutes, then transfer to a plate.
Serve hot with sesame oil and chili sauce for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy ground meat on sale and freeze in portions
Make double batch and freeze uncooked momos for quick future meals

recipes.name: Dal Bhat
recipes.description: Nepali lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse lentils and rice separately under cold water until water runs clear.
Heat oil in a large pot and add cumin seeds, letting them sizzle for 10 seconds.
Add minced garlic and ginger, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped onion and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add rinsed lentils, turmeric, and salt, stir well for 1 minute.
Pour in 3 cups of water, bring to boil, then simmer covered for 20 minutes until lentils are soft.
In a separate pot, bring 2 cups water to boil, add rice and salt, then simmer covered for 15-18 minutes until tender.
Serve rice and dal together on a plate, mixing lightly.
cheapTips: Buy lentils and rice in bulk from Indian or Asian stores
Make large batches and freeze portions for quick reheating

recipes.name: Thukpa
recipes.description: Nepali lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour with 0.5 cup water to form a sticky dough, let rest 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a large pot and add ground meat, breaking it apart with a spoon, cooking until browned.
Add diced onion, minced garlic, and ginger, cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in broth and bring to a boil, then add diced carrot.
Drop small pieces of dough directly into the boiling broth by pinching off bits and letting them fall in.
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking and cook for 10-12 minutes until dough pieces float and are cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use store-brand broth and ground meat
Add extra vegetables on hand like cabbage or spinach to stretch servings

recipes.name: Gundruk
recipes.description: Nepali lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse dried gundruk under cold water to remove excess salt and soften slightly.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add diced onion and cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and green chili, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add softened gundruk, turmeric, and salt, stir well.
Pour in water and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 12-15 minutes.
Cook until gundruk is tender and flavors have melded.
Serve hot as a side dish or with rice and lentils.
cheapTips: Buy dried gundruk from Nepali or Indian markets in bulk
Prepare in large batches as it stores well for several days

recipes.name: Sel Roti
recipes.description: Nepali breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix rice flour, all-purpose flour, sugar, salt, ginger, coconut, and crushed cardamom seeds in a bowl.
Add mashed banana and water gradually while stirring until a thick, smooth batter forms.
Heat oil in a deep pan or wok to 350°F (test with a small piece of bread).
Using a sel roti mold or large spoon, carefully dip the mold in oil then fill with batter, creating a ring shape.
Fry for 2-3 minutes until golden brown, then carefully flip and fry the other side for 2-3 minutes.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve warm, best eaten fresh on the day of making.
cheapTips: Use frozen coconut and store-brand oils to reduce costs
Make sel roti mold at home using aluminum foil if traditional mold unavailable

recipes.name: Juju Dhau
recipes.description: Nepali snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan and add crumbled paneer, stirring constantly for 3-4 minutes until lightly golden.
Add chopped cashews and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add raisins and cook for 1 minute, then sprinkle flour and mix well.
Pour in whole milk slowly while stirring to avoid lumps.
Add sweetened condensed milk and sugar, stirring continuously.
Simmer on medium-low heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring frequently, until mixture thickens.
Add crushed cardamom seeds and mix well.
Pour into a greased pan, cool completely, then cut into squares and serve.
cheapTips: Use store-brand sweetened condensed milk and paneer
Buy nuts in bulk and store in freezer for longer shelf life

recipes.name: Yomari
recipes.description: Nepali snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix jaggery, grated coconut, sesame seeds, ginger, and salt in a bowl to make the filling.
Bring water and ghee to boil, then gradually mix in rice flour until a soft dough forms.
Knead the dough until smooth and let cool slightly.
Divide dough into 6 portions and form each into a small ball.
Flatten each ball, add a spoonful of filling in the center, then fold into a leaf shape.
Bring a pot of water to boil and carefully drop yomaris in batches.
Cook until they float, then simmer for 2 more minutes and remove with a slotted spoon.
Serve warm, optionally drizzled with ghee.
cheapTips: Buy rice flour in bulk and store in an airtight container.
Use brown sugar instead of jaggery for significant savings.

recipes.name: Bara
recipes.description: Nepali breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak split black lentils in water for 4 hours, then drain completely.
Grind soaked lentils with minimal water using a food processor until fluffy and slightly airy.
Mix ground lentils with onion, green chili, ginger, cilantro, and salt.
Heat oil in a deep pan over medium-high heat until very hot.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into hot oil, gently flattening slightly with the back of the spoon.
Fry until golden brown on both sides, about 3-4 minutes total.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with chutney or curry.
cheapTips: Buy dried lentils in bulk from ethnic grocery stores.
Reuse frying oil by straining and storing for 2-3 uses.

recipes.name: Chatamari
recipes.description: Nepali snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, and salt to make a thin batter similar to crepe consistency.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet or griddle over medium-high heat.
Pour batter onto the hot griddle and spread thinly into a 10-inch circle.
Cook the base until edges start to brown, about 3 minutes.
Crack eggs directly onto the center, sprinkle meat, onion, and cilantro over the top.
Cover the skillet with a lid and cook until eggs are set, about 3-4 minutes.
Fold the chatamari in half and slide onto a plate.
Serve hot with pickled vegetables or chutney on the side.
cheapTips: Use ground chicken instead of beef for lower cost.
Buy eggs in bulk and store in the refrigerator for 4 weeks.

recipes.name: Sukuti
recipes.description: Nepali snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Trim beef to remove excess fat and cut into thin strips 4-5 inches long.
Combine salt, turmeric, chili powder, ginger-garlic paste, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Coat beef strips thoroughly with the spice mixture and let marinate for 30 minutes.
Arrange strips on a clean cloth or drying rack in direct sunlight or a dehydrator.
Dry for 6-8 hours, turning strips occasionally until completely dry and leather-like.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds, then fry dried meat strips until crispy, about 3-4 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and cool completely.
Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.
cheapTips: Buy beef during sales and freeze until ready to make sukuti.
Use a sunny windowsill for free drying instead of electricity.

recipes.name: Samay Baji
recipes.description: Nepali breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse rice thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear.
Heat ghee in a pot over medium heat and add cumin seeds.
When seeds crackle, add rice and stir for 1-2 minutes to coat with ghee.
Add water, bay leaf, turmeric, and salt, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 18 minutes.
In a separate pan, heat 1 tablespoon ghee and fry cashews and raisins until golden.
Remove from heat and let rice sit covered for 5 minutes to steam.
Fluff rice with a fork, mix in fried cashews and raisins, and serve.
cheapTips: Skip cashews and use peanuts for budget version.
Buy rice in bulk and store in a cool, dry place.

recipes.name: Aloo Tama
recipes.description: Nepali lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and add sliced onion, cooking until translucent.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric and chili powder, cooking for 30 seconds.
Add cubed potatoes and bamboo shoots, stirring to coat with spices.
Pour in water and salt, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer.
Cook covered for 20-25 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Check seasoning and adjust salt and spices as needed.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot with rice or roti.
cheapTips: Buy canned bamboo shoots on sale and stock up.
Use regular potatoes instead of specialty varieties.

recipes.name: Saag
recipes.description: Nepali lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and add diced onion.
Cook onion until soft, about 3 minutes, then add garlic and ginger.
Stir and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped spinach and mustard greens in batches, stirring as they wilt.
Pour in water and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add green chili and season with salt and black pepper.
Simmer for another 5 minutes to blend flavors.
Serve hot with rice, roti, or as a side dish.
cheapTips: Buy spinach in bulk when in season and freeze.
Use canned spinach if fresh is unavailable and adjust liquid.

recipes.name: Paneer Momo
recipes.description: Nepali snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, 0.5 teaspoon salt, and oil in a bowl, adding water gradually to make a soft dough.
Knead well for 5 minutes, cover with damp cloth, and rest for 20 minutes.
Mix grated paneer with onion, cilantro, green chili, ginger, salt, and pepper for filling.
Roll dough thin on a floured surface and cut circles using a 3-inch cutter.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, then fold and pleat edges to form a purse shape.
Bring water to boil in a large pot and carefully drop momos in batches.
Cook until they float, then simmer for 2 more minutes.
Remove with a slotted spoon and serve hot with chutney or soy sauce.
cheapTips: Make momos in bulk and freeze on a tray before storing in freezer bags.
Buy paneer from Indian markets, often cheaper than regular grocery stores.

recipes.name: Chhoyela
recipes.description: Nepali dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and add ginger-garlic paste.
Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, then add ground meat in small crumbles.
Break the meat apart with a spoon as it cooks, stirring frequently for 8-10 minutes until browned.
Add diced onion and cook for 3 more minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in cumin powder and chili powder, cooking for 1 minute.
Add green chili, cilantro, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Mix well and cook for 2-3 minutes to combine flavors.
Serve hot as a main dish with rice or alongside flattened rice (beaten rice).
cheapTips: Buy ground beef when on sale and freeze in portions.
Use less expensive ground beef instead of buffalo.

recipes.name: Sekuwa
recipes.description: Nepali dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix yogurt, chili powder, turmeric, garlic, ginger, lemon juice, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Add beef cubes and coat thoroughly with marinade, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or overnight.
Thread marinated beef and onion chunks alternately onto metal skewers.
Heat oil in a large skillet or grill pan over high heat until very hot.
Place skewers on the hot surface and cook for 3-4 minutes per side until meat is charred and cooked through.
Work in batches to avoid crowding the pan.
Transfer cooked sekuwa to a serving platter.
Serve hot with flatbread, rice, and fresh lemon wedges.
cheapTips: Buy beef chuck or shoulder cuts for kebabs, less expensive than premium cuts.
Use wooden skewers from home stores instead of metal.

recipes.name: Rasgulla
recipes.description: Bengali snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat milk to boiling point and add vinegar slowly while stirring until curds separate from whey completely.
Strain the curds through cheesecloth and hang for 10 minutes to remove excess moisture.
Knead the paneer with flour into a smooth soft dough and shape into 12 equal balls.
Boil water with sugar and crushed cardamom to make syrup and let cool to room temperature.
Gently drop paneer balls into boiling water one at a time and let them float to the surface.
Once all balls float, simmer for 8-10 minutes until they increase in size by one-third.
Remove balls with a slotted spoon and immerse immediately in cooled sugar syrup.
Add rose water to the syrup and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.
cheapTips: Buy milk when on sale and freeze for later use
Use store-brand sugar instead of specialty varieties

recipes.name: Sandesh
recipes.description: Bengali snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Crumble paneer finely by hand or with a food processor until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Heat ghee in a pan and add crumbled paneer, stirring continuously for 5 minutes.
Add condensed milk and powdered cardamom, mixing well until the mixture becomes smooth.
Cook for 3-4 minutes until the mixture thickens and leaves the sides of the pan.
Spread the mixture on a plate and let cool completely for 15 minutes.
Shape into small balls or discs and press lightly with chopped pistachios on top.
Roll some sandesh in coconut powder if desired and refrigerate until serving.
cheapTips: Make paneer at home using milk and vinegar to save 50% on cost
Substitute store-brand condensed milk for name brands

recipes.name: Mishti Doi
recipes.description: Bengali snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat milk to 82°C (180°F) and add condensed milk and sugar, stirring until dissolved.
Cool the mixture to about 43°C (110°F) and add crushed cardamom and nutmeg powder.
Whisk plain yogurt in a separate bowl and fold it gently into the cooled milk mixture.
Pour into earthenware bowls or yogurt containers, dividing the mixture equally.
Wrap containers with aluminum foil and place in an insulated cooler with hot water.
Alternatively, use a yogurt maker set to 110°F and incubate for 6-8 hours until set.
Do not disturb or move containers while yogurt is setting.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving chilled.
cheapTips: Buy milk in bulk when on sale and make multiple batches
Use powdered milk mixed with water if fresh milk is expensive in your area

recipes.name: Rosogolla
recipes.description: Bengali snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil milk and add vinegar slowly to curdle it, then strain through cheesecloth hanging for 15 minutes.
Knead the paneer with flour very gently into a smooth dough and shape into 14 small balls.
Prepare sugar syrup by boiling water with 1.5 cups sugar and crushed cardamom for 5 minutes.
In a separate pot, bring water with remaining sugar to a boil and add the paneer balls gently.
Stir gently with a spoon for 3-4 minutes to prevent sticking to the bottom.
Once balls float and increase in size, simmer for 12-15 minutes until spongy and soft.
Transfer balls to the cardamom sugar syrup using a slotted spoon.
Add rose water and let cool completely, then refrigerate for 4 hours before serving.
cheapTips: Make paneer fresh at home using milk and vinegar instead of buying
Use regular granulated sugar instead of superfine sugar

recipes.name: Khichuri
recipes.description: Bengali lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Wash rice and moong dal separately and drain well.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot and add cumin seeds and bay leaves until fragrant.
Add ginger and cook for 30 seconds, then add diced potatoes and cook for 2 minutes.
Add rice, moong dal, turmeric powder, and peas, stirring gently for 2 minutes.
Pour water and add salt, then bring to a boil over high heat.
Once boiling, reduce heat to low, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and cook for 18-20 minutes until rice and dal are tender.
Remove from heat and let rest covered for 3 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot with ghee and a squeeze of lemon juice.
cheapTips: Buy rice and dal in bulk from Indian grocery stores for 30-40% savings
Use regular potatoes instead of specialty varieties

recipes.name: Pabda Macher Jhol
recipes.description: Bengali lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat mustard oil in a deep pot and add cumin seeds until they crackle.
Add sliced onions and cook until golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomato pieces, turmeric, and red chili powder, cooking until tomatoes soften.
Pour water and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Gently place fish fillets into the gravy and simmer for 10-12 minutes until fish is cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper, then sprinkle cilantro on top.
Serve hot over steamed rice with the flavorful gravy.
cheapTips: Substitute with catfish or tilapia if pabda is unavailable or too expensive
Buy whole fish and ask the fishmonger to fillet it for free

recipes.name: Chholar Dal
recipes.description: Bengali lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried chickpeas overnight or for at least 8 hours, then drain well.
Boil chickpeas with water and turmeric until completely tender, about 30 minutes.
Heat ghee in a separate pot and add cumin seeds until fragrant.
Add minced ginger and chopped green chilies, cooking for 1 minute.
Add diced onion and cook until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Stir in grated coconut and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add cooked chickpeas with their cooking liquid to the spice mixture.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes, mashing some chickpeas to thicken the dal slightly, then serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy chickpeas dried in bulk from Indian or ethnic grocery stores
Use unsweetened coconut powder instead of fresh coconut for convenience

recipes.name: Lau Bhaja
recipes.description: Bengali snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel bottle gourd and cut into 0.25-inch thick round slices.
Mix gram flour, rice flour, turmeric, and salt in a bowl.
Add minced green chili and onion to the flour mixture.
Add water gradually while stirring to create a thick batter without lumps.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F until a small piece of batter sizzles immediately.
Dip each gourd slice into the batter, coating completely on both sides.
Fry in batches of 4-5 slices until golden brown on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per batch.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels, serve hot with chutney.
cheapTips: Buy bottle gourd in season for 50% cheaper prices
Reuse frying oil multiple times by straining it carefully

recipes.name: Kosha Mangsho
recipes.description: Bengali lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot and add cumin seeds and bay leaves until fragrant.
Add 3 sliced onions and fry until dark golden brown, about 8 minutes, then set aside.
In the same pot, add remaining ghee and fry remaining sliced onion until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant and golden.
Add meat pieces and cook on high heat for 5-7 minutes until browned on all sides.
Reduce heat and add yogurt mixed with red chili and turmeric powder, stirring well for 3 minutes.
Add water and the fried brown onions, cover and simmer on medium-low heat for 45-50 minutes until meat is very tender and gravy thickens.
Season with salt and serve hot over steamed rice or with warm bread.
cheapTips: Buy meat from ethnic butchers where it is typically 20-30% cheaper
Make in large batches and freeze portions for later meals

recipes.name: Phirni
recipes.description: Bengali snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak rice for 20 minutes, then grind it into a smooth fine paste using a grinder with minimal water.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot and add the rice paste, stirring continuously for 5-7 minutes until slightly golden and aromatic.
Heat milk separately and add to the rice paste slowly while stirring to avoid lumps.
Cook on medium heat, stirring frequently, for about 15 minutes until the mixture thickens and becomes creamy.
Add crushed cardamom powder and almond powder, mixing well.
Add sugar and cook for 2-3 minutes more while stirring until it dissolves completely.
Pour the warm phirni into earthenware bowls or dessert cups.
Top with pistachios, remaining almonds, and rose water, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving chilled.
cheapTips: Buy nuts in bulk during sales and store in an airtight container
Skip the silver leaf as it is purely decorative and adds significant cost

recipes.name: Buff Momo
recipes.description: Nepali snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour with water and salt to form a soft dough, then knead for 5 minutes and let rest for 15 minutes covered.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté onions, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add ground beef and cook until browned, then stir in soy sauce, salt, pepper, and cilantro, cooking for 3 minutes.
Divide dough into 12 equal pieces and roll each into a thin circle.
Place 1 tablespoon of filling in the center of each circle and fold into a pouch shape, pinching the top closed.
Bring water to boil in a pot and steam momos in a bamboo steamer or colander for 10 minutes until they float and are cooked through.
Serve hot with soy sauce or chili-oil dipping sauce.
cheapTips: Buy ground beef on sale and freeze for later use
Use a pot with a colander instead of purchasing a bamboo steamer

recipes.name: Roti
recipes.description: Nepali lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix whole wheat flour, salt, and oil in a bowl.
Add water gradually while mixing until a soft dough forms, then knead for 5 minutes.
Divide dough into 8 equal balls and let rest for 5 minutes.
Heat a cast iron skillet or griddle over medium-high heat.
Roll each ball into a thin circle on a floured surface.
Place roti on the hot skillet and cook for about 1 minute until bubbles form, then flip and cook the other side for 30 seconds until light brown spots appear.
Press gently with a cloth to help puff up, then transfer to a plate and brush lightly with oil.
cheapTips: Buy whole wheat flour in bulk for significant savings
Skip oil or use minimal amounts to reduce costs

recipes.name: Haleem
recipes.description: Hyderabadi lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak lentils, wheat, and barley in water for 30 minutes, then drain.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot and fry half the sliced onions until golden brown, then remove and set aside.
In the same ghee, add remaining onions and fry until soft, then add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add beef, red chili powder, and turmeric powder, then cook on high heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the soaked lentils, wheat, and barley along with 8 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally, until meat and grains completely break down into a thick paste.
Mash with the back of a spoon or an immersion blender until the mixture reaches a uniform, porridge-like consistency.
Top with fried onions, fresh mint, cilantro, and a dollop of ghee before serving hot.
cheapTips: Buy lentils and grains in bulk from Indian grocery stores
Use vegetable oil instead of ghee to reduce cost significantly

recipes.name: Double Ka Meetha
recipes.description: Hyderabadi snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Trim crusts from bread slices and cut each slice diagonally into two triangles.
Heat ghee in a deep frying pan over medium heat and fry bread pieces until golden and crispy on both sides, then remove and drain on paper towels.
In the same pan, fry almonds, cashews, and raisins until golden, then remove and set aside.
Pour condensed milk and evaporated milk into the same pan and stir well over medium heat.
Add sugar, cardamom powder, and saffron strands, stirring constantly until the mixture thickens slightly, about 5 minutes.
Add the fried bread pieces and mix gently until they are well coated with the milk mixture.
Transfer to a serving dish and top with the fried dry fruits before serving warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Use store-brand condensed and evaporated milk for savings
Skip saffron or use a tiny amount since a pinch goes a long way

recipes.name: Lukhmi
recipes.description: Hyderabadi snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, and salt to form a soft dough, then knead well and let rest for 20 minutes covered.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a pan and sauté onions until golden, then add ginger-garlic paste and green chili.
Add ground meat and cook until browned, then stir in garam masala, cilantro, and salt, cooking until dry.
Divide dough into 6 equal portions and roll each into a thin oval shape.
Place 2 tablespoons of filling on one half of each oval and fold the other half over to seal the edges with water.
Heat remaining oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat and fry lukhmi until golden brown on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with chutney or sauce.
cheapTips: Buy ground meat in bulk and portion into freezer bags
Use vegetable oil instead of ghee for significant savings

recipes.name: Shami Kebab
recipes.description: Hyderabadi snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak chana dal in water for 1 hour, then drain well.
Cook ground meat with soaked dal in a pot with water and salt for 20 minutes until meat and dal are very tender and the mixture is dry.
Cool the cooked mixture, then transfer to a food processor with ginger-garlic paste, green chili, cilantro, and garam masala.
Pulse until the mixture becomes a fine paste, then transfer to a bowl and mix in the beaten egg.
Divide into 8-10 equal portions and shape each into a thick disc about 1/2 inch thick.
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and fry kebabs for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with mint chutney and lemon wedges.
cheapTips: Buy split peas from Indian grocery stores at lower prices than specialty shops
Use cheaper ground beef instead of lamb to reduce costs

recipes.name: Seekh Kebab
recipes.description: Hyderabadi snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix ground meat with finely chopped onions, ginger-garlic paste, green chili, cilantro, mint, and garam masala in a bowl.
Add beaten egg and salt to the mixture and knead until it becomes a sticky paste.
Divide the mixture into 6-8 equal portions.
Wet your hands and mold each portion onto metal skewers, pressing firmly to elongate into a cylindrical shape.
Heat oil in a large frying pan or tawa over medium-high heat.
Carefully lay the skewers on the hot oil and rotate occasionally while frying for 10-12 minutes until all sides are golden brown and meat is cooked through.
Slide kebabs off the skewer onto a serving plate and serve hot with onion slices, lemon wedges, and mint chutney.
cheapTips: Use ground beef instead of lamb to save on costs
Cook in batches using a regular pan instead of buying expensive skewers

recipes.name: Galauti Kebab
recipes.description: Hyderabadi snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix ground meat with chopped onions, ginger-garlic paste, green chili, cilantro, mint, and raw papaya paste in a bowl.
Add garam masala, crushed black cardamom, and beaten egg, then knead the mixture until very smooth and sticky.
Refrigerate the mixture for 15 minutes to make it easier to handle.
Divide into 10-12 equal portions and gently shape each into a thin, flat disc about 1/4 inch thick using wet hands.
Heat oil in a frying pan over medium heat until shimmering.
Carefully place kebabs in the oil and fry for 2-3 minutes per side until light golden and cooked through, handling gently to prevent breaking.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with sliced onions, lemon wedges, and mint chutney.
cheapTips: Use frozen raw papaya paste or mash a fresh papaya yourself
Ground beef works fine as a substitute for lamb

recipes.name: Qubani Ka Meetha
recipes.description: Hyderabadi snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried apricots in hot water for 10 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Heat ghee in a pan and fry almonds and cashews until golden, then remove and set aside.
In the same ghee, place soaked apricots and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, crushing them slightly with the back of a spoon.
Add sugar and crushed cardamom pods, then cook for another 3 minutes while stirring constantly.
Pour in the cream or condensed milk and stir well to combine, cooking for 2-3 minutes until the mixture is warm and well blended.
Transfer to serving bowls and top with the fried nuts.
Serve warm or at room temperature as a sweet dessert dish.
cheapTips: Buy dried apricots in bulk from wholesale stores for better prices
Use evaporated milk or regular milk mixed with a bit of flour as a cream substitute

recipes.name: Karachi Haleem
recipes.description: Hyderabadi lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak chana dal, lentils, wheat, and barley in water for 30 minutes, then drain completely.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot and fry two-thirds of the sliced onions until deep golden brown and crispy, then remove and reserve for garnish.
In the same ghee, add remaining onions and fry until soft, then add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add cubed meat, red chili powder, turmeric, and 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, then cook on high heat for 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the drained lentils, dal, wheat, and barley along with 10 cups of water and bring to a rolling boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2 hours, stirring occasionally and adding water if needed to prevent sticking.
After 2 hours, the mixture should be very thick and meat should be falling apart; add remaining garam masala and stir vigorously to break down grains and lentils into a creamy consistency.
If needed, continue cooking and stirring for another 15-20 minutes until the haleem reaches a porridge-like texture.
Transfer to a serving dish, top with reserved fried onions, fresh cilantro, mint, and additional ghee, then serve steaming hot.
cheapTips: Buy lentils and grains from Pakistani or Indian markets for better prices
Use vegetable oil instead of ghee throughout to reduce total cost by 30%

recipes.name: Dahi Ke Kebab
recipes.description: Hyderabadi snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil potatoes until soft, peel, and mash them in a bowl.
Mix mashed potatoes with yogurt, minced green chilies, cilantro, ginger-garlic paste, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Refrigerate mixture for 15 minutes until firm enough to shape.
Roll mixture into oval kebab shapes and coat with breadcrumbs.
Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat and shallow fry kebabs until golden brown on all sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with mint chutney.
cheapTips: Buy potatoes in bulk
Make yogurt at home if possible

recipes.name: Pathar Ka Gosht
recipes.description: Hyderabadi lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Marinate meat with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, half the garam masala, and salt for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot and fry onions until deep golden brown, then set aside half.
Add marinated meat to remaining onions and cook on high heat for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add tomatoes and cook until they break down completely into a paste.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and cook for 45 minutes until meat is tender.
Add coriander powder, cumin powder, remaining garam masala, and green chilies.
Cook uncovered for another 10 minutes until gravy thickens.
Garnish with fried onions and fresh cilantro before serving.
cheapTips: Buy goat meat from ethnic markets
Use chicken thighs as cheaper substitute

recipes.name: Dum Pukht Murgh
recipes.description: Hyderabadi lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Marinate chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, garam masala, half the green chilies, and salt for 30 minutes.
Slice onions and fry in ghee until golden brown, then set aside half for garnish.
Layer marinated chicken with fried onions in a heavy-bottomed pot, sprinkling bay leaves between layers.
Top with remaining fried onions and mint-cilantro mixture.
Cover the pot tightly with foil, then place a tawa (griddle) or heavy pan on top.
Cook on high heat for 2 minutes until steam forms, then reduce to low heat.
Cook for 40 minutes without opening the lid until chicken is tender.
Carefully remove from heat, uncover, and serve garnished with boiled eggs if desired.
cheapTips: Buy whole chicken and cut yourself
Use chicken legs instead of thighs

recipes.name: Baghare Baingan
recipes.description: Hyderabadi lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut eggplants into thick rounds or quarters and slit halfway through without cutting completely.
Dry roast peanuts, sesame seeds, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and dried chilies in a pan for 2 minutes.
Grind roasted spices with coconut and tamarind paste into a coarse paste.
Stuff each eggplant piece with the spice paste and a few onion slices.
Heat oil in a large pan and arrange stuffed eggplants in a single layer.
Cover and cook on medium heat for 25 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally.
Uncover and continue cooking until eggplants are tender and golden brown.
Serve hot as a side dish or with rice.
cheapTips: Buy eggplants in season
Use peanut powder instead of whole peanuts

recipes.name: Mirchi Ka Salan
recipes.description: Hyderabadi lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Roast peanuts, sesame seeds, and coconut together until lightly golden.
Grind roasted mixture with tamarind paste into a coarse paste.
Slit green chilies lengthwise and carefully remove seeds, keeping the stem intact.
Stuff each chili with the peanut-coconut paste.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds, then add sliced onions and fry until soft.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, and salt, cooking until tomatoes break down into a paste.
Gently place stuffed chilies into the gravy and cook covered on low heat for 15 minutes.
Serve hot as an accompaniment with biryani or rice.
cheapTips: Buy green chilies from Indian markets
Make coconut paste at home

recipes.name: Biryani Shorba
recipes.description: Hyderabadi lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Marinate chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, half the garam masala, and salt for 20 minutes.
Boil water in a large pot with bay leaves and salt, then add rinsed basmati rice.
Cook rice until 70% done, then drain immediately.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot and add cumin seeds, then add sliced onions and fry until golden.
Add marinated chicken to onions and cook on high heat for 5 minutes.
Layer cooked rice over chicken, sprinkle remaining garam masala and herbs.
Cover tightly with foil and cook on low heat for 15 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Mix gently with a fork and serve hot with shorba as a soup accompaniment.
cheapTips: Buy basmati rice in bulk
Use regular onions instead of shallots

recipes.name: Falooda
recipes.description: Hyderabadi snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil water in a pot and cook vermicelli until soft, then drain and set aside.
Soak basil seeds in water for 15 minutes until they become gelatinous.
Mix milk with rose syrup and condensed milk, stirring well.
Pour the milk mixture into serving glasses.
Layer cooked vermicelli into each glass.
Add a scoop of ice cream on top.
Sprinkle soaked basil seeds and chopped pistachios.
Add ice cubes and serve immediately with a spoon and straw.
cheapTips: Make vermicelli at home
Use regular milk instead of specialty

recipes.name: Khubani Paka
recipes.description: Hyderabadi snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried apricots in hot water for 10 minutes, then chop them finely.
Crush jaggery into small pieces for faster melting.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan and add chopped apricots.
Roast apricots for 2 minutes, then add jaggery and water, stirring continuously.
Crush cardamom seeds and add to the mixture.
Cook on medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring frequently until the mixture becomes thick and glossy.
Chop almonds and cashews, then add to the pan along with sliced pistachios.
Cook for another 2 minutes and transfer to a greased plate to cool before cutting into pieces.
cheapTips: Buy dried apricots in bulk from Indian markets
Skip expensive nuts and use peanuts

recipes.name: Bobbat
recipes.description: Hyderabadi snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Roast rice flour in ghee over low heat for 8 minutes until fragrant, stirring constantly.
In a separate pan, dissolve jaggery in water over medium heat, stirring until fully melted.
Strain the jaggery syrup to remove any impurities.
Roast sesame seeds, peanuts, and coconut together in a dry pan until golden.
Add roasted jaggery syrup to the ghee-roasted rice flour and mix well.
Add roasted sesame-peanut-coconut mixture, cardamom powder, and salt.
Cook on low heat for 5 minutes, stirring continuously until the mixture thickens.
Transfer to a greased plate, cool, and cut into diamond or square shapes.
cheapTips: Buy jaggery from bulk bins
Toast your own peanuts and sesame

recipes.name: Aloo Ka Salan
recipes.description: Hyderabadi lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut potatoes into thick cubes and deep fry in oil until golden brown on the outside, then set aside.
Dry roast peanuts, sesame seeds, coconut, and dried chilies together until fragrant.
Grind roasted ingredients with tamarind paste into a paste, adding water if needed.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds, then add sliced onions and fry until golden.
Add tomatoes and turmeric, cooking until tomatoes break down into a paste.
Stir in the peanut paste and cook for 2 minutes over medium heat.
Add fried potatoes and mix gently to coat with the spice paste.
Add water as needed to create a thick curry consistency and simmer for 5 minutes.
cheapTips: Buy potatoes in bulk
Use peanut powder instead of whole peanuts

recipes.name: Sticky Rice
recipes.description: Laotian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse sticky rice under cold water until water runs clear, stirring gently with your hand.
Soak rice in water for at least 2 hours or overnight if possible.
Drain the soaked rice completely.
In a rice cooker or pot, combine drained rice with 2.5 cups fresh water.
Cook on high heat until water comes to a boil, then reduce to low heat and cover.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes until all water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Transfer cooked rice to a bamboo sticky rice basket or wooden bowl lined with a warm damp cloth.
Cover and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Buy sticky rice in bulk from Asian markets for 30-40% savings
No special equipment needed; a regular pot works fine with proper technique

recipes.name: Papaya Salad
recipes.description: Laotian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound garlic and chilies together in a mortar and pestle until slightly bruised.
Add green beans and tomatoes to the mortar and gently bruise them together.
Add shredded green papaya and toss everything together lightly.
Pour in lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar, then toss well for 1 minute.
Transfer to a serving plate and top with crushed peanuts.
Serve immediately while still crisp and fresh.
cheapTips: Use cabbage as a papaya substitute if green papaya unavailable
Buy pre-shredded papaya at Asian markets to save prep time

recipes.name: Khao Poon
recipes.description: Laotian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, lemongrass, and ginger for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce and taste for seasoning, adjusting as needed.
Cook rice vermicelli according to package directions, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Divide noodles between two bowls.
Pour hot broth over noodles and top with cooked shrimp.
Serve with fresh herbs, lime wedges, and additional fish sauce on the side.
Let each diner customize their bowl with desired herbs and lime juice.
cheapTips: Use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth to save 20%
Skip shrimp and use leftover rotisserie chicken for cost savings

recipes.name: Sai Oua
recipes.description: Laotian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine ground pork, minced pork skin, garlic, galangal, lemongrass, and curry paste in a bowl.
Mix in fish sauce, lime juice, and cilantro, stirring until well combined.
Stuff the mixture into pork intestine casings, tying off 4-inch links with kitchen twine.
Heat oil in a grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
Grill sausages for 8-10 minutes per side until cooked through and slightly charred.
Rest for 2 minutes and serve warm with sticky rice and nam khao.
cheapTips: Skip the casings and form into patties to avoid specialty ingredient costs
Buy pork from bulk meat counters at lower per-pound rates

recipes.name: Nam Khao
recipes.description: Laotian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast shallots and garlic in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until fragrant.
Add cooked ground pork to the pan and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pound Thai chilies in a mortar and pestle, then add to the pork mixture.
Remove from heat and stir in lime juice, fish sauce, cilantro, and mint.
Taste and adjust seasonings as needed.
Crumble rice cakes into a bowl and pour the warm pork mixture over them.
Toss well and serve immediately before rice cakes become too soft.
cheapTips: Use store-brand rice crackers instead of specialty imported ones
Substitute ground beef or chicken for pork at similar prices

recipes.name: Tam Som
recipes.description: Laotian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound garlic and Thai chilies in a mortar and pestle until slightly bruised.
Add long beans and tomatoes, bruising them gently until slightly softened.
Add shredded green papaya and toss lightly with the other ingredients.
Pour lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar into the mortar.
Toss everything together for about 1 minute until well mixed.
Transfer to a serving plate and top with crushed peanuts.
Serve immediately as a fresh, spicy salad.
cheapTips: Replace long beans with regular green beans if unavailable
Buy papaya at farmers markets where they're often cheaper

recipes.name: Ping Gai
recipes.description: Laotian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound garlic, cilantro roots, and black peppercorns together in a mortar and pestle.
Mix the paste with fish sauce, lime juice, oil, and salt.
Rub the marinade all over the spatchcocked chicken, inside and out.
Let marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or refrigerate for up to 4 hours.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat and oil the grates.
Place chicken skin-side down on the grill and cook for 20-25 minutes.
Flip and cook skin-side up for another 15-20 minutes until skin is crispy and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving with sticky rice and papaya salad.
cheapTips: Buy whole chicken instead of parts for 30% savings
Substitute cilantro stems for roots if available

recipes.name: Kaeng Om
recipes.description: Laotian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, galangal, and lemongrass for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk and water, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Add fish fillet and fish cake slices, simmering for 10-12 minutes until fish is cooked through.
Stir in fish sauce and adjust seasoning to taste.
Add dill and stir gently to avoid breaking up the fish.
Simmer for another 2-3 minutes until dill is wilted.
Serve hot in bowls with the broth and sticky rice on the side.
cheapTips: Use canned fish instead of fresh fillets for 40% cost savings
Substitute regular herbs if dill is unavailable or expensive

recipes.name: Mok Pa
recipes.description: Laotian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blanch banana leaves for 30 seconds to soften them, then pat dry.
Mix coconut milk, curry paste, fish sauce, and lime juice in a bowl.
Stir in garlic, galangal, and fresh herbs into the coconut mixture.
Divide fish fillet into two portions and place each on a banana leaf.
Pour half the coconut mixture over each fish portion.
Fold banana leaf edges over the fish to create a sealed packet, tucking in sides.
Place packets on a steamer basket or in a steamer pot filled with 2 inches of water.
Steam covered for 12-15 minutes until fish is opaque and cooked through.
Carefully transfer packets to plates and unfold to serve.
cheapTips: Skip banana leaves and wrap in aluminum foil instead
Use frozen fish fillets instead of fresh for 25% savings

recipes.name: Or Lam
recipes.description: Laotian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and sauté garlic, shallots, and galangal for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add pork ribs and brown them on all sides for 5-7 minutes.
Pour in water or broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer.
Cook pork for 15-20 minutes until nearly tender.
Add pumpkin cubes and continue simmering for 10 minutes until squash is soft.
Stir in fish sauce and taste for seasoning, adjusting as needed.
Add dill and stir gently, simmering for another 2 minutes.
Serve hot as a hearty stew with sticky rice.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs instead of pork ribs for 20% savings
Buy pumpkin puree instead of fresh squash for convenience and cost savings

recipes.name: Khao Jee
recipes.description: Laotian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice the baguette lengthwise and spread butter and pâté on the inside halves.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and scramble the eggs with fish sauce until cooked through.
Toast the baguette halves in the skillet until golden and crispy on the cut sides.
Divide the scrambled eggs between the two baguette halves and top with chopped green onions.
Serve immediately while warm.
cheapTips: Use budget pâté or substitute with canned sardines for lower cost
Buy day-old baguettes from bakery section for discounts

recipes.name: Luang Prabang Sausage
recipes.description: Laotian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak sausage casings in warm water for 30 minutes until pliable.
Mince garlic, lemongrass, and chilies finely and combine with ground pork, fish sauce, soy sauce, and salt.
Mix the filling thoroughly and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Stuff the casings using a sausage stuffer or makeshift funnel, tying off 4-inch links.
Grill or pan-fry the sausages over medium heat for 15-20 minutes, turning frequently until cooked through.
Serve hot with sticky rice and dipping sauces.
cheapTips: Buy ground pork on sale and freeze until ready to make
Skip casings and form into patties for easier preparation

recipes.name: Tam Maak Hoong
recipes.description: Laotian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound garlic and chilies together in a mortar until fragmented.
Add long beans and tomatoes to the mortar and gently bruise them.
Peel and shred the papaya using a box grater or knife.
Add papaya to the mortar with lime juice, fish sauce, and salt, and toss everything together lightly.
Transfer to a serving bowl, top with crushed peanuts, and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy papaya at discount when slightly unripe from Asian markets
Use crushed peanuts from bulk bins instead of pre-packaged

recipes.name: Khao Kha Moo
recipes.description: Laotian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Crush garlic cloves and fry in a pot with oil until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add the pork leg and brown it on all sides, approximately 10 minutes.
Pour in water, soy sauce, fish sauce, and brown sugar, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 2-3 hours until pork is very tender and falling apart.
Cook jasmine rice separately according to package directions.
Serve rice in bowls, top with pork and generous amounts of the braising liquid, and garnish with cilantro and mustard greens.
cheapTips: Buy pork leg or shank in bulk at discount grocers
Make a larger batch and freeze portions for future meals

recipes.name: Jaew Bong
recipes.description: Laotian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat and brown the ground beef, breaking it apart as it cooks for about 8 minutes.
Mince garlic and chilies finely and add to the cooked beef.
Remove the skillet from heat and stir in lime juice, fish sauce, chopped mint, and green onions.
Serve the beef mixture warm on a platter with lettuce leaves, sticky rice, and additional fresh herbs.
Diners wrap the beef mixture in lettuce leaves to eat.
cheapTips: Buy ground beef on sale and freeze until needed
Use dried mint if fresh is unavailable or expensive

recipes.name: Nam Pla Dip
recipes.description: Laotian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mince garlic and chilies together finely.
Combine fish sauce, lime juice, water, and sugar in a small bowl, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Fold in the minced garlic and chilies.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve with fresh vegetables like cabbage, carrots, and cucumber for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy fish sauce in larger bottles from Asian markets for better value
Use whatever vegetables are on sale or in your fridge

recipes.name: Khao Lam
recipes.description: Laotian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak sticky rice in water for 30 minutes, then drain well.
Mix cooked sticky rice with coconut milk and salt until evenly combined.
Prepare bamboo tubes by cutting them lengthwise or wrap a piece of aluminum foil into a tube shape, then seal one end.
Stuff each tube firmly with the rice mixture until three-quarters full, leaving room for the rice to expand.
Seal the open end with foil or a banana leaf and stand tubes upright in a pot of boiling water for about 45-60 minutes.
Remove carefully and let cool for 5 minutes, then push the rice out of the tube onto a plate and serve.
cheapTips: Use aluminum foil tubes instead of bamboo for easier cleanup and lower cost
Buy coconut milk in bulk from Asian markets

recipes.name: Pad Thai Lao
recipes.description: Laotian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak rice noodles in room temperature water for 30 minutes until pliable, then drain.
Minced garlic and fry in a wok or large skillet over high heat with oil for about 1 minute until fragrant.
Add shrimp or chicken and cook until just done, about 3-4 minutes for shrimp or 5-6 for chicken.
Push the protein to the side and scramble the eggs in the pan, then mix everything together.
Add the softened noodles, tamarind paste, fish sauce, and sugar, then toss continuously for 2-3 minutes until well combined and heated through.
Add bean sprouts and green onions, tossing for another minute.
Serve hot topped with crushed peanuts and a squeeze of fresh lime juice.
cheapTips: Buy tamarind paste in bulk from Asian grocers for significant savings
Use chicken thighs instead of shrimp for lower cost and better flavor

recipes.name: Miang Kham
recipes.description: Laotian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine coconut milk, fish sauce, tamarind paste, and palm sugar in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves, about 2-3 minutes, then set aside to cool slightly.
Mince shallots and roast the dried shrimp in a dry pan for 1 minute until fragrant.
Crush roasted peanuts coarsely and arrange them with coconut flakes, roasted shrimp, and minced shallots in small bowls.
Place betel leaves on a serving platter with the sauce in a bowl and ingredient bowls nearby.
To eat, place a spoonful of each ingredient on a betel leaf, drizzle with sauce, fold it like an envelope, and eat as a whole bite.
cheapTips: Substitute lettuce leaves or cabbage leaves if betel leaves unavailable
Buy dried shrimp in bulk from Asian markets

recipes.name: Kaeng Lueang
recipes.description: Laotian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound garlic, shallots, and turmeric together in a mortar until a smooth paste forms.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and fry the paste for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Add sliced galangal and lemongrass to the pot and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in coconut milk and water, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the fish or shrimp and long beans, simmering for 8-12 minutes until the fish is cooked through and beans are tender.
Season with fish sauce to taste and adjust heat level with additional garlic if desired.
Serve in bowls over or alongside sticky rice.
cheapTips: Use frozen fish fillets instead of fresh for consistent lower pricing
Substitute turmeric for a small amount of curry powder if needed

recipes.name: Shan Noodles
recipes.description: Burmese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook rice noodles according to package directions, drain and set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add ground pork and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Stir in soy sauce and chili flakes, cooking for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a simmer for 5 minutes.
Divide cooked noodles between bowls and pour pork broth mixture over top.
Garnish with sesame seeds, green onions, and a squeeze of lime juice before serving.
cheapTips: Buy ground pork on sale and freeze for later use
Use store-brand soy sauce to reduce cost

recipes.name: Mohinga
recipes.description: Burmese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Mix rice flour with 1/2 cup water to create a smooth paste, then stir into the pot with turmeric.
Add canned fish with its liquid and chicken broth, stirring well to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook rice vermicelli noodles according to package directions and divide into serving bowls.
Ladle the fish broth mixture over the noodles in each bowl.
Top with fried shallots, fresh cilantro, and serve with lime wedges on the side.
cheapTips: Use canned fish instead of fresh for affordability
Make fried shallots at home by frying thin-sliced shallots in oil

recipes.name: Laphet Thoke
recipes.description: Burmese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse fermented tea leaves briefly under cool water and squeeze dry.
In a large bowl, combine shredded cabbage, julienned carrots, and tea leaves.
In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, fish sauce, minced garlic, and chili flakes.
Heat vegetable oil in a small pan and toast sesame seeds for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour dressing over the cabbage mixture and toss well.
Top with crushed peanuts and toasted sesame seeds and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy peanuts in bulk and crush at home
Use regular cabbage instead of specialty greens

recipes.name: Ohn No Khao Swe
recipes.description: Burmese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook egg noodles according to package directions, drain and set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add diced chicken and cook until no longer pink, approximately 5 minutes.
Stir in turmeric and curry powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk and chicken broth, add diced potato, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until potato is tender.
Divide cooked noodles into bowls and ladle curry broth over top, serving with lime wedges on the side.
cheapTips: Buy whole chicken and cut your own breast portions
Use regular curry powder instead of specialty blends

recipes.name: Curry Puff
recipes.description: Burmese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt in a bowl, then add 1/4 cup oil and rub with fingertips until breadcrumb texture forms.
Add warm water gradually until dough comes together, knead briefly, and rest for 20 minutes covered.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a skillet and cook ground pork with garlic, onion, and potato until cooked through, about 8 minutes.
Stir in curry powder and soy sauce, cook 2 minutes more, and let filling cool slightly.
Divide dough into 8 equal pieces and roll each thin between plastic wrap.
Place 2 tbsp filling on one half of each dough circle, fold over, and crimp edges with a fork.
Heat remaining oil in a deep skillet and fry curry puffs until golden brown on both sides, about 3 minutes per side, then drain on paper towels.
cheapTips: Make dough at home instead of buying pre-made pastry
Use ground pork instead of more expensive meat fillings

recipes.name: Samusa
recipes.description: Burmese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Make dough by combining flour, salt, 2 tbsp oil, and warm water, knead until smooth, and rest covered for 20 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a skillet and cook diced potato with onion and garlic over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add peas, curry powder, and turmeric, cooking until potato is tender, about 5 more minutes, then cool completely.
Divide dough into 6 equal pieces and roll each thin between plastic wrap.
Cut dough circles in half and fold each half into a cone shape, sealing with water.
Fill each cone with 2 tbsp potato mixture and seal the top edge by pinching.
Heat remaining oil in a deep skillet to medium-high and fry samusas until golden brown, about 3 minutes per side, then drain on paper towels.
cheapTips: Use frozen peas instead of fresh for lower cost
Make large batches and freeze unbaked samusas for later

recipes.name: Tea Leaf Salad
recipes.description: Burmese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse fermented tea leaves under cool water to remove excess brine and gently squeeze dry.
In a large bowl, combine mixed greens, chopped tomato, and diced cucumber.
In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, fish sauce, minced garlic, and chili flakes.
Heat vegetable oil in a small pan and lightly toast sesame seeds for 1 minute.
Add fermented tea leaves to the greens mixture and toss gently.
Drizzle with lime dressing and toss to coat evenly.
Top with crushed peanuts and toasted sesame seeds and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy pre-packaged mixed greens on sale
Crush your own peanuts from bulk peanuts

recipes.name: Mandalay Shan Noodles
recipes.description: Burmese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook rice noodles according to package directions, drain and set aside.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok or large skillet and fry sliced shallots until crispy and golden, about 5 minutes, then set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok and sauté minced garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add ground pork and cook over high heat, breaking it up as it cooks, until browned and cooked through, about 6 minutes.
Stir in soy sauce, fish sauce, sesame seeds, and chili flakes, cooking for 1 minute.
Divide cooked noodles between bowls and top with pork mixture.
Garnish with crispy fried shallots, crushed peanuts, and a squeeze of lime juice before serving.
cheapTips: Buy shallots on sale and store in cool, dry place
Toast your own sesame seeds instead of buying pre-toasted

recipes.name: Ngapi Kyaw
recipes.description: Burmese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat and add thinly sliced shallots.
Fry shallots until golden and crispy, about 5 minutes, and remove with a slotted spoon, reserving oil in pan.
Add minced garlic to remaining oil and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add shrimp paste and cook, breaking it up and stirring constantly, for 3 minutes.
Stir in chili flakes, lime juice, sugar, and fish sauce, cooking for 1 minute.
Transfer ngapi kyaw to a serving bowl and top with crispy fried shallots and fresh cilantro.
Serve warm as a dip with crackers, rice, or vegetables.
cheapTips: Buy shrimp paste in bulk from Asian markets
Make extra and store in refrigerator for up to 2 weeks

recipes.name: Burmese Fish Curry
recipes.description: Burmese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut fish fillets into 2-inch chunks and season lightly with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion, garlic, and ginger until softened, about 4 minutes.
Stir in turmeric and curry powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, stirring constantly.
Add canned tomatoes with juice and fish broth, bringing to a simmer.
Add diced potato and cook for 10 minutes until potatoes are partially tender.
Gently add fish chunks to the curry and simmer for 10 minutes until fish is cooked through and flakes easily.
Taste and adjust seasonings as needed, then serve hot garnished with fresh cilantro over steamed rice.
cheapTips: Buy fish on sale and freeze for later use
Use tilapia instead of more expensive fish varieties

recipes.name: Chicken Coconut Curry
recipes.description: Burmese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice the onion, mince the garlic, and cut chicken into 1-inch cubes.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Stir in curry powder and cook for 1 minute until it releases its aroma.
Add the chicken pieces and brown them on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and water, then add fish sauce and diced potatoes.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 25-30 minutes until potatoes are tender and chicken is cooked through.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more fish sauce if needed.
Serve hot over steamed rice.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs instead of breast for better flavor at lower cost
Use regular curry powder from the bulk section rather than specialty brands

recipes.name: Beef Curry
recipes.description: Burmese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut beef into 1.5-inch cubes and dice onions; mince garlic and ginger.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown beef in batches, about 8 minutes total.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Stir in curry powder and turmeric, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomato paste and mix well to coat the beef.
Pour in beef broth and fish sauce, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes until beef is very tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning, then serve over rice.
cheapTips: Use beef chuck which becomes tender with slow cooking and costs less than premium cuts
Make your own curry powder blend from individual spices if buying frequently

recipes.name: Sago Pudding
recipes.description: Burmese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring 3 cups of water to a boil in a large pot.
Slowly add sago pearls while stirring to prevent clumping.
Cook for 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until pearls become translucent.
Add coconut milk, palm sugar, and salt; stir well.
Simmer for 5 minutes until sugar dissolves and mixture thickens slightly.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla extract and pandan extract if using.
Pour into serving bowls and serve warm or chilled.
cheapTips: Sago pearls are very inexpensive when bought in bulk from Asian markets
Omit pandan extract if unavailable; the pudding is delicious without it

recipes.name: Mont Lin Ma Yar
recipes.description: Burmese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix rice flour, salt, and 0.5 cup of the coconut milk in a bowl to create a thick paste.
Heat oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls of the rice mixture and flatten them into discs about 2.5 inches wide.
Cook until golden on both sides, about 4 minutes per side, then transfer to a plate.
In a saucepan, heat remaining coconut milk with water and jaggery, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Slice the banana into thin rounds.
Arrange cooked rice cakes on a serving plate, top with banana slices, and drizzle with the jaggery sauce.
Sprinkle sesame seeds on top and serve warm.
cheapTips: Use brown sugar instead of jaggery if you cannot find it locally
Buy rice flour in bulk from Asian markets for significant savings

recipes.name: Jaggery Pancake
recipes.description: Burmese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, beat egg and mix with milk and 1 tablespoon melted butter.
Combine wet and dry ingredients, stirring until just combined with some lumps remaining.
Heat 1 tablespoon butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook pancakes until golden on both sides, about 3 minutes per side.
In a saucepan, dissolve jaggery with coconut milk over medium heat, stirring constantly until syrupy, about 5 minutes.
Stack cooked pancakes on a plate and drizzle generously with jaggery syrup.
Serve warm.
cheapTips: Use store-brand flour and sugar to reduce costs
Make a double batch and freeze extras for quick breakfasts later

recipes.name: Burmese Tofu
recipes.description: Burmese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix chickpea flour with 1 cup water to form a smooth paste, then add remaining 3 cups water gradually while stirring.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into a large pot to remove lumps.
Add salt and turmeric to the strained mixture and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Stir constantly for 15-20 minutes as the mixture thickens significantly and becomes creamy.
When very thick, pour into an oiled 8x8 inch baking dish and smooth the top.
Cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour until firm.
Cut into cubes or rectangles and serve at room temperature with a side of sautéed onions, garlic, ginger, and chili powder.
Alternatively, pan-fry the pieces until golden on both sides.
cheapTips: Buy chickpea flour from bulk bins at Asian markets for significant savings
Make a large batch and freeze for multiple meals throughout the month

recipes.name: Fried Tofu
recipes.description: Burmese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Wrap tofu block in paper towels and press between two plates for 10 minutes to remove excess moisture.
Cut pressed tofu into 1-inch cubes.
Mix cornstarch, flour, salt, pepper, and garlic powder in a shallow bowl.
Coat each tofu cube evenly in the flour mixture.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep skillet or pot.
Carefully add tofu cubes in batches and fry for 3-4 minutes per batch until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with sweet chili sauce or soy sauce.
cheapTips: Buy tofu from the bulk section rather than pre-packaged when available
Reuse frying oil multiple times to reduce costs

recipes.name: Spring Roll
recipes.description: Burmese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.

ingredients.note: 2 tbsp for filling + 1 cup for frying

steps: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a skillet and cook ground pork over medium-high heat until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add shredded cabbage, diced carrot, soy sauce, and fish sauce; stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Remove from heat and stir in sliced green onion, then cool the filling completely.
Place a spring roll wrapper on a flat surface with one corner pointing toward you.
Add 2 tablespoons of filling in the center, fold the bottom corner over filling, fold in the sides, then roll tightly to the top corner.
Heat 1 cup oil to 350°F and fry spring rolls in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve with sweet chili sauce or peanut sauce.
cheapTips: Buy spring roll wrappers from Asian markets which cost less than specialty shops
Use ground chicken instead of pork for a more economical option

recipes.name: Shan Rice
recipes.description: Burmese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: If using raw rice, cook 1 cup rice according to package directions and spread on a plate to cool completely.
Slice shallots thinly and set aside 0.5 cup for garnish.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and fry remaining shallots until golden and crispy, about 5 minutes; transfer to a paper towel.
In the same skillet, brown ground pork, breaking it into small pieces, about 6 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in cooked rice, fish sauce, lime juice, and chili flakes; toss everything together for 3-4 minutes until heated through.
Transfer to a serving plate and top with crispy shallots and fresh cilantro.
Serve hot.
cheapTips: Use leftover cooked rice to save time and reduce food waste
Buy garlic and shallots at farmers markets where they are often cheaper

recipes.name: Burmese Sticky Rice
recipes.description: Burmese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse sticky rice under cold water 2-3 times until water runs clear.
Add rice and 2.5 cups water to a pot, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and cook for 15 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Heat coconut milk with salt and palm sugar in a saucepan, stirring until sugar dissolves completely, about 3 minutes.
Pour the coconut mixture into the cooked rice and stir gently to combine evenly.
Let sit covered for 5 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with toasted sesame seeds.
Serve warm as a side dish to curries or soups.
cheapTips: Buy sticky rice in bulk from Asian markets where it is significantly cheaper
Toast sesame seeds yourself in a dry skillet to save money versus pre-toasted

recipes.name: Num Pang
recipes.description: Cambodian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice the baguette lengthwise and lightly toast both halves.
Spread peanut butter on one half and butter or mayo on the other.
Layer pickled vegetables, cucumber slices, and fresh cilantro on the peanut butter side.
Drizzle sriracha over the filling and close the sandwich.
Cut in half and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy peanut butter in bulk and make your own pickled vegetables
Use day-old baguettes from the bakery for discounts

recipes.name: Fried Tarantula
recipes.description: Cambodian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean the tarantulas thoroughly and remove the fangs and hair.
Heat oil in a wok or deep pan to 350°F.
Mix salt, garlic, pepper, and fish sauce in a small bowl.
Carefully place tarantulas in hot oil and fry for 3-4 minutes until crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Toss with the garlic-salt mixture and squeeze fresh lime over top.
Serve warm as a crispy snack.
cheapTips: Source tarantulas from specialty Asian markets or online suppliers
Buy in bulk with friends to reduce per-unit cost

recipes.name: Grilled Fish Amok
recipes.description: Cambodian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix coconut milk, red curry paste, fish sauce, and egg in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in kaffir lime leaves and set aside.
Place each fish fillet on a banana leaf or parchment square.
Divide the coconut curry mixture evenly over the three fillets.
Fold the banana leaf or parchment into a packet and secure with toothpicks.
Grill packets over medium heat for 12-15 minutes until fish flakes easily.
Carefully open packets and serve over jasmine rice with the curry sauce.
cheapTips: Use frozen fish fillets instead of fresh to save 30-40%
Make your own curry paste or buy budget brands

recipes.name: Skewered Meat Satay
recipes.description: Cambodian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk together peanut butter, coconut milk, soy sauce, garlic, lime juice, brown sugar, and red pepper flakes for the sauce.
