Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pot and fry the chili paste for 3 minutes over medium heat until fragrant.
Add fish stock and tamarind liquid to the pot and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce and taste; adjust seasoning as needed.
Cook rice noodles in salted boiling water according to package directions and drain.
Place noodles in bowls and flake fish over top, then pour hot broth over everything.
Garnish with sliced cucumber, red onion, and fresh mint, then serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use canned mackerel instead of fresh fish—cheaper and just as good
Make your own tamarind paste from concentrate rather than pre-made

recipes.name: Popia
recipes.description: Chinese-Malay snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat and stir-fry garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add ground meat and cook for 3 minutes, breaking it apart until fully cooked and no pink remains.
Add shredded cabbage and carrots, then stir-fry for 3 minutes until vegetables soften slightly.
Pour in soy sauce and sesame oil, toss everything together, and season with salt and pepper; let cool for 5 minutes.
Place 2 tbsp filling on each spring roll wrapper near one corner, then roll tightly, tucking in sides as you go.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and shallow-fry rolls in batches for 2 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Drain fried popia on paper towels.
Serve warm with sweet chili sauce for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy spring roll wrappers at Asian markets instead of regular grocery stores—much cheaper
Use chicken thighs instead of pork—often on sale and more flavorful

recipes.name: Kuih Lapis
recipes.description: Malay snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix tapioca flour, rice flour, and salt in a large bowl.
Heat coconut milk with sugar until sugar dissolves completely, then add oil and remove from heat.
Divide the coconut mixture into three bowls and tint one green, one blue/pink, and leave one white.
Mix each colored mixture separately into one-third of the flour mixture until smooth, adding water as needed to achieve a thick batter consistency.
Pour the white layer first into a greased 8x8 inch baking pan and steam for 5 minutes until set.
Pour the green layer over white, steam for 5 minutes until set, repeat with colored layer.
Continue layering colors and steaming until all batter is used, creating distinct colored layers.
Cool completely, then cut into diamond or square shapes and serve at room temperature.
cheapTips: Skip food coloring—kuih lapis is delicious plain or naturally tinted
Use regular flour if tapioca is unavailable; texture differs but still tasty

recipes.name: Kuih Muih
recipes.description: Malay snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring water and palm sugar to a boil in a small pot, then remove from heat and let cool—this is your palm sugar syrup.
Mix glutinous rice flour, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Heat coconut milk until warm, then pour into flour mixture gradually while stirring until you form a smooth, soft dough.
If using pandan leaves, pound them and squeeze juice into the dough for color and flavor; if using extract, add directly.
Knead dough for 2 minutes until smooth, adding small amounts of water if too dry.
Roll dough into small balls about 1 inch diameter, then flatten slightly.
Boil salted water in a pot and drop dough balls in batches; they will float to the surface when cooked through.
Drain cooked kuih in a colander, toss gently with grated coconut and a drizzle of oil, then serve warm with palm sugar syrup for dipping.
cheapTips: Use pandan extract instead of fresh leaves—lasts longer and costs less
Skip fresh grated coconut and use frozen from Asian markets

recipes.name: Cendol
recipes.description: Malay snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat water and palm sugar in a small pot over low heat, stirring until sugar fully dissolves, then remove from heat and let cool completely.
If using fresh cendol noodles, cook in boiling water for 1-2 minutes and drain; if frozen, thaw under cold water.
Pour coconut milk into a separate container and stir in salt.
Fill four tall glasses halfway with shaved ice.
Divide cendol noodles equally among the glasses.
Pour cooled palm sugar syrup over the noodles and ice in each glass.
Top each glass with a generous pour of coconut milk and stir gently before serving.
Serve immediately while ice is still cold.
cheapTips: Buy cendol noodles frozen in bulk from Asian markets
Make your own shaved ice from water and a blender instead of buying pre-made

recipes.name: Ketupat
recipes.description: Malay lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse glutinous rice thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear.
Mix coconut milk with 3 cups water and salt in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Add rinsed rice, ginger, and garlic to the pot and stir well.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer covered for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice is nearly cooked and liquid is mostly absorbed.
Cut palm leaves or foil into 4 inch squares and fold into cone or diamond shapes.
Spoon cooked rice mixture into each palm leaf pouch until three-quarters full, then fold leaf closed and secure with toothpick if needed.
Place wrapped ketupat in a pot of boiling water and boil for 45 minutes until rice is completely cooked and very firm.
Remove from water, cool slightly, unwrap carefully, and serve warm or at room temperature with curry or sambal.
cheapTips: Use aluminum foil instead of palm leaves—easier to find and just as effective
Buy glutinous rice in bulk at Asian markets for half the price

recipes.name: Putu Mayam
recipes.description: Indian-Malay breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix rice flour, tapioca flour, salt, and turmeric in a large bowl.
Heat water to boiling, then pour into flour mixture while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Stir in 1 tbsp coconut oil until batter is smooth and pourable, similar to pancake batter.
Prepare a bamboo putu mayam maker (or use a ricer) by lightly oiling it with remaining coconut oil.
Press batter through the maker onto banana leaves or plastic wrap in coiled strands about 3-4 inches in diameter.
Sprinkle each coil lightly with grated coconut and small pieces of jaggery.
Carefully place on a steaming rack over boiling water and steam for 5-7 minutes until cooked through and firm.
Serve warm as-is or with curry sauce and extra grated coconut.
cheapTips: Use a potato ricer instead of a putu mayam maker—works just as well and costs less
Buy grated coconut frozen from Asian markets instead of fresh

recipes.name: Bak Kut Teh
recipes.description: Chinese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blanch pork ribs in boiling water for 2 minutes, drain, rinse under cold water, and set aside.
Soak dried mushrooms in 1/2 cup hot water for 10 minutes until softened, then reserve soaking liquid and chop mushrooms.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and fry crushed garlic cloves and ginger slices for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add cinnamon stick, star anise, and cloves to the pot and toast for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Pour in 8 cups water along with the reserved mushroom soaking liquid, then add the blanched ribs.
Bring to a boil, then add soy sauce, dark soy sauce, fish sauce, and chopped mushrooms.
Reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 1 to 1.5 hours until ribs are very tender and flavorful.
Taste and adjust seasoning with soy sauce or fish sauce as needed, then serve hot in bowls with the flavorful broth.
cheapTips: Buy pork spare ribs on sale and freeze—no difference in final dish quality
Skip dried shiitake and use cheaper dried mushrooms or fresh button mushrooms

recipes.name: Cemita Poblana
recipes.description: Pueblan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blend chipotle peppers with mayo, cilantro, and lime juice to make the spread.
Slice each cemita roll in half horizontally and lightly toast if desired.
Spread chipotle mayo on both sides of each roll.
Layer turkey, cheese, avocado slices, and thin onion rings on the bottom half.
Top with the other half of the roll and serve immediately.
Cut in half diagonally if desired and serve with napkins.
cheapTips: Use regular deli turkey instead of specialty meats
Substitute with part-skim mozzarella to reduce cost

recipes.name: Pipián Poblano
recipes.description: Pueblan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil chicken with half the onion and salt until fully cooked, about 20 minutes.
Toast poblano peppers directly over flame until charred, place in plastic bag for 5 minutes, then peel off skin.
Blend pepitas, roasted poblanos, garlic, cilantro, and 1 cup broth until smooth.
Heat oil in large pot and sauté remaining onion until softened.
Pour in seed mixture and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add remaining broth and shredded chicken, simmer for 10 minutes.
Finish with lime juice, salt, and pepper to taste.
Serve hot with rice or warm tortillas.
cheapTips: Buy pepitas in bulk from bulk bins
Use chicken thighs instead of breasts for richer flavor at lower cost

recipes.name: Chalupas Poblanas
recipes.description: Pueblan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in deep skillet to 350°F over medium-high heat.
Fry each tortilla for 1-2 minutes per side until golden and crispy, drain on paper towels.
Mix shredded chicken with salsa verde and warm through in a pot.
Spread refried beans onto each fried tortilla base.
Top with warm chicken mixture and sour cream.
Add shredded cabbage and crumbled queso fresco.
Squeeze fresh lime over top and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use rotisserie chicken to skip cooking time
Make salsa verde from canned tomatillos instead of fresh

recipes.name: Barbacoa Poblana
recipes.description: Pueblan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried guajillo and ancho peppers in hot water for 15 minutes, then drain.
Blend soaked peppers with garlic, vinegar, cumin, salt, and pepper into smooth paste.
Rub pepper paste all over beef chuck roast on all sides.
Place roast in slow cooker with onion, bay leaves, and beef broth.
Cook on low for 8-10 hours until meat shreds easily with a fork.
Remove bay leaves and shred meat directly in slow cooker with two forks.
Strain cooking liquid and return to slow cooker with shredded meat, simmer 15 minutes.
Serve with warm tortillas, lime, and pickled onions.
cheapTips: Use beef chuck roast when on sale and freeze until needed
Make large batch and freeze portions for later meals

recipes.name: Poblano en Escabeche
recipes.description: Pueblan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Roast poblano peppers directly over flame until completely charred.
Place charred peppers in plastic bag for 5 minutes to steam, then peel off blackened skin.
Slice peeled peppers into strips, removing seeds.
Slice carrots into thin sticks and onion into rings.
Heat olive oil in pot, add garlic and onion, cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add vinegar, water, bay leaves, oregano, salt, and pepper; bring to boil.
Add carrot sticks and cook for 5 minutes.
Layer poblano strips and cooked vegetables in jars or bowl, pour hot vinegar mixture over top.
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.
cheapTips: Make large batch to keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks
Use budget-friendly carrots and onions from discount stores

recipes.name: Manchamanteles
recipes.description: Pueblan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork shoulder into 2-inch cubes and brown in oil over medium-high heat for 5 minutes per side.
Remove pork and set aside, reserving drippings in pot.
Soak dried ancho and pasilla peppers in hot water for 15 minutes, drain.
Blend soaked peppers with garlic, onion, tomato, and 1 cup broth until smooth.
Strain sauce through fine sieve back into pot with reserved drippings.
Cook sauce for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add browned pork, remaining broth, pineapple chunks, and diced apple.
Simmer covered for 30-35 minutes until pork is tender, stirring occasionally.
Taste and adjust seasonings with salt and pepper, serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder on sale and freeze in portions
Use canned pineapple chunks to reduce costs

recipes.name: Mole Rojo
recipes.description: Pueblan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil chicken breasts in 2 cups broth with half the onion for 20 minutes until cooked, reserve broth.
Toast dried ancho and guajillo peppers in dry skillet for 1 minute per side.
Soak toasted peppers in hot water for 15 minutes, then drain.
Blend soaked peppers with tomatoes, garlic, almonds, remaining onion, and 1 cup broth until completely smooth.
Strain sauce through fine sieve, pressing solids with spoon.
Heat oil in large pot, add strained sauce and cook for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add reserved chicken broth and remaining 1 cup fresh broth, bring to simmer.
Add shredded chicken and simmer 10 minutes, season with salt and pepper.
Serve with rice and warm corn tortillas.
cheapTips: Buy almonds from bulk section instead of packaged
Use chicken thighs instead of breasts for lower cost

recipes.name: Dulce de Camote
recipes.description: Pueblan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and cut sweet potatoes into 1-inch cubes.
Bring water to boil in large pot, add sweet potatoes and cook for 15 minutes until tender.
Drain potatoes and return to pot over medium heat.
Add brown sugar, butter, cinnamon, cloves, and salt.
Mash or blend to your desired consistency, stirring frequently for 10 minutes.
Add vanilla extract and stir until combined.
Transfer to serving dish or cut into blocks once cooled.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Buy sweet potatoes when on sale and store in cool place
Use store-brand brown sugar and spices

recipes.name: Alegrías
recipes.description: Pueblan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: If using unpoppped amaranth, pop in dry skillet over medium heat for 2-3 minutes per batch, shaking frequently, until seeds pop.
Toast sesame seeds in dry skillet for 2 minutes until fragrant, set aside.
Combine piloncillo, honey, and butter in saucepan over medium heat, stirring until melted.
Cook sugar mixture for 3-4 minutes until it reaches soft-ball stage (240°F on candy thermometer).
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla and salt.
Quickly add popped amaranth and sesame seeds, stirring until coated.
Spread mixture on parchment paper and cool for 10 minutes until set.
Cut into squares or break into pieces and store in airtight container.
cheapTips: Buy amaranth seeds in bulk from health food stores
Use honey from discount stores or local beekeepers

recipes.name: Pepitorias de Pollo
recipes.description: Pueblan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut chicken breasts into bite-sized pieces and season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in large skillet over medium-high heat and brown chicken pieces for 4-5 minutes, set aside.
In same skillet, sauté diced onion and garlic until softened, about 2 minutes.
Blend pepitas, serrano peppers, tomatillos, cilantro, and broth until smooth.
Pour seed mixture into skillet and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Return chicken to skillet and add remaining broth, simmer for 15-20 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Taste and adjust seasonings with salt and pepper.
Serve hot with rice or warm tortillas.
cheapTips: Buy pepitas from bulk section in large quantities
Use chicken thighs instead of breasts for more flavor and lower cost

recipes.name: Kueh Lapis
recipes.description: Peranakan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease an 8x8 inch baking pan with butter.
In a blender, combine coconut milk, eggs, sugar, and vanilla extract, blending until smooth.
Add flour, cornstarch, and salt to the wet mixture and blend until no lumps remain.
Divide batter into separate bowls and tint each with different food coloring.
Pour the first colored layer into the baking pan and bake for 5-7 minutes until set but not browned.
Pour the next colored layer on top and bake another 5-7 minutes, repeating with remaining colors until all batter is used and layers are built.
After the final layer is set, bake the entire cake for 10 more minutes until firm.
Cool completely in the pan, then cut into squares and serve.
cheapTips: Use basic food coloring from the dollar store
Make with condensed coconut milk instead of fresh to save money

recipes.name: Hokkien Mee
recipes.description: Chinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add diced pork and stir-fry until cooked through, about 4 minutes.
Add shrimp to the wok and cook until pink and curled, about 3 minutes.
Push all ingredients to the side and add remaining oil, then toss in the fresh noodles and break them apart while cooking for 2 minutes.
Add shredded cabbage and stir-fry with the noodles for another 2 minutes.
Pour in both soy sauces and chicken broth, tossing everything together until the liquid is mostly absorbed, about 3 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more soy sauce if needed.
Serve immediately in bowls with lime wedges on the side.
cheapTips: Substitute pork with chicken breast for lower cost
Use frozen shrimp instead of fresh to save 30-40%

recipes.name: Rendang
recipes.description: Malay lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blend shallots, garlic, ginger, red chilies, and lemongrass into a smooth paste using a food processor or blender.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and fry the paste for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the cubed beef and stir-fry until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and add turmeric, galangal, and salt, stirring well to combine.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered for 40-45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender and the sauce has reduced and thickened.
The rendang is ready when the oil begins to separate from the coconut cream and the sauce coats the meat.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt if needed.
Serve hot with steamed rice.
cheapTips: Buy beef chuck instead of premium cuts for rendang
Use canned coconut milk and freeze paste in ice cube trays for future use

recipes.name: Otah
recipes.description: Malay snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blanch banana leaves briefly in hot water to soften them, then set aside to cool.
In a mixing bowl, combine flaked fish, minced shallots, garlic, and red chili.
Add fish paste, egg, cornstarch, coconut milk, salt, and white pepper, mixing until the mixture is well combined.
Place a spoonful of the fish mixture onto each banana leaf and fold the leaf to encase the filling.
Preheat oven to 400°F and place the wrapped otah parcels on a baking sheet.
Bake for 15-20 minutes until the filling is cooked through and edges of banana leaves are slightly charred.
Alternatively, grill the packets for 10-12 minutes, turning halfway through.
Let cool slightly and serve warm.
cheapTips: Use frozen fish fillets which are cheaper than fresh mackerel
Substitute banana leaves with parchment paper or foil to eliminate that cost

recipes.name: Black Pepper Crab
recipes.description: Chinese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse crabs thoroughly and cut each into quarters or chunks, leaving shells on.
Toast black peppercorns in a dry skillet for 1 minute, then coarsely crush them using a mortar and pestle.
Heat oil and butter in a large wok or skillet over high heat until very hot.
Add crab pieces and stir-fry for 3 minutes until the shells turn red.
Add minced garlic and sliced shallots, stir-frying for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle the crushed black pepper over the crabs and stir well.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, and chicken broth, then cover and cook on high heat for 5-7 minutes until crabs are cooked through and sauce slightly reduces.
Taste and adjust seasoning, then top with chopped green onions and serve immediately with steamed rice.
cheapTips: Buy pre-cut crab pieces if available to save on prep time and cost
Use blue crabs instead of larger varieties for budget-friendly options

recipes.name: Rojak
recipes.description: Peranakan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a skillet and fry the tofu cubes until golden on all sides, then drain on paper towels.
In the same skillet, fry shrimp until pink and cooked through, about 3 minutes, then remove.
In a mortar and pestle or small food processor, grind peanuts, red chilies, garlic, palm sugar, and salt into a coarse paste.
Transfer the peanut paste to a bowl and mix in tamarind paste until well combined.
In a large mixing bowl, combine tofu, shrimp, cucumber, pineapple, and bean sprouts.
Pour the peanut sauce over the mixture and toss gently to coat everything evenly.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more tamarind paste for tanginess or palm sugar for sweetness.
Serve immediately at room temperature or slightly chilled.
cheapTips: Use canned pineapple to cut down on costs
Substitute shrimp with extra tofu for a vegetarian and cheaper version

recipes.name: Poc Chuc
recipes.description: Yucatecan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a bowl, whisk together fresh orange juice, lime juice, minced garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Place pork steaks in a shallow dish and pour the citrus marinade over them, making sure they are well covered.
Marinate the pork for at least 2 hours in the refrigerator, or up to 8 hours for deeper flavor.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until hot.
Remove pork from marinade and pat dry with paper towels, reserving the marinade.
Cook pork steaks for 5-6 minutes on each side until cooked through and slightly caramelized.
Pour the reserved marinade into the skillet and add sliced red onion, simmering for 3-4 minutes.
Serve the pork with the pan sauce and pickled red onions on the side, accompanied by warm tortillas.
cheapTips: Buy citrus fruits when on sale and freeze the juice for later use
Pork shoulder is an affordable cut compared to other steaks

recipes.name: Papadzules
recipes.description: Yucatecan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Hard-boil eggs in water for 10 minutes, then cool, peel, and chop them into small pieces.
Toast pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until fragrant, then transfer to a food processor.
Add minced garlic, jalapeño if using, and vegetable broth to the pumpkin seeds and blend into a smooth sauce.
Heat oil in a skillet and fry the pumpkin seed sauce for 2 minutes, then season with salt and white pepper.
In a separate pot, warm the tomato sauce over low heat.
Warm the tortillas briefly on a skillet or open flame to make them pliable.
Place chopped eggs in the center of each tortilla, roll tightly, and arrange seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour the pumpkin seed sauce over the rolled tortillas, then drizzle tomato sauce on top and serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy raw pumpkin seeds in bulk from the bulk bin section
Use store-brand tomato sauce and eggs from the sale rack

recipes.name: Sopa de Lima
recipes.description: Yucatecan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion, minced garlic, and diced tomato for 3 minutes until softened.
Add chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Add whole chicken breast and reduce heat to medium, simmering for 15 minutes until cooked through.
Remove chicken breast from the broth and shred it using two forks, then return to the pot.
Stir in fresh lime juice and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer for 3-4 more minutes to allow flavors to blend.
To serve, ladle the hot soup into bowls and top each with fried tortilla strips and fresh cilantro.
Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side for extra acidity if desired.
cheapTips: Make your own tortilla strips by frying cut tortillas in oil instead of buying pre-made
Buy chicken when on sale and freeze until needed

recipes.name: Relleno Negro
recipes.description: Yucatecan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a large pot, heat oil over medium-high heat and brown chicken pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, cook black recado paste for 2 minutes until fragrant, stirring constantly.
Add red recado paste and stir for another minute.
Return chicken to the pot and pour in chicken broth, then bring to a simmer and cook covered for 30 minutes until chicken is tender.
Remove chicken from the broth and shred the meat, discarding bones and skin.
Chop hard-boiled eggs and combine with olives and raisins to create the filling.
Return shredded chicken to the pot along with tomato sauce and the egg-olive-raisin mixture, stirring gently to combine.
Simmer for 10 more minutes to blend flavors, then season with salt and pepper and serve with rice.
cheapTips: Make black and red recado pastes in bulk and freeze in portions for future recipes
Use chicken thighs instead of breasts as they are cheaper and more flavorful

recipes.name: Mozzarella in Carrozza
recipes.description: Neapolitan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut mozzarella into 4 equal slices and place between bread slices, trimming crusts.
Beat eggs in a shallow bowl and place flour and breadcrumbs in separate bowls.
Coat each sandwich in flour, then dip in beaten egg, then coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pan or use a thermometer to check temperature.
Fry sandwiches 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately while cheese is still warm and melted.
cheapTips: Use regular mozzarella instead of fresh for 50% savings
Buy day-old bread at discount

recipes.name: Arancini Napoletani
recipes.description: Neapolitan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat broth in a pot and keep warm on low heat throughout cooking.
Sauté diced onion in butter until softened, add rice and stir for 2 minutes.
Add warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring frequently until rice is creamy and cooked, about 18 minutes.
Stir in parmesan, season with salt and pepper, then spread on a plate to cool completely.
Beat eggs and cut mozzarella into small cubes.
Form golf-ball sized portions of rice around a cube of mozzarella, roll in egg then breadcrumbs.
Heat oil to 350°F and fry arancini 3-4 minutes until golden, turning gently.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
cheapTips: Make risotto a day ahead to save time
Use regular mozzarella instead of fresh

recipes.name: Sfogliatella
recipes.description: Neapolitan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast semolina in a dry skillet over medium heat for 5 minutes until lightly golden, then cool.
Mix ricotta, sugar, egg, candied peel, and chocolate chips in a bowl, then fold in cooled semolina.
Layer 2 phyllo sheets, brush each with melted butter, then place 2 tablespoons filling on short end.
Roll tightly like a burrito, folding in sides, then curl into a crescent shape.
Brush exterior with butter and place on parchment-lined baking sheet.
Bake at 375°F for 25-30 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Remove from oven and dust generously with powdered sugar while still warm.
Cool for 5 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Phyllo dough is cheaper than puff pastry
Skip candied peel and use raisins instead

recipes.name: Babà
recipes.description: Neapolitan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition, then add warm water.
Knead dough for 10 minutes, then gradually work in softened butter until incorporated.
Divide dough among 4 greased babà molds or ramekins and let rise 1 hour until doubled.
Bake at 375°F for 20-25 minutes until golden brown, then cool slightly.
Prepare syrup by mixing simple syrup with rum in a shallow bowl.
Dip warm babà into syrup for 10-15 seconds per side until saturated.
Place on a plate and serve at room temperature.
cheapTips: Use store-bought simple syrup to save time
Make without rum for a non-alcoholic version

recipes.name: Pastiera Napoletana
recipes.description: Neapolitan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Make pastry by mixing flour, salt, sugar, and cold butter until crumbly, then add 2 egg yolks and 2 tablespoons water until dough forms.
Wrap dough and chill 30 minutes, then press into a 9-inch springform pan.
Beat remaining eggs with sugar until pale, fold in ricotta, wheat berries, candied fruit, orange zest, and vanilla.
Pour filling into crust and bake at 350°F for 50-60 minutes until set but still slightly jiggly in center.
Cool completely in pan, then refrigerate at least 4 hours before serving.
cheapTips: Buy wheat berries in bulk bins
Use regular candied citrus peel instead of specialty candied fruit

recipes.name: Struffoli
recipes.description: Neapolitan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt, make well, add eggs, butter, and liqueur, knead until smooth dough forms.
Roll dough into thin log and cut into small pea-sized pieces.
Heat oil to 350°F and fry dough pieces in batches 2-3 minutes until golden, stirring often.
Drain on paper towels completely.
Heat honey and sugar in a large pot until melted and combined.
Add fried dough pieces and candied peel, toss gently to coat evenly.
Form into a mound on a serving plate while warm and sticky.
Serve at room temperature.
cheapTips: Skip the aniseed liqueur and use a pinch of anise extract instead
Use regular sugar syrup instead of honey

recipes.name: Calzone
recipes.description: Neapolitan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Let pizza dough come to room temperature for 30 minutes.
Mix ricotta, mozzarella, egg, parmesan, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Chop prosciutto and spinach, fold into cheese mixture.
Divide dough in half and stretch each into a 10-inch circle on a floured surface.
Spread filling on one half of each circle, leaving 1-inch border.
Fold dough over filling and press edges firmly to seal, then crimp with a fork.
Place on parchment-lined baking sheet, brush with olive oil, and bake at 400°F for 25-30 minutes until golden.
Cool 5 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Use store-bought dough to save 30 minutes
Substitute pancetta for prosciutto for savings

recipes.name: Spaghetti alle Vongole Veraci
recipes.description: Neapolitan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Scrub clams under cold running water and discard any that don't close.
Bring large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti until al dente.
Meanwhile, slice garlic thinly and heat olive oil in large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and red pepper flakes, cook 1-2 minutes until fragrant but not browned.
Add clams and white wine, cover, and steam 6-8 minutes until clams open, discarding any that don't.
Reserve 1 cup pasta water before draining spaghetti.
Add drained spaghetti to clam sauce, toss well, adding pasta water as needed for silky consistency.
Garnish with chopped parsley and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy clams on sale and freeze for later
Use canned clams for a budget option

recipes.name: Cuoppo
recipes.description: Neapolitan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, salt, yeast, and water to form a smooth, sticky batter.
Let batter rest 20 minutes at room temperature.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pan or use a thermometer.
Spoon batter into hot oil in small portions, frying 2-3 minutes per side until puffed and golden.
Drain fried dough on paper towels.
While warm, top with small mozzarella pieces and spoon marinara sauce over.
Serve warm, torn into pieces and eaten by hand.
cheapTips: Use jarred marinara sauce
Top with cooked vegetables instead of mozzarella to save money

recipes.name: Impepata di Cozze
recipes.description: Neapolitan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean mussels under cold water, removing beards and discarding any cracked or open shells.
Slice garlic thinly and heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and black pepper, cook 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add mussels and white wine, cover pot, and steam 5-7 minutes until mussels open.
Discard any mussels that didn't open.
Remove from heat, squeeze lemon juice over mussels, and scatter parsley on top.
Serve immediately in bowls with cooking broth and crusty bread for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy mussels on sale and use within 1-2 days
Skip the wine and use broth instead

recipes.name: Trippa alla Fiorentina
recipes.description: Tuscan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blanch the tripe in salted boiling water for 2 hours until tender, then drain and cut into thin strips.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion, carrot, and celery until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine and simmer until reduced by half.
Add the cooked tripe, canned tomatoes, and beef broth to the pot.
Simmer for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until flavors meld.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
cheapTips: Buy tripe from ethnic markets or butchers for 30% less than regular grocery stores
Use homemade or boxed broth instead of canned

recipes.name: Lampredotto
recipes.description: Tuscan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean the lampredotto under cold running water and blanch in salted boiling water for 3 hours until very tender.
Drain and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté chopped onion, carrot, and celery until golden.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, then deglaze with white wine.
Add the cooked lampredotto pieces, canned tomatoes, bay leaf, and beef broth.
Simmer for 90 minutes, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens and flavors concentrate.
Remove bay leaf, adjust seasoning with salt and pepper, and serve hot with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Source lampredotto from specialty butchers; call ahead for best prices
Freeze leftovers to extend cost over multiple meals

recipes.name: Arista alla Toscana
recipes.description: Tuscan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Make slits in the pork loin and insert whole garlic cloves, rosemary sprigs, and sage leaves.
Rub the roast generously with olive oil, salt, and pepper on all sides.
Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat and sear the pork on all sides until browned, about 10 minutes total.
Pour white wine and chicken broth into the skillet around the roast.
Transfer to a preheated 350°F oven and roast for 90 minutes until internal temperature reaches 145°F.
Remove roast and let rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
Strain the pan juices into a saucepan, simmer for 3 minutes, and serve as sauce over sliced pork.
cheapTips: Buy pork loin on sale and freeze until needed
Skip the wine and use extra broth for budget-friendly cooking

recipes.name: Saltimbocca alla Toscana
recipes.description: Tuscan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Place each veal cutlet between plastic wrap and pound gently to 0.25-inch thickness.
Lay 1 prosciutto slice and 2 sage leaves on each cutlet and secure with a toothpick.
Heat butter and olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sauté the saltimbocca for 3 minutes per side until golden, then transfer to a plate.
Deglaze the pan with white wine and simmer for 2 minutes, then add chicken broth.
Return the saltimbocca to the pan and cook for 2 more minutes until the sauce reduces slightly.
Season with salt and pepper and serve immediately with the pan sauce.
cheapTips: Substitute chicken cutlets for a less expensive option with similar cooking time
Buy prosciutto at the deli counter in bulk for per-pound savings

recipes.name: Zuppa di Pesce alla Toscana
recipes.description: Tuscan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, then deglaze with white wine and simmer for 3 minutes.
Pour in canned tomatoes and fish broth, bring to a simmer, and cook for 10 minutes.
Add fish fillets and shrimp, simmer for 5 minutes until partially cooked.
Add cleaned mussels, cover, and simmer for 5 minutes until mussel shells open; discard any unopened mussels.
Season with salt and pepper and stir in 2 tablespoons of fresh parsley.
Ladle soup into bowls, serve with crusty bread rubbed with garlic, and garnish with remaining parsley.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp and fish on sale; they thaw well in the warm broth
Source mussels from Asian markets for 40% less than specialty seafood shops

recipes.name: Crostini Neri
recipes.description: Tuscan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Sauté minced onion and garlic in butter over medium heat until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add chopped chicken livers and cook for 5 minutes, breaking them apart with a spoon.
Deglaze with Marsala wine and simmer for 2 minutes until alcohol cooks off.
Stir in capers and season with salt and pepper; mash to a coarse paste.
Toast baguette slices under the broiler for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Brush toasted bread with olive oil and spread generously with the chicken liver mixture.
Serve immediately or at room temperature as an appetizer.
cheapTips: Buy chicken livers from the butcher counter for half the price of prepared pâté
Use day-old baguettes from the discount bin for toasting

recipes.name: Bruschetta al Pomodoro
recipes.description: Tuscan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast baguette slices under the broiler for 2 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Cut tomatoes in half, scoop out seeds, and finely dice the flesh into a bowl.
Mince garlic and add to the tomatoes along with torn fresh basil.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic vinegar, then season with salt and let sit for 5 minutes.
Rub each toasted slice with a whole garlic clove.
Spoon the tomato mixture generously onto each bruschetta slice.
Serve immediately while the bread is still warm.
cheapTips: Make during tomato season (summer) when prices are lowest
Use discount grocery store baguettes that are perfectly fine for toasting

recipes.name: Pecorino Romano e Miele
recipes.description: Tuscan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Break walnuts into small pieces by hand.
Cut Pecorino Romano into small chunks or shards.
Arrange cheese pieces on a serving plate.
Warm honey slightly by microwaving for 15 seconds until it flows easily.
Drizzle warm honey over the cheese.
Sprinkle crushed walnuts over the top.
Serve immediately with crackers or crusty bread on the side.
cheapTips: Buy Pecorino Romano from bulk sections instead of pre-packaged wedges
Use store-brand honey instead of premium varieties

recipes.name: Pici all'Aglione
recipes.description: Tuscan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook pici pasta according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, thinly slice the garlic cloves.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes.
Cook garlic slowly for 5-7 minutes until golden and fragrant, stirring frequently to avoid burning.
Add canned tomatoes to the skillet and simmer for 10 minutes, breaking them apart with a spoon.
Drain pasta and add it to the sauce, tossing gently for 2 minutes to coat.
Serve topped with grated Pecorino Romano and fresh parsley.
cheapTips: Substitute spaghetti or linguine if pici is unavailable at the same cost
Buy garlic in bulk and store in a cool place for months of cooking

recipes.name: Tagliatelle di Lepre
recipes.description: Tuscan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Chop rabbit into bite-sized pieces and heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the rabbit pieces on all sides for about 8 minutes total, then remove and set aside.
Sauté diced onion, carrot, and celery in the same pot until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, then return rabbit to the pot.
Deglaze with red wine and simmer until reduced by half, about 5 minutes.
Add canned tomatoes and chicken broth, bring to a simmer, and cook for 2 hours until rabbit is very tender, stirring occasionally.
Cook tagliatelle according to package directions until al dente, drain, and toss with butter.
Serve tagliatelle topped with the rabbit ragù and grated Pecorino Romano.
cheapTips: Order rabbit from specialty butchers in advance for better pricing
Substitute chicken thighs if rabbit is unavailable for similar cooking time and flavor

recipes.name: Tinga de Pollo Poblana
recipes.description: Pueblan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil chicken breasts with onion and salt in water for 20 minutes until cooked through, then shred the meat.
Roast poblano peppers over an open flame or broiler until charred, place in a plastic bag for 5 minutes, then peel off skin and remove seeds.
Blend roasted poblanos, tomatoes, chipotles, garlic, and 1/2 cup chicken broth until smooth.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet and sauté diced onion for 2 minutes until softened.
Pour blended sauce into the skillet and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add shredded chicken and remaining broth, simmer for 10 minutes until flavors combine.
Taste and adjust salt, then serve hot topped with sliced avocado.
cheapTips: Buy whole chicken and cut your own for savings
Use canned chipotles from bulk sections to reduce cost

recipes.name: Huevos Divorciados
recipes.description: Pueblan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blend tomatoes, half the onion, 1 garlic clove, and salt for red sauce; strain if desired.
Blend tomatillos or salsa verde base with jalapeño, remaining onion, and garlic for green sauce.
Heat red sauce in one small skillet and green sauce in another skillet over medium heat, simmering for 5 minutes each.
Heat oil in a third skillet and fry eggs two at a time until whites set and yolks remain runny.
Place one fried egg in each sauce (one egg per sauce per serving) and simmer for 1 minute.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet until pliable.
Plate with red egg on one side and green egg on the other, garnish with cilantro, and serve with warm tortillas.
cheapTips: Buy eggs in bulk when on sale
Make sauces from fresh tomatoes and tomatillos when in season

recipes.name: Chilaquiles Poblanos
recipes.description: Pueblan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut tortillas into quarters and fry in 2 tablespoons oil in a skillet until crispy, then drain on paper towels.
Roast poblano peppers over flame or broiler until charred, place in a bag for 5 minutes, peel, and cut into strips.
Sauté diced onion and garlic in remaining oil for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Blend poblano strips, sour cream, and broth until smooth, then pour into skillet with onion.
Simmer sauce for 5 minutes, taste and adjust salt.
Add fried tortilla pieces to sauce and stir gently to coat, simmering for 3 minutes until tortillas soften slightly but retain texture.
Fry eggs in a separate skillet until whites set.
Transfer chilaquiles to a serving dish, top with fried eggs and queso fresco, and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use stale tortillas from day before to save money
Buy poblanos in bulk when in season and freeze

recipes.name: Pan de Muerto
recipes.description: Pueblan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dissolve yeast in warm water and let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Cream butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, then beat in eggs one at a time.
Mix flour and salt, then add to butter mixture alternating with yeast mixture, stirring until dough forms.
Knead dough on floured surface for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic, incorporating orange zest and anise seeds.
Place dough in oiled bowl, cover with damp cloth, and let rise in warm place for 1.5 hours until doubled.
Punch down dough and shape into a round loaf, place on parchment paper, cover, and let rise for 45 minutes.
Bake at 350°F for 45 minutes until golden brown and hollow-sounding when tapped.
Cool on wire rack before serving.
cheapTips: Buy yeast in bulk from bulk bins
Use regular sugar instead of purchasing specialty items

recipes.name: Buñuelos Poblanos
recipes.description: Pueblan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk eggs and milk together, then stir into dry ingredients until smooth batter forms.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep skillet or pot.
Using two spoons, drop batter in portions into hot oil and fry 2 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain fried buñuelos on paper towels.
Heat piloncillo and water in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring until dissolved into a syrup.
Mix sugar and cinnamon together in a shallow bowl.
Dip warm buñuelos into cinnamon-sugar mixture, then drizzle with piloncillo syrup and serve warm.
cheapTips: Use vegetable oil instead of specialty oils
Brown sugar can replace piloncillo

recipes.name: Molotes de Papa
recipes.description: Pueblan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil potatoes until tender, peel, and mash with salt and pepper.
Finely dice onion and jalapeños, then fold into mashed potatoes along with queso fresco and cilantro.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet to make them pliable.
Place 3 tablespoons potato filling on each tortilla, fold into a triangle or rectangle, and seal edges by pressing firmly.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep skillet.
Carefully place molotes in hot oil and fry 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with salsa verde for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy potatoes in bulk
Use store-brand salsa to reduce cost

recipes.name: Pappa al Pomodoro
recipes.description: Tuscan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté sliced garlic until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add canned tomatoes with juice and red pepper flakes, simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour in vegetable broth and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add bread cubes to the pot and stir frequently, cooking for 10 minutes until bread softens and absorbs liquid.
Mash some bread and tomatoes together with the back of a spoon to create a thick, porridge-like consistency.
Stir in remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil and torn basil.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot or at room temperature, topped with grated parmesan cheese.
cheapTips: Use stale bread from day-old bakery sections
Buy canned tomatoes when on sale and stock up

recipes.name: Acquacotta
recipes.description: Tuscan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast bread slices until golden, then rub with garlic and set aside.
Heat 4 tablespoons olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté minced garlic for 30 seconds.
Add diced tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in broth and bring to a boil, then add spinach and fresh herbs.
Reduce heat to a simmer and let cook for 5 minutes.
Create four wells in the broth and crack one egg into each well.
Simmer gently for 4 minutes until egg whites are set but yolks remain runny.
Place one toasted bread slice in each bowl, pour soup over it, drizzle with remaining olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and serve.
cheapTips: Buy eggs in bulk
Use frozen spinach instead of fresh to save money

recipes.name: Cacciucco
recipes.description: Tuscan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast bread slices and rub with garlic clove, set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add red pepper flakes and cook for 30 seconds, then pour in white wine and simmer for 2 minutes to reduce.
Add canned tomatoes and fish broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add firmer seafood (clams, mussels) first and cook covered for 3 minutes.
Add shrimp and any other delicate seafood, cook covered for 3 more minutes until shells open and shrimp turn pink.
Discard any unopened shells and taste the broth, adjusting salt and pepper.
Place toasted bread in bowls, pour hot cacciucco over it, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve.
cheapTips: Buy seafood in bulk when on sale and freeze
Use canned tomatoes instead of fresh to save money

recipes.name: Minestrone Toscano
recipes.description: Tuscan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion, carrots, celery, and garlic for 5 minutes until softened.
Add diced zucchini, chopped cabbage, and canned tomatoes, stir to combine.
Pour in vegetable broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add drained and rinsed white beans and continue simmering for 10 minutes.
Stir in fresh basil and taste the soup, adjusting salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot in bowls topped with grated parmesan cheese and an extra drizzle of olive oil.
cheapTips: Buy seasonal vegetables at farmer's markets
Use canned beans and tomatoes year-round for savings

recipes.name: Cinghiale in Umido
recipes.description: Tuscan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut the pork into 2-inch chunks and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the meat on all sides in batches, about 12 minutes total.
Remove the meat and sauté diced onion, carrots, and celery until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, then deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits.
Return the meat to the pot, add beef broth, bay leaves, and rosemary sprigs.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and braise in a 325°F oven for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Remove from oven, discard bay leaves and rosemary, and season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot with crusty bread or polenta.
cheapTips: Use pork shoulder instead of wild boar for authenticity on a budget
Buy carrots and celery in bulk; they're inexpensive base aromatics

recipes.name: Coniglio in Umido
recipes.description: Tuscan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat the rabbit pieces dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the meat on all sides, about 10 minutes.
Remove the meat and sauté diced onion, garlic, carrots, and celery until golden, about 6 minutes.
Pour in white wine, scraping up browned bits, and simmer until slightly reduced, about 2 minutes.
Stir in tomato sauce and chicken broth, then return the meat to the pot with sage leaves.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer gently for 1.5 hours until rabbit is tender.
Remove sage leaves, season with salt and pepper, and serve with soft polenta or wide noodles.
cheapTips: Substitute chicken thighs if rabbit is unavailable at your store
Make your own broth the night before using chicken bones and vegetable scraps

recipes.name: Zuppe di Farro
recipes.description: Tuscan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion, garlic, carrots, and celery for 5 minutes.
Add pearl farro and stir to coat with oil, toasting lightly for 2 minutes.
Pour in vegetable broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 30 minutes.
Stir in canned tomatoes with their juices, drained cannellini beans, and rosemary sprig.
Simmer uncovered for another 20 minutes until farro is tender.
Remove rosemary sprig, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy farro in bulk from the dried goods section to reduce cost significantly
Use dried beans soaked overnight instead of canned to save 50% per serving

recipes.name: Panettone Toscano
recipes.description: Tuscan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix warm milk with yeast and let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Cream butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes, then beat in eggs one at a time with vanilla extract.
Combine flour and salt, then gently fold into the butter mixture alternately with the yeast mixture in three additions.
Fold in raisins and candied citrus peel, then transfer to a greased panettone mold or tall round cake pan.
Cover with a damp towel and let rise at room temperature for 6-8 hours until the dough nearly fills the pan.
Preheat oven to 375°F and bake for 45-50 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Remove from oven and cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.
cheapTips: Make candied peel at home by simmering citrus peel with sugar for several hours
Buy raisins from bulk bins and store in an airtight container to extend shelf life

recipes.name: Schiacciata alla Fiorentina
recipes.description: Tuscan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix yeast with warm water and let sit 5 minutes until foamy, then add salt and sugar.
Add flour gradually while mixing, then knead in 2 tablespoons olive oil and anise seeds for 8 minutes until smooth.
Let dough rise in an oiled bowl covered with a damp towel for 2 hours until doubled.
Punch down the dough and stretch into a greased 9x13 inch baking pan, drizzling the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil over the top.
Cover and let rise for 1 hour until puffy.
Preheat oven to 400°F and bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown.
While still warm, dust generously with confectioners sugar and serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Buy anise seeds in bulk from the spice aisle to reduce cost
Make this in a large batch and freeze portions for extended snacking

recipes.name: Pizza Napoletana
recipes.description: Neapolitan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix yeast with warm water and let sit 5 minutes, then add salt and 1 tablespoon olive oil to create the dough starter.
Gradually mix in flour and knead for 8 minutes until smooth, then let rise in an oiled bowl covered for 1.5 hours.
Divide dough in half and stretch each portion into a thin 12-inch round on a lightly oiled baking sheet.
Combine canned tomatoes with minced garlic and let sit for 5 minutes, then spread thinly over each pizza base.
Tear fresh mozzarella into small pieces and distribute evenly over the tomato sauce, drizzle with remaining olive oil.
Bake at 500°F for 12-15 minutes until the crust is golden and cheese is melted and bubbling.
Remove from oven, top with fresh basil leaves, and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use regular whole milk mozzarella instead of fresh mozzarella to reduce cost by 50%
Buy San Marzano tomato cans on sale and stock up for future pizza nights

recipes.name: Spaghetti alla Genovese
recipes.description: Neapolitan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice onions into thin strips and heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add onions and cook slowly for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until very soft and caramelized.
Season beef chunks with salt and pepper, then nestle into the onions and brown on all sides, about 8 minutes.
Pour in white wine, scraping up browned bits, and simmer until mostly evaporated.
Add diced celery, carrots, and beef broth, then cover and simmer very gently for 2 hours until the beef is tender and sauce is thick.
Cook spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain and toss with the ragù.
Serve in bowls topped with grated Parmesan cheese.
cheapTips: Use beef stew meat on sale and freeze portions for future pasta dinners
Make a double batch and freeze half the sauce for quick meals later

recipes.name: Pasta alla Genovese
recipes.description: Neapolitan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine basil, garlic, and pine nuts in a food processor and pulse until coarsely chopped.
Add Parmesan cheese and pulse to combine, then slowly drizzle in olive oil while processing until a chunky paste forms.
Stir in salt and lemon juice to finish the pesto.
Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain and reserve 1 cup pasta water.
Toss the hot pasta with the pesto in a large bowl, adding a splash of pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce.
Divide among bowls and serve immediately with extra Parmesan on the side.
cheapTips: Substitute walnuts for pine nuts to reduce pesto cost by 60%
Make pesto in larger batches and freeze in ice cube trays for future use

recipes.name: Lasagna Napoletana
recipes.description: Neapolitan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and sauté diced onion and garlic until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add ground beef and pork, breaking up the meat as it cooks, and brown for 8 minutes until no pink remains.
Stir in tomato sauce and beef broth, then simmer uncovered for 1 hour, stirring occasionally, until the ragù is rich and thick.

Make a béchamel sauce by melting butter in a saucepan, whisking in flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisking in warm milk until a smooth sauce forms; simmer for 5 minutes and season with salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 375°F and spread a thin layer of meat ragù on the bottom of a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Layer noodles, then ragù, then béchamel, then mozzarella and Parmesan, repeating until all ingredients are used and ending with béchamel and cheeses.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then remove foil and bake uncovered for another 15-20 minutes until the top is golden and bubbling.
Allow to rest for 10 minutes before cutting and serving.
cheapTips: Buy ground beef on sale and freeze in portions for future lasagna preparations
Use store-brand tomato sauce to reduce sauce cost by 40%

recipes.name: Rigatoni alla Genovese
recipes.description: Neapolitan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice onions into thin half-moons and heat olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium-low heat.
Add onions and cook slowly for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and soft.
Season the beef chunk with salt and pepper, then nestle it into the onions and brown on all sides over medium-high heat for about 8 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, then pour in beef broth and add diced carrots and celery.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer gently for 1.5 hours until the beef is very tender and the sauce is thick and rich.
Remove beef from the pot, shred it with two forks, and return to the sauce; season with salt and pepper.
Cook rigatoni in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain and toss with the sauce.
Serve in bowls topped with grated Parmesan cheese.
cheapTips: Choose a tough, inexpensive beef cut that becomes tender with long, slow cooking
Make the sauce the day before to deepen flavors and save time on serving day

recipes.name: Pasta e Piselli
recipes.description: Neapolitan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add canned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, breaking them up with a spoon.
Pour in vegetable broth and bring to a boil.
Add pasta and peas, then reduce heat and simmer for 12-15 minutes until pasta is tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot in bowls topped with grated parmesan cheese.
cheapTips: Buy frozen peas instead of fresh—they're cheaper and just as nutritious.
Use store-brand pasta and canned tomatoes to reduce costs significantly.

recipes.name: Spaghetti al Nero di Seppia
recipes.description: Neapolitan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti until al dente, then drain.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet and sauté minced garlic until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Pour in white wine and let it reduce by half, about 2 minutes.
Add canned tomatoes and squid ink packets, stirring well to combine the ink throughout the sauce.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Toss cooked spaghetti with the sauce, season with salt and pepper, and garnish with fresh parsley.
cheapTips: Buy squid ink at an Italian specialty store or online in bulk rather than at upscale grocery stores.
Use affordable white cooking wine or even skip it and use extra broth.

recipes.name: Pani e Panelle
recipes.description: Neapolitan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk chickpea flour with water slowly to avoid lumps, then add salt and let sit for 10 minutes.
Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a large shallow pot and pour the chickpea batter, stirring constantly.
Continue stirring over medium heat for 15-20 minutes until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the pot sides.
Pour the hot batter onto an oiled baking sheet in a thin layer and let cool completely, about 10 minutes.
Cut the cooled panelle into rectangles about 3 inches by 2 inches.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet to 350°F and fry panelle until golden on both sides, about 2 minutes total.
Drain on paper towels, then place warm panelle inside the bread and drizzle with lemon juice and top with fresh parsley.
cheapTips: Buy chickpea flour in bulk from ethnic or Indian grocery stores.
Use the cheapest bread available—day-old rolls work perfectly.

recipes.name: Torta Caprese
recipes.description: Neapolitan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9-inch round cake pan.
Melt chocolate and butter together in a bowl over simmering water, then stir in vanilla extract.
Beat eggs and sugar together with an electric mixer until pale and fluffy, about 5 minutes.
Fold the chocolate mixture into the eggs gently, then fold in ground almonds and salt.
Pour batter into the prepared pan and bake for 25-30 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Let cool completely, dust with powdered sugar, and serve.
cheapTips: Buy ground almonds at Costco or ethnic markets for much better prices.
Use regular chocolate chips if dark chocolate is too expensive.

recipes.name: Amatriciana
recipes.description: Roman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti until al dente.
While pasta cooks, cut guanciale into small cubes and render in a skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add diced onion and red pepper flakes, sauté until onion is soft, about 3 minutes.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and simmer for 8-10 minutes until the sauce is thickened.
Drain pasta and reserve 1 cup pasta water, then toss pasta with the sauce.
Add pasta water as needed to loosen the sauce, then remove from heat and stir in 1/2 cup grated pecorino romano.
Plate and top each serving with additional grated pecorino romano and black pepper.
cheapTips: Substitute pancetta or bacon for guanciale if it's unavailable or too expensive.
Buy pecorino romano at a store with a good cheese selection for better prices than specialty shops.

recipes.name: Gricia
recipes.description: Roman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook pasta until al dente.
Dice guanciale and cook slowly in a large skillet over medium heat until the fat renders, about 5 minutes.
Remove skillet from heat and let cool slightly.
Drain pasta, reserving 1 1/2 cups pasta water.
Add hot pasta to the skillet with guanciale and off heat, then add black pepper and toss gently.
Slowly add grated pecorino romano while tossing constantly, adding pasta water gradually until you reach a creamy consistency.
Serve immediately with extra black pepper and pecorino romano on the side.
cheapTips: Use bacon if guanciale is unavailable—it's much cheaper and still delicious.
Buy a wedge of pecorino romano and grate it yourself rather than buying pre-grated.

recipes.name: Coda alla Vaccinara
recipes.description: Roman dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat oxtail dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and brown the oxtail pieces on all sides in batches, about 10 minutes total.
Remove oxtail and set aside, then sauté chopped onion, carrots, and celery in the same pot for 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up browned bits, then add canned tomatoes and beef broth.
Return oxtail to the pot, add bay leaves, and bring to a simmer.
Cover partially and simmer gently for 2.5-3 hours until the meat is very tender and falling off the bone.
Skim off excess fat from the surface, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot with the braising liquid.
cheapTips: Oxtail is very affordable compared to other cuts of beef—often the cheapest option at the butcher.
Make a double batch and freeze half for an easy future meal.

recipes.name: Rigatoni con la Pajata
recipes.description: Roman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse the pajata thoroughly and cut into 2-inch pieces.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté finely chopped onion, carrot, and celery for 5 minutes.
Add pajata pieces and brown lightly for 3 minutes.
Pour in white wine and let it reduce by half, about 3 minutes.
Add canned tomatoes and simmer uncovered for 1 hour until the pajata is very tender, stirring occasionally.
While the sauce simmers, cook rigatoni in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain.
Season the sauce with salt and pepper, then toss with the cooked rigatoni.
Serve hot topped with grated pecorino romano.
cheapTips: Pajata is inexpensive at Italian butchers—ask ahead as it's often not displayed.
Order online from Italian specialty suppliers if your local butcher doesn't stock it.

recipes.name: Trippa alla Romana
recipes.description: Roman dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and add tripe, then simmer for 30 minutes to partially cook and tenderize.
Drain and cut the tripe into thin strips about 2 inches long.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté chopped onion, carrot, and celery for 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the partially cooked tripe and stir for 2 minutes to coat with oil.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and beef broth, then bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 30-40 minutes until tripe is very tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir in fresh mint, then season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot topped with grated parmesan cheese.
cheapTips: Tripe is one of the cheapest cuts of beef—usually $2-3 per pound at most butchers.
Buy pre-cleaned tripe to save time; fresh mint from a grocery store's produce section is cheap.

recipes.name: Carciofi alla Romana
recipes.description: Roman dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Trim artichoke stems and cut off the top 1/4 of each artichoke, then cut each in half lengthwise.
Scoop out the fuzzy center with a spoon and discard.
Mix together minced parsley, minced garlic, bread crumbs, grated pecorino romano, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Fill the center cavity of each artichoke half with the herb mixture, dividing it evenly.
Stand the artichokes upright in a heavy pot with their cut sides up, tightly packed together.
Pour olive oil and lemon juice over them, then add water to come halfway up the sides.
Cover and simmer gently for 30-40 minutes until artichoke hearts are tender when pierced with a fork.
Serve warm or at room temperature, spooning cooking liquid over each artichoke.
cheapTips: Buy artichokes in season (spring) when they're cheapest; frozen artichoke hearts also work.
Make your own bread crumbs from stale bread instead of buying packaged.

recipes.name: Carciofi alla Giudia
recipes.description: Roman snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Trim artichoke stems and remove outer dark leaves until pale green leaves are visible.
Cut artichokes in half lengthwise and scoop out fuzzy center with a spoon.
Rub cut sides with lemon juice and mix garlic, parsley, salt, and pepper together.
Stuff the herb mixture between artichoke leaves and in the center cavity.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and place artichokes cut-side down.
Add water around the artichokes, cover, and simmer for 30-35 minutes until very tender.
Increase heat to crisp the cut sides for 2-3 minutes until golden brown.
Serve warm or at room temperature with pan juices drizzled over.
cheapTips: Buy artichokes in spring when they're cheapest.
Use budget olive oil for cooking; save expensive oil for finishing.

recipes.name: Puntarelle con Acciughe
recipes.description: Roman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut puntarelle into 3-inch pieces and soak in ice water for 15 minutes to crisp.
Chop anchovies and garlic together into a fine paste.
Whisk together vinegar, olive oil, and the anchovy-garlic paste.
Drain puntarelle thoroughly and pat dry with paper towels.
Toss puntarelle with the dressing and season with salt and pepper.
Let sit for 5 minutes before serving to allow flavors to meld.
cheapTips: Use canned anchovies in oil instead of fresh to save money.
Substitute regular chicory or endive if puntarelle isn't available.

recipes.name: Pasta e Ceci
recipes.description: Roman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté garlic until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, chickpeas with their liquid, broth, and rosemary.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add pasta and stir frequently, cooking until pasta is al dente, about 8-10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove rosemary sprigs and serve hot, drizzled with olive oil if desired.
cheapTips: Canned chickpeas are cheaper than dried and require no soaking.
Use store-brand pasta and broth to keep costs very low.

recipes.name: Gnocchi alla Romana
recipes.description: Roman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat milk in a large saucepan until steaming but not boiling.
Slowly pour in semolina while whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat to low and stir continuously for 15-20 minutes until very thick.
Remove from heat and stir in 2 tablespoons butter, egg yolks, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Spread mixture onto a wet baking sheet in a 1/4-inch layer and let cool completely.
Cut into 2-inch rounds using a glass or cutter.
Arrange rounds in a buttered baking dish, dot with remaining butter and Parmesan.
Bake at 400°F for 15-20 minutes until golden brown and crispy on top.
cheapTips: Buy generic Parmesan instead of pricey imported versions.
Use 2% milk instead of whole milk to reduce cost slightly.

recipes.name: Pappardelle alla Lepre
recipes.description: Roman dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil and brown ground rabbit, breaking apart with a spoon, then remove.
In the same pot, sauté onion, carrot, and celery until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in wine and scrape up browned bits, then add tomatoes and juniper berries.
Return rabbit to pot and simmer uncovered for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper; the sauce should be rich and concentrated.
Cook pappardelle in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain.
Toss pasta with sauce and serve topped with grated Parmesan.
cheapTips: Use ground beef if rabbit is unavailable or too expensive.
Make sauce a day ahead; flavors improve and you save on dinner prep time.

recipes.name: Spaghetti alla Gricia
recipes.description: Roman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente; reserve 1 cup pasta water before draining.
Meanwhile, cook diced guanciale in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy, about 5 minutes.
Mix black pepper into the guanciale and remove from heat.
Add hot drained pasta to the guanciale skillet.
Remove from heat and add 3/4 cup grated Pecorino Romano while tossing constantly.
Add pasta water a little at a time to create a creamy sauce without dairy.
Serve immediately with extra Pecorino Romano and cracked black pepper.
cheapTips: Pancetta is cheaper than guanciale; the flavor difference is minimal for students.
Buy Pecorino Romano in blocks and grate yourself to save 20-30%.

recipes.name: Fegato alla Veneziana
recipes.description: Roman dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add sliced onions and cook, stirring often, for 15-18 minutes until very soft and golden.
Transfer onions to a plate; set aside.
Pat liver dry and lightly dust both sides with flour, shaking off excess.
Increase heat to high and add remaining olive oil and butter to the skillet.
Quickly sear liver slices 1-2 minutes per side until browned but still slightly pink inside.
Return onions to skillet, add wine, and simmer for 2 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper, and parsley; serve immediately.
cheapTips: Beef liver is significantly cheaper than calf liver.
Buy onions in bulk during autumn when prices are lowest.

recipes.name: Maritozzo
recipes.description: Roman breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Warm milk to 110°F and mix with melted butter and egg.
Combine wet and dry ingredients, knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Let dough rise in a greased bowl for 45 minutes until doubled in size.
Divide dough into 4 portions and shape into oval buns on a baking sheet.
Let rise again for 20 minutes, then bake at 375°F for 12-15 minutes until golden.
Cool completely, then whip heavy cream with powdered sugar to stiff peaks.
Slice buns horizontally and fill generously with sweetened whipped cream.
cheapTips: Make in bulk and freeze unfilled buns; fill fresh when needed.
Use heavy cream when it's on sale and whip at home instead of buying whipped cream.

recipes.name: Supplì al Telefono
recipes.description: Roman snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat broth in a separate pot and keep at a simmer throughout risotto cooking.
Sauté onion in butter, add rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Add broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for liquid to absorb before adding more, about 18 minutes total.
Stir in Parmesan and tomato sauce; spread risotto on a baking sheet to cool completely.
Form 2-inch oval portions of risotto and insert a cube of mozzarella in the center.
Seal edges carefully; beat egg and dip each supplì in egg, then coat with bread crumbs.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pot or deep fryer.
Fry supplì until golden brown on all sides, about 3-4 minutes; drain on paper towels.
cheapTips: Make risotto a day ahead; cold risotto is easier to shape.
Buy mozzarella on sale and freeze until ready to use.

recipes.name: Escalivada
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F and line a large baking sheet with aluminum foil.
Chop eggplant, peppers, zucchini, onion, and tomatoes into 1-inch chunks.
Peel garlic cloves and leave whole.
Toss all vegetables with olive oil, salt, and pepper on the baking sheet.
Spread in a single layer and roast for 40-45 minutes, stirring halfway through.
Vegetables should be very soft and lightly charred on edges.
Transfer to a serving dish and sprinkle with fresh basil.
Serve warm or at room temperature as a side dish or light main course.
cheapTips: Buy vegetables that are in season in late summer/early fall for best prices.
Use budget olive oil; roasting brings out flavor without expensive oil.

recipes.name: Esqueixada
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak the salt cod in cold water for 24 hours, changing water every 6 hours.
Bring a pot of water to boil and poach the rehydrated cod for 8-10 minutes until tender.
Remove cod, let cool, then shred into bite-sized flakes, discarding skin and bones.
Dice tomatoes and red onion finely.
In a large bowl, combine shredded cod, tomatoes, onion, and olives.
Whisk together olive oil and vinegar, then drizzle over the salad.
Season with salt and pepper, toss gently, and garnish with parsley before serving.
cheapTips: Buy salt cod in bulk from Spanish markets for better prices
Use canned tomatoes in winter when fresh are expensive

recipes.name: Pa amb tomàquet
recipes.description: Catalan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice the bread into 1/2-inch thick slices and toast lightly until golden.
Cut tomatoes in half and rub the cut side gently across the warm toast.
Rub a peeled garlic clove lightly over each slice of bread.
Drizzle generously with extra virgin olive oil.
Sprinkle with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately while bread is still warm.
cheapTips: Buy day-old bread from bakery sections for discounts
Use seasonal tomatoes when they're cheapest

recipes.name: Calcots
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with foil.
Trim the root ends and most of the green tops from the spring onions, leaving about 3 inches of white and light green.
Arrange onions in a single layer on the baking sheet and roast for 25-30 minutes until charred and tender.
While onions roast, whisk together olive oil, vinegar, salt, pepper, minced garlic, and paprika to make romesco-style sauce.
Remove onions from oven and let cool slightly until you can handle them.
Peel away the charred outer layers to reveal the tender white flesh inside.
Arrange peeled onions on a serving platter and drizzle with the sauce.
Serve warm with crusty bread for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy spring onions at farmers markets in spring for best prices
Make extra sauce for other vegetables

recipes.name: Butifarra amb mongetes
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak beans in cold water for at least 4 hours or overnight, then drain.
In a large pot, heat olive oil and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until softened.
Add drained beans, broth, and bay leaf; bring to boil then simmer 45 minutes until beans are tender.
While beans cook, slice sausages into 2-inch pieces.
In a separate skillet, brown sausage pieces over medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes until cooked through.
Add cooked sausage to the bean pot and simmer together for 5 more minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot in bowls.
cheapTips: Buy dried beans in bulk sections instead of canned
Use Italian sausage as affordable substitute for butifarra

recipes.name: Conill amb xocolata
recipes.description: Catalan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat rabbit pieces dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven and brown rabbit pieces on all sides; remove and set aside.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in the same pot until golden.
Grind almonds with 3 tbsp water to create a paste, then add to the pot along with thyme and bay leaf.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up browned bits, then add broth.
Return rabbit to pot, bring to simmer, cover, and cook for 45-50 minutes until rabbit is tender.
Finely chop dark chocolate and stir into the stew during the last 2 minutes of cooking.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot with crusty bread or rice.
cheapTips: Look for rabbit at ethnic butchers for lower prices than specialty shops
Use chicken thighs if rabbit is unavailable

recipes.name: Fideuà
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
