steps: Heat olive oil in a wide shallow paella-like pan over medium-high heat.
Toast the dry noodles in the oil for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until lightly golden.
Add diced onion and minced garlic, cooking 2 minutes until fragrant.
Steep saffron in 1/4 cup warm broth for 2 minutes, then pour saffron broth into the pan.
Add remaining broth, stirring to combine, then nestle shrimp and squid into the noodles.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 12-15 minutes until noodles are tender and liquid is mostly absorbed.
Season with paprika, salt, and pepper to taste.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over top and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use frozen shrimp and squid for better prices
Make your own seafood broth from fish scraps

recipes.name: Suquet de peix
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until softened.
Add cubed potatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in fish broth and bring to boil, then simmer 15 minutes until potatoes are nearly tender.
Steep saffron in 1/4 cup warm broth, then stir saffron broth into the pot.
Add unpeeled shrimp and cook for 3 minutes.
Carefully add fish fillets and simmer gently for 5-7 minutes until fish is cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
cheapTips: Use frozen shrimp to save money while keeping quality high
Buy whole fish and ask the fishmonger for trimmings to make broth

recipes.name: Romesco
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Roast whole red peppers over an open flame or under the broiler until blackened all over.
Place hot peppers in a plastic bag for 10 minutes to steam, then peel away the charred skin.
Remove stems and seeds from peppers.
In a food processor, combine roasted peppers, almonds, hazelnuts, garlic, tomatoes, and paprika.
Pulse until a coarse paste forms, then add vinegar and olive oil.
Process until you reach desired consistency—slightly chunky is traditional.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve with grilled bread, grilled vegetables, or as a condiment for fish or chicken.
cheapTips: Roast peppers yourself instead of buying pre-roasted jarred versions
Buy nuts in bulk sections for significant savings

recipes.name: Coca de recapte
recipes.description: Catalan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice zucchini, pepper, eggplant, and onion into thin strips.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet and sauté vegetables with minced garlic until soft and golden, about 15 minutes; season with salt, pepper, and thyme.
Preheat oven to 425°F.
Stretch pizza dough onto an oiled rectangular baking sheet to about 1/4-inch thickness.
Spread sautéed vegetables evenly over the dough.
Drizzle any remaining oil from the pan over the vegetables and sprinkle with coarse sea salt.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until crust is golden and crispy.
Cool slightly before cutting into squares and serving.
cheapTips: Use store-bought dough to save time and money
Buy vegetables in season for best prices

recipes.name: Panellets
recipes.description: Catalan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine ground almonds, sugar, egg yolk, lemon zest, and vanilla until well mixed.
Roll mixture into balls about the size of walnuts (about 1 inch diameter).
Beat egg white lightly in a shallow bowl.
Dip each ball briefly in egg white, then roll in pine nuts to coat evenly.
Place coated balls on prepared baking sheets.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until lightly golden.
Cool on baking sheet for 5 minutes, then transfer to wire rack and dust lightly with powdered sugar before serving.
cheapTips: Buy almond flour and pine nuts in bulk sections
Make during almond harvest season (fall) for better prices

recipes.name: Txuleta de Buey
recipes.description: Basque dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Remove steaks from refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking to reach room temperature.
Heat a cast iron skillet or heavy pan over high heat until very hot.
Pat steaks dry with paper towels and season generously with sea salt and black pepper on both sides.
Place steaks in the hot pan with olive oil and sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, turning only once.
Add smashed garlic cloves to the pan in the last minute of cooking.
Remove steaks to a warm plate and let rest for 5 minutes.
Drizzle with olive oil and squeeze fresh lemon juice over the top before serving.
cheapTips: Buy steaks on sale and freeze for later
Use a cast iron skillet you already own instead of buying specialty cookware

recipes.name: Percebes a la Gallega
recipes.description: Basque lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat.
Clean percebes under running water, removing any barnacles or debris.
Add percebes to boiling salted water and cook for 8-10 minutes until tender.
Drain percebes thoroughly in a colander.
Heat olive oil in a small pan with sliced garlic, paprika, and red pepper flakes over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Arrange percebes on a serving plate and pour the hot garlic oil mixture over them.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges for squeezing.
cheapTips: Buy percebes frozen if fresh is unavailable and expensive
Skip specialty seafood markets and check Asian markets for cheaper options

recipes.name: Angulas a la Bilbaína
recipes.description: Basque dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a small clay pot or shallow pan over medium heat.
Slice the garlic thinly and add to the oil with red pepper flakes, cooking gently for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Increase heat to medium-high and add the angulas or smelt to the hot oil.
Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring gently, until the fish are cooked through.
Season with sea salt and sprinkle with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve immediately in the hot pot with crusty bread for soaking up the oil.
Each diner should use bread to eat directly from the shared pot.
cheapTips: Substitute smelt or capelin for authentic eel larvae
Buy from seafood wholesale stores instead of specialty markets

recipes.name: Bacalao al Pil Pil
recipes.description: Basque lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak salted cod in cold water for 24 hours, changing water 3 times to remove excess salt.
Cut cod into large pieces and place skin-side down in a shallow clay pot or wide pan.
Cover cod with water and poach gently over low heat for 10-12 minutes until just cooked through.
Carefully remove cod with a slotted spoon and set aside, reserving 0.5 cup of poaching liquid.
In a small saucepan, heat olive oil over low heat and cook sliced garlic with red pepper flakes for 3 minutes until softened but not browned.
Return cod to the pan with the reserved poaching liquid, shaking gently to create an emulsion.
Continue shaking and heating for 2-3 minutes until the sauce becomes creamy and pale, then finish with fresh parsley and lemon juice.
cheapTips: Buy salted cod in bulk and freeze portions
Make the emulsion with patience rather than high heat to avoid breaking it down

recipes.name: Txangurro a la Donostiarra
recipes.description: Basque lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Kill the crab humanely by chilling it first, then freezing the nervous system with a sharp knife through the center.
Boil the crab in salted water for 20 minutes, then remove and let cool enough to handle.
Separate the body from the shell, remove the meat, and clean the shell thoroughly.
Sauté diced onion and garlic in butter, add tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Deglaze with white wine and add fish stock, simmering for 10 minutes.
Stir in the crab meat and cook for 5 minutes, season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the mixture back into the crab shell, top with breadcrumbs and Parmesan, then broil for 3 minutes until golden.
cheapTips: Buy whole crabs in season rather than precooked
Make your own fish stock from bones instead of buying pre-made

recipes.name: Kokotxas en Salsa Verde
recipes.description: Basque lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium heat and sauté minced garlic for 1 minute.
Pat kokotxas dry and carefully add them to the hot oil, cooking gently for 2 minutes per side without moving them.
Add white wine and let simmer for 5 minutes, then add fish stock and clam juice.
Simmer very gently for 5-8 minutes until the kokotxas are cooked through and the sauce is beginning to emulsify.
Finely chop fresh parsley and stir it into the sauce along with lemon juice.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately in shallow bowls with plenty of sauce.
cheapTips: Substitute fish cheeks from other white fish if hake is unavailable
Use bottled clam juice instead of fresh clams to save money

recipes.name: Pintxos de Gildas
recipes.description: Basque snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice the baguette into 12 thin slices, about 0.5 inch thick.
Lightly toast the bread slices in a toaster or under the broiler until golden.
Thread one anchovy, one olive, and one pickled pepper onto each cocktail pick in that order.
Place each assembled pintxo on top of a toast slice.
Serve at room temperature as a snack or appetizer.
These can be made ahead and refrigerated for up to 2 hours before serving.
cheapTips: Buy anchovy fillets in bulk jars instead of small cans
Use regular pitted olives if guindilla peppers are unavailable

recipes.name: Ensalada de Bacalao
recipes.description: Basque lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak salted cod in cold water for 24 hours, changing water 3 times to remove salt.
Boil the desalted cod in water for 8 minutes until cooked through, then drain and cool.
Flake the cooked cod into bite-sized pieces, removing any remaining bones or skin.
Dice the red bell pepper, red onion, and celery finely and place in a large bowl.
Add the flaked cod and green olives to the vegetables.
Whisk together olive oil and red wine vinegar, then pour over the salad and toss gently.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve at room temperature.
cheapTips: Make larger batches and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days
Buy salted cod in bulk when on sale and freeze portions

recipes.name: Calamares en Salsa de Su Tinta
recipes.description: Basque lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean the squid by removing the head and innards; reserve the ink sac if present.
Cut the squid body into rings and chop the tentacles into bite-sized pieces.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in olive oil over medium heat for 4 minutes until softened.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then add the squid pieces and cook for 2 minutes.
Deglaze with white wine and simmer for 5 minutes, then add fish stock.
Dissolve squid ink in 2 tablespoons of warm water and stir into the sauce.
Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until the squid is tender, then season with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Buy frozen squid instead of fresh to save 30-40%
Use bottled squid ink if fresh squid ink is unavailable

recipes.name: Trinxat
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and cut potatoes into 1-inch cubes and boil in salted water for 10 minutes until tender.
Chop the cabbage into thin strips and add to the boiling potatoes for the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Drain the potatoes and cabbage completely and set aside.
Dice the bacon and cook in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy, then set aside.
Dice the onion and sauté in the bacon fat for 3 minutes until softened.
Add the drained potatoes and cabbage to the skillet, mashing gently with a wooden spoon to combine with the onions.
Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mixture forms a golden crust on the bottom.
Stir in the crispy bacon, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy cabbage and potatoes in bulk—they're inexpensive and keep well.
Use regular bacon instead of thick-cut varieties to reduce cost.

recipes.name: Arròs a la cassola
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper, then brown them in olive oil in a large earthenware cassola or heavy pot for 5 minutes per side.
Remove the chicken and set aside, then sauté diced onion and minced garlic in the same pot for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, then add the rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the warm chicken broth and return the chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the rice.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover partially, and simmer for 20 minutes without stirring.
Check that the liquid is mostly absorbed and the rice is tender; if needed, add a splash more broth.
Remove from heat, cover fully, and let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve directly from the pot.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs instead of breasts—they're cheaper and more flavorful.
Make your own broth from a rotisserie chicken or use low-sodium store-bought broth.

recipes.name: Botifarra negra
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice the pork fat finely and render it in a large pot over low heat for 10 minutes, then remove the solids.
Sauté finely minced onion and garlic in the rendered fat for 5 minutes until softened, then cool slightly.
In a large bowl, whisk the pork blood until smooth, then combine with the cooled onion mixture, rice or breadcrumbs, pine nuts, salt, and pepper.
Rinse the natural casings and tie off one end, then using a funnel or sausage stuffer, carefully fill the casings with the blood mixture, leaving a 0.5-inch space at the end.
Tie off the filled casings, prick them with a needle to prevent bursting, and let rest in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Bring a large pot of water or broth to 160°F (70°C) and gently place the botifarra negra in the water.
Poach at this temperature (do not boil) for 30-40 minutes until the sausages float and feel firm.
Remove and cool slightly, then serve sliced or whole, optionally pan-fried until the skin is crispy.
cheapTips: Source pork blood and casings from specialty butchers or online meat suppliers for better prices than retail.
Make in larger batches and freeze for later use.

recipes.name: Arrossejat
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Warm the seafood broth in a separate pot and stir in the saffron threads to infuse.
Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide shallow pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion and minced garlic for 3 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, then add the rice and toast for 2 minutes while stirring.
Pour in the warm saffron broth and bring to a boil, stirring occasionally for the first minute.
Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes without stirring.
Nestle the fish fillets and shrimp into the rice, season with salt and pepper, and cook for another 8-10 minutes until the rice is tender and seafood is cooked through.
Remove from heat and let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Serve directly from the pan with the seafood and rice together.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp and white fish—equally good and often cheaper than fresh.
Use a homemade fish broth made from fish heads and scraps if available.

recipes.name: Escalope a la milanesa
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Place the cutlets between plastic wrap and pound with a meat mallet to about 0.25-inch thickness.
Set up three shallow bowls with flour mixed with salt and pepper in the first, beaten eggs in the second, and breadcrumbs in the third.
Coat each cutlet lightly in flour, shaking off excess, then dip in beaten egg, and finally press firmly into breadcrumbs on both sides.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place the breaded cutlets in the hot oil and cook for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through.
Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges squeezed over the top.
cheapTips: Use chicken instead of veal to save money without sacrificing flavor.
Buy pre-panko breadcrumbs in bulk to reduce cost.

recipes.name: Mel i mató
recipes.description: Catalan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Divide the fresh mató (or ricotta) cheese into four shallow bowls or plates.
Drizzle generously with honey over the top of each portion.
Sprinkle with toasted walnuts or pine nuts.
Add a light dusting of ground cinnamon and serve immediately at room temperature.
cheapTips: Substitute ricotta or even Greek yogurt for mató to reduce cost.
Buy honey and nuts in bulk from warehouse stores.

recipes.name: Escaleta
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Season the pork chops with salt and pepper, then brown them in olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat for 4 minutes per side.
Remove the chops and set aside, then sauté diced onion and minced garlic in the same pot for 4 minutes until golden.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, then deglaze the pot with white wine, scraping up browned bits.
Return the pork chops to the pot and add the broth, bay leaf, and thyme.
Bring to a simmer, then cover and reduce heat to low, simmering gently for 25-30 minutes until the pork is very tender.
Remove the bay leaf and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Transfer the pork chops to serving plates and spoon the reduced sauce over top.
cheapTips: Buy pork chops on sale and freeze them; they maintain quality well.
Use water mixed with bouillon instead of store-bought broth to save money.

recipes.name: Bacallà à la Llauna
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak the salt cod in cold water for 24 hours, changing the water several times, then cut into serving pieces and pat dry.
Peel and cut potatoes into 1-inch cubes and boil in salted water for 8 minutes, then drain.
Heat olive oil in a large baking pan or shallow pot over medium heat and sauté thinly sliced onion and minced garlic for 4 minutes until softened.
Stir in tomato paste and paprika, then cook for 1 minute to combine the flavors.
Add the parboiled potatoes to the pan and toss gently in the oil mixture.
Arrange the salt cod pieces on top of the potatoes, add the bay leaf, and season with black pepper.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes, or bake covered at 400°F for 15 minutes, until the fish flakes easily with a fork.
Remove the bay leaf, taste and adjust seasoning, then serve directly from the pan.
cheapTips: Buy salt cod in bulk from ethnic grocery stores or online for better prices.
Skip fresh fish—salt cod is already economical and stores indefinitely when dry.

recipes.name: Xató
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: If using salt cod, soak it in cold water for 24 hours changing water several times; if using fresh cod, poach it in water for 8 minutes until cooked through, then flake into chunks.
Wash and dry the escarole or chicory, then tear into bite-sized pieces and place on a large serving platter.
Arrange the flaked cod, tuna, anchovies, olives, roasted red pepper strips, and tomato wedges over the greens.
Make the xató sauce by mashing the garlic with salt in a mortar, then whisking in olive oil, vinegar, and pepper until emulsified.
Drizzle the xató sauce over the entire salad or serve on the side for individual dressing.
Toss gently just before serving to combine all ingredients evenly.
cheapTips: Use canned tuna and jarred roasted peppers to save time and money on fresh ingredients.
Buy escarole in season when it's cheapest.

recipes.name: Esgarraet
recipes.description: Catalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: If using fresh or salt cod, cook it by poaching in water for 8 minutes, then flake into bite-sized pieces and let cool.
Roast the red peppers directly over a flame or under a broiler until charred on all sides, then place in a plastic bag for 5 minutes to steam.
Peel away the charred skin from the peppers and remove the seeds, then cut into thin strips.
Thinly slice the red onion and separate into rings.
Segment the orange by slicing off the peel and pith, then cutting between the membranes to release the segments.
In a large bowl, combine the flaked cod, roasted pepper strips, onion rings, and orange segments.
Whisk together olive oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper, then pour over the salad and toss gently to combine.
Let sit for 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld, then serve at room temperature.
cheapTips: Use canned cod packed in water instead of fresh or salt cod to save money.
Buy bell peppers when on sale and freeze them; they work just as well roasted.

recipes.name: Porrusalda
recipes.description: Basque lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut leeks into 1-inch rounds and potatoes into ½-inch cubes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add potatoes and leeks, then pour in vegetable broth and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 20 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season broth with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Add cod fillets and poach gently for 8-10 minutes until fish flakes easily.
Serve hot in bowls with broth and vegetables.
cheapTips: Use frozen cod fillets to save 30%
Buy leeks in season or substitute onions

recipes.name: Pintxos de Queso
recipes.description: Basque snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice baguette into ¼-inch thick diagonal pieces.
Rub each slice lightly with cut garlic and brush with olive oil.
Toast bread slices in a toaster oven at 400°F for 3-4 minutes until golden.
Cut manchego cheese into thin slices and place one on each toast.
Top each with a piece of roasted red pepper and one anchovy fillet.
Drizzle with remaining olive oil and sprinkle with paprika.
Serve immediately at room temperature.
cheapTips: Use canned roasted peppers instead of fresh
Substitute with Spanish cheese blend if manchego is expensive

recipes.name: Merluza a la Kaixo
recipes.description: Basque lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut potatoes into small cubes and boil separately until just tender, then drain.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet and sauté minced garlic and diced onion until softened.
Add white wine and vegetable broth, then bring to a simmer.
Gently place fish fillets in the broth, skin-side down, and cook 6-8 minutes.
Add cooked potatoes and peas, stirring gently to avoid breaking the fish.
Season with salt and pepper and cook for another 3-4 minutes.
Transfer to serving plates and garnish with fresh parsley.
cheapTips: Substitute white wine with white vinegar
Use frozen peas to reduce cost

recipes.name: Oreja a la Plancha
recipes.description: Basque lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean pork ears thoroughly and boil for 20 minutes to tenderize, then drain and cool.
Cut ears into thin slices or strips.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and add minced garlic.
Add sliced onion and cook until soft, about 3 minutes.
Place ear strips on the griddle and cook 3-4 minutes per side until crispy and browned.
Season with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Finish with fresh parsley and a squeeze of lemon juice before serving.
cheapTips: Source pork ears from local butcher at discount
Buy in bulk and freeze for meal prep

recipes.name: Bonito del Norte en Escabeche
recipes.description: Basque lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Season tuna steaks with salt on both sides.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear tuna steaks 3-4 minutes per side until light golden, then set aside.
In a saucepan, heat remaining olive oil and sauté sliced onion and garlic until soft.
Add vinegar, bay leaves, thyme, and peppercorns, bringing to a simmer.
Layer cooked tuna and onion mixture in a glass container, alternating layers.
Pour pickling liquid over all, cool to room temperature, cover, and refrigerate at least 8 hours before serving.
cheapTips: Use canned albacore tuna instead of fresh steaks
Make ahead to save on preparation time later

recipes.name: Callos a la Vizcaína
recipes.description: Basque lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean tripe thoroughly, boil for 1 hour until tender, then cut into small pieces.
Soak dried red peppers in hot water for 10 minutes, remove seeds, and blend into a paste.
Heat olive oil and sauté diced onion and garlic until soft.
Add sliced chorizo and cook for 3 minutes to release oils.
Stir in paprika and red pepper paste, cooking for 2 minutes.
Add cooked tripe, white wine, and beef broth, bringing to a simmer.
Cook for 30 minutes, then add morcilla pieces and simmer 15 minutes more.
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot in bowls.
cheapTips: Buy tripe from butcher counter at significant discount
Substitute morcilla with chorizo if unavailable

recipes.name: Chorizo a la Sidra
recipes.description: Basque dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice chorizo sausages into thick rounds.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté sliced onion and minced garlic until soft, about 3 minutes.
Add chorizo slices and cook for 5 minutes until browned on the edges.
Pour in apple cider, add bay leaf and thyme.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes until cider reduces by half and chorizo is cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper, remove bay leaf and thyme, and serve hot with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Use store-brand chorizo instead of imported
Substitute with cider vinegar if cider unavailable

recipes.name: Daube Provençale
recipes.description: Provençal dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice bacon and cook in a Dutch oven until crispy, then remove and set aside.
Cut beef into 1.5-inch cubes and brown in bacon fat in batches, then remove.
Sauté pearl onions and mushrooms until golden, then push aside.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste, stirring for 1 minute.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits.
Return beef to pot with bacon, add carrots, thyme, and bay leaves.
Cover and braise in a 325°F oven for 2-2.5 hours until beef is very tender.
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use beef chuck instead of more expensive cuts
Buy frozen pearl onions to save prep time

recipes.name: Brandade de Morue
recipes.description: Provençal lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak salt cod in cold water for 24 hours, changing water several times.
Boil potatoes and cod separately until tender, about 20 minutes each, then drain.
Flake the cooked cod, removing any remaining bones.
Peel and mash hot potatoes with minced garlic.
Heat olive oil and milk together until warm.
Combine potatoes and cod, then gradually beat in warm oil and milk mixture until fluffy.
Season with lemon juice, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Serve warm with toasted bread slices or crackers.
cheapTips: Buy salt cod in bulk from ethnic markets
Prepare a day ahead to save time

recipes.name: Tapenade
recipes.description: Provençal snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pit Kalamata olives if not already pitted.
Add olives, capers, anchovies, and minced garlic to a food processor.
Pulse until chunky (not completely smooth).
Add olive oil and lemon juice and pulse a few more times to combine.
Transfer to a bowl and stir in fresh thyme and black pepper.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve with crackers, bread, or crudités.
cheapTips: Buy canned olives and capers instead of fresh
Make in bulk and store in oil for 2 weeks

recipes.name: Pissaladière
recipes.description: Provençal snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and salt to form a soft dough, then let rest 20 minutes.
Thinly slice onions and garlic, then sauté in 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium-low heat for 25 minutes until very soft and golden.
Season the caramelized onions with thyme, salt, and pepper.
Press dough into an oiled 9x13 inch baking pan.
Spread caramelized onions evenly over dough.
Arrange anchovies in a crosshatch pattern over onions, then scatter olives between the strips.
Bake at 425°F for 15 minutes until crust is golden brown.
Cool for 5 minutes, cut into squares, and serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Use canned anchovies instead of fresh for better value
Buy onions in bulk when on sale and caramelize a large batch to freeze

recipes.name: Socca
recipes.description: Provençal snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk chickpea flour, water, salt, pepper, and onion powder together until smooth, then let rest 10 minutes.
Heat 1.5 tablespoons olive oil in a 10-inch cast iron skillet or nonstick pan over medium-high heat.
Pour half the batter into the hot pan and spread thin with a spatula.
Sprinkle with rosemary and cook 3-4 minutes until edges lift and bottom is golden.
Flip and cook another 2 minutes until set, then transfer to a plate.
Repeat with remaining oil and batter.
Cut into wedges and serve hot with salt and pepper.
cheapTips: Buy chickpea flour in bulk bins rather than packaged
Use dried rosemary if fresh is unavailable or expensive

recipes.name: Aïoli
recipes.description: Provençal lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mash garlic cloves with salt into a paste using a mortar or bowl.
Add egg yolk to garlic and whisk, then add olive oil one drop at a time while whisking continuously until emulsified, then add oil in a thin stream.
Whisk in lemon juice and adjust seasoning.
Boil potatoes, carrots, and green beans separately until just tender, about 15 minutes.
Gently poach cod fillets in simmering water for 8 minutes until cooked through.
Arrange vegetables and fish on a serving platter.
Serve aïoli alongside for dipping, with bread on the side.
cheapTips: Make aïoli with neutral oil like vegetable oil instead of premium olive oil
Use frozen cod instead of fresh to reduce costs

recipes.name: Soupe à l'Oignon Gratinée
recipes.description: Provençal lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice onions thin and cook in butter over medium heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized.
Pour in wine and scrape up browned bits, then cook 2 minutes.
Add broth, bay leaf, and thyme, then simmer 15 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and discard bay leaf and thyme sprigs.
Toast baguette slices in a 400°F oven for 3 minutes.
Ladle soup into oven-safe bowls, place a toast slice on top, and cover generously with gruyere.
Bake at 400°F for 8 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Serve immediately with caution as bowls will be very hot.
cheapTips: Use vegetable broth instead of beef broth for savings
Buy onions when on sale and caramelize in bulk to freeze

recipes.name: Bouillie de Châtaignes
recipes.description: Provençal breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Halve roasted chestnuts and add to a pot with milk and water.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat and cook 20 minutes until chestnuts begin to soften.
Mash chestnuts roughly with a potato masher or immersion blender to create a thick, chunky porridge.
Stir in honey, salt, vanilla, and cinnamon.
Simmer 2 more minutes while stirring until heated through.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot, optionally with more cinnamon on top.
cheapTips: Buy roasted, peeled chestnuts in bulk during fall season and freeze
Use evaporated milk instead of fresh milk for richer flavor at lower cost

recipes.name: Panisse
recipes.description: Provençal snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring water, salt, and olive oil to a boil in a saucepan.
Whisk chickpea flour gradually into boiling water, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat to low and cook 15-20 minutes, stirring frequently with a wooden spoon, until very thick and pulls away from pan sides.
Pour mixture into an oiled 8x8 inch pan and cool to room temperature, then refrigerate 2 hours until firm.
Cut into thick fries or rectangles, then dust with pepper and minced garlic.
Heat oil in a skillet to 350°F and fry panisse pieces 2 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with salt.
cheapTips: Buy chickpea flour from bulk sections for 30-40% savings
Reuse frying oil several times before discarding

recipes.name: Fougasse
recipes.description: Provençal breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix yeast, sugar, and warm water, then let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Combine flour and salt, then add yeast mixture and 2 tablespoons olive oil, mixing until a sticky dough forms.
Knead dough on a floured surface 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place in an oiled bowl, cover with a towel, and let rise 45 minutes until doubled.
Shape dough into an oval, then use a knife to cut a pattern of diagonal slits across the top without cutting through completely.
Place on an oiled baking sheet, brush with remaining olive oil, sprinkle with rosemary and sea salt, then let rise 15 minutes.
Bake at 400°F for 20-25 minutes until golden brown and hollow-sounding when tapped.
Cool on a wire rack for 10 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Buy yeast in bulk and store in freezer to use over many months
Use dried rosemary if fresh is unavailable

recipes.name: Calisson d'Aix
recipes.description: Provençal snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Finely chop almonds, candied melon, and candied orange peel together in a food processor.
Mix ground mixture with 1 cup powdered sugar, then bind with egg white and water to form a smooth paste.
Roll paste between two sheets of parchment to 1/4 inch thickness.
Cut into diamond or oval shapes using a small cookie cutter.
Place wafer paper on a baking sheet and arrange calissons on top, leaving small gaps.
Dust generously with remaining powdered sugar.
Dry in a 275°F oven for 10 minutes until surface is set but not browned.
Cool completely, then store in an airtight container.
cheapTips: Buy candied fruits from bulk bins instead of packaged
Make in larger batches and store for weeks to spread overhead costs

recipes.name: Soupe au Pistou
recipes.description: Provençal lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat, then sauté diced onions 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook 1 minute more until fragrant.
Stir in diced zucchini, green beans, and carrots, then cook 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes with juice and broth, then bring to a boil.
Add pasta and beans, then simmer 12 minutes until pasta is tender.
While soup cooks, blend fresh basil, 3 tablespoons olive oil, parmesan cheese, and 1 garlic clove in a food processor to make pistou.
Stir pistou into soup just before serving.
Ladle into bowls and top with extra parmesan and crusty bread.
cheapTips: Use dried basil in winter when fresh is expensive; use 1 tablespoon
Buy pasta in bulk to reduce per-serving costs

recipes.name: Poutine Niçoise
recipes.description: Provençal snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat whitebait dry with paper towels.
Mix flour, salt, and pepper in a shallow bowl.
Toss whitebait in flour mixture until lightly coated, shaking off excess.
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350°F.
Fry whitebait in batches 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy, being careful not to overcrowd the pan.
Drain on paper towels and season with additional salt immediately.
Transfer to a serving bowl, squeeze fresh lemon juice over top, and sprinkle with chopped parsley.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and crusty bread.
cheapTips: Buy frozen whitebait to save 20-30% compared to fresh
Reuse frying oil multiple times before discarding

recipes.name: Quenelles de Brochets
recipes.description: Provençal dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Make a béchamel sauce by melting 2 tablespoons butter, whisking in flour, then gradually adding milk while stirring constantly until thickened.
Finely grind or process the pike fillets until paste-like, then combine with béchamel, one egg, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Chill the mixture for 30 minutes, then shape into quenelle ovals using two warm spoons.
Bring fish broth to a gentle simmer and poach quenelles for 12-15 minutes until they float and hold their shape.
Remove quenelles with a slotted spoon and keep warm on a serving platter.
Strain 2 cups of poaching liquid into a saucepan and reduce by half over medium heat.
Whisk the remaining egg with cream, then slowly temper it into the reduced liquid while stirring constantly.
Finish the sauce with 2 tablespoons butter and pour over the warm quenelles before serving.
cheapTips: Use cod or tilapia instead of pike for 30% savings
Make béchamel from scratch rather than buying cream sauce mixes

recipes.name: Navarin d'Agneau
recipes.description: Provençal dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the lamb chunks on all sides for 5 minutes, then remove.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in the same pot until softened, then stir in tomato paste for 1 minute.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits, then return lamb to the pot with broth and rosemary.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes until lamb is nearly tender.
Cut carrots into chunks and potatoes into quarters, then add both to the pot along with pearl onions.
Simmer uncovered for another 30-35 minutes until vegetables are tender and sauce reduces slightly.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, remove rosemary sprigs, and serve hot in bowls with the sauce.
cheapTips: Use lamb neck instead of shoulder for half the price
Buy frozen pearl onions to save prep time and money

recipes.name: Crust aux Anchois
recipes.description: Provençal snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice the baguette diagonally into 12 thin pieces and arrange on a baking sheet.
Toast under the broiler for 2-3 minutes per side until lightly golden, then remove.
Mash the anchovies with minced garlic and olive oil using a fork until paste-like.
Spread the anchovy mixture generously on each toasted bread slice.
Drizzle with fresh lemon juice and garnish with chopped parsley before serving.
cheapTips: Use canned anchovies in salt and rinse them to reduce sodium and save money
Make with day-old baguette from bakery discount bins

recipes.name: Suquet de Poisson
recipes.description: Provençal dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion, minced garlic, and sliced fennel until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add diced potatoes, canned tomato with juice, and saffron steeped in warm broth, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are partially cooked.
Add white fish fillets and shrimp to the pot, nestling them into the broth, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Add mussels and simmer uncovered for another 5-8 minutes until shells open, discarding any that don't.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper, then serve hot in wide bowls with broth and seafood.
cheapTips: Skip saffron and use turmeric for similar color at 1/10 the cost
Buy frozen shrimp and mussels when fresh options are expensive

recipes.name: Ensalada Malagueña
recipes.description: Andalusian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil salted water and poach the cod fillets for 8-10 minutes until cooked through, then drain and cool slightly.
Flake the cooled fish into bite-sized pieces with a fork.
Peel oranges and segment them, removing white pith, then chop tomatoes and slice red onion thinly.
Toss romaine lettuce with orange segments, tomatoes, red onion, olives, and flaked fish in a large bowl.
Whisk together olive oil, sherry vinegar, salt, and pepper, then drizzle over the salad and toss gently before serving.
cheapTips: Use frozen cod fillets which are cheaper and work equally well
Buy seasonal oranges for 40% less cost

recipes.name: Boquerones en Vinagre
recipes.description: Andalusian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean fresh anchovies by removing heads and guts, then rinse thoroughly under cold water and pat dry.
Split each anchovy in half lengthwise and gently remove the backbone, leaving two fillets connected at the tail.
Layer anchovy fillets in a glass bowl, sprinkling salt between layers, then cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Rinse the salted anchovies under cold water and arrange them in a single layer in a clean glass jar.
Heat vinegar with water and minced garlic, then pour over the anchovies and cool to room temperature.
Once cooled, pour olive oil over the anchovies, sprinkle with parsley and red pepper flakes, then refrigerate for at least 3 hours before serving as a cold appetizer.
cheapTips: Buy whole fresh anchovies from fish counter rather than pre-cleaned
Make larger batches to reduce per-serving cost

recipes.name: Espárrago Triguero
recipes.description: Andalusian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse asparagus and snap off the tough woody bottoms by bending each spear until it breaks naturally.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and add minced garlic and red pepper flakes.
Once fragrant, add the asparagus spears and sauté for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and lightly browned.
Sprinkle with smoked paprika and salt, toss to coat, then cook for another minute.
Transfer to a serving plate, drizzle with fresh lemon juice, and serve hot as a side dish or light lunch.
cheapTips: Buy in-season asparagus from farmers markets for 50% savings
Use regular asparagus if wild varieties are unavailable

recipes.name: Berenjenas con Miel
recipes.description: Andalusian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut eggplants lengthwise into 0.5-inch thick slices and sprinkle with salt, then let sit for 15 minutes to draw out moisture.
Pat eggplant slices dry with paper towels, then brush both sides lightly with olive oil.
Heat remaining olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and fry eggplant slices in batches for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown, then transfer to a paper towel.
In the same skillet, sauté minced garlic for 1 minute, then add honey and vinegar, stirring to combine.
Layer fried eggplant slices on a serving platter and drizzle with the honey-vinegar sauce.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and let cool to room temperature before serving as a warm or cold appetizer.
cheapTips: Buy eggplants from discount bins when they have minor blemishes
Make in larger batches to freeze and serve later

recipes.name: Albóndigas en Salsa de Almendra
recipes.description: Andalusian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast almonds in a dry skillet for 3 minutes until fragrant, then grind 0.5 cup finely in a food processor.
Combine ground beef with minced onion, minced garlic, bread crumbs, egg, ground almonds, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Roll the mixture into 12-16 balls about the size of walnuts.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet and brown the meatballs on all sides for 5 minutes, then set aside.
Blend remaining whole almonds with beef broth and saffron until smooth, then pour into the skillet with meatballs.
Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 20 minutes until meatballs are cooked through and sauce thickens slightly.
Garnish with chopped parsley and serve hot with bread or rice.
cheapTips: Substitute half the almonds with inexpensive peanuts
Buy raw almonds in bulk from warehouse stores

recipes.name: Porra Antequerana
recipes.description: Andalusian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Core tomatoes and blanch in boiling water for 30 seconds, then transfer to ice water and peel away skin.
Cut peeled tomatoes in half, squeeze out seeds, then roughly chop the flesh.
Heat olive oil in a skillet and sauté minced garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped tomatoes to the skillet and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until very soft and thickened into a paste.
Season the tomato paste with salt to taste, then toast the bread slices until golden brown.
Spread the warm tomato paste generously on each toast slice, then top with jamón serrano and thin shavings of Manchego cheese before serving.
cheapTips: Omit jamón and cheese for vegetarian version costing 1.50 per serving
Use day-old bread from bakery discounts

recipes.name: Remolacha con Naranja
recipes.description: Andalusian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil unpeeled beets in salted water for 35-40 minutes until tender when pierced with a fork.
Drain beets, cool slightly, then peel under running water and cut into thin slices or wedges.
Peel oranges and segment them over a bowl to catch the juice, removing white pith.
Whisk together olive oil, vinegar, cumin, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Arrange beets and orange segments on a platter, alternating them.
Pour dressing over the salad and sprinkle with fresh parsley.
Let rest 10 minutes at room temperature before serving.
cheapTips: Buy beets in bulk during fall/winter when cheaper
Use canned beets to save time (rinse well first)

recipes.name: Chanquetes Fritos
recipes.description: Andalusian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse the small fish and pat completely dry with paper towels.
Mix flour, salt, pepper, and paprika in a shallow bowl.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pot or skillet, testing temperature with a wooden spoon (should bubble immediately).
Toss fish in the flour mixture in batches, shaking off excess.
Carefully add fish to hot oil in small batches and fry 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon to paper towels to drain.
Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges and garnish with parsley.
cheapTips: Buy frozen whitebait as a budget substitute, thaw and drain well
Reuse frying oil through a fine strainer for next use

recipes.name: Camarones
recipes.description: Andalusian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, stirring constantly.
Add shrimp to the skillet and cook for 1 minute on each side until starting to turn pink.
Sprinkle paprika and red pepper flakes over the shrimp and stir well.
Pour in white wine and squeeze lemon juice, cooking for another 2-3 minutes until shrimp are fully cooked and opaque.
Season with salt and taste for seasoning.
Serve hot in a bowl or on crusty bread, garnished with fresh parsley.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp in bulk and thaw overnight in fridge
Skip the wine and use extra lemon juice to save money

recipes.name: Atún en Adobo
recipes.description: Andalusian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and sear fresh tuna steaks on both sides for 2 minutes per side; set aside (skip if using canned tuna).
In the same skillet, toast cumin seeds and peppercorns for 1 minute, then add minced garlic and cook until fragrant.
Add paprika, salt, bay leaves, and stir to combine.
Pour in vinegar and water, bringing to a simmer.
Return tuna to the pan (or add canned tuna, breaking into chunks), reduce heat to low, and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
The liquid should reduce by half and tuna should be tender and infused with adobo flavors.
Let cool slightly, then serve warm or at room temperature with the adobo sauce spooned over.
cheapTips: Use canned tuna packed in oil for significant savings
Toast whole spices in a dry pan first to intensify flavor and use less

recipes.name: Espaldilla de Cordero Asada
recipes.description: Andalusian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and remove lamb from refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking.
Make a paste with garlic, paprika, cumin, salt, pepper, and olive oil, then rub all over the lamb shoulder.
Place lamb in a roasting pan with rosemary and thyme sprigs tucked underneath and around the meat.
Pour wine and beef broth into the pan around the lamb (not over it).
Cover tightly with foil and roast for 2 hours, basting with pan liquid every 30 minutes.
Remove foil, increase oven to 425°F, and roast uncovered for 20-30 minutes until skin is golden and crackling.
Tent with foil and rest for 15 minutes before carving, then serve with pan drippings as sauce.
cheapTips: Buy bone-in shoulder cuts rather than boneless for more flavor and lower cost
Use water instead of wine if budget is tight, add extra herbs

recipes.name: Chivo Guisado
recipes.description: Andalusian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season goat meat with salt and pepper, then brown in batches, about 3-4 minutes per side; set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onion until softened, about 5 minutes, then add garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cumin, cooking for 2 minutes to deepen flavors.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up browned bits, and reduce by half.
Return meat to pot with bay leaves, thyme, and beef broth; bring to a simmer, cover, and cook 90 minutes.
Add potatoes and continue simmering covered for 30 minutes until meat and potatoes are very tender.
Season to taste with salt and pepper, and serve hot in bowls with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Substitute lamb or beef if goat is unavailable; increase cooking time slightly for beef
Use store-brand broth and skip the wine for significant savings

recipes.name: Rabo Guisado
recipes.description: Andalusian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 325°F and heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season oxtail with salt and pepper, then brown on all sides in batches, about 4 minutes total per batch; set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the pot and cook 5-6 minutes until softened and caramelized.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute, then stir in tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits, and reduce by half.
Return oxtail to pot with bay leaves, thyme, and beef broth; bring to a simmer.
Cover tightly and braise in oven for 90 minutes until meat is fork-tender.
Remove from oven, season to taste, and serve hot with the braising liquid spooned over.
cheapTips: Oxtail is inexpensive compared to other cuts; ask butcher to cut it
Make a double batch and freeze half for future quick dinners

recipes.name: Espinacas a la Andaluza
recipes.description: Andalusian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and add minced garlic, cooking 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add pine nuts and toast for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Add raisins and cumin, stirring to combine.
Add chopped spinach in batches, stirring after each addition until wilted (about 3-4 minutes total).
Season with salt and pepper, then squeeze fresh lemon juice over the top.
Stir gently to combine and serve warm as a side dish.
cheapTips: Use frozen spinach (thawed and squeezed dry) to save time and money
Buy pine nuts in bulk or substitute with sunflower seeds for budget cooking

recipes.name: Habas a la Rondeña
recipes.description: Andalusian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced jamón, cooking for 2 minutes until jamón releases its fat.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes to deepen the flavor.
Pour in white wine and scrape up any browned bits, then reduce by half.
Add the fava beans, chicken broth, and bay leaf; bring to a simmer.
Cook uncovered for 20-25 minutes until beans are tender and liquid has reduced slightly.
Season with salt and pepper (go easy on salt as jamón provides saltiness), garnish with fresh parsley, and serve warm.
cheapTips: Use frozen fava beans year-round instead of fresh; they're cheaper and already shelled
Substitute bacon for jamón for significant cost savings while maintaining flavor

recipes.name: Weißwurst
recipes.description: Bavarian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix ground pork, ground pork fat, milk, parsley, chives, salt, white pepper, ginger, and mace in a bowl, refrigerating for 30 minutes.
Soak hog casings in warm water for 10 minutes to soften, then gently rinse and allow water to drain.
Fill a sausage stuffer with the meat mixture and carefully fill casings, tying off both ends; avoid overstuffing to prevent bursting.
Gently poke holes in each sausage with a sterilized pin to prevent bursting during cooking.
Heat beef broth or water to 160-170°F (below a full boil) in a large pot.
Carefully place sausages in the hot liquid and poach for 15 minutes, maintaining water temperature (do not boil).
Remove sausages with a slotted spoon and serve immediately while warm with sweet mustard and fresh pretzels.
cheapTips: Ask butcher to grind pork shoulder and fat together instead of buying separately
Skip fresh herbs and use 1 teaspoon dried parsley and 1/2 teaspoon dried chives to reduce cost

recipes.name: Kaiserschmarrn
recipes.description: Bavarian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Separate egg whites from yolks and beat whites until stiff peaks form.
Whisk yolks with milk, flour, salt, and sugar until smooth.
Gently fold egg whites into the batter in two additions.
Heat 2 tablespoons butter in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Pour batter into skillet and cook for 3-4 minutes until golden, then flip and cook 2 minutes more.
Tear the pancake into bite-sized pieces using two wooden spoons.
Heat remaining butter and toss pancake pieces in skillet for 2 minutes until golden.
Transfer to plate, dust with powdered sugar, and serve with warm plum jam.
cheapTips: Buy store-brand jam instead of premium brands
Use basic all-purpose flour rather than specialty flours

recipes.name: Knödel
recipes.description: Bavarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until partially cooked, then peel and grate them.
Mix grated potatoes with flour, eggs, salt, pepper, nutmeg, and parsley until combined.
Let mixture rest for 10 minutes, then shape into 8-10 balls about 2 inches diameter.
Bring a large pot of salted water to boil.
Gently drop knödel into boiling water and cook until they float, then continue cooking 3-4 minutes more.
Remove with a slotted spoon and serve hot with braised red cabbage or roasted meat.
cheapTips: Buy potatoes in bulk from discount stores
Use dried parsley if fresh is expensive

recipes.name: Obatzda
recipes.description: Bavarian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Remove camembert from refrigerator and let sit 5 minutes to soften.
Finely dice the onion.
In a bowl, mix softened camembert with butter until creamy.
Fold in diced onion, paprika, caraway seeds, salt, and pepper.
Transfer to serving bowl and drizzle with a little olive oil if desired.
Serve at room temperature with sliced pretzel bread and crackers.
cheapTips: Buy camembert when on sale and refrigerate until needed
Make your own pretzel bread or use store-brand

recipes.name: Flädlesuppe
recipes.description: Bavarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk eggs, flour, milk, salt, and pepper together until smooth batter forms.
Heat butter in a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Pour a thin layer of batter into skillet and tilt to spread evenly, cooking 1-2 minutes per side until light golden.
Repeat until all batter is used, stacking finished crêpes on a plate.
Let crêpes cool slightly, then roll and cut into thin strips.
Bring beef broth to simmer in a large pot.
Add crêpe strips and parsley to hot broth and heat through for 2-3 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chives.
cheapTips: Use store-brand beef broth to save money
Skip fresh chives and use dried if necessary

recipes.name: Käsespätzle
recipes.description: Bavarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, eggs, salt, and water together to form thick, sticky batter.
Bring a large pot of salted water to rolling boil.
Using a spätzle maker or perforated spoon, press batter through holes into boiling water.
Cook spätzle until they float, then cook 2 minutes more, then drain in colander.
While spätzle cook, slice onion and cook in butter over medium heat until golden and caramelized, about 10 minutes.
In a baking dish, layer half the spätzle, then half the cheese, then remaining spätzle and cheese.
Sprinkle with black pepper and pour caramelized onions with butter over top.
Heat in 375°F oven for 10 minutes until cheese melts and top is golden, then garnish with parsley.
cheapTips: Use shredded cheddar or gouda instead of gruyere
Skip the oven step and just toss warm spätzle with cheese and onions

recipes.name: Erdäpfelsuppe
recipes.description: Bavarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and dice potatoes into 0.5-inch cubes.
Dice onion, celery, and carrot into small pieces.
Melt butter in large pot over medium heat and sauté onion, celery, and carrot for 5 minutes.
Add diced potatoes and vegetable broth, then bring to boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes until potatoes are very tender.
Partially mash soup with potato masher to create creamy but chunky texture.
Season with salt, pepper, and marjoram.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley.
cheapTips: Buy potatoes in bulk from discount grocers
Use dried parsley if fresh herbs are expensive

recipes.name: Leberknödelsuppe
recipes.description: Bavarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Finely chop beef liver and onion together.
Combine chopped liver and onion with ground pork, bread cubes, egg, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Form mixture into 8-10 balls about 1.5 inches diameter.
Bring beef broth to gentle boil in large pot.
Carefully drop liver knödel into broth and reduce heat to simmer.
Cook for 15-20 minutes until knödel are cooked through and tender.
Test doneness by cutting one open to check that interior is no longer pink.
Serve hot in bowls with broth.
cheapTips: Buy liver on sale and freeze for later use
Use store-brand bread instead of bakery bread

recipes.name: Schweinshaxe in Biersoße
recipes.description: Bavarian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 325°F and pat pork shanks dry with paper towels.
Heat olive oil in large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown shanks on all sides, 10-12 minutes total, then remove and set aside.
Chop onion, carrot, and celery into large chunks and add to pot, cooking 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in tomato paste and cook 1 minute, then deglaze with beer, scraping up any browned bits.
Add broth, bay leaves, salt, and pepper, then return shanks to pot.
Cover and braise in oven for 2 hours until meat is very tender and falling off bone.
Transfer shanks to plate, strain braising liquid through fine sieve into saucepan, and simmer 10 minutes to reduce and intensify flavor.
Serve shanks with sauce spooned over, accompanied by mashed potatoes or bread dumplings.
cheapTips: Buy pork shanks when on sale and freeze until ready to cook
Use domestic beer instead of imported German beer

recipes.name: Bauernkrapfen
recipes.description: Bavarian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk together flour, eggs, milk, salt, and sugar until smooth batter forms.
Cook minced onion in small skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes until softened, then fold into sauerkraut.
Heat vegetable oil in heavy skillet or deep fryer to 350°F.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into hot oil and fry until bottom is golden, about 2 minutes.
Flip krapfen and fry other side until golden, about 1.5 minutes more.
Remove with slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
While still warm, make a small slit in each krapfen and fill with a spoonful of sauerkraut mixture.
Dust lightly with powdered sugar and serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy sauerkraut in bulk jars instead of cans
Reuse cooking oil by straining and storing for next use

recipes.name: Semmelknödel
recipes.description: Bavarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut bread rolls into 0.5-inch cubes and place in large bowl.
Heat milk and pour over bread cubes, let soak 10 minutes until bread absorbs milk.
Mince onion finely and mix into soaked bread with eggs, parsley, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Let mixture rest 5 minutes so flavors combine.
Shape mixture into 8 balls about 2.5 inches diameter, squeezing gently to hold together.
Bring large pot of salted water to boil.
Gently drop knödel into boiling water and cook until they float, then continue cooking 2-3 minutes more.
Remove with slotted spoon and serve hot with meat stew or mushroom sauce.
cheapTips: Buy day-old bread rolls from bakery at discount
Use dried parsley if fresh is unavailable

recipes.name: Kugelhopf Salé
recipes.description: Alsatian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine warm milk, yeast, and sugar in a bowl and let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour and salt in a large bowl, then add yeast mixture, eggs, and melted butter, kneading for 8 minutes until smooth.
Dice bacon and onion, then sauté together until bacon is crispy and onions are soft.
Fold bacon mixture and caraway seeds into dough, then cover and let rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Shape dough into a ring and place in a greased kugelhopf mold, let rise 30 minutes.
Bake at 375°F for 35-40 minutes until golden brown.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.
cheapTips: Buy bacon ends and pieces instead of sliced bacon
Use store-brand yeast and flour for savings

recipes.name: Munster Cheese
recipes.description: Alsatian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice the Munster cheese into 1/4-inch thick slices.
Arrange cheese on a serving plate and sprinkle with caraway seeds and freshly cracked pepper.
Slice crusty bread and lightly butter if desired.
Serve cheese and bread together at room temperature, allowing flavors to develop.
cheapTips: Buy cheese from the deli counter by weight rather than pre-packaged

recipes.name: Flammes
recipes.description: Alsatian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 475°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Thinly slice onions and finely chop bacon, then sauté together in olive oil for 5 minutes until softened.
Divide pizza dough into 3 portions and stretch each into a thin oval shape on the prepared baking sheet.
Spread crème fraîche evenly over each dough oval, leaving a small border.
Top each with the bacon-onion mixture, then season with salt and pepper.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until edges are golden and crispy.
Cut into strips and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use store-bought pizza dough to save time and money
Buy bacon on sale and freeze for later use

recipes.name: Presskopf au Gelée
recipes.description: Alsatian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Place pork head and feet in a large pot with quartered onions, bay leaves, thyme, and salt, then cover with water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 3 hours until meat is very tender and falls from bones.
Strain cooking liquid through cheesecloth and reserve 4 cups; let meat cool then shred finely.
Bloom gelatin in cold water for 5 minutes, then dissolve in warm broth and season with salt and pepper.
Mix shredded meat with mustard, then pour into a terrine mold and add gelatin mixture.
Refrigerate overnight until set firm.
Unmold and slice thinly, serving with crusty bread and cornichons.
cheapTips: Buy pork head and feet from specialty butchers or ethnic markets where they're cheaper
Make stock from bones to use in other dishes

recipes.name: Biberlakaes
recipes.description: Alsatian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice onions and mince garlic, then sauté in a large pot until softened.
Add ground beef and pork, breaking up with a spoon and cooking until browned, about 8 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and paprika, cooking for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add beef broth, caraway seeds, salt, and pepper, then simmer for 45 minutes until flavors meld.
Meanwhile, cook egg noodles according to package directions and drain.
Stir sour cream into the meat mixture just before serving.
Serve meat ragout over warm egg noodles.
cheapTips: Buy ground meat in bulk when on sale and freeze
Use generic egg noodles instead of name brand

recipes.name: Chicken Paprikash
recipes.description: Hungarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and season chicken thighs with salt and pepper, then brown on both sides for 6 minutes total and remove.
Add diced onions and minced garlic to the pot, sautéing for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in paprika powder and tomato paste, cooking for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot, add chicken broth, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer for 40 minutes until chicken is tender.
Remove from heat and stir in sour cream until smooth.
Cook egg noodles separately and serve topped with chicken paprikash.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs instead of breasts—they're cheaper and more flavorful
Buy paprika in bulk from ethnic markets

recipes.name: Pörkölt
recipes.description: Hungarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut beef into 1.5-inch cubes and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy pot and brown beef in batches, then remove and set aside.
Add sliced onions to the pot and cook for 8 minutes until caramelized.
Stir in paprika and minced garlic, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to pot, add tomato paste and caraway seeds, then add beef broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours until beef is very tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve over cooked egg noodles.
cheapTips: Use chuck roast and cut it yourself to save money
Make a double batch and freeze half for later

recipes.name: Halaszle
recipes.description: Hungarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté sliced onions for 8 minutes until golden.
Add minced garlic and paprika powder, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and caraway seeds, then add broth and bring to a simmer.
Cut fish into 2-inch chunks and gently add to the simmering broth.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes until fish is cooked through and flakes easily.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve in bowls with crusty bread for dipping.
cheapTips: Use frozen fish fillets on sale instead of fresh
Mix different affordable white fish varieties

recipes.name: Langos
recipes.description: Hungarian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine warm water, yeast, and a pinch of sugar in a bowl and let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour and salt in a large bowl, add yeast mixture, and knead for 5 minutes until smooth.
Cover dough and let rise for 20 minutes until puffy.
Mince garlic and mix with melted butter and chopped parsley, then set aside.
Heat oil in a deep skillet or fryer to 350°F.
Stretch dough into strips and carefully fry in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and puffy.
Drain on paper towels and brush immediately with garlic-butter mixture while still warm.
cheapTips: Reuse frying oil multiple times before discarding
Make dough ahead and refrigerate until ready to fry

recipes.name: Flódni
recipes.description: Hungarian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Make dough by combining yeast with warm water and letting sit 5 minutes, then add flour, eggs, 2 tbsp butter, and salt, kneading until smooth.
Let dough rise for 45 minutes covered until doubled.
Prepare filling by mixing diced apples, chopped walnuts, raisins, sugar, and cinnamon.
Roll dough very thin on floured surface into a rectangle, then spread with remaining melted butter.
Spread apple-walnut mixture over half the dough, then plum jam over the other half.
Roll dough tightly from long end into a log, then coil into a spiral and place in a greased 9x13 pan.
Let rise 30 minutes, brush with beaten egg, and bake at 350°F for 40-45 minutes until golden brown.
Cool in pan for 15 minutes before slicing.
cheapTips: Buy bulk walnuts from discount grocers or ethnic markets
Use seasonal apples on sale

recipes.name: Schweinshaxe mit Kartoffelsalat
recipes.description: Bavarian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat pork shank dry and season generously with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat oil in a large pot and brown the shank on all sides until golden, about 12 minutes total.
Add chopped onion, carrot, and celery, and sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Pour in beef broth, cover, and simmer for 2 hours until meat is very tender.
Boil potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until just cooked through, then drain and slice while warm.
Dress warm sliced potatoes with vinegar, mustard, and 6 tbsp of the cooking broth, tossing gently.
Remove shank from pot and strain broth, reserving 1.5 cups for gravy.
Serve shank with potato salad and pan drippings on the side.
cheapTips: Buy pork shank on sale and freeze; it braises beautifully from frozen.
Make extra potato salad and serve as a side for 2-3 meals.

recipes.name: Leberkäse mit Kartoffelsalat
recipes.description: Bavarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until just tender, then drain and slice while still warm.
Whisk together mustard, vinegar, broth, and minced onion.
Toss warm potato slices with dressing and let sit for 10 minutes to absorb flavors.
Slice leberkäse into 0.5-inch thick slices and fry in oil for 3 minutes per side until heated through and lightly golden.
Arrange leberkäse slices on a plate with potato salad on the side.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve with extra mustard.
cheapTips: Leberkäse is affordable and shelf-stable at most butcher counters.
Make potato salad in bulk and serve over 2-3 days.

recipes.name: Rahmschwammerl
recipes.description: Bavarian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook egg noodles according to package directions in salted water, then drain and set aside.
Clean mushrooms with a damp cloth and slice into 0.5-inch pieces.
Melt butter in a large skillet and cook diced onion and minced garlic for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add mushroom slices and cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they release moisture and begin to brown.
Pour in white wine and cook for 1 minute, then add broth and simmer for 3 minutes.
Reduce heat to low and stir in cream, salt, and pepper, heating through without boiling for 2 minutes.
Toss cooked noodles with the mushroom cream sauce and garnish with fresh parsley.
Serve immediately while hot.
cheapTips: Buy mushroom mix when on sale and freeze for later use.
Substitute sour cream if cream is pricey.

recipes.name: Steckerlfisch
recipes.description: Bavarian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean each fish by gutting and rinsing thoroughly inside and out, then pat dry.
Season inside each fish with salt, pepper, thin lemon slices, and a sprig of dill.
Thread each fish lengthwise onto a stick or wooden skewer, inserting through mouth and tail.
Brush oil generously over each fish and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Grill over medium-high heat for 6 minutes per side until skin is crispy and flesh flakes easily.
Butter and toast bread slices alongside the fish or on a grill rack.
Serve fish still on skewer with toasted bread, lemon wedges, and fresh parsley.
cheapTips: Buy whole fish from Asian markets for significantly lower prices.
Leftover fish can be flaked into salads or pasta the next day.

recipes.name: Apfelstrudel
recipes.description: Bavarian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel, core, and slice apples thinly into a bowl; toss with lemon juice, sugar, cinnamon, raisins, and vanilla.
Melt butter in a small saucepan and brush a baking sheet with it.
Lay out first phyllo sheet on the baking sheet and brush lightly with melted butter.
Layer remaining phyllo sheets on top, brushing each with butter and sprinkling every other sheet with breadcrumbs.
Spread apple filling evenly across the phyllo layers, leaving a 1-inch border on all sides.
Roll up tightly from the long side, tucking in ends and placing seam-side down on the baking sheet.
Brush the top with remaining butter and bake at 375°F for 35-40 minutes until golden brown.
Cool for 10 minutes, then dust with powdered sugar and serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Phyllo dough is inexpensive and found in the frozen section.
Use any firm apples you have on hand if granny smith are pricey.

recipes.name: Baeckaoffa
recipes.description: Alsatian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork and beef into 1.5-inch cubes and season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pot and brown meat in batches for 3 minutes per side, then remove and set aside.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the pot and cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Layer half the cubed potatoes on the bottom of a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven.
Top with all the browned meat, then arrange remaining potatoes on top.
Pour wine and broth over everything, then add bay leaves and thyme sprigs.
Cover tightly with foil and a lid, then braise in a 325°F oven for 2.5 hours until meat is very tender.
Remove bay leaves and thyme, season to taste, and serve directly from the pot.
cheapTips: Use chuck roast cut into chunks instead of beef chuck for savings.
Make a double batch and freeze half for a future meal.

recipes.name: Fleischnacka
recipes.description: Alsatian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt, then add water gradually while kneading until a smooth dough forms; rest 20 minutes covered.
Brown ground pork with diced onion and minced garlic for 6 minutes, then stir in parsley, pepper, and salt to taste; cool slightly.
Divide dough into 4 pieces and roll each thin into an 8x10 inch rectangle on a floured surface.
Spread one-quarter of the meat filling across each dough rectangle.
Roll up tightly from the long side and shape into a coil, tucking the end underneath.
Heat oil in a large skillet and fry the coils over medium heat for 4 minutes per side until golden.
Serve hot with mustard and a simple salad.
cheapTips: Ground pork is often cheaper than beef at most stores.
Dough can be made ahead and refrigerated up to 24 hours.

recipes.name: Kugelhopf
recipes.description: Alsatian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Warm milk to 110°F and dissolve yeast in it; let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Cream butter and sugar together, then beat in eggs one at a time.
Mix flour and salt, then add to butter mixture alternating with yeast mixture, beating until smooth.
Fold in raisins, almonds, and vanilla extract gently.
Butter and flour a kugelhopf or bundt pan, then pour batter into it.
Cover with a damp towel and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Bake at 350°F for 35-40 minutes until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes, then invert onto a wire rack and dust with powdered sugar.
cheapTips: Buy nuts in bulk at warehouse stores for significant savings.
The cake keeps well for 2-3 days wrapped in plastic wrap.

recipes.name: Bretzel
recipes.description: Alsatian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Warm milk to 110°F and dissolve yeast with sugar; let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour and salt, then add butter and yeast mixture; knead until smooth, 8 minutes.
Let dough rise covered in a warm place for 45 minutes until doubled.
Divide dough into 8 pieces, roll each into a 24-inch long rope, and shape into pretzel form.
Bring water to a boil in a large pot and dissolve baking soda in it.
Boil each pretzel for 30 seconds per side, then place on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Brush boiled pretzels with water and sprinkle generously with coarse salt.
Bake at 425°F for 12-15 minutes until deep golden brown and serve warm.
cheapTips: Pretzels are inexpensive to make at home versus buying bakery pretzels.
Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

recipes.name: Wädele
recipes.description: Alsatian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Season pork shanks generously with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat a large pot over medium-high heat and sear shanks for 4 minutes per side until browned.
Remove shanks and set aside, then add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot; cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in wine and scrape up browned bits from the bottom, then simmer 2 minutes.
Return shanks to pot, add broth, mustard, bay leaves, and thyme, then bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise in a 325°F oven for 2 hours until meat is very tender and shreds easily.
Skim fat from the surface, remove bay leaves and thyme, season to taste, and serve shanks with braising liquid spooned over.
cheapTips: Pork fore shank is often cheaper than hind shank; braises identically.
Skim and save the fat for cooking or chill overnight and lift off for stock making.

recipes.name: Dobos Torte
recipes.description: Hungarian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line baking sheets with parchment paper.
Beat 4 eggs with 0.5 cup sugar until pale, fold in 0.5 cup flour, spread thin on baking sheets and bake 8-10 minutes until golden.
Repeat step 2 with remaining eggs and flour to make 8-10 thin cake layers.
Beat 1 cup softened butter with 1 cup sugar until fluffy, sift in cocoa powder and vanilla, mix until smooth.
Spread chocolate buttercream between cooled cake layers, stack them, and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat 0.5 cup sugar in a saucepan over medium heat without stirring until golden caramel forms.
Pour caramel over top layer in a thin sheet and mark into portions with an oiled knife while still warm.
Whip heavy cream with remaining sugar and pipe around torte edges as garnish before serving.
cheapTips: Buy store-brand butter and eggs in bulk
Make caramel layer with granulated sugar instead of specialty ingredients

recipes.name: Somloi Galuska
recipes.description: Hungarian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9-inch baking dish.
Beat 2 eggs with 0.25 cup sugar until pale, fold in 0.75 cup flour, pour into baking dish, and bake 15 minutes until set.
Beat remaining 2 eggs with 0.25 cup sugar and cocoa powder, fold in 0.75 cup flour, pour over first layer, and bake 15 minutes.
Toast walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes, chop coarsely, and layer over cooled cake with chocolate chips.
Heat milk with butter and 0.25 cup sugar, pour over the assembled layers so they absorb the liquid.
Chill for at least 30 minutes until layers set together.
Top with whipped cream and chocolate shavings before serving.
cheapTips: Use cocoa powder instead of chocolate bars for the layers
Substitute store-brand whipped cream for homemade to save time

recipes.name: Chimney Cake
recipes.description: Hungarian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk together flour, milk, eggs, melted butter, and salt until smooth batter forms.
Preheat a chimney cake mold (or cone-shaped form) over medium-high heat and butter it well.
