Dip the hot mold into batter to coat all sides evenly, then hold over heat for 1-2 minutes until bottom layer sets.
Repeat dipping and heating 5-6 times, building up layers around the mold.
Mix cinnamon, sugar, and finely chopped walnuts in a shallow bowl.
Remove baked chimney from mold when golden brown, immediately roll or coat in cinnamon-walnut mixture while still warm.
Cool on a wire rack for 5 minutes before serving warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Use a metal cone or aluminum foil cone rolled into a tube as a mold instead of specialty equipment
Buy walnuts from bulk bins to reduce cost

recipes.name: Lecso
recipes.description: Hungarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice peppers and tomatoes into 1-inch chunks, slice onion into wedges, and mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté onion and garlic for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add diced bell peppers and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Break up sausage and add to the pan, cooking until browned, about 8 minutes.
Stir in paprika and cook for 1 minute until color deepens.
Add tomatoes, salt, and pepper, then simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until peppers are tender and sauce thickens.
Taste and adjust seasonings, then serve hot as a main course or side dish.
cheapTips: Use budget sausage or ground meat instead of premium cuts
Buy peppers and tomatoes on sale and freeze for later use

recipes.name: Csipetke
recipes.description: Hungarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt in a bowl, make a well, add eggs and water, and stir until crumbly dough forms.
Bring chicken broth to a boil in a large pot, add butter and diced onion, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Holding dough over the boiling broth, pinch off small pieces (about the size of a pea) and drop them directly into the broth.
Continue pinching and dropping dough pieces until all dough is used, stirring occasionally.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes after adding all dough pieces until they float and are fully cooked.
Stir in chopped parsley and taste for seasoning, adjusting salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot as a comfort soup.
cheapTips: Use store-brand chicken broth to reduce costs
Make csipetke dough ahead and freeze for quick meals

recipes.name: Palacinta
recipes.description: Hungarian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk together flour and salt, then make a well and add eggs and milk gradually, stirring until smooth batter forms.
Heat a non-stick skillet or crepe pan over medium-high heat and lightly butter it.
Pour 0.25 cup batter into the center and immediately tilt the pan in all directions to spread into a thin circle.
Cook for about 1-2 minutes on the first side until light golden, then flip and cook another 30 seconds.
Transfer crepe to a plate and repeat with remaining batter.
Spread 1 tablespoon jam on the lower third of each crepe, roll tightly, and arrange seam-side down on a platter.
Top with a dollop of sour cream, dust with powdered sugar, and serve warm.
cheapTips: Use store-brand jam and sour cream to reduce costs
Make batter ahead and refrigerate for up to 24 hours before cooking

recipes.name: Hurka
recipes.description: Hungarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil pork shoulder and liver together in salted water for 45 minutes until fully cooked, then cool and grind or finely chop.
Dice fatback finely and mix with cooked ground meat.
Finely mince onion and garlic, sauté in a pan for 2 minutes until softened, then cool.
Mix ground meat with cooled onion-garlic mixture, paprika, salt, and pepper until well combined.
Stuff sausage casings with the meat mixture using a funnel and your fingers or a sausage stuffer.
Prick casings lightly with a pin to prevent bursting and place in a pot of simmering water.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes until casings are firm and hurka floats to the surface.
Drain and serve sliced with mustard and rye bread, either hot or cold.
cheapTips: Ask a butcher counter for trimmings to reduce meat cost
Buy sausage casings in bulk from online specialty suppliers

recipes.name: Paprika Chicken
recipes.description: Hungarian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper, then heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken thighs for 5-6 minutes per side until golden, then remove and set aside on a plate.
Dice onions and mince garlic, then sauté in the same pot for 4 minutes until softened.
Stir in paprika and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, then add chicken broth and return chicken to the pot.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 40 minutes until chicken is very tender.
Remove from heat and stir in sour cream until smooth and creamy.
Taste and adjust seasonings, then serve over egg noodles or with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs instead of breasts for better flavor and lower cost
Buy paprika in bulk at ethnic markets for savings

recipes.name: Stuffed Cabbage Roll
recipes.description: Hungarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and carefully peel off whole cabbage leaves, blanching them for 2 minutes until soft, then drain on paper towels.
Brown ground pork with diced onion and minced garlic in a skillet over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, breaking up meat as it cooks.
Stir in cooked rice, paprika, salt, and pepper, then remove from heat and let cool for 5 minutes.
Place 2-3 tablespoons of filling on each cabbage leaf, fold in sides, and roll tightly into a bundle.
Arrange rolls seam-side down in a 9x13-inch baking dish, then pour tomato sauce over the top.
Cover with foil and bake at 350°F for 45 minutes until rolls are heated through.
Drizzle sour cream on top before serving warm with extra sauce on the side.
cheapTips: Cook rice ahead of time to speed up assembly
Buy ground pork on sale and freeze for use in this recipe

recipes.name: Libamaj
recipes.description: Hungarian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice onions thinly and caramelize in a skillet with 2 tablespoons butter over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden.
Finely mince or grind chicken livers and transfer to a bowl.
Beat together remaining butter, egg, bread crumbs, paprika, salt, pepper, and allspice until smooth.
Fold caramelized onions into the liver mixture until well combined.
Transfer to a loaf pan lined with plastic wrap, press down firmly, cover with foil, and chill overnight in the refrigerator.
Unmold the pâté and slice thinly before serving.
Serve chilled on rye bread with mustard and cornichons as appetizer.
cheapTips: Buy chicken livers from budget meat counters or butchers
Make in a regular container if loaf pan is unavailable

recipes.name: Coq au Riesling
recipes.description: Alsatian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut bacon into lardons and render in a large Dutch oven over medium heat until crispy, then remove and set aside.
Season chicken pieces with salt and pepper, then brown them in the bacon fat in batches until golden on all sides, about 8 minutes per batch.
Remove chicken and sauté pearl onions and mushrooms in the same pot until lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables, stir well, and cook for 2 minutes to create a roux.
Pour in Riesling wine and chicken broth, scraping up browned bits from the bottom, then return chicken and bacon to the pot.
Add garlic cloves and thyme, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 45 minutes until chicken is tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper before serving.
Serve hot with egg noodles or boiled potatoes and crusty bread.
cheapTips: Use bone-in chicken thighs instead of a whole chicken for better value and faster cooking.
Substitute cultivated mushrooms for wild mushrooms to reduce cost.

recipes.name: Schenkele
recipes.description: Alsatian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk eggs with milk, sugar, and salt in a bowl until combined.
Add flour gradually to the wet mixture, stirring until a thick, smooth batter forms.
Heat oil in a deep skillet or pot to 350°F, testing temperature with a wooden spoon handle.
Transfer batter to a pastry bag fitted with a large star tip.
Pipe 4-inch strips of batter directly into the hot oil, working in small batches to avoid crowding.
Fry until golden brown on both sides, about 3 minutes total, turning once with tongs.
Remove schenkele with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Combine powdered sugar with kirsch or rum and dust generously over warm pastries.
cheapTips: Make your own powdered sugar by blending regular sugar in a blender.
Skip the kirsch and use vanilla extract instead for flavoring.

recipes.name: Pain d'Épices
recipes.description: Alsatian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease an 8x4 inch loaf pan.
Whisk eggs with honey and brown sugar until well combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, cinnamon, cloves, anise, ginger, and salt.
Fold dry ingredients into wet ingredients until just combined, then stir in melted butter.
Pour batter into prepared pan and smooth the top.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 15 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Slice and serve with butter or store in an airtight container for up to one week.
cheapTips: Buy honey in bulk from discount stores to reduce cost significantly.
Omit the anise seed and increase cinnamon to 1.5 tsp if unavailable.

recipes.name: Knack
recipes.description: Alsatian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice the onion and slice the apple into thin wedges.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté onion until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add sauerkraut, apple, caraway seeds, white wine, and broth, stirring to combine.
Nestle knackwurst sausages into the sauerkraut mixture.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes until sausages are heated through.
Stir in mustard and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot with crusty bread and additional mustard on the side.
cheapTips: Buy sauerkraut from the bulk or deli section rather than individually packaged jars.
Use basic bratwurst if knackwurst is unavailable.

recipes.name: Presskopf
recipes.description: Alsatian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blanch pork head meat, feet, and liver in salted water with onion, garlic, thyme, and bay leaves for 2 hours until very tender.
Remove meat from broth and cool slightly, then shred or dice into bite-sized pieces, discarding bones.
Strain cooking broth through cheesecloth and reduce to 2 cups by simmering uncovered for 30 minutes.
Mix shredded meat with cooled broth, chopped parsley, pistachio nuts, salt, and pepper.
Pour mixture into a terrine or loaf pan and cool to room temperature.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 12 hours until jelled.
Unmold onto a cutting board and slice 1/2-inch thick pieces.
Serve chilled or at room temperature with mustard and crusty bread.
cheapTips: Buy pork feet and head meat from the butcher counter or ethnic markets for significant savings.
Omit pistachio nuts and use chopped peppercorns for texture at a lower cost.

recipes.name: Kachelon
recipes.description: Alsatian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and slice potatoes into 1/4-inch thick rounds.
Dice onion and mix with ground pork, eggs, bread crumbs soaked in milk, parsley, salt, and pepper to form a forcemeat.
Butter a baking dish and layer half the sliced potatoes on the bottom.
Spread the pork mixture evenly over the potato layer.
Top with remaining potato slices arranged in overlapping rows.
Pour chicken broth around and over the potatoes, cover with foil, and bake at 375°F for 50 minutes.
Remove foil and bake an additional 15 minutes until potatoes are golden and tender.
Let rest for 10 minutes before serving directly from the baking dish.
cheapTips: Use ground beef if pork is more expensive at your store.
Make your own bread crumbs from stale bread instead of buying packaged.

recipes.name: Wädele aux Champignons
recipes.description: Alsatian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork shoulder into 2-inch cubes and pat dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown pork in batches, about 4 minutes per batch, then set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onion and garlic until fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Quarter the mushrooms and add to the pot, cooking until they release their liquid, about 5 minutes.
Pour in white wine and broth, scraping up browned bits, then return pork to the pot with thyme and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 60 minutes until pork is tender.
Dissolve cornstarch in 2 tbsp cold water and stir into the sauce to thicken, simmering for 2 minutes.
Remove thyme and bay leaf, season with salt and pepper, and serve with egg noodles or potatoes.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder from the butcher counter in bulk for a better per-pound price.
Use a mix of button and cremini mushrooms instead of specialty varieties.

recipes.name: Schiffala
recipes.description: Alsatian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork shoulder and back fat into 1-inch cubes and freeze for 30 minutes until very cold.
Grind pork and fat through a meat grinder fitted with a 1/4-inch plate into a chilled bowl.
Mix in salt, curing salt, coriander, nutmeg, pepper, and minced garlic until well combined.
Stuff mixture into hog casings using a sausage stuffer, creating links about 5 inches long.
Prick casings with a needle to prevent bursting and soak in cold water for 1 hour.
Soak apple wood chips in water for 30 minutes, then prepare smoker to 225°F.
Place sausages on smoking racks and smoke for 90 minutes until internal temperature reaches 160°F.
Cool sausages completely before serving hot with sauerkraut or cold with mustard.
cheapTips: Skip smoking and bake sausages in a 350°F oven for 30 minutes if you lack a smoker.
Buy pork shoulder on sale and freeze until needed for the project.

recipes.name: Quenelles de Foie
recipes.description: Alsatian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak bread crumbs in milk for 5 minutes, then squeeze out excess liquid.
Grind pork liver, back fat, and minced shallots together until very smooth.
Mix liver forcemeat with soaked bread crumbs, eggs, salt, pepper, and nutmeg until well combined.
Bring chicken broth to a gentle simmer in a large pot or deep skillet.
Using two wet spoons, form oval quenelles by scooping mixture with one spoon and smoothing with the other, then gently drop into simmering broth.
Poach quenelles for 12-15 minutes until they float and are firm to the touch.
Remove quenelles with a slotted spoon and keep warm on a serving platter.
Serve quenelles in a light sauce or with sautéed vegetables.
cheapTips: Buy pork liver from the butcher counter; it's often very affordable.
Use store-bought panko crumbs instead of making from scratch.

recipes.name: Carlins
recipes.description: Alsatian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse split peas under cold water and drain.
Chop onion, carrot, and celery into large chunks.
Place peas, ham hock, chopped vegetables, broth, thyme, and bay leaf in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 60 minutes until peas are very tender.
Remove ham hock and cool slightly, then shred any meat from the bone and set aside.
Strain soup through a colander, reserving broth, and discard vegetables and seasonings.
Return broth to pot and stir in peas, shredded ham, and butter until smooth.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Buy dried split peas in bulk from the grocery store's bulk bins.
Substitute bacon ends and pieces for ham hock to reduce cost.

recipes.name: Beef Goulash Soup
recipes.description: Hungarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef cubes on all sides, about 8 minutes total.
Remove beef and set aside, then sauté diced onions and garlic in the same pot until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in paprika powder and tomato paste, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to pot, add beef broth and bay leaves, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer covered for 45 minutes until beef is tender.
Add potatoes and carrots, then simmer for another 25-30 minutes until vegetables are soft.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy beef chuck on sale and freeze it for later use
Use store-brand paprika and broth to reduce costs

recipes.name: Sour Cherry Soup
recipes.description: Hungarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a large pot and add frozen sour cherries, sugar, cinnamon stick, and salt.
Simmer for 10 minutes until cherries have softened and released their juice.
Mix cornstarch with 3 tablespoons of cold water to create a slurry.
Slowly stir the cornstarch mixture into the soup while simmering to thicken slightly, about 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in lemon juice.
In a small bowl, whisk sour cream until smooth, then slowly temper it by adding 1 cup of warm soup while whisking.
Stir the tempered sour cream back into the pot gently and serve warm or chilled.
cheapTips: Buy frozen sour cherries in bulk when on sale
Use regular sour cream or Greek yogurt as a cheaper alternative

recipes.name: Nokedli
recipes.description: Hungarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
In a bowl, mix flour, eggs, water, and salt until you have a thick batter that's slightly looser than dough.
Hold a colander or nokedli maker over the boiling water and push the batter through the holes in small batches to create drop noodles.
Cook the nokedli for 2-3 minutes after they float to the surface, then remove with a slotted spoon to a serving bowl.
In a separate pan, melt butter over medium heat and sauté diced onion until golden, about 5 minutes.
Stir paprika powder into the onion butter and cook for 1 minute.
Pour the paprika butter over the nokedli, season with black pepper, and toss gently to coat.
cheapTips: Use store-brand flour and eggs which are usually the cheapest options
Make a large batch and freeze portions for quick future meals

recipes.name: Gulyasleves
recipes.description: Hungarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef cubes in batches, about 10 minutes total.
Remove beef and sauté diced onions and garlic in the same pot until golden, about 8 minutes.
Stir in paprika powder and caraway seeds, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot, add beef broth and marjoram, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 60 minutes until beef is very tender.
Add potatoes and carrots, then simmer for another 35-40 minutes until all vegetables are soft.
Season generously with salt and pepper and serve steaming hot in bowls.
cheapTips: Buy beef chuck in bulk and freeze portions
Use dried marjoram instead of fresh to save money

recipes.name: Egg Barley
recipes.description: Hungarian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, 1 egg, and salt in a bowl until a crumbly dough forms, then let rest for 5 minutes.
Rub the dough between your fingers over a plate to create small barley-sized pieces, breaking up any clumps.
Heat 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium heat and toast the egg barley pieces for 5-7 minutes, stirring frequently, until lightly golden.
In a separate pot, melt remaining 2 tablespoons butter and sauté diced onion until golden, about 5 minutes.
Add the toasted egg barley to the onion and stir to combine.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 8-10 minutes until barley is tender and broth is mostly absorbed.
Stir in paprika powder, salt, and pepper, then beat the remaining egg and drizzle it over while stirring quickly to create egg ribbons, then serve.
cheapTips: Buy eggs in bulk during sales and store in the refrigerator
Make this as a side dish to stretch mains further

recipes.name: Khinkali
recipes.description: Georgian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, and 0.5 teaspoon salt in a bowl and knead for 8-10 minutes until a smooth, elastic dough forms, then cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Combine ground beef, minced onion, garlic, cilantro, black pepper, and remaining salt in a separate bowl and mix gently with the broth until moist but not wet.
Divide dough into 6-8 equal pieces and roll each into a thin circle about 4 inches across.
Place about 2 tablespoons of filling in the center of each circle, then bring the edges up and pinch to seal, creating a money pouch shape with a small opening at the top.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil and gently drop khinkali in batches.
Cook for 6-8 minutes after they float to the surface, then remove with a slotted spoon.
Serve hot with black pepper on top, traditionally holding by the twisted knot at the top and eating the juicy filling first.
cheapTips: Buy ground beef on sale and portion into freezer bags
Use dried cilantro or parsley if fresh is expensive

recipes.name: Pkhali
recipes.description: Georgian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blanch fresh spinach in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, then squeeze out excess moisture thoroughly and chop finely.
Toast chopped walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fragrant.
In a food processor, pulse walnuts until coarsely ground, then add spinach, garlic, pomegranate molasses, red bell pepper, and cilantro.
Pulse together until well combined but still slightly textured, adding water as needed to reach a paste-like consistency.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer to a serving bowl and shape into a mound, then garnish with additional pomegranate seeds or a walnut if desired.
Serve at room temperature with fresh bread or as part of a mezze platter.
cheapTips: Buy walnuts in bulk from the bin section
Use fresh spinach from the farmers market when in season for better prices

recipes.name: Lobio
recipes.description: Georgian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried kidney beans in water overnight, then drain and rinse thoroughly.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion and garlic until soft and fragrant, about 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and coriander powder, cooking for 1 minute.
Add drained beans and water, then bring to a boil and reduce heat to low.
Simmer covered for 60-70 minutes until beans are very tender, stirring occasionally and adding water if needed to maintain broth level.
Mash about one-third of the beans against the pot wall to thicken the stew.
Stir in chopped cilantro, salt, and black pepper, then serve warm in bowls, traditionally in clay pots if available.
cheapTips: Buy dried beans in bulk, which are significantly cheaper than canned
Soak beans the night before to reduce cooking time and save energy

recipes.name: Shkmeruli
recipes.description: Georgian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and black pepper.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken thighs on both sides, about 8 minutes total, then set aside.
In the same skillet, add remaining 2 tablespoons butter and sauté minced garlic over medium heat until fragrant, about 1 minute, being careful not to burn it.
Pour in cream and milk, stirring to combine, then nestle the chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Simmer covered for 20-25 minutes until chicken is cooked through and sauce has thickened slightly.
Stir in chopped cilantro and paprika powder, then adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Serve hot with the creamy garlic sauce spooned over the chicken, traditionally accompanied by fresh bread to soak up the sauce.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs on sale and freeze for later use
Use half-and-half instead of heavy cream to reduce cost slightly

recipes.name: Chakhokhbili
recipes.description: Georgian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the chicken pieces in batches, about 10 minutes total, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté sliced onions and diced bell peppers until softened, about 7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and water, scraping any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return chicken pieces to the pot and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 30-35 minutes until chicken is tender and cooked through.
Stir in chopped cilantro, season with salt and pepper to taste, and serve hot with rice or bread.
cheapTips: Use bone-in chicken pieces which are cheaper than boneless
Buy tomatoes in bulk when in season and freeze for year-round use

recipes.name: Satsivi
recipes.description: Georgian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil chicken breast in salted water for 20 minutes until fully cooked, then shred into bite-sized pieces and reserve the broth.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in a large pot for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add ground walnuts to the pot and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add 2 cups reserved chicken broth, white vinegar, paprika, salt, and pepper to the walnut mixture.
Simmer the sauce for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally until thickened.
Add shredded chicken to the sauce and simmer for 5 minutes to combine flavors.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt, pepper, or vinegar as needed.
Serve warm, garnished with fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Buy walnuts in bulk from discount stores or use half walnut and half sunflower seed butter
Use chicken thighs instead of breast for more flavor at lower cost

recipes.name: Lula Kebab
recipes.description: Georgian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Finely mince onion, garlic, parsley, and cilantro and combine in a bowl.
Add ground beef, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes to the herb mixture and mix gently with your hands until just combined.
Divide meat mixture into 8 portions and mold each onto flat metal skewers, pressing firmly into a long oval shape.
Preheat an outdoor grill or grill pan to medium-high heat and lightly oil the surface.
Grill kebabs for 6-7 minutes per side, turning once, until cooked through and charred on the outside.
Transfer to a plate and rest for 3 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Skip the grill and pan-fry over medium-high heat in a skillet without skewers
Buy ground beef on sale and freeze in 1.5 lb portions

recipes.name: Badrijani Nigvzit
recipes.description: Georgian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice eggplants lengthwise into 0.25-inch thick planks.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and fry eggplant slices in batches for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and tender, then set aside on paper towels.
Combine ground walnuts, minced garlic, pomegranate molasses, cilantro, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Spread 2 tablespoons of walnut filling on the skin side of each eggplant slice.
Roll each slice tightly and arrange seam-side down on a serving platter.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to help rolls hold their shape.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds before serving cold or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Substitute pomegranate molasses with white vinegar mixed with a pinch of sugar
Use sunflower seed butter instead of expensive walnuts

recipes.name: Adjarian Khachapuri
recipes.description: Georgian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine warm water and yeast in a small bowl and let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour and salt in a large bowl, then add yeast mixture and stir until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead dough on a floured surface for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then place in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise for 30 minutes.
Mix shredded mozzarella and crumbled feta cheese in a bowl with 1 tbsp butter.
Divide dough in half and stretch each into an oval shape on parchment paper.
Spread half the cheese mixture on each dough oval, leaving 1 inch border on all sides.
Fold edges up and pinch to create a boat shape with open ends, then brush edges with remaining melted butter.
Bake at 450°F for 15-18 minutes until crust is golden, then crack an egg into the center of each khachapuri.
Bake for additional 3-4 minutes until egg white is set but yolk is still runny, then serve hot with a pat of butter.
cheapTips: Use a mix of cheddar and cheap mozzarella to stretch the cheese further
Make dough the night before to save morning time

recipes.name: Mkhali
recipes.description: Georgian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion for 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add fresh spinach in batches, stirring until completely wilted, about 8-10 minutes total.
Drain and rinse canned kidney beans, then add to the spinach and stir well.
Toast walnuts in a dry skillet for 2 minutes, then chop finely and add to the pot.
Stir in cilantro, white vinegar, salt, and pepper and cook for 2 more minutes.
Transfer to a serving bowl and let cool to room temperature before serving.
cheapTips: Buy frozen spinach instead of fresh and thaw before cooking
Use sunflower seeds instead of walnuts to save money

recipes.name: Chakapuli
recipes.description: Georgian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut lamb into 1-inch cubes and place in a large pot with water, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes, skimming foam from the surface.
Add diced onion and minced garlic and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Add fresh or dried plums, white wine, and fresh dill to the pot.
Simmer for another 10-15 minutes until lamb is tender and plums have softened.
Stir in fresh cilantro and taste to adjust seasoning.
Serve hot in bowls with plenty of broth.
cheapTips: Use lamb stew meat or ask the butcher for trim pieces
Substitute dried prunes for fresh plums year-round at lower cost

recipes.name: Ojakhuri
recipes.description: Georgian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut meat into 1-inch cubes and potatoes into similar-sized pieces.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown meat in batches for 4-5 minutes, then set aside.
In the same skillet, sauté sliced onions for 3 minutes until softened, then add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Return meat to the skillet and add potatoes, salt, pepper, and paprika.
Cover and simmer on medium heat for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are tender and meat is cooked through.
Stir in fresh parsley and cilantro and cook for 1 more minute.
Serve hot directly from the skillet or transfer to a serving platter.
cheapTips: Buy sirloin or chuck when on sale and freeze in portions
Use regular russet potatoes instead of specialty varieties

recipes.name: Tetradze
recipes.description: Georgian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil unpeeled beets in salted water for 20-25 minutes until fork-tender, then drain and cool slightly.
Peel cooled beets and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Toast walnuts in a dry skillet for 2 minutes, then grind or finely chop into a paste with minced garlic.
Mix walnut-garlic paste with white vinegar, salt, pepper, water, and cilantro in a bowl.
Add beet pieces to the mixture and stir until fully coated.
Let sit for 10 minutes before serving to allow flavors to meld.
cheapTips: Buy beets fresh and in bulk when in season, or use canned for convenience
Toast your own walnuts instead of buying pre-roasted

recipes.name: Beef Lobio
recipes.description: Georgian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.

ingredients.note: 2 cans (15 oz each) or 1 cup dried

steps: Brown beef cubes in a large pot over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes until seared on all sides, then remove and set aside.
Sauté diced onions in the same pot for 3 minutes until softened, then add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in tomato paste and paprika and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to pot and add beef broth, then bring to a boil and reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 35-40 minutes until beef is tender.
Drain and rinse canned beans (or if using dried, soak 8 hours, then cook until tender in separate pot) and add to the pot.
Simmer uncovered for 10 more minutes, then stir in fresh cilantro and taste to adjust seasoning.
Serve hot as a thick stew in bowls.
cheapTips: Use canned beans instead of dried to save significant cooking time
Buy beef chuck on sale and freeze in portions

recipes.name: Lavash
recipes.description: Georgian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt in a large bowl.
Add warm water and oil to flour and stir until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead dough on a floured surface for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Divide dough into 3 balls, coat lightly with oil, cover with a towel, and let rest for 20 minutes.
Heat a cast iron skillet or griddle over medium-high heat.
On a floured surface, roll each dough ball into a thin, even sheet about 0.1 inches thick.
Carefully transfer rolled dough to the hot skillet and cook for 2-3 minutes per side until lightly golden and puffed in spots.
Brush both sides lightly with melted butter while still warm and stack on a plate.
cheapTips: Use just water and skip butter for plain version at minimal cost
Make large batch and freeze wrapped in plastic wrap for later use

recipes.name: Penovani
recipes.description: Georgian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk together milk, eggs, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Gradually add flour while whisking to form a smooth, thin batter.
Let batter rest for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium-high heat.
Pour 1/4 cup batter into the center and tilt the pan to spread thinly into a circle.
Cook for 1-2 minutes until the bottom is light golden, then flip and cook another 30 seconds.
Transfer to a plate and repeat with remaining batter.
Spread each pancake with butter and honey, fold in half, and serve warm.
cheapTips: Use store-brand milk and eggs to reduce costs
Make extra and freeze for quick breakfasts

recipes.name: Imeruli Khachapuri
recipes.description: Georgian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, and salt to form a soft dough, knead for 5 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Combine mozzarella and feta cheese in a bowl.
Divide dough into 3 equal portions and roll each into a thin 8-inch circle.
Spread cheese mixture evenly on each dough circle, leaving a 1/2-inch border.
Fold the edges over the cheese to create a rustic enclosed shape, then gently flatten.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook khachapuri 4-5 minutes per side until golden.
Top each with a dot of butter and brush edges with beaten egg yolk.
Serve hot, optionally cutting into wedges.
cheapTips: Substitute part of the cheese with ricotta to save money
Buy cheese in blocks and shred yourself instead of pre-shredded

recipes.name: Megruli Khachapuri
recipes.description: Georgian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Prepare dough by mixing flour, water, and salt; knead for 8 minutes and rest covered for 45 minutes.
Mix both cheeses together in a bowl.
Roll dough into a thin large circle about 14 inches in diameter.
Place dough on an oiled baking sheet and spread cheese mixture evenly over surface.
Fold edges inward about 2 inches all around to create a border frame with exposed cheese center.
Bake at 400°F for 25-30 minutes until the crust is golden and cheese begins to bubble.
Remove from oven and create 2 small wells in the cheese; crack an egg into each well and return to oven for 3-4 minutes.
Brush crust with melted butter and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Look for aged cheese sales at ethnic markets
Make dough ahead and refrigerate overnight to save active cooking time

recipes.name: Spinach Pkhali
recipes.description: Georgian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blanch spinach in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, then squeeze out excess moisture.
Toast walnuts in a dry skillet for 3 minutes until fragrant, then finely chop.
Sauté minced onion in a skillet for 3 minutes until softened, add garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Finely chop the blanched spinach and combine with walnuts, onion mixture, and all spices.
Stir in pomegranate seeds or vinegar and adjust seasoning.
Mound the mixture onto a serving plate and shape into a dome or patties.
Chill for 10 minutes before serving at room temperature.
cheapTips: Buy frozen spinach instead of fresh to save cost and prep time
Use regular vinegar if pomegranate seeds are unavailable

recipes.name: Kharcho
recipes.description: Georgian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown beef in batches for 3-4 minutes, set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onion for 5 minutes until soft, add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Return beef to pot, add broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in rice and all spices, simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender.
Mix ground walnuts with 1/4 cup warm broth to form a paste and stir into soup.
Simmer for 5 more minutes, adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Use chuck roast when on sale and freeze for later use
Substitute walnuts with peanut butter if budget is tight

recipes.name: Kutab
recipes.description: Ukrainian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, salt, and oil to form a soft dough, knead for 5 minutes, cover and rest 20 minutes.
Brown ground meat in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it apart as it cooks.
Add onion and garlic to the meat, sauté for 5 minutes until softened, season with pepper and salt.
Divide dough into 6 equal pieces and roll each into a thin oval shape.
Place 2-3 tablespoons of meat filling on half of each oval, fold dough over to create a crescent and seal edges.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat and fry kutabs for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
cheapTips: Use ground beef trimmings or the cheapest ground meat available
Make a double batch and freeze extras for quick meals

recipes.name: Mlyntsi
recipes.description: Ukrainian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk together eggs, milk, flour, salt, and sugar to form a smooth thin batter.
Heat oil and butter in a 10-inch non-stick skillet over medium-high heat.
Pour 1/4 cup batter into center and immediately tilt pan to spread into a thin circle.
Cook for about 1 minute until underside is golden, then flip and cook 30 seconds more.
Transfer to a plate and repeat with remaining batter.
Fill each mlyntsi with jam, chocolate spread, or sour cream.
Roll up and serve warm with a dollop of sour cream and dusting of powdered sugar if desired.
cheapTips: Use regular milk instead of whole milk to reduce fat
Make a big batch and refrigerate or freeze for quick reheating

recipes.name: Banush
recipes.description: Ukrainian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring water or broth to boil in a large pot, add salt.
Slowly whisk in cornmeal while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat to low and continue stirring for 20-25 minutes until thick and creamy.
Sauté mushrooms and onion in 1 tablespoon butter in a separate skillet until golden.
Stir cheese, remaining butter, and mushroom mixture into the cornmeal.
Fold in sour cream gently until combined.
Transfer to a serving dish and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use regular feta instead of bryndza to save money
Buy mushrooms on sale and freeze for later use

recipes.name: Baba
recipes.description: Ukrainian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix warm milk, yeast, and 1 tablespoon sugar; let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, combine flour, remaining sugar, salt, and melted butter.
Add yeast mixture and eggs to dry ingredients, stir until a soft dough forms.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic, fold in dried fruit.
Place dough in a greased bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let rise for 45 minutes until doubled.
Transfer dough to a greased tall cylindrical or round mold, cover and let rise 20 minutes more.
Bake at 375°F for 35-40 minutes until golden and a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Cool slightly and dust with powdered sugar before serving.
cheapTips: Use store-brand yeast which is cheaper per serving than instant packets
Substitute dried fruit with chopped apples to reduce cost

recipes.name: Halushky
recipes.description: Ukrainian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, eggs, salt, and water to form a thick batter.
Boil potatoes in a large pot until nearly tender, about 8 minutes.
Push batter through a colander or halushky maker directly into the boiling potato water.
Stir gently and cook for 3-4 minutes until halushky float to the surface.
In a separate skillet, sauté diced onion in butter until golden and crispy.
Drain halushky and potatoes, transfer to a serving bowl.
Pour caramelized onions and butter over top and fold in sour cream gently.
Serve warm and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
cheapTips: Buy potatoes in bulk when on sale and store in cool place
Use half sour cream and half plain Greek yogurt to reduce cost

recipes.name: Kapusnyak
recipes.description: Ukrainian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add sliced carrots and cook for another 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add diced potatoes and stir well, cooking for 2 minutes to coat with oil.
Pour in beef broth and bring to a boil, then add bay leaf and reduce heat to medium.
Simmer for 10 minutes until potatoes begin to soften.
Add chopped cabbage, tomato paste, and minced garlic, stirring well.
Continue simmering for 15-20 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy cabbage and potatoes in bulk; they're inexpensive and store well
Use vegetable broth instead of beef broth to reduce costs

recipes.name: Zharkoye
recipes.description: Ukrainian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef cubes in batches, about 3 minutes per side; set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onion until golden, about 4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to pot and add tomato paste, stirring to coat the meat.
Pour in beef broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 30 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrots, increase heat to medium, and simmer uncovered for 25-30 minutes until meat is tender and vegetables are cooked.
Stir in Worcestershire sauce and season generously with salt and pepper.
Simmer for 5 more minutes and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy beef chuck on sale and freeze for later use
Substitute carrots with turnips or parsnips for variation and lower cost

recipes.name: Deruny
recipes.description: Ukrainian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Finely grate potatoes and onion using a box grater or food processor.
Place grated mixture in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out excess liquid over a sink.
Transfer squeezed mixture to a bowl and add egg, flour, salt, and black pepper; mix until combined.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Drop spoonfuls of potato mixture into hot oil, flattening each with the back of a spatula to create thin pancakes.
Fry for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Transfer cooked deruny to a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve warm with sour cream on the side.
cheapTips: Buy potatoes in 5-lb bags for the cheapest per-pound price
Use store-brand sour cream instead of name-brand varieties

recipes.name: Salo
recipes.description: Ukrainian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork fatback into thin slices about 1/4 inch thick.
In a small bowl, combine salt, black pepper, garlic, paprika, and thyme.
Rub the spice mixture on both sides of each fatback slice.
Layer slices in a glass or ceramic container, alternating with bay leaves.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 3 days (up to 2 weeks) before serving.
Remove from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve thinly sliced with dark bread and pickles as a traditional appetizer.
cheapTips: Buy pork fatback from ethnic markets or butchers where it's cheaper than mainstream stores
Make large batches and keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks

recipes.name: Okroshka
recipes.description: Ukrainian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Hard-boil eggs, cool, peel, and dice into small pieces.
In a large bowl, combine diced potatoes, cucumbers, radishes, green onions, dill, and diced eggs.
In a separate bowl, whisk together kefir, chilled broth, mustard, salt, and black pepper.
Pour the kefir mixture over the vegetable mixture and stir gently to combine.
Chill the okroshka in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Stir well and adjust seasonings with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Serve in chilled bowls with extra fresh dill and sour cream on the side.
cheapTips: Make this soup when cucumbers are in season for cheaper prices
Use regular yogurt instead of kefir if kefir is not available or too expensive

recipes.name: Solyanka
recipes.description: Ukrainian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and brown meat cubes over medium-high heat for 5 minutes; set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onion and carrots until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Return meat to pot and add beef broth, sauerkraut, pickled cucumbers, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 35-40 minutes until meat is tender.
Add olives and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot in bowls with a dollop of sour cream and fresh dill.
cheapTips: Buy sauerkraut in bulk from European markets for lower costs
Use chicken instead of beef for a cheaper protein option

recipes.name: Pashtet
recipes.description: Ukrainian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté chopped onion until golden, about 4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Increase heat to medium-high, add chicken livers, and cook until no longer pink inside, about 8-10 minutes.
Season with salt, black pepper, and dried thyme.
Transfer cooked liver mixture to a food processor along with remaining butter, hard-boiled eggs, and heavy cream.
Blend until smooth and creamy, scraping down sides as needed.
Transfer pashtet to a serving bowl and smooth the top with a spatula.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving with dark bread and pickles.
cheapTips: Buy chicken livers from the butcher counter where they are usually discounted
Make large batches and refrigerate for up to 5 days

recipes.name: Sirniki
recipes.description: Ukrainian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a large bowl, combine farmer's cheese, eggs, flour, sugar, salt, and vanilla extract; mix until well combined.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Drop spoonfuls of cheese mixture onto the hot skillet, flattening each slightly with the back of a spoon.
Fry for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy on the edges.
Transfer cooked sirniki to a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve warm with sour cream and jam or honey drizzled on top.
cheapTips: Buy cottage cheese on sale and freeze for later use
Use store-brand jam instead of premium brands to save money

recipes.name: Zharkoe
recipes.description: Ukrainian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown meat cubes in batches, about 3 minutes per side; set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onion until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return meat to pot and stir in tomato paste, coating the meat well.
Add water and bay leaves, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover partially.
Simmer for 30 minutes until meat is nearly tender.
Add potatoes and carrots, increase heat to medium, and simmer uncovered for 25-30 minutes until all vegetables are soft and meat is very tender.
Season generously with salt and black pepper, then serve hot in bowls with plenty of broth.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder when on sale and freeze for later
Use root vegetables like turnips or parsnips instead of carrots for variation

recipes.name: Kutup
recipes.description: Ukrainian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.

ingredients.note: 2 tablespoons for dough plus 2 for fryin

steps: Mix flour, salt, water, and 2 tablespoons oil in a bowl until a soft dough forms; knead until smooth, then cover and rest for 15 minutes.
While dough rests, sauté diced onion in 1 tablespoon oil until golden, then mix with mashed potatoes, cheese, salt, and black pepper.
Divide dough into 4 equal pieces and roll each into a thin oval about 8 inches long.
Spread potato-cheese filling down the center of each oval, leaving edges clear.
Roll up tightly like a jelly roll, pinching seams to seal, then coil each roll.
Heat remaining oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry coiled kutup rolls for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot with sour cream or melted butter drizzled on top.
cheapTips: Make large batches and freeze unbaked rolls for quick meals later
Use store-brand cheddar instead of name-brand varieties

recipes.name: Rassolnik
recipes.description: Russian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring beef broth to a boil and add beef chuck, simmering for 20 minutes to tenderize.
Add diced potatoes, pearl barley, chopped onion, and carrot, cooking for 15 minutes until vegetables soften.
Dice the pickles and add them to the pot along with pickle juice.
Simmer for 5 more minutes, then season with salt, pepper, and fresh dill before serving.
cheapTips: Use beef bones with some meat instead of chuck to reduce cost
Make your own beef broth from bones and scraps

recipes.name: Kvass
recipes.description: Russian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast rye bread slices in a 350°F oven for 15 minutes until dark brown.
Boil 10 cups of water and pour over toasted bread in a large pot, covering and letting sit at room temperature for 12 hours.
Strain the bread liquid through cheesecloth into a clean container, discarding bread solids.
Stir in sugar, salt, and yeast, then let ferment at room temperature for 24-36 hours covered with cloth.
Bottle the kvass and refrigerate for up to 2 weeks, serving chilled.
cheapTips: Buy day-old rye bread from bakeries at discount
The raisins can be omitted or replaced with dried apricots

recipes.name: Kissel
recipes.description: Russian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a pot and add frozen berries, sugar, and salt.
Simmer berries for 5 minutes until they soften and release their juices.
Mix potato starch with 3 tablespoons cold water to form a slurry.
Slowly pour starch slurry into simmering berry mixture while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Simmer for 2-3 minutes until the liquid thickens and becomes translucent, then stir in lemon juice and serve warm or chilled.
cheapTips: Use frozen berries instead of fresh for year-round affordability
Substitute cornstarch for potato starch at same ratio

recipes.name: Syrniki
recipes.description: Russian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix cottage cheese, eggs, flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl until well combined.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls of mixture onto the skillet, flattening each into a 2-inch pancake.
Fry for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown, working in batches.
Serve warm topped with sour cream and jam.
cheapTips: Buy cottage cheese on sale and freeze for later use
Use any fruit jam on hand or make homemade if available

recipes.name: Tvorog
recipes.description: Russian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat milk in a pot to 185°F (just below boiling), stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and stir in vinegar, letting curds separate for 10 minutes.
Line a colander with cheesecloth and carefully pour curds through to drain.
Gather the cloth and hang over a bowl for 1-2 hours until whey stops dripping.
Transfer tvorog to a bowl, stir in salt and honey, and serve with fresh berries.
cheapTips: Buy milk on sale when making tvorog in bulk to freeze
Use seasonal berries to reduce cost and improve freshness

recipes.name: Ciorbă de burtă
recipes.description: Romanian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean tripe thoroughly under running water, then blanch in boiling water for 5 minutes and drain.
Cut cleaned tripe into thin strips about 2 inches long.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in a large pot, then add paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add beef broth, tripe strips, diced potatoes, and carrot, bringing to a boil then simmering for 90 minutes until tripe is tender.
Stir in vinegar and season with salt and pepper, then remove from heat.
Stir in sour cream and top with fresh parsley before serving hot.
cheapTips: Buy tripe from ethnic meat markets where it's much cheaper than mainstream grocery stores
Make your own beef broth to save money

recipes.name: Mici
recipes.description: Romanian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine ground beef, ground pork, minced garlic, paprika, salt, and pepper in a bowl, mixing with broth until sticky.
Wet your hands and shape mixture into 8-10 cylindrical sausages about 3 inches long.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and arrange mici in a single layer.
Cook for 12-15 minutes, turning frequently with tongs to brown all sides evenly.
Serve hot with mustard on the side or drizzled over top.
cheapTips: Buy ground meat on sale and freeze when prices are low
Skip expensive spice blends and use basic paprika and garlic

recipes.name: Sarmale
recipes.description: Romanian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil cabbage head for 10 minutes until leaves soften, then carefully peel off and set aside 12-14 leaves.
Mix ground beef, ground pork, rice, minced onion, minced garlic, paprika, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Place 2 tablespoons filling on each cabbage leaf, fold in sides, and roll tightly from bottom to top.
Layer remaining cabbage pieces in a pot and arrange rolls seam-side down in rows.
Mix tomato paste with beef broth and pour over rolls, bringing to a boil then simmering covered for 60 minutes.
cheapTips: Buy ground meat in bulk and freeze portions before use
Use white or savoy cabbage when cheaper than green varieties

recipes.name: Mămăligă
recipes.description: Romanian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring milk and water to a boil in a large pot with salt and sugar.
Slowly whisk in cornmeal while stirring constantly to avoid lumps, then reduce heat to low.
Stir frequently for 15 minutes as the mixture thickens significantly.
Stir in butter and cheddar cheese until melted and fully combined.
Transfer to a serving bowl and top with sour cream, then serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy cornmeal in bulk from ethnic markets where it's cheaper
Use store-brand butter and cheese to reduce costs

recipes.name: Papanasi
recipes.description: Romanian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar in a bowl, then whisk eggs and yogurt together separately.
Mix wet ingredients into dry ingredients until a thick dough forms.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pot or Dutch oven.
Drop spoonfuls of dough carefully into hot oil, frying 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Dust papanasi with powdered sugar while warm and serve immediately topped with sour cream and jam.
cheapTips: Make your own powdered sugar by blending granulated sugar if prices are high
Use any jam on hand or make from frozen fruit

recipes.name: Shchi
recipes.description: Russian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat broth in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add diced onion and carrots, simmer for 5 minutes.
Add potatoes and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in chopped cabbage and tomato paste with bay leaf.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle into bowls and serve topped with a dollop of sour cream.
cheapTips: Buy cabbage in bulk when on sale; it stores for weeks
Use chicken broth instead of beef to reduce cost

recipes.name: Blini
recipes.description: Russian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.

ingredients.note: 3 tablespoons melted, plus more for pan

steps: Whisk together flour, sugar, salt, and baking powder in a bowl.
In another bowl, beat eggs then add milk and melted butter.
Combine wet and dry ingredients until smooth batter forms.
Heat a buttered skillet or griddle over medium-high heat.
Pour small 2-3 inch circles of batter and cook 1-2 minutes per side until golden.
Stack blini on a warm plate as they finish cooking.
Serve warm with sour cream and jam or caviar on top.
cheapTips: Skip the caviar and use jam or honey for authentic flavor at lower cost
Make a double batch and freeze extras for quick future breakfasts

recipes.name: Piroshki
recipes.description: Russian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Warm milk to 110°F and mix with yeast, sugar, salt, and egg.
Stir in oil then add flour gradually, kneading into smooth dough for 8 minutes.
Cover and let rise 45 minutes until doubled.
Meanwhile, brown ground beef with minced onion over medium heat, season with salt and pepper, then cool.
Divide dough into 12 equal pieces and roll each into a thin circle.
Place 1 tablespoon filling in center of each circle, fold in half, and seal edges with water.
Heat oil to 350°F and fry piroshki 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
cheapTips: Use ground beef on sale or substitute ground pork for savings
Make filling in bulk and freeze for multiple batches

recipes.name: Pirozhki
recipes.description: Russian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Whisk together yogurt and egg in another bowl.
Combine wet and dry ingredients until dough forms.
Knead lightly and divide dough into 10 equal pieces.
Mix mashed potatoes with shredded cheese, salt, and pepper for filling.
Flatten each dough piece, add 1 tablespoon filling in center, fold and seal.
Place on greased baking sheet, brush with melted butter.
Bake at 375°F for 25-30 minutes until golden brown.
cheapTips: Replace cheese with caramelized onions for a vegetarian budget option
Bake instead of fry to reduce oil costs significantly

recipes.name: Herring Under a Fur Coat
recipes.description: Russian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toss herring pieces with potatoes, beets, carrots, and apple in a large bowl.
Mix mayonnaise and sour cream together in a small bowl.
Add minced pickle to the mayo mixture and stir to combine.
Fold the sauce into the herring mixture until well coated.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer to a serving dish and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Sprinkle with fresh dill and serve cold or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Buy canned herring on sale; it keeps for months
Substitute mayonnaise with equal parts sour cream and Greek yogurt to reduce costs

recipes.name: Kasha
recipes.description: Russian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast buckwheat groats in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
In a separate pot, bring water or broth to boil.
Add toasted groats to boiling liquid with salt.
Reduce heat and simmer covered for 15 minutes until tender and liquid is absorbed.
Meanwhile, melt 1 tablespoon butter and sauté diced onion until golden.
Fluff kasha with a fork and stir in remaining butter, sautéed onion, and black pepper.
Serve hot, optionally topped with a fried egg.
cheapTips: Buy buckwheat in bulk from ethnic or discount grocery stores for lowest price
Use water instead of broth to further reduce costs

recipes.name: Coulibiac
recipes.description: Russian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Sauté onion in butter until softened, add mushrooms and cook until liquid evaporates, about 8 minutes.
Combine cooked rice, sautéed mushroom mixture, flaked salmon, chopped hard-boiled eggs, and dill in a bowl; season with salt and pepper.
Roll out puff pastry and place on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Spoon filling down the center of the pastry, leaving 2 inches on each side.
Fold long sides of pastry over filling, sealing edges with water; fold short ends under.
Brush top and sides with beaten egg yolk.
Bake at 400°F for 30-35 minutes until golden brown.
Cool 10 minutes before slicing and serving.
cheapTips: Use frozen salmon instead of fresh for significant savings
Buy puff pastry on sale and keep frozen for meal planning

recipes.name: Plov
recipes.description: Russian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown cubed meat on all sides, about 5-7 minutes; remove and set aside.
Sauté onion and carrot slices in the same pot for 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and cumin, cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Return meat to pot and add rice; stir to coat with oil.
Pour in broth, add bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Let stand covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and serve.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs instead of beef for budget-friendly protein
Buy rice in bulk to reduce per-serving cost to under $2

recipes.name: Shashlik
recipes.description: Russian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine olive oil, vinegar, minced garlic, bay leaves, paprika, salt, and pepper in a bowl to make marinade.
Add meat cubes to marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 30 minutes.
Thread marinated meat alternately with onion quarters and bell pepper chunks onto skewers.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill skewers for 10-15 minutes, turning occasionally, until meat is cooked through and has light char marks.
Let rest for 3-5 minutes before serving hot.
cheapTips: Use pork instead of beef for lower cost with similar taste
Buy meat on sale and freeze in marinade for several weeks

recipes.name: Kholodets
recipes.description: Russian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Place bones or knuckles in a large pot and cover with water; bring to boil and drain.
Rinse bones and return to pot with fresh water, carrots, onion halves, bay leaves, and peppercorns.
Simmer covered for 2-3 hours until meat is very tender and falls from bones.
Remove meat from pot and shred; strain broth through cheesecloth and discard solids.
Return shredded meat to broth, stir in minced garlic and salt to taste.
If broth lacks natural gelatin, dissolve powdered gelatin in cold water and stir in.
Pour mixture into a shallow dish and refrigerate uncovered for 4-6 hours until set into gelatin.
Cut into squares, arrange on a plate, and serve cold with mustard and fresh herbs.
cheapTips: Buy beef or pork bones at the butcher counter for a fraction of the price
Skip powdered gelatin if bones are rich in collagen; long cooking naturally creates gelatin

recipes.name: Tocană de vie
recipes.description: Romanian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut beef into 1.5-inch cubes and pat dry with paper towels.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches, about 3 minutes per side, then set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onions and minced garlic until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and paprika powder, cooking for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot and add red wine, beef broth, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 60-75 minutes until beef is very tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot with crusty bread or polenta.
cheapTips: Use beef chuck which is inexpensive and becomes tender when braised
Buy wine for cooking instead of drinking wine to save money

recipes.name: Ciorbă de perisoare
recipes.description: Romanian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix ground beef with cooked rice, minced onion, minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Form mixture into small meatballs about the size of walnuts.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and brown the meatballs in batches, about 2 minutes, then remove.
In the same pot, combine beef broth with tomato paste and bring to a simmer.
Add meatballs back to the pot and simmer for 20-25 minutes until cooked through.
Stir in fresh dill and lemon juice just before serving.
Season with additional salt and pepper to taste and serve hot.
cheapTips: Cook rice in bulk at home to save money on meatball fillings
Use dried dill if fresh is unavailable for a similar authentic taste

recipes.name: Tochitura de porc
recipes.description: Romanian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork shoulder into 1-inch cubes and season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown pork in batches, about 3 minutes per side, then set aside.
Add sliced onions and minced garlic to the pot and sauté until golden, about 6 minutes.
Stir in paprika powder and tomato paste, cooking for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Return pork to the pot and add broth, bay leaves, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 90 minutes until pork is very tender.
Remove bay leaves, taste, and adjust seasonings with salt and pepper.
Serve hot over polenta, rice, or with fresh bread to soak up the sauce.
cheapTips: Pork shoulder is an economical cut that becomes tender during long cooking
Make extra and freeze portions for quick weeknight dinners

recipes.name: Salată de boeuf
recipes.description: Romanian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil beef in salted water for 30-40 minutes until cooked through, then cool and cut into small dice.
Boil potatoes and carrots separately until tender, then cool and cut into small dice.
Finely dice the onion and combine in a large bowl with beef, potatoes, carrots, and pickles.
In a separate bowl, mix mayonnaise with mustard, salt, and pepper.
Pour mayonnaise mixture over the salad ingredients and toss gently until well combined.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Transfer to a serving dish and sprinkle with paprika before serving.
cheapTips: Use less expensive beef cuts like chuck roast which become tender when boiled
Make this a day ahead so flavors develop and you have a ready meal

recipes.name: Mămăligă cu brânză și smântână
recipes.description: Romanian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring water or milk to a boil in a large pot with salt.
Slowly pour cornmeal into boiling liquid while stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat to low and stir constantly for 20-25 minutes until thick and creamy.
The mämäligä is ready when it pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Stir in butter until melted and well combined.
Transfer to a serving bowl or platter and create a well in the center.
Top with crumbled feta cheese and a dollop of sour cream, then sprinkle with black pepper and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy cornmeal in bulk from warehouse stores to save significantly
Use store-brand sour cream and feta to reduce costs

recipes.name: Cozonac
recipes.description: Romanian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix warm milk with yeast and 1 tbsp sugar, let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, combine flour, remaining sugar, and salt, then make a well in the center.
Add yeast mixture, eggs, and soft butter to the well, then mix until a soft dough forms.
Knead dough for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then let rise in an oiled bowl for 1 hour until doubled.
Mix ground walnuts with cocoa powder and vanilla extract to make the filling.
Roll out dough into a rectangle, spread walnut-cocoa filling evenly, then roll tightly like a log.
Coil the roll into a spiral shape and place in a buttered loaf pan, let rise 45 minutes.
Bake at 350°F for 40-45 minutes until golden brown and a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.
cheapTips: Buy walnuts from bulk bins and grind them yourself to save money
Make the dough the night before to save time on baking day

recipes.name: Clătite
recipes.description: Romanian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine flour, salt, and sugar in a large mixing bowl.
Create a well in the center and crack eggs into it, then pour in milk and water.
Whisk from the center outward until smooth, then stir in melted butter.
Let batter rest for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Heat a non-stick skillet or crêpe pan over medium-high heat and lightly oil it.
Pour about 1/4 cup batter into the center and tilt the pan to spread evenly into a thin circle.
Cook for about 1-2 minutes until the bottom is light golden, then flip and cook the other side for 30 seconds.
Transfer to a plate and repeat with remaining batter.
Serve warm with jam, honey, sour cream, or Nutella according to preference.
cheapTips: Use water to thin batter instead of all milk to reduce dairy costs
Serve with budget-friendly toppings like homemade jam or sugar with lemon

recipes.name: Jumări
recipes.description: Romanian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork fatback into small 1/2-inch cubes.
Place cubes in a heavy skillet over medium heat.
Cook slowly for 40-50 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the fat melts and cubes become crispy and golden.
The cubes will shrink as the fat renders out.
Drain the crispy pieces on paper towels using a slotted spoon.
While still warm, sprinkle with salt, black pepper, and garlic powder.
Allow to cool completely, then store in an airtight container for up to 1 week.
Serve as a snack on their own or crumbled over polenta or salads.
cheapTips: Buy pork fatback from the butcher counter where it is much cheaper than pre-packaged
Save the rendered lard for cooking other dishes to maximize value

recipes.name: Ciorbă de fasole
recipes.description: Romanian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse dried beans and soak overnight in cold water, then drain.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onions and minced garlic until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in vegetable broth and add the drained beans, bay leaves, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 60-75 minutes until beans are very tender.
Stir in lemon juice and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove bay leaves and serve hot as a thick, hearty soup.
cheapTips: Buy dried beans in bulk which are significantly cheaper than canned
Soak beans overnight to reduce cooking time and save on gas or electricity

recipes.name: Mâncare de fasole
recipes.description: Romanian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onions and minced garlic, sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and paprika powder, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add canned tomato sauce and drained beans, stirring well to combine.
Add bay leaf, salt, and pepper, then bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Remove bay leaf, taste, and adjust seasonings as needed.
Serve hot as a side dish with polenta, rice, or as a main course with bread.
cheapTips: Use canned beans to save time and reduce cooking costs significantly
Buy store-brand canned tomatoes and sauce to lower the overall cost

recipes.name: Pastrama
recipes.description: Romanian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine water, kosher salt, pink curing salt, peppercorns, coriander seeds, garlic, and bay leaves in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Cool the brine completely to room temperature, then refrigerate until chilled.
Submerge beef brisket in the cold brine and refrigerate for 7 days, turning occasionally.
Remove meat from brine and rinse thoroughly under cold water.
Mix paprika, mustard seeds, and cracked peppercorns together and coat the entire surface of the meat.
Wrap meat in cheesecloth and hang in a cool place or refrigerate for 2-3 days to develop flavor.
Slice thinly and serve cold or steam the whole piece for 3 hours before slicing.
cheapTips: Buy brisket on sale and make large batches
Use regular salt instead of pink curing salt for a simpler version

recipes.name: Bulz
recipes.description: Romanian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring salted water to a rolling boil in a large pot.
Slowly whisk cornmeal into boiling water to avoid lumps, stirring constantly.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 25-30 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent sticking and burning.
Meanwhile, cook bacon until crispy, then chop into small pieces.
When polenta is thick and creamy, remove from heat and stir in butter, cheese, and bacon.
Let cool slightly, then form into balls or logs using two spoons and place on a plate.
Top with sour cream and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use store-brand cornmeal and regular cheddar cheese
Make ahead and reheat in a skillet with butter

recipes.name: Ciorba de zdrente
recipes.description: Romanian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef on all sides, about 8 minutes total.
Add diced onions, carrots, and celery, cooking until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and minced garlic, cooking for 1 minute.
Pour in beef broth and add bay leaves, bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes until beef is tender.
Cut potatoes into chunks and add to the pot, simmering for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Remove from heat and stir in vinegar or sour cream just before serving, season with salt and pepper.
cheapTips: Use affordable stew meat cuts
Skip sour cream and use vinegar for tangy flavor at lower cost

recipes.name: Foie gras à la roumaine
recipes.description: Romanian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean livers by removing any green bile spots and membranes under cool water.
Dice onions and apples finely, then sauté in butter over medium heat until caramelized, about 10 minutes.
Increase heat to medium-high and add livers, browning on all sides for 6-8 minutes.
Pour brandy over livers and carefully ignite it, letting flames subside for 1 minute.
Add cream, salt, pepper, thyme, and minced garlic, simmering for 5 minutes.
Transfer mixture to a blender and purée until completely smooth.
Press through a fine sieve for extra refinement, chill for 2 hours, and serve on toasted bread.
cheapTips: Use chicken liver instead of true foie gras
Prepare one day ahead and chill overnight for easier serving

recipes.name: Ardei umpluți
recipes.description: Romanian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut off tops of peppers and carefully remove seeds and membranes, leaving peppers intact.
Cook rice according to package directions, then set aside.
Heat oil in a large skillet and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Add ground meat, breaking it up with a spoon, and cook until browned, about 8 minutes.
Stir in cooked rice, paprika, salt, and pepper, then remove from heat.
Stuff each pepper with the meat and rice mixture, packing gently but not too tight.
Place stuffed peppers upright in a baking dish, pour tomato sauce and broth around them, and cover with foil.
Bake at 350°F for 45 minutes until peppers are tender.
cheapTips: Buy peppers in season or on sale and freeze
Use store-brand tomato sauce and ground meat on special

recipes.name: Mâncare de cartofi cu carne
recipes.description: Romanian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut beef into 1-inch cubes and heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown meat on all sides, about 8 minutes, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onion until golden, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste, stirring for 1 minute.
Return meat to pot, add paprika, bay leaf, salt, and pepper, then pour in broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 30 minutes.
Cut potatoes into large chunks and add to the pot, simmering for 25 minutes until potatoes are tender.
cheapTips: Buy beef on sale and freeze for later use
Use water instead of broth to reduce cost

recipes.name: Plăcintă cu brânză
recipes.description: Romanian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix ricotta, feta, egg, dill, salt, and pepper in a bowl until well combined.
Melt butter and brush a 9x13 baking dish lightly with it.
Lay one phyllo sheet in the dish, brush with melted butter, and repeat until you have 4 layers.
Spread the cheese mixture evenly over the phyllo.
Layer remaining 4 phyllo sheets on top, brushing each with melted butter.
Tuck edges down into the baking dish and brush the top with remaining butter.
Bake at 375°F for 35-40 minutes until golden brown and crispy, then serve with sour cream on the side.
cheapTips: Use store-brand phyllo sheets
Substitute cottage cheese mixed with a little feta for ricotta

recipes.name: Fatayer
recipes.description: Levantine snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, salt, oil, and warm water in a bowl, kneading until a soft dough forms, then let rest for 20 minutes.
Finely chop spinach and onion, then combine with lemon juice, sumac, pine nuts, salt, and pepper.
Divide dough into 12 equal balls and roll each into a thin circle about 4 inches wide.
Place a spoonful of spinach filling on each circle, then fold into a triangle, pinching edges to seal.
Place filled triangles on an oiled baking sheet.
Bake at 375°F for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.
cheapTips: Use frozen spinach instead of fresh
Omit pine nuts and add chickpeas for a cheaper filling

recipes.name: Manakish
recipes.description: Levantine breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, salt, oil, and warm water, kneading until a soft dough forms, then rest for 20 minutes.
Combine zaatar, sumac, sesame seeds, olive oil, and salt in a small bowl to create the topping mixture.
