Divide dough into 8 pieces and roll each into a thin oval about 0.25 inch thick.
Spread zaatar mixture generously over each oval, starting from the center and spreading outward.
Place on baking sheets and let rest for 10 minutes.
Bake at 425°F for 12-15 minutes until golden and crispy.
cheapTips: Buy zaatar and sumac from Middle Eastern stores for better prices
Make large batches and freeze unbaked for quick breakfasts

recipes.name: Halloumi
recipes.description: Levantine snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut halloumi cheese into 0.25-inch thick slices.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Place cheese slices in the hot pan and cook for 2-3 minutes until a golden crust forms.
Flip each slice carefully and cook the other side for another 2-3 minutes until golden.
Transfer to a plate and immediately squeeze fresh lemon juice over the top.
Sprinkle with dried oregano, thyme, black pepper, and salt, then serve hot.
cheapTips: Watch stores for halloumi sales and stock up
Serve with store-bought pita bread instead of buying sides

recipes.name: Freekeh
recipes.description: Levantine dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and season chicken with salt and pepper.
Brown the chicken cubes on all sides, then remove and set aside.
Sauté diced onion and garlic in the same pot until softened and fragrant.
Add freekeh and allspice, stirring constantly for 2 minutes to toast lightly.
Pour in vegetable broth and return chicken to the pot, bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until freekeh is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Let rest for 5 minutes off heat, then fluff with a fork and serve.
cheapTips: Buy freekeh in bulk from Middle Eastern markets for 40% savings
Use chicken thighs instead of breasts for better flavor and lower cost

recipes.name: Waraq Enab
recipes.description: Levantine lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix ground beef, uncooked rice, diced onion, tomato paste, 2 tablespoons olive oil, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and cinnamon in a bowl.
Rinse grape leaves under cool water and pat dry with paper towels.
Lay a grape leaf flat and place 1 tablespoon of filling near the stem end.
Fold the stem end over the filling, then fold in the sides and roll tightly toward the tip.
Arrange rolls seam-side down in a pot lined with extra grape leaves.
Pour vegetable broth and remaining olive oil over the rolls, then cover with a plate to keep them compressed.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Serve warm with extra lemon juice on the side.
cheapTips: Buy jarred grape leaves at discount stores like Costco
Use half ground beef and half ground lamb for authentic flavor at same price

recipes.name: Saltah
recipes.description: Yemeni lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and brown ground beef with chopped onion, breaking it apart as it cooks.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato sauce, sahawiq, water, salt, and pepper, then bring to a simmer.
Add fenugreek leaves and cilantro, stirring well to combine, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Create 4 wells in the mixture and crack an egg into each well.
Cover the pot and simmer for 8 minutes until egg whites set but yolks remain runny.
Serve hot directly from the pot with bread for scooping.
cheapTips: Make homemade sahawiq with jalapeños and garlic instead of buying bottled
Substitute fenugreek with fresh spinach if unavailable at similar cost

recipes.name: Madhbi
recipes.description: Yemeni lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat ghee in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken pieces on all sides in batches, then set aside and reserve.
In the same pot, cook sliced onions until deeply caramelized, about 15 minutes.
Add minced garlic and ginger, cooking for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Toast fenugreek seeds, cloves, and cardamom pods in a dry skillet for 1 minute, then add to pot.
Return chicken to pot, add bay leaves, chicken broth, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Uncover and simmer for another 15 minutes to reduce liquid slightly.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve with rice or bread.
cheapTips: Buy whole chicken and cut it yourself to save 30% versus pre-cut pieces
Use butter instead of ghee to reduce cost by half

recipes.name: Zurbian
recipes.description: Yemeni lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and brown chicken cubes seasoned with salt and pepper, then set aside.
Sauté sliced onions in the same pot until golden, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and ginger, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add turmeric, cardamom pods, and cinnamon stick, stirring for 30 seconds to bloom spices.
Return chicken to pot, add unrinsed basmati rice, and stir constantly for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover tightly.
Simmer without stirring for 20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Let rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and garnish with cilantro and mint.
cheapTips: Buy basmati rice in 10-lb bags at ethnic markets for 40% savings
Use chicken breasts instead of thighs and reduce cooking time by 5 minutes

recipes.name: Salta
recipes.description: Yemeni lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown lamb pieces seasoned with salt, pepper, and cumin.
Remove lamb and set aside, then sauté chopped onion in the same pot until softened.
Add minced garlic and jalapeño peppers, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then return lamb to pot.
Add water and chopped cilantro, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 30 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning, then create 4 wells in the stew.
Crack an egg into each well, cover, and simmer for 8 minutes until eggs are set.
Serve hot from the pot with flatbread for scooping.
cheapTips: Substitute lamb with beef chuck roast for 25% savings in cost
Buy cilantro in bulk from warehouse clubs

recipes.name: Fahsa
recipes.description: Yemeni lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown cubed meat with salt and pepper.
Remove meat and set aside, then sauté chopped onion until golden brown.
Add minced garlic, ginger, and turmeric, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return meat to pot, add water, and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 35 minutes.
Add sliced beef liver and diced tomato, simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Stir in chopped cilantro and simmer for another 5 minutes until liver is cooked through.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed, then serve piping hot with rice or bread.
cheapTips: Buy beef liver on sale and freeze for later use
Omit liver and double the cubed meat for vegetable-averse cooks

recipes.name: Aseed
recipes.description: Yemeni breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons ghee in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté diced onion until deeply caramelized, about 8 minutes.
In a separate bowl, gradually add water to flour while stirring to form a thick paste, then mix in salt.
Transfer the flour mixture to the skillet with caramelized onion and begin stirring constantly.
Add remaining ghee in stages while continuing to stir the mixture for 8 minutes until it becomes a cohesive dough.
Shape the aseed into a mound on a serving plate and create a well in the center.
Drizzle honey into the well and crack eggs around the top of the mound.
Serve immediately while still warm, eating the creamy dough and eggs together.
cheapTips: Use butter instead of ghee to save 30%
Buy local honey in bulk at farmers markets

recipes.name: Bint Al-Sahn
recipes.description: Yemeni lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, salt, and 1/4 cup ghee together, then gradually add warm water to form a soft dough.
Knead dough for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then let rest covered for 30 minutes.
Divide dough into 8 equal portions and roll each into a thin circle, stretching gently with your hands.
Brush a 9x13 baking dish generously with melted ghee and layer 4 dough circles, brushing each with ghee.
Beat eggs together and pour evenly over the layered dough, then layer remaining 4 dough circles with ghee between each.
Brush the top layer with remaining ghee and sprinkle with sesame seeds and nigella seeds.
Bake at 375°F for 30-35 minutes until the top is golden brown and crispy.
Remove from oven and immediately pour warm honey over the entire dish, then let cool for 5 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Make ghee at home by clarifying butter to save 40%
Buy honey in bulk when on sale and store for months

recipes.name: Jachnun
recipes.description: Yemeni breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, salt, yeast, and sugar in a bowl, then add warm water and oil, stirring until a soft dough forms.
Knead dough for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic, then place in an oiled bowl covered for 45 minutes until doubled.
Punch down dough and roll into a thin rectangle about 10x14 inches on a floured surface.
Spread softened butter over entire surface, then sprinkle evenly with brown sugar and cinnamon.
Starting from a long side, roll the dough tightly into a log, then cut into 8 equal spiral pieces.
Place spirals cut-side up in a greased 9x13 baking dish.
Beat 2 eggs and brush over the top of each roll, then bake at 375°F for 25-30 minutes until golden brown.
Cool for 5 minutes in the pan before serving warm with honey or jam.
cheapTips: Buy instant yeast in bulk and store in freezer for 6 months of savings
Use margarine instead of butter to save 20%

recipes.name: Harees
recipes.description: Yemeni lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse wheat grains thoroughly and soak in water for 30 minutes.
Heat ghee in a large pot and sauté diced onion, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add chicken breast, turmeric, salt, and pepper, cooking for 5 minutes.
Add drained wheat grains and 8 cups water, bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer covered for 90 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
When wheat is very soft and broken down, continue cooking and stirring until mixture becomes a thick, porridge-like consistency.
Shred the cooked chicken with a fork and mix thoroughly into the harees.
Serve hot in a mound, drizzle with ghee, and garnish with fried onions if desired.
cheapTips: Buy wheat grains in bulk from Middle Eastern or Indian markets for significant savings.
Use chicken thighs instead of breast for richer flavor at lower cost.

recipes.name: Thareed
recipes.description: Yemeni dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat ghee in a large pot and brown the diced meat on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onion and minced garlic until golden brown.
Add cumin and coriander, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return meat to pot, add tomato sauce and water, bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 60 minutes until meat is tender.
Tear or cut pita bread into bite-sized pieces and layer them in a large serving dish.
Pour the hot meat and sauce mixture over the bread pieces.
Let it soak for 2 minutes, then toss gently to combine and serve warm.
cheapTips: Use beef chuck or stewing meat for better value than premium cuts.
Make your own tomato sauce from canned tomatoes if available for less cost.

recipes.name: Malawah
recipes.description: Yemeni breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt in a large bowl, then add water gradually while kneading into a soft dough.
Knead for 5 minutes until smooth, cover with a damp cloth, and let rest for 15 minutes.
Divide dough into 6 equal balls and flatten each into a thin disk.
Brush generously with ghee, then fold in half and brush again, then fold in half once more into a triangle.
Heat oil in a heavy skillet to 350°F and fry each malawah triangle for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and arrange on a serving plate.
Beat eggs lightly and pour over the warm malawah.
Drizzle generously with honey and serve immediately while still warm.
cheapTips: Make your own dough rather than buying pre-made to save significantly.
Use regular oil instead of ghee for a budget-friendly version.

recipes.name: Shafut
recipes.description: Yemeni breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut bread into bite-sized cubes and layer them in a serving bowl.
In a skillet, melt ghee over medium heat and fry eggs until yolks are set but still slightly runny.
Place fried eggs on top of the bread cubes.
Heat yogurt gently in a saucepan without boiling, stirring occasionally.
Pour the warm yogurt over the bread and eggs.
Drizzle honey over the entire dish and sprinkle with a pinch of salt.
Serve immediately while warm, mixing gently before eating.
cheapTips: Buy store-brand yogurt and eggs in bulk during sales for lower costs.
Use day-old bread which is often discounted.

recipes.name: Kabsa
recipes.description: Yemeni lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat ghee in a large pot and brown the chicken pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté sliced onion until golden, then add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add cumin, cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaves, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return chicken to pot, add tomato sauce and chicken broth, bringing to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 30 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Remove chicken, shred it into bite-sized pieces, and set aside.
In the same broth, add rice and bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender.
Fluff rice with a fork, mix in shredded chicken, and serve hot, preferably arranged on a platter with rice on bottom and chicken on top.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs instead of breasts for better flavor and lower cost.
Use vegetable broth or water with bouillon cubes if chicken broth is expensive.

recipes.name: Bazeen
recipes.description: Yemeni dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat half the ghee in a large skillet and brown the ground meat, breaking it apart as it cooks.
Add diced onion, garlic, and tomato paste, cooking until onion is soft, about 5 minutes.
Add water, cumin, salt, and pepper, then simmer the meat sauce for 15 minutes.
In a separate large pot, melt remaining ghee over medium heat and toast flour for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly until lightly golden.
Gradually add the meat mixture to the flour while stirring constantly to combine into a thick, pliable dough.
Continue stirring and cooking for 5 minutes until the bazeen comes together as a cohesive mass.
Mound the bazeen into a dome shape on a serving platter, making an indentation on top.
Pour any remaining meat sauce into the indentation and serve warm with additional ghee drizzled on top if desired.
cheapTips: Use ground beef instead of lamb for significant cost savings.
Toast flour in butter to save money versus using expensive ghee exclusively.

recipes.name: Saleeg
recipes.description: Yemeni lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a large pot, bring chicken broth to a boil and add whole chicken pieces with half the sliced onions.
Reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Remove chicken, shred into bite-sized pieces, and set aside, keeping broth in the pot.
In a separate skillet, heat ghee and sauté remaining sliced onion and minced garlic until golden.
Add turmeric and stir, then add rice and stir to coat with ghee, cooking for 2 minutes.
Transfer rice mixture to the chicken broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat.
Cover and simmer for 25 minutes until rice is very soft and creamy, stirring occasionally.
Mix in the shredded chicken, adjust seasoning with salt and pepper, and serve warm in bowls.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs or a whole chicken cut into pieces for better value.
Make broth from scratch using chicken bones and water for significant savings.

recipes.name: Maraq
recipes.description: Yemeni lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat ghee in a large pot and brown the meat pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onion until soft, then add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add cumin and coriander, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return meat to pot and add tomato sauce and water, bringing to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until meat is very tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot in bowls as a thick soup or stew.
Traditionally served with bread for dipping or over rice.
cheapTips: Use beef chuck or shoulder cuts which are cheaper and become tender with cooking.
Make from canned tomatoes instead of tomato sauce for better value.

recipes.name: Haneed
recipes.description: Yemeni lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a large pot, brown the meat pieces with bones on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot with remaining ghee, sauté sliced onion and minced garlic until golden.
Add tomato paste, cumin, salt, and pepper, stirring for 1 minute.
Return meat to pot, add water, and bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 45 minutes until meat is very tender.
In a separate bowl, mix flour with melted ghee to form a thick paste.
Remove meat pieces from the pot and set aside, keeping the cooking liquid.
Form flour and ghee mixture into a dough ball and wrap it in cloth, then place it in the center of a large serving dish.
Arrange cooked meat around the dough ball, pour remaining cooking liquid over everything, and serve by tearing pieces of the dough and dipping in the meat sauce.
cheapTips: Use beef chuck or shoulder with bones instead of lamb for lower cost.
Buy meat on sale and freeze until ready to use.

recipes.name: Areesh
recipes.description: Yemeni breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Tear or cut bread into bite-sized pieces and layer in a shallow serving bowl.
Warm ghee in a small skillet over medium-low heat until just melted.
Chop dates and roughly chop nuts, then mix together.
Pour warm ghee evenly over the bread pieces.
Warm yogurt gently in a saucepan without boiling, stirring occasionally.
Pour warm yogurt over the bread and ghee.
Sprinkle date and nut mixture on top.
Drizzle honey generously over everything and serve immediately while warm, stirring gently before eating.
cheapTips: Use day-old bread for significant savings.
Buy dates and nuts in bulk from Middle Eastern markets for better prices.

recipes.name: Brik
recipes.description: Tunisian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350°F.
Mix drained tuna, minced onion, chopped parsley, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Place one phyllo sheet on a clean surface and spoon tuna mixture in the center.
Crack an egg into the center of the filling and fold the phyllo into a triangle, sealing edges.
Carefully place the folded brik into hot oil and fry 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with harissa or lemon wedges.
cheapTips: Buy canned tuna on sale and freeze for later use
Use store-brand phyllo dough instead of name brands

recipes.name: Tajine
recipes.description: Tunisian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown chicken thighs on both sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same skillet, sauté diced onions and minced garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add paprika, salt, and pepper to the onion mixture and stir for 1 minute.
Return chicken to the skillet, add water, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add diced potatoes and continue cooking covered for 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Make 4 wells in the mixture and crack an egg into each well, then cover and cook for 4-5 minutes until eggs are set.
Serve hot directly from the skillet.
cheapTips: Use chicken legs instead of thighs for budget savings
Buy potatoes in bulk during sales and store in cool, dark place

recipes.name: Maklouba
recipes.description: Tunisian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice eggplant and zucchini and sauté in olive oil in a large pot until lightly browned, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onions and minced garlic for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add rice and stir to coat with oil, cooking for 2 minutes.
Pour in vegetable broth, paprika, salt, and pepper, and bring to a boil.
Return cooked vegetables to the pot and stir in diced tomatoes.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes, then invert onto a serving platter to flip the rice cake.
cheapTips: Buy rice in bulk from ethnic markets for lower prices
Use seasonal vegetables that are on sale for cost reduction

recipes.name: Lablabi
recipes.description: Tunisian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a pot and sauté minced garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in harissa paste and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add drained chickpeas, cumin, caraway seeds, salt, and water or broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 8 minutes until slightly thickened.
Tear bread into chunks and divide among serving bowls.
Ladle hot chickpea mixture over the bread.
Serve immediately with extra harissa and olive oil on the side.
cheapTips: Buy canned chickpeas in bulk when on sale
Use store-brand harissa paste instead of imported brands

recipes.name: Ftira
recipes.description: Tunisian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt in a large bowl, create a well, and gradually add water while mixing to form a soft dough.
Knead dough for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then let rest for 30 minutes covered.
Divide dough into 4 equal portions and roll each thin, then brush generously with olive oil.
Layer the oiled dough sheets together, fold into quarters, and let rest for 10 minutes.
Roll out each ftira to a thin circle, heat olive oil in a skillet, and fry until puffed and light brown on both sides.
Mix drained tuna, minced onion, harissa, and chopped parsley together for filling.
Crack an egg into the center of each hot ftira, top with tuna mixture, fold edges inward, and cook until egg is set.
cheapTips: Make dough in advance and refrigerate to save prep time
Buy canned tuna in bulk for better prices

recipes.name: Chorba
recipes.description: Tunisian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown beef chunks on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onions and minced garlic for 3 minutes until softened.
Stir in harissa paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomatoes with their juice, beef broth, caraway seeds, salt, and pepper.
Return meat to the pot, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 25 minutes.
Add drained chickpeas and continue simmering for 10 more minutes until meat is tender.
Taste and adjust seasonings, then serve hot in bowls.
cheapTips: Use beef stew meat from budget cuts like chuck
Buy canned tomatoes and chickpeas on sale and stock up

recipes.name: Merguez
recipes.description: Tunisian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak sausage casings in warm water for 30 minutes to soften them.
Mix ground lamb, harissa, minced garlic, caraway seeds, paprika, salt, and pepper in a bowl until well combined.
Fit a sausage casing onto a sausage stuffer nozzle and fill slowly with meat mixture, pricking air pockets as you go.
Twist the filled casing into 4-inch links and secure with kitchen twine if needed.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook merguez sausages for 12-15 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through.
Serve hot with bread and harissa or in couscous.
cheapTips: Use ground beef instead of lamb to reduce cost
Skip natural casings and make as patties instead

recipes.name: Kaftaji
recipes.description: Tunisian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut potatoes into small cubes and fry in olive oil until crispy and golden, then remove and drain on paper towels.
In the same pot, brown ground beef with minced onion and garlic, breaking it apart as it cooks, about 8 minutes.
Stir in harissa paste, salt, and pepper, then cook for 2 minutes.
Return fried potatoes to the pot and mix well with the meat.
Create 3 wells in the mixture and crack an egg into each well, then cover and cook for 4-5 minutes until eggs are set.
Sprinkle with fresh cilantro and serve hot from the pot.
cheapTips: Use ground beef trimmings or cheaper cuts when available
Make extra fried potatoes in advance to save time

recipes.name: Ojja
recipes.description: Tunisian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice merguez sausages and cook in olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until browned, about 5 minutes, then remove.
In the same skillet, sauté diced onion and bell pepper for 3 minutes until softened.
Add diced tomatoes and harissa paste, then cook for 2 minutes.
Return sausage to the skillet and reduce heat to medium.
Pour eggs directly into the mixture and scramble gently, stirring occasionally, until eggs are cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot with bread.
cheapTips: Use regular sausage instead of merguez to save money
Buy eggs in bulk for breakfast meal prep

recipes.name: Slata Mechouia
recipes.description: Tunisian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Char whole peppers and tomatoes over an open flame or under a broiler until skin is blackened all over, about 10 minutes.
Place charred peppers and tomatoes in a plastic bag for 5 minutes to steam and loosen skin.
Peel off the charred skin, remove seeds, and dice the peppers and tomatoes into a bowl.
Dice cucumber and red onion, then add to the peppers and tomatoes.
In a small bowl, whisk together minced garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, harissa, salt, and pepper.
Pour dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.
Let chill for 10 minutes, garnish with fresh cilantro, and serve cold or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Buy peppers and tomatoes when in season for best prices
Use bottled lemon juice to save prep time

recipes.name: Salata Djeaj
recipes.description: Tunisian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil chicken breast in salted water for 20 minutes until fully cooked, then shred into bite-sized pieces.
Dice tomatoes and onions into small pieces and place in a serving bowl.
Mince garlic and mix with olive oil, lemon juice, harissa, and caraway seeds.
Toss shredded chicken with the dressing and combine with tomatoes and onions.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.
cheapTips: Buy chicken on sale and freeze until needed
Use fresh seasonal tomatoes instead of premium varieties

recipes.name: Harissa
recipes.description: Tunisian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Remove seeds from dried red chili peppers and soak in warm water for 15 minutes until softened.
Toast caraway and coriander seeds in a dry skillet for 1 minute until fragrant, then grind into powder.
Drain softened peppers and place in a food processor with minced garlic and ground spices.
Pulse into a paste, then slowly add olive oil while blending until smooth.
Add salt and adjust consistency with a splash of water if needed, then store in an airtight jar.
cheapTips: Buy dried chilis in bulk from international sections
Make large batches and freeze in ice cube trays

recipes.name: Deglet Noor
recipes.description: Tunisian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Remove the pit from each date by making a small slit with a knife and gently pressing out the seed.
Toast whole almonds in a dry skillet for 3 minutes over medium heat until fragrant.
Stuff each pitted date with a teaspoon of almond butter and one toasted almond.
Sprinkle lightly with sea salt and serve at room temperature.
cheapTips: Buy dates in bulk during sales
Make your own almond butter to save money

recipes.name: Hlelem
recipes.description: Tunisian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until golden, about 4 minutes.
Add ground beef and cook over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, breaking apart as it cooks, until browned.
Stir in tomato paste, diced chili pepper, salt, and pepper, cooking for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add water and bring to a simmer, then reduce heat and cook uncovered for 15 minutes until sauce thickens.
Taste and adjust seasonings, then finish with fresh parsley and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use 80/20 ground beef instead of leaner cuts
Buy tomato paste in bulk cans and freeze portions

recipes.name: Pasta Skhoun
recipes.description: Tunisian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil pasta according to package directions in salted water, then drain and set aside.
Heat olive oil and sauté diced onion and garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add ground beef and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it apart, until browned, then stir in harissa and tomatoes.
Simmer sauce for 10 minutes until thickened, then season with salt and pepper.
Beat eggs in a small bowl, then slowly stir into the hot meat sauce to create ribbons while stirring constantly.
Toss cooked pasta with the meat sauce and top with Parmesan cheese before serving.
cheapTips: Use generic pasta brands
Buy ground beef in bulk when on sale and freeze

recipes.name: Fricassée
recipes.description: Tunisian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut white bread into small cubes and fry in olive oil over medium-high heat for 5 minutes until golden and crispy.
Push croutons to the side and add minced garlic to the oil, cooking for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Beat eggs with water, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Pour beaten eggs over croutons and stir gently until eggs are soft and custard-like, about 4 minutes.
Finish with fresh cilantro and serve immediately while warm.
cheapTips: Use day-old or discount bread
Buy eggs in bulk when on sale

recipes.name: Mloukhia
recipes.description: Tunisian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring chicken broth to a boil in a large pot and add chicken breast with diced onion, simmering for 20 minutes until cooked.
Remove chicken, shred it, and return to the broth.
Heat olive oil in a separate skillet and sauté minced garlic and toasted coriander seeds for 1 minute.
Add frozen mloukhia (or finely chop fresh) and stir into the garlic oil until wilted, about 3 minutes.
Pour the mloukhia mixture into the chicken broth and simmer for 10 minutes, then season with salt and pepper.
Stir in fresh cilantro and serve hot in bowls with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Buy frozen mloukhia instead of fresh for year-round availability
Use chicken bone broth for deeper flavor and nutrition

recipes.name: Kessra
recipes.description: Tunisian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, salt, and 2 tablespoons olive oil in a bowl, then gradually add water and knead into a soft dough for 5 minutes.
Divide dough into 3 equal balls and let rest for 10 minutes under a cloth.
Roll each ball very thin on a floured surface, then brush with remaining olive oil.
Spread pitted dates mixed with cinnamon across each thin dough sheet, then roll tightly like a spiral.
Coil the rolled dough and flatten slightly, then pan-fry in butter over medium heat for 5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Cut into wedges and serve warm, optionally drizzled with honey.
cheapTips: Buy dates in bulk
Use store-brand flour and butter

recipes.name: Tham
recipes.description: Tunisian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Drain and rinse canned chickpeas, then pat dry with paper towels.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and add minced garlic and caraway seeds, cooking for 1 minute.
Add chickpeas and stir-fry for 5 minutes until heated through and slightly crispy on the edges.
Season with salt, pepper, and paprika, then finish with lemon juice and serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy canned chickpeas in bulk during sales
Use basic spices from bulk bins

recipes.name: Chorba Frik
recipes.description: Algerian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and brown meat pieces on all sides over medium-high heat, about 8 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Sauté diced onion and garlic in the same pot for 3 minutes until softened, then stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Return meat to pot and add beef broth, bringing to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Add frik and drained chickpeas to the pot and simmer for another 15 minutes until frik is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, garnish with fresh cilantro, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy frik from Middle Eastern markets instead of specialty stores
Use beef chuck roast instead of premium cuts and cook longer

recipes.name: Mandazi
recipes.description: Kenyan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
Whisk together eggs and milk in a separate bowl.
Combine wet and dry ingredients, stirring until a soft dough forms.
Knead dough for 5 minutes until smooth, then let rest 15 minutes.
Roll dough to 0.5-inch thickness and cut into squares or diamond shapes.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pan or skillet.
Fry mandazi 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and puffed.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm, optionally dusted with sugar.
cheapTips: Buy oil in bulk and reuse for multiple batches of frying.
Make dough night before and refrigerate to save time.

recipes.name: Matoke
recipes.description: Kenyan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel plantains by cutting off ends and slicing skin lengthwise, then peel away skin.
Chop plantains into 2-inch rounds and set aside.
Heat oil in a large pot and sauté diced onions and minced garlic until softened.
Add diced tomatoes and cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add plantain pieces, salt, and pepper, then pour in vegetable broth.
Cover pot and simmer 30-35 minutes until plantains are very tender.
Mash plantains partially with a fork to create chunky texture while cooking.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot as a main course or side dish.
cheapTips: Buy plantains in bulk when in season for better prices.
Use canned tomatoes instead of fresh to reduce cost.

recipes.name: Mukate
recipes.description: Kenyan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk egg and water together, then add to flour with 2 tablespoons oil.
Knead dough for 8 minutes until elastic and smooth, adding water if too dry.
Divide dough into 6 balls and cover with damp cloth for 15 minutes.
Roll each ball very thin into a circle, about 8 inches diameter.
Heat frying oil to 350°F in a deep skillet or wok.
Fry each bread 2 minutes per side until golden, puffy, and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with bean stew or as is.
cheapTips: Reuse frying oil multiple times by straining.
Make larger batches and freeze for future use.

recipes.name: Githeri ya Mahindi
recipes.description: Kenyan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté diced onions and minced garlic until golden.
Add diced tomatoes and cook 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add corn kernels and green beans, stirring well to combine.
Pour in vegetable broth, then season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 25-30 minutes.
Stir occasionally to ensure even cooking of all vegetables.
Test corn and beans for tenderness; adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot as a main course or side dish.
cheapTips: Buy frozen corn and beans in bulk at warehouse stores.
Use canned tomatoes to save prep time and money.

recipes.name: Beans and Maize
recipes.description: Kenyan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse dried beans and soak in water for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Drain beans and boil in fresh water for 45 minutes until partially cooked.
Heat oil in a large pot and sauté diced onions and minced garlic until soft.
Stir in tomato paste and cook 2 minutes to deepen flavor.
Add partially cooked beans with cooking liquid to the pot.
Add corn kernels, salt, and pepper, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 20-25 minutes until beans are completely tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with cornbread or rice.
cheapTips: Buy dried beans in bulk for significant savings.
Soak beans overnight to reduce cooking time and fuel cost.

recipes.name: Nyama na Irio
recipes.description: Kenyan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut beef into 1.5-inch cubes and pat dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown beef in batches, 5 minutes total.
Remove beef and sauté diced onions and garlic until softened, about 5 minutes.
Return beef to pot, add diced tomatoes and tomato paste, simmer 2 minutes.
Pour in broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and cover; simmer 30 minutes.
Add cubed potatoes, corn, and peas; season with salt and pepper.
Continue simmering covered for 20-25 minutes until potatoes and meat are very tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with ugali or rice.
cheapTips: Buy beef chuck on sale and freeze for later use.
Use frozen vegetables to reduce prep time and food waste.

recipes.name: Mukimo
recipes.description: Kenyan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and cut potatoes into 1-inch cubes.
Heat oil in a large pot and sauté diced onions until soft, about 3 minutes.
Add potato cubes and stir well to coat with oil.
Pour in water and bring to a boil, then reduce heat.
Simmer covered for 15 minutes until potatoes soften.
Add corn kernels and season with salt and pepper, stirring well.
Continue simmering 5-7 minutes until potatoes are very tender.
Mash mixture coarsely with a wooden spoon until chunky, then serve hot garnished with green onions.
cheapTips: Use canned corn to reduce prep work.
Buy potatoes in bulk for lower per-pound cost.

recipes.name: Arrowroot
recipes.description: Kenyan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix arrowroot flour with water in a bowl to make a smooth paste, stirring well.
Heat milk in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming but not boiling.
Slowly pour arrowroot paste into hot milk while stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Continue stirring for 3-4 minutes as mixture thickens.
Add sugar, salt, and vanilla extract, stirring until fully combined.
Cook 1 more minute until desired thickness is reached.
Pour into bowls and serve hot, optionally topping with cinnamon or honey.
cheapTips: Buy arrowroot flour in bulk for significant savings.
Use powdered milk to reduce cost further if needed.

recipes.name: Ndengu
recipes.description: Kenyan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse mung beans thoroughly and soak in water for 2 hours, then drain.
Boil beans in fresh water for 30 minutes until partially cooked, then drain.
Heat oil in a large pot and sauté diced onions, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes and cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add partially cooked beans and pour in 4 cups fresh water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 20-25 minutes.
Stir occasionally and add more water if beans appear too dry.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot as main course or with rice.
cheapTips: Buy mung beans dried and in bulk for lowest cost.
Soak beans overnight to reduce cooking time significantly.

recipes.name: Mutura
recipes.description: Kenyan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean beef casings by running cold water through them multiple times.
Mix ground beef, chopped liver, onions, garlic, ginger, and hot peppers in a large bowl.
Season meat mixture generously with salt, pepper, cumin, and coriander; mix thoroughly.
Using a sausage stuffer or piping bag, carefully fill casings with meat mixture.
Tie off casings at 4-inch intervals with kitchen twine to form individual sausages.
Prick each sausage multiple times with a fork to prevent bursting.
Grill or pan-fry sausages over medium-high heat for 15-20 minutes, turning frequently.
Serve hot with grilled onions, tomato sauce, and bread as street food or appetizer.
cheapTips: Buy beef liver at butcher counter for significant discount.
Purchase casings in bulk and freeze for future batches.

recipes.name: Mshikaki
recipes.description: Kenyan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Thread beef cubes, onions, tomatoes, and bell peppers alternately onto soaked wooden skewers.
Mix oil, salt, pepper, garlic, and lemon juice in a bowl and brush generously over the skewers.
Heat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat until very hot.
Place skewers on the hot grill and cook for 12-15 minutes, turning every 3 minutes until meat is charred and cooked through.
Remove from heat and let rest for 2 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Buy beef on sale and freeze until ready to use
Use seasonal vegetables like zucchini or mushrooms to bulk out the skewers cheaply

recipes.name: Posho and Bean Stew
recipes.description: Kenyan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring 5 cups of water to a boil in a large pot with salt.
Slowly add cornmeal while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring frequently until thick and creamy.
In another pot, heat oil and sauté onions and garlic until softened.
Add diced tomatoes, beans, cumin, and 1 cup water; simmer for 12 minutes until stew thickens.
Serve hot posho on plates with bean stew spooned over top.
cheapTips: Buy dried beans and cook in bulk to save 50% versus canned
Use cornmeal in bulk from ethnic markets for better prices

recipes.name: Uji
recipes.description: Kenyan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix cornmeal and millet flour with 1 cup cold water in a bowl, stirring until smooth to avoid lumps.
Bring milk to a simmer in a saucepan over medium heat.
Slowly pour the flour mixture into the simmering milk while stirring constantly.
Add sugar, salt, and cinnamon, and continue stirring for 8-10 minutes until thick and creamy.
Serve hot in bowls while still warm.
cheapTips: Buy grains in bulk and store in airtight containers
Use powdered milk instead of fresh milk to reduce cost by 40%

recipes.name: Mbaazi
recipes.description: Kenyan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onions, garlic, and ginger for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add potatoes, pigeon peas (drained), coconut milk, salt, and cumin.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 25 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Stir occasionally and adjust seasoning to taste before serving hot.
cheapTips: Buy canned pigeon peas in bulk from African or Asian markets
Use light coconut milk instead of full-fat to save money

recipes.name: Misir Kik Alicha
recipes.description: Ethiopian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse lentils under cold water until water runs clear.
Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onions, garlic, and ginger for 4 minutes until soft.
Add turmeric and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add lentils, water, salt, and pepper; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lentils are very soft and creamy.
Adjust seasoning and stir in cayenne pepper before serving.
cheapTips: Buy lentils in bulk from health food or ethnic stores
This dish freezes well, so make a large batch and portion for later meals

recipes.name: Dulet
recipes.description: Ethiopian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat niter kibbeh in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic, ginger, and jalapeños; sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced liver and tripe, stirring constantly for 5-7 minutes until partially cooked.
Add green onions, salt, and pepper, continuing to cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add water and simmer for 8-10 minutes until liver is fully cooked and tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with injera.
cheapTips: Buy liver and tripe from butcher counters, often cheaper than packaged
Substitute all tripe if liver is unavailable and expensive

recipes.name: Firfir
recipes.description: Ethiopian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat niter kibbeh in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onions, garlic, and ginger for 3 minutes until soft.
Stir in berbere spice and salt, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add torn injera pieces and water or broth, stirring gently to combine.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until bread breaks down and mixture is thick and creamy.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot.
cheapTips: Make or buy injera in bulk when on sale and freeze
Use store-brand spices or make your own berbere blend to save money

recipes.name: Shiro Firfir
recipes.description: Ethiopian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix shiro powder with 1 cup cold water in a bowl, stirring until smooth.
Heat niter kibbeh in a pot and sauté onions, garlic, and ginger for 3 minutes.
Slowly pour shiro mixture into the pot while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Add remaining 2 cups water and salt, stirring frequently.
Simmer over low heat for 12-15 minutes, stirring often, until thick and smooth.
Tear injera into pieces and stir into shiro, or serve on the side.
cheapTips: Buy shiro powder online or at ethnic stores for bulk prices
Use vegetable oil instead of niter kibbeh to reduce cost by 30%

recipes.name: Misir Tibs
recipes.description: Ethiopian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat niter kibbeh in a large pot over high heat and sear beef cubes for 4-5 minutes until browned; set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onions, garlic, and ginger for 3 minutes until soft.
Add tomatoes and berbere spice, cooking for 2 minutes while stirring.
Return beef to pot with lentils, water, and salt; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer covered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lentils are tender and beef is cooked through.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with injera or rice.
cheapTips: Buy beef on sale and freeze; cube when partially frozen for easier prep
Lentils are already inexpensive; don't skimp on quality

recipes.name: Doro Alecha
recipes.description: Ethiopian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat niter kibbeh in a large pot and sauté onions, garlic, and ginger for 5 minutes until golden.
Add turmeric and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces and brown on all sides for 6-7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add potatoes, water, salt, and pepper; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until chicken is cooked and potatoes are tender.
Peel hard-boiled eggs and add to pot; simmer for 2-3 minutes to heat through.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with injera.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs instead of breasts; they're cheaper and stay moist
Make eggs in bulk and keep in fridge for quick protein additions

recipes.name: Fulba
recipes.description: Ethiopian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat and sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Mix chickpea flour with water to form a thick, smooth paste.
Add the flour mixture to the pan and stir constantly to avoid lumps.
Season with cayenne pepper and salt, stirring continuously.
Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring frequently, until the mixture thickens and darkens slightly.
Transfer to a serving plate and shape into a mound using an oiled spatula.
cheapTips: Buy chickpea flour in bulk from international or online stores
Use basic pantry spices to reduce costs

recipes.name: Bobotie
recipes.description: Cape Malay dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Sauté onion and garlic in a large skillet until softened, then add ground beef and brown.
Stir in curry powder, raisins, and bay leaf, cooking for 2 minutes.
Soak bread in half the milk, then crumble into the meat mixture and stir well.
Transfer mixture to a greased baking dish and press down evenly.
Whisk eggs with remaining milk, salt, and pepper, then pour over the meat layer.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the custard topping is set and lightly golden.
cheapTips: Use ground chuck instead of premium cuts
Buy curry powder from bulk sections

recipes.name: Bunny Chow
recipes.description: Durban Indian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté onion, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add curry powder and chili powder, stirring for 1 minute until toasted.
Add chicken cubes and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in coconut milk and broth, bring to a boil, then simmer for 25-30 minutes until chicken is tender.
Cut the top off the bread loaf and hollow out the inside, reserving the removed bread.
Tear the reserved bread into chunks and add to the curry.
Simmer for 5 minutes until bread softens into the sauce, then stir in cilantro.
Fill the bread hollows with the curry and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy rotisserie chicken and shred instead of raw chicken breast
Use light coconut milk to reduce fat and cost

recipes.name: Sosaties
recipes.description: Cape Malay dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, garlic, ginger, and curry powder in a bowl.
Marinate lamb cubes in the mixture for at least 30 minutes.
Thread lamb, onion chunks, and apricots alternately onto skewers.
Reserve marinade and brush skewers with it.
Heat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat and cook skewers for 12-15 minutes, turning occasionally and basting with reserved marinade.
Serve hot with rice or flatbread.
cheapTips: Substitute lamb with beef chuck for lower cost
Buy dried apricots from bulk bins

recipes.name: Boerewors
recipes.description: South African dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast coriander seeds, cloves, and allspice in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then grind into powder.
Mix ground beef and pork with garlic, spices, salt, vinegar, and 1/4 cup water until combined.
Soak sausage casings in warm water for 10 minutes.
Stuff casings with meat mixture using a sausage stuffer, twisting into 6-inch links.
Prick casings gently with a fork to prevent bursting.
Grill or pan-fry over medium heat for 15-20 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Buy meat on sale and freeze until ready to make
Order casings online in bulk for better pricing

recipes.name: Koeksister
recipes.description: South African snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Combine melted butter, egg, and milk, then add to dry ingredients and mix until a soft dough forms.
Roll dough on a floured surface to 1/8-inch thickness and cut into strips 3 inches long.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pan.
Mix sugar, ginger, and cinnamon in a shallow bowl.
Fry dough strips in batches for 1-2 minutes per side until golden.
Immediately roll hot koeksisters in the sugar-spice mixture while still warm.
Cool on a wire rack and serve warm.
cheapTips: Make a double batch and freeze unbaked dough
Use oil sparingly and strain for reuse

recipes.name: Biltong
recipes.description: South African snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast coriander seeds in a dry pan for 1 minute, then crush coarsely.
Mix salt, sugar, pepper, coriander, garlic powder, and paprika in a bowl.
Rub beef slices thoroughly with vinegar, then coat evenly with spice mixture.
Layer coated beef in a container, cover, and refrigerate for 6-12 hours.
Pat beef dry with paper towels.
Hang strips from hooks or string in a warm, well-ventilated area (70-75°F), or use a dehydrator at 160°F.
Dry for 5-7 days until beef is completely dry but still slightly flexible.
Store in an airtight container.
cheapTips: Buy beef when on sale and freeze until ready to make
Use a home dehydrator or oven on lowest setting to save space

recipes.name: Droëwors
recipes.description: South African snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast coriander seeds and grind finely.
Mix ground beef with salt, pepper, coriander, garlic, and vinegar.
Soak casings in warm water for 10 minutes.
Stuff casings loosely with beef mixture and tie into 3-inch links.
Prick casings with a fork.
Hang in a warm, dry place (65-70°F) with good air circulation for 4-6 days until completely dry.
Store in an airtight container in a cool place.
cheapTips: Buy ground beef in bulk and portion before making
Order casings online for better prices

recipes.name: Milk Tart
recipes.description: South African snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F and place pie crust in a 9-inch pie dish.
Heat milk in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling.
Mix sugar, cornstarch, and salt in a bowl, then whisk in eggs.
Slowly pour hot milk into egg mixture while whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened (about 3 minutes).
Remove from heat and stir in butter and vanilla.
Pour filling into pie crust and sprinkle cinnamon on top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden and set but slightly jiggly in the center.
cheapTips: Use store-bought pie crust to save time and money
Buy eggs and milk on sale and freeze when possible

recipes.name: Vetkoek
recipes.description: South African breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Add milk and water to form a soft, sticky dough.
Let dough rest for 10 minutes.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pan.
Divide dough into 8 balls and carefully place into hot oil.
Fry for 2-3 minutes per side until puffed and golden brown.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve warm with honey or jam drizzled on top and a pat of butter.
cheapTips: Use generic all-purpose flour
Reuse frying oil and strain between uses

recipes.name: Pap
recipes.description: South African breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring 4 cups of water to a boil in a large pot with salt.
Slowly pour cornmeal into boiling water while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat to low and continue stirring frequently for 15-20 minutes until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Stir in butter and milk until smooth and creamy.
Serve hot in bowls while still warm.
cheapTips: Buy cornmeal in bulk from ethnic markets for lower cost
Use water instead of milk for a cheaper version

recipes.name: Umngqusho
recipes.description: Xhosa lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak corn and beans in separate bowls of water overnight, then drain.
Boil corn and beans together in 6 cups of fresh water for 60 minutes until very tender.
Dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat butter in a large pan and sauté onion and garlic until golden.
Add the cooked corn and beans to the pan with their cooking liquid.
Mash some of the mixture with a wooden spoon to create a thick consistency while keeping some kernels whole.
Season with salt and pepper and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve hot as a side dish or main course.
cheapTips: Buy dried corn and beans in bulk from wholesale stores
Omit butter and use oil to reduce cost

recipes.name: Chakalaka
recipes.description: South African lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and julienne the carrots into thin sticks.
Chop the cabbage, green beans, onion, and mince the garlic.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add onion and garlic, sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add carrots, cabbage, and green beans, stirring well for 5 minutes.
Stir in canned tomatoes with their juice, chili powder, cumin, and salt.
Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes until vegetables are tender but slightly crisp.
Taste and adjust seasoning, then serve hot.
cheapTips: Use frozen vegetables instead of fresh to save money
Buy carrots and cabbage from discount grocery bins

recipes.name: Sorghum Porridge
recipes.description: South African breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse sorghum grain thoroughly under cold water to remove debris.
Bring 4 cups of water to a boil in a pot with salt.
Add sorghum grain slowly to boiling water, stirring constantly.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 35-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until grains are very soft and porridge thickens.
Stir in butter, honey, and cinnamon until well combined.
Slice banana and add to the porridge just before serving.
Serve hot in bowls.
cheapTips: Buy sorghum grain from African or health food stores in bulk
Use millet as a cheaper substitute if sorghum is unavailable

recipes.name: Braai
recipes.description: South African dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Prepare charcoal or firewood in a braai grill or barbecue, allowing coals to become hot and glowing.
Pat meat dry and season steaks, chops, and chicken with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Drizzle meat with olive oil and lemon juice.
Place sausages on the grill first as they take longer, cooking for 8-10 minutes with frequent turning.
Add chicken breasts to the grill and cook for 6-7 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Add steaks and chops to the grill in the final 5-8 minutes, cooking to desired doneness.
Toast bread rolls lightly on the grill.
Arrange all meats and bread on a platter and serve hot with traditional sides.
cheapTips: Use cheaper cuts of beef like chuck steak instead of premium cuts
Buy meat on sale and freeze until braai day

recipes.name: Potjiekos
recipes.description: South African dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut beef into 1½-inch cubes and cut potatoes, carrots, and onions into large chunks.
Heat a large iron pot or heavy Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef pieces in batches, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onions and garlic for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot and add beef broth, salt, pepper, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 45 minutes until beef is tender.
Add potatoes and carrots, simmer for 20 minutes, then add cabbage and cook another 10 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Serve hot directly from the pot or in bowls.
cheapTips: Use chuck roast instead of stewing meat and cut into pieces yourself
Make a larger batch and freeze portions for later

recipes.name: Durban Curry
recipes.description: Durban Indian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut chicken breasts into bite-sized pieces and set aside.
Finely mince garlic and ginger, then dice onions.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add onions and cook for 4 minutes until softened, then add garlic and ginger, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add curry powder and turmeric, stirring constantly for 1 minute to bloom the spices.
Add chicken pieces and stir well to coat with spice mixture, cooking for 5 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and salt, stir well and bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 30-40 minutes until chicken is cooked through and sauce thickens slightly.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot over rice.
cheapTips: Buy chicken on sale and freeze for later use
Use standard curry powder instead of premium brands

recipes.name: Sosaties skewers
recipes.description: Cape Malay dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes before grilling.
Cut meat into 1½-inch cubes and dice onions into chunks.
Make marinade by mincing garlic and ginger, then mixing with curry powder, turmeric, coconut milk, oil, and salt.
Toss meat with marinade and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes.
Thread marinated meat and onion pieces alternately onto skewers.
Heat grill or barbecue to medium-high heat with coals or burner ready.
Grill skewers for 12-15 minutes, turning occasionally, until meat is cooked through and browned.
Serve hot with rice and chutney.
cheapTips: Use beef instead of lamb for significant savings
Make marinade from scratch rather than buying expensive spice blends

recipes.name: Koesisters
recipes.description: South African snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Whisk together egg and milk in another bowl.
Combine wet and dry ingredients until a thick dough forms.
Heat oil to 350°F (175°C) in a deep pot, using a thermometer to monitor temperature.
Pipe dough into oil using a pastry bag with a small round tip, creating 2-3 inch long pieces, frying 3-4 at a time.
Fry each koesister for 1-2 minutes per side until golden brown.
Remove with a slotted spoon and immediately dip into warm honey syrup or roll in cinnamon-sugar mixture.
Place on a wire rack to cool slightly before serving.
cheapTips: Buy honey or corn syrup in large bottles and store for multiple batches
Use oil multiple times by filtering and reusing until it darkens

recipes.name: Gatsby
recipes.description: South African lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Grill or fry sausages and cook eggs (fried or scrambled) until done.
Slice the long loaf of bread lengthwise and butter the inside of both halves.
Slice tomatoes and onions into thin pieces.
Spread mayonnaise on the bottom half of the bread.
Layer lettuce, tomato slices, and onion on the mayonnaise.
Add the cooked sausages and eggs on top of the vegetables.
Drain and add the canned fish on top.
Drizzle with chili sauce and top with the other bread half.
Cut into 4 portions and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use budget hot dogs instead of sausages to reduce cost
Buy bread day-old from the bakery section for 50% off

recipes.name: Baghrire
recipes.description: Algerian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and egg until combined.
Stir in yogurt and water gradually to form a smooth, thin batter that drips slowly from a spoon.
Heat a non-stick skillet or crepe pan over medium heat and lightly oil it.
Using a ladle, pour batter in a circular motion to create a honeycomb-textured pancake, cooking until the bottom sets and top is full of holes.
Flip carefully and cook the other side for 30 seconds until light golden.
Transfer to a plate and repeat with remaining batter.
Warm honey and butter together, then drizzle over warm baghrire before serving.
cheapTips: Use plain yogurt from bulk sections instead of premium brands
Make honey drizzle optional and serve with jam instead

recipes.name: Kefta Mechoui
recipes.description: Algerian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix ground meat, parsley, minced onion, garlic, egg, breadcrumbs, cumin, salt, and pepper in a bowl until just combined.
Shape mixture into oval or sausage-shaped patties about 3 inches long.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Place kefta patties in the skillet and sear for 3-4 minutes per side until browned.
Pour tomato sauce over kefta, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer for 8-10 minutes.
Serve hot with bread for dipping or over couscous.
cheapTips: Buy ground beef on sale and freeze until ready to use
Skip fresh parsley and use 1 tsp dried parsley as substitute

recipes.name: Matlouh
recipes.description: Algerian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt in a bowl, add water gradually while kneading to form a soft dough, let rest 20 minutes covered.
Brown ground meat with diced onion, cilantro, caraway seeds, and salt in a skillet, then set filling aside to cool.
Divide dough into 6 balls and roll each very thin on a floured surface.
Brush rolled dough with oil, spread a thin layer of meat filling, then roll tightly into a cylinder.
Coil the cylinder into a spiral shape on a parchment or oiled surface.
Heat oil in a large skillet to medium temperature and fry coiled matlouh 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot, optionally drizzled with honey or harissa sauce.
cheapTips: Make dough from basic pantry staples to cut costs
Stretch dough by hand instead of using a rolling pin

recipes.name: Kaab El Ghzal
recipes.description: Algerian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a bowl, mix almond paste, powdered sugar, egg white, orange blossom water, and salt until a pliable filling forms.
Lay out one phyllo sheet and brush lightly with melted butter.
Spoon 2 tablespoons of filling along one long edge of the phyllo, leaving 1 inch margins.
Roll phyllo tightly around filling, then curve it into a crescent shape (gazelle horn).
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350°F and carefully place kaab el ghzal in oil.
Fry 2-3 minutes until golden brown, turning once, then drain on paper towels.
While still warm, dust generously with powdered sugar, then drizzle with honey if desired.
cheapTips: Use regular sugar mixed with water instead of orange blossom water
Buy phyllo dough on sale and freeze for later use

recipes.name: Rejjala
recipes.description: Algerian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown beef cubes on all sides in batches, about 10 minutes total.
Add sliced onions and minced garlic, sauté until onions are soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and paprika, cooking for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in beef broth and bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Add sliced carrots and cubed potatoes, season with salt and pepper, and simmer covered for 15-20 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning, then stir in fresh cilantro before serving.
Serve hot in bowls, optionally with bread for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy beef chuck on sale and freeze until cooking day
Use carrots and potatoes from bulk bins for better prices

recipes.name: Ugali
recipes.description: Kenyan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring water or broth to a boil in a large pot and add salt.
Slowly pour cornmeal into boiling liquid while stirring constantly with a wooden spoon to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat to medium-low and continue stirring constantly for 10-15 minutes until the mixture becomes thick and pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Stir in butter until fully incorporated.
Transfer ugali to a serving plate or mold it into a dome shape.
Serve hot alongside cooked vegetables, beans, or a stew for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy cornmeal in bulk from international or wholesale stores
Skip butter and use oil to reduce costs further

recipes.name: Nyama Choma
recipes.description: Kenyan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat beef cubes dry with paper towels and season generously with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Heat oil in a large skillet or grill pan over high heat until very hot and just smoking.
Working in batches to avoid overcrowding, sear beef cubes for 2-3 minutes per side until deeply browned and cooked to your preference.
Transfer cooked meat to a serving plate and squeeze fresh lemon or lime juice over the top.
Serve immediately while still hot, optionally with grilled onions and tomatoes on the side.
Accompany with ugali, rice, or fresh salad.
cheapTips: Buy less expensive cuts like chuck steak and marinate for tenderness
Grill outdoors to save on electricity or gas costs

recipes.name: Chapati
recipes.description: Kenyan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt in a large bowl, then add water gradually while kneading until a soft, elastic dough forms.
Knead dough for 5-8 minutes until smooth, then cover and let rest for 20 minutes.
Divide dough into 6 equal portions and roll each into a thin circle about 8 inches in diameter.
Brush each circle lightly with oil, then fold it in half and roll again into a thin quarter-circle or thin square.
Heat a cast iron skillet or griddle over medium-high heat until very hot.
Place one chapati on the hot surface and cook for about 1-2 minutes until bubbles form, then flip.
Press the chapati gently with a cloth to help it puff, cook another 1-2 minutes until light golden with brown spots.
Brush with a little butter and place on a plate covered with a cloth to keep warm.
Repeat with remaining dough and serve immediately with eggs, beans, or avocado.
cheapTips: Make large batches and refrigerate extras for quick reheating
Use vegetable oil throughout instead of adding separate butter

recipes.name: Githeri
recipes.description: Kenyan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion and garlic until soft and fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes and turmeric, cooking for 2 minutes to release flavors.
Stir in corn kernels and cooked beans, then add water or broth.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until flavors meld and mixture thickens slightly.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot as a main dish or side, optionally with chapati or ugali on the side.
cheapTips: Use canned beans and frozen corn for convenience and cost savings
Buy dried beans and cook in bulk, then freeze portions

recipes.name: Irio
recipes.description: Kenyan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring salted water to a boil in a large pot and add cubed potatoes.
Cook potatoes for 8 minutes, then add corn and peas, cooking for another 5-7 minutes until potatoes are very tender.
Drain well, reserving 1/4 cup of cooking liquid.
Return vegetables to the pot and add butter and sautéed diced onion (cooked separately if preferred).
Mash together roughly until creamy but still with some texture, adding reserved cooking liquid as needed.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve warm as a side dish or main course, optionally with grilled meat or beans.
cheapTips: Buy frozen peas and corn instead of fresh for lower prices
Use oil instead of butter to significantly reduce costs

recipes.name: Pap en Vleis
recipes.description: South African dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the ground beef, breaking it apart as it cooks.
Add diced onion and minced garlic, cooking for 3 minutes until softened.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in beef broth and bring to a simmer, cooking for 15 minutes.
In a separate pot, bring 4 cups of water to a boil with salt.
Slowly pour cornmeal into boiling water while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat to low and stir continuously for 10-15 minutes until the pap thickens and pulls away from the pot sides.
Serve the meat stew over a mound of pap on each plate.
cheapTips: Buy ground beef on sale and freeze it
Use store-brand tomato paste and beef broth

recipes.name: Melktert
recipes.description: South African snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and place the pre-made pie crust in a 9-inch pie pan.
Heat milk in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming but not boiling.
In a bowl, whisk together cornstarch, sugar, and salt.
Add 3 tbsp of hot milk to the cornstarch mixture and whisk until smooth, then return this mixture to the pot.
Whisk in butter and vanilla extract, cooking for 2 minutes while stirring constantly until thickened.
Remove from heat and let cool for 5 minutes, then whisk in the eggs.
Pour the custard into the pie crust and sprinkle cinnamon on top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the custard is set but slightly jiggly in the center.
Cool completely before slicing.
cheapTips: Use store-brand pie crust to save money
Buy eggs and milk in bulk

recipes.name: Samoosa
recipes.description: Durban Indian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt in a bowl, then add water gradually while mixing to form a stiff dough; rest for 20 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan and fry onions until golden, then add ginger-garlic paste and green chili.
Add ground beef and curry powder, cooking until beef is done; stir in cilantro and lemon juice, then cool completely.
Divide dough into 12 balls and flatten each into a thin square with your hands or a rolling pin.
Cut each square diagonally to form two triangles.
Place 1 tbsp filling on each triangle, fold into a smaller triangle, and seal edges by pressing firmly.
Heat 3 cups oil in a deep pan to 350°F and fry samosas in batches until golden brown on both sides, about 2-3 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with chutney.
cheapTips: Make filling in advance and refrigerate
Reuse frying oil multiple times for cost savings

recipes.name: Kenkey
recipes.description: Ghanaian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak corn husks or banana leaves in warm water for 10 minutes to soften.
Bring 3 cups water to a boil with salt and slowly pour in cornmeal while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat and stir for 15 minutes until the mixture thickens and becomes difficult to stir.
Divide the cornmeal mixture into 4 portions and wrap each firmly in a soaked corn husk or banana leaf, creating a rectangular parcel.
Place wrapped kenkey in a pot with about 2 inches of water and steam for 30 minutes.
While steaming, heat oil in a pan and sauté onion, tomato, ginger, and chili to make a simple sauce.
Remove kenkey from leaves and serve hot with the tomato sauce on the side or spooned over the top.
cheapTips: Buy cornmeal in bulk from African or international markets
Use homemade tomato sauce instead of canned

recipes.name: Ampesi
recipes.description: Ghanaian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel green plantains, yams, and cocoyam by cutting off the skin with a knife and rinsing thoroughly.
Cut all vegetables into 2-3 inch chunks and place in a large pot with water, onion, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 25-30 minutes until all vegetables are tender when pierced with a fork.
In a separate pan, heat palm oil and sauté tomato and garlic for 3-4 minutes.
Drain the cooked vegetables and arrange on a serving platter.
Pour the tomato and palm oil sauce over the vegetables and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy plantains and yams when they're on sale and store in a cool place
Purchase palm oil from African markets for better prices

recipes.name: Palm Soup
recipes.description: Ghanaian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat palm oil in a large pot over medium heat and fry onion, garlic, and ginger for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add meat and brown on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add stock cubes, water, and whole Scotch bonnet pepper and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 30-35 minutes until meat is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot in bowls with a spoon and fufu or rice on the side.
cheapTips: Buy beef cuts on sale and freeze until ready to use
Use chicken instead of beef for a more budget-friendly option

recipes.name: Light Soup
recipes.description: Ghanaian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and brown the meat over medium-high heat, about 4 minutes.
Add onion and garlic, cooking for 2 minutes until softened.
Add diced tomato and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in vegetable broth and bring to a boil.
Add carrots and green beans, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot as a light and nutritious meal.
cheapTips: Use seasonal vegetables for lower costs
Buy chicken pieces on sale and freeze

recipes.name: Gari Foto
recipes.description: Ghanaian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion, garlic, and green chili for 2 minutes.
Add diced tomato and cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Gradually add gari to the pot, stirring continuously to break up any lumps.
Add water slowly while stirring to achieve a porridge-like consistency.
Reduce heat to low and stir frequently for 10-15 minutes, allowing the gari to cook through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot in bowls as a breakfast porridge.
cheapTips: Buy gari from African grocery stores in bulk
Use dried chili powder if fresh chili is unavailable

recipes.name: Tuo Zaafi
recipes.description: Ghanaian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and brown the meat over medium-high heat for 5 minutes.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger, cooking for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add 6 cups of water and bring to a boil, then simmer meat for 30 minutes until tender.
In a separate bowl, mix cornmeal and millet flour with 2 cups water to form a smooth paste without lumps.
Slowly pour the grain mixture into the simmering broth while stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Add salt and continue stirring for 15-20 minutes until the mixture thickens to a smooth, pourable consistency.
Serve hot, poured into bowls.
cheapTips: Buy millet flour from African or health food stores
Use beef chuck or stewing meat for better value

recipes.name: Fried Plantain
recipes.description: Ghanaian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel the ripe plantains by slicing off the skin with a knife and removing it completely.
Slice plantains diagonally into 0.5-inch thick pieces.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F.
Carefully add plantain slices to hot oil in batches without overcrowding the pan.
Fry for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and slightly crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Sprinkle with salt and chili powder while still hot and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy plantains in bunches when on sale and ripen at home
Reuse frying oil multiple times by straining it

recipes.name: Shakla Mhancha
recipes.description: Algerian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix ground almonds, powdered sugar, 2 tablespoons melted butter, cinnamon, orange blossom water, salt, and 1 beaten egg in a bowl until paste forms.
Melt remaining butter in a shallow pan and brush one phyllo sheet lightly with butter.
Spread 2 tablespoons almond mixture along the long edge of the phyllo sheet and roll tightly into a cylinder.
Coil the filled phyllo roll into a spiral shape and place on a buttered baking sheet; repeat with remaining sheets.
Beat remaining 2 eggs and brush over the spiral pastry.
Bake at 350°F for 35-40 minutes until golden brown.
Combine honey and water in a saucepan, heat until warm, and pour over the hot pastry immediately after removing from oven.
Cool for 15 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Buy phyllo dough on sale and freeze for later use
Use regular sugar instead of powdered sugar and blend with almonds

recipes.name: Couscous Royale
recipes.description: Algerian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and brown chicken and lamb pieces on all sides for 5 minutes.
Add chopped onions and cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste, turmeric, salt, and pepper, cooking for 1 minute.
