Cover with foil and bake at 350°F for 40-45 minutes until masa is set.
Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Buy masa harina in bulk from Hispanic markets for better prices.
Make sofrito in batches and freeze.

recipes.name: Arroz Blanco
recipes.description: Cuban lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse rice under cold water in a fine-mesh strainer until water runs clear.
Heat olive oil in a medium pot over medium heat.
Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add rinsed rice and stir constantly for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in water and salt, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and simmer for 15-18 minutes.
Remove from heat and let stand covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy rice in bulk for significant savings.
Use vegetable broth instead of water for added flavor at no extra cost.

recipes.name: Flan Cubano
recipes.description: Cuban snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
In a saucepan, combine 3/4 cup sugar and water over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves and turns golden amber, about 5-7 minutes.
Quickly pour caramel into a round baking dish, tilting to coat the bottom evenly.
Blend condensed milk, evaporated milk, eggs, and vanilla in a blender until smooth.
Pour custard mixture into the caramel-coated baking dish.
Place the baking dish in a larger roasting pan and fill the roasting pan with hot water to halfway up the sides of the baking dish.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until the custard is set but slightly jiggly in the center.
Cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving.
Run a knife around edges and invert onto a serving plate so caramel runs over custard.
cheapTips: Buy evaporated and condensed milk on sale and stock up.
Use regular sugar instead of trying specialty caramel products.

recipes.name: Ropa Vieja Tacos
recipes.description: Cuban lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook beef in a pot of simmering salted water for 40 minutes until very tender.
Remove beef, let cool slightly, then shred using two forks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté onion and garlic for 3 minutes until softened.
Add shredded beef, red and yellow peppers, cumin, and salt.
Cook for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add tomato sauce and beef broth, then simmer for 10 minutes until peppers are tender and flavors meld.
Warm tortillas in a skillet for 30 seconds per side.
Fill tortillas with ropa vieja mixture and serve with lime wedges.
cheapTips: Buy flank steak on sale and freeze for future use.
Use store-brand tomato sauce to reduce costs.

recipes.name: Vaca Vieja
recipes.description: Cuban dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown beef cubes in batches on all sides, about 3 minutes per batch, then set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onion and garlic for 4 minutes until softened.
Add diced red pepper and cook for 2 minutes.
Return beef to the pot and add tomato sauce, beef broth, cumin, bay leaves, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 50-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until beef is very tender.
Taste and adjust seasonings before serving over rice.
cheapTips: Use chuck roast on sale; it becomes tender from long cooking.
Make a double batch and freeze half for easy future meals.

recipes.name: Malanga Frita
recipes.description: Cuban snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel malanga roots under running water and slice into 1/4-inch thick rounds or sticks.
Pat slices dry with paper towels to remove excess moisture.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or fryer to 350°F.
Carefully add malanga slices in batches, frying for 4-5 minutes until golden and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
While still warm, toss fried malanga with salt and minced garlic.
Drizzle with lime juice and serve immediately as a snack or side dish.
cheapTips: Buy malanga at Hispanic or international markets where it's cheaper.
Reuse frying oil for multiple batches to reduce waste.

recipes.name: Quesitos
recipes.description: Puerto Rican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Thaw puff pastry sheets at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Cut each sheet into 2x3 inch rectangles.
Place a small piece of cheese and guava paste in the center of each rectangle.
Fold pastry in half and seal edges with a fork, then brush with beaten egg.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F and fry quesitos 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
cheapTips: Use store-brand puff pastry to save 30%
Buy cheese on sale and freeze for later use

recipes.name: Buñuelos de Viento
recipes.description: Puerto Rican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring water and salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Remove from heat and stir in flour until a smooth paste forms.
Heat oil to 375°F in a deep pan.
Using two spoons, carefully drop spoonfuls of dough into hot oil.
Fry buñuelos 3-4 minutes per side until golden and puffed.
Drain on paper towels.
Mix powdered sugar and cinnamon together.
Dust warm buñuelos with cinnamon-sugar mixture and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Make your own powdered sugar by blending regular sugar with cornstarch
Buy oil in bulk to reduce per-serving cost

recipes.name: Cabezada
recipes.description: Puerto Rican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean and cut pork into chunks, season with adobo and let sit 15 minutes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and brown meat on all sides.
Add sofrito and minced garlic, cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in tomato sauce and broth, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer 60 minutes until meat is tender.
Add olives and raisins, simmer uncovered 10 more minutes.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with rice and beans.
cheapTips: Use pork shoulder instead of head to save money and reduce prep difficulty
Buy olives in bulk from the deli section

recipes.name: Gandinga
recipes.description: Puerto Rican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Wash liver thoroughly and cut into 1-inch chunks.
Boil liver in salted water for 15 minutes, drain and set aside.
Heat olive oil and sauté diced onion until soft.
Add sofrito and cook 1 minute, then add tomato sauce.
Add cooked liver, adobo, bay leaves, olives, and capers.
Simmer uncovered 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove bay leaves and adjust seasoning.
Serve hot with white rice or on a Puerto Rican bread roll.
cheapTips: Buy liver when it goes on sale and freeze
Make sofrito at home with cilantro, peppers, and onions

recipes.name: Arroz con Maíz
recipes.description: Puerto Rican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté minced garlic for 1 minute.
Add sofrito and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Add corn, adobo, and pimientos, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer 18-20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use frozen corn year-round to save money
Buy rice in bulk from wholesale stores

recipes.name: Pupusas
recipes.description: Salvadoran snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix masa harina, warm water, and salt until dough forms.
Let dough rest 5 minutes, then knead until smooth.
Flatten a handful of dough in your palm into a thin disc.
Add a spoonful of filling (cheese, beans, or chicharrón) to the center.
Fold edges over filling and gently flatten again into a thick disc.
Heat oil on a griddle or large skillet to medium-high heat.
Cook pupusas 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot with curtido (pickled cabbage slaw) and tomato sauce.
cheapTips: Buy masa harina in bulk from Hispanic markets for 40% savings
Use store-brand refried beans instead of homemade

recipes.name: Curtido
recipes.description: Salvadoran snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice cabbage thinly and place in a large bowl.
Julienne carrots and slice jalapeños and onion.
Add carrots, jalapeños, and onion to cabbage.
Whisk together vinegar, water, salt, and oregano.
Pour vinegar mixture over vegetables and toss well.
Let sit at room temperature for 1 hour before serving.
Serve as a side with pupusas or other dishes.
cheapTips: Buy cabbage and carrots from the discount bin
Make large batches and store in the fridge for 2 weeks

recipes.name: Tamales Salvadoreños
recipes.description: Salvadoran breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak corn husks in warm water for 20 minutes until pliable.
Boil chicken with salt until cooked through, shred and set aside.
Beat together masa harina, chicken fat, and 1 cup chicken broth until light and fluffy.
Spread 2 tablespoons masa on each corn husk.
Add a spoonful of chicken, jalapeño slice, olive, and raisin to center.
Fold sides of husk over filling and fold bottom up.
Stand tamales upright in a steamer pot with water below a steamer basket.
Steam for 45 minutes, then rest 5 minutes before serving.
Serve warm with hot chocolate or coffee.
cheapTips: Prepare filling the day before to save time
Buy chicken when on sale and freeze

recipes.name: Yuca con Chicharrón
recipes.description: Salvadoran lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork shoulder into 2-inch cubes and season with adobo.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and brown pork on all sides.
Add chopped onion and garlic, cook 2 minutes.
Peel and cut yuca into 2-inch pieces.
Add yuca and water to pot, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer 35 minutes until yuca is tender.
Add salt and lime juice, adjust seasoning.
Serve hot, often with curtido and tortillas on the side.
cheapTips: Buy yuca from Hispanic markets where it's cheaper than supermarkets
Use pork on sale and store in the freezer

recipes.name: Enchiladas Salvadoreñas
recipes.description: Salvadoran lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice and boil potatoes until tender, then mash lightly.
Peel and dice green plantain, boil until tender, then mash.
Mix mashed potato and plantain with salt.
Heat oil and sauté diced onion and garlic, add tomato sauce and simmer 5 minutes.
Warm tortillas on a comal or skillet.
Spread potato-plantain mixture on each tortilla, top with cheese, and roll.
Arrange enchiladas seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour tomato sauce over enchiladas and bake at 350°F for 20 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with additional cheese if desired.
cheapTips: Buy plantains when on sale and freeze in portions
Make your own tomato sauce from canned tomatoes to save 50%

recipes.name: Patacón
recipes.description: Venezuelan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and cut plantains into 1-inch thick rounds.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pan or skillet.
Fry plantain rounds for 3-4 minutes per side until golden.
Remove and flatten each round to ¼-inch thickness using a tostonera or glass.
Fry again for 1-2 minutes per side until crispy.
Drain on paper towels and season with salt.
Prepare garlic sauce by mincing garlic and mixing with water and salt.
Serve hot patacones with garlic sauce for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy plantains in bulk when on sale and freeze for later use
Reuse frying oil for 3-4 batches before discarding

recipes.name: Bollo Pelón
recipes.description: Venezuelan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine milk and water in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Slowly whisk in cornmeal while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Add butter, salt, and sugar to the mixture.
Reduce heat to medium-low and stir constantly for 20-25 minutes until very thick and creamy.
Add vanilla extract and stir well.
Pour into a buttered bowl or mold and let cool slightly.
Turn out onto a plate and serve warm with additional butter or cheese on top.
cheapTips: Use store-brand cornmeal and milk to reduce costs
Make in large batches and refrigerate; reheat portions as needed

recipes.name: Ajiaco
recipes.description: Venezuelan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until fragrant.
Add chicken breast and brown on both sides.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Peel and cut potatoes and cassava into chunks; add to pot.
Cut corn into 2-inch pieces and add to the pot.
Reduce heat and simmer for 35-40 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in fresh cilantro and serve hot in bowls.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs instead of breast for more flavor and lower cost
Buy frozen corn if fresh is unavailable or expensive

recipes.name: Arepa de Huevo
recipes.description: Venezuelan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix arepa flour, warm water, and salt in a bowl until smooth dough forms.
Let dough rest for 5 minutes.
Shape dough into 3 thick oval patties about 1/2-inch thick.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep skillet.
Carefully fry arepas for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Drain briefly on paper towels.
Make a pocket in each arepa and slide in one raw egg and cheese if desired.
Serve immediately while still warm.
cheapTips: Use bulk arepa flour purchased at Latin grocery stores for better pricing
Skip the cheese to reduce costs

recipes.name: Relleno de Papas
recipes.description: Venezuelan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil potatoes until tender, peel, and mash with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a skillet and sauté diced onion and garlic.
Add ground beef and cook until browned, breaking it apart as it cooks.
Stir in cumin, olives, and raisins; cook for 2 minutes.
Form potato mixture into patties and make an indentation in the center.
Fill each patty with meat mixture and seal edges with more potato.
Beat eggs in a bowl and dip patties to coat.
Fry in 350°F oil for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use ground turkey instead of beef for savings
Make filling in large batch and freeze for quick future meals

recipes.name: Tamale Loco
recipes.description: Venezuelan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak corn husks in warm water for 30 minutes until pliable.
Beat butter with masa harina and chicken broth until light and fluffy.
Sauté diced onion and garlic, then add chicken, olives, and raisins.
Spread 2 tablespoons masa on center of each corn husk.
Add 2 tablespoons filling to center and fold husk edges over filling.
Fold bottom and top of husk to seal completely.
Place tamales in steamer pot with water below and steam for 45 minutes.
Carefully unwrap and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy masa harina in bulk at Latin markets for significant savings
Use leftover rotisserie chicken to save money and prep time

recipes.name: Dulce de Lechoza
recipes.description: Venezuelan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel papaya, remove seeds, and cut into 1-inch cubes.
Combine sugar and water in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Add cinnamon stick and cloves to the syrup.
Add papaya cubes and stir gently.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
The papaya should become translucent and the syrup thick.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla extract.
Serve warm or chilled as a dessert or sweet snack.
cheapTips: Buy papaya in season when prices are lowest
Store finished dulce in jars; keeps for 2 weeks in refrigerator

recipes.name: Buñuelos de Queso
recipes.description: Venezuelan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk eggs with milk in another bowl.
Combine wet and dry ingredients until just mixed.
Fold in shredded cheese gently.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep skillet.
Drop rounded tablespoons of batter into hot oil carefully.
Fry for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and puffed.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot, optionally with powdered sugar.
cheapTips: Use block white cheddar and grate at home instead of pre-shredded
Reuse frying oil for one additional batch of buñuelos

recipes.name: Asado Negro
recipes.description: Venezuelan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Season beef brisket generously with salt, pepper, and cumin on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear brisket on all sides until dark brown caramelization forms.
Remove meat and set aside; sauté diced onions and minced garlic until golden.
Return meat to pot and pour soy sauce and Worcestershire sauce over it.
Scrape up browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Add beef broth and tomato paste; bring to a simmer.
Cover tightly and braise in a 325°F oven for 1.5-2 hours until very tender, turning halfway.
Remove from oven, shred or slice meat, and serve with pan sauce spooned over top.
cheapTips: Ask butcher for brisket trimmings or less-ideal cuts that are cheaper
Make extra sauce to serve with rice or potatoes for extended meals

recipes.name: Pernil
recipes.description: Puerto Rican dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Score pork skin in a crosshatch pattern, cutting only through skin and fat.
Mince garlic and combine with sofrito, adobo, oregano, salt, pepper, and olive oil to form a paste.
Rub paste generously all over pork, especially into scores and under skin.
Let marinate for at least 4 hours or overnight in the refrigerator.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Place pork skin-side up in a large roasting pan and add chicken broth to bottom.
Roast for 4-5 hours, basting every 30-45 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 180°F and skin is crackling.
Rest for 20 minutes before carving and serving with pan drippings.
cheapTips: Buy pork leg when on sale during holidays and freeze until ready to use
Use leftover pulled pork for carnitas, sandwiches, or rice dishes throughout the week

recipes.name: Pollo Guisado
recipes.description: Salvadoran lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and season chicken with salt and pepper.
Brown the chicken on both sides for 5 minutes, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté minced garlic, diced onion, and bell pepper for 3 minutes until softened.
Add tomato sauce and cumin, stirring well to combine.
Return the chicken to the pot and add broth and diced potatoes.
Cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes until chicken is cooked through and potatoes are tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed before serving.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs on sale and freeze for later use
Use canned tomato sauce instead of fresh tomatoes

recipes.name: Ropa Vieja Salvadoreña
recipes.description: Salvadoran lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Place beef brisket in a large pot, cover with water, add salt and bay leaves, and boil for 45 minutes until very tender.
Remove beef and let cool slightly, then shred with two forks into thin strands.
Heat olive oil in another pot and sauté minced garlic, diced onion, and peppers for 4 minutes.
Add tomato sauce, cumin, and pepper, stirring well.
Add shredded beef and 1 cup of the beef broth to the sauce.
Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until flavors meld and sauce thickens.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with rice or pupusas.
cheapTips: Buy beef brisket when on sale and freeze for weeks
Use generic tomato sauce brands to save 30%

recipes.name: Cazuela de Mariscos
recipes.description: Salvadoran lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large clay pot or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Sauté minced garlic and diced onion for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add tomato sauce and white wine, simmering for 2 minutes.
Pour in seafood broth and bring to a gentle boil.
Add clams and mussels first, cooking for 3 minutes until they begin to open.
Add shrimp and fish pieces, cooking for 5-7 minutes more until shrimp is pink and fish is opaque.
Remove any unopened clams or mussels, season with salt and pepper, and serve in the same pot.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp and thaw beforehand to save 40%
Check seafood counters for deals on imperfect mussels

recipes.name: Ceviche Salvadoreño
recipes.description: Salvadoran lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut fish into small 1-inch cubes and place in a glass bowl.
Pour lime juice over fish completely, ensuring all pieces are submerged.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes to cure the fish.
While fish cures, dice onion, tomato, bell pepper, and jalapeño finely.
After curing, drain excess lime juice from fish.
Mix cured fish with diced vegetables, cilantro, salt, and black pepper.
Fold in sliced avocado gently just before serving to prevent browning.
cheapTips: Use tilapia or mahi-mahi instead of expensive sea bass
Buy limes when in season and squeeze juice ahead of time

recipes.name: Sopa de Pata
recipes.description: Salvadoran lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean beef feet thoroughly under running water and cut into sections.
In a large pot, boil beef feet with salt for 2 hours until very tender.
Heat olive oil in another pan and sauté minced garlic, diced onion, and bell pepper for 4 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes and cook for 2 more minutes until slightly soft.
Add the sautéed vegetables to the broth with the beef feet.
Add diced potatoes, carrots, and plantain; simmer for 20-25 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Season with black pepper and cilantro, simmer 5 more minutes, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy beef feet from ethnic markets at 50% less than regular butchers
Make a double batch and freeze for quick future meals

recipes.name: Atol de Elote
recipes.description: Salvadoran breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blend frozen corn kernels with 1 cup of milk until completely smooth.
Strain the blended corn mixture through a fine sieve to remove large pieces, pressing to extract all liquid.
In a large pot, heat remaining 3 cups of milk over medium heat.
Dissolve cornstarch in 3 tablespoons of water and add to the heating milk, stirring constantly.
Add the strained corn liquid, sugar, salt, and butter to the pot.
Simmer for 10-12 minutes, stirring frequently, until thickened and corn flavor develops.
Stir in vanilla and cinnamon, then serve hot in bowls as a thick, warm drink.
cheapTips: Buy frozen corn in bulk during off-season sales
Use evaporated milk instead of whole milk to save 25%

recipes.name: Atol Shuco
recipes.description: Salvadoran breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat water in a large pot over medium-high heat.
In a bowl, mix corn flour with 1 cup of cold water to create a smooth slurry without lumps.
Slowly pour the corn flour mixture into boiling water while stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Sauté minced garlic and diced onion in butter until softened, then add to the pot.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Season with salt and black pepper, stirring well.
Serve hot and top each bowl with shredded cheese for a savory, hearty drink.
cheapTips: Buy corn flour in bulk from Latin markets for 40% savings
Use store-brand shredded cheese to reduce costs

recipes.name: Ayote en Dulce
recipes.description: Salvadoran dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel butternut squash, remove seeds, and cut into 2-inch chunks.
In a large pot, combine water, brown sugar, cinnamon sticks, and cloves; bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium and add squash pieces, stirring gently.
Simmer uncovered for 20-25 minutes until squash is very tender but still holds its shape.
Add butter, vanilla extract, and salt, stirring gently to combine.
Continue simmering for 3-5 minutes to infuse flavors.
Transfer to a serving bowl and cool slightly; serve warm or at room temperature with the sweet sauce.
cheapTips: Buy whole butternut squash on sale and store in cool pantry for months
Use regular sugar instead of brown sugar if needed

recipes.name: Arroz con Leche
recipes.description: Salvadoran dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear, then drain well.
In a large pot, heat milk over medium heat with cinnamon stick.
Once milk is hot (not boiling), add rice, sugar, and salt, stirring well.
Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice is tender and creamy.
Stir in butter and raisins, cooking for 2 more minutes.
Remove from heat and add vanilla extract, stirring gently.
Transfer to serving bowl and sprinkle with additional cinnamon on top if desired.
cheapTips: Use evaporated milk instead of regular milk to save money
Skip raisins or use dried cranberries if on sale

recipes.name: Torrejas
recipes.description: Salvadoran dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut bread into 0.5-inch-thick diagonal slices.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla, and cinnamon until well combined.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Dip each bread slice into the egg mixture, coating both sides, and carefully place in hot oil.
Fry for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Transfer fried torrejas to a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Serve warm, drizzled generously with honey syrup or warm piloncillo sauce.
cheapTips: Use day-old bread from bakery discount bins or bread stores
Make honey syrup at home by heating honey instead of buying prepared sauce

recipes.name: Yuca Frita
recipes.description: Dominican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel the yuca root and cut into 3-inch sticks, removing any woody center core.
Boil yuca sticks in salted water for 15 minutes until fork-tender.
Drain yuca completely and pat dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350°F and carefully fry yuca sticks in batches until golden brown, about 4-5 minutes.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Season with salt, garlic powder, and black pepper while still warm.
cheapTips: Buy yuca in bulk at Latin markets for better prices
Reuse oil multiple times for frying to save costs

recipes.name: Casabe
recipes.description: Dominican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and grate the yuca root finely using a box grater or food processor.
Place grated yuca in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze out excess moisture over a bowl, pressing firmly.
Collect the liquid in the bowl and let it sit for 30 minutes; a starch will settle at the bottom.
Discard the water carefully, keeping the starch at the bottom of the bowl.
Mix the squeezed yuca with the reserved starch and salt until combined.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet or griddle over medium-high heat without oil.
Spread the yuca mixture evenly in the skillet to form a flat cake about 0.25-inch thick.
Cook for 8-10 minutes until the bottom is golden and crispy, then carefully flip and cook the other side until golden brown.
Remove and cool on a wire rack, then cut into wedges.
cheapTips: Buy yuca on sale and freeze for later use
This recipe makes a large quantity of cassava bread from minimal ingredients

recipes.name: Alcapurrias
recipes.description: Dominican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel plantains and yuca, then boil separately until tender, about 20 minutes each.
Drain and mash both together until smooth, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a skillet and sauté ground beef with onion, garlic, and sofrito until cooked through.
Stir in olives and cook 2 minutes more, then remove filling and let cool slightly.
With wet hands, take a spoonful of plantain-yuca mixture and flatten into a disc on a plastic bag.
Place a spoonful of meat filling in the center, fold the edges up, and shape into an oval ball.
Heat oil to 350°F and fry alcapurrias in batches until golden brown, about 5-6 minutes total.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with vinegar or hot sauce.
cheapTips: Make filling ahead of time and refrigerate
Fry in batches and reuse oil to reduce costs

recipes.name: Pastelitos
recipes.description: Dominican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt, then work in butter with your fingertips until breadcrumb texture forms.
Add water gradually until a soft dough forms, knead briefly, and let rest 15 minutes.
Brown ground beef in a skillet with onion, garlic, and sofrito until cooked through.
Stir in olives, cook 2 minutes, then remove from heat and let cool.
Roll dough between plastic sheets to thin sheets, cut into 3-inch squares.
Place a spoonful of meat filling on each square, fold into a triangle, and seal edges with a fork.
Heat oil to 350°F and fry pastelitos until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with vinegar or hot sauce.
cheapTips: Use store-bought empanada wrappers to save time and effort
Bulk brown the meat filling and freeze for quick future batches

recipes.name: Quipes
recipes.description: Dominican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pour hot water over bulgur wheat, cover, and let soak for 20 minutes until softened.
Heat oil in a skillet and brown ground beef with onion and garlic, stirring occasionally.
Add raisins, olives, salt, and pepper to the meat and cook 2 more minutes.
Fluff the bulgur with a fork and let cool slightly, then squeeze out any excess moisture.
Mix cooled bulgur with the meat filling until well combined.
With wet hands, form mixture into oval or torpedo shapes about 2.5 inches long.
Heat oil to 350°F and fry quipes until golden brown on all sides, about 5-6 minutes total.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.
cheapTips: Bulgur wheat is cheaper than many grain alternatives at bulk stores
Make filling and bulgur separately ahead of time for quick assembly

recipes.name: Cachapa
recipes.description: Venezuelan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blend corn kernels with milk until mostly smooth but with small corn pieces remaining.
Strain mixture through a fine sieve to remove large pieces, pressing gently.
Whisk eggs with sugar and salt, then fold into the corn mixture.
Heat butter on a griddle or large skillet over medium heat.
Pour 0.25 cup of batter per cachapa onto the hot griddle and cook 3-4 minutes until edges set.
Place a strip of cheese in the center and fold the cachapa in half like a pancake.
Cook 1-2 minutes more until golden brown on both sides.
Serve warm, optionally with additional cheese or avocado on the side.
cheapTips: Use frozen corn when fresh corn is unavailable or expensive
Make a large batch and refrigerate or freeze for quick reheating

recipes.name: Pabellón Criollo
recipes.description: Venezuelan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook or prepare rice and black beans separately according to package directions.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté onions and garlic until softened.
Add shredded beef, sofrito, cumin, salt, and cook stirring for 3 minutes.
Pour in tomato sauce and beef broth, simmer 15-20 minutes until flavors meld and liquid reduces.
Peel ripe plantains and cut diagonally into thin slices.
Heat oil in a separate skillet and fry plantain slices until golden brown on both sides, about 3-4 minutes total.
Heat black beans in a separate pot with a little water if needed.
Serve rice as the base, top with shredded beef mixture, served alongside fried plantains and black beans.
cheapTips: Use cheaper cuts of beef that shred easily when cooked slowly
Buy plantains when on sale and freeze for later use

recipes.name: Hallaca
recipes.description: Venezuelan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and brown beef cubes on all sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onion and garlic until soft, add sofrito and cook 1 minute.
Return beef to pot, add tomato sauce, salt, cumin, and 1 cup water; simmer 45 minutes until tender.
Stir in olives and raisins, cook 5 more minutes, then let filling cool completely.
Soften plantain leaves by holding briefly over a flame or dipping in hot water.
Lay a plantain leaf flat, place 2 tablespoons dough in the center, top with 2 tablespoons filling.
Fold leaf edges up and over the filling to create a neat packet, then wrap in a second leaf.
Tie packets with kitchen twine or thin strips of plantain leaf.
Boil hallacas in a large pot of salted water for 40 minutes, keeping them submerged.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain, and serve hot with additional broth or sauce on the side.
cheapTips: Prepare and freeze hallacas in advance for holiday meals
Buy plantain leaves at Latin markets in bulk for better prices

recipes.name: Tequeños
recipes.description: Venezuelan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt together in a bowl.
Cut butter into small cubes and work into the flour until mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Whisk egg yolk with water, then add to flour mixture and mix until a soft dough forms.
Knead dough for 2 minutes, wrap in plastic, and refrigerate 15 minutes.
Roll dough between plastic sheets until very thin, about 1/16-inch thick.
Cut dough into 2-inch by 4-inch rectangles.
Place a cheese stick at the edge of each rectangle and roll tightly, sealing the edge with a little water.
Heat oil to 350°F and fry tequeños until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with pepper sauce or hot sauce for dipping.
cheapTips: Use store-bought empanada wrappers instead of making dough from scratch
Freeze uncooked tequeños and fry straight from freezer when needed

recipes.name: Pastel de Carne
recipes.description: Venezuelan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Heat butter in a skillet and brown ground beef with onion and garlic, stirring frequently.
Add sofrito, tomato sauce, olives, and raisins; simmer 10 minutes and let cool slightly.
Spread the meat mixture evenly in the prepared baking dish.
Whisk together eggs, milk, flour, salt, and black pepper until smooth.
Pour egg mixture over the meat layer, spreading evenly to the edges.
Sprinkle shredded cheese over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the egg layer is set and cheese is melted and lightly golden.
Cool 5 minutes, cut into squares, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use ground beef on sale and freeze for later cooking
Make larger batches and refrigerate or freeze portions for easy reheating

recipes.name: Arroz con Gandules
recipes.description: Puerto Rican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion, garlic, and red bell pepper for 2 minutes.
Add sofrito and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice and cook for 2 minutes, stirring frequently to coat with oil.
Pour in chicken broth and add drained pigeon peas, olives, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 18-20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Fluff rice with a fork and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy rice in bulk to reduce cost
Use store-brand canned peas instead of premium brands

recipes.name: Bacalaítos
recipes.description: Puerto Rican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak salted cod in water for 4 hours, changing water twice, then shred finely.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
In another bowl, combine water, garlic, onion, cilantro, and shredded cod.
Fold wet ingredients into dry ingredients until a thick batter forms.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep skillet or pot.
Drop spoonfuls of batter into hot oil and fry 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with hot sauce.
cheapTips: Find salted cod at discount ethnic markets
Reuse frying oil for multiple batches to save cost

recipes.name: Pasteles
recipes.description: Puerto Rican dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and grate bananas, plantains, taro root, and yuca into a large bowl, then squeeze out excess moisture.
Brown ground pork in a pot, add sofrito, olives, and raisins, and cook for 5 minutes to make the filling.
Soften plantain leaves over a flame or hot water, then lay out two overlapping leaves on a flat surface.
Spread 3 tablespoons of the vegetable mixture in the center of the leaves, add 2 tablespoons of pork filling on top.
Fold the leaves around the filling to create a rectangular packet, then wrap in aluminum foil.
Bring pork broth to a boil in a large pot and carefully place pasteles inside.
Boil for 30-35 minutes until pasteles are firm and cooked through.
Remove with a slotted spoon and let cool for 5 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Buy root vegetables in bulk at Asian or Latin markets for better prices
Make pasteles in batches and freeze for later use

recipes.name: Rellenos de Papa
recipes.description: Puerto Rican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil peeled and diced potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 15 minutes, then drain and mash.
Brown ground beef in a skillet, add sofrito, olives, raisins, salt, and pepper, and cook for 5 minutes until meat is cooked through.
Mix mashed potatoes with egg and salt until you have a smooth, moldable consistency.
Form a small ball of potato mixture in your palm, press in a tablespoon of beef filling, and cover completely with more potato mixture.
Roll stuffed ball in flour to coat lightly on all sides.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep skillet and fry rellenos 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with ketchup or hot sauce.
cheapTips: Buy potatoes on sale and store for weeks to reduce costs
Use affordable ground beef from discount grocers

recipes.name: Arañitas
recipes.description: Puerto Rican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel green plantains by cutting off ends and making lengthwise cuts through the skin, then remove skin completely.
Grate peeled plantains using the largest holes on a box grater into a bowl.
Mash garlic cloves with salt until it forms a paste, then mix into grated plantains with water.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Drop spoonfuls of plantain mixture into hot oil and use the back of a spoon to flatten into thin, lacy patties.
Fry for 2 minutes per side until golden and crispy, then drain on paper towels.
Serve immediately while still crispy, optionally with a squeeze of fresh lime juice.
cheapTips: Buy plantains when on sale and store in a cool place
Reuse frying oil for multiple batches

recipes.name: Caldo Santo
recipes.description: Puerto Rican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut beef into bite-sized chunks and season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown beef on all sides, about 8 minutes total.
Add sofrito and minced garlic, stirring constantly for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beef broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Peel and cut yuca into 1-inch chunks and peel and cut plantains into 1-inch pieces.
Add yuca and plantains to the pot and simmer covered for 15 minutes until vegetables are tender and beef is cooked through.
Stir in fresh cilantro, taste, and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Use bone-in beef chuck or chuck roast on sale for better flavor and lower cost
Buy yuca and plantains at Latin markets for significant savings

recipes.name: Piononos
recipes.description: Puerto Rican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and slice plantains lengthwise into thin strips, then fry in 350°F oil for 2 minutes per side until golden and pliable, then drain.
Brown ground beef in a skillet, add sofrito, olives, raisins, and beef broth, then simmer for 5 minutes until flavors combine.
Lay two fried plantain strips in an overlapping cross pattern on a plate, creating a circle shape.
Place a generous spoonful of beef filling in the center of the circle, then fold the plantain strips up and around to enclose the filling into a nest shape.
Beat egg in a small bowl, then carefully dip the filled piononos into the egg wash to coat lightly.
Fry the egg-coated piononos in 350°F oil for 2-3 minutes until the egg coating is golden brown and set.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot, optionally topped with more sofrito sauce.
cheapTips: Buy ripe plantains in bulk when on sale and use within a few days
Reuse frying oil multiple times to reduce waste and cost

recipes.name: Empanadillas
recipes.description: Puerto Rican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt, then cut in cold butter with a fork until mixture resembles coarse crumbs, then add ice water until dough just comes together.
Wrap dough in plastic and refrigerate for 15 minutes while you prepare the filling.
Brown ground beef in a skillet, add sofrito, olives, raisins, and cook for 5 minutes until cooked through.
Roll chilled dough thin between two sheets of plastic wrap, then cut into 3-inch circles using a glass or cutter.
Place a teaspoon of beef filling on each dough circle, fold in half, and seal edges firmly with a fork.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep skillet and fry empanadillas in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with ketchup, hot sauce, or adobo sauce.
cheapTips: Make dough and filling ahead, assemble, and freeze empanadillas for quick later preparation
Use store-brand butter and flour for significant cost savings

recipes.name: Sorullitos de Maíz
recipes.description: Puerto Rican breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring milk and butter to a boil in a pot over medium-high heat.
Slowly whisk cornmeal into boiling milk, stirring constantly to prevent lumps, then reduce heat to medium-low.
Continue stirring for 5-7 minutes until mixture is thick and pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Remove from heat, stir in salt, sugar, and shredded mozzarella cheese until melted and combined.
Pour mixture onto a wet plate or cutting board and let cool until you can handle it, about 5 minutes.
Form mixture into 3-inch-long, finger-thick cylinders, then set aside on a plate.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep skillet and fry sorullitos 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with a sprinkle of salt or with sweet raisins on the side.
cheapTips: Buy cornmeal in bulk at discount stores or ethnic markets
Use store-brand cheese instead of premium brands to reduce cost

recipes.name: Longaniza
recipes.description: Puerto Rican breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak pork casings in warm water for 30 minutes until softened and pliable.
Mince garlic cloves very finely and mix with adobo, cumin, oregano, black pepper, and salt.
Combine ground pork and pork fat in a large bowl, then add garlic and spice mixture and mix thoroughly with your hands until well combined.
Fit the sausage stuffer attachment onto a meat grinder or use a manual sausage filler, then carefully feed soaked casings onto the nozzle.
Feed pork mixture into the grinder slowly while guiding the filled casing onto a baking sheet, about 4-5 inches per link.
Tie off each end of the casings with kitchen twine or by twisting to create individual sausage links, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight to allow flavors to meld.
Pan-fry longaniza in a skillet over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until the casings are deeply browned and meat is cooked through, turning occasionally.
Serve immediately while hot for breakfast with bread, eggs, and fresh lime juice.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder on sale and grind it yourself instead of purchasing pre-ground meat
Order casings online in bulk to reduce unit costs compared to butcher shop pricing

recipes.name: Semita de Méjico
recipes.description: Salvadoran snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cream together butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Beat in eggs one at a time, then add vanilla extract.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and anise seeds.
Alternate adding dry ingredients and milk to the butter mixture, beginning and ending with dry ingredients.
Drop rounded tablespoons of dough onto the prepared baking sheet, spacing them 2 inches apart.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until the edges are golden brown and a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.
cheapTips: Buy anise seeds in bulk from the spice aisle
Use store-brand butter and sugar to reduce costs

recipes.name: Quesadillas Salvadoreñas
recipes.description: Salvadoran snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix masa harina with warm water and salt until you have a soft, pliable dough.
Chop tomatoes, onion, and cilantro finely; combine with loroco if using.
Divide dough into 8 portions and form into balls.
Flatten each ball between plastic wrap into a thin disc about 3 inches wide.
Place cheese and 1 tablespoon of the tomato mixture on one half of the disc.
Fold the masa over to create a half-moon shape and press edges to seal.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat and fry quesadillas 3-4 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with tomato sauce on the side.
cheapTips: Buy masa harina in bulk from Latin markets instead of pre-made quesadillas
Use regular mozzarella cheese instead of imported quesillo

recipes.name: Chicharrones Prensados
recipes.description: Salvadoran snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork shoulder into 2-inch chunks and place in a large pot with water, salt, garlic, bay leaves, cumin, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 3-4 hours until pork is very tender and falling apart.
Remove pork from broth and shred finely with two forks.
Strain the broth and return shredded pork to the pot with 1 cup of broth.
Simmer mixture for 30 minutes until pork absorbs the liquid and begins to stick together.
Spread the cooked pork mixture onto a parchment-lined baking sheet and press firmly with a spatula or another baking sheet.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours until the mixture is completely set and firm.
Cut into rectangles, heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat, and fry chicharrones until crispy on both sides, about 3 minutes per side.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder on sale and freeze until ready to cook
Use homemade broth instead of discarding the cooking liquid

recipes.name: Pastelitos de Queso
recipes.description: Salvadoran snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine masa harina, warm water, and salt until a smooth dough forms.
Dice cheese, bell pepper, and onion finely, then mix together with black pepper.
Divide dough into 12 equal portions and form into balls.
Flatten each ball between plastic wrap into a 3-inch circle.
Place 1 tablespoon of cheese mixture in the center of each circle.
Fold edges over the filling and seal, forming a small pouch, then gently flatten.
Heat oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat and fry pastelitos 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.
cheapTips: Make dough in bulk and freeze portions for quick snacks later
Buy store-brand mozzarella in blocks and shred yourself

recipes.name: Pepián
recipes.description: Guatemalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces and season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and sear chicken on all sides until browned, about 5 minutes total; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onion and minced garlic until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Remove stems and seeds from dried chiles, then toast them lightly in a dry skillet for 30 seconds; soak in hot water for 10 minutes and drain.
Blend soaked chiles, pumpkin seeds, tomatoes, and 1 cup of chicken broth until smooth.
Pour the blended mixture through a fine-mesh strainer into the pot, discarding solids.
Add remaining chicken broth and return the cooked chicken to the pot.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes until chicken is cooked through and flavors blend together; taste and adjust seasonings.
cheapTips: Buy dried chiles in bulk from Latin markets for better prices
Use chicken thighs instead of breast for more flavor and lower cost

recipes.name: Fiambre
recipes.description: Guatemalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil chicken, pork, and beef separately in salted water for 1-1.5 hours until tender; cool, then cut into bite-sized pieces.
Boil potatoes, carrots, and beets separately in salted water until just tender; cool and cut into chunks.
Thinly slice cabbage, radishes, and red onion into a large mixing bowl.
Add all cooked meats, vegetables, and frozen peas to the bowl.
Whisk together vinegar, oil, salt, and pepper, then pour over the mixture.
Toss everything gently but thoroughly until well combined.
Let the fiambre marinate at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Taste and adjust seasonings with additional salt, pepper, or vinegar as needed.
cheapTips: Buy tougher cuts of meat (chuck, shoulder) on sale and use for stewing
Use frozen vegetables instead of fresh for lower cost and equal taste

recipes.name: Kaq ik
recipes.description: Guatemalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil chicken in salted water for 25-30 minutes until fully cooked; shred into bite-sized pieces and reserve 4 cups of broth.
Toast dried guajillo and ancho chiles in a dry skillet for 30 seconds, then soak in hot water for 10 minutes; drain and remove stems and seeds.
Blend soaked chiles, tomatoes, half the onion, and garlic with 1 cup of the reserved chicken broth until completely smooth.
Strain the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a pot, pressing solids to extract all liquid.
Heat the strained sauce over medium heat and simmer for 5 minutes to cook off raw chile flavor.
Add remaining 3 cups of broth, shredded chicken, and diced remaining onion; simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Stir in fresh cilantro and adjust seasonings with salt and pepper.
Serve hot in bowls, traditionally with corn tortillas on the side.
cheapTips: Buy whole dried chiles instead of pre-ground chili powder for more flavor per dollar
Use store-brand chicken broth or make your own from leftover bones

recipes.name: Rellenitos de Plátano
recipes.description: Guatemalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel plantains, cut into chunks, and boil in salted water for 15-20 minutes until very tender; drain well.
Mash the cooked plantain until smooth and creamy.
In a saucepan, combine black beans, sugar, cinnamon, cloves, and salt; simmer for 10 minutes until thickened, then remove whole cloves.
Divide plantain mixture into 8 portions and flatten each into a thin disc between plastic wrap.
Place 2 tablespoons of the spiced black bean mixture onto the center of each plantain disc.
Fold the plantain around the filling and seal, forming an oval shape.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and fry rellenitos 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot, optionally with tomato sauce.
cheapTips: Buy plantains when discounted and freeze until ready to use
Cook beans from dried instead of using canned for major savings

recipes.name: Enchiladas Guatemaltecas
recipes.description: Guatemalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil chicken in salted water for 25 minutes until cooked through; shred and set aside.
Toast dried pasilla and guajillo chiles in a dry skillet for 30 seconds; soak in hot water for 10 minutes, then remove stems and seeds.
Blend softened chiles with onion, garlic, tomatoes, and 1 cup of chicken broth until smooth; strain through a fine-mesh sieve.
Heat oil in a large skillet and add the strained chile sauce; simmer for 5 minutes, then add remaining 1 cup broth and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet until pliable.
Dip each tortilla into the warm sauce, then fill with shredded chicken, roll tightly, and place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour remaining sauce over the rolled enchiladas, covering them completely.
Bake at 350°F for 20 minutes until the enchiladas are heated through and sauce bubbles at the edges.
cheapTips: Buy dried chiles in bulk from Latin grocery stores
Use rotisserie chicken instead of boiling your own to save time

recipes.name: Hilachas
recipes.description: Guatemalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut beef into chunks and boil in salted water for 1.5 hours until very tender; drain and shred with two forks into thin strands.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add tomato sauce and cumin to the skillet, stirring well to combine.
Add shredded beef to the tomato sauce along with beef broth and sliced jalapeños; stir well.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until flavors blend and mixture thickens slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt, pepper, or cumin as needed.
Serve hot as a stew in bowls, traditionally with white rice and corn tortillas on the side.
cheapTips: Buy beef chuck on sale and freeze for future use
Use canned tomato sauce instead of fresh tomatoes for budget savings

recipes.name: Pulique
recipes.description: Guatemalan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring water and milk to a boil in a large pot with the cinnamon stick.
Mix cornmeal with 1 cup cold milk in a bowl until smooth with no lumps.
Slowly pour the cornmeal mixture into the boiling liquid while stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add sugar, vanilla extract, and salt, stirring until combined.
Continue cooking for 5 more minutes until the mixture thickens.
Remove cinnamon stick and serve hot in bowls.
cheapTips: Buy cornmeal in bulk from warehouse stores
Use store-brand milk to reduce costs

recipes.name: Tostadas Guatemaltecas
recipes.description: Guatemalan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Fry each tortilla for 1-2 minutes per side until crispy and golden brown.
Drain fried tortillas on paper towels.
Warm refried beans in a saucepan over low heat.
Spread a thin layer of refried beans on each crispy tortilla.
Top with crumbled queso fresco, tomatoes, cabbage, avocado slices, and a dollop of sour cream.
Serve immediately while tortillas are still warm and crispy.
cheapTips: Use canned refried beans instead of making from scratch
Buy avocado when on sale and freeze for later use

recipes.name: Hígado Encebollado
recipes.description: Guatemalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse beef liver and slice into 1/4-inch pieces, removing any membranes.
Slice onions into thin rings and chop peppers and tomatoes into chunks.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add liver pieces and cook for 3-4 minutes per side until browned but still slightly pink inside.
Remove liver and set aside, then add onions and bell peppers to the same skillet and cook for 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, salt, and pepper, then return liver to the skillet.
Simmer for 5 minutes until flavors meld, then garnish with cilantro and serve.
cheapTips: Buy beef liver from budget butchers or sale sections
Use seasonal onions and peppers to reduce cost

recipes.name: Chow Mein Guatemalteco
recipes.description: Guatemalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil salted water and cook egg noodles according to package directions, then drain and set aside.
Cut chicken into bite-sized cubes and slice vegetables into thin strips.
Heat oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat.
Add chicken and cook until golden brown and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Add minced garlic and sliced onions to the wok and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add carrots, green beans, and cabbage, stir-frying for 4-5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Return chicken to the wok with cooked noodles and pour soy sauce over everything.
Toss everything together for 2-3 minutes until heated through and well combined.
Season with white pepper and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy chicken in bulk when on sale and freeze
Use pre-shredded cabbage to save prep time

recipes.name: Consomé de Pollo
recipes.description: Guatemalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Place chicken thighs in a large pot and cover with chicken broth.
Add halved onion, smashed garlic, and chopped celery to the broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes, skimming any foam that rises.
Add diced carrots and diced potatoes and continue simmering for 15 minutes.
Remove chicken thighs and shred the meat into bite-sized pieces, discarding skin and bones.
Return shredded chicken to the pot and season with salt and pepper.
Simmer for 5 more minutes until potatoes are tender.
Ladle into bowls, garnish with fresh cilantro, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs instead of breasts for better price
Make your own stock from chicken bones if available

recipes.name: Molotes
recipes.description: Guatemalan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix masa harina with warm water and 1/2 teaspoon salt until a soft dough forms.
Cook ground beef with minced garlic and diced onion in a skillet until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add canned tomatoes, cumin, and salt to the meat mixture and simmer for 8 minutes, then cool slightly.
Form masa dough into 12 small balls, flatten each into a thin disk in your palm.
Place a spoonful of meat filling in the center of each masa disk.
Fold the masa over the filling to create a half-moon shape and seal the edges by pinching.
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350°F and fry molotes in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy masa harina in bulk or from Latin markets
Use lean ground beef or ground turkey to save money

recipes.name: Totopos
recipes.description: Guatemalan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Stack corn tortillas and cut them into quarters with a sharp knife.
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350°F.
Fry tortilla quarters in batches for 1-2 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Sprinkle warm totopos with salt while still hot.
Transfer to a serving plate and top with guacamole, salsa, sour cream, and queso fresco.
Serve immediately while totopos are still warm and crispy.
cheapTips: Cut tortillas yourself instead of buying pre-cut chips
Make fresh salsa at home with canned tomatoes

recipes.name: Chapines
recipes.description: Guatemalan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Cut butter into small cubes and work into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Pour in milk and mix gently until a soft dough forms.
Roll dough out on a floured surface to 1/4-inch thickness.
Cut dough into 2-inch squares or rectangles.
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 350°F.
Fry dough pieces in batches for 1-2 minutes per side until golden brown.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
While still warm, sprinkle with sugar and sesame seeds, then serve.
cheapTips: Buy store-brand flour and baking powder in bulk
Use margarine instead of butter to reduce costs

recipes.name: Quesadillas Guatemaltecas
recipes.description: Guatemalan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl.
Cut in butter until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Add warm water and mix until a soft dough forms, then knead for 2 minutes.
Divide dough into 8 equal portions and roll each into a thin circle.
Place a strip of quesillo cheese in the center of each dough circle.
Fold the dough in half to create a half-moon and seal edges by pressing with a fork.
Heat oil on a griddle or skillet over medium heat.
Cook quesadillas for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and cheese begins to melt.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve hot.
cheapTips: Substitute mozzarella if quesillo cheese is unavailable
Make dough ahead and refrigerate to save morning time

recipes.name: Tamalitos de Pollo
recipes.description: Guatemalan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried corn husks in warm water for 30 minutes until pliable.
Cook chicken breast in water with half the onion until fully cooked, then shred and set aside.
Beat butter until creamy, then gradually mix in masa harina with warm chicken broth and salt until soft and spreadable.
Combine shredded chicken with canned tomatoes, olives, raisins, and remaining diced onion.
Lay a soaked corn husk flat and spread about 2 tablespoons masa in the center.
Place a spoonful of chicken mixture in the middle of the masa.
Fold corn husk sides over the filling, then fold up the bottom and leave the top open.
Stand tamalitos upright in a pot with 2 inches of water at the bottom, open side up.
Cover pot with extra corn husks and steam for 30 minutes until masa is cooked through.
Serve warm in the corn husks.
cheapTips: Buy masa harina and corn husks from Latin markets for better prices
Use chicken thighs instead of breasts to reduce cost

recipes.name: Patín en Escabeche
recipes.description: Guatemalan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and season fish fillets with salt and pepper on both sides.
Cook fish fillets 3-4 minutes per side until lightly browned and cooked through, then carefully remove and set aside.
In the same skillet, sauté sliced onions and garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add vinegar, water, bay leaves, jalapeños, and cumin to the skillet and bring to a simmer.
Return fish to the skillet and simmer gently for 5 minutes to absorb flavors.
Transfer fish and sauce to a glass container and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight before serving.
cheapTips: Buy whole fish and fillet yourself to save 30% on cost
Use regular vinegar instead of specialty vinegars

recipes.name: Salteñas
recipes.description: Bolivian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour with 1 teaspoon salt and cut in cold butter until mixture resembles breadcrumbs, then add egg yolk and warm water to form dough and refrigerate 30 minutes.
Heat olive oil and brown ground beef with diced onion, then add diced potato, peas, cumin, chili powder, and broth, simmering until potatoes are tender.
Season filling with salt and pepper, then cool completely before using.
Divide dough into 12 pieces and roll each into a 4-inch circle.
Place 2 tablespoons filling in center of each dough circle, fold in half, and crimp edges with a fork to seal.
Brush each salteña with egg wash and place on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Bake at 400°F for 20-25 minutes until golden brown and serve warm.
cheapTips: Make dough ahead and freeze unbaked salteñas for quick reheating
Use ground turkey instead of beef to reduce cost by 40%

recipes.name: Api
recipes.description: Bolivian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and dice red potatoes into 0.5-inch cubes.
Bring water to a boil in a large pot and add diced potatoes, cooking until very soft, about 15 minutes.
Mash potatoes directly in the pot until smooth and creamy.
Mix cornstarch with 0.5 cup cold water until smooth, then slowly stir into the potato mixture.
Add milk, cinnamon stick, cloves, sugar, salt, and butter, stirring constantly over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Simmer for another 5 minutes until thick and creamy, stirring frequently to prevent lumps.
Remove cinnamon stick and serve hot in bowls.
cheapTips: Buy potatoes in bulk from warehouse stores to save 50%
Substitute evaporated milk for fresh milk at similar cost

recipes.name: Picana
recipes.description: Bolivian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown beef cubes in batches, about 3 minutes per side, then set aside.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in the same pot until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Return beef to pot and add beef broth, cumin, paprika, and chili powder, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 35 minutes until beef begins to tender.
Add cubed potatoes and continue simmering covered for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use a cheaper cut like beef stew meat which becomes tender with long cooking
Substitute chicken thighs for beef to reduce cost by 50%

recipes.name: Ají de Lengua
recipes.description: Bolivian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Place beef tongue in a pot of water with salt and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 1.5 hours until very tender.
Remove tongue, let cool slightly, then peel off the outer skin and cut into bite-sized cubes.
Toast dried chili and ají peppers in a dry skillet for 30 seconds, then soak in 1 cup hot water for 10 minutes and blend until smooth.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Strain the blended chili mixture into the pot and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add cooked tongue pieces, cubed potatoes, beef broth, and cumin, then simmer for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy tongue from butcher counter in bulk for 40% discount compared to pre-packaged
Use canned chili peppers instead of dried to save prep time

recipes.name: Chairo
recipes.description: Bolivian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until softened, about 2 minutes.
Add cubed potatoes to the pot and cook for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in vegetable or chicken broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes begin to soften.
Stir in turmeric powder and ground cumin, and add drained hominy to the pot.
Continue simmering for 10 more minutes until potatoes are fully tender and flavors meld.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then serve hot garnished with fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Buy canned hominy in bulk or from discount stores to save 30%
Use store-brand turmeric instead of premium brands

recipes.name: Caldo de Huesos
recipes.description: Bolivian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Place beef bones in a large pot and cover with water, then bring to a rolling boil and drain, rinsing bones well under cold water.
Return cleaned bones to the pot with fresh water, then add halved onion, unpeeled garlic, carrots, celery, bay leaves, and thyme sprigs.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 2 hours, skimming any impurities from the surface as they appear.
Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot, discarding solids.
Return strained broth to heat and simmer for another 30 minutes to concentrate flavors.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste and serve hot as a clear broth.
cheapTips: Ask your butcher for beef bones at a discount or sometimes free
Save vegetable scraps to add to the broth for extra flavor at no cost

recipes.name: Fricasé
recipes.description: Bolivian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown pork cubes on all sides in batches, about 3 minutes per batch, then set aside.
In the same pot, sauté sliced onion and minced garlic until softened and translucent, about 4 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the onion mixture and stir constantly for 1 minute to create a roux.
Return pork to pot and pour in beef broth, then add vinegar and cumin, stirring well to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes until pork is tender.
Add cubed potatoes and continue simmering covered for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot, ensuring the sauce is creamy and coats the ingredients.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder in bulk and freeze portions for savings of 35%
Use cornstarch slurry instead of flour for thickening to save 10%

recipes.name: Ranga Ranga
recipes.description: Bolivian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil tripe or liver in a separate pot of salted water for 20 minutes to remove impurities, then drain and cut into small cubes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add cubed beef tripe or liver to the pot and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in beef broth and bring to a boil, then add cubed potatoes, corn kernels, cumin, and chili powder.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender and the broth is flavorful.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot in bowls.
cheapTips: Buy tripe or liver from butcher counter where prices are 60% lower than pre-packaged
Use frozen corn instead of fresh to save 40% year-round

recipes.name: Silpancho
recipes.description: Bolivian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil peeled and sliced potatoes in salted water until tender, about 12 minutes, then drain well and set aside.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a skillet over medium heat and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add ground beef and cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until fully browned, about 6 minutes, then season with cumin, salt, and pepper.
In the same skillet, arrange the cooked potato slices in a single layer and top with the cooked ground beef mixture.
Heat remaining oil in another skillet and fry 4 eggs sunny-side up.
Divide cooked rice among 4 plates and top each portion with a potato-beef patty.
Place one fried egg on top of each patty and garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
cheapTips: Cook rice in bulk and refrigerate to save time and reduce overall cooking cost
Use ground turkey instead of beef to reduce cost by 40%

recipes.name: Red Rice
recipes.description: Soul Food dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion for 3 minutes until softened.
Add rice to the pot and stir constantly for 2 minutes to lightly toast the grains.
Pour in tomato sauce and chicken broth, stirring well to combine.
Add salt, pepper, and garlic powder, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 18-20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let stand covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
cheapTips: Buy rice in bulk from warehouse stores to reduce per-serving cost.
Use store-brand tomato sauce and broth for significant savings.

recipes.name: Collard Green Soup
recipes.description: Soul Food lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Place ham hock in a large pot with 6 cups of chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes to flavor the broth.
Add diced onion and minced garlic, simmering for 3 minutes.
Stir in chopped collard greens, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes.
Simmer uncovered for 20-25 minutes until greens are very tender.
Remove ham hock, shred any meat from the bone, return meat to soup, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy ham hocks on sale and freeze them for later use.
Purchase collard greens in season or frozen for the lowest price.

recipes.name: Cornmeal Mush
recipes.description: Soul Food breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat milk in a large saucepan over medium heat until it begins to steam but does not boil.
Slowly whisk cornmeal into the hot milk, stirring constantly to prevent lumps from forming.
Add butter, salt, sugar, and cinnamon, continuing to stir.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent sticking and scorching.
The mixture will thicken significantly and pull away slightly from the sides of the pan when done.
Pour into bowls and serve hot, optionally topped with additional butter or cinnamon.
cheapTips: Buy cornmeal in bulk from ethnic or specialty sections.
Use store-brand milk for better value.

recipes.name: Candied Yams
recipes.description: Soul Food dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 baking dish.
Arrange sliced yams in the prepared baking dish in a single layer.
In a small saucepan, melt butter and mix in brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and vanilla extract.
Pour the butter mixture evenly over the yams and sprinkle chopped pecans on top.
Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes until yams are tender.
Remove foil and top with marshmallows if desired, then bake uncovered for 5-8 minutes until golden.
cheapTips: Skip the marshmallows to cut costs while maintaining flavor.
Buy yams in bulk when prices are lowest.

recipes.name: Hush Puppies
recipes.description: Soul Food snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine cornmeal, flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Whisk together egg and buttermilk in a separate bowl, then add to dry ingredients with finely diced onion.
Stir until a thick, sticky batter forms.
Heat oil in a deep heavy pot or fryer to 350°F.
Drop spoonfuls of batter carefully into hot oil and fry for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels, then serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy vegetable oil at warehouse stores in bulk.
Make a large batch and freeze extras for quick reheating.

recipes.name: Neck Bones and Rice
recipes.description: Soul Food dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Brown pork neck bones in a large pot over medium-high heat for 5 minutes on each side, then set aside.
In the same pot, sauté diced onion and minced garlic in butter for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add rice and stir for 2 minutes to lightly toast, then pour in chicken broth and bay leaf.
Return neck bones to the pot, add salt and black pepper, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 45-50 minutes until rice is tender and meat is falling off bones.
Remove bay leaf, stir gently, and serve with meat and rice together.
cheapTips: Neck bones are an inexpensive cut; buy when on sale.
Use store-brand broth to reduce overall cost.

recipes.name: Chili Con Carne
recipes.description: Tex-Mex dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Brown ground beef in a large pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up with a spoon, then drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and minced garlic, cooking for 3 minutes until softened.
Stir in chili powder and cumin, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add drained kidney beans, diced tomatoes with juice, tomato sauce, and beef broth.
Season with salt and pepper, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 30-35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until flavors meld and sauce thickens.
cheapTips: Buy ground beef on sale and freeze in portions.
Use store-brand canned goods to save money.

recipes.name: Fajitas
recipes.description: Tex-Mex dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine lime juice, 2 tablespoons olive oil, minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Toss beef slices in this marinade and let sit for 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over high heat and cook beef in batches for 2-3 minutes, then set aside.
In the same skillet, cook bell peppers and onion slices for 5-7 minutes until slightly charred and tender.
Return beef to the skillet, stir everything together, and cook for 2 minutes to combine flavors.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet or over a flame for 30 seconds per side, then serve with beef and vegetable mixture.
cheapTips: Use sirloin instead of skirt steak for cheaper options.
Buy tortillas on sale and freeze for later use.

recipes.name: Chile Con Queso
recipes.description: Tex-Mex snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine cubed Velveeta cheese and half-and-half cream in a saucepan over medium heat.
Stir constantly until cheese is fully melted and creamy, about 5 minutes.
Add drained canned green chiles, diced jalapeño if using, garlic powder, cumin, and salt.
Stir well to combine and heat through for 2-3 minutes.
Transfer to a serving bowl or cheese warmer and serve immediately with tortilla chips for dipping.
cheapTips: Watch for sales on Velveeta and buy in bulk.
Use store-brand tortilla chips instead of name brands.

recipes.name: Chimichanga
recipes.description: Tex-Mex dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Brown ground beef with diced onion in a skillet over medium-high heat, then drain fat.
Mix in drained black beans, 1 cup shredded cheese, sour cream, 0.5 cup salsa, salt, and cumin.
Warm each flour tortilla in a dry skillet and place on a work surface.
Divide beef mixture evenly among tortillas, placing filling in the center of each, then roll tightly and fold in the sides like a burrito.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F and carefully fry each chimichanga seam-side down for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels, top with remaining cheese and salsa, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Make filling ahead and refrigerate to save time.
Use ground beef on sale and freeze in portions.

recipes.name: Choclo con Queso
recipes.description: Ecuadorian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Add corn cobs and boil for 15-20 minutes until kernels are tender.
Drain the corn and brush each ear generously with butter.
Sprinkle salt and pepper evenly over all corn.
Top each ear with crumbled queso fresco cheese.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve immediately while warm.
cheapTips: Buy corn in season (summer) for best prices
Use regular cheddar if queso fresco is unavailable

recipes.name: Corvina a la Sal
recipes.description: Ecuadorian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Mix sea salt with egg whites and water to form a paste that holds together.
Clean and scale the fish, leaving head and tail intact.
Spread half the salt mixture on the baking sheet and place the fish on top.
Cover the entire fish with remaining salt mixture, pressing firmly to seal.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until the salt crust is hard and golden.
Crack open the salt crust and carefully remove the fish, brushing away excess salt.
Serve with a drizzle of olive oil infused with garlic and lemon juice.
cheapTips: Buy whole fish from the seafood counter instead of fillets
Make this dish when fish is on sale at local markets

recipes.name: Tigrillo
recipes.description: Ecuadorian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel green plantains and boil in salted water for 12-15 minutes until very tender.
Drain plantains thoroughly and mash until smooth.
Heat butter in a skillet and sauté diced onion until softened.
Stir the mashed plantains into the onion mixture and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove from heat and fold in shredded cheese until melted.
Form the mixture into patties and cook in a buttered skillet until golden on both sides.
Fry eggs to your preference and serve alongside the tigrillo patties.
cheapTips: Buy plantains when on sale and freeze extras
Use any melting cheese you have on hand
