Bake at 400°F for 8-10 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly.
cheapTips: Buy chicken breasts on sale and freeze for later
Use store-bought tomato sauce instead of making from scratch

recipes.name: Pâté en Croûte
recipes.description: French lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mince pork liver with shallots and garlic, then mix with ground pork, brandy, thyme, and seasonings.
Cube veal or chicken breast into small pieces and fold into the forcemeat along with pistachios.
Line a terrine mold with bacon strips, letting them hang over the edges.
Fill the terrine with the forcemeat mixture, pressing down firmly with each layer.
Fold bacon strips over the top, cover with foil, and place in a water bath.
Bake at 325°F for 50-60 minutes until the internal temperature reaches 160°F.
Cool completely, then refrigerate overnight before unmolding and slicing.
Serve chilled with crusty bread and cornichons.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder and liver from a butcher counter for better prices
Make ahead and freeze for up to 2 weeks

recipes.name: Chicken Pastilla
recipes.description: Moroccan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Poach chicken breasts in water with onions, garlic, and ginger for 20 minutes, then shred the meat.
Heat 2 tablespoons butter and sauté remaining onions until caramelized, add chicken and cinnamon, and cook for 5 minutes.
Toast almonds in a dry pan until fragrant, then set aside.
Scramble eggs in a pan until just set, then fold into the chicken mixture along with herbs.
Layer phyllo sheets on a baking sheet, brushing each with melted butter.
Spread chicken filling down the center of the phyllo stack, add toasted almonds, then fold edges over to enclose.
Brush the entire pastry with remaining melted butter and bake at 375°F for 25-30 minutes until golden.
Dust with powdered sugar and cinnamon before serving.
cheapTips: Use phyllo dough from the frozen section instead of fresh
Buy almonds in bulk or use cheaper blanched almonds

recipes.name: Banitsa
recipes.description: Bulgarian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix crumbled feta cheese with beaten eggs, yogurt, herbs, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Brush a 9x13 baking dish with melted butter.
Layer 4 phyllo sheets in the dish, brushing each sheet with melted butter.
Spread the cheese and egg mixture evenly over the phyllo.
Layer the remaining 4 phyllo sheets on top, brushing each with butter.
Cut the banitsa into squares or diagonal pieces with a sharp knife.
Bake at 375°F for 25-30 minutes until the top is golden brown and crispy.
cheapTips: Buy phyllo dough from the frozen section for significant savings
Use store-brand feta cheese instead of imported varieties

recipes.name: Enchilada Pie
recipes.description: Mexican dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Brown ground beef with diced onion and garlic, then add chili powder, black beans, and corn.
Simmer the beef mixture for 5 minutes, then stir in 1/2 cup sour cream.
Spread a thin layer of enchilada sauce on the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish.
Layer 4 tortillas, breaking to fit, then half the beef mixture, 1/2 cup sauce, and 1 cup cheese.
Repeat with remaining tortillas, beef mixture, sauce, and cheese.
Cover with foil and bake at 375°F for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10 more minutes until cheese is bubbly.
Garnish with remaining sour cream and fresh cilantro if desired.
cheapTips: Use store-brand enchilada sauce instead of making from scratch
Buy ground beef on sale and freeze until ready to use

recipes.name: Cornish Hen Pie
recipes.description: British dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F and roast the Cornish hens for 40 minutes until golden.
Cool hens slightly, then shred meat from bones and set aside.
Dice carrots and celery, then simmer in chicken broth for 10 minutes until tender.
Make pie dough by mixing flour, butter, salt, and ice water until crumbly, then chill for 15 minutes.
Combine shredded hen meat, cooked vegetables, peas, and broth in a pie dish.
Roll out dough and place over filling, then brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 400°F for 25-30 minutes until crust is golden brown.
Cool for 5 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Use chicken instead of Cornish hens for significant savings.
Make pie dough from scratch rather than buying pre-made.

recipes.name: Molote
recipes.description: Mexican snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, and salt to form a dough and let rest for 10 minutes.
Brown ground beef with diced onion, minced garlic, and cumin in a skillet.
Finely chop jalapeño and stir into beef mixture along with shredded cheese.
Divide dough into 8 portions and flatten each into a thin circle.
Place 2 tablespoons of beef filling on one half of each dough circle.
Fold dough in half to enclose filling and press edges to seal.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F and fry molotes until golden on both sides, about 3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with salsa.
cheapTips: Buy ground beef on sale and freeze for later use.
Use white cheddar instead of mozzarella for a cheaper alternative.

recipes.name: Tarte à l'Oignon
recipes.description: French lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, butter, and salt with a fork until crumbly, then add ice water and form a dough.
Chill dough for 20 minutes, then roll out and press into a pie dish.
Prick crust with a fork and bake at 375°F for 10 minutes.
Slice onions thinly and cook slowly in butter for 30 minutes until very soft and golden.
Whisk together cream, egg yolks, cheese, pepper, and thyme in a bowl.
Spread caramelized onions in the partially baked crust.
Pour cream mixture evenly over onions.
Bake at 375°F for 25-30 minutes until custard is set and lightly golden.
cheapTips: Use sharp cheddar instead of Gruyère to reduce costs.
Caramelize onions ahead of time to reduce active cooking time.

recipes.name: Aglio e Olio
recipes.description: Italian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente.
Slice garlic cloves thinly and heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat.
Add garlic and red pepper flakes to oil and cook gently for 3-4 minutes until fragrant but not brown.
Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water, then drain spaghetti.
Add hot spaghetti to the skillet with garlic oil and toss well.
Add 1/4 cup reserved pasta water a little at a time to create a light sauce, tossing constantly.
Season with salt and black pepper, then remove from heat.
Divide onto plates and top with fresh parsley and lemon juice.
cheapTips: Buy garlic in bulk and peel multiple cloves at once.
Use regular olive oil instead of extra virgin to save money.

recipes.name: Bolognese
recipes.description: Italian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice onion, carrots, celery, and garlic finely to create a soffritto base.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté soffritto over medium heat for 5 minutes until softened.
Add ground beef and cook, breaking it apart, until browned about 8 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then add canned tomatoes with juices.
Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in milk and season with salt and pepper.
Simmer for 5-10 more minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Serve over cooked pasta with grated Parmesan cheese.
cheapTips: Use ground chuck instead of premium beef to reduce costs.
Make a double batch and freeze half for quick future meals.

recipes.name: Spaghetti alla Puttanesca
recipes.description: Italian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti according to package directions.
Mince garlic and anchovies together into a paste.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook garlic-anchovy paste for 2 minutes.
Add canned tomatoes with juices, olives, capers, and red pepper flakes.
Simmer sauce for 10 minutes, breaking up tomatoes with a spoon.
Drain spaghetti and add to the sauce, tossing well to combine.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately in bowls.
cheapTips: Buy olives and capers from bulk bins instead of jars.
Use canned anchovies sold in bulk rather than small tins.

recipes.name: Arrabbiata
recipes.description: Italian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente.
Slice garlic thinly and heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat.
Add garlic and red pepper flakes to oil and cook gently for 2-3 minutes until fragrant but not brown.
Add canned tomatoes with juices and stir well.
Simmer sauce for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally and breaking up tomatoes.
Reserve 1 cup pasta water, then drain spaghetti and add to the sauce.
Toss spaghetti in sauce, adding pasta water a little at a time to reach desired consistency.
Season with salt and black pepper, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy generic canned tomatoes instead of name brands.
Use dried parsley instead of fresh to reduce cost.

recipes.name: Cacio e Pepe Pasta
recipes.description: Italian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Coarsely grind black peppercorns in a spice grinder or with a mortar and pestle.
Bring 6 cups of salted water to a boil in a large pot and add pasta.
Toast ground pepper in a large skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Grate Pecorino Romano finely and set aside in a bowl.
When pasta is al dente, reserve 2 cups of pasta cooking water and drain pasta.
Add 1 cup of hot pasta water to the skillet with pepper and stir.
Add hot pasta to the skillet and toss continuously while gradually sprinkling cheese over it.
Keep tossing, adding pasta water gradually to create a creamy sauce, then serve immediately.
cheapTips: Grate your own Pecorino cheese rather than buying pre-grated.
Buy whole peppercorns in bulk and grind as needed.

recipes.name: Spaghetti al Pomodoro
recipes.description: Italian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente.
Mince garlic cloves finely and heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add minced garlic and cook gently for 2 minutes until fragrant but not browned.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and stir well, then bring to a simmer.
Simmer sauce for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Tear basil leaves and stir into sauce along with salt and pepper.
Drain spaghetti and transfer to the skillet with sauce, tossing well to coat.
Divide onto plates and top generously with grated Parmesan cheese.
cheapTips: Buy whole garlic and mince it yourself rather than using jarred.
Use dried basil instead of fresh to save money.

recipes.name: Baked Ziti
recipes.description: Italian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F and cook ziti according to package directions until al dente, then drain.
Brown ground beef with diced onion and minced garlic in a skillet until cooked through.
Mix ricotta, egg, 1 cup mozzarella, Parmesan, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Stir marinara sauce into the cooked ground beef.
In a 9x13 inch baking dish, combine cooked pasta, meat sauce, and half the ricotta mixture.
Dollop remaining ricotta mixture over pasta and sprinkle remaining mozzarella on top.
Cover with foil and bake at 375°F for 20 minutes.
Remove foil and bake for another 10-15 minutes until cheese is bubbly and slightly golden.
cheapTips: Buy ground beef on sale and freeze until ready to use.
Use store-brand ricotta and mozzarella to reduce overall cost.

recipes.name: Peperoni Ripieni
recipes.description: Italian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut the tops off peppers and remove seeds and membranes, then set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat and sauté diced onion and garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add ground beef to the pan and cook until browned, breaking it apart as it cooks for about 5 minutes.
Stir in uncooked rice and cook for 2 minutes, then add canned tomatoes with their juice and 1 cup of water or broth.
Simmer the mixture for 15 minutes until rice is partially cooked, then season with salt and pepper.
Stir in half the parmesan cheese into the meat and rice mixture.
Stuff each pepper loosely with the filling and place upright in a baking dish, pour remaining tomato sauce around peppers, and top each with remaining parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake at 375°F for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake another 10 minutes until peppers are tender.
cheapTips: Buy bell peppers on sale or use a mix of colors for same price
Use regular long-grain rice instead of arborio to save 30%

recipes.name: Yalanci Dolma
recipes.description: Turkish lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a pan and sauté diced onion until translucent, about 4 minutes.
Add rice to the onion and stir for 1 minute, then add tomato paste, mint, and pine nuts and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in water and lemon juice, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 8 minutes until rice is partially cooked.
Season the filling with salt and pepper and let cool slightly for easier handling.
Rinse grape leaves and lay them shiny-side down, place about 1 tablespoon filling on each leaf near the stem, then fold in sides and roll tightly.
Arrange rolled dolmas seam-side down in a tight row in a pot, drizzle with remaining olive oil, cover with an inverted plate to keep them from unrolling.
Add 1 cup water to the pot, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes, then serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Jarred grape leaves are usually cheaper than fresh in US grocery stores
Omit pine nuts and use sesame seeds for half the cost

recipes.name: Mahshi Kossa
recipes.description: Egyptian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Wash zucchini and trim ends, then use an apple corer or small knife to hollow out the centers, reserving the scooped flesh.
Heat olive oil in a large pan and sauté minced onion and garlic until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add ground beef and cook until browned, breaking it apart, about 5 minutes, then add rice and stir for 1 minute.
Mix in the reserved zucchini flesh, salt, pepper, and cumin, then cook for 2 minutes and remove from heat.
Stuff each hollowed zucchini tightly with the meat and rice mixture using a small spoon.
Arrange stuffed zucchini in a pot, pour canned tomatoes and water around them, season the liquid with salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 35-40 minutes until zucchini is tender but not falling apart.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot with the tomato broth spooned over top.
cheapTips: Buy zucchini in season (summer) when prices drop significantly
Use ground chicken instead of beef for 20-30% savings

recipes.name: Gefüllte Paprika
recipes.description: German dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut the tops off peppers and remove seeds and membranes, then set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat and sauté diced onion until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add ground meat to the pan and cook until browned, breaking it apart, about 5 minutes.
Stir in uncooked rice, paprika powder, salt, and pepper, then cook for 2 minutes.
Remove the pan from heat, let cool slightly, then beat in the egg to bind the mixture.
Stuff each pepper with the meat and rice mixture and place upright in a baking dish.
Mix canned tomatoes with beef broth and pour around the peppers, then cover with foil and bake at 375°F for 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake for another 10-15 minutes until peppers are very tender and the filling is cooked through.
cheapTips: Use ground pork which is usually 20% cheaper than beef
Make rice from bulk bins for 40% less than packaged

recipes.name: Pimiento Relleno de Queso
recipes.description: Spanish lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Drain jarred roasted peppers and carefully pat dry with paper towels.
Gently insert one cheese slice into each pepper, folding the pepper around it to enclose completely.
Pour flour into a shallow bowl and beat eggs in another shallow bowl.
Dredge each stuffed pepper in flour, shaking off excess, then dip in beaten egg to coat completely.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F and fry peppers until golden brown on all sides, about 3 minutes total, then transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate.
In a separate saucepan, heat tomato sauce over medium heat and stir in minced garlic, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Simmer the sauce for 5 minutes until flavors blend.
Serve fried peppers hot, spooning warm tomato sauce over and around them.
cheapTips: Buy jarred roasted peppers on sale and stock up; they keep for months
Use cheddar instead of manchego for 50% savings on cheese

recipes.name: Bacalı Dolma
recipes.description: Turkish lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: If using salt cod, soak it in cold water for 12 hours, changing water every 3 hours, then drain and flake the fish.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a pan and sauté diced onion until soft, about 4 minutes.
Add rice to the onion and stir for 1 minute, then add the flaked fish, dill, and pine nuts and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in water and lemon juice, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 8 minutes until rice is partially cooked.
Season with black pepper and let the mixture cool slightly.
Rinse grape leaves and lay them shiny-side down, place about 1 tablespoon filling on each leaf, then fold in sides and roll tightly.
Arrange rolled dolmas seam-side down in a pot, drizzle with remaining olive oil, cover with an inverted plate to prevent unrolling.
Add 1 cup water to the pot, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 20 minutes, then serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Use canned mackerel or sardines instead of salt cod to skip soaking and save money
Omit pine nuts and use sesame seeds for 60% savings

recipes.name: Baghali Polo ba Morgh
recipes.description: Persian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak saffron threads in 1/4 cup hot water for 10 minutes until water turns golden.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and sauté sliced onions until golden, about 6 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and turmeric, then brown them in the same pot for 3 minutes per side.
Return onions to the pot with chicken, add 1 cup water, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 25 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
While chicken cooks, rinse rice and bring 4 cups water to a boil in a separate pot, salt generously, add rice and cook for 5 minutes, then drain when partially cooked.
Heat remaining 2 tablespoons oil in a clean pot and add drained rice, mixing gently with a fork.
Layer dill and peas over rice, then pour saffron water evenly over the top.
Cover the pot with foil and a tight-fitting lid, cook over medium heat for 15 minutes until rice is fluffy and a golden crust forms on the bottom.
Serve rice on a platter topped with the chicken and sauce.
cheapTips: Skip saffron and use 1/4 tsp turmeric instead to save $3-4 per serving
Use chicken drumsticks or breasts on sale instead of thighs

recipes.name: Stuffed Tomatoes Provençal
recipes.description: French lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut a thin slice off the top of each tomato and scoop out the insides with a small spoon, reserving the pulp and discarding seeds.
Heat olive oil in a pan and sauté minced onion and garlic until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add ground meat and cook until browned, breaking it apart, about 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and mix in breadcrumbs, reserved tomato pulp, basil, thyme, egg, salt, and pepper.
Stuff each tomato shell generously with the meat mixture, then place upright in an oiled baking dish.
Drizzle a little olive oil over the top of each stuffed tomato.
Bake at 375°F for 25-30 minutes until tomatoes are tender and filling is cooked through.
Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally garnished with fresh basil.
cheapTips: Use ground beef on sale and freeze for later, or use pork for 15% less cost
Make breadcrumbs from stale bread instead of buying packaged

recipes.name: Piquante Paprika
recipes.description: Hungarian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut tops off peppers and remove seeds and membranes, reserving one pepper for sauce.
Heat oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add ground pork and cook until browned, breaking it apart, about 5 minutes.
Stir in paprika and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, then add rice and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in beef broth and canned tomatoes with juice, then add salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 12 minutes until rice is partially cooked.
Stuff each pepper with the meat and rice mixture and place upright in the pot.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until peppers are tender and filling is cooked through.
Serve peppers hot with a dollop of sour cream on top and broth spooned around them.
cheapTips: Buy Hungarian paprika from ethnic grocery stores for half the supermarket price
Skip sour cream or use Greek yogurt mixed with a pinch of paprika as a cheaper substitute

recipes.name: Farci de Légumes
recipes.description: Moroccan dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Halve zucchini and eggplant lengthwise, scoop out centers leaving 1/4-inch shells, and chop the scooped flesh; halve peppers and remove seeds.
Heat oil in a large pan and sauté minced onion and garlic until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add ground meat and cook until browned, breaking it apart, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the chopped zucchini and eggplant flesh, cinnamon, cumin, salt, and pepper, then cook for 3 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in dry couscous until well combined.
Generously fill each vegetable shell with the couscous and meat mixture, mounding slightly.
Arrange filled vegetables skin-side up in a baking dish, pour canned tomatoes and their juice around (not over) vegetables.
Cover with foil and bake at 375°F for 35-40 minutes until vegetables are tender and filling is heated through.
cheapTips: Buy vegetables at farmers markets near closing time for 30-50% discounts
Use ground beef instead of lamb for 25% savings

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Chicken Souvlaki
recipes.description: Greek dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut chicken breasts into 1.5-inch cubes and place in a bowl.
Mix olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper in a bowl, then add chicken and marinate for 15 minutes.
Chop bell peppers and red onion into chunks and toss with cherry tomatoes on a sheet pan.
Add marinated chicken to the sheet pan with vegetables and distribute evenly.
Roast at 425°F for 18-22 minutes until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender.
Stir halfway through cooking for even browning.
cheapTips: Buy chicken breasts on sale and freeze for later
Use seasonal bell peppers for lower prices

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Vegetable Frittata
recipes.description: Italian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F and grease a sheet pan with olive oil.
Chop zucchini, bell pepper, and onion into small pieces.
Sauté chopped vegetables in olive oil on the stovetop for 3 minutes, then spread on the sheet pan.
Whisk together eggs, milk, salt, and pepper, then pour over vegetables.
Sprinkle cheddar cheese and fresh spinach over the egg mixture.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until eggs are set and top is lightly golden.
Cool for 2 minutes, then slice and serve.
cheapTips: Buy eggs in bulk when on sale
Use frozen spinach instead of fresh to save money

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Shrimp Fried Rice
recipes.description: Chinese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F and divide rice across a sheet pan to dry it slightly for 5 minutes.
Season shrimp with salt and pepper, then spread on the sheet pan around the rice.
Roast for 5-7 minutes until shrimp turn pink, then push to the side.
Scramble eggs in a bowl, then add to the pan and break into small pieces.
Add frozen peas and carrots, minced garlic, and ginger to the pan and mix well.
Drizzle soy sauce and sesame oil over everything and toss to combine.
Roast for another 3-4 minutes until vegetables are heated through.
Garnish with chopped green onions before serving.
cheapTips: Use frozen shrimp instead of fresh for lower cost
Make rice ahead of time and store in the fridge

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Chicken Marsala
recipes.description: Italian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound chicken breasts to 1/4-inch thickness and coat lightly with flour mixed with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side, then transfer to a sheet pan.
In the same skillet, sauté sliced mushrooms and minced garlic for 3 minutes.
Deglaze the pan with Marsala wine, then add chicken broth.
Pour the mushroom and sauce mixture over the chicken on the sheet pan.
Bake at 375°F for 12-15 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
cheapTips: Use cooking wine instead of Marsala to cut costs
Buy chicken when on sale and freeze

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Tofu Stir-Fry
recipes.description: Chinese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Press tofu between paper towels for 10 minutes to remove excess moisture, then cut into 3/4-inch cubes.
Toss tofu cubes with cornstarch, soy sauce, and sesame oil in a bowl.
Spread tofu and all chopped vegetables on a sheet pan and drizzle with vegetable oil.
Sprinkle minced garlic and ginger over everything and toss well.
Roast at 425°F for 20-25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until vegetables are tender and tofu is golden.
Serve hot with additional soy sauce if desired.
cheapTips: Buy tofu in bulk and freeze extra for later
Use frozen broccoli to save money

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Baked Cod with Vegetables
recipes.description: American dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
Chop zucchini, asparagus into 2-inch pieces, and slice lemon into thin rounds.
Arrange vegetables on the sheet pan and drizzle with olive oil, then season with salt, pepper, thyme, and minced garlic.
Roast vegetables for 10 minutes, then push to the sides and place cod fillets in the center.
Season cod with salt, pepper, and thyme, then top with lemon slices.
Roast for another 10-12 minutes until cod flakes easily with a fork.
Serve immediately with vegetables.
cheapTips: Buy cod when on sale and freeze
Use seasonal vegetables for better prices

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Sausage and Potatoes
recipes.description: American dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F and cut baby potatoes in half.
Toss potatoes with olive oil, minced garlic, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper on a sheet pan.
Roast potatoes for 15 minutes.
Add sausage links and chopped peppers and onions to the pan around the potatoes.
Roast for another 15-20 minutes until sausage is cooked through and potatoes are tender.
Top with grated parmesan cheese before serving.
cheapTips: Buy sausage on sale and freeze for later
Use russet potatoes cut small instead of baby potatoes

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Chicken Parmesan
recipes.description: Italian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound chicken breasts to 1/2-inch thickness and set up a breading station with flour, beaten eggs, and panko mixed with parmesan.
Coat each chicken breast in flour, then egg, then panko mixture.
Heat olive oil in a skillet and sear breaded chicken for 2-3 minutes per side until golden.
Transfer chicken to a sheet pan and top each piece with marinara sauce and mozzarella cheese.
Bake at 375°F for 12-15 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Let cool for 2 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Buy chicken breasts on sale and freeze
Use store-brand marinara sauce to save money

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Beef and Broccoli
recipes.description: Chinese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice beef flank steak against the grain into thin strips.
Mix soy sauce, sesame oil, cornstarch, brown sugar, minced garlic, and ginger in a bowl, then coat beef strips and let sit for 10 minutes.
Spread broccoli florets on a sheet pan and drizzle with vegetable oil, then roast at 425°F for 8 minutes.
Push broccoli to the sides and add marinated beef to the center of the pan.
Roast for another 8-10 minutes until beef is cooked through and broccoli is tender with crispy edges.
Garnish with chopped green onions before serving.
cheapTips: Buy flank steak on sale and freeze for later
Use frozen broccoli to save money and prep time

recipes.name: Chettinad Chicken
recipes.description: Indian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dry roast coriander seeds and black peppercorns in a skillet for 2 minutes until fragrant, then grind to a powder.
Chop onions, tomatoes, and garlic, then blend with shredded coconut, ground spices, chili powder, and turmeric to make a paste.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot and fry chicken thighs until lightly browned, then set aside.
In the same pot, fry chopped onions until golden, then add the coconut spice paste and cook for 5 minutes.
Return chicken to the pot and stir to coat with the paste.
Simmer on medium heat for 25-30 minutes until chicken is cooked through and sauce thickens.
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking and adjust salt to taste.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs instead of breasts for lower cost
Use frozen shredded coconut instead of fresh

recipes.name: Carnitas
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork shoulder into 2-inch cubes and season generously with salt.
Heat lard in a large heavy pot over medium heat until shimmering.
Add pork cubes, garlic, oregano, cumin, bay leaves, and onion to the hot lard.
Reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 2 to 2.5 hours until pork is very tender and shreds easily.
Uncover and increase heat to medium-high, stirring occasionally, until pork browns and fat renders out (about 30 minutes).
Drain excess fat, shred pork with two forks, and stir in lime juice.
Warm tortillas and serve carnitas with diced onion, cilantro, and lime wedges.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder on sale and freeze for later use.
Render your own lard from pork trimmings to save money.

recipes.name: Lengua
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse beef tongue and place in a large pot with water, half the onion, garlic, salt, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 3 hours until tongue is very tender.
Remove tongue and let cool slightly, then peel off the outer skin with a knife.
Slice the peeled tongue into thin pieces.
In a skillet, sauté remaining onion and jalapeños until softened.
Add sliced tongue to the skillet and cook until lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Serve on warm tortillas with cilantro, diced onion, and lime.
cheapTips: Beef tongue is often inexpensive at butcher counters.
Save the broth for soups and other dishes.

recipes.name: Cabeza
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Request pre-cut beef head meat from the butcher and have them clean it thoroughly.
Place beef head meat in a large pot with water, half the onion, garlic, salt, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, skim foam from the surface, then simmer covered for 4 hours until meat is very tender.
Remove meat and let cool, then shred with two forks and remove any remaining bones or cartilage.
Heat oil in a skillet and sauté remaining onion and jalapeños until golden.
Add shredded meat and sauté until edges crisp up slightly, about 8 minutes.
Serve on warm tortillas with diced onion, cilantro, jalapeños, and fresh lime juice.
cheapTips: Beef head meat is economical; ask your butcher for the best parts.
Use the cooking broth as a base for menudo or other soups.

recipes.name: Tripe
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse tripe thoroughly under cold water and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Place tripe in a large pot with water, half the onion, 3 garlic cloves, salt, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 2.5 hours until tender.
Drain and reserve 1 cup of broth.
In a skillet, sauté remaining onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add cooked tripe, cumin, oregano, and reserved broth; simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve on warm tortillas with diced onion, cilantro, jalapeños, and lime.
cheapTips: Buy tripe in bulk and freeze portions for later use.
Make menudo with the leftover cooking broth.

recipes.name: Chorizo
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice potatoes into small cubes and sauté in oil over medium-high heat until golden, about 10 minutes.
Remove casing from chorizo and crumble the meat into the skillet with potatoes.
Cook chorizo until browned and fat renders, stirring frequently, about 8 minutes.
Add diced onion, jalapeños, and minced garlic; cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Warm tortillas and serve chorizo mixture with diced onion, cilantro, and lime wedges.
cheapTips: Buy chorizo on sale and freeze in portions.
Use smaller potatoes to stretch the recipe further.

recipes.name: Pollo Asado
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine garlic, cumin, oregano, paprika, vinegar, lime juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper in a blender until smooth.
Pat chicken dry and rub the marinade all over the chicken, inside and out.
Marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature.
Preheat oven to 425°F and place chicken breast-side up in a roasting pan.
Roast for 1 hour until skin is golden and a meat thermometer reads 165°F in the thickest part of the thigh.
Let rest for 5 minutes, then carve and serve with lime wedges and warm tortillas.
cheapTips: Buy whole chickens instead of parts for better value.
Make extra and use leftovers for tacos the next day.

recipes.name: Pescado
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Season fish fillets with salt, pepper, and 2 tablespoons lime juice.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and add minced garlic.
Place fish in the skillet and cook for 3-4 minutes per side until opaque and flakes easily.
Remove fish and set aside, then sauté diced onion and jalapeños in the same skillet for 2 minutes.
Return fish to skillet, add remaining lime juice and cilantro, and cook for 1 minute.
Serve fish on warm tortillas with sautéed onions, jalapeños, and fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Buy frozen white fish fillets for lower cost.
Use tilapia or cod as budget-friendly white fish options.

recipes.name: Chicharrón Prensado
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork skin into 2-inch pieces and place in a large pot with water, salt, onion, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 3 hours until skin and fat are very tender.
Drain and cool slightly, then shred the pork skin mixture with two forks.
Spread shredded mixture on a parchment-lined baking sheet and press flat, then refrigerate for 2 hours until set.
Cut into squares and pan-fry in a skillet over medium-high heat until crispy edges form, about 5 minutes per side.
Serve on warm tortillas with salsa, diced onion, cilantro, and lime.
cheapTips: Pork skin is inexpensive at butcher shops.
Make a large batch and freeze portions for later.

recipes.name: Rajas con Queso
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Char poblano peppers directly over a gas flame or under the broiler until blackened all over.
Place charred peppers in a plastic bag for 5 minutes to steam, then peel off the skin under cool running water.
Remove seeds and slice peppers into thin strips.
Heat oil in a skillet and sauté sliced onion and minced garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add pepper strips and cook for 2 minutes, then pour in cream and simmer for 3 minutes.
Tear Oaxaca cheese into pieces and stir into the rajas until melted, season with salt and pepper.
Serve rajas on warm tortillas garnished with cilantro.
cheapTips: Use regular mozzarella if Oaxaca cheese is unavailable.
Buy poblanos in season and freeze for later use.

recipes.name: Huitlacoche
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat butter in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add drained huitlacoche and diced jalapeños to the skillet.
Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until huitlacoche darkens slightly and flavors blend.
Add epazote leaves and stir to combine, then season with salt and pepper.
Cook for 2 more minutes until epazote wilts slightly.
Serve huitlacoche mixture on warm tortillas topped with crumbled queso fresco and additional epazote if desired.
cheapTips: Canned huitlacoche is convenient and affordable year-round.
Fresh corn husks can replace epazote if unavailable.

recipes.name: Bánh Canh Cua
recipes.description: Vietnamese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil tapioca pearls in salted water for 15-20 minutes until translucent, then drain and set aside.
Heat chicken broth in a large pot over high heat.
Mince garlic and slice onion, then add to broth and simmer for 5 minutes.
Flake crab meat and add to broth along with fish sauce, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cooked tapioca pearls to the broth and stir gently.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Divide into bowls and top with chopped scallions, fried shallots, and a squeeze of fresh lime.
Serve immediately while hot.
cheapTips: Use canned crab instead of fresh to save money
Buy tapioca pearls in bulk at Asian markets for better prices

recipes.name: Mien Lạnh
recipes.description: Vietnamese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook rice vermicelli noodles according to package directions, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Make dipping sauce by combining fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, minced garlic, and sliced chilies in a bowl.
Chill the cooked noodles in the refrigerator for at least 15 minutes.
Thinly slice cucumber and chop fresh mint leaves.
Arrange chilled noodles in bowls and top with cucumber, mint, and shrimp.
Drizzle with the prepared dipping sauce and serve cold.
cheapTips: Use frozen shrimp instead of fresh to reduce cost significantly
Buy herbs from Asian markets where they're cheaper

recipes.name: Kari Laksanoodles
recipes.description: Malaysian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook egg noodles according to package directions, drain and set aside.
Cut chicken breast into bite-sized pieces and dice onion and garlic.
Heat oil in a large pot and sauté garlic and onion until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add curry powder and turmeric, stirring constantly for 1 minute.
Pour in coconut milk and chicken broth, bring to a simmer.
Add chicken pieces and cook for 10 minutes, then add shrimp and cook for another 3 minutes.
Stir in cooked noodles, fish sauce, and lime juice, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve in bowls garnished with chopped scallions.
cheapTips: Buy curry powder in bulk from Indian or Asian stores
Use canned coconut milk which is cheaper than fresh

recipes.name: Ramen Frio
recipes.description: Argentine lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook ramen noodles according to package directions, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Dice tomato, cucumber, and red onion into small pieces.
Mince garlic clove and chop fresh parsley.
Whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Toss cold noodles with diced vegetables in a large bowl.
Pour vinaigrette over noodle mixture and toss well to combine.
Chill in refrigerator for at least 10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve cold.
cheapTips: Buy instant ramen in bulk packs for under $0.30 per package
Use whatever fresh vegetables are on sale

recipes.name: Ajitsuke Tamago
recipes.description: Japanese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil water in a pot and gently add eggs, cooking for 7 minutes for soft-boiled eggs.
Transfer eggs to ice water immediately and let cool for 5 minutes, then gently peel.
Combine soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and water in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Bring marinade to a boil, stirring to dissolve sugar, then remove from heat and let cool.
Place peeled eggs in a container or zip-lock bag.
Pour cooled marinade over eggs, ensuring they are fully submerged.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight for best flavor.
Cut eggs in half to serve and drizzle with extra marinade if desired.
cheapTips: Buy eggs in bulk and make multiple batches
Use regular soy sauce instead of premium brands

recipes.name: Pho Lanh
recipes.description: Vietnamese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat beef broth in a pot over medium-high heat.
Slice onion in half, and add to broth along with sliced ginger, star anise, and cinnamon stick.
Simmer broth for 15 minutes to infuse flavors, then strain out spices.
Thinly slice beef sirloin against the grain.
Cook rice noodles according to package directions, drain, and chill in cold water.
Season broth with fish sauce and let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Divide chilled noodles and beef into bowls and pour cold broth over top.
Serve with fresh mint, cilantro, lime wedges, and sliced jalapeño on the side.
cheapTips: Buy beef broth in bulk or make your own stock
Use cheaper beef cuts and slice thinly for tenderness

recipes.name: Beef with Broccoli
recipes.description: Chinese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice beef sirloin into thin strips and toss with cornstarch, 1 tablespoon soy sauce, and set aside.
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling salted water for 3 minutes, then drain.
Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Cook beef in batches for 2-3 minutes per batch until browned, then remove and set aside.
Add remaining oil and stir-fry minced garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Return broccoli to the pan and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return beef to the pan and add soy sauce, oyster sauce, water, and sesame oil.
Stir everything together and cook for 2 minutes until sauce thickens, then serve over rice.
cheapTips: Buy beef when on sale and freeze for later use
Buy broccoli at farmers markets for cheaper prices

recipes.name: Singapore Mei Fun
recipes.description: Chinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak rice vermicelli noodles in warm water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Beat eggs in a small bowl and set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over high heat and scramble eggs, then remove.
Add remaining oil and stir-fry minced garlic and diced onion for 1 minute.
Add shrimp and cook until pink, about 2 minutes, then add diced carrots and cook 1 minute more.
Sprinkle curry powder over the ingredients and stir for 30 seconds to coat.
Add drained noodles and soy sauce, tossing constantly for 2-3 minutes.
Add scrambled eggs back and toss with chopped scallions, then serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp which is cheaper than fresh
Use eggs as the main protein instead of additional shrimp

recipes.name: Szechuan Shrimp
recipes.description: Chinese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, and chili oil in a bowl to make sauce.
Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add minced garlic, ginger, and Szechuan peppercorns, stirring for 30 seconds.
Add shrimp to the wok and cook for 2-3 minutes until they begin to turn pink.
Pour sauce over shrimp and toss constantly for 1-2 minutes.
Add chopped scallions and stir for another 30 seconds.
Serve immediately over steamed rice or with steamed vegetables on the side.
cheapTips: Buy shrimp when on sale and freeze for future use
Make your own chili oil to save money versus bottled versions

recipes.name: Cashew Chicken
recipes.description: Chinese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut chicken breast into bite-sized pieces and toss with cornstarch and 1 tablespoon soy sauce.
Toast cashews in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, shaking frequently, then set aside.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over high heat and cook chicken in batches until golden, then remove.
Add remaining oil and stir-fry minced garlic for 30 seconds.
Add diced onion and bell pepper, cooking for 2 minutes until softened.
Return chicken to the wok and add remaining soy sauce and oyster sauce.
Add toasted cashews and toss everything together for 1 minute.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve over steamed rice.
cheapTips: Buy cashews in bulk at warehouse stores for significant savings
Use chicken thighs instead of breast for a more budget-friendly option

recipes.name: Nopales
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Trim the spines and bumps from the nopales with a sharp knife and rinse thoroughly.
Dice the cleaned nopales into 1/4-inch pieces and place in a large pot of boiling salted water.
Add half the onion and garlic to the pot and boil for 12 minutes until tender, then drain well.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and sauté the remaining diced onion and jalapeño for 2 minutes.
Add the cooked nopales to the skillet and cook for 3 minutes, stirring frequently.
Remove from heat and stir in cilantro, lime juice, and salt to taste.
Serve warm as a side dish or salad.
cheapTips: Buy nopales in season at Mexican markets for better prices
Use dried nopales if fresh are unavailable and less expensive

recipes.name: Hongos
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean mushrooms with a damp cloth and slice them into 1/4-inch pieces.
Mince garlic, dice jalapeños, and chop onion into small pieces.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add onion and garlic, sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms and jalapeños, cook for 8 minutes stirring occasionally until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown.
Season with salt to taste and stir in cilantro and lime juice.
Serve warm with tortillas or as a side dish.
cheapTips: Buy regular white or cremini mushrooms instead of specialty varieties
Purchase mushrooms loose rather than packaged for better pricing

recipes.name: Frijoles Refritos
recipes.description: Mexican breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Drain and rinse the canned pinto beans under cold water.
Dice the onion and jalapeño, and mince the garlic.
Heat lard or oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion and garlic, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add beans to the skillet and mash them with a potato masher while cooking, breaking them into a thick paste, about 5 minutes.
Stir in jalapeño, cumin, salt, and black pepper.
Continue cooking and stirring for 3 more minutes until beans are fully combined and creamy.
Serve warm with tortillas or as a breakfast side.
cheapTips: Use store-brand canned beans to reduce costs significantly
Cook dried beans in bulk and freeze portions for even better savings

recipes.name: Huevos Revueltos
recipes.description: Mexican breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice onion, jalapeño, and tomato into small pieces.
Crack eggs into a bowl and whisk them together with salt and black pepper until combined.
Heat butter or oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat until melted.
Add diced onion and jalapeño to the skillet and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in whisked eggs and let them sit for 10 seconds, then gently push the eggs around the pan with a spatula, cooking until barely set but still slightly wet, about 3-4 minutes.
Add diced tomato and cilantro during the last minute of cooking.
Serve immediately while eggs are still moist.
cheapTips: Buy eggs in bulk or use store-brand options
Chop your own vegetables rather than buying pre-cut

recipes.name: Chorizo y Huevos
recipes.description: Mexican breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Remove chorizo from casing and crumble it into small pieces.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and add crumbled chorizo without additional oil.
Cook chorizo for 5-6 minutes, breaking it up as it cooks and stirring frequently, until browned.
Dice onion and jalapeño, then add to the skillet with chorizo and cook for 1 minute.
Crack eggs directly into the skillet with the chorizo and gently scramble together with a spatula.
Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until eggs are fully cooked but still tender.
Season with salt and black pepper, garnish with cilantro, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy chorizo on sale and freeze it in portions
Use store-brand chorizo for better value

recipes.name: Papas con Chorizo
recipes.description: Mexican breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel potatoes and cut them into 1/2-inch cubes, then rinse under cold water to remove starch.
Remove chorizo from casing and crumble into small pieces.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and add diced onion and garlic.
Add crumbled chorizo to the skillet and cook for 3 minutes until starting to brown.
Add potato cubes and cook for 15-18 minutes, stirring frequently, until potatoes are tender and slightly crispy at the edges.
Add diced jalapeño during the last 2 minutes of cooking.
Season with salt and black pepper, and serve hot with warm tortillas.
cheapTips: Buy potatoes in bulk bags for much better pricing
Make this dish when chorizo is on sale and freeze portions

recipes.name: Sesos
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak brains in cold water for 30 minutes, then carefully remove the thin outer membrane under running water.
Place cleaned brains in a pot of boiling salted water with half the onion and 1 garlic clove and boil for 15 minutes.
Drain brains and cut them into small pieces.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and sauté diced onion and remaining garlic for 1 minute.
Add brain pieces and diced jalapeños to the skillet and cook for 5 minutes, stirring gently.
Season with salt and squeeze lime juice over the dish.
Stir in cilantro and serve immediately with warm tortillas.
cheapTips: Buy brains from local butcher shops rather than supermarkets for better prices
This is an organ meat that is often very affordable and nutritious

recipes.name: Albóndigas
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a bowl, combine ground beef, bread crumbs, egg, minced half the onion, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Form the mixture into 1-inch balls and set aside.
Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Carefully place meatballs into the hot oil and brown them on all sides for about 5 minutes, working in batches if needed.
Remove meatballs and set aside, then sauté remaining diced onion for 1 minute.
Pour in tomato sauce and beef broth, stirring to combine.
Return meatballs to the pot, reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until sauce thickens.
Serve hot with rice or in a warm broth bowl.
cheapTips: Use ground beef that's on sale and freeze portions
Make a larger batch and freeze unbaked meatballs for quick meals later

recipes.name: Asador
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat steak dry and season both sides generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat a grill or grill pan over high heat until very hot.
Place steak on the grill and cook for 5-6 minutes per side for medium-rare, adjusting time based on thickness.
While steak cooks, char jalapeños and onion slices on the grill for 3-4 minutes until slightly blackened.
In a small bowl, mash minced garlic with cilantro, lime juice, and salt to make a paste.
Remove steak from heat and let rest for 3 minutes.
Slice steak against the grain into strips and arrange on a plate with grilled vegetables.
Top with cilantro-garlic paste and serve immediately with warm tortillas.
cheapTips: Buy skirt steak when on sale and freeze in portions
Check warehouse stores for bulk meat pricing

recipes.name: Croque Madame
recipes.description: French lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Spread Dijon mustard on one side of each bread slice.
Layer 2 slices of bread mustard-side up, then add ham and cheese on each slice, then top with second bread slice mustard-side down.
Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place sandwiches in the skillet and cook for 3-4 minutes until golden brown on the bottom, pressing gently with a spatula.
Flip sandwiches carefully and cook the other side for 2-3 minutes until cheese melts and bread is golden.
Remove sandwiches from skillet and set aside on a plate.
Add remaining butter to the skillet and crack eggs into it, cooking sunny-side up for 2-3 minutes.
Place one fried egg on top of each sandwich, season with salt and pepper, and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use Swiss or cheddar cheese instead of Gruyère for substantial savings
Buy deli meat on sale and slice your own ham from a whole piece

recipes.name: Seafood Linguine
recipes.description: Italian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook linguine until al dente, about 9 minutes.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and sauté minced garlic and red pepper flakes for 30 seconds.
Add clams to the skillet, pour in white wine, cover, and cook for 3-4 minutes until clams open.
Add shrimp and cook uncovered for 2 minutes, then stir in crushed tomatoes and simmer for 3 minutes.
Drain pasta and add to the skillet, tossing gently to combine with seafood and sauce.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp and clams to save 30-40%
Use canned tomatoes instead of fresh for year-round affordability

recipes.name: Hiyamen
recipes.description: Japanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook ramen noodles according to package directions, then drain and rinse under cold water until chilled.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, mirin, rice vinegar, and water to make the dipping sauce.
Slice cucumber into thin matchsticks and cut ham into strips.
Boil an egg for 6-7 minutes for a soft-boiled yolk, then cool in ice water and peel.
Fill two bowls with ice cubes and place chilled noodles on top.
Arrange cucumber, ham, and halved egg on the noodles, sprinkle sesame seeds, and serve with dipping sauce on the side.
cheapTips: Use instant ramen to cut costs by 50%
Substitute egg with tofu for extra savings

recipes.name: Zaru Soba
recipes.description: Japanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to boil and cook soba noodles according to package directions, about 4 minutes.
Drain noodles and rinse thoroughly under cold running water until cooled.
In a small saucepan, combine dashi, soy sauce, and mirin, then heat through and let cool slightly.
Finely grate daikon radish and slice scallions into thin rounds.
Cut nori into thin strips.
Fill bowls with ice and arrange noodles on top in a bundle.
Serve with dipping sauce on the side, topped with wasabi, grated daikon, scallions, nori, and sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Make dashi from scratch with kombu and bonito flakes for 1/3 the cost
Buy daikon and radish when on sale and store in the fridge

recipes.name: Hiyashi Chuka
recipes.description: Japanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil chicken breast in salted water for 12 minutes, then cool, slice thinly, and set aside.
Cook ramen noodles according to package directions, drain, rinse under cold water, and chill.
In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, mirin, rice vinegar, and dashi to make the sauce.
Boil eggs for 6-7 minutes, cool in ice water, peel, and halve.
Slice cucumber into thin matchsticks and cut ham into strips.
Divide chilled noodles between two bowls and arrange chicken, cucumber, egg, and ham on top.
Drizzle sauce over noodles and garnish with sesame seeds.
cheapTips: Use rotisserie chicken instead of boiling for convenience
Buy eggs on sale and store long-term

recipes.name: Bibim Naengmyeon
recipes.description: Korean lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to boil and cook buckwheat noodles according to package directions, about 5 minutes.
Drain noodles and rinse under cold water until completely chilled.
In a small bowl, whisk together gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and sugar to make the sauce.
Pan-fry thinly sliced beef in a hot skillet for 2-3 minutes per side, season with salt and pepper, and set aside.
Blanch fresh spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, squeeze dry, and toss with a pinch of salt and sesame oil.
Boil eggs for 6-7 minutes, cool, peel, and halve.
Divide noodles between bowls, arrange beef, spinach, cucumber matchsticks, and egg on top, then drizzle sauce over and toss well before eating.
cheapTips: Use ground beef instead of sirloin to save 40%
Buy gochujang in bulk Asian markets for half the price

recipes.name: Jjamppong
recipes.description: Korean lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat sesame oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and sauté minced garlic and chopped onion until softened.
Add gochugaru and gochujang, stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil, then add soy sauce.
Add squid and mussels to the broth and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add shrimp and cook for another 2 minutes until shrimp are pink.
Cook ramen noodles according to package directions and divide among bowls.
Ladle seafood and broth over noodles, garnish with scallions, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy frozen seafood mix to save 30-50%
Use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth for a vegetarian version

recipes.name: Liang Pi
recipes.description: Chinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: If using wheat starch dough, steam thin sheets for 2 minutes, then cool and cut into wide noodles; if using rice paper, soften in water and cut into strips.
In a bowl, mix soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, chili oil, minced garlic, and water to make the sauce.
Julienne cucumber and slice scallions thinly.
Place noodles in serving bowls and arrange cucumber and scallions on top.
Pour sauce over noodles and garnish with sesame seeds.
Toss well before eating and serve at room temperature or chilled.
cheapTips: Use pre-made rice paper wrappers to save time and cost
Buy sesame oil from bulk or Asian markets for 50% savings

recipes.name: Maozi
recipes.description: Chinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook egg noodles according to package directions, drain, and rinse under cold water until chilled.
In a small bowl, whisk together peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, minced garlic, and water until smooth.
Julienne cucumber and slice scallions thinly.
Divide chilled noodles between two bowls.
Pour peanut sauce over noodles and toss well to coat.
Top with cucumber, scallions, and crushed peanuts, then serve.
cheapTips: Use store-brand peanut butter to save 30%
Buy cucumber and scallions at farmer's markets for fresh deals

recipes.name: Liangmian
recipes.description: Chinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook wheat noodles according to package directions, drain, and rinse under cold water until completely cooled.
In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, chili oil, minced garlic, and water to make the sauce.
Julienne cucumber and carrot into thin matchsticks.
Place noodles in serving bowls and arrange cucumber and carrot on top.
Pour sauce over noodles and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Toss well before eating and serve immediately at room temperature.
cheapTips: Buy carrots and cucumbers in bulk when in season and store in the fridge
Make your own chili oil by steeping chili flakes in oil

recipes.name: Bánh Chưng
recipes.description: Vietnamese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak glutinous rice in water for 30 minutes, then drain and cook in fresh water until sticky and tender, about 20 minutes.
Boil pork belly with salt and black pepper for 15 minutes until partially cooked, then cut into cubes.
Mix cooked rice with cooked pork, minced garlic, fish sauce, and salt to combine.
Blanch banana leaves briefly in boiling water to soften them, then pat dry.
Place a banana leaf square on work surface, add a layer of rice mixture in the center, then a spoonful of mung bean paste, then more rice mixture.
Fold banana leaf corners over filling to form a square parcel, then wrap another banana leaf around it and tie with string.
Boil parcels in water for 45 minutes until the rice is fully cooked through and holds together.
Cool slightly before unwrapping and serving with fish sauce dipping sauce.
cheapTips: Buy glutinous rice in bulk Asian markets for 50% less than regular stores
Use canned mung bean paste instead of homemade to save significant time

recipes.name: Laksa Lemak
recipes.description: Malaysian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to boil and cook rice noodles according to package directions, then drain and set aside.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté laksa paste, garlic, and ginger for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add coconut milk and chicken broth to the pot and bring to a simmer.
Add cubed chicken and cook for 8 minutes until nearly cooked through.
Stir in green beans, shrimp, fish sauce, and lime juice, then simmer for 5 minutes until shrimp is pink.
While the curry simmers, boil eggs in a separate pot for 6-7 minutes for soft-boiled eggs, then peel and halve them.
Divide cooked noodles among four bowls and ladle laksa broth with chicken and shrimp over top.
Garnish each bowl with egg halves and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy laksa paste in bulk at Asian markets; use frozen shrimp instead of fresh to save money

recipes.name: Dopiaza
recipes.description: Indian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook diced onion from 2 onions until golden, about 8 minutes, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add chicken pieces and cook until browned on all sides, about 6 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Add remaining diced onion to the pan and sauté for 3 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomato paste, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chili powder, cooking for 2 minutes while stirring constantly.
Return chicken to the pan and add coconut milk, then simmer for 15 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the reserved golden onions and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve over rice with the sauce.
cheapTips: Buy chicken on sale and freeze; use canned tomato paste instead of fresh tomatoes

recipes.name: Dhansak
recipes.description: Indian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse red lentils thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown chicken pieces on all sides, about 6 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic, ginger, tomato paste, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chili powder, cooking for 2 minutes.
Add lentils and chicken broth to the pot and bring to a boil.
Return chicken to the pot and reduce heat to low, then simmer covered for 30 minutes until lentils are soft and chicken is tender.
Mash some of the lentils against the side of the pot to thicken the sauce.
Season with salt and pepper and serve over rice.
cheapTips: Red lentils are very affordable; buy chicken thighs instead of breasts for better value

recipes.name: Phaal
recipes.description: Indian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Prepare hot peppers by removing stems and seeds if less heat is desired, then mince finely using gloves.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat and add cumin seeds, allowing them to pop for 30 seconds.
Add diced onions and cook until dark golden brown, about 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add minced garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in all minced hot peppers and tomato paste and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add cubed chicken and stir well to coat with the spice paste, cooking for 5 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and reduce heat to medium, then simmer for 20 minutes until chicken is fully cooked and sauce is thick.
Season with salt and serve with rice, yogurt, and plenty of water available.
cheapTips: Use habaneros instead of ghost peppers to reduce cost; buy peppers in season at farmer's markets

recipes.name: Madras
recipes.description: Indian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown chicken pieces on all sides, about 6 minutes, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add diced onions and cook until golden, about 6 minutes.
Add minced garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste, madras curry powder, turmeric, and chili powder, cooking for 2 minutes while stirring constantly.
Return chicken to the pan and add coconut milk and chicken broth.
Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 20 minutes until chicken is cooked through and sauce has thickened slightly.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve over steamed rice.
cheapTips: Make your own madras powder blend; buy chicken breasts on sale and freeze

recipes.name: Jalfrezi
recipes.description: Indian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat and cook diced chicken until browned on all sides, about 6 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pan and cook until softened, about 4 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add cumin, coriander, chili powder, and turmeric and cook for 1 minute while stirring.
Return chicken to the pan and add diced tomatoes and bell pepper slices.
Stir well and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until chicken is cooked through and peppers are tender-crisp.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot over rice or with naan bread.
cheapTips: Use whatever bell peppers are on sale; fresh tomatoes can be replaced with canned diced tomatoes

recipes.name: Karahi
recipes.description: Pakistani dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large karahi or thick-bottomed skillet over high heat until very hot.
Add chicken pieces and cook until browned on all sides, about 8 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Add onion chunks to the karahi and cook until lightly browned, about 4 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add coriander powder, cumin, and chili powder and cook for 1 minute while stirring.
Return chicken to the karahi and add diced tomatoes and bell pepper chunks.
Cook over high heat for 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through and most liquid has evaporated.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and season with salt and pepper, then serve immediately in the karahi or on a platter.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs instead of breasts for juicier results at lower cost; fresh cilantro from dollar stores

recipes.name: Phal
recipes.description: Indian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Wear gloves and carefully prepare hot peppers by removing stems and seeds, then mince very finely.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and cook diced onions until deep golden brown, about 12 minutes.
Add minced garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute until very fragrant.
Stir in all minced hot peppers and tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add cubed chicken and stir thoroughly to coat with the spice paste, cooking for 5 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and reduce heat to medium, then simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until chicken is tender and sauce is thick.
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking and ensure even cooking.
Season with salt and serve with rice and yogurt to cool the heat.
cheapTips: Buy peppers when in season; habaneros are cheaper than scotch bonnets at most markets

recipes.name: Gaeng Hang Lay
recipes.description: Thai dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown pork cubes on all sides, about 8 minutes, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, add red curry paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in 1 can of coconut milk slowly, stirring to combine with the curry paste.
Return pork to the pot and add the second can of coconut milk, then bring to a simmer.
Add sliced ginger, minced garlic, sliced shallots, fish sauce, and palm sugar, stirring well.
Add cubed potatoes and simmer covered for 30 minutes until pork is tender and potatoes are cooked through.
Stir in lime juice and adjust seasoning with more fish sauce or sugar if needed.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve over jasmine rice.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder on sale and freeze; make red curry paste at home with dried chilies

recipes.name: Al Pastor
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Remove stems and seeds from dried chilies and soak in hot water for 10 minutes until softened.
Blend soaked chilies with garlic, onion, cumin, oregano, vinegar, and 0.5 cup soaking water until a smooth paste forms.
Strain the paste through a fine mesh strainer if a smoother texture is desired.
Toss pork slices with the chili paste until well coated and let marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat and cook marinated pork in batches until crispy and caramelized, about 4-5 minutes per batch.
Return all cooked pork to the skillet and add diced pineapple, cooking for 3 minutes to warm through and combine flavors.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet or over a flame for 30 seconds per side.
Serve al pastor pork in tortillas garnished with cilantro and lime wedges.
cheapTips: Use frozen pineapple instead of fresh; buy pork shoulder on sale and slice yourself

recipes.name: Pad Phed Ped Yang
recipes.description: Thai dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and add curry paste, stirring for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk slowly while stirring to combine with the curry paste into a smooth sauce.
Shred the rotisserie chicken into bite-sized pieces and add to the pan.
Stir in fish sauce and brown sugar, then add diced red peppers and bamboo shoots.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes until peppers are tender and sauce thickens slightly.
Remove from heat and fold in fresh basil just before serving.
Serve over jasmine rice.
cheapTips: Use rotisserie chicken to save time and money versus buying raw chicken breasts.
Buy curry paste and coconut milk at an Asian market for 40% less than mainstream groceries.

recipes.name: Chicken Satay Stir-fry
recipes.description: Indonesian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut chicken breast into 1-inch cubes and set aside.
In a small bowl, whisk together peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, minced garlic, red pepper flakes, coconut milk, and brown sugar until smooth.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat and cook chicken cubes until golden on all sides, about 8 minutes, then remove to a plate.
Add remaining oil to the pan and stir-fry sliced bell peppers and onion until just tender-crisp, about 4 minutes.
Return chicken to the pan and pour in the peanut sauce, tossing everything to coat evenly.
Cook for 3-4 minutes more until sauce thickens and coats the chicken.
Serve over steamed rice.
cheapTips: Make your own satay sauce with pantry staples instead of buying pre-made sauce packets.
Buy chicken when on sale and freeze for later use.

recipes.name: Vietnamese Shaking Beef
recipes.description: Vietnamese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut beef into 1-inch cubes and pat dry with paper towels.
Combine soy sauce, fish sauce, lime juice, minced garlic, and sugar in a small bowl to make the sauce.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat until very hot and smoking slightly.
Cook beef cubes in batches until browned on all sides but rare inside, about 4-5 minutes total, then remove to a plate.
In the same pan, add remaining oil and quickly cook sliced shallots and red onion until softened, about 2 minutes.
Return beef to the pan, pour in the sauce, and shake the pan vigorously for 1-2 minutes to coat everything (this is where the dish gets its name).
Season with black pepper and serve immediately over lettuce or with steamed rice.
cheapTips: Use sirloin instead of pricier cuts like tenderloin for the same great results.
Buy beef on sale and freeze for meal prep.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Chicken Fajitas
recipes.description: Mexican dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F and line a large sheet pan with parchment paper.
Slice chicken breasts into 0.5-inch thick strips and cut bell peppers and onion into 0.5-inch wide strips.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, peppers, and onion with olive oil, lime juice, cumin, chili powder, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Spread everything in a single layer on the prepared sheet pan.
Roast for 18-22 minutes until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender with some charred edges.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet or over a gas flame for 30 seconds per side.
Serve fajita mixture with warm tortillas and desired toppings (sour cream, salsa, guacamole, cilantro).
cheapTips: Buy chicken on sale and freeze; bell peppers are cheapest at warehouse clubs.
Skip restaurant-quality sides and use basic toppings like lime, cilantro, and hot sauce from home.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Salmon with Vegetables
recipes.description: American dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F and line a large sheet pan with parchment paper.
Toss broccoli, cherry tomatoes, and sliced zucchini with 2 tablespoons olive oil, minced garlic, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on the sheet pan and roast for 8 minutes.
Create four small spaces among the vegetables and place salmon fillets skin-side down, then drizzle with remaining olive oil and season with salt, pepper, and thin lemon slices.
Roast for 12-14 minutes until salmon flakes easily with a fork and vegetables are tender.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over everything before serving.
cheapTips: Buy salmon when on sale and freeze; check for farm-raised salmon which is cheaper than wild.
Use frozen broccoli instead of fresh to save 30-40%.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Sausage and Peppers
recipes.description: Italian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F and line a large sheet pan with parchment paper.
Cut sausage links in half and slice bell peppers and onion into 1-inch strips.
Toss sausage, peppers, and onion with olive oil, minced garlic, basil, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Spread in a single layer on the sheet pan and roast for 15 minutes until sausage is cooked through.
Drizzle marinara sauce over everything and toss gently to combine.
Roast for an additional 3-4 minutes until sauce is warm.
Serve on Italian rolls or over pasta.
cheapTips: Buy sausage in bulk packs when on sale and freeze individual portions.
Use store-brand marinara sauce instead of premium brands for equal quality at 30% less cost.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Teriyaki Chicken
recipes.description: Japanese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F and line a large sheet pan with parchment paper.
Whisk together soy sauce, mirin, rice vinegar, minced garlic, and grated ginger in a small bowl.
Pat chicken thighs dry and place on the sheet pan, then pour half the teriyaki sauce over them.
Roast chicken for 15 minutes, then toss broccoli with olive oil and add to the pan around the chicken.
Pour remaining teriyaki sauce over broccoli and roast for 12-15 minutes more until chicken is cooked through and broccoli is tender.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and sliced green onions before serving.
Serve over steamed rice.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs instead of breast—they are cheaper and more flavorful.
Make teriyaki sauce from scratch with soy sauce and brown sugar instead of buying bottled sauce.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Shrimp Scampi
recipes.description: Italian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F and line a large sheet pan with parchment paper.
Arrange trimmed asparagus and cherry tomatoes on the sheet pan.
Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat and add minced garlic and red pepper flakes, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in white wine and lemon juice, then remove from heat.
Place shrimp on the sheet pan with vegetables and pour the garlic-butter mixture over everything, then season with salt and pepper.
Roast for 12-15 minutes until shrimp is pink and cooked through.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve over pasta or with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp instead of fresh—it's cheaper and lasts longer.
Use budget asparagus or green beans as a substitute for premium asparagus.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Steak Fajitas
recipes.description: Mexican dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 450°F and line a large sheet pan with parchment paper.
Slice steak thinly against the grain and cut bell peppers and onion into strips.
Whisk together olive oil, lime juice, Worcestershire sauce, cumin, chili powder, and garlic powder.
Toss steak and vegetables with the marinade and season with salt and pepper.
Spread on the sheet pan in a single layer and roast for 12-15 minutes, stirring halfway through, until steak is cooked to your liking and vegetables are tender.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side.
Serve steak and vegetable mixture with warm tortillas and toppings (sour cream, salsa, cilantro, guacamole).
cheapTips: Choose flank steak over pricier cuts like ribeye—it's more flavorful and affordable for this preparation.
Buy store-brand tortillas and toppings to reduce costs.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Roasted Vegetables
recipes.description: American lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F and line a large sheet pan with parchment paper.
Chop all vegetables into 1-inch pieces and place in a large bowl.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with garlic powder, paprika, thyme, salt, and pepper, then toss until all vegetables are evenly coated.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on the sheet pan.
Roast for 22-25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until vegetables are tender and edges are lightly caramelized.
Drizzle with balsamic vinegar and toss gently.
Serve warm as a side dish or cool and use in salads, grain bowls, or wraps.
