Meanwhile, cook rice noodles in a separate pot of boiling water according to package directions, then drain and divide between two bowls.
Add soy sauce, white pepper, and salt to the hot broth and stir to combine.
Pour the hot broth with cooked meat over the noodles in each bowl.
Slice green onions and sprinkle over the soup along with fresh cilantro.
Drizzle sesame oil over each bowl and serve immediately while steaming hot.
cheapTips: Make your own broth by simmering chicken or pork bones overnight
Buy rice noodles in bulk from Asian markets

recipes.name: Aloo Bhaat
recipes.description: Maharashtrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Wash and soak basmati rice for 15 minutes, then drain.
Cut potatoes into small cubes and finely chop onions and green chilies.
Heat oil in a pot and add mustard seeds until they splutter.
Add curry leaves, onions, and green chilies, then sauté until onions turn golden.
Add potato cubes and turmeric powder, stir well and cook for 3 minutes.
Add drained rice to the pot and stir continuously for 2 minutes.
Pour water, add salt, and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes until rice and potatoes are fully cooked and water is absorbed.
cheapTips: Buy rice and potatoes in bulk from warehouse stores
Use basic mustard seeds and curry leaves which are inexpensive

recipes.name: Dal Bhaat
recipes.description: Maharashtrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Wash rice and lentils separately under running water and drain.
Heat oil in a large pot and add mustard seeds until they crackle.
Add curry leaves, chopped onions, and green chilies, sauté until onions soften.
Add diced tomato, turmeric powder, and salt, then cook for 2 minutes.
Add washed lentils and rice to the pot, stir well.
Pour water and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 18-20 minutes until lentils and rice are soft and water is absorbed.
Stir gently with a fork to fluff the mixture and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy lentils in bulk from Indian grocery stores or online
Purchase rice in large quantities for better value

recipes.name: Pitla
recipes.description: Maharashtrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan and add mustard seeds until they splutter.
Add chopped onions and green chilies, sauté until onions turn golden brown.
Add turmeric powder and asafetida, then stir quickly.
Add gram flour slowly while stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Pour water gradually while stirring to create a smooth, thick batter.
Continue cooking and stirring constantly for 8-10 minutes until the mixture thickens and becomes pale.
Add salt and chopped cilantro, then mix well.
Cook for another 2 minutes until the pitla becomes crumbly and slightly moist but not runny.
cheapTips: Gram flour is inexpensive at Indian stores or bulk sections
Use basic pantry staples like onions and oil

recipes.name: Shrikhand
recipes.description: Maharashtrian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Hang plain yogurt in a cheesecloth for 2-3 hours or overnight to remove whey.
Crush cardamom pods and extract the seeds, then grind into fine powder.
Soak saffron strands in 2 tablespoons of warm milk for 5 minutes.
Slice almonds and pistachios into thin strips, then roast them lightly in ghee.
In a bowl, combine hung yogurt, sugar, cardamom powder, and saffron with milk.
Whisk vigorously until smooth and creamy, then divide into serving bowls.
Top each bowl with roasted nuts and a few strands of saffron.
cheapTips: Make hung yogurt from store-bought plain yogurt instead of buying it
Skip saffron or use a pinch to reduce cost

recipes.name: Sabudana Khichdi
recipes.description: Maharashtrian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak sabudana in water for 30 minutes until each pearl swells and becomes translucent, then drain.
Cut potatoes into small cubes and roast peanuts lightly in a dry pan.
Heat oil in a large pan and add cumin seeds until fragrant.
Add finely chopped onion and green chili, sauté until onion softens.
Add potato cubes and turmeric powder, stir and cook for 5 minutes.
Add drained sabudana and roasted peanuts, mix well and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add salt to taste and sprinkle cilantro, then stir gently.
cheapTips: Buy sabudana and peanuts in bulk from warehouse stores
Use regular potatoes which are very affordable

recipes.name: Jhunka Bhakri
recipes.description: Maharashtrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine cornmeal, wheat flour, and gram flour in a bowl, then mix well.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a pan and add chopped onions and green chilies, sauté until golden.
Add the flour mixture, turmeric powder, and salt to the pan, then toast for 2-3 minutes on low heat while stirring.
Gradually add water while stirring continuously to avoid lumps, creating a thick crumbly texture.
Cook the jhunka for 5-7 minutes on medium heat, stirring often until cooked through.
Add cilantro and cook for 1 more minute, then remove from heat.
For bhakri, knead remaining wheat flour with water and salt to form a stiff dough.
Roll dough between plastic into thin circles, cook on a hot griddle for 1-2 minutes per side until puffed and cooked.
cheapTips: Buy flours in bulk from Indian stores or warehouse clubs
Cornmeal and gram flour are economical staples

recipes.name: Kolhapuri Mutton
recipes.description: Maharashtrian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut mutton into medium pieces and clean thoroughly.
Dry roast coriander and cumin seeds, then grind to a fine powder.
Heat oil in a heavy pot and add sliced onions, cook until deeply browned.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute, then add tomatoes and cook until soft.
Add red chili powder and ground spices, then stir for 2 minutes on low heat.
Add mutton pieces and salt, sear on high heat for 3-4 minutes while stirring.
Grind coconut finely and add to the pot, pour water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer for 45-50 minutes until meat is completely tender, stirring occasionally.
cheapTips: Buy mutton from Indian or ethnic butcher shops for better prices
Use budget-friendly spices like red chili powder in bulk

recipes.name: Kombdi Vade
recipes.description: Maharashtrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Marinate chicken pieces in yogurt, turmeric, salt, and minced ginger-garlic for 30 minutes.
Soak rice and dal separately for 30 minutes, then drain.
Grind drained rice, dal, chopped onions, green chilies, and remaining ginger-garlic into a coarse paste.
Heat oil in a pan and add the ground paste, cooking for 5 minutes on low heat.
Mix marinated chicken into the paste, stirring well to coat evenly.
Shape the mixture into oval or round fritters on a wet palm.
Heat oil in a deep pan and carefully slide fritters into hot oil.
Fry on medium heat for 6-8 minutes until golden brown on all sides, turning gently, then drain on paper towels.
cheapTips: Buy whole chicken and portions it yourself for savings
Rice and dal are inexpensive protein sources

recipes.name: Surli
recipes.description: Maharashtrian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Crush cardamom pods and remove seeds, then grind to a fine powder.
Heat 2 tablespoons ghee in a pan and roast gram flour for 3-4 minutes on low heat, stirring constantly.
Add semolina and roast for another 2 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Heat remaining 2 tablespoons ghee in the same pan and add cashews and raisins, fry until golden.
Add roasted flour mixture, grated coconut, and cardamom powder to the pan.
Crumble jaggery into the mixture while stirring continuously.
Cook for 3-4 minutes on low heat until all ingredients are well combined and heated through.
Spread on a plate to cool slightly, then shape into small balls or diamonds when cool enough to handle.
cheapTips: Buy jaggery and gram flour in bulk from Indian stores
Grate fresh coconut at home instead of buying pre-grated

recipes.name: Chikali
recipes.description: Maharashtrian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat ghee in a heavy pan and add rice flour, toast on low heat for 4-5 minutes while stirring constantly.
In a separate pan, heat water and dissolve jaggery over low heat, stirring until completely melted.
Crush cardamom pods and remove seeds, then grind to a fine powder.
Pour jaggery liquid into the toasted flour mixture, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Add roasted peanuts, sesame seeds, cardamom powder, and salt, then mix well.
Cook the mixture on low heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly until it thickens and comes together.
Spread on a greased plate while still warm and cut into squares or diamonds when cool.
cheapTips: Buy rice flour and sesame seeds in bulk from grocery stores
Use budget jaggery from Indian or ethnic markets

recipes.name: Chettinad Fish Curry
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast coriander and cumin seeds in a dry pan for 1 minute until fragrant.
Soak dried red chilies in warm water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Blend toasted spices, soaked chilies, garlic, ginger, and 2 tbsp coconut milk into a smooth paste.
Heat coconut oil in a heavy pan and add chopped onions, cook until golden brown.
Stir in the spice paste and cook for 2-3 minutes until raw smell disappears.
Add turmeric powder and curry leaves, then pour in remaining coconut milk and stir well.
Gently place fish fillets into the curry and simmer for 8-10 minutes until fish is cooked through.
Season with salt to taste and serve hot with steamed rice.
cheapTips: Use frozen white fish instead of fresh to save 20-30%
Buy dried chilies and spices in bulk from Indian grocery stores

recipes.name: Karuvepilai Chicken
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut chicken breast into bite-sized pieces and set aside.
Slice onions thinly and mince garlic and green chilies.
Heat coconut oil in a large pan and temper with black mustard seeds until they pop.
Add curry leaves and immediately stir in minced garlic and ginger, cook for 1 minute.
Add sliced onions and cook until translucent and starting to turn golden.
Add turmeric powder, chili powder, and green chilies, stir constantly for 1 minute.
Add chicken pieces and cook on high heat for 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Pour in water, reduce heat to medium, and simmer covered for 15-20 minutes until chicken is fully cooked.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice or flatbread.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs instead of breast for more flavor and better price
Grow curry leaves at home or buy fresh bundles to use multiple times

recipes.name: Chettinad Prawn Curry
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast coriander and fennel seeds for 1 minute in a dry pan until aromatic.
Soak dried red chilies in warm water for 5 minutes and drain.
Blend toasted spices, soaked chilies, garlic, ginger, and 3 tbsp coconut milk into a smooth paste.
Heat coconut oil in a pan and sauté chopped onions until light golden brown.
Add the spice paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in turmeric powder, curry leaves, and tamarind paste, cook for 1 minute.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add prawns and cook for 5-6 minutes until they turn pink and opaque, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and serve with rice or naan.
cheapTips: Use frozen shrimp from warehouse stores for 30% savings
Replace tamarind paste with lemon juice for similar tanginess at lower cost

recipes.name: Chettinad Biryani
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut chicken into medium pieces and marinate in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, and turmeric for 15 minutes.
Slice 3 onions thinly; cut 1 onion into rings.
Soak basmati rice in water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Boil water in a large pot with bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves; add drained rice with salt and cook until 70% done, then drain.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot and fry onion slices until deep golden, remove and set aside.
In the same pot, heat remaining ghee and add marinated chicken, cook on high heat for 3 minutes while stirring.
Sprinkle half the fried onions over chicken, then layer half-cooked rice evenly on top.
Sprinkle remaining fried onions, then drizzle coconut milk over rice.
Cover tightly with foil then place lid on top, cook on high heat for 2 minutes until steam forms, then reduce to low heat for 20-25 minutes.
Turn off heat and let rest covered for 5 minutes, then gently mix with a fork and serve.
cheapTips: Use regular long-grain rice instead of basmati to cut cost in half
Buy whole spices in bulk and grind at home

recipes.name: Nandu Masala
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean crab and cut into quarters; rinse thoroughly under cold water.
Toast coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and black peppercorns in a dry pan for 1 minute.
Grind toasted spices with garlic, ginger, and 2 tbsp water into a smooth paste.
Heat coconut oil in a large pan and add chopped onions, cook until golden brown.
Add green chilies and curry leaves, stir for 30 seconds.
Add the ground spice paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring frequently.
Stir in chili powder and turmeric powder, cook for 1 minute.
Add crab pieces and cook on high heat for 3 minutes while stirring to coat with masala.
Pour in water, cover, and simmer for 12-15 minutes until crab is fully cooked and meat is tender.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice.
cheapTips: Buy frozen crab when on sale and store for later use
Use crab legs instead of whole crab for easier preparation

recipes.name: Chettinad Egg Curry
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Hard boil eggs for 10 minutes, then peel and cut into halves.
Toast coriander and cumin seeds in a dry pan for 1 minute until fragrant.
Blend toasted spices with garlic, ginger, green chilies, and 3 tbsp coconut milk into a paste.
Heat coconut oil in a pan and sauté chopped onions until golden brown.
Add the spice paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in turmeric powder, chili powder, and curry leaves, cook for 1 minute.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Gently add egg halves and simmer for 3-4 minutes to heat through.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice or dosa.
cheapTips: Buy eggs in bulk from wholesale stores
Reduce coconut milk by half and add water to stretch budget further

recipes.name: Thalippu Sadam
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat coconut oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add black mustard seeds and let them pop for about 30 seconds.
Add urad dal and cook until golden brown, about 1 minute.
Add dried red chilies and curry leaves, fry for 30 seconds.
Add chopped onions and cook until translucent, about 2 minutes.
Stir in peas and cashews, cook for 1 minute.
Add asafoetida powder and stir well.
Add cooked rice and mix gently but thoroughly, breaking up any lumps.
Season with salt to taste and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use leftover rice from previous meals to make this instantly
Skip cashews and use peanuts for half the cost

recipes.name: Nattu Kozhi Roast
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and black peppercorns in a dry pan for 1 minute.
Grind toasted spices with garlic, ginger, and green chilies into a coarse paste.
Cut chicken thighs into medium pieces.
Heat coconut oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Add sliced onions and cook until caramelized, about 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the ground spice paste and cook for 2 minutes while stirring.
Stir in chili powder and turmeric powder, cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken pieces and curry leaves, cook on high heat for 5 minutes while stirring to coat thoroughly.
Reduce heat to medium-low and cook uncovered for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through and onions are deeply caramelized and crispy.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice or flatbread.
cheapTips: Use chicken leg quarters instead of thighs for better price
Caramelize extra onions in advance to save time

recipes.name: Kandhari Chicken
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast coriander seeds in a dry pan for 1 minute until aromatic.
Soak dried red chilies in warm water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Blend toasted coriander seeds, soaked chilies, garlic, and ginger into a smooth paste.
Cut chicken breast into bite-sized pieces.
Heat coconut oil in a pan and sauté chopped onions until golden brown.
Add the spice paste and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in turmeric powder and chili powder, cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken pieces and curry leaves, stir-fry for 5 minutes on high heat.
Pour in water, reduce heat to medium, cover and simmer for 12-15 minutes until chicken is fully cooked.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice or flatbread.
cheapTips: Buy chicken in bulk and freeze portions
Make double batch and freeze half for meal prep

recipes.name: Chettinad Parotta
recipes.description: Chettinad breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt in a bowl, then gradually add water to form a soft dough, knead for 5 minutes until smooth.
Cover dough with a damp cloth and let rest for 20 minutes.
Divide dough into 8 equal portions and shape into balls.
On an oiled surface, stretch one dough ball into a very thin rectangle about 12x8 inches.
Brush generously with ghee, then sprinkle finely chopped onion, green chili, curry leaves, and black cumin seeds.
Starting from one long edge, tightly roll the dough into a long rope, then coil it into a spiral and flatten slightly.
Repeat with remaining dough portions.
Heat a cast-iron griddle or skillet over medium-high heat.
Place one parotta on the griddle and cook for 2-3 minutes until golden spots appear, brush with ghee and flip.
Cook the other side for 2-3 minutes until golden and crispy, pressing gently with a spatula.
Serve hot with curry, sambar, or chutney.
cheapTips: Use butter instead of ghee to cut cost by 40%
Make dough in advance and store in refrigerator for up to 3 days

recipes.name: Akhoi
recipes.description: Assamese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat ghee in a large pan over medium heat.
Add jaggery and stir constantly until it melts completely and turns golden.
Add puffed rice, peanuts, and sesame seeds to the melted jaggery and mix quickly.
Sprinkle salt and ginger powder, stirring constantly to coat everything evenly.
Transfer the mixture onto a greased surface or parchment paper and press gently with a greased spatula.
Let it cool for 10 minutes until firm enough to handle.
Cut into squares or diamonds and serve once completely cooled.
cheapTips: Buy jaggery in bulk from Indian grocery stores
Use store-brand puffed rice instead of premium brands

recipes.name: Til Pitha
recipes.description: Assamese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons ghee in a pan and roast sesame seeds for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Add jaggery to the roasted sesame seeds and mix well, then cool this filling.
Mix rice flour with salt and 1 tablespoon ghee, then add water gradually to make a soft dough.
Divide dough into 8-10 balls and flatten each one with your palm.
Place a spoonful of sesame-jaggery filling in the center, fold edges, and seal into a ball.
Heat coconut oil in a deep pan to 350°F and fry the pithas until golden brown on all sides.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels before serving warm.
cheapTips: Make filling in larger batches and refrigerate
Use vegetable oil instead of coconut oil to save cost

recipes.name: Ghila Pitha
recipes.description: Assamese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix rice flour with salt in a bowl and slowly add warm water, whisking to avoid lumps until you get a smooth batter.
Heat ghee in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour 1/4 cup batter into the center and spread gently with the back of a spoon into a thin 6-inch circle.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the bottom is golden, then carefully flip and cook the other side.
Place some grated coconut and a teaspoon of jaggery on one half of the cooked pitha.
Fold the pitha in half over the filling and press gently.
Serve warm, repeating the process with remaining batter and filling.
cheapTips: Use unsweetened shredded coconut from bulk bins
Buy jaggery from Indian stores for better prices

recipes.name: Xandoh
recipes.description: Assamese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut chicken into medium pieces and set aside.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sauté sliced onions until golden brown, then add minced garlic and ginger, cooking for 1 minute.
Add chicken pieces and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally until lightly browned.
Add turmeric powder and mix well, then add chopped tomatoes and green chilies.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until chicken is tender, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, and serve hot with rice.
cheapTips: Buy bone-in chicken thighs on sale and freeze in portions
Use onions and garlic from discount bins

recipes.name: Arisa
recipes.description: Assamese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Wash and soak rice and moong dal separately in water for 30 minutes.
Drain both and grind separately to a fine paste using minimal water, creating thick creams.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat and add the rice paste.
Stir continuously for 5-7 minutes until the paste turns light golden and fragrant.
Add moong dal paste and continue stirring for another 5 minutes.
Gradually add milk while stirring to avoid lumps and cook until the mixture thickens.
Add jaggery, crushed cardamom pods, and ginger powder, stirring until well combined and creamy.
Serve hot in bowls, garnished with a drizzle of ghee if desired.
cheapTips: Buy rice and dal in bulk from Indian grocery stores
Use evaporated milk instead of regular milk to reduce cost

recipes.name: Muga Momos
recipes.description: Assamese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Make dough by mixing flour with water and a pinch of salt, knead until smooth, and rest for 15 minutes.
Grind chicken breast with onions, garlic, ginger, and green chilies to a fine paste.
Mix chicken filling with salt, pepper, cilantro, and sesame oil.
Roll dough thin and cut into 3-inch circles using a glass or cutter.
Place a teaspoon of filling on each circle, gather edges, and pleat to form a closed pouch.
Boil water in a large pot and place a steamer basket or colander over it.
Arrange momos on steamer, cover, and steam for 15-18 minutes until translucent.
Serve hot with chili sauce or dipping sauce made from soy sauce, garlic, and vinegar.
cheapTips: Make filling in bulk and freeze momos for later use
Buy chicken breast on sale and freeze in portions

recipes.name: Baghaar
recipes.description: Assamese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel bottle gourd and cut into medium pieces, discarding seeds.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat until shimmering.
Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds, letting them crackle and pop for 30 seconds.
Add dried red chilies and curry leaves, cooking for another 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds without browning.
Add gourd pieces, turmeric powder, and salt, stirring to coat evenly.
Add water, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until gourd is tender, stirring occasionally.
Serve hot as a side dish with rice or flatbread.
cheapTips: Buy bottle gourd in season when prices are lowest
Use vegetable oil instead of mustard oil to save money

recipes.name: Oopa Tenga
recipes.description: Assamese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut fish fillets into medium pieces and set aside.
Chop tomatoes, onions, and green chilies roughly.
Heat oil in a pan and add minced garlic and ginger, cooking for 1 minute.
Add chopped onions and cook until soft and translucent, about 3-4 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes and green chilies, cooking until tomatoes break down, about 5 minutes.
Add turmeric powder and salt, stirring well.
Add fish pieces and gently stir to coat with the sauce.
Pour water, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 12-15 minutes until fish is cooked through.
Serve hot with steamed rice.
cheapTips: Buy frozen fish fillets when on sale and use within 3 months
Use canned tomatoes instead of fresh to save money in off-season

recipes.name: Batata Vada
recipes.description: Maharashtrian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil potatoes until tender, peel, and mash them roughly with some texture remaining.
Add green chilies, ginger, salt, pepper, and turmeric to the mashed potatoes and mix well.
Shape mixture into 8-10 oval or round balls, about 2 inches in diameter.
Make batter by whisking gram flour, rice flour, and salt with water until you get a smooth, thick coating consistency.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F.
Dip each potato ball into the batter, coating evenly, and carefully place into the hot oil.
Fry 3-4 minutes per batch until golden brown and crispy on all sides.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels before serving hot with dry garlic chutney.
cheapTips: Use potatoes from bulk bins to save 30%
Make batter just before frying to avoid separation

recipes.name: Puran Poli
recipes.description: Maharashtrian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Boil chana dal with water and a pinch of salt for 15-20 minutes until very soft, then drain well.
Mash cooked dal into a smooth paste and set aside.
Grind jaggery and cardamom pods together into small pieces.
Mix mashed dal with jaggery pieces, 1 tablespoon ghee, and turmeric powder to make the filling.
Knead flour with water, salt, and 1 tablespoon ghee until you get a smooth, soft dough, and rest for 15 minutes.
Divide dough into 6 equal balls, roll each very thin between plastic wrap, and place filling in center.
Carefully seal edges and roll gently to distribute filling evenly without tearing.
Heat a cast-iron griddle or tawa over medium heat and cook poli for 2-3 minutes per side until light brown spots appear.
Brush with ghee while cooking and serve hot, folded or rolled.
cheapTips: Buy chana dal in bulk from Indian grocery stores
Make filling in advance and refrigerate up to 3 days

recipes.name: Pilliyar Pandi Curry
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast dried red chilies, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and peppercorns in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant, then grind to a coarse paste with 2 tablespoons water.
Heat coconut oil in a heavy-bottomed pot and fry sliced onions until golden brown, then add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the pork pieces and cook on high heat for 5 minutes, stirring to seal the meat on all sides.
Stir in the ground spice paste and cook for 2 minutes until the raw smell disappears.
Add chopped tomatoes and salt, then cook for 3 minutes until tomatoes soften.
Add water and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until pork is tender.
Uncover and simmer for another 5 minutes to reduce the gravy slightly until it coats the meat.
Taste and adjust salt and spices, then serve hot with rice or flatbread.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder on sale and freeze; it's often cheaper than other cuts
Toast and grind whole spices yourself instead of buying pre-ground to save 30-40%

recipes.name: Chettinad Appam
recipes.description: Chettinad breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak rice, urad dal, and fenugreek seeds together in water for 4 hours or overnight.
Drain well and grind to a smooth batter using a wet grinder or blender, adding water gradually to achieve a thick, slightly liquid consistency.
Add salt, crushed peppercorns, and cumin seeds to the batter and mix well.
Let the batter rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Heat an appam pan (or non-stick skillet) over medium heat and lightly oil each mold or the bottom.
Pour batter into the appam molds until three-quarters full and cook covered for 2-3 minutes until the bottom turns golden brown.
Flip carefully and cook the other side for 1-2 minutes until light brown.
Remove and serve warm with sambar, chutney, or curry.
cheapTips: Buy rice and urad dal in bulk from Indian grocery stores for 50% less
Make batter in large batches and refrigerate up to 2 days

recipes.name: Chettinad Vazhakkai Fry
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel plantains, cut lengthwise into thin strips, and soak in salt water for 10 minutes.
Drain plantain strips thoroughly with paper towels until dry.
Heat coconut oil in a large skillet over medium heat and add chana dal, urad dal, red chilies, and curry leaves, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add plantain strips and turmeric powder, then stir continuously for 8-10 minutes until golden and crispy.
Add grated coconut and salt, then cook for another 2 minutes while stirring.
Taste and adjust salt, then transfer to a serving plate and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy plantains in season (summer-fall) for 30% savings
Use frozen grated coconut instead of fresh to save time and money

recipes.name: Chettinad Dhal
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse toor dal thoroughly under running water until water runs clear, then add to a pot with turmeric powder and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes until dal is completely soft and mushy, stirring occasionally.
While dal cooks, toast dried red chilies, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and black peppercorns in a dry pan for 2 minutes and grind to a coarse powder.
Heat coconut oil in a small pan over medium heat and add curry leaves and asafetida, cooking for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour the seasoned oil into the cooked dal along with the ground spice powder and salt, stirring well to combine.
Simmer for 2-3 more minutes to infuse flavors, then serve hot with rice or flatbread.
cheapTips: Buy toor dal in 5-lb bags from Indian stores for lowest per-pound cost
Toast whole spices in bulk and store in airtight containers for a month

recipes.name: Murungai Keerai Stir Fry
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Separate murungai leaves from the woody stems by rubbing gently between your fingers; discard stems and rinse leaves thoroughly.
Heat coconut oil in a large skillet over medium heat and add black mustard seeds, letting them crackle for 20 seconds.
Add chana dal and dried red chilies, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chopped onion and cook for 2 minutes until translucent, then add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies.
Add turmeric powder and cook for 30 seconds, then add the murungai leaves and stir continuously for 4-5 minutes until leaves wilt completely.
Add salt to taste and cook for another 1-2 minutes until all moisture evaporates.
Serve hot as a side dish with rice, dhal, and sambar.
cheapTips: Buy drumstick leaves from Indian markets in spring-summer when in season and cheaper
Fresh leaves keep 3-4 days refrigerated; freeze extras in portions

recipes.name: Chettinad Puttu
recipes.description: Chettinad breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons ghee in a pan and fry cashews and raisins until golden brown, about 2 minutes, then set aside on a plate.
In the same pan, add remaining ghee and roast rice flour on medium heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly until light brown and fragrant.
Add grated coconut to the roasted flour and cook for 2 minutes while stirring.
Add water slowly while stirring continuously to avoid lumps, then cook for 2-3 minutes until the mixture thickens.
Remove from heat and add grated jaggery, crushed cardamom, salt, and the fried cashews and raisins, stirring well to combine.
While still warm, press the mixture into a cylindrical puttu mold or greased container to set, then allow to cool for 5-10 minutes.
Unmold and cut into 1-inch thick discs, then serve at room temperature or lightly warm.
cheapTips: Buy jaggery in bulk and store in a cool, dry place for 2-3 months
Use dried coconut instead of fresh and rehydrate for 50% cost savings

recipes.name: Chettinad Rasam
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dry roast black peppercorns, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, and dried red chilies in a pan for 2 minutes until fragrant, then grind coarsely.
Heat water in a pot and add chopped tomatoes and tamarind paste, bringing to a boil.
Reduce heat and add the ground spice powder and salt, then simmer for 8-10 minutes until tomatoes are soft.
Strain the rasam through a fine sieve or cheesecloth, pressing the pulp to extract maximum flavor, discarding solids.
Return the strained rasam to the pot and bring to a simmer over low heat.
Heat coconut oil in a small pan, add mustard seeds and let them crackle, then add curry leaves and asafetida for 30 seconds.
Pour the seasoned oil into the rasam and mix well, then serve hot in small bowls with rice.
cheapTips: Make tamarind paste from tamarind pods yourself for 60% savings
Buy whole spices and grind fresh for better flavor and cost

recipes.name: Kulambu
recipes.description: Chettinad lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Grind dried red chilies, coriander seeds, black peppercorns, and grated coconut together with 0.5 cup water to form a smooth paste.
Heat coconut oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and fry sliced onions until golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute, then add beef or mutton and cook until sealed on all sides, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the ground spice-coconut paste to the meat and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring continuously until the raw smell disappears.
Add chopped tomatoes and tamarind paste, then cook for 2-3 minutes until tomatoes soften.
Add water and salt, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-35 minutes until meat is tender.
Uncover and simmer for another 5 minutes to reduce the gravy slightly until it coats the meat.
Taste and adjust salt and spices, then serve hot with rice or with flatbread.
cheapTips: Buy meat on sale and portion into 1 lb servings before freezing
Make the spice paste in larger batches and freeze in ice cube trays

recipes.name: Chettinad Vada
recipes.description: Chettinad snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak urad dal and chana dal together in water for 2 hours, then drain thoroughly.
Grind the soaked dals using a wet grinder or food processor, adding minimal water to form a thick, fluffy batter that holds its shape.
Transfer batter to a bowl and fold in green chilies, ginger, onion, curry leaves, salt, crushed peppercorns, and cumin seeds, mixing gently.
Let the mixture rest for 15 minutes while you heat the coconut oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Wet your hands and take a portion of the batter (about 2 tablespoons), shape into a ball, then make a hole in the center with your thumb and gently enlarge to form a donut shape.
Carefully slide the vadas into the hot oil and fry 3-4 at a time, ensuring they don't overcrowd the pan.
Fry for 3-4 minutes, turning once, until both sides are golden brown and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels, then serve warm with coconut chutney or sambar.
cheapTips: Buy urad dal in bulk and store in airtight containers for months
Reuse frying oil by straining; it lasts 3-4 frying sessions

recipes.name: Assamese Pitha
recipes.description: Assamese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix grated jaggery, coconut, black sesame seeds, and salt together in a bowl to form the filling.
Add water gradually to the rice flour while mixing with your fingers until it resembles breadcrumbs and holds together when pressed.
Take a small portion of the dough (about 2 tablespoons), flatten it in your palm, and place 1 tablespoon of the filling in the center.
Fold the dough edges up and around the filling, gently pressing to seal into a smooth ball shape.
Heat ghee in a flat skillet or griddle over medium heat and place the pitha on it.
Cook for 3-4 minutes on the first side until golden brown, then carefully flip and cook the other side for another 3-4 minutes until evenly browned.
Remove to a plate and cool for 2-3 minutes before serving warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Buy jaggery and sticky rice flour from Indian or Asian grocery stores at half the supermarket price
Make filling in large batches and refrigerate up to 5 days

recipes.name: Sate Babi
recipes.description: Balinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes.
Cut pork into 1-inch cubes and thread onto skewers.
Blend peanut butter, coconut milk, garlic, ginger, chili powder, lime juice, soy sauce, and brown sugar into smooth sauce.
Brush pork skewers with sauce and let marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat and cook skewers 3-4 minutes per side until cooked through.
Serve skewers with remaining warm sauce for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder on sale and freeze until needed
Use regular peanut butter instead of premium brands

recipes.name: Plecing Kangkung
recipes.description: Balinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blanch kangkung in boiling salted water for 2 minutes until tender, then drain well.
Pound shallots, garlic, and red chilies together in a mortar until coarse.
Heat oil in pan and fry pounded mixture for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add coconut milk, lime juice, and salt, stirring for 1 minute.
Pour sauce over drained kangkung and toss gently to combine.
Top with crushed peanuts and serve at room temperature.
cheapTips: Use frozen spinach if kangkung unavailable; thaw and squeeze dry
Buy peanuts in bulk and crush by hand

recipes.name: Sambal Matah
recipes.description: Balinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Thinly slice red chilies, green onions, shallots, and garlic, keeping them separate.
Heat oil in pan until shimmering and pour over shallots and garlic in a bowl.
Stir in lime juice, salt, and shrimp paste while oil is still hot.
Add sliced chilies and green onions and mix well.
Let cool to room temperature before serving, allowing flavors to meld.
cheapTips: Buy shallots and garlic in bulk at ethnic markets
Make large batches and store in refrigerator for a week

recipes.name: Bubuh Injin
recipes.description: Balinese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse black sticky rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Bring water to boil, add black rice, and simmer covered for 25 minutes until tender.
Heat coconut milk with brown sugar and salt until sugar dissolves, then stir in pandan extract.
Cook white sticky rice separately according to package directions.
Divide black rice among bowls and top with white sticky rice.
Pour warm coconut milk mixture over top and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy black and white sticky rice in bulk at Asian markets
Skip pandan extract if unavailable; vanilla works as substitute

recipes.name: Jaja Beras
recipes.description: Balinese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine brown sugar, water, and pandan leaves in saucepan and simmer for 5 minutes, then strain.
Mix glutinous rice flour, coconut milk, salt, and pandan syrup into smooth dough.
Knead dough for 2 minutes and divide into small balls about 1 inch diameter.
Heat oil in pan and lightly fry balls until they float and turn golden brown.
Toast shredded coconut in dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Roll warm balls in toasted coconut and serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Skip pandan leaves and use green food coloring if unavailable
Buy shredded coconut in bulk at warehouse stores

recipes.name: Nasi Goreng Bali
recipes.description: Balinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound shallots, garlic, chilies, and shrimp paste together into paste.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in wok or large pan over high heat and fry paste for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add shrimp and cook until pink, about 3 minutes.
Push mixture to side of pan, add remaining oil, and scramble eggs until cooked, then mix with shrimp.
Add rice, breaking up clumps, and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until rice is heated through.
Pour soy sauce over rice and toss well, then fold in green onions and serve.
cheapTips: Use day-old leftover rice; fresh rice becomes mushy
Substitute shrimp with canned sardines or leftover chicken for savings

recipes.name: Tinutuan
recipes.description: Balinese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Heat oil in pot and sauté garlic and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice and stir for 1 minute to coat with oil.
Pour in chicken broth and turmeric, bring to boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice breaks down into porridge.
Season with salt and black pepper, then ladle into bowls and top with sliced green onions and fried shallots.
cheapTips: Use store-bought fried shallots instead of making from scratch
Substitute chicken broth with vegetable broth to save money

recipes.name: Sate Udang
recipes.description: Balinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes.
Peel and devein shrimp, leaving tails on for handling.
Blend peanut butter, coconut milk, garlic, ginger, chili powder, lime juice, soy sauce, and brown sugar until smooth.
Thread 5-6 shrimp onto each skewer and brush generously with peanut sauce.
Heat grill or grill pan to medium-high and cook skewers 2-3 minutes per side until shrimp turn pink.
Serve hot with remaining warm sauce for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp on sale and thaw before cooking
Make sauce in larger batches to use throughout the week

recipes.name: Cabe Goreng
recipes.description: Balinese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Wash chilies and pat completely dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in small pan to 350°F (test with wooden spoon; bubbles should form immediately).
Carefully place 2-3 chilies at a time in hot oil and fry for 30-45 seconds until skin blisters slightly.
Remove with slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
In small bowl, mix minced garlic, shallots, lime juice, salt, and sugar.
Serve warm fried chilies with the sambal dipping sauce alongside.
cheapTips: Buy chilies in season when prices are lowest
Reuse cooking oil for multiple batches

recipes.name: Nam Prik Ong
recipes.description: Northern Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried chilies in hot water for 5 minutes until soft, then remove stems and seeds.
Pound soaked chilies, garlic, shallots, and shrimp paste together into paste.
Heat oil in pan and fry paste for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and darkened.
Add canned tomatoes with juice and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add shrimp, fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar, cooking for 5 minutes until shrimp are pink.
Serve warm with fresh vegetables like long beans, cabbage, or cucumber slices for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp instead of fresh to save 30-40%
Omit shrimp and use this as vegetarian paste over rice

recipes.name: Sai Oua Tod
recipes.description: Northern Thai snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix ground pork with curry paste, fish sauce, garlic, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves in a bowl.
Stuff the mixture into hog casings using a sausage stuffer or piping bag, twisting into 3-inch links.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat and add the sausages.
Cook sausages for 12-15 minutes, turning occasionally until browned and cooked through.
Serve hot with sticky rice and sliced cucumbers and tomatoes on the side.
cheapTips: Buy ground pork on sale and freeze for later use
Skip the hog casings and form into patties instead

recipes.name: Nam Prik Noom
recipes.description: Northern Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Char the green chilies, shallots, and garlic over a gas flame or under a hot broiler until blistered and softened.
Place the charred vegetables in a mortar and pestle and pound until paste-like.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar, adjusting to taste.
Heat oil in a small pan and add the chile paste, stirring for 2 minutes to cook through.
Transfer to a serving dish and serve warm with sticky rice and fresh cucumber slices.
cheapTips: Use regular jalapeños if Thai chilies are unavailable
Buy shallots and garlic in bulk and store in a cool place

recipes.name: Jae Bai Tod
recipes.description: Northern Thai snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix all-purpose flour, rice flour, turmeric, and salt together in a bowl.
Add water gradually to create a batter with the consistency of pancake batter.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pot or wok.
Dip banana blossom slices in batter, coating evenly, and fry in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with sweet chili sauce or dipping sauce.
cheapTips: Buy banana blossoms at Asian markets where they're cheaper
Reuse oil for frying multiple batches to save money

recipes.name: Khao Man Gai
recipes.description: Northern Thai breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring chicken broth to a boil with ginger slices and add chicken breast, simmering for 15 minutes until cooked through.
Remove chicken, let cool slightly, then shred or slice into bite-sized pieces.
In the same broth, cook jasmine rice until tender, about 15-18 minutes.
Mix fish sauce, soy sauce, and lime juice together as a dipping sauce.
Divide rice among bowls, top with chicken, and drizzle with sauce, garnishing with cilantro and green onions.
cheapTips: Buy chicken in bulk when on sale and freeze
Use generic jasmine rice brands for significant savings

recipes.name: Sator Pad
recipes.description: Northern Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add garlic and Thai chilies, stir-frying for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add shrimp paste and stir to combine with the garlic mixture for 30 seconds.
Add stink beans and stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until tender and lightly charred.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, toss well, and serve over jasmine rice.
cheapTips: Buy stink beans frozen instead of fresh for lower cost
Make a double batch and use leftovers for lunch the next day

recipes.name: Nam Prik Aw
recipes.description: Northern Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried chilies in hot water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Char shallots and garlic in a dry pan over medium-high heat until softened, about 5 minutes.
Place soaked chilies, charred shallots, and garlic in a mortar and pound into a coarse paste.
Heat oil in a wok and add the paste, stir-frying for 2 minutes.
Stir in shrimp paste, tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar, cooking for another 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Serve warm with sticky rice and fresh cucumber slices on the side.
cheapTips: Buy dried chilies in bulk from Asian markets
Tamarind paste can be made at home by soaking tamarind pods

recipes.name: Pad Ped Ped Yang
recipes.description: Northern Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and add curry paste, stirring for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk slowly, stirring to combine with the paste.
Add the sliced roasted duck and bring to a simmer.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, tasting and adjusting as needed.
Add Thai chilies and Thai basil, cooking for 2-3 minutes more.
Serve over jasmine rice.
cheapTips: Buy pre-roasted duck from Asian markets to save time
Use chicken as a cheaper substitute for duck

recipes.name: Kaeng Khanun
recipes.description: Northern Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat a pot over medium-high heat and add curry paste, stirring for 1-2 minutes.
Pour in half the coconut milk and stir to create a paste consistency.
Add shredded jackfruit and the broth, bringing to a simmer for 10 minutes.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and add kaffir lime leaves.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, simmering for 10 more minutes.
Add Thai basil just before serving and serve over jasmine rice.
cheapTips: Buy canned jackfruit in brine if fresh is unavailable
Make curry paste in bulk and freeze for later use

recipes.name: Pad Pak Boong
recipes.description: Northern Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a wok over high heat until very hot and shimmering.
Add garlic and chilies, stirring constantly for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the water spinach in batches, tossing continuously for 3-4 minutes until just wilted.
Season with fish sauce and soy sauce, tossing well to coat.
Serve immediately over jasmine rice while still hot.
cheapTips: Buy water spinach at Asian markets, much cheaper than Western stores
Use regular spinach if water spinach is unavailable

recipes.name: Tam Khanun
recipes.description: Northern Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a mortar, pound chilies and garlic together until coarsely broken down.
Add shallots and pound gently a few times to slightly bruise them.
Add shredded jackfruit and long beans, lightly tossing everything together with the pestle.
Add lime juice, fish sauce, and dried shrimp, tossing well to combine.
Transfer to a serving dish, top with crushed peanuts, and serve with sticky rice.
cheapTips: Use canned jackfruit to reduce prep time and cost
Buy dried shrimp in bulk from Asian markets for better pricing

recipes.name: Pithla
recipes.description: Maharashtrian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a pot and add cumin seeds until they crackle.
Add chopped onion, green chili, and ginger, then sauté until onion turns golden.
Mix in gram flour and turmeric powder, stirring constantly for 2 minutes to remove raw smell.
Gradually add water while stirring to avoid lumps.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 8-10 minutes until it reaches a thick porridge consistency.
Season with salt and garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.
Serve hot with bhakri or puri on the side.
cheapTips: Buy gram flour in bulk
Use seasonal onions and chilies

recipes.name: Ukdiche Modak
recipes.description: Maharashtrian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix jaggery with grated coconut, crushed cardamom, and nutmeg in a bowl.
Heat water and add rice flour gradually while stirring to form a soft dough.
Add salt and let the dough cool slightly.
Wet your hands and take a small portion of dough, flatten it, and add a spoonful of jaggery-coconut filling.
Close the dough into a modak shape (like a pyramid with ridges).
Lightly oil a steamer or idli maker and arrange modaks inside.
Steam for 12-15 minutes until firm and cooked through.
Remove and serve warm with ghee drizzle.
cheapTips: Make jaggery at home if available
Buy coconut whole and grate fresh

recipes.name: Annarsa
recipes.description: Maharashtrian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Grind soaked rice and chana dal together with minimal water to form a coarse mixture.
Heat ghee in a pan and add the ground mixture, stirring constantly.
Add jaggery, grated coconut, and cardamom powder while stirring over medium heat.
Cook for 8-10 minutes until the mixture becomes thick and leaves the pan sides.
Cool the mixture completely on a plate.
Roll into balls or discs and flatten slightly.
Heat oil to 350°F and deep fry annarsa until golden brown on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve at room temperature.
cheapTips: Soak grains the night before
Buy jaggery in bulk during harvest season

recipes.name: Sate Lilit
recipes.description: Balinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Grind shallots, garlic, red chilies, and galangal into a fine paste using a food processor.
Mix ground meat with the spice paste, grated coconut, turmeric, lime juice, and salt.
Divide mixture into portions and wrap each around a lemongrass stalk, forming an oval shape.
Grill over charcoal or on a hot grill pan for 4-5 minutes per side until cooked through.
Brush with oil while grilling to keep moist.
Serve hot with sambal (chili paste) and lime wedges on the side.
cheapTips: Buy ground meat on sale and freeze
Use shallots instead of premium spices

recipes.name: Babi Guling
recipes.description: Balinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast coriander and cumin seeds lightly and grind them coarsely.
Create a paste by grinding turmeric, galangal, garlic, shallots, and red chilies together.
Mix the ground spices and herb paste, then rub thoroughly over the entire pork.
Marinate the pork for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Heat oil in a large roasting pan and sear the pork on all sides until browned.
Add coconut milk and cover the pan with foil.
Roast at 325°F for 3-4 hours, basting occasionally, until pork is tender and golden.
Remove foil for the last 30 minutes to crisp the skin.
Slice and serve with rice, sambal, and lawar (chopped vegetable salad).
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder instead of whole pig
Prepare a day ahead to reduce cooking time stress

recipes.name: Bebek Betutu
recipes.description: Balinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blend garlic, shallots, red chilies, galangal, turmeric, and ginger into a smooth paste.
Rub the paste generously over all duck pieces and let sit for 30 minutes.
Layer banana leaves in a deep baking dish and arrange lemongrass stalks in the center.
Place duck pieces on top and pour coconut milk over them.
Fold banana leaves over to enclose the duck completely.
Wrap the entire dish in foil and place in a roasting pan with hot water (water bath).
Bake at 300°F for 4-5 hours until duck is extremely tender.
Open carefully and serve with the cooking liquid spooned over rice.
cheapTips: Buy duck when on sale and freeze
Skip banana leaves and use foil only

recipes.name: Lawar
recipes.description: Balinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Grind shallots, garlic, red chilies, and turmeric into a fine paste.
Heat oil in a large pan and fry the paste for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Add ground meat and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until cooked through (8 minutes).
Add grated coconut, long beans, and cabbage, stirring well.
Cook for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are softened but still have texture.
Add lime juice and salt, mixing thoroughly.
Taste and adjust seasoning, then serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Use cabbage year-round instead of rare vegetables
Buy whole fresh coconuts and grate

recipes.name: Nasi Campur Bali
recipes.description: Balinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok and scramble eggs until cooked, then set aside.
In the same wok, add 1 tbsp oil and fry minced garlic and shallots until aromatic.
Add ground meat and cook until browned, breaking it into pieces.
Add long beans and cabbage, stir-frying for 5 minutes.
Add cooked rice and soy sauce, mixing well and breaking up clumps.
Stir in red chili and the cooked eggs, tossing gently.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use leftover rice
Buy eggs in bulk

recipes.name: Bakso Bali
recipes.description: Balinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix ground beef with breadcrumbs, egg, minced garlic, minced shallots, and turmeric.
Season with salt and pepper, then form into small balls (about 1.5 inches diameter).
Bring beef broth to a boil in a large pot.
Carefully drop meatballs into boiling broth and simmer for 8-10 minutes until they float and are cooked through.
Add long beans and continue cooking for 5 minutes.
Add bok choy and soy sauce, cooking for another 3-4 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot in bowls with broth and vegetables.
cheapTips: Make meatballs in advance and freeze
Use vegetable broth if beef broth is expensive

recipes.name: Jaja Laklak
recipes.description: Balinese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix glutinous rice flour with coconut milk, salt, and green food coloring to form a soft dough.
Divide dough into small portions and flatten into thin circles (about 3 inches diameter).
Cook each circle on a hot non-stick pan or griddle for 1-2 minutes per side until slightly cooked but still soft.
Mix grated coconut with palm sugar and turmeric powder.
Place a spoonful of the coconut-sugar mixture in the center of each cooked pancake.
Fold pancake in half gently while still warm.
Serve warm as is or arrange on a plate and serve with additional palm sugar sauce if desired.
cheapTips: Buy glutinous rice flour in bulk
Use jaggery instead of palm sugar

recipes.name: Pad Sataw
recipes.description: Northern Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut long beans into 2-inch pieces.
Mince garlic, chilies, and shallots together.
Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add minced aromatics and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add ground pork and stir-fry until cooked through, 3-4 minutes.
Add long beans and fish sauce, toss constantly for 3-4 minutes until beans are tender-crisp.
Finish with lime juice and remove from heat.
cheapTips: Buy long beans at Asian markets instead of regular supermarkets for better prices
Use regular garlic instead of pre-minced to save 30%

recipes.name: Grilled chicken (Gai yang)
recipes.description: Isaan Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound garlic and cilantro together in a mortar to create a paste.
Mix garlic-cilantro paste with fish sauce, soy sauce, lime juice, black pepper, and oil.
Cut chicken in half lengthwise and rub the marinade all over, inside and out.
Let marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill chicken skin-side down for 15-18 minutes, then flip and grill for another 12-15 minutes until internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Buy whole chickens on sale and freeze; they're usually cheaper per pound than parts
Make paste with a knife if you don't have a mortar

recipes.name: Tam khao pod
recipes.description: Isaan Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound garlic and chilies in a mortar until roughly broken down.
Add shallots and pound lightly to bruise.
Add corn and tomatoes, gently bruise with the pestle for 30 seconds.
Add lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar, toss everything together.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Transfer to a serving plate and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use frozen corn year-round; it's cheaper than fresh and just as good
Skip palm sugar and use regular sugar if needed

recipes.name: Koi tod
recipes.description: Isaan Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean chicken gizzards thoroughly under running water and cut in half.
Boil gizzards in salted water for 20 minutes until tender, then drain.
Mince garlic, chilies, and shallots together.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Add minced aromatics and fry until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add boiled gizzards and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
Add fish sauce and lime juice, toss well.
Garnish with cilantro and serve.
cheapTips: Chicken gizzards are very affordable, usually under $2 per pound
Skip fresh cilantro garnish if on a tight budget

recipes.name: Isan sausage
recipes.description: Isaan Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mince garlic and chilies finely.
Mix ground pork with minced garlic, chilies, fish sauce, salt, black pepper, and sticky rice until well combined.
Rinse hog casings under cold water to remove salt.
Fill casings with pork mixture using a sausage stuffer or piping bag, leaving 1 inch at each end.
Tie off ends with kitchen twine.
Grill sausages over medium-high heat for 12-15 minutes, turning frequently, until cooked through.
Serve with sticky rice and spicy dipping sauce.
cheapTips: Ask your butcher for free hog casings when you buy ground pork
Make without casings as a loose sausage patty if casings are unavailable

recipes.name: Pad thai kua gai
recipes.description: Isaan Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak rice noodles in room temperature water for 30 minutes until pliable, then drain.
Dice chicken breast into small pieces.
Mince garlic cloves.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and add minced garlic, cook until fragrant.
Add diced chicken and stir-fry until cooked through, about 4-5 minutes.
Add drained noodles and dried shrimp, stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar, toss constantly for 2-3 minutes until noodles are tender.
Serve with lime wedges on the side.
cheapTips: Buy rice noodles at Asian markets instead of regular stores; 3x cheaper
Tamarind paste can be made by mixing tamarind concentrate with water

recipes.name: Nam prik pla duk
recipes.description: Isaan Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Deep fry catfish fillets in oil heated to 350°F until golden and crispy, about 8-10 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and flake into bite-sized pieces with a fork.
Pound garlic, chilies, and shallots together in a mortar until roughly combined.
Add flaked catfish to the mortar and pound gently to incorporate.
Add lime juice and fish sauce, stir to combine.
Transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with cilantro.
Serve with raw vegetables like cabbage, cucumber, and long beans for dipping.
cheapTips: Use cheaper frozen catfish fillets; they work just as well when fried crispy
Make with canned sardines instead of fresh catfish to cut cost in half

recipes.name: Som tam poo
recipes.description: Isaan Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound garlic and chilies in a mortar until roughly crushed.
Add shredded green papaya and pound gently for 30 seconds to bruise.
Add cherry tomatoes and pound lightly for another 20 seconds.
Add crab meat, lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Toss everything together thoroughly with the pestle.
Transfer to a serving plate immediately and serve.
cheapTips: Canned crab is cheaper than fresh and works perfectly in this dish
Pre-shredded papaya from some stores saves prep time and money

recipes.name: Grilled fish (Pla yang)
recipes.description: Isaan Thai dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound garlic and cilantro together until it forms a paste.
Mix the paste with fish sauce, lime juice, black pepper, and oil.
Clean fish and score the skin diagonally on both sides.
Rub the marinade inside the cavity and all over the exterior.
Let sit for 20 minutes.
Grill fish over medium heat for 6-7 minutes per side until flesh is opaque and skin is crispy.
Garnish with chopped scallions and serve with lime wedges.
cheapTips: Buy whole fish from Asian markets; much cheaper per pound than fillets
Ask the fishmonger to clean and scale for free

recipes.name: Beef jerky (Neua dad diaw)
recipes.description: Isaan Thai snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice beef sirloin against the grain into 1/4-inch thick strips.
Pound garlic and chilies together, then mix with fish sauce, soy sauce, palm sugar, black pepper, and oil.
Marinate beef strips in the mixture for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Pat beef dry with paper towels.
Arrange strips on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Bake at 160°F for 3-4 hours, stirring occasionally, until beef is completely dried but still slightly flexible.
Cool completely before storing in an airtight container.
cheapTips: Buy beef on sale and freeze; make jerky to use it before spoiling
Use a dehydrator instead of oven for more even drying and lower energy cost

recipes.name: Tam makua
recipes.description: Isaan Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Char eggplants directly over a gas flame or under a broiler for 5-7 minutes until the skin blackens and flesh softens.
Let eggplants cool, then peel away charred skin and roughly chop the flesh.
Pound garlic and chilies together in a mortar until broken down.
Add palm sugar and pound briefly, then add eggplant and gently bruise together.
Stir in lime juice, fish sauce, halved cherry tomatoes, and sliced shallots.
Toss gently to combine and taste for balance of salty, sour, and spicy.
Transfer to a plate, top with fresh cilantro, and serve with sticky rice.
cheapTips: Buy eggplants on sale and in season (summer)
Use regular garlic and dried chilies if Thai chilies are expensive

recipes.name: Larb moo
recipes.description: Isaan Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook ground pork, breaking it apart, until cooked through (5-7 minutes).
Pound garlic, chilies, and shallots in a mortar until fragrant and broken down.
Add the pounded mixture to the pork and stir well over heat for 1 minute.
Remove from heat and stir in lime juice, fish sauce, and let cool slightly.
Fold in fresh mint, cilantro, and half the roasted peanuts.
Transfer to a plate, top with remaining peanuts and more fresh herbs.
Serve at room temperature with lettuce leaves and sticky rice.
cheapTips: Buy ground pork on sale and freeze for later
Use regular peanut butter if roasted peanuts are expensive

recipes.name: Fried chicken (Gai tod)
recipes.description: Isaan Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound garlic, cilantro roots, and black pepper together in a mortar until paste-like.
Rub chicken thighs with the garlic paste, then add fish sauce and salt, coating well.
Let chicken marinate for at least 30 minutes or up to overnight in the refrigerator.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pot or wok.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels, then carefully place in hot oil.
Fry for 12-15 minutes, turning halfway, until skin is deep golden brown and internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Drain on paper towels and serve with lime wedges and sticky rice.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs in bulk and portion at home
Reuse cooking oil by straining and storing in the refrigerator

recipes.name: Nam prik num
recipes.description: Isaan Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Char chilies, shallots, and garlic under a broiler or over a flame until lightly blackened (3-5 minutes).
Let cool slightly, then pound in a mortar until chunky paste forms.
Heat oil in a pan and add the pounded mixture, stirring for 2-3 minutes.
Add shrimp paste and stir well to combine.
Remove from heat and stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar.
Add whole cherry tomatoes and stir gently to combine.
Transfer to a serving bowl and serve with fresh vegetables and sticky rice.
cheapTips: Buy shallots and garlic in bulk from Asian markets
Make a larger batch and freeze in portions

recipes.name: Khao tod
recipes.description: Isaan Thai snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Spread cooked rice on a baking sheet and let dry for several hours or overnight.
Heat oil to 350°F in a wok or deep pot.
Working in batches, carefully add dried rice to hot oil and fry for 2-3 minutes until puffed and golden.
Drain on paper towels and place in a bowl while still warm.
Pound garlic and chilies together, then mix with salt and sugar.
Toss the fried rice with the garlic-chili mixture while still warm.
Serve immediately with lime wedges for squeezing over top.
cheapTips: Use leftover rice to avoid waste
Make a larger batch and store in an airtight container

recipes.name: Tam rad pla
recipes.description: Isaan Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Shred green papaya into thin strips and set aside.
Cut long beans into 2-inch pieces.
Pound garlic and chilies in a mortar until broken down.
Add dried shrimp and pound briefly, then add palm sugar and lightly bruise.
Add shredded papaya and long beans and gently pound to release juices (10-15 times).
Stir in lime juice, fish sauce, cherry tomatoes, and roasted peanuts.
Toss gently and transfer to a plate, serving with sticky rice.
cheapTips: Buy green papaya from Asian markets for better prices
Use frozen long beans if fresh are unavailable

recipes.name: Lumpia Semarang
recipes.description: Javanese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mince shallots and garlic, then cook in 2 tablespoons oil until fragrant.
Add ground pork, breaking it apart, and cook until no longer pink (5-7 minutes).
Add diced carrots and shredded cabbage, stirring for 3-4 minutes until vegetables soften slightly.
Stir in soy sauce, salt, and pepper, then let filling cool for 5 minutes.
Place a lumpia wrapper on a flat surface and add 2 tablespoons filling near one corner.
Roll tightly, tucking in sides as you go, then seal the edge with a drop of water.
Heat oil to 350°F and fry lumpia in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve with sweet chili sauce or soy dipping sauce.
cheapTips: Buy lumpia wrappers from Asian markets in bulk
Make and freeze unbaked lumpia for quick future meals

recipes.name: Ayam Goreng Jawa
recipes.description: Javanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pound garlic, shallots, ginger, turmeric, and coriander seeds together into a paste.
Rub chicken thighs with the paste, salt, and palm sugar, coating well.
Heat oil to 325°F in a deep pot or wok.
Carefully place chicken in hot oil and fry for 5 minutes until lightly golden.
Remove chicken and set aside, leaving 3 tablespoons oil in the pot.
Add the remaining spice paste to the oil and cook for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in coconut milk, return chicken to pot, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until cooked through.
Remove chicken and place on a rack, then increase heat and deep-fry again for 3-5 minutes until skin is crispy.
Finish with lime juice and serve with rice and sambal.
cheapTips: Buy chicken thighs on sale and freeze in portions
Use coconut milk from a can or make from powder

recipes.name: Pecel
recipes.description: Javanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a pot of salted water to boil and blanch cabbage for 2 minutes, then drain.
Blanch carrots for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp, then drain.
Blanch spinach for 1 minute, squeeze dry, and chop roughly.
Blanch bean sprouts for 1 minute and drain well.
Pound roasted peanuts, garlic, and chilies together until chunky paste forms.
Stir in palm sugar, lime juice, salt, and coconut milk to create a sauce.
Arrange all blanched vegetables on a plate and drizzle with peanut sauce.
Serve at room temperature with steamed rice and hard-boiled eggs on the side.
cheapTips: Buy vegetables on sale and use what's available
Make peanut sauce in bulk and refrigerate up to 1 week

recipes.name: Nasi Goreng Jawa
recipes.description: Javanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mince shallots, garlic, and ginger together.
Dice chicken breast into small pieces and peel shrimp.
Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat.
Add minced aromatics and cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add chicken and shrimp, stirring constantly for 4-5 minutes until cooked through.
Add cold rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes.
Pour in soy sauce and sweet soy sauce, tossing to coat evenly.
Push rice to the side, scramble eggs in the empty space, then mix with rice.
Finish with lime juice and sliced scallions, then serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use leftover rice for this dish to reduce waste
Substitute shrimp with additional chicken if budget is tight

recipes.name: Lodeh
recipes.description: Javanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté garlic, shallots, and ginger until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add zucchini, cabbage, green beans, and carrots, then stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and add turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Add cubed tofu and simmer for another 10 minutes until tofu is heated through.
Taste and adjust seasoning, then serve hot with rice.
cheapTips: Buy coconut milk in bulk Asian markets for 40% less
Use seasonal vegetables like pumpkin or long beans as substitutes

recipes.name: Rawon
recipes.description: Javanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and brown beef cubes on all sides, about 8 minutes total.
Add garlic, shallots, ginger, and galangal, stirring until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add turmeric and ground black nuts, stirring constantly for 1 minute.
Pour in beef broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 60 minutes until beef is tender.
Add salt, pepper, and lime juice, then taste and adjust seasonings.
Simmer for another 5 minutes and serve hot with rice.
cheapTips: Use beef chuck or shoulder instead of premium cuts
Make stock from beef bones the day before to save money

recipes.name: Onde-Onde
recipes.description: Javanese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix glutinous rice flour with 0.75 cup coconut milk and salt until a soft dough forms, adding water if needed.
Divide dough into 12 small balls, flatten each, and place a pinch of brown sugar in the center, then seal.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pot or wok.
Fry balls in batches until they float and turn golden, about 4-5 minutes per batch.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Roll warm balls in a mixture of shredded coconut and sesame seeds until fully coated.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Buy glutinous rice flour in Asian markets instead of specialty stores
Use regular shredded coconut instead of fresh, store brand

recipes.name: Tahu Goreng Kuah
recipes.description: Javanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Press tofu between paper towels for 15 minutes to remove excess moisture.
Heat 3 cups oil to 350°F and deep-fry tofu cubes until golden on all sides, about 6 minutes total, then drain on paper towels.
In a separate pot, heat 2 tablespoons oil and sauté garlic, shallots, and ginger until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add vegetable broth, soy sauce, and turmeric, then bring to a boil.
Mix cornstarch with 3 tablespoons water and stir into broth to thicken slightly.
Add fried tofu cubes, salt, and pepper, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Garnish with green onions and serve hot with rice.
cheapTips: Buy tofu in bulk from Asian grocery stores at half the price
Reuse frying oil by straining and storing in a container

recipes.name: Gula Jawa Kue Putri Mandi
recipes.description: Javanese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9-inch square baking pan.
Whisk together eggs and palm sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Fold in melted butter and vanilla extract until combined.
In a separate bowl, sift together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Gently fold dry ingredients into wet ingredients, alternating with coconut milk in three additions.
Fold in shredded coconut until evenly distributed.
Pour batter into prepared pan and bake for 25-30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely, and cut into squares.
cheapTips: Substitute palm sugar with brown sugar for similar flavor
Buy eggs in bulk during sales and store in refrigerator

recipes.name: Opor Ayam
recipes.description: Javanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté garlic, shallots, ginger, and galangal until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add chicken pieces and brown on all sides, about 8 minutes.
Add turmeric and stir to coat the chicken, then cook for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil, then add lemongrass and reduce heat to simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Add coconut milk and simmer uncovered for another 15 minutes until chicken is tender and sauce is creamy.
Season with salt, pepper, and lime juice, then taste and adjust as needed.
Remove lemongrass and serve hot with rice.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs instead of breasts for more flavor and lower cost
Make fresh lemongrass paste from frozen lemongrass

recipes.name: Oseng-Oseng
recipes.description: Javanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until very hot.
Add beef and stir-fry until browned, about 4 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Add garlic, shallots, and ginger to the wok and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add cabbage, carrots, and long beans, then stir-fry for 5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Return beef to the wok and add soy sauce, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Toss everything together for 2 minutes until well combined and heated through.
Serve immediately with rice.
cheapTips: Substitute beef with chicken breast for 30% cost savings
Buy vegetables at farmers markets when in season

recipes.name: Karedok
recipes.description: Javanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blanch green beans in boiling salted water for 3 minutes, then drain and cool.
In a small bowl, mix peanut butter, garlic, shallots, ginger, lime juice, soy sauce, brown sugar, and water until smooth.
Combine cabbage, bean sprouts, blanched green beans, cucumber, and carrots in a large bowl.
Pour peanut sauce over vegetables and toss gently until all vegetables are coated.
Let sit for 5 minutes to allow flavors to blend, then serve at room temperature or chilled.
cheapTips: Use store-brand peanut butter instead of natural brands
Buy vegetables loose at the store and choose the smallest sizes for better prices

recipes.name: Jenang Kuning
recipes.description: Javanese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a pot, mix glutinous rice flour with 0.5 cup water to form a smooth paste.
Heat butter in the pot over medium heat and add the rice flour paste, stirring constantly.
Slowly add coconut milk while stirring to prevent lumps from forming.
Add palm sugar, turmeric, and salt, continuing to stir frequently.
Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mixture becomes thick and pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Transfer to a serving dish or individual bowls.
Top with shredded coconut and serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy palm sugar in bulk from Asian markets at lower prices
Use unsweetened shredded coconut from the baking aisle

recipes.name: Gulai Tambusu Telur
recipes.description: Padang lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté garlic, shallots, and ginger until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add turmeric, cumin, and coriander, then stir for 30 seconds until bloomed.
Add hard-boiled eggs and gently turn to coat with spices, then cook for 1 minute.
Pour in vegetable broth and coconut milk, then bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 25-30 minutes to allow flavors to develop, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt, pepper, and lime juice, then taste and adjust as needed.
Serve hot with rice.
cheapTips: Buy eggs in bulk during sales and store in the refrigerator
Use canned coconut milk from discount stores

recipes.name: Sambal Goreng Ati Ampela
recipes.description: Padang lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean and cut chicken liver and gizzards into 1-inch pieces, then parboil for 10 minutes and drain.
