Serve immediately in a bowl or on a lettuce leaf as an appetizer.
cheapTips: Use tilapia or any affordable fresh white fish
Buy limes in bulk when on sale and juice them yourself

recipes.name: Linarang Isda
recipes.description: Bicolano lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat and sauté garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add sliced onion and cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Season with fish sauce, salt, and turmeric powder, stirring well.
Carefully place fish fillets into the simmering sauce, arranging them in a single layer.
Add red chili peppers and cook uncovered for 12-15 minutes until fish is tender and cooked through.
Avoid stirring the fish to prevent it from breaking apart.
Serve hot with the rich sauce spooned over steamed rice.
cheapTips: Buy fish fillets on sale and freeze for later use
Use generic coconut milk brands for cost savings

recipes.name: Sarciado
recipes.description: Bicolano lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pan and sauté garlic and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced onion and cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Stir in tomato sauce and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add potato slices and cook for 8-10 minutes until they begin to soften.
Nestle fish fillets into the sauce, arranging them in a single layer.
Add bell pepper strips and season with fish sauce, salt, and pepper.
Simmer uncovered for 12-15 minutes until fish is cooked through and potatoes are tender.
Serve hot with the vegetable-tomato sauce spooned over steamed white rice.
cheapTips: Use canned tomato sauce instead of fresh tomatoes
Buy fish and potatoes at the farmer's market for better prices

recipes.name: Ginataang Langka
recipes.description: Bicolano lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a large pot and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger for 2 minutes.
Add shredded jackfruit and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned.
If using meat, add it now and cook until browned.
Pour in coconut milk gradually, stirring constantly to combine.
Add green chili peppers, fish sauce, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes.
Stir occasionally until jackfruit is tender and sauce reduces slightly.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot with steamed rice.
cheapTips: Buy canned young jackfruit (in brine) from Asian markets if fresh is unavailable
Skip the meat to reduce costs while keeping dish flavorful

recipes.name: Burong Dalag
recipes.description: Bicolano snack — a popular dish you can make at home.

ingredients.note: 1.5 lbs, cleaned and cut into chunks

steps: Combine vinegar and water in a pot and bring to a boil.
Add salt, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, chili peppers, and peppercorns.
Stir until sugar and salt are fully dissolved.
Add fish chunks carefully to the boiling mixture.
Return to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 8-10 minutes until fish is cooked through.
Remove from heat and allow to cool to room temperature.
Transfer fish and pickling liquid to a glass jar and refrigerate.
Serve chilled or at room temperature as an appetizer or side dish; keeps refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.
cheapTips: Buy catfish or mudfish whole and clean at home to save money
Make large batches that keep refrigerated for weeks

recipes.name: Fried Bicolano Camarones
recipes.description: Bicolano lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat shrimp dry with paper towels to remove excess moisture.
Mix flour, salt, white pepper, and garlic powder in a shallow bowl.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F over medium-high heat.
Coat shrimp evenly in the flour mixture, shaking off excess.
Carefully place shrimp in hot oil and fry 1.5-2 minutes per side until golden brown.
Use a slotted spoon to transfer cooked shrimp to a paper towel-lined plate.
Serve hot with lime wedges for squeezing and minced onion on the side as condiment.
Eat immediately while shrimp is crispy.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp on sale and thaw overnight in the refrigerator
Reuse frying oil by straining it through a fine mesh after cooling

recipes.name: Ginataang Calamansi Tilapia
recipes.description: Bicolano lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic, ginger, and sliced onions until fragrant.
Add tilapia fillets and cook for 2 minutes on each side until lightly browned.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add lime juice, fish sauce, and green chilies.
Simmer for 10 minutes until fish is cooked through and flakes easily.
Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot with rice.
cheapTips: Use frozen tilapia when fresh is expensive
Substitute calamansi with affordable lime or lemon juice

recipes.name: Linarang Baboy
recipes.description: Bicolano lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil and sauté garlic, ginger, and sliced onions until golden.
Add cubed pork and brown on all sides for 8 minutes.
Add dried chilies and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in coconut milk and fish sauce.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 35 minutes until pork is tender.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with rice.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder on sale and freeze for later
Use budget-friendly dried chilies instead of fresh

recipes.name: Sinigang na Hipon
recipes.description: Bicolano lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil and sauté garlic and ginger slices until fragrant.
Add sliced onions and cook until translucent.
Pour in water and bring to a boil.
Add tamarind paste and cubed radish; simmer for 15 minutes.
Add shrimp and green chilies, cooking for 4 minutes.
Add spinach and fish sauce, simmering for 2 more minutes.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice.
cheapTips: Use frozen shrimp to save money
Buy tamarind paste in bulk from Asian markets

recipes.name: Ginisang Langka
recipes.description: Bicolano lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil and sauté minced garlic and onion until fragrant.
Add ground pork and cook until browned, breaking it apart as it cooks.
Drain jackfruit cans and add jackfruit to the pan.
Add diced tomato and fish sauce.
Simmer for 15 minutes until flavors combine.
Add green beans if using, and cook for 3 more minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve with rice.
cheapTips: Canned jackfruit is affordable and shelf-stable
Use ground pork trimmings or cheaper cuts when available

recipes.name: Rellenong Alimasag
recipes.description: Bicolano lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Kill crabs humanely and carefully remove meat from shells, keeping shells intact.
Sauté minced garlic and onion in oil until fragrant.
Add ground pork and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Mix cooked pork with crab meat, egg, breadcrumbs, and fish sauce.
Stuff the mixture into the crab shells, packing firmly.
Heat remaining oil in a pan and carefully place stuffed crabs shell-side down.
Add water to the pan, cover, and steam for 15 minutes until cooked through.
Remove to plate and serve hot with rice.
cheapTips: Buy crabs on sale and freeze until ready to use
Use cheaper ground pork to stretch the filling

recipes.name: Camarones sa Gata
recipes.description: Bicolano lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil and sauté garlic, ginger, and sliced onion until aromatic.
Add shrimp and cook for 2 minutes per side until pink.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add fish sauce and simmer for 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately over steamed rice.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp in bulk for better pricing
Use canned coconut milk which is cheaper than fresh

recipes.name: Tiyula ng Bicolano
recipes.description: Bicolano lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil and sauté garlic, ginger slices, and sliced onion until golden.
Add beef cubes and brown on all sides, about 8 minutes.
Pour in water and bring to a boil.
Add dried chilies and reduce heat, simmering covered for 25 minutes until beef is tender.
Add coconut milk and fish sauce.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with rice.
cheapTips: Use chuck roast and cut into cubes for economy
Buy dried chilies in bulk from ethnic markets

recipes.name: Puro at Timpla
recipes.description: Bicolano lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean and dice kidney and liver into bite-sized pieces.
Heat oil and sauté garlic, ginger, and sliced onion until fragrant.
Add diced organ meats and cook for 3 minutes.
Add water and fish sauce, simmer for 10 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and green chilies.
Simmer for 10 more minutes until tender.
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot with rice.
cheapTips: Organ meats are very inexpensive at butcher counters
Buy in bulk and freeze for meal prep

recipes.name: Ginataang Puso ng Saging
recipes.description: Bicolano lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak banana heart slices in salt water for 10 minutes to prevent darkening.
Heat oil and sauté garlic, ginger, and sliced onion until fragrant.
Add ground pork and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Drain banana heart and add to the pan.
Pour in coconut milk and fish sauce, stirring well.
Simmer for 20 minutes until banana heart is tender.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with rice.
cheapTips: Use canned hearts of palm as cheaper alternative to fresh banana heart
Use ground pork trimmings when available

recipes.name: Fried Malaga
recipes.description: Bicolano snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel malanga roots and cut into thin matchstick fries about 3 inches long.
Soak cut malanga in cold salt water for 10 minutes to remove starch.
Drain and pat completely dry with paper towels.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pot or fryer.
Fry malanga in small batches for 3-4 minutes until golden and crispy.
Remove with slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Season immediately with salt, garlic powder, and black pepper while hot.
cheapTips: Buy malanga in bulk when on sale and freeze
Reuse frying oil multiple times by straining through cheesecloth

recipes.name: Tinumok
recipes.description: Bicolano lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic, ginger, and onions until fragrant.
Add bell peppers and cook for 3 minutes, then add salt and pepper.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a simmer, stirring well.
Place banana leaves on a work surface and divide the fish fillets among them.
Spoon the coconut pepper mixture over each fillet and fold the banana leaf to enclose it completely.
Arrange wrapped packets seam-side down in a baking pan and add 1/4 cup water.
Cover with foil and bake at 375°F for 35-40 minutes until fish is cooked through.
Carefully open packets and transfer to serving plates.
cheapTips: Buy whole tilapia and fillet yourself to save 30%
Frozen banana leaves are cheaper than fresh and work just as well

recipes.name: Moules à la Normande
recipes.description: Norman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean mussels by scrubbing shells and removing beards; discard any that don't close.
Melt butter in a large pot and sauté minced shallots and garlic until softened.
Pour in white wine and bring to a boil.
Add mussels, cover, and cook for 5-7 minutes, shaking the pot occasionally until shells open.
Remove mussels with a slotted spoon and discard any unopened shells.
Stir cream into the cooking liquid and simmer for 2 minutes.
Return mussels to the pot, add chopped parsley, salt, and pepper, and gently toss.
Serve in bowls with the sauce and crusty bread for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy mussels in bulk when on sale and freeze for later
Use affordable white wine like Pinot Grigio instead of expensive varieties

recipes.name: Sole Normande
recipes.description: Norman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F and butter a baking dish.
Sauté shallots and mushrooms in butter until golden, then spread in the baking dish.
Pat sole dry and arrange fillets over the mushroom mixture.
Pour wine and fish stock over the sole, season with salt and pepper, and cover with parchment paper.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until sole is just cooked through.
Meanwhile, sauté shrimp in butter until pink, then add cleaned mussels and cook until shells open.
Remove baking dish from oven and carefully pour the cooking liquid into a saucepan.
Whisk in cream and lemon juice, then add shrimp and mussels to the sauce.
Arrange sole on serving plates, top with seafood and sauce, and garnish with parsley.
cheapTips: Substitute flounder for sole to reduce cost by 40%
Use frozen shrimp and mussels instead of fresh

recipes.name: Tripes à la Mode de Caen
recipes.description: Norman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean tripe thoroughly under running water and cut into 2-inch strips.
Blanch tripe and beef feet in boiling salted water for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Heat oil in a heavy pot and brown the blanched tripe and beef feet on all sides.
Add diced onions, carrots, celery, and garlic, cooking until vegetables soften.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then deglaze with white wine.
Add beef broth, bay leaves, and thyme, then bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook at 300°F in the oven for 3-4 hours until tripe is very tender.
Season with salt and pepper, remove bay leaves, and serve in shallow bowls with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Tripe is an inexpensive cut; buy from butcher counter or ethnic markets
Make a larger batch and freeze portions for easy future meals

recipes.name: Andouille de Vire
recipes.description: Norman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut andouille into 1/2-inch slices and peel and quarter potatoes.
Dice onions and sauté in butter in a large pot until softened.
Add sausage slices and brown lightly on both sides.
Pour in cider and broth, then add potatoes, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 20-25 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Stir in mustard and season with salt and pepper.
Simmer uncovered for 5 more minutes to meld flavors.
Remove bay leaf and serve in bowls.
cheapTips: Use smoked kielbasa as a budget-friendly substitute for andouille
Buy potatoes in bulk and peel ahead of time

recipes.name: Camembert de Normandie
recipes.description: Norman snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Remove Camembert from refrigerator 30 minutes before serving to reach room temperature.
Slice bread and toast lightly if desired.
Slice apples thinly and toss with a squeeze of lemon juice to prevent browning.
Place cheese wheel on a serving board and drizzle with honey.
Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.
Arrange bread, apple slices, and walnuts around the cheese.
Serve immediately, spreading soft cheese on bread as desired.
cheapTips: Buy standard brie instead of authentic Camembert for 50% savings
Make your own candied walnuts with brown sugar and butter

recipes.name: Livarot
recipes.description: Norman snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Remove Livarot from refrigerator 20 minutes before serving.
Slice baguette into 1/4-inch rounds and arrange on a serving plate.
Core and slice the pear into thin wedges.
Place cheese in center of board with the wrapper still on.
Arrange bread, pear slices, and hazelnuts around the cheese.
Add a small bowl of fig jam and sprinkle chives over the cheese.
Serve at room temperature with guests spreading cheese on bread as they eat.
cheapTips: Substitute with aged cheddar for similar texture at lower cost
Buy store-brand fig jam instead of premium brands

recipes.name: Pont-l'Évêque
recipes.description: Norman snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Remove cheese from refrigerator 15 minutes before serving.
Arrange cheese wheel on a wooden board, keeping it in its box to support it.
Scatter crackers, cornichons, and salami around the board.
Add walnut halves and celery pieces to the arrangement.
Garnish the cheese with fresh rosemary sprigs.
Serve at room temperature with people helping themselves to crackers and small portions of cheese.
cheapTips: Buy the cheese from cheese counter and ask for slight discount on day-old stock
Use store-brand crackers and cured meats from deli counter

recipes.name: Teurgoule
recipes.description: Norman dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 300°F and butter a large earthenware or ceramic dish.
Combine rice, milk, sugar, butter, and cinnamon stick in the baking dish.
Stir well and sprinkle ground cinnamon and nutmeg over the top.
Bake uncovered for 2.5-3 hours, stirring occasionally (every 45 minutes) to prevent sticking.
The rice should absorb the milk and develop a golden crust on top.
Remove from oven and discard cinnamon stick.
Stir in vanilla extract and additional salt to taste.
Serve warm in bowls, scraping the flavorful crust from the sides if desired.
cheapTips: Buy rice in bulk from ethnic grocery stores for 50% savings
Use store-brand milk and spices rather than premium brands

recipes.name: Bourride
recipes.description: Norman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté sliced fennel and onion until softened.
Add diced potatoes, fish stock, minced garlic, and saffron, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are nearly tender.
Gently add fish fillets and poach for 8-10 minutes until cooked through.
Remove fish and potatoes with a slotted spoon and keep warm on a serving platter.
Strain cooking liquid into a bowl and let cool slightly, then whisk in mayonnaise and egg yolks until smooth.
Return the mixture to the pot over low heat, stirring constantly until it reaches sauce consistency without boiling.
Pour the saffron sauce over the fish and vegetables, garnish with fennel fronds, and serve with toasted bread.
cheapTips: Use frozen white fish instead of fresh to save 35%
Substitute regular paprika for expensive saffron threads

recipes.name: Galette Normande
recipes.description: Norman snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt, then cut in cold butter until mixture resembles breadcrumbs.
Add water gradually until dough just comes together, then chill for 20 minutes.
Peel, core, and thinly slice apples, then toss with sugar and cinnamon.
Roll dough into thin round sheet and transfer to baking sheet.
Arrange apple slices in overlapping pattern on dough, leaving 2-inch border.
Fold edges of dough over apples in rustic pleats.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 400°F for 25-30 minutes until golden.
cheapTips: Buy store-brand butter and flour in bulk
Use seasonal apples for better prices

recipes.name: Huîtres Normandes
recipes.description: Norman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Fill a plate with crushed ice as a base.
Shuck oysters carefully using an oyster knife, keeping liquid in shell.
Arrange shucked oysters on ice, checking for any shell fragments.
Combine minced shallots and white wine vinegar in small bowl.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice and add to shallot mixture.
Place small amount of vinaigrette in each oyster.
Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges and black pepper.
cheapTips: Buy oysters on sale from seafood counter mid-week
Ask fishmonger to shuck them if service is available

recipes.name: Rillettes de Tours à la Normande
recipes.description: Norman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork shoulder and belly into 2-inch chunks and place in pot.
Add water to cover, salt, pepper, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 2.5 hours until very tender.
Drain pork, reserving 1/2 cup cooking liquid, and let cool slightly.
Shred pork with two forks into fine strands.
Cook minced shallots in butter until soft, then add to shredded pork.
Mix in reserved cooking liquid until mixture reaches spreadable consistency.
Transfer to terrine or serving dish, cool, and refrigerate until firm.
Serve on toasted bread with pickles and cornichons.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder and belly on sale, freeze until ready
Make large batch and freeze portions for future meals

recipes.name: Arroz a Banda
recipes.description: Valencian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat fish stock in pot and steep saffron threads in warm broth.
Heat olive oil in wide paella pan over medium heat.
Sauté diced onion and garlic until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add rice and stir constantly for 2 minutes until lightly toasted.
Pour in saffron-infused stock and bring to boil, then reduce to simmer.
Season fish with salt and pepper, place on top of rice without stirring.
Cook uncovered for 18-20 minutes until rice is tender and fish is cooked through.
Remove from heat, squeeze lemon juice over dish, and serve fish alongside rice.
cheapTips: Use frozen fish stock instead of fresh, more economical
Buy saffron in bulk or use turmeric for similar color at lower cost

recipes.name: Arroz Negro
recipes.description: Valencian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat fish stock in pot and keep warm.
Cut squid bodies into rings and tentacles into pieces.
Heat olive oil in paella pan and sauté onion and garlic for 2 minutes.
Add squid pieces and cook for 3 minutes, then add white wine and simmer 1 minute.
Stir in rice and toast for 2 minutes until lightly golden.
Mix squid ink with warm stock, then add to rice pan.
Bring to boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 18-20 minutes until rice is tender.
Season with salt and pepper, let rest 2 minutes, and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy squid when on sale and freeze until needed
Check Asian markets for lower squid ink prices

recipes.name: All i Pebre
recipes.description: Valencian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Make a paste by grinding garlic with salt in mortar and pestle, stir in paprika.
Heat olive oil in heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sauté onion, red pepper, and potatoes for 5 minutes until starting to soften.
Add fish cubes and cook for 3 minutes, stirring gently.
Add garlic-paprika paste and stir to combine with vegetables.
Pour in water or fish stock and bring to boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 45-50 minutes until potatoes are tender and fish is cooked.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve in shallow bowls.
cheapTips: Catfish is more affordable than eel, both work equally well
Buy potatoes in bulk for better per-pound price

recipes.name: Espencat
recipes.description: Valencian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut eggplant lengthwise and score flesh, then roast skin-side up at 400°F for 15 minutes.
Roast whole red peppers and tomatoes on same tray for final 10 minutes of eggplant cooking.
Remove from oven and let cool slightly, then peel skin from vegetables.
Chop roasted vegetables into small pieces and transfer to bowl.
Mix in minced garlic and olive oil, then season with salt.
Let sit at room temperature for at least 5 minutes to allow flavors to develop.
Serve at room temperature with toasted bread slices for dipping or spreading.
cheapTips: Buy eggplant and peppers in season for lowest prices
Make large batch and refrigerate up to 5 days

recipes.name: Buñuelos de Bacalao
recipes.description: Valencian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: If using salted cod, soak in cold water for 24 hours, changing water every 6 hours.
Cook soaked cod in simmering water for 10 minutes, drain, cool, and flake into small pieces.
Whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper in bowl.
Beat egg with milk in separate bowl, then combine with flour mixture until smooth batter forms.
Fold in flaked cod, minced onion, and chopped parsley.
Heat oil in deep pan to 350°F.
Drop spoonfuls of batter carefully into hot oil and fry until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with aioli or tomato sauce.
cheapTips: Buy salt cod at Spanish markets for better prices
Reuse frying oil after cooling and straining

recipes.name: Coques Saladas
recipes.description: Valencian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix yeast with warm water and let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Combine flour and salt in bowl, then add yeast mixture and olive oil.
Knead dough for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place in oiled bowl, cover, and let rise 45 minutes until doubled.
Divide dough into 3 portions and shape into flat ovals about 1/2-inch thick.
Place on parchment-lined baking sheet and let rise 20 minutes uncovered.
Brush tops with olive oil, sprinkle with rosemary and coarse sea salt.
Bake at 400°F for 15-18 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
cheapTips: Buy bread flour in bulk for lower cost per pound
Make multiple batches at once and freeze extras

recipes.name: Lluç a la Sal
recipes.description: Valencian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Mix sea salt with egg white and water to create paste-like consistency.
Spread half of salt mixture on baking sheet.
Place fish fillet on top of salt base.
Cover fish completely with remaining salt mixture, pressing gently.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until salt crust is hard and golden.
Remove from oven and carefully crack and remove salt crust.
Fillet fish if needed, drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice, garnish with fresh herbs, and serve.
cheapTips: Use coarse sea salt in bulk or buy store brand for savings
Buy whole fish at market and request filleting service

recipes.name: Bollit de Peix
recipes.description: Valencian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until softened.
Add fish stock and bring to a boil, then add diced potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in saffron threads and season with salt and pepper.
Gently add fish fillets and shrimp to the broth and simmer for 8-10 minutes until cooked through.
Serve hot in bowls with the broth, fish, shrimp, and potatoes together.
cheapTips: Use frozen shrimp and fish to reduce costs
Substitute saffron with a pinch of turmeric

recipes.name: Gazpachos Manchegos
recipes.description: Valencian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, paprika, and salt in a bowl and gradually add water and olive oil to form a soft dough.
Knead the dough for 2 minutes until smooth, then let rest for 10 minutes covered.
Bring water to boil in a large pot and tear dough into irregular pieces.
Add dough pieces to boiling water and stir frequently to prevent sticking, cooking for 15 minutes.
In a separate pan, fry diced ham and garlic until crispy, then add to the soup.
Crack eggs into the pot while stirring gently to create egg threads, then simmer 2 minutes more.
Season with salt and serve hot in bowls.
cheapTips: Use bacon instead of cured ham to save money
Make in large batches and freeze portions

recipes.name: Moje de Peix
recipes.description: Valencian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until golden.
Sprinkle flour over the aromatics and stir constantly for 2 minutes to make a roux.
Gradually pour in fish stock while stirring to avoid lumps.
Add saffron threads and paprika, then bring to a simmer.
Cut fish into chunks and gently add to the broth, cooking for 10-12 minutes until opaque.
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot as a thick stew.
cheapTips: Use frozen white fish instead of fresh
Make your own fish stock from fish bones

recipes.name: Arròs amb Costra
recipes.description: Valencian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a wide paella pan over medium-high heat and brown diced chicken and meat on all sides.
Add minced garlic and diced tomato, cooking until tomato softens, about 3 minutes.
Stir in rice and coat well with oil for 2 minutes, then add green beans.
Pour hot stock over rice, stir in saffron and paprika, and do not stir again.
Simmer uncovered for 18-20 minutes until rice is tender and stock is absorbed.
Increase heat to high for the last 2-3 minutes to create a crispy golden crust (costra) on the bottom.
Remove from heat, cover with foil, and rest for 5 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs instead of breast for more flavor and lower cost
Substitute rabbit with pork shoulder

recipes.name: Gachasmigas
recipes.description: Valencian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring salted water to a boil in a large pot.
Slowly whisk in cornmeal while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent sticking and burning.
While cornmeal cooks, dice ham and mince garlic, then heat olive oil in a skillet.
Sauté garlic and ham in oil until crispy and fragrant.
Stir the ham and garlic mixture into the cooked cornmeal and season with black pepper.
Serve hot in bowls with the cooking liquid for a porridge-like consistency.
cheapTips: Buy cornmeal in bulk from ethnic markets
Use bacon instead of cured ham

recipes.name: Coca de Ametlla
recipes.description: Valencian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix warm water, yeast, and 1 teaspoon sugar in a bowl and let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Combine flour, remaining sugar, and salt, then make a well and add yeast mixture and olive oil.
Mix until a dough forms, then knead on a floured surface for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Let dough rise in an oiled bowl covered with a damp towel for 30 minutes until doubled.
Press dough onto an oiled baking sheet into a thin, even rectangle.
Brush the top with beaten egg and scatter sliced almonds evenly over the surface.
Bake at 375°F for 20-25 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
cheapTips: Buy almonds at discount stores or in bulk
Store leftover coca in an airtight container for 3 days

recipes.name: Horchata de Chufa con Fartons
recipes.description: Valencian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried tiger nuts in water for 2 hours, then drain and blend with 3 cups fresh water until very smooth.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve or cheesecloth, pressing to extract all liquid, then squeeze the pulp dry.
Stir sugar and salt into the horchata and chill until serving.
For fartons, mix flour, sugar, and baking powder, then combine beaten egg, milk, and vanilla separately.
Combine wet and dry ingredients until just mixed, then drop small spoonfuls onto a greased baking sheet.
Bake at 375°F for 12-15 minutes until golden, then cool slightly and dust with powdered sugar.
Serve horchata chilled in glasses alongside warm fartons for dipping.
cheapTips: Order tiger nuts online in bulk rather than specialty stores
Make horchata concentrate and store in fridge for a week

recipes.name: Arròs del Senyoret
recipes.description: Valencian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a wide paella pan and sauté minced garlic and diced onion until softened.
Add rice and stir for 2 minutes to coat with oil without browning.
Pour hot stock into the pan, stir in saffron and paprika, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium and simmer without stirring for 15-18 minutes until rice is nearly tender.
Arrange shrimp, fish chunks, and cleaned mussels on top of the rice in the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Cook until seafood is done, rice is tender, and mussels open.
Remove from heat, cover with foil, rest for 2 minutes, then serve directly from the pan.
cheapTips: Use frozen shrimp and mussels to reduce costs
Buy mixed seafood packages at warehouse stores

recipes.name: Tanda de Verdures
recipes.description: Valencian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pan and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until fragrant.
Add diced eggplant and zucchini, cooking for 5 minutes while stirring occasionally.
Stir in diced bell peppers and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes with their juices and season with salt, pepper, and herbs.
Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, stirring gently, until vegetables are tender and flavors meld.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot or at room temperature as a main dish or side.
cheapTips: Buy seasonal vegetables when prices are lowest
Use canned tomatoes instead of fresh if cheaper

recipes.name: Umbricelli al Tartufo
recipes.description: Umbrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook umbricelli until al dente, about 10-12 minutes.
While pasta cooks, warm olive oil in a large skillet over low heat and add thinly sliced garlic.
Cook garlic gently for 2 minutes until fragrant but not browned, then turn off heat.
Drain pasta, reserving 1 cup cooking water, and add pasta to the garlic oil.
Add truffle oil or finely shaved truffle and toss gently over low heat, adding pasta water a bit at a time to create a light sauce.
Remove from heat and stir in butter and grated parmesan until creamy.
Season with black pepper and serve immediately in warm bowls with extra parmesan on the side.
cheapTips: Use truffle oil instead of fresh truffles to save significantly
Substitute with a mixture of mushroom powder and olive oil

recipes.name: Torta al Testo
recipes.description: Umbrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, salt, and olive oil in a large bowl, then gradually add warm water until a soft dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes until smooth, then divide into 4 equal pieces and let rest 15 minutes.
Sauté spinach with minced garlic in olive oil until wilted, then season with salt and pepper.
Heat a cast-iron skillet or griddle over medium-high heat until very hot.
Roll each dough ball thin and cook on the hot skillet for 2 minutes per side until light golden spots appear.
Fold the cooked flatbread in half and fill with prosciutto, mozzarella, and cooked spinach.
Fold in half again to create a quarter-circle shape and serve immediately while warm.
cheapTips: Use regular spinach from frozen to save money on fresh greens
Substitute with deli ham if prosciutto is too expensive

recipes.name: Ciaramicola
recipes.description: Umbrian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Warm milk to 110°F and dissolve yeast in it, then let sit 5 minutes.
Cream together butter and sugar, then beat in eggs and vanilla extract.
Mix flour and salt together, then alternately add flour mixture and yeast mixture to butter mixture.
Knead dough for 8 minutes until smooth, then place in oiled bowl and let rise 1 hour until doubled.
Punch down dough and shape into a ring on parchment paper, then let rise 30 minutes more.
Preheat oven to 350°F and bake the ring for 25 minutes until golden brown.
Mix powdered sugar with water to create a glaze and drizzle over cooled cake, then top with sprinkles.
cheapTips: Make your own simple glaze instead of buying icing
Omit sprinkles or use natural food coloring to reduce cost

recipes.name: Panpepato
recipes.description: Umbrian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 325°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Chop almonds and candied orange peel into small pieces.
Warm honey and butter together in a saucepan until melted.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, pepper, and cinnamon in a bowl.
Stir honey mixture into flour mixture, then fold in almonds and candied orange peel.
Spread mixture onto baking sheet and bake for 25 minutes until golden.
Cool completely, then break into irregular pieces and dust with powdered sugar.
cheapTips: Use raw almonds instead of roasted and candied to save significantly
Replace candied orange peel with raisins or dried cranberries

recipes.name: Pasta alla Norcina
recipes.description: Umbrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook pasta according to package directions.
Heat butter in a large skillet and sauté minced garlic until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add ground pork and cook, breaking it apart, until browned completely.
Deglaze the pan with white wine and simmer for 2 minutes.
Reduce heat and stir in heavy cream, then simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Drain pasta and add to the sauce, tossing well to combine.
Stir in parmesan cheese and fresh parsley, then season with salt and pepper to taste.
cheapTips: Use ground pork instead of specialty truffle versions to save money
Buy parmesan in wedges and grate at home instead of pre-grated

recipes.name: Strangozzi al Tartufo
recipes.description: Umbrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt, then gradually add water and 1 tablespoon olive oil to form a stiff dough.
Knead dough for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then wrap and rest 20 minutes.
Divide dough into 4 pieces and roll each into a thin rope, then cut into irregularly shaped pasta pieces.
Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook pasta until al dente, about 4-5 minutes.
Melt butter in a large skillet with minced garlic and fresh thyme over low heat.
Drain pasta and add to butter mixture, tossing gently.
Drizzle with truffle oil, add grated parmesan, season with pepper, and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use truffle oil instead of fresh truffles to achieve flavor at a fraction of the cost
Make homemade pasta dough instead of buying fresh to save significantly

recipes.name: Ragu di Lepre
recipes.description: Umbrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut rabbit or pork into 2-inch chunks and pat dry with paper towels.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven and brown meat on all sides in batches, then set aside.
Finely chop onion, carrot, and celery together (soffritto) and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then deglaze with red wine.
Return meat to pot, add beef broth and bay leaf, then bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise in a 325°F oven for 2.5 hours, stirring occasionally, until meat is very tender.
Cook pasta according to package directions and serve topped with ragu and pan juices.
cheapTips: Substitute rabbit with pork shoulder which is significantly cheaper and has similar texture
Make a double batch and freeze half for future meals

recipes.name: Orzotto
recipes.description: Umbrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat broth in a separate pot and keep at a gentle simmer throughout cooking.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms and cook until golden, about 5 minutes, then set aside.
Toast barley in the same pan for 2 minutes, then deglaze with white wine.
Add warm broth one cup at a time, stirring frequently, waiting until liquid is mostly absorbed before adding more.
Continue for about 30-35 minutes until barley is tender and creamy.
Stir in butter, parmesan, cooked mushrooms, and season with salt and pepper before serving.
cheapTips: Buy barley in bulk from the grain or natural foods section to save significantly
Use any available mushrooms or omit for a simpler version

recipes.name: Flan di Tartufo
recipes.description: Umbrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 325°F and butter 4 ramekins or flan dishes thoroughly.
Heat milk and cream together until steaming, then remove from heat.
Whisk eggs with grated parmesan, salt, white pepper, and nutmeg until well combined.
Slowly temper eggs by adding hot milk mixture while whisking constantly.
Stir in truffle oil, then strain mixture through a fine sieve.
Pour into prepared ramekins and place in a water bath (bain-marie) that reaches halfway up the sides.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until centers are just set but still slightly jiggly, then cool and chill before serving.
cheapTips: Skip truffle oil and use regular mushroom powder or finely minced mushrooms mixed into the custard
Make in a loaf pan instead of individual ramekins for easier preparation

recipes.name: Nocino
recipes.description: Umbrian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Wearing gloves, cut green unripe walnuts into quarters and place in a clean glass jar.
Pour vodka or grain alcohol over walnuts until fully submerged.
Cover jar loosely and let steep in a cool, dark place for 2 weeks, shaking occasionally.
Heat sugar and water together to create a simple syrup, then cool completely.
Strain out walnut pieces and add cinnamon stick, cloves, and star anise to the infused liquid.
Stir in cooled simple syrup and let infuse for another 1-2 weeks.
Strain again and bottle for a digestive liqueur that improves with age.
cheapTips: Make in summer when green walnuts are in season for lowest cost
Use less expensive vodka or even everclear for the infusion base

recipes.name: Tozzetti
recipes.description: Umbrian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cream together butter and sugar until light and fluffy, then beat in eggs and vanilla.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and anise seeds together in a separate bowl.
Fold dry ingredients into wet ingredients, then fold in whole almonds.
Divide dough in half and shape each half into a long log on the baking sheet.
Bake logs for 20-25 minutes until golden and firm to the touch.
Cool slightly, then slice diagonally into 0.75-inch thick pieces and bake cut-side down for 8 minutes to harden into biscotti.
cheapTips: Buy almonds in bulk or use cheaper whole or sliced almonds from bulk bins
Omit or reduce anise seeds to lower cost further

recipes.name: Marmite Dieppoise
recipes.description: Norman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Chop onions and celery finely, then sauté in butter over medium heat for 5 minutes until softened.
Add flour to create a roux, stirring constantly for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine and stock, stirring to remove lumps, and bring to a simmer.
Add fish fillets and cook for 8 minutes until partially cooked.
Add shrimp, mussels, and scallops, cooking for another 5 minutes until seafood is done.
Stir in heavy cream and season with salt and pepper.
Simmer for 5 more minutes, then garnish with fresh parsley and serve in deep bowls.
cheapTips: Use frozen seafood instead of fresh to save 20-30%
Substitute half the cream with milk to reduce dairy costs

recipes.name: Cider-Braised Pork Chops
recipes.description: Norman dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat pork chops dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown pork chops 3-4 minutes per side, then remove and set aside.
In the same skillet, sauté diced onion for 3 minutes until softened.
Peel, core, and slice apples into thick rings.
Add cider and mustard to the skillet, scraping up browned bits, then return pork chops and add thyme.
Arrange apple slices over and around the chops, then cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove pork chops and apples to a plate, stir cream into the sauce, and simmer 2 minutes.
Pour sauce over pork chops and apples, then serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder chops instead of rib chops to save 40%
Use apple juice concentrate mixed with water instead of real cider

recipes.name: Calvados Apple Tart
recipes.description: Norman dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F and place pie crust in a tart pan, pricking with a fork.
Peel, core, and slice apples into thin half-moons.
Heat butter and sugar in a large skillet over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Add apples, vanilla, and cinnamon, cooking and stirring for 10 minutes until apples soften slightly.
Remove from heat and carefully add Calvados, stirring gently.
Arrange apple slices in overlapping circles on the crust, then pour any remaining liquid over top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until crust is golden and apples are tender.
Heat apricot jam with 1 tablespoon water and brush over warm tart as glaze before serving.
cheapTips: Skip the Calvados and use regular brandy or omit entirely for vanilla-cinnamon version
Buy apples in fall when they're cheapest

recipes.name: Flan Normand
recipes.description: Norman dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 325°F and place a 9-inch flan dish or pie pan in a larger roasting pan.
Combine 1/4 cup sugar and water in a saucepan, heating over medium heat until melted and light amber (about 5 minutes), then immediately pour into flan dish, coating bottom and sides evenly.
Heat milk and cream with cinnamon stick over medium heat until steaming, then remove from heat and let cool 5 minutes.
Whisk eggs, egg yolks, and remaining sugar together until pale and thick (about 3 minutes), then whisk in vanilla.
Slowly pour warm milk mixture into eggs while whisking constantly to temper them, then strain through a fine sieve.
Pour custard into caramel-lined flan dish.
Add hot water to roasting pan until it reaches halfway up the sides of the flan dish, then bake for 40-45 minutes until custard is set but slightly jiggly in the center.
Cool completely on a wire rack, then refrigerate at least 4 hours before running a knife around edges and inverting onto a serving plate.
cheapTips: Use evaporated milk instead of half heavy cream to cut dairy costs in half
Buy eggs from discount stores or in bulk

recipes.name: Crème Fraîche
recipes.description: Norman snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pour heavy cream into a clean glass jar with a lid.
Add buttermilk or sour cream and stir well to combine.
Cover loosely and let sit at room temperature (65-75°F) for 12-24 hours until thickened and tangy.
Stir once more, then cover tightly and refrigerate for up to 2 weeks before serving.
cheapTips: Make in bulk and store in fridge for up to 2 weeks instead of buying premade
Use regular heavy whipping cream from store brands, not boutique versions

recipes.name: Fruits de Mer Normands
recipes.description: Norman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Scrub mussels and clams under cold running water, removing beards from mussels and discarding any open shells.
Mince shallots finely and place in a large pot with butter and white wine over medium-high heat.
Add mussels and clams, cover, and cook for 5-7 minutes until shells open, shaking pot occasionally.
Add shrimp and oysters, cover again, and cook 3-4 minutes more until shrimp is pink and oyster shells open.
Discard any unopened shells, then transfer all seafood to a serving platter using a slotted spoon.
Boil remaining liquid in the pot for 2 minutes to reduce slightly, then pour over seafood.
Garnish generously with fresh parsley and lemon wedges, then serve immediately with crusty bread for dipping.
cheapTips: Buy seafood from fish counter at closing time for 20-30% discount
Mix in more mussels (cheapest option) and fewer oysters

recipes.name: Normande Sauce
recipes.description: Norman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mince shallot and mushrooms finely, then sauté in butter over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables, stirring constantly for 2 minutes to cook out raw flour taste.
Gradually add fish stock while stirring to prevent lumps, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Add white wine and simmer 3 more minutes to reduce slightly.
In a small bowl, whisk egg yolks and cream together, then slowly ladle hot sauce into eggs while whisking constantly to temper.
Pour egg mixture back into sauce pot and stir constantly over low heat for 2-3 minutes until thickened, never allowing it to boil.
Season with salt, white pepper, and lemon juice, then strain through a fine sieve if you prefer a smoother sauce.
cheapTips: Use chicken or vegetable stock instead of expensive fish stock
Substitute heavy cream with half-and-half to reduce fat and cost

recipes.name: Filet de Turbot à la Normande
recipes.description: Norman lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean mussels by scrubbing under cold water and removing beards, discarding any open shells.
Finely mince shallot and place in a wide skillet with half the butter, white wine, and fish stock.
Add mussels, cover, and steam for 4-5 minutes until they open, then remove with slotted spoon and set aside, discarding any unopened ones.
Pat turbot fillets dry and season with salt and pepper, then gently place in the simmering poaching liquid.
Simmer fillets gently for 6-8 minutes until just cooked through, adding shrimp for the last 2 minutes, then carefully transfer to warm serving plates.
Boil remaining poaching liquid until reduced by half, then whisk in cream and remaining butter away from heat.
Pour sauce around fish, arrange mussels and shrimp on top, then garnish with fresh lemon and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Substitute turbot with more affordable halibut or cod
Buy frozen mussels and shrimp instead of fresh to save significantly

recipes.name: Escalope de Veau à la Normande
recipes.description: Norman dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Place cutlets between plastic wrap and pound to 1/4-inch thickness using a meat mallet.
Set up breading stations with flour in one bowl, beaten eggs in another, and breadcrumbs in a third.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess, then dip in egg and coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Heat 3 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook breaded cutlets 3-4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through, then set aside on a warm plate.
In the same skillet, sauté sliced mushrooms and minced shallot in remaining butter for 4 minutes until tender.
Deglaze pan with white wine, scraping up browned bits, and simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream and simmer gently for 2-3 minutes until sauce thickens slightly, then season with salt and pepper.
Arrange escalopes on serving plates and spoon mushroom cream sauce over top.
cheapTips: Use chicken breast instead of veal to cut cost in half
Buy pre-sliced mushrooms from the store to save prep time

recipes.name: Crêpes Normandes
recipes.description: Norman breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine flour and salt in a large bowl, making a well in the center and adding eggs and half the milk.
Whisk eggs and milk together, gradually drawing flour in from the sides, then add remaining milk and water, stirring until smooth.
Let batter rest for 30 minutes at room temperature, then stir in melted butter.
Heat a lightly buttered 8-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until hot, then pour 1/4 cup batter in and immediately tilt pan to spread thinly and evenly.
Cook crêpe for about 1 minute until bottom is light golden, then flip and cook other side for 30 seconds, transferring to a plate.
Peel, core, and slice apples thinly, then cook in butter with sugar and cinnamon for 5 minutes until soft.
Add Calvados if desired and simmer 1 minute more, then remove from heat.
Fill each warm crêpe with apple mixture, fold in quarters, and serve immediately with a dollop of crème fraîche or whipped cream.
cheapTips: Skip the Calvados and use vanilla extract instead
Make crêpe batter the night before to save morning prep time

recipes.name: Empanada Galega
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, 2 tablespoons olive oil, and salt until a soft dough forms; knead for 5 minutes and let rest 30 minutes covered.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pan and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until soft.
Add ground beef and cook until browned, then stir in tomato sauce, paprika, bay leaf, and salt; simmer 15 minutes.
Divide dough in half and roll each portion into a thin circle on a floured surface.
Place one dough circle on a baking sheet, spread filling evenly on it, then top with second dough circle; seal edges by pressing with a fork.
Brush top with olive oil and bake at 375°F for 30-35 minutes until golden brown.
Cool for 5 minutes before slicing and serving.
cheapTips: Buy ground beef on sale and freeze it for later use
Make filling a day ahead to save prep time

recipes.name: Filloas
recipes.description: Galician breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk together flour, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
In another bowl, beat eggs and gradually add milk while stirring.
Pour wet ingredients into flour mixture and whisk until smooth batter forms; let rest 15 minutes.
Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat.
Pour 1/4 cup batter into the center and immediately tilt and rotate the pan to spread batter thinly across the entire surface.
Cook for 1-2 minutes until the bottom is light golden, then flip and cook the other side for 30 seconds.
Transfer to a plate and repeat with remaining batter, adding butter as needed.
Serve warm with honey drizzled over and melted butter on the side.
cheapTips: Buy eggs in bulk when on sale
Use store-brand milk and butter

recipes.name: Lacón con Grelos
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Place ham hock in a large pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil; discard first water and rinse the meat.
Return meat to pot with fresh water, add onion, garlic, and bay leaf; bring to boil then simmer for 90 minutes.
Peel and quarter potatoes, then add them to the pot after 90 minutes; cook for 20 minutes.
Wash turnip greens thoroughly, remove tough stems, and chop roughly.
Add greens to the pot and cook for 10-15 minutes until tender.
Remove meat from pot and shred or cut into pieces; season broth with salt and pepper.
Return meat to pot and serve hot in bowls with potatoes, greens, and broth.
cheapTips: Buy ham hocks at discount when they go on sale
Substitute with canned turnip greens if fresh unavailable

recipes.name: Percebes
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring salted water to a rolling boil in a large pot with garlic cloves.
Add percebes to boiling water and cook for 8-10 minutes until shells turn orange-red.
Drain percebes in a colander and rinse under cold water to cool.
Arrange percebes on a serving plate and drizzle with olive oil.
Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side for squeezing.
cheapTips: Buy percebes during their peak season (October-April) for better prices
Check Asian markets which often have lower prices than specialty seafood shops

recipes.name: Zamburiñas
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Season scallops with salt and add them to the skillet in a single layer; cook for 2 minutes on each side.
Sprinkle paprika over scallops and pour white wine around them; cook for 2 more minutes.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the scallops and stir gently.
Transfer to serving plates and drizzle with pan sauce; serve immediately hot.
cheapTips: Buy frozen scallops on sale and thaw before cooking
Skip the wine and use more lemon juice to save money

recipes.name: Caldeirada de Peixe
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until softened, about 5 minutes.
Peel and dice potatoes into small cubes; add to pot and cook for 10 minutes.
Pour in fish broth, add bay leaf, and bring to a simmer for 10 minutes until potatoes are almost tender.
Stir in tomato sauce and simmer for 5 minutes to blend flavors.
Cut fish fillets into chunks and gently add to the simmering broth; cook for 8-10 minutes until fish is opaque.
Season with salt and pepper, then remove from heat.
Ladle into bowls, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve hot with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Use frozen fish fillets instead of fresh for lower cost
Make your own broth from fish scraps or use store-brand

recipes.name: Raxo
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Season pork slices with salt and pepper, then add them to the skillet in a single layer; cook 2 minutes per side until lightly golden.
Remove pork to a plate and set aside.
Add minced garlic to the skillet and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Sprinkle paprika over the pan and stir, then pour in white wine and lemon juice; scrape up any browned bits.
Return pork to the skillet and toss gently in the sauce for 1-2 minutes.
Transfer to serving plates and spoon sauce over the meat; serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy pork loin on sale and slice it yourself with a sharp knife
Skip the wine and use more lemon juice and broth

recipes.name: Croquetas de Jamón Gallego
recipes.description: Galician snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat, then whisk in flour to create a roux; cook stirring for 2 minutes.
Gradually add milk while whisking constantly to avoid lumps; continue cooking and stirring until sauce thickens, about 8 minutes.
Finely dice jamón and fold into the béchamel sauce; season with salt and white pepper.
Spread mixture onto a parchment-lined baking sheet to cool for 30 minutes, then refrigerate for 1 hour until firm.
Shape cooled mixture into 12-16 croquette logs about 2 inches long.
Beat eggs in one bowl; place breadcrumbs in another bowl.
Dip each croquette in beaten egg, then coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pan and fry croquettes in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden; drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with lemon wedges or alioli sauce.
cheapTips: Use regular deli ham instead of expensive jamón
Make filling a day ahead to save prep time on serving day

recipes.name: Caldo de Marisco
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and minced garlic for 5 minutes until soft.
Pour in white wine and scrape up any browned bits; let simmer for 2 minutes.
Add fish broth and bring to a boil; add diced potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add clams and mussels, cover, and cook for 5 minutes until shells begin to open.
Add shrimp and fish chunks, then simmer gently for 5-8 minutes until seafood is cooked through.
Discard any unopened shells, season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into serving bowls, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Buy frozen seafood mix on sale instead of individual items
Use store-brand seafood broth to reduce costs

recipes.name: Nécoras
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring salted water to a boil in a large pot with bay leaf.
Carefully place live crabs into boiling water and cover; cook for 15-18 minutes depending on size.
Remove crabs with tongs and place on a cooling rack to cool slightly.
While crabs cool, heat olive oil in a small pan and sauté minced garlic for 30 seconds.
Arrange cooled crabs on a serving plate and drizzle with garlic-infused olive oil.
Serve hot or at room temperature with fresh lemon wedges and crusty bread for dipping in juices.
cheapTips: Buy crabs from local fish markets which often have better prices
Buy in season (fall/winter) when prices are lowest

recipes.name: Minestrone d'Umbria
recipes.description: Umbrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion, celery, and carrots for 5 minutes until softened.
Add diced potatoes and zucchini, then stir and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in canned tomatoes with juices and chicken broth, bringing the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Drain and rinse cannellini beans, then add them to the pot.
Stir in fresh spinach and cook for 3 minutes until wilted.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then serve hot with grated Parmesan cheese.
cheapTips: Buy carrots, celery, and onions in bulk; they store well for weeks
Use dried beans soaked overnight instead of canned to save 40%

recipes.name: Spaghetti al Tartufo Nero
recipes.description: Umbrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, melt butter in a large skillet over low heat and add minced garlic, stirring gently for 1 minute until fragrant.
Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain spaghetti and add it to the skillet with garlic butter.
Pour truffle oil over the pasta and toss gently to coat, adding pasta water a little at a time to create a light sauce.
Remove from heat and stir in half the Parmesan cheese.
Divide pasta between serving bowls and top with remaining Parmesan cheese and cracked black pepper.
cheapTips: Truffle oil is expensive; use less and compensate with extra Parmesan
Buy spaghetti on sale and store in a dry pantry for months

recipes.name: Polenta alla Norcina
recipes.description: Umbrian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: In a large pot, bring milk and vegetable broth to a simmer over medium heat.
Slowly whisk in cornmeal in a steady stream, stirring constantly to avoid lumps, for about 3 minutes.
Reduce heat to low and continue stirring frequently for 25-30 minutes until polenta is thick and pulls away from the sides of the pot.
In a separate skillet, heat olive oil and sauté diced onion and garlic for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add ground pork to the skillet, breaking it apart with a spoon, and cook for 5-7 minutes until browned.
Deglaze the skillet with white wine and simmer for 3 minutes, then season with salt and pepper.
Stir butter and Parmesan cheese into the cooked polenta until creamy.
Divide polenta into serving bowls and top with the pork sauce.
cheapTips: Buy cornmeal in bulk at warehouse stores for 50% savings
Use ground beef instead of pork to reduce cost by $1 per serving

recipes.name: Salame di Norcia
recipes.description: Umbrian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Grind pork and pork fat together in a food processor until well combined, keeping the mixture cold.
In a large bowl, combine ground pork mixture with salt, cure salt, crushed peppercorns, minced garlic, and white wine, mixing thoroughly.
Soak hog casings in lukewarm water for 20 minutes until pliable, then rinse gently.
Using a meat grinder with sausage attachment or a piping bag, stuff the casing with the pork mixture, leaving 2 inches at each end.
Tie the ends with kitchen twine and prick small holes all over the casing with a needle to release air.
Hang the salame in a cool (55-60°F), humid place with good air circulation for 4-6 weeks until completely dry and firm to the touch.
When ready to serve, slice thinly and serve with bread or cheese.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder and trim fat yourself instead of pre-ground meat
Make larger batches to amortize equipment and space costs

recipes.name: Capocollo di Todi
recipes.description: Umbrian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Trim the pork shoulder to form a compact roll, keeping the meat whole.
In a small bowl, combine salt, cure salt, cracked peppercorns, minced garlic, and chopped rosemary.
Rub the spice mixture all over the pork shoulder, working it into the surface thoroughly.
Place the rubbed pork in a non-reactive container, pour red wine over it, cover, and refrigerate for 7 days, turning daily.
Remove pork from brine and pat dry, then wrap it tightly in muslin cloth and tie with kitchen twine.
Hang the wrapped pork in a cool (55-60°F), humid room with good air circulation for 3-4 weeks until the exterior is dry and firm.
Unwrap the capocollo and slice very thinly to serve with bread, cheese, or in sandwiches.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder when it is on sale and cure immediately
Skip specialty muslin and use clean cotton kitchen towels instead

recipes.name: Porchetta di Perugia
recipes.description: Umbrian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat the pork belly dry and score the skin in a crosshatch pattern with a sharp knife, cutting only through the skin and fat layer.
In a small bowl, combine chopped fennel fronds, rosemary, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper.
Rub the herb mixture all over the meat side of the pork belly and roll it skin-side out, tying securely with kitchen twine at 2-inch intervals.
Rub the skin with olive oil and place the porchetta seam-side down on a roasting pan.
Roast at 325°F for 2.5-3 hours, basting with white wine every 30 minutes, until the skin is golden and crispy and the meat reaches 160°F internal temperature.
Allow the porchetta to rest for 15 minutes before carving.
Slice and serve warm or at room temperature with crusty bread and roasted vegetables.
cheapTips: Buy pork belly from butchers who may offer discounts for bulk orders
Substitute affordable dried rosemary for fresh to save 30%

recipes.name: Anguilla alla Perugina
recipes.description: Umbrian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Ask your fishmonger to clean and cut the eel into 2-inch pieces, or do this yourself by making a cut behind the head and peeling the skin down.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and sear the eel pieces for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Remove the eel pieces and set aside, then sauté diced onion, celery, and carrots for 5 minutes until softened.
Return the eel to the skillet and pour in white wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Add canned tomatoes with juices and bay leaves, then bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 25-30 minutes until the eel is tender and sauce has thickened.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve over soft polenta or with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Buy eel from Asian markets where prices are 40% lower than specialty fish shops
Ask the fishmonger to clean it free; they are usually happy to help

recipes.name: Biscottini da Tè
recipes.description: Umbrian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, cream together softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Beat in eggs one at a time, then stir in vanilla extract.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, anise seeds, and lemon zest.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients until a soft dough forms.
Transfer dough to a piping bag and pipe 3-inch-long fingers onto the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until golden and firm, then cool on a wire rack.
Serve with tea or coffee for dunking, or store in an airtight container for up to one week.
cheapTips: Buy flour in bulk and store in airtight containers
Use granulated sugar instead of specialty sugars to cut 20% off ingredient costs

recipes.name: Pulpo à Galega
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean the octopus under running water, removing the ink sac and mouth.
Bring a large pot of water with bay leaves and half the onion to a rolling boil.
Add the octopus and simmer for 45-50 minutes until tender, checking doneness with a fork.
In a separate pot, boil diced potatoes in salted water for 15-20 minutes until fork-tender, then drain.
Remove the cooked octopus, cool slightly, and cut the tentacles into bite-sized pieces.
Combine the octopus pieces and potatoes in a serving bowl.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and sprinkle with paprika powder and sea salt flakes.
Serve warm or at room temperature with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Buy frozen octopus, which is cheaper and requires no cleaning
Buy potatoes in bulk as they store for months

recipes.name: Caldo Galego
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add the ham bone or diced ham and chorizo, sliced into rounds, and cook for 5 minutes until the chorizo releases its oils.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil, then add diced potatoes.
Reduce heat to medium and simmer for 20 minutes until potatoes are almost tender.
Drain and rinse the white beans, then add them to the pot along with the chopped kale.
Simmer for another 10-12 minutes until the kale is tender and potatoes are completely cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot in deep bowls, drizzling each serving with additional olive oil if desired.
cheapTips: Use a ham hock from the grocery store butcher counter at 50% off regular ham prices
Buy kale when it is on sale and freeze portions for later use

recipes.name: Anguila Guisada
recipes.description: Galician dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut eel fillets into 3-inch pieces and pat dry with paper towels.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and minced garlic until softened.
Stir in tomato paste and paprika, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add eel pieces and brown on all sides for 3 minutes.
Deglaze with white wine and scrape up browned bits from the bottom.
Add stock and bay leaves, then simmer covered for 25 minutes until eel is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, then serve hot with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Buy eel from an Asian market where it's often cheaper than specialty fish shops.
Use vegetable stock instead of fish stock to reduce costs.

recipes.name: Choco à Galega
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Clean cuttlefish thoroughly, removing the skin and internal organs, then cut into rings and tentacles.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet and sauté minced garlic and diced onion for 2 minutes.
Add cuttlefish rings and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally until it begins to release liquid.
Sprinkle paprika and stir well, then pour in white wine and simmer for 10 minutes covered.
Season with salt and pepper, then cook uncovered for another 3 minutes until tender.
Finish with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice and serve hot in a shallow bowl with its own sauce.
cheapTips: Buy frozen cuttlefish which is less expensive than fresh and works equally well.
Purchase paprika in bulk from ethnic markets for significant savings.

recipes.name: Roblón de Betanzos
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork shoulder into large chunks and season generously with salt and pepper.
Dice salt pork and render it in a large Dutch oven over medium heat until crispy.
Remove rendered pork, then brown pork shoulder chunks on all sides in the fat.
Add diced onions, minced garlic, bay leaves, and thyme, cooking for 3 minutes.
Deglaze with white wine and scrape up browned bits, then add stock and rendered pork.
Cover and braise in a 325°F oven for 60 minutes until pork is very tender.
Remove bay leaves, adjust seasoning, and serve hot with the braising liquid spooned over.
cheapTips: Buy pork shoulder on sale and freeze for later use.
Use chicken stock instead of beef stock if on a tight budget.

recipes.name: Morcilla Gallega
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice onions finely and cook slowly in olive oil for 15 minutes until very soft and caramelized.
In a large bowl, combine pork blood, cooked rice, diced pork fat, minced garlic, paprika, salt, and pepper with the cooled onions.
Mix filling thoroughly until well combined, then carefully fill prepared pork casings using a funnel and meat stuffer.
Tie casings at 4-inch intervals to form individual morcilla links.
Bring a large pot of water to a gentle simmer and poach morcilla for 30 minutes, keeping temperature below 180°F.
Cool morcillas in ice water for 10 minutes, then refrigerate until ready to serve.
To serve, slice and pan-fry in a skillet with olive oil for 3 minutes per side until lightly crisped.
cheapTips: Order pork blood and casings from a butcher in advance to get bulk pricing.
Use store-brand paprika to save money on this key ingredient.

recipes.name: Tarta de Santiago
recipes.description: Galician snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9-inch round cake pan.
Grind blanched almonds into a fine powder using a food processor.
Beat eggs and sugar together until pale and thick, about 5 minutes.
Fold in ground almonds, melted butter, lemon zest, cinnamon, and salt until fully combined.
Pour batter into prepared pan and smooth the top.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until golden and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool completely in the pan, then dust the top generously with powdered sugar before serving.
cheapTips: Buy whole almonds and grind them yourself instead of purchasing pre-ground almond flour.
Use store-brand powdered sugar for dusting.

recipes.name: Poularda Galega
recipes.description: Galician dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat chicken dry and season inside and out with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven and brown chicken on all sides until golden, about 10 minutes total.
Remove chicken and sauté diced onions and minced garlic in the same pot for 3 minutes.
Return chicken to pot, then add wine, stock, bay leaves, and thyme sprigs.
Cover and simmer for 75 minutes until chicken is very tender and cooked through.
Remove chicken and let rest for 5 minutes, then carve into serving portions.
Strain cooking liquid, season to taste, and serve over chicken pieces with vegetables if desired.
cheapTips: Buy whole chickens on sale and freeze for later use.
Make your own stock from chicken bones to save money on broths.

recipes.name: Centolla à Galega
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F and if using shells, clean them thoroughly and place on a baking sheet.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil and sauté diced onion and minced garlic for 2 minutes.
Mix in breadcrumbs, paprika, crab meat, salt, and pepper until well combined.
Fill crab shells generously with mixture, or spoon into a buttered baking dish.
Drizzle remaining olive oil over the top and bake for 20 minutes until golden brown.
Squeeze lemon juice over the top immediately upon removing from oven.
Serve hot as an elegant appetizer or light main course.
cheapTips: Buy frozen crab meat which is much less expensive than fresh and works well in this dish.
Use panko breadcrumbs instead of regular for better texture at similar cost.

recipes.name: Camarones Gallegos
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat shrimp dry and season lightly with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn.
Add paprika and red pepper flakes, stirring for a few seconds.
Add shrimp and cook for 2 minutes on the first side, then flip and cook another 2 minutes.
Drizzle with lemon juice and toss to coat evenly, cooking for another 30 seconds.
Transfer to a serving platter and serve immediately with crusty bread to soak up the oil.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp which is more economical than fresh and thaws quickly.
Buy paprika at discount ethnic markets for significant savings.

recipes.name: Tajarin
recipes.description: Piedmontese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt, then create a well in the center and crack eggs into it.
Using a fork, gradually incorporate flour into eggs until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead dough for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide dough into quarters and roll very thin by hand or machine into long, thin ribbons.
Cut ribbons into fine strands and lay on a floured surface to dry slightly.
Bring salted water to a boil and cook tajarin for 2-3 minutes until they float and are tender.
In a skillet, melt butter with sage and minced garlic, then toss with drained pasta and grated cheese.
cheapTips: Make fresh pasta in bulk and freeze extras for quick future meals.
Use less expensive hard cheese or Pecorino Romano as a substitute for Parmigiano.

recipes.name: Brasato al Barolo
recipes.description: Piedmontese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pat beef dry and season generously with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven and brown beef on all sides until deeply caramelized.
Remove beef and sauté diced onions, carrots, celery, and minced garlic for 5 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, then deglaze with entire bottle of Barolo wine.
Return beef to pot, add stock and bay leaves, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise in a 325°F oven for 2.5 to 3 hours until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef and let rest, then strain braising liquid, reduce it by half on the stovetop, and pour over sliced meat to serve.
cheapTips: Use a less expensive Italian red wine if Barolo is too costly; the dish will still be delicious.
Buy beef chuck roast when on sale and freeze until ready to braise.

recipes.name: Bagna Cauda
recipes.description: Piedmontese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mince garlic cloves finely and cook in butter over low heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add anchovy fillets to the butter and stir constantly for 3 minutes until completely dissolved.
Pour in heavy cream and whisk to combine, keeping heat low and sauce warm.
Cut all vegetables into bite-sized pieces or sticks suitable for dipping.
Transfer the bagna cauda to a small fondue pot or warm serving dish.
Arrange vegetables and bread pieces on a platter around the warm sauce.
Serve immediately, keeping sauce warm throughout the meal.
cheapTips: Buy anchovies in bulk or use canned anchovy paste instead of jarred fillets
Use seasonal vegetables from a farmers market to save on produce costs

recipes.name: Panissa Vercellese
recipes.description: Piedmontese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried beans for 6 hours or overnight, then drain and rinse thoroughly.
Dice onion, garlic, and salami into small pieces.
Heat butter in a large pot and sauté onion, garlic, and salami for 5 minutes until fragrant.
Add drained beans and stir for 2 minutes, then pour in red wine and let it reduce.
Add warm vegetable broth and bring to a simmer, cooking for 20 minutes until beans soften.
Stir in rice and continue simmering for 18 minutes, stirring frequently until rice is tender.
Remove from heat and stir in grated Parmesan cheese until fully combined.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy dried beans in bulk from the rice and beans section to save significantly
Use affordable Arborio rice and skip expensive broth by making your own vegetable stock

recipes.name: Fritto Misto alla Piemontese
recipes.description: Piedmontese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Whisk together flour, eggs, milk, and a pinch of salt to create a smooth batter.
Cut zucchini and eggplant into 1/4-inch thick rounds, quarter mushrooms, slice apples, and crumble amaretto cookies.
Heat oil to 350°F in a heavy pot or deep fryer.
Dip vegetable and fruit pieces in batter to coat completely on all sides.
Carefully place battered items into hot oil in small batches, avoiding overcrowding.
Fry for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Remove with slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve immediately, sprinkled with powdered sugar and salt.
cheapTips: Buy apples on sale and use seasonal vegetables to reduce produce costs
Reuse frying oil by straining and storing in a cool place for multiple uses

recipes.name: Gnocchi di Ricotta e Spinaci
recipes.description: Piedmontese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
