Use affordable shredded cheese rather than specialty varieties

recipes.name: Chipa Soja
recipes.description: Paraguayan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Mix cassava starch, soy flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, beat eggs with melted butter and milk, then stir in shredded cheese.
Combine wet and dry ingredients until a thick, sticky dough forms.
Scoop tablespoon-sized portions onto the prepared baking sheet and shape into small mounds.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden brown and firm to the touch.
Cool on a wire rack before serving.
cheapTips: Buy soy flour in bulk at health food stores or online
Make a double batch and freeze for quick snacks

recipes.name: Caldo Blanco
recipes.description: Paraguayan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring chicken broth to a boil in a large pot with halved onion.
Add chicken breasts and simmer for 15 minutes until cooked through.
Remove chicken, shred it into bite-sized pieces, and return to broth.
Peel cassava and cut into 2-inch chunks, then add to the broth.
Cut corn into 2-inch pieces and add to the pot with salt and pepper.
Simmer for 15 minutes until cassava is tender.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Use chicken thighs instead of breasts for better flavor and lower cost
Buy cassava at Latin markets where it's cheaper than specialty stores

recipes.name: Cornish Pastie
recipes.description: British lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt, then cut in cold butter until mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs, add ice water to form dough, chill for 30 minutes.
Peel and dice potatoes, rutabaga, and onion into 0.5-inch cubes, cut beef into similar-sized pieces.
Preheat oven to 400°F and divide dough into 4 portions.
Roll each portion into a 6-inch circle on a floured surface.
Divide filling ingredients equally among pastie halves, season with salt and pepper, fold dough over and crimp edges with a fork.
Place on a baking sheet, brush with beaten egg, and cut small slits in the top.
Bake for 45 minutes until golden brown.
cheapTips: Buy cheaper cuts of beef and slow-roast; they work well in pasties
Make pastie dough from scratch to save versus buying premade pie crust

recipes.name: Gougères
recipes.description: French snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
Bring water, butter, salt, pepper, and nutmeg to a boil in a saucepan.
Remove from heat and stir in flour until a ball forms, cool for 5 minutes.
Beat in eggs one at a time, stirring vigorously after each addition, then fold in grated cheese.
Spoon golf-ball-sized portions onto prepared baking sheets, leaving 2 inches between each.
Bake for 25 minutes until puffed and golden brown.
Cool on baking sheet for 5 minutes before serving warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Use sharp cheddar cheese instead of expensive gruyere for similar results
Make dough ahead and refrigerate for convenient baking later

recipes.name: Empanada Gallega
recipes.description: Galician lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Make dough by mixing flour, salt, olive oil, and water until smooth, knead for 5 minutes, let rest 20 minutes.
Heat olive oil in a skillet and sauté diced onions and minced garlic until soft.
Add ground meat and cook until browned, then stir in tomato sauce and paprika, simmer 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 375°F and divide dough in half, roll each into a 12-inch circle.
Place one dough circle on a baking sheet, spread filling on half, fold over and seal edges.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 40 minutes until golden brown.
Cool slightly and slice into wedges before serving.
cheapTips: Use ground pork instead of beef for better flavor at lower cost
Make filling ahead and refrigerate to speed up assembly

recipes.name: Pastel de Nata
recipes.description: Portuguese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat milk and cream together in a saucepan until steaming, do not boil.
Whisk egg yolks with sugar until pale, then whisk in cornstarch and salt.
Slowly pour hot milk mixture into egg mixture while whisking constantly.
Return to saucepan and cook over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly until thickened, add vanilla and cinnamon.
Press plastic wrap directly onto custard surface and cool to room temperature, then refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 475°F and lightly grease a muffin tin, cut puff pastry into 3-inch squares and press into cups.
Spoon custard into pastry cups and bake for 15-18 minutes until custard is set and pastry is puffed and golden.
Cool in pan for 5 minutes, dust with cinnamon, and serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Use store-bought puff pastry to save time and effort
Make custard filling a day ahead for easier assembly

recipes.name: Briouate
recipes.description: Moroccan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Melt butter and mix with almond butter, honey, cinnamon, salt, and water until combined.
Lay one phyllo sheet on a clean surface and brush lightly with melted butter.
Spread about 1 tablespoon almond mixture along one edge, fold sides in and roll tightly into a cigar shape.
Place seam-side down on prepared baking sheet and repeat with remaining phyllo and filling.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Dust generously with confectioners sugar while still warm and serve at room temperature.
cheapTips: Buy phyllo dough on sale and keep frozen for months
Substitute tahini for almond butter at lower cost

recipes.name: Empanada de Atún
recipes.description: Spanish lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Make dough by combining flour, salt, cut-up cold butter, egg yolk, and water until a ball forms, chill 30 minutes.
Sauté diced onion in a skillet until soft, add drained tuna and cook for 3 minutes.
Chop roasted peppers, hard-boiled eggs, and olives, then mix into tuna filling and cool completely.
Preheat oven to 375°F and divide dough in half, roll each into a 10-inch circle.
Place one dough circle on a baking sheet, spread filling on half, fold over and crimp edges with a fork.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 35-40 minutes until golden brown.
Cool for 5 minutes and slice into wedges before serving.
cheapTips: Buy canned tuna on sale and stock up for budget meals
Use jarred roasted peppers to save chopping time

recipes.name: Cranachan
recipes.description: Scottish snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast the rolled oats in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring frequently, until lightly golden and fragrant.
Transfer toasted oats to a plate and let cool slightly, then stir in melted butter and a pinch of salt.
In a large bowl, whip heavy cream to soft peaks using an electric mixer or whisk.
Fold Greek yogurt and honey into the whipped cream gently until combined, then add whisky if using.
Layer the cream mixture with toasted oats and fresh raspberries in serving glasses or bowls, starting and ending with cream.
Serve immediately or refrigerate up to 2 hours before serving.
cheapTips: Buy frozen raspberries in bulk when on sale and thaw before using.
Use store-brand heavy cream and yogurt to reduce costs.

recipes.name: Mince Pie
recipes.description: British snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt in a bowl, then cut cold butter into small cubes and work into flour with your fingertips until resembling breadcrumbs.
Add cold water gradually, mixing gently until dough just comes together; wrap in plastic and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Combine mincemeat, brandy, and finely diced apple in a small bowl.
Preheat oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Roll out dough between two sheets of plastic wrap to 1/8-inch thickness and cut 24 circles using a 2.5-inch round cutter.
Place 1 teaspoon of filling on each of 12 circles, brush edges with beaten egg, and top with remaining circles, pressing edges to seal.
Brush tops with egg wash and prick with a fork, then bake for 15-18 minutes until golden brown.
Cool on a wire rack and dust with powdered sugar before serving.
cheapTips: Make your own mincemeat from dried fruit, raisins, and suet to save significantly.
Prepare dough ahead and freeze up to 1 month.

recipes.name: Soufganiyah
recipes.description: Jewish snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine warm water, yeast, and 1 tablespoon sugar in a small bowl and let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour, salt, and remaining sugar in a large bowl, then add yeast mixture and knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover dough with a damp cloth and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Roll out dough to 1/4-inch thickness and cut into 3-inch circles using a glass or cookie cutter.
Let cut dough rest for 15 minutes covered.
Heat oil in a deep pot or fryer to 350°F and fry doughnuts 1-2 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels, then use a skewer to poke a hole and fill with jam using a pastry bag or spoon.
Dust generously with powdered sugar while still warm and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Use store-brand jam to reduce filling costs.
Reuse frying oil by straining and storing in the refrigerator.

recipes.name: Hot Cross Bun
recipes.description: British breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Combine warm milk, yeast, and 1 tablespoon sugar in a bowl and let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour, remaining sugar, salt, and spices in a large bowl, then add yeast mixture, melted butter, and egg.
Knead dough for 10 minutes until smooth, then fold in currants and let rise 1 hour covered until doubled.
Divide dough into 12 equal balls, place on a parchment-lined baking sheet, cover, and let rise 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°F and pipe a cross on each bun using a pastry bag with plain tip and thin flour paste.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden brown and buns sound hollow when tapped.
While still warm, brush with a glaze made from 1/4 cup water and 2 tablespoons sugar heated together.
Cool slightly before serving.
cheapTips: Buy currants in bulk at ethnic markets or substitute with raisins.
Make the cross with a simple flour paste instead of piping bags.

recipes.name: Bundt Cake
recipes.description: American snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a Bundt pan thoroughly with butter.
Cream butter and sugar together in a large bowl for 2-3 minutes until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, then add vanilla extract and mix until combined.
Whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt in a separate bowl.
Alternate adding flour mixture and sour cream to the butter mixture in three additions, mixing gently after each.
Sprinkle 1/3 of the cinnamon-brown sugar mixture into the prepared pan, then add half the batter, another 1/3 of the mixture, remaining batter, and top with remaining cinnamon mixture.
Bake for 45-50 minutes until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 15 minutes, then invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
cheapTips: Use store-brand sour cream and butter.
Skip glazing and dust with powdered sugar instead for less cost.

recipes.name: Sopa Paraguaya
recipes.description: Paraguayan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F and grease a 9-inch round baking dish with butter.
Sauté diced onion in butter over medium heat until softened, about 5 minutes.
Combine corn flour, fresh corn kernels, sautéed onion, cheese, and salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Beat eggs in a separate bowl and add to the corn mixture along with milk or broth, stirring until you have a thick batter-like consistency.
Pour mixture into prepared baking dish and smooth the top.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until golden brown and a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Cool for 5 minutes before serving warm.
Cut into wedges and serve as a side dish or light meal.
cheapTips: Use frozen corn to save money and reduce prep time.
Buy block cheese and shred it yourself instead of pre-shredded.

recipes.name: Chipa
recipes.description: Paraguayan breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Mix cassava starch, shredded cheese, and salt in a large bowl.
Beat eggs with melted butter and milk, then pour into the starch mixture and mix until a dough forms.
Add anise seeds if using and knead gently for 1-2 minutes until combined.
Shape dough into long oval rings or sticks about 4 inches long and 1/2 inch thick.
Place on prepared baking sheet spacing them 2 inches apart.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown and slightly crispy on the outside.
Cool on wire rack and serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Buy cassava starch from Latin American markets where it is cheaper.
Use basic cheddar instead of fresh cheese for lower cost.

recipes.name: Empanada Paraguaya
recipes.description: Paraguayan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour and salt in a bowl, cut in cold butter until resembling breadcrumbs, then add cold water until dough comes together; refrigerate 30 minutes.
Brown ground beef with diced onion in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it apart as it cooks, about 8 minutes; drain excess fat.
Stir 1 beaten egg and shredded cheese into the cooked beef; season with salt and pepper and cool slightly.
Roll out dough thin between plastic wrap and cut into 3-inch squares.
Place 1 tablespoon filling on each square, fold diagonally to form a triangle, and seal edges by pressing with a fork.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F and fry empanadas in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.
Optional: brush with beaten egg before frying for a shinier finish.
cheapTips: Buy ground beef on sale and freeze until ready to use.
Strain and reuse frying oil by filtering through coffee filters.

recipes.name: Pastel Mandio
recipes.description: Paraguayan snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix cassava starch, shredded cheese, and salt in a large bowl.
Beat eggs with melted butter and milk, then pour into starch mixture and knead until a sticky dough forms.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 350°F.
Using wet hands or two spoons, carefully form dough into oblong patties about 3 inches long and 1/2 inch thick.
Gently slide each patty into hot oil using a spoon, frying 3-4 at a time without overcrowding.
Fry for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve warm as a snack or side dish.
cheapTips: Make in bulk and freeze unfried for easy reheating later.
Use American cheese instead of fresh mozzarella to reduce cost.

recipes.name: Chipa Guazú
recipes.description: Paraguayan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F and lightly oil a 9-inch baking dish.
Sauté diced onion in butter over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until softened.
In a blender or food processor, blend 2 cups of corn kernels with milk until slightly chunky (not smooth).
Mix blended corn with whole corn kernels, sautéed onion, shredded cheese, beaten eggs, salt, and pepper.
Pour mixture into prepared baking dish and smooth the top.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until golden brown and a knife inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool for 5 minutes before cutting into squares.
Serve warm as a main dish or side.
cheapTips: Buy frozen corn in bulk when on sale; no thawing needed.
Use sharp cheddar instead of fresh cheese for better flavor at lower cost.

recipes.name: Atchara
recipes.description: Filipino snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and julienne the green papaya into thin matchsticks.
Slice the carrots into thin matchsticks and cut the bell pepper into strips.
Combine vinegar, sugar, and salt in a pot and bring to a boil.
Add minced ginger, crushed garlic cloves, and black peppercorns to the boiling mixture.
Pour the hot vinegar mixture over the papaya and vegetables in a clean jar.
Let cool to room temperature, then cover and refrigerate for at least 24 hours before serving.
Shake the jar occasionally to distribute flavors evenly.
cheapTips: Buy green papaya from Asian markets for better prices
Make large batches and store for weeks to maximize value

recipes.name: Balık Turşusu
recipes.description: Turkish snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut white fish fillets into bite-sized pieces and lightly salt them.
Heat olive oil in a large pan and pan-fry the fish pieces for 3-4 minutes per side until light golden.
Remove fish and set aside on paper towels.
In the same pan, sauté sliced onions and carrots with crushed garlic for 5 minutes until softened.
Add vinegar, water, bay leaves, and peppercorns to the vegetables and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 10 minutes to develop the pickling brine.
Layer the cooked fish and vegetables in sterilized jars, then pour hot brine over them.
Cool completely, seal, and refrigerate for at least 3 days before serving.
cheapTips: Use frozen white fish fillets which are often cheaper than fresh
Buy onions and carrots in bulk from discount grocers

recipes.name: Chutney Mango
recipes.description: Indian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel and dice the mangoes into small chunks, removing the pit.
Combine diced mango, sugar, and vinegar in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Add minced ginger, crushed garlic, and chopped red chilies to the pot.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add mustard seeds, salt, and turmeric, then simmer for 5 more minutes until thickened.
Transfer to clean jars while still hot and seal tightly.
Cool to room temperature before refrigerating for up to 2 weeks.
cheapTips: Buy mangoes when they're on sale and freeze them for off-season use
Make large batches to reduce per-serving cost

recipes.name: Daikon Radish Pickle
recipes.description: Japanese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut daikon radish into thin half-moon slices or matchsticks.
In a bowl, whisk together rice vinegar, sugar, salt, and water until sugar dissolves.
Layer daikon slices in a clean jar with the dried chili pepper and garlic clove.
Pour the vinegar mixture over the daikon until completely submerged.
Add kombu seaweed if using and stir gently.
Cover and let sit at room temperature for 2-3 hours, then refrigerate.
Serve chilled as a side dish or snack, keeps up to 2 weeks refrigerated.
cheapTips: Buy daikon radish from Asian markets where it's much cheaper
Rice vinegar from discount stores provides best value

recipes.name: Fukujinzuke
recipes.description: Japanese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice daikon, cucumber, carrot, and lotus root into small uniform cubes.
In a pot, combine rice vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, mirin, and salt.
Bring the mixture to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Add diced vegetables and sliced red chili to the hot liquid.
Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat and let cool to room temperature.
Transfer to clean jars, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and refrigerate.
Serve chilled as a topping for rice or as a breakfast side dish.
cheapTips: Skip lotus root if expensive; daikon and cucumber are sufficient
Buy vegetables on sale and prep multiple jars at once

recipes.name: Gari
recipes.description: Ghanaian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Peel fresh ginger root with a spoon or knife and slice thinly into matchsticks.
In a pot, combine vinegar, sugar, water, and salt.
Bring the mixture to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Add sliced ginger, sliced red chili, and crushed garlic cloves to the boiling liquid.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes.
Pour ginger and brine into a clean jar and cool to room temperature.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 24 hours before serving with meals or as a snack.
cheapTips: Buy fresh ginger in bulk and peel only what you need
Store in the freezer to extend shelf life and availability

recipes.name: Halim
recipes.description: Iranian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak wheat grains, chickpeas, and split peas in water for 2 hours, then drain.
Cut lamb into small cubes and dice onions.
Heat ghee in a large heavy pot and sauté onions until golden brown.
Add lamb pieces and brown them on all sides for 5 minutes.
Add soaked grains, chickpeas, and split peas to the pot with 8 cups water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 2 hours, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Add turmeric, salt, and pepper, then continue cooking for 30 minutes until mixture becomes very thick and porridge-like.
Stir constantly in the final stages to achieve a smooth, creamy consistency.
cheapTips: Buy lamb on sale and freeze for later use
Purchase dried legumes in bulk bins for significant savings

recipes.name: Krasnaya Ikra
recipes.description: Russian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Prepare a brine by dissolving salt and sugar in boiling water with bay leaves, peppercorns, and mustard seeds.
Cool the brine completely to room temperature.
Gently rinse salmon roe under cool water to remove any debris.
Place the roe in a sterilized glass jar with a crushed garlic clove.
Pour the cooled brine over the salmon roe, ensuring it's fully covered.
Seal the jar and refrigerate for 24-48 hours before serving.
Serve chilled on toasted bread or with sour cream as a breakfast or appetizer.
cheapTips: Buy salmon roe during sales or from fishmongers at end of day
Make small batches only if fresh ingredients aren't readily available

recipes.name: Limpa Pickle
recipes.description: Swedish lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice cucumbers into spears or rounds and thinly slice onion.
In a pot, combine vinegar, sugar, water, and salt, then bring to a boil.
Add mustard seeds, black peppercorns, and fresh dill to the boiling brine.
Layer cucumbers and onion slices in clean jars.
Pour the hot brine over cucumbers until fully submerged.
Cool to room temperature, then seal and refrigerate.
Allow flavors to develop for at least 24 hours before serving with sandwiches or cured meats.
cheapTips: Buy cucumbers in bulk when in season and freeze-pickle extras
Use dried dill instead of fresh to reduce costs

recipes.name: Mango Pickle
recipes.description: Indian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Wash green mangoes and cut into thin slices or strips, removing the pit.
Mix mango pieces with salt in a clean jar and let sit for 2 hours at room temperature.
In a small pan, heat oil and add mustard seeds and fenugreek seeds until they pop.
Add minced ginger, crushed garlic, and asafetida to the oil mixture.
Stir in red chili powder and turmeric powder, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour the spiced oil over the salted mango slices and mix thoroughly.
Transfer to clean jars, cover tightly, and let cure at room temperature for 7-10 days before serving.
Keep refrigerated and shake jar occasionally to distribute oils.
cheapTips: Buy raw green mangoes in bulk during mango season from Indian markets
Use inexpensive vegetable oil instead of premium coconut oil

recipes.name: Horchata de Arroz
recipes.description: Spanish snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak the rice in water for 20 minutes, then drain thoroughly.
Blend the soaked rice with 2 cups of fresh water until completely smooth and milky white.
Strain the mixture through a fine mesh strainer lined with cheesecloth, pressing to extract all liquid.
Combine the strained rice liquid with remaining 3 cups water, milk, sugar, cinnamon, and vanilla in a large pitcher.
Stir until sugar dissolves completely and chill for at least 1 hour.
Stir again before serving and pour over ice into glasses.
cheapTips: Buy rice in bulk from ethnic markets for significant savings
Make large batches and store in the refrigerator for up to 5 days

recipes.name: Cream of Rice
recipes.description: American breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
Slowly whisk in the cream of rice cereal while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Stir in butter, milk, brown sugar, salt, and cinnamon until combined.
Simmer for 2-3 more minutes until thick and creamy.
Pour into bowls and serve immediately while hot.
cheapTips: Store-brand cream of rice is significantly cheaper than name brands
Use evaporated milk instead of fresh milk to extend shelf life

recipes.name: Farina
recipes.description: Italian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat milk in a saucepan over medium heat until it begins to steam.
Slowly pour farina into the hot milk while whisking constantly to prevent lumps from forming.
Continue stirring and reduce heat to low, cooking for 8-10 minutes until thickened.
Stir in butter, sugar, salt, and cinnamon until fully combined.
Pour into bowls and serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy semolina flour in bulk from Italian or Middle Eastern markets
Use generic milk brands to save money

recipes.name: Manná
recipes.description: Portuguese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat milk in a large saucepan over medium heat until steaming.
Slowly sprinkle semolina into the hot milk while whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Stir continuously and cook for 10-12 minutes until the mixture thickens significantly.
Remove from heat and stir in butter, honey, cinnamon, and salt.
Whisk in the egg yolk quickly, stirring well to combine.
Divide into bowls and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy semolina in bulk at warehouse stores
Use store-brand honey instead of premium varieties

recipes.name: Kaanga Pirau
recipes.description: Māori lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut corn kernels from the cob and set aside; reserve the cobs.
Dice potatoes and onion into small pieces.
Heat butter in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion until softened.
Add diced potatoes and cook for 5 minutes while stirring occasionally.
Add corn kernels, cobs, milk, salt, and pepper to the pot.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 20-25 minutes until potatoes are very tender.
Remove corn cobs and mash the soup slightly to thicken it, leaving some texture.
cheapTips: Buy corn in season and freeze kernels for year-round savings
Use canned or frozen corn if fresh is unavailable

recipes.name: Caldo de Arroz
recipes.description: Portuguese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and dice onion, carrots, and celery.
Sauté the vegetables for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Pour in chicken broth and add bay leaves, bringing to a boil.
Add rice and stir well, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-18 minutes until rice is tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove bay leaves and serve hot.
cheapTips: Make your own broth from chicken bones to reduce costs significantly
Buy rice in bulk from warehouse stores

recipes.name: Milho Cozido
recipes.description: Brazilian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Fill a large pot with water and bring to a rolling boil.
Add salt to the boiling water.
Place corn cobs into the pot carefully.
Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes until corn kernels are tender.
Drain corn cobs and place on a serving platter.
Brush generously with butter and season with salt and pepper.
cheapTips: Buy corn in bulk at farmers markets when in season
Use frozen corn cobs if fresh are unavailable

recipes.name: Barley Porridge
recipes.description: Scottish breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring water to a boil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat.
Add pearl barley and salt, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 20-25 minutes until barley is very soft.
Stir in milk and butter, heating through without boiling.
Drizzle with honey and stir to combine.
Serve warm in bowls.
cheapTips: Buy pearl barley in bulk from health food stores
Store in airtight containers to keep fresh for months

recipes.name: Zhoug
recipes.description: Israeli breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Roughly chop parsley, cilantro, garlic, and jalapeño into manageable pieces.
Add herbs and vegetables to a food processor along with lemon juice and salt.
Pulse while slowly drizzling in olive oil until sauce reaches desired consistency.
Add cumin and pulse once more to combine.
Transfer to a bowl and serve with bread, eggs, or vegetables.
cheapTips: Buy herbs in bulk at farmers markets and freeze in ice cube trays
Use regular olive oil instead of premium for cost savings

recipes.name: Baguette
recipes.description: French breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, salt, and yeast in a large bowl until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough by hand for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover with a damp cloth and let rise at room temperature for 4-5 hours until doubled.
Shape the dough into a long baguette form on a baking sheet.
Cover and let rise for 1-2 hours until puffy.
Score the top with a sharp knife in diagonal cuts.
Bake in a preheated 450°F oven for 25-30 minutes until golden brown and crusty.
cheapTips: Buy flour from bulk bins to save significantly
Make multiple baguettes at once to maximize oven efficiency

recipes.name: Miso Paste
recipes.description: Japanese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried soybeans in water overnight, then drain and rinse thoroughly.
Cook soybeans in fresh water for 2-3 hours until very soft and mashable.
Drain soybeans and let cool to room temperature.
Mix koji spores with salt, then combine with cooled soybeans and mash until paste-like.
Transfer to a clean glass jar and pack down firmly to remove air pockets.
Cover with plastic wrap and place in a dark, warm location (68-75°F) for 6-12 months, stirring occasionally.
cheapTips: Buy soybeans in bulk from Asian markets
Koji spores are reusable from previous batches

recipes.name: Nattō
recipes.description: Japanese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak soybeans in water for 8 hours, then drain and rinse.
Cook soybeans in fresh water for 45 minutes until tender but not mushy.
Drain soybeans and let cool to 104°F (40°C).
Mix natto spores with a small amount of warm water, then stir into cooked soybeans.
Place in an insulated container or oven with light on and maintain temperature between 100-108°F for 16-24 hours.
Remove when beans develop sticky, stringy coating and strong aroma.
cheapTips: Buy natto spores online in bulk
Reuse spores from finished batches for next fermentation

recipes.name: Oba Koro
recipes.description: Nigerian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat palm oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add ginger powder and cayenne pepper, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add roasted peanuts, cashews, and coconut flakes, stirring constantly for 3-4 minutes.
Pour in honey and stir well to coat all ingredients evenly.
Continue cooking and stirring for 5-7 minutes until mixture is caramelized and aromatic.
Spread onto parchment paper to cool completely before breaking apart and storing.
cheapTips: Buy bulk nuts at Sam's Club or Costco
Use raw nuts and toast them yourself to save 30%

recipes.name: Pappadam
recipes.description: Indian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix urad dal flour, salt, cumin seeds, and peppercorns in a bowl.
Gradually add water while kneading into a stiff dough, adding water slowly until consistency is firm.
Knead dough for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Divide dough into small balls and place on plastic wrap or parchment.
Using another piece of plastic or a thin spoon, roll each ball into extremely thin, translucent rounds about 6 inches wide.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F and fry each pappadam for 2-3 seconds until puffed and crispy, turning once.
Drain on paper towels and store in an airtight container once cooled.
cheapTips: Buy urad dal flour online in bulk from Indian grocers
Store dried pappadums for weeks in airtight containers

recipes.name: Pikliz
recipes.description: Haitian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Prepare a clean glass jar by washing with hot water and letting it air dry.
Layer cabbage, carrots, shallots, and garlic in the jar.
Tuck whole Scotch bonnet peppers and thyme sprigs throughout the vegetables.
In a separate bowl, mix vinegar and salt until salt dissolves completely.
Pour vinegar mixture into jar until vegetables are fully submerged.
Cover jar loosely and let sit at room temperature for at least 3 days before eating.
cheapTips: Make large batches and refrigerate for months
Buy vegetables when on sale and freeze until ready to pickle

recipes.name: Tsukemono
recipes.description: Japanese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice cucumbers into thin rounds or spears, sprinkle with salt, and let sit for 30 minutes.
Rinse cucumber pieces thoroughly and squeeze out excess water gently.
In a bowl, combine rice vinegar and sugar, stirring until sugar dissolves.
Layer cucumbers in a clean glass jar with kombu seaweed, red chili, and ginger slices.
Pour vinegar mixture over cucumbers until fully covered.
Cover jar and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, though flavors improve over 1-2 days.
cheapTips: Use regular cucumbers instead of pickling varieties
Make in bulk when cucumbers are in season

recipes.name: Cháo
recipes.description: Vietnamese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse jasmine rice under cold water twice until water runs clear.
Bring chicken broth and water to a boil in a large pot.
Add rinsed rice and stir occasionally for 2-3 minutes.
Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 30-40 minutes, stirring frequently, until rice breaks down into a creamy porridge.
Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
Serve in bowls topped with green onions, fried shallots, and fresh cilantro.
cheapTips: Make large batches and freeze portions for quick reheating
Buy jasmine rice in bulk from Asian markets

recipes.name: Cream of Wheat
recipes.description: American breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring milk to a simmer in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Slowly whisk in cream of wheat cereal while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Reduce heat to low and stir frequently for 3-4 minutes until creamy and thickened.
Stir in butter, sugar, salt, and cinnamon until fully combined.
Cook for 1-2 more minutes until reaching desired consistency.
Pour into bowls and serve immediately while hot.
cheapTips: Buy store-brand cream of wheat instead of Cream of Wheat brand
Use budget milk or evaporated milk to reduce cost

recipes.name: Bubur
recipes.description: Indonesian breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse glutinous rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Bring water to a boil in a large pot and add rinsed rice.
Stir and simmer for 20-25 minutes until rice is very soft and broken down.
Pour in coconut milk and add pandan leaves, stirring well.
Add palm sugar and salt, simmering for another 5 minutes while stirring occasionally.
Remove pandan leaves and adjust sweetness and consistency as desired.
Serve warm in bowls and drizzle with brown sugar syrup if desired.
cheapTips: Use canned coconut milk instead of fresh
Substitute pandan leaves with vanilla extract if unavailable

recipes.name: Lugaw
recipes.description: Filipino breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat a large pot and lightly toast minced garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and water, bringing to a boil.
Add sliced ginger and rinsed rice, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 35-40 minutes, stirring frequently, until rice completely breaks down into a creamy porridge.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Remove ginger slices and stir in most of the green onions.
Serve hot in bowls, topped with remaining green onions.
cheapTips: Use homemade broth or budget store brands
Make large batches and portion for quick weekday breakfasts

recipes.name: Ciabatta
recipes.description: Italian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, yeast, and salt in a large bowl until shaggy dough forms.
Let dough rest 15 minutes, then stretch and fold it every 30 minutes for 2 hours until it becomes elastic and bubbly.
Transfer dough to an oiled surface and gently shape into a rectangle, being careful not to deflate the bubbles.
Place on parchment paper and let rise for 1 hour until puffy.
Preheat oven to 450°F and place a baking sheet inside.
Carefully transfer ciabatta to hot baking sheet and bake 25-30 minutes until golden brown and crusty.
Cool on a wire rack for at least 10 minutes before slicing.
cheapTips: Buy flour and yeast in bulk to reduce costs
Use tap water instead of filtered water

recipes.name: Sourdough
recipes.description: American breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, and sourdough starter in a bowl until all flour is hydrated.
Let rest 30 minutes, then add salt and mix thoroughly.
Perform stretch and fold every 30 minutes for 2.5 hours.
Transfer dough to a floured banneton basket and refrigerate overnight.
Preheat oven to 500°F with Dutch oven inside for 45 minutes.
Score the top of the cold dough with a knife and carefully place in hot Dutch oven.
Bake covered for 20 minutes, then uncovered for 25 minutes until deep golden brown.
Cool completely on a wire rack before slicing.
cheapTips: Maintain a sourdough starter at home to eliminate yeast purchases
Use all-purpose flour instead of bread flour if needed

recipes.name: Pumpernickel
recipes.description: German breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix rye flour, all-purpose flour, water, yeast, salt, and molasses in a bowl.
Knead dough for 10 minutes, then add caraway seeds and oil.
Knead another 5 minutes until dough is smooth, then let rise 1.5 hours.
Shape dough into a round loaf and place on parchment paper.
Let rise 1 hour until increased in size by about 50 percent.
Preheat oven to 400°F and bake for 40-45 minutes until dark brown.
Cool on a wire rack for at least 20 minutes before slicing.
cheapTips: Buy rye flour in bulk sections to save 30-40%
Omit caraway seeds if budget is tight

recipes.name: Bagel
recipes.description: Jewish-American breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, yeast, salt, and sugar until a stiff dough forms.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then let rise 1 hour.
Divide dough into 8 equal pieces and roll each into a ball.
Poke your thumb through each ball to create a hole and gently stretch into a bagel shape.
Let bagels rise on parchment paper for 45 minutes.
Bring a large pot of water to boil and add honey.
Boil each bagel 30 seconds per side, then place on a lined baking sheet.
Bake at 425°F for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.
cheapTips: Skip boiling step for faster homemade bagels
Make a double batch and freeze extras

recipes.name: Brioche
recipes.description: French breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, milk, and yeast and let rest 30 minutes.
Add 2 eggs, sugar, and salt, then mix until combined.
Gradually add softened butter in pieces while kneading for 8 minutes until smooth.
Let dough rise 1.5 hours until doubled in size.
Shape dough into a round and place in a greased loaf pan.
Let rise 1 hour until puffy.
Beat remaining egg and brush over top, then bake at 375°F for 25-30 minutes until golden.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes, then remove to a wire rack.
cheapTips: Use margarine instead of butter to reduce costs
Buy eggs when on sale and store in refrigerator

recipes.name: Pain de Campagne
recipes.description: French lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix bread flour, whole wheat flour, water, yeast, and salt in a bowl.
Let rest 15 minutes, then knead until smooth.
Perform stretch and fold every 30 minutes for 2 hours until dough is elastic.
Shape dough into a round boule and place on parchment paper.
Let rise 1.5 hours until puffy and jiggly.
Preheat oven to 450°F and score the top of dough with a knife.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until deep golden brown and hollow sounding when tapped.
Cool on a wire rack for at least 15 minutes before slicing.
cheapTips: Use store-brand flour to save money
Skip whole wheat flour and use all bread flour

recipes.name: Flute
recipes.description: French lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, yeast, and salt in a bowl until shaggy dough forms.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth, then let rise 1 hour.
Gently shape dough into a long, thin baguette-like loaf on parchment paper.
Let rise 1 hour until increased in volume by about 50 percent.
Preheat oven to 450°F and score the top with diagonal cuts.
Place flute on a baking sheet and bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Cool on a wire rack for at least 10 minutes before serving.
cheapTips: Buy flour in 5-pound bags instead of small packages
Use instant yeast instead of active dry yeast

recipes.name: Boule
recipes.description: French lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, yeast, and salt until dough comes together.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Shape dough into a tight ball and place on parchment paper.
Let rise 1 hour until nearly doubled in size.
Preheat oven to 450°F and score the top of the boule.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until golden brown and crusty.
Cool on a wire rack for at least 10 minutes.
cheapTips: Skip the scoring step to save time
Use self-rising flour as an alternative

recipes.name: Mantou
recipes.description: Chinese breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, water, yeast, sugar, and salt until dough forms.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Let rise 45 minutes until doubled in size.
Divide dough into 8 equal pieces and roll each into a ball.
Place on parchment squares and let rise 30 minutes.
Fill a steamer pot with water and bring to a boil.
Steam mantou for 12-15 minutes until fluffy and cooked through.
Remove carefully and serve warm.
cheapTips: Buy flour and yeast in bulk at Asian markets
Use a bamboo steamer basket for multiple batches

recipes.name: Taftan
recipes.description: Persian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Warm milk and dissolve saffron threads in it, then let cool slightly.
Mix flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Add saffron milk, 1 beaten egg, and butter, then knead for 10 minutes until smooth.
Let dough rise 1.5 hours until doubled in size.
Shape dough into a round and place on a baking sheet lined with parchment.
Let rise 45 minutes until puffy.
Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle nigella seeds on top.
Bake at 375°F for 25-30 minutes until golden brown.
cheapTips: Omit saffron and use turmeric for color instead
Use sesame seeds instead of nigella seeds

recipes.name: Caldo de Mariscos
recipes.description: Mexican lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and sauté diced onion and minced garlic for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add tomato sauce, chicken broth, and oregano, then bring to a boil.
Add fish fillet pieces and simmer for 5 minutes until cooked through.
Add shrimp and clams, stirring occasionally for 6-8 minutes until shrimp turns pink and clam shells open.
Discard any unopened clams and add lime juice, salt, and pepper to taste.
Ladle into bowls and garnish generously with fresh cilantro before serving.
cheapTips: Buy frozen shrimp and clams instead of fresh to save 30-40%
Use canned tomato sauce instead of fresh tomatoes for consistency and savings

recipes.name: Bouillabaisse Marseillaise
recipes.description: French lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté sliced onion, minced garlic, and diced fennel for 5 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes, fish stock, saffron, and orange zest, bringing to a simmer.
Season with salt and pepper, then simmer the broth for 10 minutes to develop flavor.
Add fish pieces and simmer for 4 minutes, then add mussels and shrimp.
Continue cooking for 4-6 minutes until fish flakes easily, mussels open, and shrimp are pink.
Toast baguette slices and divide seafood and broth into bowls, serving with toasted bread on the side.
cheapTips: Skip saffron and use turmeric for color and earthy flavor at 80% less cost
Buy frozen fish and mussels from discount stores

recipes.name: Sopa de Marisco
recipes.description: Spanish lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté diced onion and minced garlic for 3 minutes.
Add paprika and stir for 30 seconds, then add white wine and simmer for 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Pour in fish stock and diced tomatoes with their juice, add bay leaf, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and add clams and mussels, simmering for 5 minutes.
Add shrimp and continue simmering for 4-5 minutes until all seafood is cooked and shells have opened.
Remove bay leaf, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot in deep bowls.
cheapTips: Use chicken broth instead of fish stock to save $2-3 per pot
Buy pre-peeled frozen shrimp to reduce prep time and cost

recipes.name: Chowder
recipes.description: American lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Dice potatoes, onion, and celery, setting them aside separately.
Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion and celery for 4 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and stir constantly for 1 minute to create a roux.
Gradually add chicken broth while stirring to avoid lumps, then add potatoes, bay leaf, and thyme.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Drain clams, reserving their juice, and add both clams and clam juice to the pot along with heavy cream.
Simmer for 5 minutes without boiling, season with salt and pepper, remove bay leaf, and serve hot.
cheapTips: Canned clams are cheaper than fresh and work perfectly for chowder
Make your own broth from vegetable scraps instead of buying

recipes.name: Nabemono
recipes.description: Japanese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces, chop cabbage into wedges, slice mushrooms, cut tofu into cubes, and cut carrots into thin rounds.
In a large shallow pot or Dutch oven, combine broth, soy sauce, mirin, sake, and ginger, bringing to a boil.
Add chicken pieces and simmer for 5 minutes until cooked through.
Arrange vegetables and tofu around the pot in organized sections so diners can cook at their own pace.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes, allowing vegetables to soften and flavors to meld.
Chop green onions and sprinkle over the top, then serve directly from the pot with individual bowls.
cheapTips: Use regular mushrooms instead of shiitake to cut costs by 50%
Buy chicken thighs on sale and freeze for later use

recipes.name: Zarzuela
recipes.description: Spanish dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pan and sauté diced onion and minced garlic for 4 minutes until softened.
Add paprika and saffron, stirring for 30 seconds, then deglaze with white wine and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes and fish stock, bringing to a simmer and cooking for 5 minutes.
Cut monkfish into chunks and squid into rings, then add both to the broth and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add shrimp, scallops, and mussels, simmering for 5-7 minutes until mussels open and seafood is cooked.
Toast almonds in a dry pan and grind half of them, then stir into the zarzuela for body and richness.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with remaining whole almonds, and serve in shallow bowls.
cheapTips: Substitute half the seafood with firm white fish to reduce cost
Skip saffron or use a tiny amount as it's expensive; paprika alone works well

recipes.name: Aqua e Coze
recipes.description: Italian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and add thinly sliced garlic and red pepper flakes, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add clams and white wine, cover, and simmer for 3-4 minutes until clams begin to open.
Pour in fish broth and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add fish cut into large chunks and simmer uncovered for 5-7 minutes until fish is just cooked through and remaining clams have opened.
Discard any unopened clams and taste for seasoning, adjusting salt and pepper as needed.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley and serve in shallow bowls with crusty bread for soaking up the broth.
cheapTips: Use frozen clams and fish from discount stores to save 25-30%
Substitute vegetable broth for fish broth if cost is a concern

recipes.name: Danzai Noodles
recipes.description: Chinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium-high heat and brown the ground pork, breaking it apart as it cooks for 4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and ginger to the meat and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil, then add soy sauce and chili flakes.
Cook the ramen noodles separately in boiling salted water for 3 minutes, then drain.
Divide cooked noodles between two bowls and ladle the hot pork broth over them.
Drizzle with sesame oil and top with green onions before serving.
cheapTips: Buy ramen in bulk packs for under $0.30 per serving
Use ground pork shoulder instead of premium cuts

recipes.name: Malatang
recipes.description: Chinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Toast Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan for 1 minute, then crush roughly and set aside.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and add dried chilies and garlic, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken broth and bring to a boil, then stir in toasted peppercorns, soy sauce, and rice vinegar.
Add tofu, napa cabbage, and mushrooms to the broth and simmer for 8 minutes until vegetables soften.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more soy sauce or chili as desired.
Drizzle with sesame oil and garnish with green onions before serving hot.
cheapTips: Buy tofu from Asian markets for significantly less
Use regular black pepper if Sichuan peppercorns are unavailable

recipes.name: Cold Sesame Noodles
recipes.description: Chinese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook noodles in boiling salted water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water until chilled.
Whisk together sesame paste, soy sauce, rice vinegar, minced garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and chili oil in a bowl until smooth.
Add 2 tablespoons of warm water to the sauce to reach desired consistency.
Toss the cold noodles with the sauce until evenly coated.
Divide noodles between two bowls and top with julienned cucumber and chopped green onions.
cheapTips: Make your own sesame sauce from tahini instead of pricey sesame paste
Use regular spaghetti instead of ramen for savings

recipes.name: Bánh Mì Lạnh
recipes.description: Vietnamese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a bowl and toss with julienned cucumber and carrot, letting sit for 5 minutes.
Slice baguette lengthwise and lightly toast the cut sides if desired.
Spread mayonnaise on the bottom half and pâté on the top half of the baguette.
Layer the cold meats on the bottom half, then add the pickled vegetables, jalapeño slices, and cilantro.
Close the sandwich and cut in half, serving cold or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Use standard deli turkey or ham instead of Vietnamese cold cuts
Skip the pâté to reduce cost significantly

recipes.name: Gỏi Cuốn
recipes.description: Vietnamese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook vermicelli noodles according to package directions, then drain and cool.
Fill a shallow bowl with warm water and dip one rice paper wrapper in it for 10 seconds until pliable.
Lay wrapper on a clean surface and arrange lettuce leaf, then layer noodles, cucumber, shrimp, mint, and cilantro.
Fold the sides inward and tightly roll the wrapper away from you, similar to a spring roll.
Repeat with remaining wrappers and filling ingredients.
Whisk together peanut butter, hoisin sauce, lime juice, and water to make dipping sauce.
Serve spring rolls with sauce on the side for dipping.
cheapTips: Use frozen cooked shrimp which is usually cheaper than fresh
Replace shrimp with tofu for vegetarian version at lower cost

recipes.name: Tom Yum Sod
recipes.description: Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Bring chicken broth to a boil in a pot over high heat.
Add lemongrass, galangal, and lime leaves, simmering for 5 minutes to infuse flavors.
Add diced chicken and mushrooms, cooking for 5 minutes until chicken is nearly cooked through.
Add shrimp and Thai chilies, cooking for 2 minutes until shrimp turns pink.
Remove from heat and stir in lime juice and fish sauce, tasting and adjusting to balance spicy, sour, and salty flavors.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot.
cheapTips: Use frozen shrimp to reduce costs
Substitute ginger for galangal if unavailable

recipes.name: Soba Gaki
recipes.description: Japanese snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix buckwheat flour and salt in a bowl, then gradually add water while stirring until a thick batter forms.
Heat oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat and drop spoonfuls of batter into the pan, flattening slightly with the back of the spoon.
Cook each soba cake for 3-4 minutes on each side until golden brown and crispy.
Mix soy sauce, mirin, and dashi broth in a small bowl to create a glaze.
Brush the glaze on both sides of each cooked soba cake.
Plate the soba gaki and top with chopped green onions and sesame seeds before serving.
cheapTips: Buy buckwheat flour from bulk sections at grocery stores
Use regular soy sauce and skip mirin for budget version

recipes.name: Ramen Hiyashi
recipes.description: Japanese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook ramen noodles in boiling salted water for 3 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water until chilled.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook sliced chicken breast for 4 minutes until cooked through, seasoning with soy sauce and mirin.
Mix dashi broth with soy sauce and mirin to make a chilled broth, then refrigerate.
Boil eggs for 6-7 minutes for soft-boiled, then cool and halve.
Divide chilled noodles between two bowls and pour cold broth over them.
Top with chicken, cucumber, tomato, soft-boiled egg halves, nori strips, sesame seeds, and green onions.
cheapTips: Buy ramen noodles in bulk for minimal cost
Use store-brand soy sauce to cut costs

recipes.name: Puy Lentil Stew
recipes.description: French dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion, carrot, and celery for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in puy lentils, vegetable broth, bay leaf, and thyme sprigs.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 30-35 minutes until lentils are tender but not mushy.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs before serving hot.
cheapTips: Buy lentils from bulk bins for significant savings
Use vegetable scraps for homemade broth

recipes.name: Caldo de Habas
recipes.description: Spanish lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse dried fava beans and soak in water for at least 4 hours or overnight, then drain.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onion and ham for 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and paprika, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and add soaked beans, diced potatoes, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 25-30 minutes until beans and potatoes are tender.
Taste and season with salt and pepper as needed, then serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy dried beans in bulk for significant savings
Use standard deli ham instead of expensive jamón

recipes.name: Fogo de Chão
recipes.description: Brazilian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes.
Cut all meats into 2-inch chunks and thread onto skewers, alternating varieties.
Season all skewered meats heavily with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Heat a charcoal grill or gas grill to high heat until very hot.
Grill skewers 3-4 minutes per side until meat is browned and cooked through.
Serve immediately with rice, black beans, and chimichurri sauce on the side.
cheapTips: Buy sirloin or chuck instead of premium cuts to reduce cost by $2-3 per serving.
Skip variety and use one type of meat for a simpler, cheaper version.

recipes.name: Mojo Pork
recipes.description: Cuban dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mince garlic and combine with lime juice, orange juice, salt, pepper, cumin, and olive oil to make marinade.
Score the pork skin with a knife in a crosshatch pattern.
Place pork in a large roasting pan and cover completely with mojo marinade.
Cover tightly with foil and refrigerate for at least 8 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat oven to 350°F and bake covered for 4 hours, basting every 45 minutes.
Remove foil, increase heat to 425°F, and bake uncovered for 30 minutes until skin is crispy.
Rest for 10 minutes, then shred meat with two forks and serve with reserved pan sauce.
cheapTips: Pork shoulder is one of the cheapest cuts; marinating overnight makes it tender and flavorful.
Use bottled lime and orange juice instead of fresh to save $1-2 per serving.

recipes.name: Tsipouro Skewers
recipes.description: Greek snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut fish into 1-inch cubes and cut red onion into thick wedges.
Whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Thread fish cubes, onion pieces, and cherry tomatoes alternately onto skewers.
Brush skewers generously with the olive oil mixture on all sides.
Heat a grill or grill pan to high heat and cook skewers 2-3 minutes per side until fish is opaque.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and crusty bread for dipping.
cheapTips: Use frozen white fish fillets instead of fresh sea bass; thaw and cut into cubes.
Buy canned or jarred tomatoes if fresh are expensive, though texture will differ slightly.

recipes.name: Galbi
recipes.description: Korean dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut beef short ribs between the bones into individual ribs and place in a large bowl.
Peel and grate pear and ginger, then mince garlic.
Combine soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, rice vinegar, pear, ginger, and garlic to make marinade.
Pour marinade over ribs, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat a grill or cast-iron skillet to high heat.
Grill ribs 3-4 minutes per side until browned and cooked to desired doneness.
Arrange on a platter, garnish with sliced green onion and sesame seeds, and serve with rice.
cheapTips: Beef short ribs are typically cheaper than other premium cuts; marinating tenderizes them.
Omit the pear and use an extra tablespoon of brown sugar for nearly the same sweetness.

recipes.name: Carne à Brás
recipes.description: Portuguese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut beef into thin strips about 2 inches long and 0.5 inch wide.
Cut potatoes into thin matchstick fries and soak in cold water for 15 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and sauté sliced onion and minced garlic until soft.
Add beef strips and cook 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned on the edges.
Stir in tomato paste and cook 1 minute, then add beef broth and bay leaf, and simmer 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat remaining oil in a deep skillet to 350°F and fry potatoes in batches 4-5 minutes until golden and crispy; drain on paper towels and season with salt.
Combine the cooked beef mixture with crispy potatoes, toss gently, and serve hot garnished with fresh parsley.
cheapTips: Use chuck roast instead of sirloin and slice thinly; long cooking tenderizes it.
Bake potatoes in the oven at 425°F instead of frying to reduce oil cost by $0.50-1.00.

recipes.name: Cataplana
recipes.description: Portuguese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Scrub clams under cold water and discard any that are open or cracked.
Slice chorizo into thin rounds, dice onion, and mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or cataplana over medium-high heat and sauté chorizo 2 minutes until fat releases.
Add onion and garlic, cooking 3 minutes until softened.
Add wine and simmer 2 minutes to reduce slightly, then stir in canned tomatoes, bay leaves, salt, and pepper.
Add clams and sea bass fillets, cover, and simmer 12-15 minutes until clams open and fish is cooked through, discarding any clams that don't open.
Serve hot in shallow bowls, garnished with fresh parsley, with crusty bread for soaking up the sauce.
cheapTips: Buy frozen clams and thaw overnight; they're usually $2-3 cheaper per pound.
Substitute with mussels, which are often less expensive and cook similarly.

recipes.name: Brodetto
recipes.description: Italian lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Scrub mussels under cold water and remove beards, discarding any open or cracked mussels.
Dice onion, mince garlic, and cut fish fillets into 2-inch chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion and garlic 4 minutes until soft.
Add white wine and simmer 2 minutes to reduce, then stir in crushed tomatoes, fish broth, salt, and pepper flakes.
Bring to a simmer and add fish chunks, then cook 4 minutes before adding shrimp and mussels.
Cover and cook 6-8 minutes until shrimp is pink, mussels open, and fish is opaque, discarding any mussels that don't open.
Stir in fresh basil and serve hot in bowls with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Buy whatever white fish is on sale; frozen cod, pollock, or tilapia work well.
Skip the shrimp and use extra mussels to save $1-2 per serving.

recipes.name: Caldeirada
recipes.description: Portuguese lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut potatoes into 0.75-inch cubes and slice onions into thick rounds.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté onion and minced garlic 4 minutes until soft.
Add potatoes, canned tomatoes, fish broth, bay leaves, salt, and pepper, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes until potatoes are almost tender.
Add fish fillets and simmer gently 8-10 minutes until fish is cooked through and potatoes are tender.
Season with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Ladle into bowls, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve hot with crusty bread.
cheapTips: Use the cheapest white fish available: tilapia, pollock, or frozen cod.
Buy potatoes in bulk; they're inexpensive and store well.

recipes.name: Bouillie
recipes.description: Provençal lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Scrub mussels, remove beards, and discard any open or cracked mussels.
Cut fish into 2-inch chunks; dice onion, mince garlic, and thinly slice fennel.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté onion, garlic, and fennel 5 minutes until soft.
Add crushed tomatoes, fish broth, bay leaves, saffron, orange zest, salt, and pepper, and bring to a simmer.
Simmer 10 minutes, then add fish chunks and cook 5 minutes.
Add mussels and shrimp, cover, and simmer 6-8 minutes until shrimp is pink, mussels open, and fish is opaque, discarding unopened mussels.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with toasted bread and rouille (garlic mayonnaise).
cheapTips: Omit the saffron (expensive) or use a tiny pinch; turmeric can substitute for color.
Use only mussels and skip shrimp and extra fish to reduce cost by $1.50-2.00 per serving.

recipes.name: Pla Rad Prik
recipes.description: Thai lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: If using whole fish, clean and gut it; pat fish dry with paper towels.
Heat oil in a deep pan or wok to 350°F.
Carefully lower fish into hot oil and fry 8-10 minutes per side for whole fish, or 4-5 minutes per side for fillets, until golden and crispy.
Remove fish and drain on paper towels.
Pour off most oil, leaving 2 tablespoons in the pan; add minced garlic, sliced shallots, and dried chilies, cooking 2 minutes until fragrant.
Whisk together fish sauce, lime juice, and brown sugar in a small bowl.
Pour sauce over crispy fish, sprinkle with sliced green onion and cilantro, and serve immediately with jasmine rice.
cheapTips: Buy whole tilapia or mackerel, which are cheaper than fillets and stay crispy when fried.
Use frozen fish fillets and thaw to save $1.00-1.50 per serving versus fresh.

recipes.name: Cholent
recipes.description: Jewish lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak kidney beans in water for 8 hours or overnight, then drain.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef chuck on all sides, about 8 minutes total.
Add diced onions and minced garlic to the pot and sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Stir in paprika, salt, and black pepper, then add drained beans, barley, and 8 cups of water.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 8 hours (or cook in a slow cooker on low for 8-10 hours).
Stir occasionally and add water if the liquid reduces too much.
The cholent is done when the meat is very tender and beans are completely soft.
cheapTips: Buy dried beans in bulk instead of canned to save money
Use the cheapest beef chuck cuts available; long cooking tenderizes tough cuts

recipes.name: Dal Tadka
recipes.description: Indian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Rinse the split peas under cold water until the water runs clear.
In a large pot, bring 4 cups of water to a boil and add the rinsed dal, turmeric, and salt.
Reduce heat to medium and simmer for 25-30 minutes until the dal is soft and breaks apart easily.
Heat ghee in a small pan over medium heat and add cumin seeds, letting them crackle for about 30 seconds.
Add minced garlic and diced onion to the ghee and cook until the onion is golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Add the dried red chilies to the pan and cook for 1 minute, then pour the entire mixture into the cooked dal.
Stir well, add lemon juice, and garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.
cheapTips: Buy split peas in bulk from Indian or Asian grocery stores
Use vegetable oil instead of ghee to reduce costs

recipes.name: Pinto Bean Stew
recipes.description: New Mexican dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak pinto beans overnight in water, then drain.
Cook bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crispy, remove and chop into pieces.
In the same pot, sauté diced onion and minced garlic in bacon fat until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the drained beans, bacon pieces, dried chile peppers, beef broth, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 60-75 minutes until beans are very tender.
Remove the whole dried chile peppers and mash some of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the stew.
Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper to taste.
cheapTips: Buy beans dried in bulk to save significantly over canned
Use bacon ends and pieces instead of whole strips

recipes.name: Lobia
recipes.description: Afghan lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak dried black-eyed peas in water for 6 hours or overnight, then drain.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté diced onions until golden, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, then stir in tomato paste, turmeric, and cumin.
Add the drained peas and 6 cups of fresh water to the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 45-50 minutes until peas are completely tender.
Season with salt and black pepper, and stir in fresh cilantro.
Simmer for an additional 5 minutes and serve hot.
cheapTips: Buy black-eyed peas dried in bulk for lowest cost
Omit cilantro garnish to save a few cents per serving

recipes.name: Picanha
recipes.description: Brazilian dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Remove the picanha from the refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking to bring it to room temperature.
Score the fat cap in a crosshatch pattern without cutting into the meat.
Rub the entire steak generously with coarse sea salt and black pepper on both sides.
Heat olive oil in a large cast iron skillet or grill to high heat until smoking.
Place the steak fat-side down in the hot pan first and sear for 6-7 minutes to render and crisp the fat.
Flip the steak and sear the meat side for 5-6 minutes for medium-rare doneness, then add garlic and rosemary to the pan.
Remove from heat, tent loosely with foil, and rest for 8 minutes before slicing against the grain and squeezing fresh lime juice over top.
cheapTips: Shop sales at butcher counters for better picanha prices
Sirloin cap is less expensive than premium steaks but very flavorful

recipes.name: Tiptoe
recipes.description: Thai snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cook sticky rice according to package directions and let it cool slightly.
Heat coconut milk in a small saucepan with brown sugar and salt until the sugar dissolves completely.
Mix the warm coconut mixture into the cooked sticky rice and let it absorb for 5 minutes.
Warm banana leaves over a flame or boiling water to make them pliable.
Place a portion of the coconut-sticky rice mixture in the center of each banana leaf.
Sprinkle generously with sesame seeds over the rice.
Fold the banana leaf into a triangle or pouch and serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Buy sticky rice in bulk from Asian markets
Use parchment paper instead of banana leaves to save money

recipes.name: Gyros
recipes.description: Greek lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Pulse minced onion and garlic in a food processor until very finely chopped.
Combine ground lamb, ground beef, minced onion mixture, oregano, paprika, cumin, salt, and black pepper in a bowl and mix until just combined.
Form the mixture into a loaf shape on a sheet pan lined with foil.
Bake at 400°F for 25-30 minutes until the internal temperature reaches 160°F.
Remove from oven and let rest for 5 minutes, then slice thinly with a sharp knife.
Warm pita bread in the oven or over a flame for 1-2 minutes until pliable.
Fill each pita with sliced gyro meat, diced tomato, sliced red onion, and a generous dollop of tzatziki sauce.
cheapTips: Mix lamb with cheaper ground beef to stretch the meat and reduce costs
Make tzatziki at home with yogurt, cucumber, and garlic instead of buying pre-made

recipes.name: Chicharon
recipes.description: Filipino snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Cut pork skin into 1-inch by 1-inch squares with some fat attached.
Bring 6 cups of water to boil with 1 teaspoon salt and crushed garlic cloves.
Add pork skin pieces and boil for 20-25 minutes until the skin becomes soft and fat renders slightly.
Drain the pork skin completely and spread on paper towels to dry for 10 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil to 375°F in a deep skillet or pot.
Carefully add dried pork skin pieces in batches and fry for 3-4 minutes per batch, stirring constantly until they puff up and turn golden brown.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on fresh paper towels, then season immediately with remaining salt and black pepper while hot.
cheapTips: Buy pork skin from Asian butchers or from the butcher counter where it's often inexpensive
Reuse cooking oil for multiple batches to minimize oil cost

recipes.name: Lamb Tikka
recipes.description: Indian snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Blend yogurt, minced garlic, grated ginger, garam masala, turmeric, paprika, lemon juice, and salt into a smooth paste.
Coat lamb cubes thoroughly with the yogurt marinade and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, preferably overnight.
Preheat oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with foil.
Thread marinated lamb onto wooden skewers (soaked in water for 30 minutes) and place on the prepared baking sheet.
Brush skewers lightly with vegetable oil and bake for 18-22 minutes until the lamb is cooked through and slightly charred at the edges.
Alternatively, grill the skewers over medium-high heat for 12-15 minutes, turning occasionally.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and sliced onions.
cheapTips: Use lamb shoulder instead of premium cuts to save money
Make your own garam masala blend or buy it from Indian grocery stores for better prices

recipes.name: Grilled Lamb Kofta
recipes.description: Lebanese dinner — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Soak wooden skewers in water for at least 30 minutes before grilling.
Finely mince onion, mint, parsley, and garlic using a food processor or knife.
Combine ground lamb with minced herb mixture, allspice, cumin, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl.
Mix gently with your hands until just combined, being careful not to overwork the meat.
Divide mixture into 8 equal portions and mold each firmly onto a soaked skewer into a long, thin shape.
Brush kofta with olive oil and place on a preheated grill over medium-high heat.
Grill for 10-12 minutes, turning every 2-3 minutes until cooked through with slight charring.
Remove from grill and serve immediately with lemon wedges and pita bread.
cheapTips: Buy ground lamb when on sale and freeze for later use
Use dried mint and parsley instead of fresh to reduce costs

recipes.name: Huevos con Chorizo
recipes.description: Tex-Mex breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Remove chorizo from casing and crumble into a skillet over medium heat, cooking until browned and cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Dice the onion and jalapeño, then add to the chorizo and cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Crack eggs into a bowl, beat lightly with salt and pepper, then pour into the skillet with the chorizo mixture.
Stir gently and cook until eggs are scrambled and set, about 3-4 minutes.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side.
Divide the chorizo and egg mixture between tortillas and serve immediately.
cheapTips: Buy chorizo in bulk when on sale and freeze individual portions
Use regular onion instead of sweet onion to save 20 cents per serving

recipes.name: Crispy Tacos
recipes.description: Tex-Mex lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and warm each tortilla briefly until pliable, about 15 seconds per side.
Fold each tortilla in half and fry in hot oil until crispy and golden, about 1 minute per side, then drain on paper towels.
Brown ground beef in the same skillet, breaking it apart with a spoon, about 5 minutes.
Add taco seasoning and water to the beef, stirring well, and simmer for 2 minutes.
Fill each crispy taco shell with seasoned beef, then top with cheese, lettuce, and tomatoes.
Serve warm with sour cream on the side.
cheapTips: Make your own taco seasoning from cumin, chili powder, and paprika for half the cost
Buy ground beef when on manager's special and freeze immediately

recipes.name: Sopapillas
recipes.description: Tex-Mex snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl, then add warm water and stir until a soft dough forms.
Knead dough on a floured surface for 2 minutes until smooth, then let rest 10 minutes covered with a damp towel.
Roll dough out to 1/8-inch thickness and cut into 3-inch squares using a knife.
Heat oil in a deep skillet to 375°F and carefully fry dough squares until golden and puffed, about 1 minute per side.
Drain fried sopapillas on paper towels.
Mix cinnamon and sugar in a shallow dish and toss warm sopapillas to coat lightly.
Serve warm with honey drizzled over or on the side for dipping.
cheapTips: Reuse frying oil by straining through cheesecloth and storing in the refrigerator
Buy honey in bulk or use agave nectar as a cheaper alternative

recipes.name: Corned Beef Sandwich
recipes.description: Jewish Deli lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice corned beef into 1/8-inch thick slices if not pre-sliced.
Spread mustard lightly on two slices of rye bread.
Layer half of the corned beef on each mustard-coated slice, then top with one slice of Swiss cheese and onion slices.
Top with remaining rye bread slices.
Butter the outside of each sandwich lightly on both sides.
Toast in a skillet over medium heat until bread is golden and cheese melts, about 3 minutes per side.
Cut diagonally and serve immediately with kosher pickles on the side.
cheapTips: Buy day-old rye bread from the bakery section for 30-50% off
Use store-brand corned beef instead of premium brands

recipes.name: Half-Sour Pickles
recipes.description: Jewish Deli snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Wash cucumbers thoroughly and trim off the blossom ends to prevent mushiness.
Pack cucumbers upright into a clean quart jar with dill, garlic, and peppercorns.
Combine water, vinegar, salt, and red pepper flakes in a pot and bring to a boil, stirring until salt dissolves.
Pour the hot brine over cucumbers in the jar until completely covered, leaving 1/2 inch headspace.
Cover loosely and let cool to room temperature.
Refrigerate for at least 3 hours before eating; they will keep for 2-3 weeks.
cheapTips: Buy cucumbers during peak season in summer for best prices
Use white vinegar instead of specialty pickling vinegar to save 40%

recipes.name: Knish
recipes.description: Jewish Deli snack — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Mix flour, 1 egg, oil, salt, and 1/2 cup water to form a soft dough, then knead until smooth and let rest 15 minutes.
Peel and chop potatoes, then boil until tender, about 12 minutes, and drain well.
Dice onion and sauté in butter until golden, about 5 minutes.
Mash hot potatoes with the cooked onion, butter, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Roll dough thin between parchment paper, then spread potato filling evenly over it.
Roll dough tightly into a log and coil it, then place seam-side down on a greased baking sheet.
Brush with beaten egg wash and bake at 375°F until golden brown, about 25-30 minutes.
Cool slightly, then slice and serve warm or at room temperature.
cheapTips: Make filling ahead and refrigerate to streamline prep work
Buy potatoes in bulk bags during sales for significant savings

recipes.name: Chopped Liver
recipes.description: Jewish Deli lunch — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Hard-boil eggs in a pot of water for 10 minutes, then cool and peel.
Dice onion and cook in chicken fat over medium heat until deeply caramelized, about 8 minutes, then set aside.
Add chicken liver to the same pan and cook over medium-high heat until no longer pink inside, about 4-5 minutes.
Place cooled liver, hard-boiled eggs, and caramelized onion in a food processor.
Pulse until chopped but not completely smooth, maintaining a rustic texture.
Season with kosher salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve at room temperature on matzo crackers or rye bread as an appetizer or spread.
cheapTips: Chicken livers are often on sale at ethnic or kosher markets
Use rendered chicken fat saved from cooking chicken instead of butter

recipes.name: Lox and Bagel
recipes.description: Jewish Deli breakfast — a popular dish you can make at home.
steps: Slice bagels in half horizontally and toast in a toaster until golden and crispy.
Spread 2 tablespoons of cream cheese on each toasted bagel half.
Layer lox evenly over cream cheese on each bagel.
